default.q.n3-1-q36-36.explanation:
Meaning: “I hear that my friend Naka really likes Kyoto and has apparently been there many times.”
Structure: Interrogative indicating quantity + も = emphasizes a large quantity (e.g., 何度も - many times, 何回も - many times, 何枚も - many sheets/pieces).
Example: この映画はとても面白いので、もう何度も見ました。 (This movie is very interesting, so I have already watched it many times.)
default.q.n3-1-q36-36.why.0: (a) 「何度も」 combines an interrogative quantity word with 「も」 to emphasize a high frequency or quantity (“many times”), fitting the preceding statement that the speaker likes Kyoto very much.
default.q.n3-1-q36-36.why.1: (b) 「は」 does not directly follow 「何度」 to emphasize a large number of times in this affirmative sentence.
default.q.n3-1-q36-36.why.2: (c) 「など」means “such as” or “for example” and is used to list examples; it does not combine with 「何度」to express frequency.
default.q.n3-1-q36-36.why.3: (d) 「ぐらい」 indicates an approximate amount (“about” or “approximately”) and is commonly used in questions such as 「何回ぐらい」. It is not used to emphasize having gone many times.
default.q.n3-1-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 4. なんか.
default.q.n3-1-q37-37.explanation:
Meaning:
A: “Hey, would you like to have lunch together?”
B: “Sure, let's go. What should we eat?”
A: “Since it is so cold, how about some hot udon?”
Pattern: N + なんか is the casual spoken form of など and is used when giving an example or making a gentle suggestion.
Example: 疲れたときは、温かいお風呂に入るなんかどうですか。 (When you are tired, how about taking a hot bath?)
default.q.n3-1-q37-37.why.0: (a) 「に」 cannot directly combine to form 「うどんにどう」; to make a suggestion with 「に」, use the pattern 「〜にする？」 (What shall we choose/order?).
default.q.n3-1-q37-37.why.1: (b) 「だけ」means “only.” The expression “only udon, how about that?” is unnatural and does not function as a suggestion for a dish.
default.q.n3-1-q37-37.why.2: (c) 「まで」 means “up to” or “even,” and is not used in the context of suggesting menu items.
default.q.n3-1-q37-37.why.3: (d) 「なんか」 is the spoken form of 「など」. After a noun, it forms 「N + なんかどう？」, which offers a gentle suggestion such as “How about N?”
default.q.n3-1-q38-38.verdict: The answer given in the question is 3. でしか (however, with the affirmative predicate 「伝えられる」, the grammatically correct answer should be 1. でなら).
default.q.n3-1-q38-38.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “I always write letters on my parents’ birthdays. That is because only through handwritten letters (or by writing a letter) can I express the gratitude I usually feel too embarrassed to say aloud.”
Note: The pattern 「〜でなら」 means “if it is by means of N, then it is possible to...,” and is used with an affirmative statement. The pattern 「〜でしか...ない」 means “can only be done by means of N” and must be followed by a negative ending.
default.q.n3-1-q38-38.why.0: (a) 「でなら」 expresses a condition involving a means or method (“if it is by letter…”). Combined with the potential form 「伝えられる」 in the following clause, it is grammatically the most appropriate choice.
default.q.n3-1-q38-38.why.1: (b) 「になら」uses the particle 「に」inappropriately to indicate the means or manner of writing a letter to convey one's feelings.
default.q.n3-1-q38-38.why.2: (c) As given in the answer choices, 「でしか」 would mean "only by letter," but according to standard grammar, 「〜しか」 must be followed by a negative predicate (「伝えられない」), whereas the question uses the affirmative 「伝えられる」.
default.q.n3-1-q38-38.why.3: (d) 「にしか」 incorrectly uses the particle 「に」 to indicate means and also requires the negative ending 「〜ない」.
default.q.n3-1-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 2. あまりに.
default.q.n3-1-q39-39.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “I usually ride my bicycle to university even when it rains, but this morning it was raining so heavily that I took the bus.”
Adverb: あまりに / あまりにも: excessively, so much that it leads to an unusual result.
Example: あまりに忙しくて、朝ご飯を食べる時間がなかった。 (I was so busy that I did not even have time to eat breakfast.)
default.q.n3-1-q39-39.why.0: (a) 「ちっとも」 means “not even a little” and is always used with the negative form 「〜ない」.
default.q.n3-1-q39-39.why.1: (b) 「あまりに」 (or あまりにも) means “excessively” or “too much.” It modifies 「強かった」 to express that the rain was unusually heavy, making it appropriate as the reason for taking the bus.
default.q.n3-1-q39-39.why.2: (c) 「次第に」 means “gradually” or “little by little” and is usually used with verbs expressing change, such as 次第に強くなった. It does not directly modify the adjective 「強かった」 to state an immediate reason in this way.
default.q.n3-1-q39-39.why.3: (d) 「今にも」 means “any moment now” or “very soon,” and commonly occurs with the structure 「〜そうだ」 (for example, 今にも雨が降りそうだ — “It looks like it is about to rain.”).
default.q.n3-1-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 3. にしたがって.
default.q.n3-1-q40-40.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “I went mountain climbing last week. Although it was a hot day, the higher we climbed, the cooler the wind became, which felt wonderful.”
Pattern: V-る / N + にしたがって (as..., in accordance with...) = the more... the more... / as A changes, B changes accordingly.
Kanji meaning: 登山 (mountain climbing).
Example: 台風が近づくにしたがって、風雨が強くなってきた。 (As the typhoon approached, the wind and rain grew increasingly stronger.)
default.q.n3-1-q40-40.why.0: (a) 「とすると」 means “assuming that” or “if that is the case” and is used in hypothetical sentences. It does not express simultaneous change over an actual progression.
default.q.n3-1-q40-40.why.1: (b) 「のと比べると」means “compared with,” and is used to compare two objects; it does not express a proportional change resulting from climbing a mountain.
default.q.n3-1-q40-40.why.2: (c) 「にしたがって」 (V-る + にしたがって) means “the more... the more...” or “as... progresses.” It accurately expresses that the higher one climbs, the colder the wind becomes.
default.q.n3-1-q40-40.why.3: (d) 「のに対して」 means “in contrast to / as opposed to,” and is used to compare two contrasting clauses, so it does not fit here.
default.q.n3-1-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 読み終わったら.
default.q.n3-1-q41-41.explanation:
Sentence meaning:
Younger sister: “Sis, have you finished reading this manga? Can I borrow it?”
Older sister: “Oh, I'm still in the middle of reading that one. I'll lend it to you when I finish.”
Structure: V-stem + 終わる = finish doing V; V-たら = after... then...
Example: この本を読み終わったら、図書館に返してください。 (After you finish reading this book, please return it to the library.)
default.q.n3-1-q41-41.why.0: (a) 「読んでいたら」 means “if one is reading” or “if one has read” and cannot express the completed reading needed before lending the item.
default.q.n3-1-q41-41.why.1: (b) 「読み続けたら」 means “if you continue reading,” which does not fit the context because the book must be finished before it can be lent.
default.q.n3-1-q41-41.why.2: (c) 「読んでおいたら」 means “if you read it in advance,” which does not match the sister’s intention: she is still reading it and will lend it out once she has finished.
default.q.n3-1-q41-41.why.3: (d) 「読み終わったら」combines naturally with V-stem + 終わる to mean “after finishing reading.” It fits the context in which the sister is still reading and promises to lend the book to her younger sibling once she finishes.
default.q.n3-1-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 帰ってしまう前に.
default.q.n3-1-q42-42.explanation:
Meaning: “Before my friend leaves the country, I want to do many things together.”
Pattern: V-る + 前に = before doing V. Adding 「〜てしまう」emphasizes the regret associated with the event.
Example: 日本を離れてしまう前に、富士山に登ってみたい。 (Before leaving Japan, I would like to try climbing Mount Fuji.)
default.q.n3-1-q42-42.why.0: (a) 「帰っていて」indicates that you have returned to your country and are there now; in that situation, the two people are far apart and cannot “do many things together.”
default.q.n3-1-q42-42.why.1: (b) 「帰ってしまえば」means “if you have already gone back to your country,” which conflicts with the desire to do many things together in the present.
default.q.n3-1-q42-42.why.2: (c) 「帰っている間」 means “while you are returning” or “while you are in your country.” It cannot express doing several activities together during that time.
default.q.n3-1-q42-42.why.3: (d) 「帰ってしまう前に」 (V-てしまう前に) means “before you leave the country.” The pattern V-る + 前に expresses the point in time before an event occurs, which fits the desire to make the most of the time with the friend.
default.q.n3-1-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 建てられたのは.
default.q.n3-1-q43-43.explanation:
Meaning: “This temple is the oldest temple in the prefecture; it is said to have been built more than 1,000 years ago.”
Pattern: Passive form (受身形) + のは〜だ: a cleft sentence pattern that emphasizes a time, cause, or object.
Sino-Japanese readings: 寺 (てら: temple), 県内 (けんない: within the prefecture).
Example: この橋が造られたのは、江戸時代のことだ。(This bridge was built during the Edo period.)
default.q.n3-1-q43-43.why.0: (a) 「建てられてからは」 means “since it was built,” so the following clause must describe an ongoing state, not a time reference such as 「今から1000年以上前だ」.
default.q.n3-1-q43-43.why.1: (b) 「建てられたのは」 combines the passive form 「建てられた」 with the nominalizing 「のは」 to create the focus structure 「〜のは ... だ」, meaning “The time when it was built was more than 1,000 years ago.” This is completely correct.
default.q.n3-1-q43-43.why.2: (c) 「建てさせるまでは」 uses the causative form 「建てさせる」 (“make or allow someone to build”) and 「までは」 (“until”), making both the meaning and grammar completely inappropriate.
default.q.n3-1-q43-43.why.3: (d) 「建てさせたときは」 uses the causative form 「建てさせた」 (“when someone was made or allowed to build”); it does not fit because the subject is the temple being built.
default.q.n3-1-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 3. みたいだ.
default.q.n3-1-q44-44.explanation:
Meaning:
Younger brother: “Yes. That restaurant seems to be very popular. Yesterday, when I walked past it, I saw a long line of people waiting outside.”
Pattern: Plain form + みたいだ = seems like / appears to be, based on direct evidence.
Example: あのレストランはいつも混んでいるから、料理が美味しいみたいだ。 (That restaurant is always crowded, so its food must be delicious.)
default.q.n3-1-q44-44.why.0: (a) 「ことだ」 is used to give advice (“should / should not do something”) or express emotion; it is not used to make a judgment about a state or condition.
default.q.n3-1-q44-44.why.1: (b) 「せいだ」 means “because of…” or “due to…,” indicating a cause that leads to a bad result, so it is unsuitable here.
default.q.n3-1-q44-44.why.2: (c) 「みたいだ」is used to make a judgment or inference based on observable evidence (“it seems that / apparently”), which fits the evidence that many people were seen lining up yesterday.
default.q.n3-1-q44-44.why.3: (d) 「つもりだ」 means “to intend to do something” or “to believe mistakenly that something is true.” It is not used to judge the qualities of a shop.
default.q.n3-1-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 教えてほしいんですが.
default.q.n3-1-q45-45.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence:
Mori: “Excuse me, Oshita. If you know of a good eye clinic nearby, could you please tell me where it is? My eyes have been itchy since this morning.”
Structure: V-てほしい = want someone to do V; V-てほしいんですが is used to make a polite, tactful request.
Kanji compound: 眼科 (ophthalmology; eye clinic).
Example: 駅への行き方を教えてほしいんですが。 (Could you tell me how to get to the station?)
default.q.n3-1-q45-45.why.0: (a) 「教えたいんですが」 means “I want to show you” or “I would like to tell you.” The direction of the action is wrong because Mori wants to be shown the clinic.
default.q.n3-1-q45-45.why.1: (b) 「教えてもいいですか」 means “May I show or teach you?”, so the direction of the action is reversed.
default.q.n3-1-q45-45.why.2: (c) 「教えてもらうんですか」 asks, “Are you being taught by someone?” It is not a request for someone’s help.
default.q.n3-1-q45-45.why.3: (d) 「教えてほしいんですが」 combines the structure 「〜てほしい」 (wanting someone to do something for oneself) with 「んですが」 to make a polite request (“If you know, I would appreciate it if you could tell me”), so it is completely correct.
default.q.n3-1-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 2. わからないはずがない.
default.q.n3-1-q46-46.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "Since this is a chart made by Mr. Hayashi himself, there is no way I could fail to understand it."
Structure: V-ない + はずがない = a double negative meaning "there is no way that... / surely..."
Example: 毎日一生懸命練習したのだから、合格できないはずがない。(You practiced hard every day, so there is no way you cannot pass.)
default.q.n3-1-q46-46.why.0: (a) 「わからないに違いない」 means “must not understand,” which contradicts the confidence expressed in the preceding clause: “because it was done by Hayashi.”
default.q.n3-1-q46-46.why.1: (b) 「わからないはずがない」 uses the double-negative structure 「〜ないはずがない」, meaning "there is no way that he does not understand" or "he is certain to understand." It expresses absolute confidence in Hayashi's ability.
default.q.n3-1-q46-46.why.2: (c) 「わからないかもしれない」 means "might not understand," expressing uncertain doubt; this does not match the assertive reasoning expressed by 「〜なのだから」.
default.q.n3-1-q46-46.why.3: (d) 「わからないでもしかたない」 means "even if one does not understand it, there is nothing to be done," expressing resignation and conflicting with the sentence's trusting attitude.
default.q.n3-1-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 買ってきてくれる.
default.q.n3-1-q47-47.explanation:
Meaning: "Whenever my father goes on a business trip, he is sure to bring gifts home for my mother and me."
Pattern: V-てくる (do something and return to the original location); V-てくれる (someone does something for me or someone on my side).
Kanji notes: 出張 means business trip; お土産 means souvenir or specialty gift.
Example: 兄は旅行のお土産に美味しいお菓子を買ってきてくれた。(My older brother bought and brought me some delicious sweets as a souvenir from his trip.)
default.q.n3-1-q47-47.why.0: (a) 「買ってきてあげる」uses 「あげる」for an action the speaker does for someone else. It should not be used when another person, such as the father, does something for the speaker or the speaker's family.
default.q.n3-1-q47-47.why.1: (b) 「買っていってあげる」 uses the wrong direction of movement in 「ていく」 (away from the speaker) and the wrong giving-and-receiving auxiliary 「あげる」.
default.q.n3-1-q47-47.why.2: (c) 「買ってきてくれる」correctly combines the direction of movement in「てくる」(buy something and bring it back here) with the giving-and-receiving structure「くれる」(someone does something for me or a member of my family).
default.q.n3-1-q47-47.why.3: (d) 「買っていってくれる」 incorrectly uses 「ていく」, meaning to buy something and take it elsewhere. The father goes on a business trip and brings gifts back home for his mother and me.
default.q.n3-1-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 出られそうだ.
default.q.n3-1-q48-48.explanation:
Meaning: “I will probably be able to go to school tomorrow.”
Pattern: potential form of V (without ます) + そうだ = it looks like / I will probably be able to V (a judgment based on one’s health, time, or other circumstances).
Example: 熱が下がったので、明日の試合には出られそうだ。 (My fever has gone down, so I will probably be able to participate in tomorrow’s match.)
default.q.n3-1-q48-48.why.0: (a) 「出られそうだ」combines the potential form 「出られる」with ます removed and 「そうだ」, meaning “it seems/probably I can attend.” It expresses the speaker’s judgment about their own ability to attend the class.
default.q.n3-1-q48-48.why.1: (b) 「出られるそうだ」 uses 「plain form + そうだ」 to convey hearsay ('I hear that it is possible to participate'), not the speaker's own plans or circumstances in this sentence.
default.q.n3-1-q48-48.why.2: (c) 「出そうだ」 is formed from the stem of the regular verb 「出る」 plus そうだ, meaning “looks as if it is about to appear / come out.” It does not express whether someone may be able to attend school.
default.q.n3-1-q48-48.why.3: (d) 「出るそうだ」 expresses hearsay (“I hear that [someone] will participate”) and is not used when the subject is the speaker themself.
default.q.n3-1-q49-49.verdict: The correct order is: 1 → 4 → 3 → 2. The star ★ (gap 3) is in position 3 (について).
default.q.n3-1-q49-49.explanation:
Complete sentence: 昨日、本屋で小説 2 冊とレポートの書き方についての本を 1 冊買った。
Meaning: Yesterday, I bought two novels and one book about how to write reports at a bookstore.
default.q.n3-1-q49-49.why.0: (a) Choice 1 (と): Placed in the first slot, it follows the quantity expression 「小説 2 冊」and links it to the next noun phrase ("2 novels and...").
default.q.n3-1-q49-49.why.1: (b) Choice 2 (の): In gap 4, it follows 「〜について」 and modifies the noun 「本」 immediately after gap 4, forming 「N1 についての N2」 (a book about...).
default.q.n3-1-q49-49.why.2: (c) Choice 3 (について): It occupies the ★ blank in the third position and follows the noun 「レポートの書き方」 to form the grammar pattern 「〜について」(about a topic / concerning some content).
default.q.n3-1-q49-49.why.3: (d) Choice 4 (レポートの書き方) occupies position 2, follows the particle 「と」 in position 1, and functions as the noun preceding 「について」 in position 3.
default.q.n3-1-q50-50.verdict: Correct order: 3 → 2 → 1 → 4. The ★ position (slot 3) is answer choice 1 (で).
default.q.n3-1-q50-50.explanation:
Complete sentence: A 「あの喫茶店、テレビか何かで見たことがあるよ。入ってみない？」B 「いいね。」
Meaning: A: "I think I’ve seen that café on TV or somewhere. Shall we go in and check it out?" B: "Sounds good."
default.q.n3-1-q50-50.why.0: (a) Choice 1 (で): At the ★ position (slot 3), this particle indicates the means or source through which information is received (“on TV / via TV”). It follows「テレビか何か」and modifies「見た」in slot 4.
default.q.n3-1-q50-50.why.1: (b) Choice 2 (か何か): It occupies the second blank and directly follows the noun 「テレビ」 to express an uncertain guess ("on TV or something similar").
default.q.n3-1-q50-50.why.2: (c) Answer choice 3 (テレビ): It occupies slot 1 and is the noun introducing the adverbial phrase indicating the source of information.
default.q.n3-1-q50-50.why.3: (d) Choice 4 (見たこと): In gap 4, it combines with the following 「がある」 to form the experience pattern 「V-たことがある」 (have done something before).
default.q.n3-1-q51-51.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 1 → 4 → 3. The ★ position (slot 3) is choice 4 (弾けるように).
default.q.n3-1-q51-51.explanation:
Complete sentence: 半年前にギターを習い始めてから、毎日練習している。弾けば弾くほど上手に弾けるようになっていくのが自分でもわかり、とても楽しい。
Meaning: I have practiced every day since I started learning guitar six months ago. I can feel myself getting better the more I play, and it is a lot of fun.
default.q.n3-1-q51-51.why.0: (a) Choice 1 (上手に): It goes in blank 2 and is an adverb that directly modifies the potential-form verb 「弾ける」 in blank 3.
default.q.n3-1-q51-51.why.1: (b) Choice 2 (弾くほど): It occupies the first blank and combines with the conditional form 「弾けば」before it to create the grammar pattern 「V-ば V-るほど」(the more..., the more...).
default.q.n3-1-q51-51.why.2: (c) Choice 3, なっていくのが: It occupies blank 4, following 「〜ように」 to form 「〜ようになっていく」 (“gradually come to become…”). のが nominalizes the entire clause so it can function as the complement of 「自分でもわかり」.
default.q.n3-1-q51-51.why.3: (d) Choice 4 (弾けるように): It occupies the ★ position (the third slot), is modified by「上手に」in slot 2, and combines with「なっていく」in slot 4 according to the pattern「〜ようになる」(to become able to do something).
default.q.n3-1-q52-52.verdict: The correct order is: 4 → 1 → 2 → 3. The ★ position (slot 3) is answer choice 2 (のは).
default.q.n3-1-q52-52.explanation:
Complete passage: 今の会社に就職したときに、北町で一人暮らしを始めた。会社から遠いのに北町を選んだのはずっと北町に住んでみたかったからだ。
Meaning: When I started working for my current company, I began living alone in Kitamachi. I chose Kitamachi even though it was far from the company because I had always wanted to try living there.
default.q.n3-1-q52-52.why.0: (a) Choice 1 (北町を選んだ): It occupies the second slot and follows「〜のに」in slot 1 to form a paradoxical clause: “Although it was far from the company, [they] chose Kitamachi.”
default.q.n3-1-q52-52.why.1: (b) Choice 2 (のは): It occupies the ★ position (the third blank), nominalizing the preceding clause and combining with 「〜からだ」 at the end to form the explanatory/emphatic pattern 「〜のは、...からだ」 (The reason ... is that...).
default.q.n3-1-q52-52.why.2: (c) Choice 3 (ずっと北町に住んでみたかった): It occupies slot 4, states the core reason, and connects directly with 「からだ」at the end of the sentence.
default.q.n3-1-q52-52.why.3: (d) Choice 4 (のに): It occupies slot 1 and follows the -i adjective phrase「会社から遠い」to express contrast or concession (〜のに: although...but).
default.q.n3-1-q53-53.verdict: Correct order: 4 → 2 → 3 → 1. The position marked ★ (gap 3) is choice 3 (ぬれたままにしない).
default.q.n3-1-q53-53.explanation:
Complete sentence: お風呂は家の中でも特にかびが生えやすい場所だ。かびを防ぐためには使った後ぬれたままにしないことが重要なしい。
Translation: The bathroom is the place in the house where mold is especially likely to grow. To prevent mold, it is important not to leave it wet after use.
default.q.n3-1-q53-53.why.0: (a) Choice 1 (ことが): It goes in position 4, following the verb phrase 「ぬれたままにしない」 to nominalize the entire phrase and make it the subject of the predicate 「重要...」 at the end of the sentence.
default.q.n3-1-q53-53.why.1: (b) Choice 2 (使った後): It occupies slot 2 and functions as an adverbial phrase indicating time (“after using it”), modifying the action in slot 3.
default.q.n3-1-q53-53.why.2: (c) Choice 3 (ぬれたままにしない): It occupies position ★ (slot 3) and uses the pattern 「〜ままにする」(leave something in its current state) in the negative form 「〜ままにしない」(not leave it wet).
default.q.n3-1-q53-53.why.3: (d) Choice 4 (ためには): It occupies blank 1 and follows the dictionary-form verb 「防ぐ」 to express purpose (V-る + ためには: “in order to prevent...” ).
default.q.n3-1-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 思っていたからです.
default.q.n3-1-q54-54.explanation: The author previously says: "日本に来たばかりのころ、コンビニに行くとき、コンビニの会社の違いはあまり気にしていませんでした。" (When I had just arrived in Japan, I did not pay much attention to the differences between convenience-store chains when I went to a convenience store.) The next sentence explains the reason for this attitude: at that time, the author thought that even if the companies were different, the products they sold were the same (会社が違っても、売っている商品は同じだと思っていたからです). The structure 「〜ていたから（です）」expresses an ongoing thought in the past and gives the reason for the preceding sentence.
default.q.n3-1-q54-54.why.0: (a) 「思います」 is in the present tense, so it does not fit recounting thoughts and realizations from the past when the speaker had just arrived in Japan.
default.q.n3-1-q54-54.why.1: (b) 「思ってしまいます」 expresses accidentally or involuntarily thinking something, often with a nuance of regret. It does not fit a context explaining the cause of an attitude in the past.
default.q.n3-1-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「思っていたからです」: Correct because the past progressive form 「思っていた」combined with 「から（です）」explains why the author “was not particularly concerned about the differences between the chains” in the preceding sentence.
default.q.n3-1-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「思ったことです」means “it is something I thought,” giving a definition or stating content rather than linking to an explanation of the reason.
default.q.n3-1-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 4. でも.
default.q.n3-1-q55-55.explanation: The preceding sentence states the common point: "Items such as beverages, food, household goods, and magazines are sold in the same way by all companies" (売られているのは同じです). The following sentence presents a unique difference: "Each company's convenience stores have their own desserts, bread, and boxed meals that other companies' convenience stores do not have" (ほかの会社のコンビニにはない...があるのです). The relationship between the two sentences is contrast (the same >< distinctive features), so the contrastive conjunction 「でも」 (but/however) is the correct answer.
default.q.n3-1-q55-55.why.0: (a) 「つまり」means “in other words” or “in summary,” and is used to summarize or rephrase the preceding content. It is inappropriate because the two sentences express a contrast.
default.q.n3-1-q55-55.why.1: (b) 「ところで」 means “by the way” or “incidentally” and is used to shift completely to a new topic, so it does not fit a passage comparing similarities and differences.
default.q.n3-1-q55-55.why.2: (c) 「ちなみに」means “by the way/as an additional note” and is used to add related supplementary information; it does not express contrast between two sentences.
default.q.n3-1-q55-55.why.3: (d) 「でも」: Correct because it is a conjunction meaning “but” or “however,” connecting two contrasting points: the similarities among basic products and the differences in items exclusive to each chain.
default.q.n3-1-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 1. どの.
default.q.n3-1-q56-56.explanation: Earlier, the author says: "会社ごとにおいしいデザートやパンや弁当を考えて、自分たちだけの新しい商品を作っているようです。" (Each company seems to be creating its own new products, such as delicious desserts, bread, and boxed meals.) This describes the efforts of all the companies. In the sentence containing the blank, the particle 「も」 follows the structure 「どの＋noun＋も」, meaning “any... / every...” (どの会社も〜がんばっている: every company seems to be making an effort). Therefore, the interrogative determiner 「どの」 is the correct choice.
default.q.n3-1-q56-56.why.0: (a) 「どの」: Correct because, followed by the particle 「も」, it forms 「どの会社も」, meaning “every company” or “any company,” encompassing all the convenience-store chains.
default.q.n3-1-q56-56.why.1: (b) 「その」: 「その会社」 refers to a specific company mentioned earlier and is unsuitable because the context is discussing the efforts of all companies in general.
default.q.n3-1-q56-56.why.2: (c) 「この」: 「この会社」 means “this company,” located near the speaker, which does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-1-q56-56.why.3: (d) 「あの」: 「あの会社」 means “that company,” known to both the speaker and listener; it is not used to generalize about all companies.
default.q.n3-1-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 場所なのです.
default.q.n3-1-q57-57.explanation: In the preceding sentence, the author begins the conclusion: "私にとってコンビニは買い物をするだけの場所ではありません。" (For me, a convenience store is not merely a place to shop.) The next sentence adds to this and confirms what a convenience store really is: "It is a place where so many delicious foods and new products are displayed, making you feel happy whenever you go there" (行くと楽しい気分になれる場所なのです). The corresponding pair 「〜場所ではありません。...場所なのです」 (not a place for A, but rather a place for B), together with the sentence ending 「〜のです」, is used to assert and clearly express the writer's feelings and conclusion at the end of the passage.
default.q.n3-1-q57-57.why.0: (a) 「場所にしたのです」: The verb 「〜にする」 expresses an intentional action that changes something into a place (“made it into a place…”), so it does not suit the author’s description of a natural impression.
default.q.n3-1-q57-57.why.1: (b) 「場所なのです」: Correct because it combines the negative structure in the previous sentence, 「〜場所ではありません」, with the affirmative structure here, 「〜場所なのです」 (“it is not place A but rather place B”). 「のです」 emphasizes the author’s concluding realization.
default.q.n3-1-q57-57.why.2: (c) 「場所にするのでしょう」 has the nuance of speculating about a future action (“will probably turn it into a place...”), so it does not suit the expression of the speaker's present feelings.
default.q.n3-1-q57-57.why.3: (d) 「場所なのでしょうか」is an interrogative or self-question (“could it be a place...?”), so it does not fit a concluding sentence that states the writer’s firm impression.

default.q.n3-1-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 4: On the day of the event, bring the annual membership fee (年会費) and a drink (飲み物).

What must someone who intends to become a member while attending the outing do?

default.q.n3-1-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the notice clearly states: "希望する方は、当日、年会費（2,000円）を払えば、会員になることができます。その場合、参加費は無料になります" Anyone who wishes to join can pay the annual membership fee on the day, after which the participation fee is waived. Therefore, it is unnecessary to bring the participation fee (参加費).
default.q.n3-1-q59-59.why.3: (d) Correct according to the passage: no advance contact is required (「参加の連絡は不要」); participants must bring their own drinks (「飲み物は持参してください」); those who wish to join can pay the annual membership fee that day (「当日、年会費（2,000円）を払えば、会員になることができます」), in which case participation is free (「その場合、参加費は無料になります」). default.q.n3-1-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Create gradients between stations to reduce the amount of energy consumed by the train.
default.q.n3-1-q61-61.explanation:
Main point summary:
The Tokyo subway was designed to save energy by placing stations in shallow underground locations and digging the track deeper in the sections between stations. Because this creates sloped terrain, trains naturally accelerate downhill just after leaving a station, then slow down and stop more easily while using less energy as they approach the next station.

Translation of the question and answer choices:
- Question: What improvement initiative does the author say the Tokyo subway implemented in this passage?
- Choice 1: Creating slopes between stations to reduce the amount of energy used by the trains.
- Choice 2: Using trains that can run on slopes while consuming little energy.
- Choice 3: Reducing the slopes so that trains can accelerate while using less energy.
- Choice 4: Trying to reduce the number of trains in operation as much as possible to lower energy consumption.
default.q.n3-1-q61-61.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage says: 「東京の地下鉄は、できるだけ、駅を地下の浅いところに作り、駅と駅の間は中心部分が深くなるように掘ってある。これは、少ないエネルギーで電車を走らせるための工夫だ。」 Tokyo’s subway stations are built as close to the surface as possible, while the sections between stations are excavated deeper, creating slopes that help save energy.
default.q.n3-1-q61-61.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage does not mention using trains that can run uphill with little energy (少ないエネルギーで坂を走れる電車を使用する); it presents a solution involving the structure of the tunnel.
default.q.n3-1-q61-61.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage says that slopes were built between the stations, not that the slopes were reduced (坂を減らして).
default.q.n3-1-q61-61.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage states 「東京では、毎日数多くの電車が走るので」 (“because many trains run in Tokyo every day”), not that the number of trains in operation is reduced as much as possible (走る電車の数をできるだけ少なくして).

default.q.n3-1-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The author finds it interesting that although the finished product is different each time, investigating the causes and gradually making improvements brings great enjoyment.
default.q.n3-1-q68-68.explanation:
• Main point: The author explains that the joy of baking bread lies in the process itself. Because temperature and humidity vary, the results differ each time and failures sometimes occur; however, the time spent thinking about the causes, experimenting, and improving the recipe is what the author finds extremely enjoyable.

• Question translation: Why does the author find baking bread enjoyable?
• Answer choices:
1. Because if the same ingredients are always used, anyone can bake delicious bread without failing.
2. Because although the finished product differs each time, thinking about the reasons and experimenting with improvements is still enjoyable.
3. Because it is possible to make bread that is more perfect and attractive than bread sold in stores.
4. Because the dough can be fermented easily in a short time and eaten immediately.
default.q.n3-1-q68-68.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage clearly states that even with the same formula, the volume of the batter changes depending on temperature and humidity, and sometimes the result still fails; it is not easy for everyone to bake successfully.
default.q.n3-1-q68-68.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct. The second paragraph states: 「思い通りにいかずに失敗することもあるが、どうしてうまくいかなかったのかを考え、工夫を重ねていく時間がとても楽しいのだ。」 (There are times when things do not go as planned and we fail, but the time spent thinking about why things did not work and making repeated improvements is very enjoyable).
default.q.n3-1-q68-68.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the author admits that the cakes they make may be 「多少形が不格好であっても」 (“even if their shape is somewhat awkward”), rather than saying they make them more beautiful and perfect than store-bought cakes.
default.q.n3-1-q68-68.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because paragraph 2 emphasizes 「時間をかけてじっくり発酵させることだ」 (taking time to ferment the dough thoroughly), which is the opposite of fermenting it quickly so it can be eaten immediately.
default.q.n3-1-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The author says that concentrating on kneading dough relieves stress and that freshly baked bread has a particularly delicious flavor.
default.q.n3-1-q69-69.explanation:
• Main point: The passage highlights two benefits baking brings the author: concentrating on kneading dough by hand is a wonderful opportunity to forget the fatigue and stress of work and refresh the mind, while a cake baked by oneself has a uniquely delicious flavor that store-bought cakes cannot match.

• Question translation: What did the author say about baking bread?
• Answer choices:
1. At first, the author’s goal was to eat delicious bread, but after failing every time, they became exhausted.
2. To avoid failure, the author plans never to try making new kinds of bread again.
3. Concentrating helps relieve stress and refresh the mind, and bread made by oneself has a uniquely delicious flavor.
4. Since poorly shaped bread does not taste good, the author feels that store-bought bread is still superior.
default.q.n3-1-q69-69.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the author is completely absorbed in baking and sees it as an opportunity to dispel fatigue, not as something that causes exhaustion through constant failure.
default.q.n3-1-q69-69.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because in the final sentence the author states: 「これからも新しいレシピに挑戦しながら、パン作りを長く楽しんでいきたい。」 (From now on, I would like to continue enjoying breadmaking for a long time while trying new recipes.)
default.q.n3-1-q69-69.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct. The passage states: 「手で生地をこねている間は余計なことを考えずに集中できるため、仕事の疲れやストレスを忘れる良い機会にもなっている」 (Kneading the dough provides an opportunity to concentrate without thinking about unnecessary things and forget the fatigue and stress of work) and 「自分で焼き上げたパンは、多少形が不格好であっても、店で買ったものにはない格別な味わいがある」 (Bread baked by oneself has a special flavor that store-bought bread does not, even if its shape is somewhat unattractive).
default.q.n3-1-q69-69.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the author says that even if the appearance is somewhat clumsy, homemade cake has a uniquely delicious flavor compared with cake bought at a shop. The author does not say that unattractive cake tastes bad.

default.q.n3-1-q1-1.explanation: Meaning: This is a photograph of a Western-style building. / Sino-Japanese roots: 西 (west) + 洋 (ocean) = 西洋 (the West, Western world). / Example: 西洋の文化に興味があります。(I am interested in Western culture.)
default.q.n3-1-q1-1.why.0: (a) せよう: Incorrect because 西 in this word is read 「せい」, combined with 洋 read as 「よう」; 「せ」 is an incorrect shortened reading.
default.q.n3-1-q1-1.why.1: (b) せいゆう: Incorrect because 「洋」 has the long vowel 「よう」, not 「ゆう」.

default.q.n3-1-q1-1.why.3: (d) せゆう: Incorrect because both kanji require long vowels: 「西」 is correctly read せい and 「洋」 is correctly read よう.

default.q.n3-1-q3-3.why.0: (a) たんじん: incorrect because 「他」is not read as 「たん」, and 「人」is read as 「にん」here, not 「じん」.

default.q.n3-1-q5-5.explanation:

default.q.n3-1-q5-5.why.0: (a) しゅうでん: Incorrect because 「点」 is read 「てん」 and does not undergo voicing; 「しゅうでん」 is the word 「終電」 (the last train of the day).

default.q.n3-1-q5-5.why.3: (d) じゅうてん: Incorrect because 「終」 is not read 「じゅう」; it is easily confused with 「重点」: じゅうてん - the main point.

Meaning: There are many apartment buildings around here.
Sino-Japanese roots: 辺 (beside, surrounding area).

default.q.n3-1-q9-9.why.1: (b) 「辺り」(on-reading association: BIEN) is read 「あたり」and means “the surrounding area” or “around here,” fitting the context 「このあたり」(this area).
default.q.n3-1-q9-9.why.2: (c) 「返り」 is read as 「かえり」 (return, coming back), not 「あたり」.
default.q.n3-1-q9-9.why.3: (d) 「廻り」 is read as 「まわり」 (around, surrounding), not 「あたり」.

Sentence meaning: Please look at the following diagram.
Kanji: 図 (ず／と): map, diagram, or figure. Its on-readings are 「ズ」 (as in 図 and 地図 - ちず) and 「ト」 (as in 図書館 - としょかん).

default.q.n3-1-q10-10.why.1: (b) 「図」 is read as 「ず」 and means “drawing,” “diagram,” or “illustration,” which matches the 「ず」 in the question.
default.q.n3-1-q10-10.why.2: (c) 「表」 is read 「ひょう」 (table/chart) or 「おもて」 (front/outward appearance), not 「ず」.

Meaning: My savings have decreased a little.
Kanji reading: 減 (げん — decrease, diminish).
Example: 体重が2キロ減りました。 (I lost 2 kilograms.)
default.q.n3-1-q11-11.why.0: (a) 「細りました」 is from the verb 「細る」, read as 「ほそりました」 (to become thinner, waste away), not 「へりました」.
default.q.n3-1-q11-11.why.1: (b) 「低りました」 is not a valid Japanese word or conjugation; the kanji 低 is normally used in the i-adjective 「低い」(ひくい).
default.q.n3-1-q11-11.why.2: (c) 「消りました」 does not exist in Japanese; 消 is used in 「消える」 (きえる) or 「消す」 (けす).
default.q.n3-1-q11-11.why.3: (d) 「減りました」 comes from the verb 「減る」 (read 「へりました」), meaning “decrease” or “be reduced,” which is completely appropriate for savings that have declined.

Meaning of the sentence: I hear that a pedestrian path/sidewalk will be built here next year.
Kanji: 歩 (walk), 道 (road) → 歩道 (pedestrian path, sidewalk). Related word: 車道 (しゃどう: roadway for vehicles).

default.q.n3-1-q12-12.why.0: (a) 「歩動」 combines the kanji incorrectly. 「動」 means movement and does not form a word meaning a walking route.

default.q.n3-1-q12-12.why.2: (c) 「歩道」(on-reading association: BŌDŌ) is formed from 「歩」(ほ – walking) and 「道」(どう – road), read 「ほどう」, and means “sidewalk” or “pedestrian path.”
default.q.n3-1-q12-12.why.3: (d) 「走動」 is an incorrect kanji compound combining 走 (to run) and 動 (to move); it does not mean sidewalk.

Meaning: The sound of a computer keyboard being struck can be heard.
Kanji reading: 打 (to strike, hit, type).

default.q.n3-1-q14-14.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 性格.
default.q.n3-1-q14-14.explanation:
Meaning: Mr./Ms. Yamada has a very serious and upright personality.
Kanji compound: 性 (character, nature) + 格 (character, standards) → 性格 (personality). Distinguish it from 姓名 (せいめい: full name) and 正確 (せいかく: accurate).

default.q.n3-1-q14-14.why.0: (a) 「姓格」 uses the wrong kanji; 「姓」 means a surname and is not used in the word for personality.
default.q.n3-1-q14-14.why.1: (b) 「性名」 is an incorrect kanji compound; the correct term for one's family and given names is 「姓名」 - せいめい.
default.q.n3-1-q14-14.why.2: (c) 「性格」 is read as 「せいかく」 and means “personality, character.” It fits the context perfectly in 「まじめな性格」 (“a serious, upright personality”).
default.q.n3-1-q14-14.why.3: (d) 「姓名」 (surname and given name) is read 「せいめい」 and means “full name,” not 「せいかく」.
default.q.n3-1-q15-15.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 時差 (time difference).
default.q.n3-1-q15-15.explanation:
Meaning: “There is a 12-hour time difference between my country and Japan, so day and night are reversed.”
Related vocabulary:
- 時差: time difference.
- 時代: era, generation.
- 時期: period, time.
- 時速: speed per hour.
Example: 外国に行くと、時差ボケで眠れなくなることがある。(When I go abroad, I sometimes cannot sleep because of jet lag.)
default.q.n3-1-q15-15.why.0: (a) 「時代」(じだい) means a historical era or generation; it is not used to indicate the time difference between two places.
default.q.n3-1-q15-15.why.1: (b) 「時期」(じき) means a period, stage, or time for carrying out an activity, so it does not fit the context of a 12-hour time difference.
default.q.n3-1-q15-15.why.2: (c) 「時速」(じそく) means the speed traveled per hour (e.g., 時速60キロ); it is not used to describe the time difference between countries.
default.q.n3-1-q15-15.why.3: (d) 「時差」(じさ - time difference): the difference between time zones. 「時差が12時間ある」 means that the time difference is 12 hours, which fits perfectly with the following statement that day and night are reversed.
default.q.n3-1-q16-16.verdict: The correct answer is 3. しかたない (there is no other choice).
default.q.n3-1-q16-16.explanation:
Meaning: “My bicycle broke down, so I had no choice but to walk home.”
Related vocabulary:
- しかたない (仕方ない): there is no other way, it cannot be helped.
- 詳しい (くわしい): detailed, knowledgeable.
- だらしない: sloppy, untidy, undisciplined.
- 羨ましい (うらやましい): envious, jealous, admiring.
Example: 雨が降ってきたが、傘がないので濡れて帰るしかない。(It started raining, but since I don’t have an umbrella, I have no choice but to walk home soaked.)
default.q.n3-1-q16-16.why.0: (a) 「くわしい」(詳しい): thorough, detailed, well-informed about something; it is not used for an unavoidable situation.
default.q.n3-1-q16-16.why.1: (b) 「だらしない」 means sloppy, untidy, or careless. It describes a person's character or conduct, not an unavoidable cause.
default.q.n3-1-q16-16.why.2: (c) 「しかたない」(仕方ない) means "there is no other way" or "it cannot be helped." Combined with 「～ので」, it expresses that because the car broke down and there was no alternative, the person had to walk home.
default.q.n3-1-q16-16.why.3: (d) 「うらやましい」(羨ましい): to envy someone, to wish to be like someone else; it does not fit the context at all.
default.q.n3-1-q17-17.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 決心 (determination, decision).
default.q.n3-1-q17-17.explanation:
Meaning: "Because I wanted to cure people's illnesses, I decided in high school to become a doctor."
Related vocabulary:
- 決心: to make up one's mind, resolve; expressions include 決心する and 決心が固い.
- 予想: prediction or prognosis.
- 証明: proof or verification.
- 仮定: assumption or hypothesis.
Example: 彼は日本へ留学することを決心した。(He decided to study abroad in Japan.)
default.q.n3-1-q17-17.why.0: (a) 「予想」(よそう): predicting what will happen based on available information; it is not used with 「～になることを予想する」 when referring to one's own will or dreams.
default.q.n3-1-q17-17.why.1: (b) 「決心」(けっしん - determination): To resolve to do something; the structure 「～になることを決心する」 expresses resolving to become someone, which fits the context of wanting to cure illnesses and save people.
default.q.n3-1-q17-17.why.2: (c) 「証明」(しょうめい — proof, demonstration): to clarify or prove the validity of something; it is not used for a personal decision.
default.q.n3-1-q17-17.why.3: (d) 「仮定」(かてい): setting up a supposition or assuming something that has not happened; it does not mean the will to pursue a career.
default.q.n3-1-q18-18.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 冗談 (a joke, joking).
default.q.n3-1-q18-18.explanation:
Meaning: "He is an interesting person who is always joking and making everyone laugh."
Related vocabulary and kanji compounds:
- 冗談: joke; joking remark (冗談を言う: to tell a joke; to joke).
- 感想: impressions; thoughts after an experience.
- 文句: complaint; grumbling (文句を言う: to complain).
- 自慢: boasting; pride in oneself.
Example: 冗談はさておき、本題に入りましょう。(Joking aside, let's get to the main topic.)
default.q.n3-1-q18-18.why.0: (a) 「感想」(かんそう - personal impressions): thoughts and impressions (as in 感想を言う), not something humorous or amusing.
default.q.n3-1-q18-18.why.1: (b) 「文句」(もんく: complaint, grumbling; as in 文句を言う) has a negative nuance and annoys other people; it does not make them laugh.
default.q.n3-1-q18-18.why.2: (c) 「冗談」(じょうだん): a joke; 「冗談を言う」 naturally combines with the following clause 「みんなを笑わせる」 (“make everyone laugh”).
default.q.n3-1-q18-18.why.3: (d) 「自慢」(じまん - boasting, conceit): to boast or be conceited (as in 自慢を言う/する), not to say something jokingly or humorously.
default.q.n3-1-q19-19.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 預けて (to leave something in someone's care).
default.q.n3-1-q19-19.explanation:
Meaning: "I went to the hotel, but since I still couldn’t enter my room, I left my luggage at the front desk and went out."
Related vocabulary:
- 預ける: to leave or entrust an object or money with someone for safekeeping (distinguish it from 預かる, to look after or keep something for someone).
- 泊める: to let someone stay overnight (the object is a person).
- 配る: to distribute, hand out to several people.
- 与える: to give, cause (an influence or harm).
Example: 貴重品はホテルのフロントに預けてください。(Please leave your valuables at the hotel front desk.)
default.q.n3-1-q19-19.why.0: (a) 「預けて」 (あずけて - 預ける): means “to leave something in someone’s care.” 「受付に荷物を預ける」 means “to leave one’s luggage at the reception desk,” which fits the context of arriving before hotel check-in time.
default.q.n3-1-q19-19.why.1: (b) 「泊めて」 (とめて - 泊める): Let someone stay or spend the night; the object must be a person, not luggage (荷物).
default.q.n3-1-q19-19.why.2: (c) 「配って」(くばって - 配る): means to distribute materials, flyers, or gifts to multiple people, and is not used for sending luggage to a single destination.
default.q.n3-1-q19-19.why.3: (d) 「与えて」(あたえて, 与える): to give or bring about an opportunity or influence; it is not used to express sending luggage.
default.q.n3-1-q20-20.verdict: The correct answer is 2. アナウンス (an announcement over a loudspeaker or public-address system).
default.q.n3-1-q20-20.explanation:
Meaning: “When I arrived at the airport, I heard an announcement over the public-address system that the flight had been delayed.”
Related vocabulary:
- アナウンス (announcement): an announcement made over a public-address system.
- ガイダンス (guidance): an orientation session or instructional material.
- コマーシャル (commercial / CM): a commercial broadcast on television or radio.
- スピーチ (speech): a speech or formal address delivered before an audience.
Example: 駅のアナウンスで電車の遅れを知った。(I learned that the train was delayed from an announcement at the station.)
default.q.n3-1-q20-20.why.0: (a) 「ガイダンス」 (guidance): instruction or an orientation session for students or new employees. It is not used for announcing a delayed flight at an airport.
default.q.n3-1-q20-20.why.1: (b) 「アナウンス」(announcement) means a public-address announcement at places such as airports and train stations. 「飛行機の出発が遅れるというアナウンスが聞こえた」 is therefore the most accurate expression.
default.q.n3-1-q20-20.why.2: (c) 「コマーシャル」(commercial) means an advertisement on the radio or television and is unrelated to announcing a flight's status.
default.q.n3-1-q20-20.why.3: (d) 「スピーチ」 (speech): a speech or address at an event or conference; it is not used for an airport public-address system.
default.q.n3-1-q21-21.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 案外 (unexpectedly, contrary to expectations).
default.q.n3-1-q21-21.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: "I thought the roads would be congested on a day off, but they were unexpectedly quiet."
Related Sino-Japanese vocabulary:
- 案外 (あんがい): unexpectedly, contrary to expectations (= 意外に/予想外に).
- 突然 (とつぜん): suddenly, unexpectedly.
- 当然 (とうぜん): naturally, of course.
- 年中 (ねんじゅう): all year round, constantly.
Example: この料理は難しそうに見えるが、作ってみると案外簡単だ。(This dish looks difficult, but it is surprisingly easy when you actually try making it.)
default.q.n3-1-q21-21.why.0: (a) 「突然」(とつぜん; sudden): Describes something happening unexpectedly and abruptly in a moment; it is not used to contrast a state with a previous thought or prediction.
default.q.n3-1-q21-21.why.1: (b) 「当然」 (とうぜん - “of course,” “naturally”) directly conflicts with the contrastive conjunction 「～と思いましたが」 (“I thought..., but...” ).
default.q.n3-1-q21-21.why.2: (c) 「年中」(ねんじゅう): Means “all year round” or “constantly,” describing an ongoing habit or condition, and is not used for road conditions on one specific day off.
default.q.n3-1-q21-21.why.3: (d) 「案外」(あんがい): unexpectedly, contrary to expectations. It combines with the preceding clause to create a contrast: one expects a traffic jam, but the roads are unexpectedly quiet.
default.q.n3-1-q22-22.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 努力 (effort / hard work).
default.q.n3-1-q22-22.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "He faced many hardships in his youth, but through wholehearted effort he became an outstanding politician."
Related Sino-Japanese vocabulary:
- 努力: effort, hard work (expressions: 一生懸命努力する / 努力を重ねる).
- 納得: understand fully, agree, be convinced (expression: 納得がいく).
- 期待: expectations, anticipation of someone or the future.
- 注意: attention, caution, a reminder/warning.
Example: 夢を叶えるために、毎日努力しています。(I work hard every day to make my dream come true.)
default.q.n3-1-q22-22.why.0: (a) 「努力」(どりょく – effort): effort or endeavor; the phrase 「一生懸命努力する」describes making one's utmost effort to overcome difficulties and succeed, so it is completely correct.
default.q.n3-1-q22-22.why.1: (b) 「納得」(なっとく): understanding and accepting a reason or viewpoint; it does not describe working hard to build a career.
default.q.n3-1-q22-22.why.2: (c) 「期待」(きたい) means expectation or anticipation directed toward another person or object; it does not mean self-discipline or making an effort.
default.q.n3-1-q22-22.why.3: (d) 「注意」(ちゅうい — attention, warning): It means paying attention or warning someone and does not express overcoming difficulties and becoming successful.
default.q.n3-1-q23-23.verdict: The correct answer is 3. べこべこ (extremely hungry, famished).
default.q.n3-1-q23-23.explanation:
Meaning: “I had no time, so I could not eat either breakfast or lunch, and now my stomach is rumbling with hunger.”
Onomatopoeia:
- おなかがべこべこ (or ぺこぺこ): to be very hungry, to have a rumbling stomach.
- のどがからから: to have a completely dry throat.
- べらべら: to talk rapidly and fluently, or to blab confidential information.
- どきどき: to feel nervous, or for one’s heart to pound.
Example: 朝から何も食べていないので、おなかがぺこぺこだ。(I have not eaten anything since this morning, so I am starving.)
default.q.n3-1-q23-23.why.0: (a) 「べらべら」 describes speaking fluently or talking too much and letting secrets slip; it has nothing to do with being hungry.
default.q.n3-1-q23-23.why.1: (b) 「からから」: parched, extremely dry; it is commonly used with the throat when thirsty, as in 「のどがからから」, not with an empty stomach.
default.q.n3-1-q23-23.why.2: (c) 「べこべこ」: extremely hungry, ravenous (a sound variant of ぺこぺこ; it can also mean dented or badly deformed). It fits the context of not having eaten all day.
default.q.n3-1-q23-23.why.3: (d) 「どきどき」: a pounding heartbeat caused by nervousness, tension, anxiety, or excitement; it is not used for hunger.
default.q.n3-1-q24-24.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 確実 (certain, reliable).
default.q.n3-1-q24-24.explanation:
Meaning: "I heard directly from Mr. Hayashi himself that he is leaving his job, so this is definite and reliable information."
Related Sino-Japanese compounds:
- 確実: certain, reliable, trustworthy (expressions: 確実な情報 / 確実な証拠).
- 満足: satisfaction, contentment (a person's emotional state).
- 正常: normal, functioning properly, healthy (antonym: 異常).
- 完全: complete, perfect, without flaws.
Example: その情報は確実ですか。(Is that information reliable/certain?)
default.q.n3-1-q24-24.why.0: (a) 「満足」(まんぞく): satisfaction; describes a person's emotional state and is not used as an adjective modifying information (情報).
default.q.n3-1-q24-24.why.1: (b) 「正常」(せいじょう - normal): functioning normally without defects, used for machines or bodily functions; it does not collocate with 「情報」 in this context.
default.q.n3-1-q24-24.why.2: (c) 「完全」(かんぜん - COMPLETE): whole and without defects (e.g., 完全な勝利); it is not used to indicate the reliability of information one has heard.
default.q.n3-1-q24-24.why.3: (d) 「確実」(かくじつ): certain, reliable, accurate. The phrase 「確実な情報」 fits perfectly because it was heard directly from someone involved, 林さんから直接聞いた.
default.q.n3-1-q25-25.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 取り付けて (install, attach).
default.q.n3-1-q25-25.explanation:
Meaning: “The electrician came and installed an air conditioner on the wall for me.”
Related compound verbs:
- 取り付ける: install or attach equipment or a machine in a fixed location.
- 取り上げる: pick up; confiscate; bring up for discussion.
- 受け入れる: accept, receive, or admit (an opinion, refugees, international students, etc.).
- 引き受ける: undertake or take responsibility for (work or a responsibility).
Example: ドアに新しい鍵を取り付けた。(I installed a new lock on the door.)
default.q.n3-1-q25-25.why.0: (a) 「取り付けて」 (とりつけて - 取り付ける): to install a device or machine by attaching it securely to something. 「壁にエアコンを取り付ける」 means "to install an air conditioner on the wall," and is completely correct.
default.q.n3-1-q25-25.why.1: (b) 「取り上げて」(とりあげて - / 取り上げる): pick up, confiscate an object, or bring up a topic for discussion; it is not used for installing machinery.
default.q.n3-1-q25-25.why.2: (c) 「受け入れて」(うけいれて, from 受け入れる): to accept or receive (international students, opinions, reality, etc.). It does not mean physically attaching something to a wall.
default.q.n3-1-q25-25.why.3: (d) 「引き受けて」(ひきうけて - 引き受ける): It means to undertake or take responsibility for a task. It does not combine with a specific location in 「壁にエアコンを～」.
default.q.n3-1-q26-26.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (きれいな).
default.q.n3-1-q26-26.explanation:
Translation: "Please wipe it with a clean cloth."
・清潔 means clean, hygienic, or spotless.
・Another example: いつも部屋を清潔に保つ。(I always keep the room clean.)
default.q.n3-1-q26-26.why.0: (a) 柔らかい (やわらかい) means “soft,” so it is not synonymous with 清潔な (clean, hygienic).
default.q.n3-1-q26-26.why.1: (b) ぬれた (濡れた) means “wet,” so it is not synonymous with 清潔な.
default.q.n3-1-q26-26.why.2: (c) 乾いた (かわいた) means “dry,” not “clean.”
default.q.n3-1-q26-26.why.3: (d) きれいな means “clean” or “spotless” and is a complete synonym of 清潔な (clean, hygienic).
default.q.n3-1-q27-27.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (少し前に).
default.q.n3-1-q27-27.explanation:
Sentence translation: “I already ate a little while ago.”
・さっき: just now, a little while ago; casual spoken language, synonymous with 少し前に; the more polite/formal form is 先ほど.
・Another example: さっき電話があったよ。(There was a phone call a little while ago.)
default.q.n3-1-q27-27.why.0: (a) 急いで (いそいで) means “hurriedly” or “in a rush”; it does not express a recently occurring time point.
default.q.n3-1-q27-27.why.1: (b) 少し遅れて (すこしおくれて) means “a little late,” so it is incorrect.
default.q.n3-1-q27-27.why.2: (c) 少し前に (すこしまえに) means “a little while ago” or “just now,” and is synonymous with さっき.
default.q.n3-1-q27-27.why.3: (d) ゆっくり means leisurely or slowly, describing a state or speed rather than a point in time.
default.q.n3-1-q28-28.explanation:
Sentence: «Please put this in the kitchen.»
・キッチン (kitchen, an English loanword): kitchen; synonymous with the native Japanese word 台所 (だいどころ).
・Another example: 台所に新しい冷蔵庫を置いた。(I put a new refrigerator in the kitchen.)
default.q.n3-1-q28-28.why.0: (a) 居間 (いま—living room, common room) does not mean kitchen.
default.q.n3-1-q28-28.why.1: (b) 台所 (だいどころ) means “kitchen” and is the native Japanese equivalent of the loanword キッチン.
default.q.n3-1-q28-28.why.2: (c) 廊下 (ろうか) means corridor or hallway, so it is incorrect here.
default.q.n3-1-q28-28.why.3: (d) 風呂 (ふろ) / お風呂 means “bathtub” or “bathroom,” so it is incorrect.
default.q.n3-1-q29-29.explanation:
Meaning: “Mr./Ms. Noguchi is giving guidance now.”
・指導 (しどう): guidance, instruction, or direction (similar to 教える).
・Another example: 先生が熱心に指導してくれた。(The teacher instructed me enthusiastically.)
default.q.n3-1-q29-29.why.0: (a) 調べて (しらべて) means “look up, investigate, or find out,” and is not synonymous with 指導.
default.q.n3-1-q29-29.why.1: (b) 答えて (こたえて) means “answer” or “respond,” not “give instructions” or “provide guidance.”
default.q.n3-1-q29-29.why.2: (c) 聞いて (きいて) means “listen” or “ask,” so it is not equivalent.
default.q.n3-1-q29-29.why.3: (d) 教えて (おしえて) means “to teach,” “instruct,” or “guide,” and is synonymous with 指導しています (“is instructing/guiding”).
default.q.n3-1-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (終わりにしましょう).
default.q.n3-1-q30-30.explanation:
Translation: «Let's get ready to finish up.»
・おしまい (お終い: the end, completion, being finished; synonymous with 終わり (おわり)).
・Another example: 今日の仕事はこれでおしまい。(That's all for today's work.)
default.q.n3-1-q30-30.why.0: (a) 休みましょう means “let’s take a break,” not “let’s finish the work we are doing.”
default.q.n3-1-q30-30.why.1: (b) 食事にしましょう means “let’s have a meal / let’s eat,” so the meaning is incorrect.
default.q.n3-1-q30-30.why.2: (c) 終わりにしましょう means “let's finish/stop,” and is completely synonymous with おしまいにしましょう.
default.q.n3-1-q30-30.why.3: (d) 寝ましょう means “Let’s go to sleep,” narrowing the meaning to sleeping rather than bringing something to a general end.
default.q.n3-1-q31-31.explanation:
「握る」（にぎる）means to grasp or hold something tightly in the palm (used for hands, steering wheels, microphones, sushi, etc.). Figuratively, it can mean to hold or possess power, evidence, someone's weakness, and so on.
Example: 彼女は緊張してハンカチをぎゅっと握りしめた。(She nervously clutched her handkerchief tightly.)
default.q.n3-1-q31-31.why.0: When moving heavy furniture, use a verb meaning to carry or lift, such as 「運んだ」 or 「持った」; 「にぎった」 is not appropriate.
default.q.n3-1-q31-31.why.1: 「手を握る」 is the standard collocation for expressing the action of gripping someone’s hand tightly—in this case, the younger brother’s hand to avoid getting separated.
default.q.n3-1-q31-31.why.2: When chasing after a hat blown away by the wind to catch it, use 「つかまえてくれた」 (“caught it”) or 「拾ってくれた」 (“picked it up for me”), not 「にぎってくれた」.
default.q.n3-1-q31-31.why.3: For carefully holding or carrying a newborn baby, use 「抱いている」（だいている）or 「抱っこしている」, not 「にぎっている」, which can suggest gripping or squeezing tightly.
default.q.n3-1-q32-32.explanation:
「修理」（しゅうり）means repairing objects, machines, vehicles, or mechanical/electronic equipment that has been damaged or malfunctioning so that it can operate normally again.
Example: パソコンが動かなくなったので、メーカーに修理を依頼した。(My computer stopped working, so I asked the manufacturer to repair it.)
default.q.n3-1-q32-32.why.0: To make up and repair a relationship between people, such as a married couple, use 「仲直り（したい）」 or 「修復（したい）」, not 「修理」.
default.q.n3-1-q32-32.why.1: Treating a bodily injury (such as an arm injury) at a hospital requires 「治療（ちりょう）」 or 「手当て（てあて）」; 「修理」 is used only for objects or machines.
default.q.n3-1-q32-32.why.2: 「修理」is the correct word for repairing damaged mechanical devices or vehicles, such as a bicycle (「自転車を修理する」).
default.q.n3-1-q32-32.why.3: To correct misspelled writing in red ink, use 「直してくれた」or「訂正（ていせい）してくれた」, not「修理」.
default.q.n3-1-q33-33.explanation:
「目的」（もくてき） is the aim or purpose one has when carrying out an action or undertaking something; it answers the question “What is it for?” It differs from 「目標」, a specific measurable target, and 「予定」, a plan or schedule.
Example: 日本へ来た目的は、大学で建築を学ぶためです。(The purpose of coming to Japan is to study architecture at a university.)
default.q.n3-1-q33-33.why.0: A specific amount of money or sales target to be reached (100,000 yen) requires 「目標」(もくひょう, a measurable target), not 「目的」.
default.q.n3-1-q33-33.why.1: A personal request or preference when making a reservation, such as choosing a seat near the window, should use 「希望」（きぼう） or 「要望」, not 「目的」.
default.q.n3-1-q33-33.why.2: A predetermined plan or business-trip schedule should be expressed with 「予定」(よてい), as in 「出張する予定なので」, not 「目的なので」.
default.q.n3-1-q33-33.why.3: 「目的」 correctly fits the structure 「〜の目的は…ことです」, which states the purpose or objective of a research topic.
default.q.n3-1-q34-34.explanation:
「懐かしい」（なつかしい） is an i-adjective expressing a nostalgic, fond feeling when something brings back memories or experiences from the past that the speaker personally experienced.
Example: 故郷の歌を聞くと、昔のことが思い出されて懐かしい。(When I hear a song from my hometown, it brings back memories of the past and makes me feel nostalgic.)
default.q.n3-1-q34-34.why.0: 「懐かしい気持ち」is a natural expression for the nostalgic feelings experienced when recalling one’s own fond memories from the past, such as when looking at childhood photos.
default.q.n3-1-q34-34.why.1: A temple built 800 years ago expresses long-standing historical value, so 「歴史のある」 or 「古い」 should be used. 「懐かしい」 is not appropriate because it is used for memories the speaker personally experienced.
default.q.n3-1-q34-34.why.2: For a long-standing, close marital relationship, use 「親しい関係」 or 「深い関係」, not 「懐かしい関係」.
default.q.n3-1-q34-34.why.3: To describe becoming close and getting along immediately after meeting, use 「親しい友達」 or 「仲の良い友達」. Do not use 「懐かしい」 because they have no shared memories from the past.
default.q.n3-1-q35-35.explanation:
「変化」（へんか）is a noun and a Group 3 verb referring to a change in state, appearance, or qualities over time. It is commonly used for everyday life, climate, eras, and psychological states. It differs from 「変更」(a deliberate change to a schedule or rule) and 「交代」(taking turns or replacing a person).
Example: 季節の変わり目は、気温の変化が激しい。(Around the change of seasons, temperature changes are extreme.)
default.q.n3-1-q35-35.why.0: When a meal appointment is moved to another time due to rescheduling, use 「変更になった」 or 「延期になった」, not 「変化した」.
default.q.n3-1-q35-35.why.1: After moving, an address should be described with 「変わった」 or 「（住所の）変更」, not 「変化した」.
default.q.n3-1-q35-35.why.2: 「変化」 is exactly appropriate for describing the major changes in the appearance, nature, and methods of social life caused by the Internet (「生活が大きく変化する」).
default.q.n3-1-q35-35.why.3: Changing the person responsible for a position or role, such as hosting a program, requires 「交代する」 or 「変更になる」, not 「変化する」.
default.q.n3-10-q36-36.explanation:
Sentence translation: I wore the kimono my parents bought for me to attend my university graduation ceremony.
• In addition to indicating the location, means, or method of an action, the particle で can also indicate the clothing worn or the state a person is in while performing an action (Example: スーツで面接に行く – go to an interview in a suit).
• On'yomi-based kanji associations: 両親 (parents), 着物 (kimono/clothing), 卒業式 (graduation ceremony), 出席 (attendance).
default.q.n3-10-q36-36.why.0: (a) 「を」 marks a direct object affected by the action, so it is not appropriate here because the predicate is 「出席した」, which takes the particle に: 卒業式に出席した.
default.q.n3-10-q36-36.why.1: (b) 「が」 marks the subject of a sentence, so it is inappropriate here because the person carrying out the action of attending the graduation ceremony is the speaker (“I”).
default.q.n3-10-q36-36.why.2: (c) 「で」 indicates clothing or the state in which an action is performed—in this case, wearing a kimono to attend the graduation ceremony.
default.q.n3-10-q36-36.why.3: (d) 「に」 indicates a destination, time, or target, and does not follow a clothing noun to modify the action 出席した.
default.q.n3-10-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 4. いつのまにか.
default.q.n3-10-q37-37.explanation:
Sentence translation: While I was absorbed in reading, five whole hours had passed before I knew it.
• いつの間にか (before one knows it) describes something that has happened or time that has passed outside the speaker’s expectations without the speaker noticing.
• Kanji: 経つ (tatsu: for time to pass).

The conjunction「ただ」(however, the thing is) adds a caveat, limitation, or exception to the preceding statement, matching this gentle shift in topic.
