default.q.n3-10-q15-15.explanation:
Meaning: Because of the typhoon, it was decided that the marathon event would be postponed.
- Kanji: 延期 means postponement, 台風 means typhoon, and 大会 means event or tournament.
- Example: 雨のため、試合は明日に延期された。(Because of the rain, the match was postponed until tomorrow.)
default.q.n3-10-q15-15.why.0: (a) 遅刻 (ちこく) means arriving late or being late, used for students or employees, not for events.
default.q.n3-10-q15-15.why.1: (b) 運休 (うんきゅう) means a temporary suspension of service or cancellation of a run (for trains, buses, airplanes, etc.); it is not used for a sporting event.
default.q.n3-10-q15-15.why.2: (c) 延期 (えんき): postponement, rescheduling for a later time. Combined with 「される」 as 「延期される」 (“be postponed”), it fits the context of the marathon being postponed because of a typhoon.
default.q.n3-10-q15-15.why.3: (d) 早退 (そうたい): leaving early, before the end of school or work; it is not used for an event.
default.q.n3-10-q16-16.verdict: The correct answer is 4. かれて (枯れる – wither, dry up).
default.q.n3-10-q16-16.explanation:
Meaning: If you do not water the flowers every day, they will wither.
- Sino-Japanese note: 枯 (か: to wither, dry up).
- Expression: 水をやる (to water plants / give food or drink to a pet).
- Example: 水やりを忘れて、観葉植物が枯れてしまった。(I forgot to water it, so the houseplant withered.)
default.q.n3-10-q16-16.why.0: (a) とめて (止める/留める/泊める): to stop, park, retain, or provide lodging; it is not used for flowers or plants.
default.q.n3-10-q16-16.why.1: (b) きめて (決める): to decide, choose; it does not fit the meaning of the sentence.
default.q.n3-10-q16-16.why.2: (c) やせて (痩せる): to become thin, lose weight (for people or animals), or become barren (of land); it is not used for flowers wilting from lack of water.
default.q.n3-10-q16-16.why.3: (d) かれて (枯れる): to wither, fade, or die from drying out, used for plants and flowers. 「花が枯れてしまう」(the flowers end up withering) is natural and accurate.
default.q.n3-10-q17-17.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 訓練 (くんれん - training, practice).
default.q.n3-10-q17-17.explanation:
Sentence meaning: This dog was trained from a young age, so it is very well-behaved and gentle even around many people.
- Kanji meaning: 訓練: training; おとなしい: obedient, gentle, quiet.
- Example: 警察犬になるために毎日厳しい訓練を受けている。(It undergoes rigorous training every day to become a police dog.)
default.q.n3-10-q17-17.why.0: (a) 工夫 (くふう) means devising, thinking deeply, or improving a method; it is not used for training a dog.
default.q.n3-10-q17-17.why.1: (b) 用意 (ようい): preparation (luggage, money, meals, etc.); does not fit the context of animal training.
default.q.n3-10-q17-17.why.2: (c) 計画 (けいかく - plan): to plan or make arrangements; it is not used to mean teaching or training a pet.
default.q.n3-10-q17-17.why.3: (d) 訓練 (くんれん — training): training or practicing skills, for working dogs, pets, or people. The passive form 「訓練されている」 (being trained) is entirely appropriate for raising and training a dog from a young age.
default.q.n3-10-q18-18.verdict: The correct answer is 2. セット (set, set the time).
default.q.n3-10-q18-18.explanation:
Meaning: Since I am going out at 7 tomorrow, I set the alarm for 6.
- Expression: 目覚まし時計をセットする (set an alarm clock), 目覚まし時計 (alarm clock).
- Example: 明日の朝寝坊しないように、アラームを6時半にセットした。(I set the alarm for 6:30 so I would not oversleep tomorrow morning.)
default.q.n3-10-q18-18.why.0: (a) スタート (start): to begin, start up; it is not used with an alarm clock in the sense of setting an alarm time.
default.q.n3-10-q18-18.why.1: (b) セット means “set” or “program” a setting, such as an alarm time; the fixed expression is 「目覚まし時計を～時にセットする」 (“set the alarm clock for ～ o’clock”).
default.q.n3-10-q18-18.why.2: (c) ストップ (stop): to stop or bring something to a halt; it is not used for setting a timer before sleep.
default.q.n3-10-q18-18.why.3: (d) マーク (mark): to mark or keep track of something; it is not used for setting a clock timer.
default.q.n3-10-q19-19.verdict: The correct answer is 4. もったいない (wasteful, what a waste).
default.q.n3-10-q19-19.explanation:
Meaning: Being made to wait like this while I’m busy is such a waste of time.
- Expression: 時間がもったいない (it’s a waste of time), 待たされる (be made to wait—the causative-passive form of 待つ).
- Example: 食べ残しを捨てるのはもったいない。(It’s wasteful to throw away leftover food.)
default.q.n3-10-q19-19.why.0: (a) だらしない: untidy, careless, sloppy (in one's character or appearance); it is not used to describe wasted time.
default.q.n3-10-q19-19.why.1: (b) しようがない (仕様がない): there is nothing else to do; it cannot be combined with 「時間が～」 to express wasting time.
default.q.n3-10-q19-19.why.2: (c) なさけない (情けない): pathetic, shameful, blameworthy, or regrettable, especially regarding oneself; it does not express regret over lost time.
default.q.n3-10-q19-19.why.3: (d) もったいない (勿体無い): Wasteful, a waste; 「時間がもったいない」 (it is a waste of time) fits the situation of being busy but forced to wait for a long time.
default.q.n3-10-q20-20.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 材料 (ざいりょう - ingredients, materials).
default.q.n3-10-q20-20.explanation:
Meaning: The cake I ate at your house was delicious, so you showed me its ingredients and how to make it.
- Kanji meaning: 材料 (ingredients), 作り方 (how to make something), 友人 (friend).
- Example: カレーを作るためにスーパーで材料を買った。(I bought ingredients at the supermarket to make curry.)
default.q.n3-10-q20-20.why.0: (a) 資源 (しげん) means natural resources, such as minerals, oil, or energy; it is not used for baking or cooking.
default.q.n3-10-q20-20.why.1: (b) 材料 (ざいりょう): Ingredients, materials; together with 「作り方」 (“how to make it”), 「材料と作り方」 (“ingredients and instructions”) is completely appropriate in a cooking or baking context.
default.q.n3-10-q20-20.why.2: (c) 部品 (ぶひん): component, part, mechanical or electronic spare part; it is not used for food.
default.q.n3-10-q20-20.why.3: (d) 原因 (げんいん): the cause of an event or problem; it is unrelated to how to make a cake.
default.q.n3-10-q21-21.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 者 (しゃ—a suffix referring to a person: 愛用者—a person who favors or regularly uses something).
default.q.n3-10-q21-21.explanation:
Meaning: We conducted an opinion survey of people who like using this sofa.
- Word formation: 愛用 (to use regularly, to be fond of using) + 者 (person) -> 愛用者 (あいようしゃ - a regular user, loyal customer).
- Similar compounds with 「者」: 利用者 (user), 参加者 (participant), 経験者 (experienced person).
- Example: この化粧品は長年の愛用者が多い。(This cosmetic product has many loyal users who have used it for years.)
default.q.n3-10-q21-21.why.0: (a) 屋 (や): A suffix indicating a shop or business (本屋, 花屋), or a person with a particular personality trait or occupation (頑張り屋, 気分屋); it does not combine with 愛用.
default.q.n3-10-q21-21.why.1: (b) 人 (じん/にん) generally indicates nationality (日本人) or a number/type of people; it does not form a compound suffix with 愛用.
default.q.n3-10-q21-21.why.2: (c) 者 (しゃ: person): A suffix indicating a person who performs an action or belongs to a particular group; it forms the compound 「愛用者」 (あいようしゃ: a regular user or loyal customer of a product).
default.q.n3-10-q21-21.why.3: (d) 員 (いん - member): A suffix indicating a member of an organization or institution (社員, 会員, 店員); it is not used to mean a product user.
default.q.n3-10-q22-22.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 渋滞 (じゅうたい: traffic jam, congestion).
default.q.n3-10-q22-22.explanation:
Meaning: Because of construction work, the road is congested, and the cars cannot move forward even after waiting for a long time.
- Sino-Japanese readings: 渋滞 (traffic jam), 道路 (road), 工事 (construction work).
- Expressions: 道路が渋滞する (the road is congested), なかなか～ない (cannot ... despite waiting a long time).
- Example: 事故で高速道路がひどく渋滞している。(The expressway is severely congested because of an accident.)
default.q.n3-10-q22-22.why.0: (a) 渋滞 (じゅうたい): traffic congestion, a traffic jam. The expression 「道路が渋滞している」 (“the roads are congested”), making it difficult for vehicles to move forward, is completely accurate.
default.q.n3-10-q22-22.why.1: (b) 故障 (こしょう): breakdown, malfunction (used for machines and vehicles); not used to describe congested traffic or blocked roads.
default.q.n3-10-q22-22.why.2: (c) 増加 (ぞうか - increase): To increase or rise in quantity; it is not used as a verb in「道路が～している」in the context of vehicles being unable to move forward.
default.q.n3-10-q22-22.why.3: (d) 集合 (しゅうごう): gathering or assembling people; it is not used for roads.
default.q.n3-10-q23-23.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 効果 (こうか: effect, effectiveness).
default.q.n3-10-q23-23.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: The medicine has started to work, so I feel a little better.
- Sino-Japanese readings: 効果 (effect, efficacy), 具合 (physical condition, state of health).
- Phrases: 効果が出る (take effect, produce results), 具合がよくなる (one's condition improves).
- Example: この風邪薬を飲んだら、すぐに効果が現れた。(This cold medicine took effect immediately after I took it.)
default.q.n3-10-q23-23.why.0: (a) 成績 (せいせき): results or scores in school, or performance in work or competition; it is not used for medicine.
default.q.n3-10-q23-23.why.1: (b) 効果 (こうか): Effect, efficacy; 「薬の効果が出る」(the medicine takes effect) fits perfectly with the context of health improving.
default.q.n3-10-q23-23.why.2: (c) 応援 (おうえん): encouragement, support, or assistance; it is not used for medicine.
default.q.n3-10-q23-23.why.3: (d) 価値 (かち — value): material or spiritual value; it does not combine with 「～が出る」 in the context of a change in health.
default.q.n3-10-q24-24.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ペラペラ (fluent, able to speak a foreign language fluently).
default.q.n3-10-q24-24.explanation:
Sentence meaning: He has lived in Japan for only one year, but he can already speak Japanese very fluently.
- Expression: 外国語 / 日本語がペラペラだ (to speak a foreign language / Japanese fluently, effortlessly).
- Structure: ～しか...ない (only...).
- Example: 彼女は英語もフランス語もペラペラに話せる。(She can speak both English and French fluently.)
default.q.n3-10-q24-24.why.0: (a) さらさら: An onomatopoeic/mimetic word describing smoothness, such as smooth hair, the gentle sound of flowing water, or rustling leaves; it is not used for language ability.
default.q.n3-10-q24-24.why.1: (b) ばらばら: scattered, disconnected, uncoordinated, or dispersed in different places; it is not used to describe linguistic fluency.
default.q.n3-10-q24-24.why.2: (c) ふらふら: staggering, swaying, feeling dizzy or light-headed (from fatigue or intoxication); it does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-10-q24-24.why.3: (d) ペラペラ: an ideophone describing speaking a foreign language very fluently; 「日本語がペラペラだ」is completely correct.
default.q.n3-10-q25-25.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 身につけたい (身につける—to acquire, develop, or equip oneself with something).
default.q.n3-10-q25-25.explanation:
Sentence meaning: I intend to study hard at this school to acquire and develop knowledge and skills.
- Kanji-related vocabulary: 知識 (knowledge), 技術 (skills, technology), 一生懸命 (with all one’s might, diligently).
- Phrase: 知識／技術を身につける (to acquire, develop, or equip oneself with knowledge and skills), ～と思っている (to intend to do something).
- Example: 留学中に生きた英会話力を身につけたい。(I want to develop practical English conversation skills while studying abroad.)
default.q.n3-10-q25-25.why.0: (a) 身につけたい (from 身につける): to acquire, absorb, or master knowledge or skills; 「知識や技術を身につける」(acquire knowledge and skills) is the most natural and accurate expression.
default.q.n3-10-q25-25.why.1: (b) 気に入りたい comes from 「気に入る」 (“to like, to be pleased with”) and is not used with the object 「知識や技術」 to express acquiring knowledge or skills.
default.q.n3-10-q25-25.why.2: (c) 押し込みたい (from 押し込む): want to push or stuff in, force one's way in; it is not used for taking in knowledge.
default.q.n3-10-q25-25.why.3: (d) 取り上げたい (from 取り上げる) means “to confiscate,” “to deprive someone of,” or “to take up a topic for discussion.” It is not used to mean that learners independently develop their own knowledge or skills.
default.q.n3-10-q26-26.verdict: The correct answer is 3. いろいろな (various, diverse), synonymous with 「さまざま」.
default.q.n3-10-q26-26.explanation:
Sentence meaning: At today’s meeting, many diverse opinions were expressed.
- さまざま (様々): many different kinds, diverse, varied (= いろいろな).
- Example: 世の中にはさまざまな考え方の人がいる。(There are people with many different ways of thinking in the world.)
default.q.n3-10-q26-26.why.0: (a) 「とくべつ」（特別） means “special,” not “varied” or “of many kinds” like 「さまざま」.
default.q.n3-10-q26-26.why.1: (b) 「すばらしい」（素晴らしい）means wonderful or excellent and is used to praise quality or character, so it is not equivalent in meaning.
default.q.n3-10-q26-26.why.2: (c) 「いろいろな」（色々な） means many, varied, or diverse, and is completely synonymous with 「さまざま（な）」.
default.q.n3-10-q26-26.why.3: (d) 「あたらしい」（新しい - new）describes the newness of a thing or situation and is not appropriate here.
default.q.n3-10-q27-27.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 知らせて (to notify, to inform), equivalent in meaning to 「報告して」.
default.q.n3-10-q27-27.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Please report it to me or let me know as soon as possible.
- 報告する (ほうこくする - to report): to inform someone of a situation or result (= 知らせる).
- Example: 結果が分かり次第、すぐに知らせてください。(Please let me know as soon as the result is known.)
default.q.n3-10-q27-27.why.0: (a) 「頼んで」(頼む: to ask a favor, request) is incorrect because it describes a different action.
default.q.n3-10-q27-27.why.1: (b) 「知らせて」（知らせる - to inform, let someone know）is the most appropriate replacement for「報告する」（to report a situation or result）.
default.q.n3-10-q27-27.why.2: (c) 「尋ねて」（尋ねる: to ask, inquire）means asking for information, which is the opposite of reporting.
default.q.n3-10-q27-27.why.3: (d) 「探して」 (from 探す - to search) does not mean to convey or provide information.
default.q.n3-10-q28-28.verdict: The correct answer is 4. かならず (certainly, without fail), synonymous with 「絶対に」.
default.q.n3-10-q28-28.explanation:
Meaning: I think Mr./Ms. Yamada will definitely come.
- 絶対に (ぜったいに: absolutely, definitely, without fail = 必ず - かならず).
- Example: 約束は必ず守らなければなりません。(You must keep your promise.)
default.q.n3-10-q28-28.why.0: (a) 「あとで」（後で: later, afterward）is an adverb indicating a time point; it does not express a degree of certainty.
default.q.n3-10-q28-28.why.1: (b) 「すぐに」（直ぐに: immediately）refers to speed or urgency in time and is not equivalent in meaning.
default.q.n3-10-q28-28.why.2: (c) 「たぶん」(多分 – probably, perhaps) indicates uncertain speculation, in contrast to the 100% certainty of 「絶対に」.
default.q.n3-10-q28-28.why.3: (d) 「かならず」（必ず - surely, certainly）is completely synonymous with 「絶対に」when affirming that something will happen.
default.q.n3-10-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is 1. おわり (end, finish), synonymous with 「おしまい」.
default.q.n3-10-q29-29.explanation:
Meaning: This story ends here / That's all.
- おしまい (仕舞 / 終): end, finish, come to an end (= 終わり - おわり).
- Example: 今日の授業はこれでおしまいです。(This concludes today's class.)
default.q.n3-10-q29-29.why.0: (a) 「おわり」 (終わり: ending, the end) is completely synonymous with 「おしまい」.
default.q.n3-10-q29-29.why.1: (b) 「すごい」（凄い - amazing, wonderful）is an adjective expressing evaluation or emotion and is unrelated here.
default.q.n3-10-q29-29.why.2: (c) 「はじめて」(初めて – for the first time) expresses beginning or being the first time, which is opposite to the meaning of ending.
default.q.n3-10-q29-29.why.3: (d) 「おもしろい」（面白い - interesting, engaging）describes the nature of a story's content and is not synonymous.
default.q.n3-10-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 遊びたくて、学校を休んでしまった (I wanted to play, so I ended up skipping school), which accurately explains the meaning of 「サボる」.
default.q.n3-10-q30-30.explanation:
Meaning: “I skipped school last week.”
- サボる (derived from the French word “sabotage”): to skip school or work without permission out of laziness or a desire to have fun (= 遊びたくて/怠けて休む).
- Distinction: 休む means to take a day off from school or work, possibly for a legitimate reason; 辞める means to quit school or leave a job permanently; サボる means to skip school or work without permission.
default.q.n3-10-q30-30.why.0: (a) It is incorrect both in cause (being sick) and in the nature of the action (「辞める」 means quitting permanently, whereas 「サボる」 means skipping one class or a short period of time).
default.q.n3-10-q30-30.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「サボる」means deliberately skipping or cutting class because of laziness or wanting to have fun, not taking time off because of illness (病気).
default.q.n3-10-q30-30.why.2: (c) The error is in the verb 「辞める」 (to quit or drop out permanently); 「サボる」 does not mean to quit for good.
default.q.n3-10-q30-30.why.3: (d) This accurately explains the meaning of 「サボる」: skipping or cutting class because of laziness or a desire to have fun.
default.q.n3-10-q31-31.explanation:
「オーバー」(over) means exceeding a limit, budget, standard, or prescribed amount, as in 予算オーバー (over budget), 時間オーバー (over the time limit), or exceeding the weight limit.
Example: 荷物の重さが規定を2キロオーバーしてしまった。(The luggage exceeded the weight limit by 2 kg.)
default.q.n3-10-q31-31.why.0: Incorrect for the context; when saying that an airplane's departure time has been delayed or postponed, use 「遅れた」 or 「変更になった」, not 「時間がオーバーになった」.
default.q.n3-10-q31-31.why.1: Correct in context. 「オーバーする」(over) means to exceed an expected amount or budget. Here, because there were no inexpensive items, spending exceeded the budget by 10,000 yen: 「1万円もオーバーしてしまった」. This is a natural and accurate usage.
default.q.n3-10-q31-31.why.2: The context is incorrect; when overthinking makes your mind overloaded or confused, use「頭がパンクした」or「混乱した」, not「頭がオーバーになった」.
default.q.n3-10-q31-31.why.3: Incorrect for this context; when too much food has been cooked and there is extra, use 「料理が余って」 or 「多すぎて」, not 「料理がオーバーして」.
default.q.n3-10-q32-32.explanation:
「欠点」(けってん) means a flaw, weakness, or shortcoming in a thing, place, or person. It is the opposite of 長所 (strength/advantage) or 利点 (benefit).
Example: 彼の短気なところが唯一の欠点だ。(His short temper is his only flaw.)
default.q.n3-10-q32-32.why.0: The usage is appropriate; 「欠点」 means a limitation or undesirable feature of a place, thing, or person, and 「駅から遠いという欠点」 ('the drawback of being far from the station') is completely correct.
default.q.n3-10-q32-32.why.1: This does not fit the context. A nutritional deficiency or imbalance is expressed with 「栄養の偏り」 or 「栄養不足」, not 「栄養に欠点」.
default.q.n3-10-q32-32.why.2: The context is incorrect; when a vehicle is scraped or damaged in a collision, use「傷 (キズ) が付いてしまった」, not「欠点が付く」.
default.q.n3-10-q32-32.why.3: The context is incorrect; when checking whether an email address contains an error or mistake, use 「誤り」 or 「間違いがないか」, not 「欠点」.
default.q.n3-10-q33-33.explanation:
「親しい」(したしい) is an i-adjective used to describe a close, familiar, and intimate relationship between people, as in 親しい友人 and 親しい間柄.
Example: 彼女とは子どものころから親しくしている。(She and I have been close since childhood.)
default.q.n3-10-q33-33.why.0: The context is incorrect; for a favorite subject or one that someone is good at, use 「得意だった」 or 「好きだった」. 「親しい」 is not used for school subjects.
default.q.n3-10-q33-33.why.1: The context is incorrect. When talking about a familiar route whose layout one knows well, use 「詳しい道」 or 「わかりやすい道」. 「親しい」 is not used to modify a road.
default.q.n3-10-q33-33.why.2: The context is incorrect. When feeling happy or nostalgic about seeing friends again after a long time, use 「懐かしかった」, 「楽しかった」, or 「嬉しかった」, not 「親しかった」.
default.q.n3-10-q33-33.why.3: This fits the context. 「親しい」 describes a close relationship between people, and 「親しい人」 (“a close acquaintance” or “someone close to you”) is a completely standard usage.
default.q.n3-10-q34-34.explanation:
「詰める」(つめる — to pack, stuff, or cram) is a transitive verb meaning to put many things into a space or container until it is full, such as packing things into a suitcase or putting rice into a bento box: 弁当箱に詰める.
Example: スーツケースに荷物をいっぱいに詰めた。(I packed the suitcase full of luggage.)
default.q.n3-10-q34-34.why.0: This fits the context. 「詰める」 means to put, stuff, or pack things tightly into a container, so 「かばんに洋服やお土産を詰めた」 is natural and accurate.
default.q.n3-10-q34-34.why.1: The context is wrong; when arranging dishes on a table, use 「並べて」 (arrange, lay out), not 「詰めて」.
default.q.n3-10-q34-34.why.2: Incorrect for this context; when writing important things in a notebook, use「書いた」,「記録した」, or「メモした」, not「詰めた」.
default.q.n3-10-q34-34.why.3: Incorrect for the context; when reaching into or putting one's hand into a pocket, use 「手を入れて」or「手を突っ込んで」, not 「手を詰めて」.
default.q.n3-10-q35-35.explanation:
「支給」(しきゅう) is a noun and a Group 3 verb meaning for an organization, company, or public agency to provide or pay money, supplies, or benefits to an individual under established rules or a welfare system. Examples include 交通費を支給する, 手当を支給する, and 制服を支給する.
Example: アルバイトにも交通費が全額支給される。(Even part-time employees are reimbursed for their full transportation costs.)
default.q.n3-10-q35-35.why.0: The context is incorrect. When giving a birthday present to one’s mother, use 「プレゼントをあげる」 or 「贈る」. 「支給」 is used when an organization or institution distributes something according to regulations.
default.q.n3-10-q35-35.why.1: Incorrect for this context; when going to submit a report to a teacher, use 「提出しに行く」 or 「出しに行く」, not 「支給」.
default.q.n3-10-q35-35.why.2: Correct in context; 「支給する」(to provide or pay) is used when an organization or company provides money or goods to employees as part of a benefits system. Here, 「交通費を支給してくれる」(the company pays transportation expenses) is the correct collocation.
default.q.n3-10-q35-35.why.3: It does not fit the context; when distributing materials to everyone before a meeting, use 「配ってください」(くばる) or 「配布してください」(はいふ), not 「支給」.
default.q.n3-11-q36-36.verdict: The correct answer is 2. ほど.
default.q.n3-11-q36-36.explanation:
Meaning: This summer is not as hot as last summer.
Pattern: [Noun A] は [Noun B] ほど + adjective/verb in the negative form (〜ない): A is not as ... as B.
Example: 今年の冬は去年ほど寒くない。(This winter is not as cold as last winter.)
default.q.n3-11-q36-36.why.0: (a) 「から」means “from”; it is not used in a negative degree comparison structure.
default.q.n3-11-q36-36.why.1: (b) 「ほど」 is used with the negative in the pattern 「AはBほど…ない」, meaning "A is not as... as B," here expressing that this summer is not as hot as last summer.
default.q.n3-11-q36-36.why.2: (c) 「まで」 means “up to” or “until,” and does not form a degree comparison structure.
default.q.n3-11-q36-36.why.3: (d) 「しか」 is used with the negative pattern 「〜しか…ない」 to mean “only,” so it does not fit the comparative meaning of the sentence.
default.q.n3-11-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 1. か/か.
default.q.n3-11-q37-37.explanation:
Meaning: This morning, a very pleasant fragrance came from the person sitting next to me on the train, although I could not tell whether it was shampoo or something else.
Structure: 〜か何かわからない / 〜か〜かわからない: not know whether it is... or something / not be sure whether it is A or B.
Example: 夢か本当かわからない。(I do not know whether it is a dream or reality.)
default.q.n3-11-q37-37.why.0: (a) 「か/か」 forms the pattern 「〜か何かわからない」 (“I don’t know whether it is shampoo or something else”), used when making an uncertain guess.
default.q.n3-11-q37-37.why.1: (b) 「は/は」 is a particle indicating the topic or emphasis; it cannot be combined with 「何」 to express an unclear guess.
default.q.n3-11-q37-37.why.2: (c) 「が/が」 is a particle marking the subject; it is not used to list unspecified possibilities.
default.q.n3-11-q37-37.why.3: (d) 「で/で」 is the particle used for means, location, or cause; it is not used in this sentence pattern.
default.q.n3-11-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 4. だけなら.
default.q.n3-11-q38-38.explanation:
Sentence meaning:
Section chief: "Sorry to ask you at such short notice, Lâm, but could you finish both tomorrow's business-trip report and the meeting materials by around noon today?"
Lâm: "It seems difficult to do both. But if it's only the meeting materials, I think I can finish them..."
Structure: [Noun] + だけなら: If it is only... (used to narrow the scope of the condition under which the following action is possible).
Example: 一人だけなら部屋に入れます。(If it is only one person, they can enter the room.)
default.q.n3-11-q38-38.why.0: (a) 「とでも」 means “for example” or “as if,” and is not appropriate for setting a limiting condition.
default.q.n3-11-q38-38.why.1: (b) 「となら」 means “if together with,” and does not express a limitation on the scope of the work.
default.q.n3-11-q38-38.why.2: (c) 「だけでも」 means “even just...” or “just ... alone is enough,” indicating a minimum degree. When presenting a limiting condition for completing the task, 「だけなら」 is more appropriate.
default.q.n3-11-q38-38.why.3: (d) 「だけなら」 means “if it is only...,” expressing the limiting condition that the work can be finished if it consists only of the meeting materials.
default.q.n3-11-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 3. ちっとも.
default.q.n3-11-q39-39.explanation:
Meaning: These days, I'm really frustrated because my son absolutely refuses to listen to me.
Structure: ちっとも + V-ない / A-くない / Na-ではない: not at all, not even a little (synonymous with 少しも〜ない and 全く〜ない).
Example: 昨夜はちっとも眠れなかった。(I couldn't sleep at all last night.)
default.q.n3-11-q39-39.why.0: (a) 「やっと」 means “finally” and commonly occurs with an affirmative sentence expressing an expected result achieved after considerable effort.
default.q.n3-11-q39-39.why.1: (b) 「きっと」 means “certainly” and is commonly used with conjectural forms such as 「〜だろう / 〜はずだ」.
default.q.n3-11-q39-39.why.2: (c) 「ちっとも」 is always used with the negative form 「〜ない」 and means “not at all” or “not even a little,” expressing frustration that the son does not listen at all.
default.q.n3-11-q39-39.why.3: (d) 「せっかく」 means “with considerable effort” or “after going to the trouble,” and commonly combines with 「〜のに」 or 「〜から」.
default.q.n3-11-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 1. おかげで.
default.q.n3-11-q40-40.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Our lives have become much more convenient thanks to advances in technology.
Pattern: [Noun + の / short-form verb] + おかげで: thanks to..., expressing a positive result and gratitude.
Kanji readings: 技術 (ぎじゅつ: technology), 進歩 (しんぽ: progress), 便利 (べんり: convenient).
Example: 薬を飲んだおかげで、熱が下がった。(Thanks to taking medicine, my fever went down.)
default.q.n3-11-q40-40.why.0: (a) 「おかげで」 means “thanks to” and indicates a cause leading to a positive result, such as life becoming more convenient thanks to advances in technology.
default.q.n3-11-q40-40.why.1: (b) 「ようで」is the connective form of 「ようだ」, meaning “seems like”; it does not express a cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.n3-11-q40-40.why.2: (c) 「ことで」 means “by means of” or “through the act of,” and does not naturally follow the noun 「進歩のこと」 to indicate the cause of a positive result.
default.q.n3-11-q40-40.why.3: (d) 「ほかで」 means “elsewhere” or “besides,” and does not form a structure expressing a cause.
default.q.n3-11-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 着いたとしても.
default.q.n3-11-q41-41.explanation:
Sentence meaning: The Hotel Y where I stayed on a business trip was right in front of the station, so I felt reassured even if I arrived at the station late at night.
Pattern: [plain form / V-た] + としても: even if..., even supposing that... (concessive hypothetical condition).
Vocabulary: 出張 (business trip), 安心 (relief, peace of mind).
Example: たとえ雨が降ったとしても、試合は行われます。(Even if it rains, the match will be held.)
default.q.n3-11-q41-41.why.0: (a) 「着いたり」belongs to the action-listing pattern 「〜たり〜たりする」and cannot stand alone to connect with a clause expressing a psychological state such as 「安心だ」.
default.q.n3-11-q41-41.why.1: (b) 「着いたため」 means “because [someone] arrived,” indicating the cause of an event that actually occurred. It is not used for a hypothetical future event.
default.q.n3-11-q41-41.why.2: (c) 「着いたとしても」means “even if” or “even supposing that one arrives,” presenting a concessive hypothetical situation: even if one arrives at the station late at night, one can still feel reassured.
default.q.n3-11-q41-41.why.3: (d) 「着いたかどうか」means “whether they have arrived or not,” and does not form a logical connection with the following clause.
default.q.n3-11-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 営業していて.
default.q.n3-11-q42-42.explanation:
Meaning: This is my second time visiting Japan. I came once before, 20 years ago, and I was very surprised that the café I visited then is still in business.
Structure: まだ + V-ている: “still be doing ...” or “remain in a state.” A verb in the て-form before an emotion verb (驚く, 嬉しい, 困る, etc.) indicates the reason for that emotion.
Kanji readings and meanings: 喫茶店 (café), 営業 (business, operation), 驚く (to be surprised).
Example: 昔の友達がまだ私を覚えていてくれて嬉しかった。(I was happy that an old friend still remembered me.)
default.q.n3-11-q42-42.why.0: (a) 「営業して」 is simply the te-form of a verb and cannot express the state of continuing to operate throughout the past 20 years.
default.q.n3-11-q42-42.why.1: (b) 「営業しなくて」means “not doing business,” and does not combine logically with the adverb「まだ」(still).
default.q.n3-11-q42-42.why.2: (c) 「営業していて」 uses the progressive form 「〜ている」 with 「まだ」 to express the state of “still being open and operating.” The following clause uses the て-form to give the cause of the speaker's surprise.
default.q.n3-11-q42-42.why.3: (d) 「営業していなくて」 means “not currently operating.” If the restaurant had already closed, 「もう」 would be used instead of 「まだ」.
default.q.n3-11-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 読んでもらってから.
default.q.n3-11-q43-43.explanation:
Meaning: When I was little, my parents always read picture books to me before I went to bed.
Grammar:
- [Recipient] は [Giver] に + V-てもらう: have someone do something for you.
- V-てから: after doing V, indicating a clear sequence of events.
Kanji: 絵本 (picture book).
Example: 宿題を終わらせてから遊びに行きます。(I will go out to play after finishing my homework.)
default.q.n3-11-q43-43.why.0: (a) 「読んでくれてから」is incorrect because when the recipient of the action is marked by 「親に」, 「もらう」must be used; 「くれる」requires 「親が」as the subject.
default.q.n3-11-q43-43.why.1: (b) 「読んでもらってから」 correctly combines the benefactive structure 「〜に〜てもらう」 (having one's parents read to one) with the sequence 「〜てから」 (after... and then going to sleep).
default.q.n3-11-q43-43.why.2: (c) 「読んでくれるから」 has the wrong subject with the particle 「親に」 and means “because my parents read it for me,” which does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-11-q43-43.why.3: (d) 「読んでもらうから」 expresses a reason (“because someone will read it”), but it does not express the temporal sequence of one action happening before another, as 「〜てから」 does.
default.q.n3-11-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 変わってきたら.
default.q.n3-11-q44-44.explanation:
Meaning: First, stir-fry the meat in a pan. When the meat starts to change color, add the vegetables.
Grammar:
- V-てくる: describes a gradual change beginning to appear.
- V-たら、〜てください: when / after doing V, please... (used for instructions or requests).
Example: お湯が沸いたら、火を止めてください。(When the water boils, please turn off the heat.)
default.q.n3-11-q44-44.why.0: (a) 「変わっていって」is only a te-form connective expression and does not create a suitable conditional clause for the instruction.
default.q.n3-11-q44-44.why.1: (b) 「変わってくるのに」means “although” or “in order to,” so it does not fit the structure of this cooking instruction at all.
default.q.n3-11-q44-44.why.2: (c) 「変わっていくと」 uses the direction of change 「〜ていく」 incorrectly, and the conditional conjunction 「〜と」 cannot be followed by a request or command such as 「〜てください」.
default.q.n3-11-q44-44.why.3: (d) 「変わってきたら」 combines the change-direction pattern 「〜てくる」, expressing a gradual change that has begun to appear in the color of the meat, with the conditional 「〜たら」 (“when/after...”), and correctly precedes the request 「〜てください」.
default.q.n3-11-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 聞かせる.
default.q.n3-11-q45-45.explanation:
Meaning: When the baby would not go to sleep, I heard that playing classical music for the baby would help them sleep very well.
Pattern: [person affected] に + V-(さ)せる (causative form): to let or make someone perform an action. 聞く becomes 聞かせる in the causative form (to let someone hear, play something for someone to hear).
Kanji note: 音楽 means music.
Example: 子供に好きな本を読ませる。(I let my child read the book they like.)
default.q.n3-11-q45-45.why.0: (a) 「聞かせる」 is the causative form (使役形) of 「聞く」, meaning “let someone hear” or “play something for someone to hear.” Combined with 「赤ちゃんに」, it expresses an adult playing music for a baby.
default.q.n3-11-q45-45.why.1: (b) 「聞かれる」is the passive or honorific form of 「聞く」; it does not mean actively playing music for someone else to enjoy.
default.q.n3-11-q45-45.why.2: (c) 「聞かされる」is the causative-passive form meaning “be made to listen,” which does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-11-q45-45.why.3: (d) 「聞いている」 is the progressive form “is listening.” With this meaning, it cannot take 「赤ちゃんに」 as the recipient or listener.
default.q.n3-11-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 2. いらっしゃいます.
default.q.n3-11-q46-46.explanation:
Meaning of the dialogue:
Mori: "Yes, Kitayama Japanese Language School speaking."
Lee: "Hello, this is Lee from the intermediate class. Is Mr. Mori there?"
Mori: "Oh, Lee. This is Mr. Mori. What can I do for you?"
Honorific language:
- The 尊敬語 (respectful form) of いる / 行く / 来る is いらっしゃる (polite form: いらっしゃいます).
- The 謙譲語 (humble form) of 見る is 拝見する, and that of 会う is お目にかかる.
Sino-Japanese terms: 中級 (intermediate level), 拝見 (拜见).
Example: 田中先生は研究室にいらっしゃいます。(Professor Tanaka is in the research laboratory.)
default.q.n3-11-q46-46.why.0: (a) 「ございます」 is the polite form of 「ある / です」 and is used for objects or matters, not people (in this case, the teacher).
default.q.n3-11-q46-46.why.1: (b) 「いらっしゃいます」 is the honorific language (尊敬語) form of 「います」, used to politely and respectfully ask whether one’s superior, Mr. Mori, is there.
default.q.n3-11-q46-46.why.2: (c) 「拝見します」 is the humble form (謙譲語) of the verb 「見ます」 (to see, look at), used for one's own action.
default.q.n3-11-q46-46.why.3: (d) 「お目にかかります」 is the humble form (謙譲語) of 「会います」 (to meet), used for one’s own action.
default.q.n3-11-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ばかりしていても.
default.q.n3-11-q47-47.explanation:
Meaning of the exchange:
A: "My child is starting swimming lessons next week, and I'm worried about so many things."
B: "Worrying endlessly before it has even started won't solve anything. It will be fine!"
Pattern: [Noun] + ばかりしていても仕方がない / V-てばかりいても仕方がない: There is no point in doing nothing but... / It will not solve anything to keep...
Kanji vocabulary: 水泳 (swimming), 教室 (classroom, class), 心配 (worry, concern).
Example: 悩んでばかりいても仕方がないから、行動しよう。(There is no point in worrying endlessly, so let's take action.)
default.q.n3-11-q47-47.why.0: (a) 「よりしていれば」 is grammatically incorrect because the particle 「より」 is not used to express an action that continues or occurs repeatedly.
default.q.n3-11-q47-47.why.1: (b) 「よりしていても」 is grammatically incorrect and does not form a meaningful phrase in Japanese.
default.q.n3-11-q47-47.why.2: (c) 「ばかりしていれば」 uses the conditional ending 「〜ば」 and cannot combine with the pattern expressing futility 「〜しかたない」; the 「〜ても」 form must be used.
default.q.n3-11-q47-47.why.3: (d) 「ばかりしていても」 combines 「〜ばかりする」 (keep doing; do nothing but...) with 「〜てもしかたがない」 (even if one does..., it is useless). Together, it means "there is no point in continuing to worry; it will not solve anything."
default.q.n3-11-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 1. しなきゃならなくなった.
default.q.n3-11-q48-48.explanation:
Meaning of the exchange:
Husband: “I’m going to the office now.”
Wife: “What? But today is your day off.”
Husband: “The company called a little while ago, so I suddenly have to go to work.”
Grammar:
- V-なきゃ = V-なければ, a contraction used in casual spoken language.
- V-なければならない + ようになる: come to have to do something because of a change in external circumstances.
Kanji reading: 出勤 (しゅっきん - go to work).
Example: 急な仕事が入って、旅行に行けなくなった。(Unexpected work came up, so I can no longer go on the trip.)
default.q.n3-11-q48-48.why.0: (a) 「しなきゃならなくなった」 is the contracted spoken form of 「〜しなければならなくなった」 (came to have to do something). It describes an unexpected objective circumstance that forced the speaker to go to work even though it was a day off.
default.q.n3-11-q48-48.why.1: (b) 「しちゃいけなくなった」 is a contracted form of 「〜してはいけなくなった」, meaning “it became prohibited to do...,” which is the exact opposite of the context requiring someone to go to work.
default.q.n3-11-q48-48.why.2: (c) 「するつもりでいる」 means “to be planning to do something,” expressing a personal intention formed in advance rather than a situation passively arising because the company called.
default.q.n3-11-q48-48.why.3: (d) 「しないようにしている」 means “am trying not to do” or “make a habit of not doing,” describing one's own habit or effort, so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-11-q49-49.verdict: The correct order is: 4 → 2 → 1 → 3. The ★ position, at the third gap, is choice 1 (などの).
default.q.n3-11-q49-49.explanation: この喫茶店はコーヒーだけでなくスパゲティなどの料理もおいしい。 (This café serves not only good coffee but also delicious dishes such as spaghetti.)
default.q.n3-11-q49-49.why.0: (a) Position 3: It modifies the following noun phrase 「料理も」 to form 「スパゲティなどの料理も」 (dishes such as spaghetti).
default.q.n3-11-q49-49.why.1: (b) Position 2: It comes after 「だけでなく」 and before 「などの」 to introduce an example in a list (スパゲティなどの...).
default.q.n3-11-q49-49.why.2: (c) Position 4: It comes before the predicate 「おいしい」 to form the correlative structure 「〜だけでなく〜も」 (“not only... but also...”).
default.q.n3-11-q49-49.why.3: (d) Position 1: It follows the noun 「コーヒー」to form the grammar pattern「コーヒーだけでなく」(not only coffee).
default.q.n3-11-q50-50.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 3 → 1. The star (★) is in the third blank, so the answer is choice 3 (あと3分).
default.q.n3-11-q50-50.explanation:
(At a movie theater)
妻:「私、ちょっとジュース買いに行ってくるね。」
夫:「うん。あ、でも、映画が始まるまであと3分しかないよ。急いでね。。。。」
((At a movie theater)
Wife: "I'm going to buy some juice and come back."
Husband: "Okay. Oh, but there are only 3 minutes left before the movie starts. Hurry....")
default.q.n3-11-q50-50.why.0: (a) Position 4: It follows the quantity expression 「あと3分」 and forms the limiting pattern with a negative nuance, 「〜しかない」(there are only 3 minutes left), before the sentence-ending particle 「よ」.
default.q.n3-11-q50-50.why.1: (b) Position 1: It follows the subject 「映画が」 and modifies the time expression before the particle 「まで」 (映画が始まるまで: “until the movie starts”).
default.q.n3-11-q50-50.why.2: (c) Position 3: It comes after 「まで」 and before 「しかない」 to indicate the short amount of time remaining (あと3分しかない).
default.q.n3-11-q50-50.why.3: (d) Position 2: It follows the dictionary-form verb 「始まる」 to form the time structure 「V-る + まで」 (until...).
default.q.n3-11-q51-51.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 4 → 2 → 1. The star (★) at the third slot is choice 2 (いい).
default.q.n3-11-q51-51.explanation: 今度の日曜日に友人の結婚式がある。晴れるといいのだが。。。 (My friend’s wedding is next Sunday. I hope the weather will be sunny that day...)
default.q.n3-11-q51-51.why.0: (a) Position 4: It follows the adjective 「いい」 to form the nominalizing or explanatory structure 「〜のだが」, which comes before the trailing conjunction 「が」.
default.q.n3-11-q51-51.why.1: (b) Position 3: It follows the conditional particle 「と」 to form the pattern expressing a wish or hope, 「〜といい」 (I hope... / If only...).
default.q.n3-11-q51-51.why.2: (c) Position 1: It comes at the beginning of the clause after the period and is the dictionary form of the verb 「晴れる」, describing a weather phenomenon.
default.q.n3-11-q51-51.why.3: (d) Position 2: It follows the verb 「晴れる」 to form the conditional clause 「晴れると」 (“if the weather is sunny, then...” ).
default.q.n3-11-q52-52.verdict: Correct order: 1 → 4 → 3 → 2. The ★ is in the third gap, which is choice 3 (続けているのは).
default.q.n3-11-q52-52.explanation: 息子は、サッカークラップの練習がきついとよく言っているが、それでもやめずに続けているのは、やっぱりサッカーが好きだからだと思う。 (My son often says that soccer club practice is tough, but I think he keeps going without quitting because he really does love soccer.)
default.q.n3-11-q52-52.why.0: (a) Position 1: It comes directly after the quotative particle 「きついと」 to form the contrastive clause 「きついとよく言っているが」 (often complains that it is hard, but...).
default.q.n3-11-q52-52.why.1: (b) Position 4: It comes before the adjective 「好きだから」 to mark what is liked: 「やっぱりサッカーが好きだから」 (as expected, because [I] like soccer).
default.q.n3-11-q52-52.why.2: (c) Position 3: It follows 「やめずに」 and serves as the subject of the explanatory pattern 「〜のは〜からだ」 (the reason it continues is that...).
default.q.n3-11-q52-52.why.3: (d) Position 2: follows the conjunction 「が」 and modifies the verb 「続けている」, expressing concession in 「それでもやめずに」 (even so, continuing without quitting...).
default.q.n3-11-q53-53.verdict: Correct order: 1 → 3 → 4 → 2. The ★ is in the third gap, which is choice 4 (自転車で行けば).
default.q.n3-11-q53-53.explanation: うちから学校まで自転車で 40 分かかる。電車なら 20 分だが、朝のこんでいる電車は嫌いだし、自転車で行けばよい運動になるから、自転車で通っている。 (It takes 40 minutes to get from my house to school by bicycle. It would take only 20 minutes by train, but I dislike crowded morning trains, and cycling is good exercise, so I commute by bicycle.)
default.q.n3-11-q53-53.why.0: (a) Position 1: It follows the attributive modifier 「朝の」 to form the noun phrase 「朝のこんでいる電車は」 (“as for the crowded morning train...” ).
default.q.n3-11-q53-53.why.1: (b) Position 4 comes before the result clause 「自転車で通っている」 and states the reason with 「〜から」 (because it will be good exercise...).
default.q.n3-11-q53-53.why.2: (c) Position 2: It follows the predicate 「嫌い」 and connects the first item in a list of reasons with 「〜し」 (“I dislike trains, and besides…”).
default.q.n3-11-q53-53.why.3: (d) Position 3: It follows 「嫌いだし」 to introduce a conditional assumption for the second reason, 「自転車で行けばよい運動になる」 (“if one goes by bicycle, it would be good exercise”).
default.q.n3-11-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 待っているのです.
default.q.n3-11-q54-54.explanation: In the preceding sentence, the author describes an observed scene: 「東京の街を歩いていると、飲食店の前にたくさんの人が並んでいるのをよく見ます。」(When walking through the streets of Tokyo, I often see many people lined up in front of restaurants.) The sentence containing blank [19] explains that scene: the people are lining up because they are waiting to enter the restaurant. The structure 「〜ているのです」expresses the ongoing action and uses 「〜のです」to explain and clarify the phenomenon just observed. Therefore, choice 4 is the most appropriate answer.
default.q.n3-11-q54-54.why.0: (a) 「待つことです」expresses a definition or goal/task (“it is waiting”), so it is unsuitable for describing the ongoing action of people standing in line.
default.q.n3-11-q54-54.why.1: (b) 「待ちにくいからです」expresses a negative reason (“because it is difficult to wait”), which is completely semantically inappropriate in context.
default.q.n3-11-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「待ったところです」 describes an action that has just been completed ("have just finished waiting"), so it does not fit a scene in which everyone is currently lining up.
default.q.n3-11-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「待っているのです」 combines the progressive form 「〜ている」(is waiting) with 「〜のです」(an explanation of the situation shown in the preceding sentence), making it natural and accurate.
default.q.n3-11-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 1. でも.
default.q.n3-11-q55-55.explanation: Before blank [20], the author says: "店に着くと、やはりたくさんの人が並んでいました。" (When I arrived at the shop, there were indeed many people lining up—a situation that usually makes waiting feel tiring or lengthy.) After the blank: "友達と話しながら待っていたら、長い時間待ったとは感じませんでした。" (However, when I waited while talking with a friend, I did not feel that I had waited for a long time.) The two clauses contrast in terms of the psychological experience and result, so the contrastive conjunction 「でも」 (but, however) is needed.
default.q.n3-11-q55-55.why.0: (a) 「でも」 is a conjunction expressing contrast (“but,” “however”), so it logically connects the fact that the restaurant is very crowded with the fact that the speaker does not feel they have waited long.
default.q.n3-11-q55-55.why.1: (b) 「また」is an additive conjunction meaning “in addition” or “furthermore”; it does not express contrast.
default.q.n3-11-q55-55.why.2: (c) 「つまり」 means “in other words” or “to sum up” and is used to explain or condense the preceding idea, so it does not fit the flow of the passage.
default.q.n3-11-q55-55.why.3: (d) 「そのうえ」means “moreover” or “in addition,” adding information in the same direction, so it does not fit a contrastive context.
default.q.n3-11-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 言われて.
default.q.n3-11-q56-56.explanation: Context: The senior is the person who says 「いいなあ。私も今度行ってみよう。」 (“That sounds nice. I'll try going next time too.”), and the speaker feels happy upon hearing the senior say this. The grammatical pattern marking the agent with the particle に is 「[Person] に [Quoted content] と言われて、[Emotion/Action]」 (“being told by someone that ... and then feeling ...”). Therefore, the passive form 「言われて」 is the most accurate answer.
default.q.n3-11-q56-56.why.0: (a) 「言えて」is the potential form ("can say") and does not fit the context, in which the author hears words from a senior person (used with 「先輩に」).
default.q.n3-11-q56-56.why.1: (b) 「言われて」is the passive form (“was told”), fitting the structure 「先輩に……と言われてうれしかった」, which describes the author receiving words from a senior and feeling happy.
default.q.n3-11-q56-56.why.2: (c) 「言ってきて」 describes an action directed toward the speaker, but it does not form a natural construction expressing the cause of the mood in this sentence.
default.q.n3-11-q56-56.why.3: (d) 「言ってくれて」 carries a nuance of someone doing a favor or providing help and is usually used with 「が」 to mark the person, as in 先輩が. It does not fit the agent structure 「先輩に……と言われて」 in this emotional context.
default.q.n3-11-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 別の.
default.q.n3-11-q57-57.explanation: In the previous section, after tasting the delicious cheesecake, the author came to understand to some extent how people feel when they line up at popular restaurants ("人気の店に並んで待つ気持ちが少しわかりました"). Therefore, the author expresses a broader wish for the future: if given the opportunity, they would like to try lining up at "other popular restaurants as well" (「別の人気店でも」). The word 「別の」(other) indicates expanding the experience to other popular restaurants besides the cheesecake shop just visited.
default.q.n3-11-q57-57.why.0: (a) 「その」 refers specifically to that bakery, so it does not fit the idea of trying other bakeries together with the particle 「でも」.
default.q.n3-11-q57-57.why.1: (b) 「どの」 (which) requires a different structure and does not clearly express the intention to try another café besides the one already visited.
default.q.n3-11-q57-57.why.2: (c) 「別の」means “different” or “another,” forming「別の人気店でも」(at other popular restaurants as well), expressing the desire to try more restaurants if the opportunity arises.
default.q.n3-11-q57-57.why.3: (d) 「チーズケーキの」 is repeated and narrows the scope, whereas the author is trying to broaden it to famous cafés in general.
default.q.n3-11-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (売り場を見て、自分の日常生活との違いを感じたいから。).

Main point and analysis:
The author recounts moving from their inland hometown to the present seaside town. They were extremely surprised by the large fish counter and the wide variety of fish, which made them realize that "different places have different ways of life." Since then, whenever traveling to a new place, the author has made a habit of visiting a supermarket first. By seeing how the displays differ from those in everyday life, the author senses the distance—the difference—from their ordinary life and finds it fascinating. Therefore, choice 4 is the best answer.

Translation of the question:
Why does the author visit a supermarket first when arriving at a travel destination?

Translation of the choices:
1. Because it feels like returning to a beloved hometown.
2. Because they want to see how large the fish counter is and how varied the selection of fish is.
3. Because they want to compare its size with the supermarket they usually use.
4. Because they want to look at the displays and experience how they differ from their everyday life.
default.q.n3-11-q58-58.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage does not mention that the writer feels nostalgic or feels as if they have returned home when entering a supermarket in the tourist destination.
default.q.n3-11-q58-58.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Being surprised by the size and variety of the fish counter was a past experience from when the author moved from the countryside to the present coastal town, as described in paragraph 1. It was not the purpose of visiting a supermarket while traveling.
default.q.n3-11-q58-58.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage does not mention wanting to compare the size or area of supermarkets in tourist destinations with ordinary supermarkets.
default.q.n3-11-q58-58.why.3: (d) Correct. The final sentence of the passage provides the evidence: 「いつも見ているのとは違う売り場の景色から、自分の日常生活との距離が感じられて、楽しくなるからだ。」 (Because seeing a sales floor different from the one I usually see makes me feel the distance—the difference—from my everyday life, which I enjoy).
default.q.n3-11-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The period spent walking along an unlit road on a bright full-moon night without needing to turn on a flashlight.
default.q.n3-11-q59-59.explanation:
- Main point summary: The author and their spouse have a habit of taking walks at night. Normally, when they go far from residential areas and the road is no longer lit, they have to turn on the flashlight they carry. However, on brilliantly bright nights with a full moon, they can clearly see the scenery and their shadows even on an unlit road without turning on the flashlight, creating the feeling of being in a fantastical world different from the daytime. This is the time the author likes best.

- Question translation: The passage says, "the time I like best." What kind of time is this?
- Answer choice translations:
  1. The time spent walking along a lit road without turning on a flashlight on a dark, moonless night.
  2. The time spent walking along an unlit road while turning on a flashlight on a dark, moonless night.
  3. The time spent walking along an unlit road without needing to turn on a flashlight on a brilliantly bright full-moon night.
  4. The time spent walking at night, when they do not walk during the day, while turning on a flashlight on a brilliantly bright full-moon night.
default.q.n3-11-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author likes nights with a full moon, not moonless dark nights. The passage mentions walking along an unlit road, not walking on a brightly lit road.
default.q.n3-11-q59-59.why.1: (b) Incorrect because taking a walk on a moonless night and having to use a flashlight on a dark road is merely an ordinary daily habit, not the time the author likes best.
default.q.n3-11-q59-59.why.2: (c) Correct because the passage states: 「だが、大きな丸い月が出る満月の夜はちょっと違う。明るく輝く月の下では、懐中電灯がなくても周りの景色がわかるのだ。道には私たちの黒い影がはっきり見え、昼間と違う不思議な世界にいる気分になれる。私の最も好きな時間だ。」 (But a full-moon night, when a large round moon appears, is different. Under its bright light, the surrounding scenery can be seen without a flashlight. Our black shadows are clearly visible on the road, making us feel as if we are in a mysterious world unlike the daytime. It is my favorite time).
default.q.n3-11-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not say that the road is not used during the day; it only compares how it feels with how it feels in the daytime. On a full-moon night, there is no need to turn on a flashlight (「懐中電灯がなくても」).
default.q.n3-11-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 3: At 9:00 on the 13th, put on gloves and go to Park No. 1.

default.q.n3-11-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 2: Everyone gives Mr. Nakamura a gift together.

**Summary:**
This is an email from Ishida to everyone in the sales department (営業部の皆様), announcing that Nakamura will leave the company next month. Ishida proposes that everyone in the department jointly give Nakamura flowers and a commemorative gift. Anyone who knows Nakamura’s preferences may offer advice, and those who agree with the proposal should reply within the week; the contribution amount will be announced later.

- 1. Organizing a farewell party for Nakamura.
- 2. Everyone jointly giving Nakamura a gift.
- 3. Each person independently buying and giving Nakamura something he likes.
- 4. Asking Nakamura what gift he would like to receive.

default.q.n3-11-q61-61.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because the passage clearly presents Ishida's proposal to the entire sales department: 「そこで、中村さんに花束と記念品を差し上げたいと思いますが、いかがでしょうか。」 It also mentions shared expenses: 「代金などについては、また後で連絡いたします。」 This shows that the proposal is for everyone to contribute toward giving Nakamura flowers and a commemorative gift.
default.q.n3-11-q61-61.why.2: (c) Answer choice 3 is incorrect because this is a department-wide plan involving shared payment for the gift (代金), not a proposal for each person to buy and give a separate gift (それぞれが買って贈る).
default.q.n3-11-q61-61.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because Ishida asks colleagues who know Nakamura’s preferences to offer advice (「中村さんのお好きなものなど、ご存知の方がいらっしゃったら、アドバイスをいただければうれしいです」), rather than asking Nakamura directly.
default.q.n3-11-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 3: ある食べ物が、ある日急に売れ出すこと (A certain food suddenly starts selling well one day).

- Main point & explanation: The store changed its policy so that before asking customers whether they wanted more fries, employees were required to say, "Thank you," first (「...聞く前に、必ず「ありがとうございます。」と店員に言わせるようにしました」). Therefore, the employees say thank you first and then ask whether the customer would like more fries.
default.q.n3-11-q66-66.why.0: (a) Incorrect because this is the old way of speaking, before the change (「何も言わずに「ご一緒にポテトはいかがですか。」と聞いたとき」); under the new rule, one must say thank you first.
default.q.n3-11-q66-66.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states: 「「ご一緒にポテトはいかがですか。」と聞く前に、必ず「ありがとうございます。」と店員に言わせるようにしました。」 Before asking, “Would you like some fries as well?”, the store required employees to say, “Thank you.” Thus, the employee had to say thank you before offering the fries.
default.q.n3-11-q66-66.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the employee still asks whether the customer would like to buy potatoes; that offer should not be omitted.
default.q.n3-11-q66-66.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the order is reversed from the passage: the rule is to say thank you BEFORE asking whether the customer would like to buy potatoes, not to ask first and thank them afterward.
default.q.n3-11-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (ハンバーガーと一緒にポテトを頼む客が増えたと聞いたから): The author thought so because they heard that more customers had started ordering fries with their hamburgers.
default.q.n3-11-q67-67.explanation:

  1. Because the author heard that the number of customers visiting the hamburger shop had increased.
  2. Because the author heard that the number of customers ordering only hamburgers had increased.

default.q.n3-11-q67-67.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage does not mention an increase in the total number of customers at the restaurant. It only says that the number of customers ordering fries increased (ポテトを注文する客が増えた).
default.q.n3-11-q67-67.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the number of customers ordering additional potatoes increased, not the number ordering only hamburgers.

default.q.n3-11-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The knives from City S are carefully crafted one by one by artisans and are extremely sharp.

  Question: Why does “I” use a knife from City S?

It also says, 「S 市の包丁は職人、つまり...高い技術を持っている人たちが、一本ずつ丁寧に作っているので、...工場で大量に生産された包丁とは全く違うのだ。」 Knives from S City are carefully made one by one by skilled craftspeople, so they are completely different from knives mass-produced in factories.
default.q.n3-11-q68-68.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage states that S-city knives are handmade one by one, completely different from knives mass-produced in a factory (「工場で大量に生産された包丁とは全く違う」).

default.q.n3-11-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The number of knife craftsmen in City S is steadily declining.

default.q.n3-11-q69-69.why.3: (d) Incorrect because paragraph 2 states that City S produces more than 90% of professional knives and that exports overseas have recently increased (「海外への輸出も増えてきた」), not that knife sales have declined.
default.q.n3-11-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The speaker wants them to continue preserving and making knives in the fine traditional way that has been followed up to now.

default.q.n3-11-q70-70.why.0: (a) Incorrect because wanting to make knives for top chefs is the statement of a young apprentice in the article, not the author's wish. The author never says that they want to make knives only for top chefs.
default.q.n3-11-q70-70.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author highly values and wants to preserve traditional craftsmanship, with no intention of suggesting a shift to mass production in factories.
default.q.n3-11-q70-70.why.2: (c) Correct. The final part of the passage states: 「この若い職人たちにも頑張ってもらって、ずっと続いてきた S 市の素晴らしい包丁作りの技術を守っていってほしい。」 (I hope these young craftspeople will also work hard and preserve S City's excellent knife-making techniques, which have been passed down for a long time—that is, maintain the traditional methods unchanged.)
default.q.n3-11-q70-70.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the author hopes that the existing technique will be preserved (「技術を守っていってほしい」), not that knives will be made using a new and different technique.

default.q.n3-11-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ちょうさ because the kanji「調査」(investigation) has the on-reading「ちょうさ」.
default.q.n3-11-q1-1.explanation:
Sentence meaning: First, I will investigate this matter.
• Kanji-based meaning: 調査 means “investigation.”
• Example: 原因を調査する。(Investigate the cause.)
default.q.n3-11-q1-1.why.0: (a) Correct: 「調」is read as ちょう and 「査」as さ, forming 「ちょうさ」, meaning investigation or survey.
default.q.n3-11-q1-1.why.1: (b) Incorrect:「査」is read only as さ, not さつ (easily confused with 察).
default.q.n3-11-q1-1.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「調」 has the long vowel ちょう, not the short sound ちょ.
default.q.n3-11-q1-1.why.3: (d) Incorrect: Both kanji readings are wrong: 「調」 is missing the long vowel (becoming ちょ), and 「査」 has an extra つ sound (becoming さつ).
default.q.n3-11-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 3. しゅるい, because the kanji「種類」is read as「しゅるい」.
default.q.n3-11-q2-2.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “What kinds are there?”
• Kanji-based meaning: 種類 means “type” or “kind.”
• Example: お菓子の種類が多い。(There are many kinds of sweets.)
default.q.n3-11-q2-2.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「類」is read as るい, not れい; it is easily confused with 「例」.
default.q.n3-11-q2-2.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「種」does not undergo rendaku to become じゅ, and the reading of 「類」is incorrectly given as れい.
default.q.n3-11-q2-2.why.2: (c) Correct: 「種」is read as しゅ and 「類」as るい, forming 「しゅるい」, meaning type or kind.
default.q.n3-11-q2-2.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「種」is read with しゅ in this word, not the voiced sound じゅ.
default.q.n3-11-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 2. いわ because the kanji「岩」has the kun-reading「いわ」.
default.q.n3-11-q3-3.explanation:
Sentence meaning: This area has many rocks.
• Kanji-based meaning: 岩 means “rock” or “boulder.”
• Example: 大きな岩に腰掛ける。(Sit on a large rock.)
default.q.n3-11-q3-3.why.0: (a) Incorrect:「かい」is the reading of「貝」(shellfish, shell) or「会」「回」.
default.q.n3-11-q3-3.why.1: (b) Correct:「岩」is read in kun'yomi as「いわ」, meaning a rock or rocky outcrop.
default.q.n3-11-q3-3.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「すな」 is the reading of 「砂」 (sand).
default.q.n3-11-q3-3.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「どろ」 is the reading of 「泥」 (mud).
default.q.n3-11-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 4. こうりゅう, because the kanji「交流」is read「こうりゅう」.
default.q.n3-11-q4-4.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Interact with many people.
• Kanji-based meaning: 交流 means “interaction” or “exchange.”
• Example: 文化交流イベントに参加する。(Take part in a cultural exchange event.)
default.q.n3-11-q4-4.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「交」 is read as こう, not the voiced ごう, and 「流」 requires the long vowel りゅう.
default.q.n3-11-q4-4.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「交」is read with the sound こう, not voiced as ごう like 「合」.
default.q.n3-11-q4-4.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「流」 has the long vowel りゅう, not the short sound りゅ.
default.q.n3-11-q4-4.why.3: (d) Correct: 「交」is read as こう, and 「流」as りゅう, forming 「こうりゅう」(交流, interaction and exchange).
default.q.n3-11-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 3. あずけて, because the verb「預ける」is read「あずける」.
default.q.n3-11-q5-5.explanation:
Meaning: I have already left my luggage at the reception desk.

default.q.n3-11-q5-5.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「とどけて」 is the te-form of the verb 「届ける」 (to deliver, send, or report).

default.q.n3-11-q5-5.why.2: (c) Correct: 「預ける」 is read as 「あずける」, and its te-form is 「あずけて」, meaning to entrust or deposit.
default.q.n3-11-q5-5.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「ととけて」has no meaning and is easily confused with とどけて or とけて.
default.q.n3-11-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ふつう, because the kanji「普通」is read as「ふつう」.
default.q.n3-11-q6-6.explanation:
Sentence meaning: I usually wake up at 7 o’clock.
• Kanji-based meaning: 普通 means “ordinary” or “usual.”

default.q.n3-11-q6-6.why.0: (a) Incorrect: Both kanji are wrong. The word「ふうだん」does not exist;「普通」and「普段」are easily confused.
default.q.n3-11-q6-6.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「普」 is read with the short sound ふ; it does not have the long reading ふう.
default.q.n3-11-q6-6.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「ふだん」 is the reading of 「普段」, meaning usually or ordinarily.
default.q.n3-11-q6-6.why.3: (d) Correct: 「普」(普: ふ) and「通」(通: つう) combine to form「ふつう」, meaning ordinary or normal.
default.q.n3-11-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 2. うたがって, because the te-form of the verb 「疑う」 is 「うたがって」.
default.q.n3-11-q7-7.explanation:
Meaning: I think we should not suspect others without a reason.
• Sino-Japanese reading: 疑 (GI — 疑う: suspect, doubt)

default.q.n3-11-q7-7.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「ことわって」 is the te-form of the verb 「断る」, meaning “to refuse.”
default.q.n3-11-q7-7.why.1: (b) Correct: 「疑う」 is read 「うたがう」, and its te-form is 「うたがって」, meaning to doubt or suspect.
default.q.n3-11-q7-7.why.2: (c) Incorrect:「きらって」is the te-form of the verb「嫌う」(to hate).
default.q.n3-11-q7-7.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「おこって」 is the te-form of 「怒る」 (to become angry) or 「起こる」 (to occur).
default.q.n3-11-q8-8.verdict: The correct answer is 1. るす, because the kanji 「留守」 has the special reading 「るす」.
default.q.n3-11-q8-8.explanation:
Meaning: I will be away from home next week because I am going on a trip.
• Kanji reading: 留守 (りゅうす — being away from home)

default.q.n3-11-q8-8.why.0: (a) Correct: 「留」 is read る and 「守」 is read す, combining to form 「るす」 (being away from home).
default.q.n3-11-q8-8.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「守」is read as す in this word, not しゅ.
default.q.n3-11-q8-8.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「留」 in this word is read as る, not its usual on-reading りゅう.
default.q.n3-11-q8-8.why.3: (d) Incorrect: both readings are wrong for 「留守」; 留 is read as りゅう and 守 as しゅ.
default.q.n3-11-q9-9.explanation:
Meaning: "That's the opposite."
• 逆 means "reverse, opposite."
• Example: 予想と逆の結果になった。(The result was completely opposite to what was expected.)
default.q.n3-11-q9-9.why.0: (a) 「途」 has the on-readings 「ト/ズ」, as in 「途中」 (とちゅう) and 「用途」 (ようと); it is not read as 「ぎゃく」.
default.q.n3-11-q9-9.why.1: (b) 「迅」 has the on-reading 「ジン」 (as in 「迅速」 じんそく), not 「ぎゃく」.
default.q.n3-11-q9-9.why.2: (c) 「逆」 means “opposite” or “contrary,” with the on-reading 「ギャク」, so it fits the context perfectly.
default.q.n3-11-q9-9.why.3: (d) 「造」 is the kanji for “make/create,” with the on-reading 「ゾウ」 (as in 「構造」 こうぞう and 「造船」 ぞうせん); it is not read as 「ぎゃく」.
default.q.n3-11-q10-10.explanation:
Meaning: It is said that the temperature will drop tomorrow morning.
• 低 means "low."
• Example: この山は標高が低い。(This mountain has a relatively low elevation above sea level.)
default.q.n3-11-q10-10.why.0: (a) 「冷」is the kanji used in 「冷たい」(つめたい) and 「冷える」(ひえる), and is not used to write the i-adjective 「ひくい」.
default.q.n3-11-q10-10.why.1: (b) 「低」is the kanji meaning low, with the kun-reading 「ひく・い」(used for temperature, height, or position). Its linking form is 「低く」, so this is correct.
default.q.n3-11-q10-10.why.2: (c) 「底」is the kanji for 底 (そこ) and 海底 (かいてい); there is no i-adjective 「底く」.
default.q.n3-11-q10-10.why.3: (d) 「令」 is the kanji for “command” in 「命令」 めいれい; it is not part of the word 「ひくく」.
default.q.n3-11-q11-11.explanation:
Sentence meaning: During class, we observed the shapes and colors of various flowers.
• Sino-Japanese reading: 観察 (KANSATSU).
• Example: 植物の成長を観察して記録をつける。(Observe the growth of plants and keep records.)
default.q.n3-11-q11-11.why.0: (a) 「観祭」 combines the kanji 観 with 祭 (as in 「祭り」 まつり), forming a word that does not exist in Japanese.
default.q.n3-11-q11-11.why.1: (b) 「視察」is read as 「しさつ」and means an on-site inspection or survey; it is not read as 「かんさつ」.
default.q.n3-11-q11-11.why.2: (c) 「観察」 means observation (read 「かんさつ」), referring to carefully observing a form or change, so it is completely correct.
default.q.n3-11-q11-11.why.3: (d) 「視祭」combines 視 with 祭; it is meaningless and has both incorrect kanji and reading.

Meaning: Mr./Ms. Tamura read the letter and cried.

default.q.n3-11-q13-13.explanation:
Sentence meaning: The fee will increase after 11 p.m.
• Sino-Japanese reading: 以降 (IKŌ: from that point in time onward).

default.q.n3-11-q13-13.why.1: (b) 「以向」 combines 以 with 向, but this word does not exist in Japanese.
default.q.n3-11-q13-13.why.2: (c) 「移降」combines the kanji 移 and 降 and is not an existing Japanese word.
default.q.n3-11-q13-13.why.3: (d) 「移向」combines the kanji for “move” and “direction,” but is not an existing word. It is easily confused with 「意向」(いこう: intention, inclination).
default.q.n3-11-q14-14.explanation:
Meaning: My feelings are very complicated and confused right now.
• Sino-Japanese roots: 複雑 (PHỨC TẠP).

default.q.n3-11-q14-14.why.3: (d) 「複雑」 means “complex” or “complicated,” read as 「ふくざつ」, and is correct in both kanji and context.

Meaning: “While taking a walk through the city during my trip, I happened to run into a former schoolmate, so I was very surprised.”

default.q.n3-11-q15-15.why.3: (d) 偶然 (“by chance”): Means accidentally or coincidentally meeting someone or having something happen, which fits the context perfectly: while walking down the street, the person happens to meet an old school friend again and is very surprised.

default.q.n3-11-q16-16.why.0: (a) カロリー (calorie): the amount of calories or energy in food; it is not used to describe a person’s personality.

default.q.n3-11-q16-16.why.2: (c) ユーモア (humor): a sense of humor, humor. 「ユーモアのある人」 means “a person with a sense of humor” or “a funny person,” which fits perfectly with “is fun to talk to.”
default.q.n3-11-q16-16.why.3: (d) レジャー (leisure): Recreational activities or free time; it is not combined as 「レジャーのある人」 to describe someone’s personality.

default.q.n3-11-q17-17.why.2: (c) 意識 (awareness, consciousness): means awareness, perception, or alertness and does not combine with '行きたい場所の' to express a desire to go somewhere.
default.q.n3-11-q17-17.why.3: (d) 決心 (determination): a person’s firm decision or resolve. It is not used to mean hearing everyone’s determination about the place they want to visit.
default.q.n3-11-q18-18.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 登場 (to appear, to go on stage; for a character to appear in a work).

default.q.n3-11-q18-18.why.0: (a) 登場 (appearance): to appear or make an entrance, as when a character appears in a story, movie, or play. The phrase '物語に登場する人' (people who appear in this story) is completely correct.
default.q.n3-11-q18-18.why.1: (b) 発生 (arise, occur): Used for events or phenomena that arise or occur, such as accidents, incidents, or bacteria. It is not used for a character in a story.
default.q.n3-11-q18-18.why.2: (c) 外出 means going out; it is not used in '物語に外出する'.
default.q.n3-11-q18-18.why.3: (d) 入門 (nyuumon): entering the study of a profession or discipline; an introduction to the basics (not used for characters in a story).

default.q.n3-11-q19-19.explanation:
Meaning: “The shoes I tried on earlier were a little loose, but this pair fits perfectly.”

default.q.n3-11-q19-19.why.1: (b) しっかり: firmly, steadily, seriously (e.g., しっかり掴む: to hold firmly; しっかり勉強する: to study diligently).

default.q.n3-11-q19-19.why.3: (d) そっくり: exactly alike, identical (for example, 父親にそっくりだ—exactly like one’s father).
default.q.n3-11-q20-20.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 配達 (delivery, sending).
default.q.n3-11-q20-20.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “Since I bought too many things, I asked them to deliver my purchases to my home.”
Sino-Japanese reading notes: 配達, 報告, 送信, 訪問.
Common expressions: 配達員 (delivery person), 宅配 (home delivery), 郵便配達 (mail delivery).

default.q.n3-11-q20-20.why.2: (c) 送信: sending data, email, or an electronic message; the opposite of 受信 (receiving).
default.q.n3-11-q20-20.why.3: (d) 訪問 (ほうもん): to visit, call on someone or visit a place, e.g., 訪問客 = visitor.

default.q.n3-11-q21-21.why.1: (b) 受け取った means received or took delivery of something concrete, such as a parcel, letter, or money.
default.q.n3-11-q21-21.why.2: (c) 取り付けた: to install equipment, or to obtain/secure agreement or an appointment.
default.q.n3-11-q21-21.why.3: (d) 引き受けた (undertook, accepted): means to take on or agree to do a task, responsibility, or role such as serving as an emcee (司会). Combined with 頼まれた (was asked by a friend), it creates a complete and natural sentence.
