default.q.n3-11-q31-31.explanation: 「割引」（わりびき）means reducing part of the price or cost from the original amount; discount. It commonly combines with nouns related to prices or money, such as 料金, 値段, and 入場料 (e.g., 割引料金, 2割引). Another example: 学生証を提示すれば、映画のチケットが2割引になります (If you show your student ID, the movie ticket will be 20% off).
default.q.n3-11-q31-31.why.0: "割引" means a monetary discount and is not used for a decline in population; in this case, use "減少している" or "減っている".
default.q.n3-11-q31-31.why.1: 「料金が割引になる」 is a completely natural and accurate collocation, meaning that the ticket price or tuition is discounted when registering as a group.
default.q.n3-11-q31-31.why.2: “割引” is not used for a decrease in body weight; this sentence should use “減って” (体重が少し減ってきた).
default.q.n3-11-q31-31.why.3: “割引” is not used for time; this sentence should use “減っている” or “削られている” (眠る時間が減っている).
default.q.n3-11-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (電車に忘れ物をしたことに気づいた).
default.q.n3-11-q32-32.explanation: 「気づく」（きづく）means to suddenly realize, notice, or discover a fact, event, or change that one had previously overlooked or been unaware of. It commonly follows the patterns ～に気づく / ～ことに気づく. Another example: 自分の間違いに気づいて、すぐに謝った (I realized my mistake and apologized immediately).
default.q.n3-11-q32-32.why.0: 「気づく」means to realize something that had been overlooked or was previously unknown. It is not used for nostalgic feelings when looking at a painting; this sentence should use 「思い出して」 (ふるさとの景色を思い出して).
default.q.n3-11-q32-32.why.1: Because the noise makes it difficult to sleep, do not use "声に気づいて"; 「声が気になって」 (being bothered by or unable to stop thinking about the voice) or 「声がうるさくて」 is appropriate here.
default.q.n3-11-q32-32.why.2: 「忘れ物をしたことに気づいた」 (realized that I had left something behind) is a completely standard usage when discovering something one had not noticed before.
default.q.n3-11-q32-32.why.3: Do not use "気づく" for imagining or thinking about the near future; this sentence should use "考えると" (大学生活のことを考えると、とても楽しみだ).
default.q.n3-11-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (栄養が足りないと).
default.q.n3-11-q33-33.explanation: 「栄養」（えいよう: nutrition, nutrients）refers to the nutrients necessary for the life, growth, and health of living organisms, obtained through eating. Common expressions: 栄養をつける (to nourish oneself), 栄養のバランス (nutritional balance), 栄養不足 (malnutrition). Another example: バランスの良い食事をとって、十分な栄養を摂取することが大切です (It is important to eat a balanced diet and get sufficient nutrition).
default.q.n3-11-q33-33.why.0: The phrase 「栄養が足りない」(lacking nutrients) is precise and natural in the context of eating for health and preventing colds.
default.q.n3-11-q33-33.why.1: A company's sales and profits increase; 「栄養」 (nutrition) is not used here. The appropriate words are 「利益」 (profit) or 「売上」 (sales revenue).
default.q.n3-11-q33-33.why.2: An airplane consumes money or fuel, not “nutrition.” This sentence should use 「費用」(cost) or 「燃料」(fuel).
default.q.n3-11-q33-33.why.3: A lecture provides knowledge and learning value; it does not contain “nutrition.” This sentence should use「学び」or「ためになる内容」.
default.q.n3-11-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (体がふらふらする).
default.q.n3-11-q34-34.explanation: 「ふらふら」 (dizzy, unsteady, staggering / aimless, drifting) describes a loss of physical balance caused by fatigue, fever, or drunkenness, or an aimless mental state or course of action. Common uses include: 頭／体がふらふらする, ふらふらと歩く. Another example: 徹夜で勉強したせいで、頭がふらふらする (I feel dizzy and light-headed because I stayed up all night studying).
default.q.n3-11-q34-34.why.0: “ふらふら” is not used for vegetables that have wilted in the heat. This sentence should use “しおれている” (wilted).
default.q.n3-11-q34-34.why.1: "体がふらふらする" is the standard expression for a body that is staggering, dizzy, or unable to stand steadily because of a fever.
default.q.n3-11-q34-34.why.2: After playing an instrument all day, do not use 「ふらふら」 for tired fingers; use 「指が疲れた」 or 「指がくたくただ」.
default.q.n3-11-q34-34.why.3: When the voice trembles because of stress or nervousness, use 「声が震えた」 (ふるえた), not 「ふらふら」.
default.q.n3-11-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (東京に滞在します).
default.q.n3-11-q35-35.explanation: 「滞在」（たいざい - to stay, temporary residence）refers to staying in a particular area or another country, away from one's usual place of residence, for a set period of time, such as for a business trip or travel. Common expressions include: ～に滞在する, 滞在期間, 滞在先. Other example: 来月、旅行でハワイに一週間滞在する予定です (Next month, I plan to stay in Hawaii for a week on vacation.)
default.q.n3-11-q35-35.why.0: For a train stopping at a platform, use 「停車している」 (ていしゃ) or 「止まっている」, not 「滞在」, which refers to people staying somewhere.
default.q.n3-11-q35-35.why.1: To stop by a café and rest for a while, use 「（喫茶店で）休みませんか」, not 「滞在」, which is generally used for staying in a region or hotel for an extended period.
default.q.n3-11-q35-35.why.2: For a car left at a repair shop, use "預けてあります" (has been left in someone's care) or "置いてあります" (has been left there); do not use "滞在" for objects or vehicles.
default.q.n3-11-q35-35.why.3: 「東京に滞在します」 is completely correct for expressing that a person will stay or reside temporarily in another city or area, Tokyo, for a certain period, one week, because of work.
default.q.n3-12-q36-36.explanation:
- Sentence translation: "I spent a really enjoyable day in Kyoto with a friend from high school."
- Pattern: 「〜（時間）を過ごす」 means to spend/go through a period of time doing something.
- Example: 家族と一緒に楽しい時間を過ごしました。(I spent an enjoyable time with my family.)
default.q.n3-12-q36-36.why.0: (a) 「と」 indicates being together with someone or something, or marks a quotation. It cannot be used with the object indicating the time spent with the verb 「過ごす」.
default.q.n3-12-q36-36.why.1: (b) 「を」: The particle marking the object or period of time affected by the verb 「過ごす」 (楽しい一日を過ごす: spend an enjoyable day).
default.q.n3-12-q36-36.why.2: (c) 「も」 expresses “also” or “to the extent of,” so it sounds unnatural when describing simply having an enjoyable day in this sentence.
default.q.n3-12-q36-36.why.3: (d) 「が」 marks the subject, whereas 「一日」 is a period of time or object of the verb 「過ごす」, not the entity performing the action.
default.q.n3-12-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 1. って.
default.q.n3-12-q37-37.explanation:
- Translation: "A: 'Where did you buy this cake? It's absolutely delicious.' B: 'At a bakery called \"Ribbon\," you know?'"
- Grammar: 「N1 ＋ って ＋ N2」 is the informal spoken form of 「N1 という N2」 (an N2 called or named N1).
- Example: 「さくら」ってカフェで待ち合わせしよう。(Let's meet at a café called "Sakura".)
default.q.n3-12-q37-37.why.0: (a) 「って」: an informal spoken form of 「という」used to state a name or designation (『リボン』っていう店: a shop called “Ribbon”).
default.q.n3-12-q37-37.why.1: (b) 「とか」 is used to list examples (“such as...”); it is not used immediately after a specific proper name before a noun indicating a type.
default.q.n3-12-q37-37.why.2: (c) 「だって」is used to give a reason (“because...”) or mean “even,” and it cannot follow a proper name to modify the noun 「店」.
default.q.n3-12-q37-37.why.3: (d) 「なんか」 introduces an example with a dismissive or uncertain nuance (“things such as...”); it is not used to identify the name of a restaurant.
default.q.n3-12-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 4. いつのまにか.
default.q.n3-12-q38-38.explanation:
- Sentence translation: “When I got on the train, it was still nearly empty, but while I was absorbed in reading, I suddenly realized that it had become packed with people.”
- Vocabulary & Sino-Japanese readings: いつの間にか (いつのまにか: before one realizes it), 満員 (まんいん: full of people, packed).
- Example: 夢中でゲームをしていたら、いつの間にか外が暗くなっていた。(While I was engrossed in playing a game, it had become dark outside before I knew it.)
default.q.n3-12-q38-38.why.0: (a) 「もっと」: Means “more” or “further” and is used to compare degree; it does not express the unnoticed passage of time.
default.q.n3-12-q38-38.why.1: (b) 「いまにも」 means “just about to,” and commonly appears in the pattern 「いまにも〜そうだ」. It does not go with the completed statement 「満員になった」.
default.q.n3-12-q38-38.why.2: (c) 「もしかしたら」means “perhaps” or “possibly” and usually accompanies 「〜かもしれない」to express speculation. It does not fit an event that has already occurred.
default.q.n3-12-q38-38.why.3: (d) 「いつのまにか」means “before one knows it” or “without realizing when,” describing a change that occurs unnoticed because one is deeply focused on something.
default.q.n3-12-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 4. いくつか.
default.q.n3-12-q39-39.explanation:
Translation: I have several frying pans of different sizes at home, but I only use the smallest one.
- Grammar: An interrogative + 「か」 forms an indefinite pronoun or quantifier (いくつかのN / いくつかある = there are several / some).
- Example: 質問がいくつかあります。(I have a few questions.)
default.q.n3-12-q39-39.why.0: (a) 「どれ」 is an interrogative meaning “which one,” used in questions involving a choice; it does not indicate quantity in an affirmative sentence.
default.q.n3-12-q39-39.why.1: (b) 「いくつ」 is an interrogative meaning “how many” or “how many items,” used to ask about quantity.
default.q.n3-12-q39-39.why.2: (c) 「どれか」means “one of them” (choosing one from several), and is not used to indicate multiple objects existing together.
default.q.n3-12-q39-39.why.3: (d) 「いくつか」 means “a few / several” and refers to an unspecified number of objects in an affirmative sentence.
default.q.n3-12-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 見終わったら.
default.q.n3-12-q40-40.explanation:
- Sentence translation: “Morita: ‘Ishiyama, I brought the DVD you said you wanted to watch.’ — Ishiyama: ‘Thanks.’ — Morita: ‘Hayashi wants to watch it too, so could you pass it on to Hayashi after you finish watching it?’”
- Grammar: 「V (ます-stem) + 終わる」 (finish doing something) + 「〜たら」 (after/when; if).
- Example: この本を読み終わったら、貸してください。(Please lend me this book when you have finished reading it.)
default.q.n3-12-q40-40.why.0: (a) 「見たあったら」: The grammar is incorrect. The standard form for a resulting state is 「〜てある」; there is no form 「〜たある」.
default.q.n3-12-q40-40.why.1: (b) 「見ていたら」means “if someone was watching,” which is illogical because the DVD must be watched to completion before handing it to someone else.
default.q.n3-12-q40-40.why.2: (c) 「見終わったら」 means “after finishing watching.” It combines the verb stem, 「終わる」, and 「たら」 to indicate that the completed action must occur before the next action.
default.q.n3-12-q40-40.why.3: (d) 「見続けたら」means “if one continues watching,” which does not fit the context of returning a borrowed disc after watching it.
default.q.n3-12-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 買うことにしている.
default.q.n3-12-q41-41.explanation:
- Sentence translation: “Every year on my birthday, I keep up the habit of buying a book I want to read at that time and placing it on my bookshelf. It is interesting to notice how my taste in books changes.”
- Grammar: 「V-る / V-ない ＋ ことにしている」 expresses a personal habit or rule that one has decided on and consistently follows.
- Example: 健康のために、毎朝ジョギングをすることにしている。(For my health, I make it a habit to jog every morning.)
default.q.n3-12-q41-41.why.0: (a) 「買うはずだ」 expresses a well-founded judgment (“is sure to...”); it is not used to describe the speaker’s own habit or rule.
default.q.n3-12-q41-41.why.1: (b) 「買うことにしている」: Describes a habit or rule that one has decided on personally and continues to follow regularly ("I maintain the habit of buying...").
default.q.n3-12-q41-41.why.2: (c) 「買うところだ」 indicates that an action is about to take place (“be about to buy”), so it does not fit a repeated yearly action marked by 「毎年」.
default.q.n3-12-q41-41.why.3: (d) 「買うようになっている」 expresses an objective change of state or an automatic system, so it is not used for a habit that a person has chosen to adopt deliberately.
default.q.n3-12-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 見つかってよかった.
default.q.n3-12-q42-42.explanation:
- Sentence translation: “A: You said yesterday that you had lost your phone. Have you found it yet? — B: Yes. It had actually fallen inside the car. — A: I see. It's a relief that you found it.”
- Grammar: 「V-て ＋ よかった」expresses happiness, relief, or shared joy about a good result that has occurred.
- Example: 試験に合格できて本当によかった。(I'm really glad I passed the exam.)
default.q.n3-12-q42-42.why.0: (a) 「見つかってよかった」: The pattern 「〜てよかった」 is used to share someone's happiness and express relief ("I'm glad/lucky it was found").
default.q.n3-12-q42-42.why.1: (b) 「見つかるほうがいい」uses the pattern「〜ほうがいい」to give advice (“it would be better to find it”), which is inappropriate when the other person has already found the phone.
default.q.n3-12-q42-42.why.2: (c) 「見つかったようだ」 expresses an indirect inference ("it seems to have been found"); it is unsuitable because the listener has just been directly informed of the result.
default.q.n3-12-q42-42.why.3: (d) 「見つかりそうだった」: Means “was almost found,” which contradicts the fact that the phone was found.
default.q.n3-12-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 3. おっしゃいましたか？.
default.q.n3-12-q43-43.explanation:
- Sentence translation: "Teacher: 'What did your parents say when you told them you were going to study abroad?' - Hana: 'They encouraged me to do my best.'"
- Honorific language: 「言う」 → the respectful form (sonkeigo) is 「おっしゃる」.
- Example: 社長は何とおっしゃいましたか。(What did the company president say?)
default.q.n3-12-q43-43.why.0: (a) 「うかがいましたか？」: 「伺う」 is the humble form of “hear,” “ask,” or “visit” when referring to one’s own action toward the other person. It is not used for the actions of students’ parents.
default.q.n3-12-q43-43.why.1: (b) 「もうしあげましたか？」: 「申し上げる」 is the humble form of 「言う」, used to humble oneself when speaking to a superior. It is not used for the actions of the other person’s parents.
default.q.n3-12-q43-43.why.2: (c) 「おっしゃいましたか？」: 「おっしゃる」 is the special honorific form of 「言う」, used to ask respectfully about Hoa's parents' words.
default.q.n3-12-q43-43.why.3: (d) 「お聞きになりましたか？」: This is the honorific form of 「聞く」 (to hear/ask), so it is unsuitable for asking about someone's words or advice when the reply directly quotes 「頑張れ」.
default.q.n3-12-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 1. までしか.
default.q.n3-12-q44-44.explanation:
- Translation: "Passenger: 'Excuse me, does this bus go to Hanamori Station?' - Driver: 'No, this bus only goes as far as the next bus stop.'"
- Grammar: 「N + までしか + negative V」= only do something as far as N. The pattern 「〜しか…ない」means “only...”.
- Example: この電車は次の駅までしか行きません。(This train only goes as far as the next station.)
default.q.n3-12-q44-44.why.0: (a) 「までしか」combines the endpoint particle 「まで」(up to) with 「しか」, which always accompanies a negative ending such as 「〜いきません」, meaning “goes only as far as the next bus stop.”
default.q.n3-12-q44-44.why.1: (b) 「までだけ」: 「だけ」 generally follows an affirmative form to mean “only”; in this context, it does not go with the negative ending 「いきません」.
default.q.n3-12-q44-44.why.2: (c) 「からしか」: 「から」means “from” (the starting point), so it is semantically incorrect when referring to the destination of a vehicle.
default.q.n3-12-q44-44.why.3: (d) 「からだけ」 is incorrect both in its meaning of the starting point 「から」 and in its combination with a negative predicate.
default.q.n3-12-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 食べようと思って.
default.q.n3-12-q45-45.explanation:
- Sentence translation: “After class, I planned to have lunch, so I went to the university cafeteria, but it was very crowded, so I went to a ramen shop near the university instead.”
- Grammar: 「V-よう (volitional form) ＋ と思う」expresses the speaker’s intention or plan.
- Example: 日本へ行こうと思って、日本語を勉強しています。(I am studying Japanese because I plan to go to Japan.)
default.q.n3-12-q45-45.why.0: (a) 「食べていて」: the progressive form 「〜ていて」indicates that someone is eating, which is illogical because lunch cannot already be in progress before arriving at the cafeteria.
default.q.n3-12-q45-45.why.1: (b) 「食べているのに」 expresses contrast (“even though [someone] is eating”), which is illogical in terms of the action and sequence of events.
default.q.n3-12-q45-45.why.2: (c) 「食べようと思って」: The volitional form is combined with 「〜と思う」(intend to do something), and the ending is changed to 「〜て」 to connect a sentence expressing an intention before going to the restaurant.
default.q.n3-12-q45-45.why.3: (d) 「食べようと思うのに」: The particle 「のに」 expresses surprise or contrast (“although I intended to eat”), so it does not appropriately connect to the planned action 「食堂に行った」.
default.q.n3-12-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 終わってからでも.
default.q.n3-12-q46-46.explanation:
- Translation: The hair salon near my home is open until 9 p.m., so I can still stop by even after I finish work, which is very convenient.
- Grammar: 「V-てから ＋ でも」 = even after doing V / even if it is after doing V, something is still possible.
- Example: 今から準備しても、間に合いますか？ - 今からでも大丈夫です。(Will there still be enough time if I start preparing now? - Starting now is still fine.)
default.q.n3-12-q46-46.why.0: (a) 「終わる前は」 means “before it ends”; this does not make sense because one cannot go get one's hair done while still at work.
default.q.n3-12-q46-46.why.1: (b) 「終わったからは」: This is a grammatically incorrect combination (it should be 「終わってから」), and it lacks the nuance of "even/although" used to emphasize convenience.
default.q.n3-12-q46-46.why.2: (c) 「終わる前でも」means “even before finishing,” which is illogical because one cannot leave before the task is complete.
default.q.n3-12-q46-46.why.3: (d) 「終わってからでも」: The pattern 「〜てからでも」means “even after..., it is still possible to...,” which fits the context perfectly: because the shop is open until 9 p.m., one can still go there even after finishing work late.
default.q.n3-12-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 通ってみたことがある.
default.q.n3-12-q47-47.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: “When I was a high school student, I once tried attending a guitar class, but it was too difficult, so I quit after three months.”
- Grammar: 「V-てみる」 (try doing something) + 「V-たことがある」 (have experienced doing something).
- Example: 一度日本料理を作ってみたことがあります。(I have tried cooking Japanese food once.)
default.q.n3-12-q47-47.why.0: (a) 「通ってみたところだ」: 「〜ところだ」 indicates something that has just happened in the present (“have just tried attending”), so it cannot be used for an event during high school in the past, 「高校生のとき」.
default.q.n3-12-q47-47.why.1: (b) 「通ってみたことがある」combines 「〜てみる」(try doing something) with 「〜たことがある」(have done something before) to express past experience: "I have tried attending school."
default.q.n3-12-q47-47.why.2: (c) 「通っておいたところだ」: 「〜ておく」means to do or prepare something in advance, while 「〜ところだ」indicates that something has just been done. This fits neither the intended preparation nor the past timing.
default.q.n3-12-q47-47.why.3: (d) 「通っておいたことがある」: 「〜ておく」 means to do something in advance as preparation for a purpose, so it is unsuitable for attending piano lessons as an experience or trial.
default.q.n3-12-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 4. なりたいと思っていた.
default.q.n3-12-q48-48.explanation:
- Translation: “When I was young, I used to want to become a singer in the future.”
- Grammar: 「V-たいと思っていた」 expresses a desire or aspiration that one held and maintained for a period of time in the past.
- Example: 昔は医者になりたいと思っていました。(I used to want to become a doctor.)
default.q.n3-12-q48-48.why.0: (a) 「なりたそうだ」: The pattern 「〜そうだ」 expresses an outward impression or inference about another person's desire (third person), so it cannot be used for the speaker's own feelings with 「私」.
default.q.n3-12-q48-48.why.1: (b) 「なることができた」 means “was able to become,” describing a successful event in the past; it does not express a childhood dream.
default.q.n3-12-q48-48.why.2: (c) 「なっていたと思う」: It means "I think I had become...," which is factually and logically incorrect in the context of a childhood dream.
default.q.n3-12-q48-48.why.3: (d) 「なりたいと思っていた」 combines the desire form 「〜たい」 with 「〜と思っていた」, the past progressive, to express a wish that continued or was cherished in the past ("When I was young, I wanted to become...").
default.q.n3-12-q49-49.verdict: Correct order: 3 → 2 → 4 → 1. Choice 4 is placed at ★ (使わせてほしい).
default.q.n3-12-q49-49.explanation:
Complete sentence: 昨日父に、来週友達と旅行に行くので車を使わせてほしいと頼んだが、断られてしまった。
Meaning: Yesterday, I asked my father to let me use the car because I was going on a trip with a friend next week, but he turned me down.
default.q.n3-12-q49-49.why.0: (a) 1. と: The particle quoting the content of the request, placed immediately before the verb「頼んだ」in position 4.
default.q.n3-12-q49-49.why.1: (b) 2. 車を: This object phrase goes with the permission/request expression 「使わせてほしい」(please let me use the car), so it occupies the second position.
default.q.n3-12-q49-49.why.2: (c) 3. ので: It follows the verb 「旅行に行く」 to give the reason (“because I am going on a trip next week…”) and is in the first position.
default.q.n3-12-q49-49.why.3: (d) 4. 使わせてほしい: The causative + てほしい form means “I want someone to let me do something.” It forms「車を使わせてほしい」and occupies position 3 (the ★ slot).
default.q.n3-12-q50-50.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 1 → 3. The ★ position is choice 1 (に対する).
default.q.n3-12-q50-50.explanation:
Complete sentence: 桜大学は学生の働くことに対する考え方についてアンケート調査を行った。
Meaning: Sakura University conducted a questionnaire survey about students’ views on working.
default.q.n3-12-q50-50.why.0: (a) 1. に対する: The structure「Nに対するN」(toward, regarding...) follows「働くこと」and modifies the noun「考え方」(one's views regarding working). It appears in the third position (the ★ blank).
default.q.n3-12-q50-50.why.1: (b) 2. の: The possessive particle connects the noun「学生」to the following phrase「働くことに対する考え方」(“students’ way of thinking about working”), and it is in position 1.
default.q.n3-12-q50-50.why.2: (c) 3. 考え方: The noun is modified by 「働くことに対する」 and appears before 「について」 in position 4.
default.q.n3-12-q50-50.why.3: (d) 4. 働くこと: nominalizes the action of working and comes before 「に対する」 to form 「働くことに対する」, so it belongs in the second position.
default.q.n3-12-q51-51.verdict: The correct order is: 1 → 4 → 2 → 3. The ★ position is choice 2 (ばかりの).
default.q.n3-12-q51-51.explanation:
Complete sentence: 食事のときに買ったばかりの白いＴシャツを汚してしまった。
Meaning: While eating, I accidentally stained the white T-shirt I had just bought.
default.q.n3-12-q51-51.why.0: (a) 1. ときに: The pattern 「Nのときに」 means “when/while...”; combined with 「食事の」, it becomes 「食事のときに」 (“while eating”), and it is in position 1.
default.q.n3-12-q51-51.why.1: (b) 2. ばかりの: The pattern 「V-た + ばかりの + N」 means “just ...,” and follows 「買った」 to modify the noun 「白いＴシャツ」 in the third position (the ★ slot).
default.q.n3-12-q51-51.why.2: (c) 3. 白いＴシャツ: The noun is the direct object of 「汚してしまった」 (“made the white T-shirt dirty”) and comes before the particle 「を」 in position 4.
default.q.n3-12-q51-51.why.3: (d) 4. 買った: The past-form verb comes before 「ばかりの」to form 「買ったばかりの」(just bought), occupying the second position.
default.q.n3-12-q52-52.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 3 → 1. The ★ position is answer choice 3 (一番早く着くのか).
default.q.n3-12-q52-52.explanation:
The complete sentence: 昨日初めて花川駅に行った。花川駅までどの電車で行けば一番早く着くのかわからなくて電車に乗る前に駅員に聞いた。
Meaning: Yesterday was my first time going to Hanakawa Station. I did not know which train would get me there fastest, so I asked a station employee before getting on the train.
default.q.n3-12-q52-52.why.0: (a) 1. わからなくて: The te-form of 「わからない」 (“because I do not know” / “because it is unclear”) appears at the end of the indirect question phrase 「〜のか」 to explain why the speaker asked the station employee; it occupies position 4.
default.q.n3-12-q52-52.why.1: (b) 2. どの電車で: an interrogative phrase indicating the means of transportation (“by which train”), placed immediately after「花川駅まで」in position 1.
default.q.n3-12-q52-52.why.2: (c) 3. 一番早く着くのか: the indirect question clause 「〜のか」(whether one will arrive fastest) directly precedes 「わからなくて」and occupies position 3 (the ★ slot).
default.q.n3-12-q52-52.why.3: (d) 4. 行けば: The conditional「〜ば」form combines with the interrogative in「どの電車で行けば」(“which train should I take?”), and it is in position 2.
default.q.n3-12-q53-53.verdict: Correct order: 4 → 1 → 3 → 2. Choice 3 is placed at ★ (行くんだったら).
default.q.n3-12-q53-53.explanation:
Complete dialogue: A 「ねえ、昨日のパーティーに行く？会場のレストランが駅から遠くてちょっと不便だから行こうか迷っているんだけど」
B 「私、車で行くつもりだからもし行くんだったら乗せていってあげるよ。」
Meaning:
A: "Hey, are you going to yesterday's party? The restaurant where it is being held is far from the station and a little inconvenient, so I am wondering whether I should go."
B: "I am planning to drive, so if you go, I can give you a ride."
default.q.n3-12-q53-53.why.0: (a) 1. もし: The hypothetical adverb “if,” used with the conditional form 「〜んだったら」 that follows, and placed in the second position.
default.q.n3-12-q53-53.why.1: (b) 2. 乗せていって: The verb 「乗せていく」 (to give someone a ride or drive someone somewhere) is combined in te-form with 「あげるよ」 to form 「乗せていってあげるよ」 (“I’ll drive you there”), and occupies the fourth position.
default.q.n3-12-q53-53.why.2: (c) 3. 行くんだったら: The hypothetical structure 「V-る + んだったら」 (“if you are going...”) combines with 「もし」 and precedes 「乗せていって」, so it occupies the third position (the ★ slot).
default.q.n3-12-q53-53.why.3: (d) 4. 行くつもりだから: The structure「V-る + つもりだから」means “because [someone] intends to go...”; combined with「車で」, it forms「車で行くつもりだから」(because I intend to go by car), occupying the first position.
default.q.n3-12-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 2. この.
default.q.n3-12-q54-54.explanation: In the preceding sentence, the author recounts that, because they were busy, they could not clean up, and before they knew it, December had arrived again (そのまま、また12月になってしまいました). Immediately afterward, there is a direct thought in quotation marks 「...」 about their actual situation at that time. In a direct quotation of one's thoughts or words, the こ demonstrative 「この」 is used to refer to the situation currently unfolding for the speaker: 「この状態が続くと...」 (If this situation continues...). Therefore, choice 2 is the most accurate.
default.q.n3-12-q54-54.why.0: (a) 「ある」 (“some” or “a certain”) refers to an unspecified object or state, so it is unsuitable when the speaker is describing their own specific actual condition.
default.q.n3-12-q54-54.why.1: (b) 「この」(this) is a demonstrative from the ko-series, used in direct inner speech or thought (「...」) to refer to the exact situation the speaker is currently facing (“this situation”).
default.q.n3-12-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「その」 (that) belongs to the そ demonstratives and usually points to something just mentioned in indirect narration. However, in the direct quotation of one's thoughts 「...」 about one's own situation, 「この」 is more natural and accurate.
default.q.n3-12-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「あの」(that, over there) belongs to the あ-series and is used when both speaker and listener clearly know the object, typically because it is distant or belongs to the past. It is not used for the speaker's current condition.
default.q.n3-12-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 1. まず.
default.q.n3-12-q55-55.explanation: After deciding to do a thorough cleaning in December last year (去年は12月に大掃除をすることにしました), the author began listing the cleaning tasks in order: first, they threw away all unnecessary items in the house (【20】、家の中の不要品を全部捨てました), then they cleaned the dirt on the windows and the grease in the kitchen (そして、窓の汚れや...), and so on. Therefore, the sequence adverb 「まず」 (first; to begin with) fits the flow of the passage best.
default.q.n3-12-q55-55.why.0: (a) 「まず」 (“first,” “to begin with”) is an adverb used to open a sequence of actions in chronological order, perfectly matching the passage’s list of cleaning steps.
default.q.n3-12-q55-55.why.1: (b) 「または」 (or) presents a choice between two or more options; it is not used to list a sequence of actions.
default.q.n3-12-q55-55.why.2: (c) 「すると」 (“then / immediately afterward”) expresses a subsequent event or an unexpected result following an action or event. It is not used at the beginning of a sequence of cleaning actions.
default.q.n3-12-q55-55.why.3: (d) 「ところが」 means “however” or “nevertheless” and marks a contrast or an unexpected result, so it does not fit a normal continuation of the passage.
default.q.n3-12-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 3. まで.
default.q.n3-12-q56-56.explanation: At the beginning of the passage, the author defines 大掃除 as cleaning places that are not usually cleaned very often (あまり掃除しないところをきれいにすること). The 換気扇 is a place where a lot of grease accumulates, making it difficult to clean, and it is normally left untouched. The particle 「まで」 emphasizes that the action extends even to a particularly difficult object: 「換気扇まで掃除したのは初めてでした」 (It was the first time I had even cleaned the ventilation fan).
default.q.n3-12-q56-56.why.0: (a) 「なら」is used to introduce a topic or assumption ("if it is..."), so it does not express the degree intended in this retelling.
default.q.n3-12-q56-56.why.1: (b) 「でも」 (“even...; even if...”) commonly accompanies examples that present a possibility or a general request. In this context, it does not express the extreme extent of cleaning emphasized by 「まで」.
default.q.n3-12-q56-56.why.2: (c) 「まで」 (“even/as far as”) is a particle expressing an extension of scope to a special or extreme object. “Even the ventilation fan was cleaned” is very natural when describing thorough cleaning.
default.q.n3-12-q56-56.why.3: (d) 「ばかり」 means “nothing but” or “only,” focusing on a single thing. This contradicts the context, in which the author cleans several different things—throwing items away, wiping windows, washing curtains, and so on.
default.q.n3-12-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 迎えることができたと思います.
default.q.n3-12-q57-57.explanation: The passage recounts an experience of cleaning in December of last year (去年の話). After finishing, the house was cleaner and brighter, allowing the author to welcome the New Year (新しい年) in a relaxed state of mind. Because this was a personal experience in the past, the past potential form 「迎えることができた」 must be used, together with 「～と思います」 to express the writer's judgment or feeling. Therefore, choice 4 is the best answer.
default.q.n3-12-q57-57.why.0: (a) 「迎えることができそうです」 means “it seems that [someone] will be able to welcome or reach [something].” It expresses a present or future prediction and does not fit an event that had already been completed last year.
default.q.n3-12-q57-57.why.1: (b) 「迎えることができたらしいです」 (“apparently, they were able to welcome [them]”) uses 「らしい」 to convey an indirect report or conjecture based on an outside source. It is not used for the author’s own direct emotional experience.
default.q.n3-12-q57-57.why.2: (c) 「迎えることができればいいです」 (“it would be good if [someone] could welcome or receive [them]”) expresses a wish about the future, so it does not fit when recounting the result of a past event.
default.q.n3-12-q57-57.why.3: (d) 「迎えることができたと思います」 (“I think I was able to welcome it”) uses the correct past potential form (できた) combined with the speaker’s personal reflection (と思います), expressing the author’s complete experience last year.
default.q.n3-12-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 決められた.
default.q.n3-12-q58-58.explanation: At the beginning, the author explains that they previously avoided the year-end deep cleaning because they disliked cleaning at a time decided in advance by someone else (誰かが決めた時期に掃除をするというのが嫌だった). In the conclusion, after contrasting this with “thinking and deciding for oneself” (自分で考えて決める), the author realizes that occasionally doing something at a “predetermined time” (決められた時期), such as Japan's December deep-cleaning custom, is not necessarily bad. The passive form 「決められた」 correctly modifies the noun 「時期」 as an attributive expression.
default.q.n3-12-q58-58.why.0: (a) 「決めた」 (“decided”—active voice) cannot express a contrast with “deciding for oneself” (自分で決める) stated in the preceding clause.
default.q.n3-12-q58-58.why.1: (b) 「決められた」 (decided or set in advance; passive form) modifies 「時期」 to form "a time period set by someone else or by custom," directly corresponding to 「誰かが決めた時期」 in paragraph 1.
default.q.n3-12-q58-58.why.2: (c) 「決めさせた」 (made/allowed someone else to decide—the causative form) is incorrect in meaning for this context.
default.q.n3-12-q58-58.why.3: (d) 「決めさせられた」(was forced to decide — the causative-passive form) means that someone else made the person make a decision. It does not match the idea that the time had already been predetermined.
default.q.n3-12-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 2: Someone with experience teaching mathematics to exam candidates who can teach twice a week.
default.q.n3-12-q59-59.explanation:
Main point:
A university student is being sought as a private math tutor for a twelfth-grade student preparing for entrance to medical school, at the request of the student's parent, Takashima. The requirements are two sessions per week, two hours per session; on weekdays from 19:00 to 21:00 except Tuesday, and on Saturdays and Sundays from 9:00 to 19:00. No particular department or mathematics major is required, but an cheerful personality and previous experience teaching mathematics to entrance-exam candidates are preferred.

Translation of the question:
Which of the following matches Mr. or Ms. Takashima's wishes regarding the tutor?

Translation of the answer choices:
1. A medical student who can teach on Tuesday and Saturday.
2. Someone with experience teaching mathematics to entrance-exam candidates who can teach twice a week.
3. A mathematics major who can teach for two hours a week.
4. Someone cheerful who can teach from 19:00 to 21:00 on Saturday and Sunday.
default.q.n3-12-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The notice clearly says "学部の希望は特にありません" (there is no particular department requirement) and "平日(火曜以外)" (weekdays except Tuesday), so requiring a medical student and Tuesday lessons is wrong.
default.q.n3-12-q59-59.why.1: (b) Correct. The text states 「回数:週2回」 and 「学部の希望は特にありませんが、受験生に数学の指導をしたことがある...方にお願いしたいです。」 The requester has no specific department requirement but would like someone with experience teaching mathematics to exam candidates.
default.q.n3-12-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage states 「数学が専門でなくてもけっこうです」 and gives the schedule as 「1回2時間」 and 「週2回」—two hours per session, twice a week, or four hours per week. It does not require a mathematics specialist or only two hours of teaching per week.
default.q.n3-12-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage states that on weekends, "土曜、日曜は9時から19時の間で都合のいい時間をお知らせください" (Saturday and Sunday, please specify a convenient time between 9:00 and 19:00). The 19:00–21:00 time slot is available only on weekdays other than Tuesday.
default.q.n3-12-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (プリンタの黒のインク2箱).
default.q.n3-12-q60-60.explanation:
**Summary of the passage:**
This is an email from Honda Midori to the Nakano stationery store reporting that items were missing from an order delivered the previous day. She ordered 1 box of copy paper, 3 boxes of black printer ink, and 1 box of blue printer ink, but the package contained only 1 box of black ink (meaning that 2 boxes of black ink were missing).

**Question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** What was missing?
- **1.** 1 box of copy paper, 2 boxes of black printer ink, and 1 box of blue printer ink.
- **2.** 1 box of copy paper and 1 box of black printer ink.
- **3.** 2 boxes of black printer ink.
- **4.** 1 box of black printer ink.
default.q.n3-12-q60-60.why.0: (a) Incorrect, because one box of copy paper and one box of blue ink were delivered in full; nothing was missing.
default.q.n3-12-q60-60.why.1: (b) Incorrect because no copy paper is missing, and the shortage is two boxes of black ink, not one.
default.q.n3-12-q60-60.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: 「注文したのは、コピー用紙1箱とプリンターの黒のインク3箱と青のインク1箱でしたが、黒のイ ンクは1箱しか入ってしませんでした。」 (The order was one box of copy paper, three boxes of black printer ink, and one box of blue ink, but only one box of black ink was included.) Thus, the missing items were two boxes of black printer ink.
default.q.n3-12-q60-60.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the sender ordered 3 black ink cartridges but received only 1, so the shortage is 2 cartridges, not 1.
default.q.n3-12-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The senior employee feels tense when talking with the narrator, who has just joined the company.
default.q.n3-12-q61-61.explanation:
Summary:
The narrator started working at a new company last week and feels that a senior colleague is frightening because this person always smiles at others but does not smile when speaking with the narrator. Assuming that the senior colleague disliked them, the narrator asked the person sitting nearby and was told that the senior colleague becomes tense when meeting newcomers for the first time and therefore cannot smile; with a little more time, they will get used to each other.

Translation of the question:
According to the person sitting nearby, why does the senior colleague stop smiling when speaking with the narrator?

Translation of the answer choices:
1. Because speaking with the narrator, who has just joined the company, makes the senior colleague tense.
2. Because the senior colleague is worried about the narrator, who has just joined the company.
3. Because the senior colleague does not want to speak with the narrator, who is afraid of them.
4. Because the senior colleague dislikes the narrator, who is afraid of them.
default.q.n3-12-q61-61.why.0: (a) Correct according to the passage. The person sitting nearby says: 「あの人は、初めて会う人が苦手で、緊張しちゃって笑えなくなるんだよ。」 (That person has difficulty with people they meet for the first time and becomes too nervous to smile.) This is consistent with the fact that the narrator only started working there the previous week.
default.q.n3-12-q61-61.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage does not mention that the senior person is worried (心配している) about “me” at all.
default.q.n3-12-q61-61.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage contains no detail saying that the senior person did not want to talk (話したくない) with “me.”
default.q.n3-12-q61-61.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the real reason was stress when meeting new people, and the speaker also realized that they were not actually disliked: 「自分が嫌われているのではないらしいことがわかって、安心した。」
default.q.n3-12-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 聴く音楽に合わせて複数のイヤホンを買って、音楽を楽しむこと.
default.q.n3-12-q62-62.explanation:
**Relevant summary:** The author stops by the headphone counter at a large electronics store and is surprised by the wide variety of headphones. A sales clerk explains that recently many people own several pairs and switch between them depending on the genre of music they are listening to, such as rock or classical music. The author has always listened to music through speakers but now wants to try doing the same thing—owning several headphones and switching between them according to the music genre.

**Question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** What did the author want to try? (何をやってみたくなったのか。)
- **Choice 1:** Buy one expensive pair of headphones to enjoy music compared with the sound from speakers.
- **Choice 2:** Buy one expensive pair of headphones to enjoy various genres of music.
- **Choice 3:** Buy several speakers suited to the genre of music being listened to and enjoy the music.
- **Choice 4:** Buy several pairs of headphones suited to the genre of music being listened to and enjoy the music.
default.q.n3-12-q62-62.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage only mentions headphones costing over 100,000 yen and headphones that are not particularly expensive but still sound very good. The author never says they want to buy expensive headphones to compare them with the sound of speakers.
default.q.n3-12-q62-62.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The author wants to follow the method described by the store employees—owning multiple pairs of earphones and changing them according to the music genre—not buy a single pair for listening to many types of music.
default.q.n3-12-q62-62.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The author has so far listened through speakers (スピーカー), but now wants to try using multiple earphones (イヤホン) suited to different types of music, not buying multiple speakers.
default.q.n3-12-q62-62.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage states: 「店の人によると、最近は、複数のイヤホンを持ち、ロックやクラシックなど聴く音楽に合わせて、使うイヤホンを変える人もいるそうだ。私は今まではスビーカーでしか聞いていなかったが、同じようにやってみなくなった。」 (that is, やってみたくなった). The phrase 「同じように」 directly refers to owning several pairs of earphones and changing them according to the type of music.
default.q.n3-12-q63-63.explanation:
- Main idea: The author sees an advertisement for a photography studio and decides to ask a professional photographer for help because the author wants photographs capturing the natural smile of their four-year-old daughter, but has been unable to take a good picture themselves and feels frustrated.
- Translation of the question: Why did "I" decide to ask a professional photographer for help?
- Translation of the choices:
1. Because I wanted to use a picture of my daughter for a poster.
2. Because my daughter said she wanted a professional photographer to take her picture.
3. Because my daughter liked having her picture taken in the park.
4. Because I could not take a good picture of my daughter's natural smile myself.
default.q.n3-12-q63-63.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the author merely saw the poster at a nearby photo studio and had no intention of using a photograph of their daughter for the poster.
default.q.n3-12-q63-63.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is incorrect because the passage does not mention the daughter saying that she wanted a professional photographer to take her picture.
default.q.n3-12-q63-63.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the passage does not mention the daughter’s interest in taking pictures in the park.
default.q.n3-12-q63-63.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because it accurately quotes the passage: 「娘の自然な笑顔が撮りたいのですが、自分ではなかなかうまくいかなくて、困っていたので。」 (I wanted to photograph my daughter's natural smile, but I could not manage it well myself, so I was having trouble.)
default.q.n3-12-q64-64.explanation:
- **Summary of the relevant passage:** On the day of the photo shoot, the photographer began taking pictures from very close to the little girl as she played on the swing. Noticing that her daughter was rather self-conscious and embarrassed in front of the camera, the mother worried and wondered whether taking pictures that way would produce good photos.
- **Question translation:** What does the phrase "doing it that way" refer to?
- **Answer choices:**
1. Continuing to photograph the daughter while she played on the swing.
2. Starting to take pictures while playing on the swing together with the daughter.
3. Starting to take pictures right next to the daughter, who was conscious of the camera.
4. Continuing to photograph the daughter for nearly...
default.q.n3-12-q64-64.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because “continued taking pictures” happened afterward (「その後もしばらくそのまま撮り続けていました」), whereas the mother became concerned as soon as the photographer began taking pictures close to the child.
default.q.n3-12-q64-64.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the photographer only stood and took pictures of the daughter playing on the swing; he did not play on the swing with her.
default.q.n3-12-q64-64.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because the passage states: 「当日、カメラマンは公園のブランコで遊ぶ娘のすぐ近くで撮り始めました。娘がカメラをかなり気にしていたので、私はそんなやり方でいい写真が撮れるのだろうかと思いました。」 On that day, the photographer began taking pictures very close to the author's daughter as she played on the swing in the park. Because the daughter was paying considerable attention to the camera, the author wondered whether good photographs could be taken that way.
default.q.n3-12-q64-64.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the subsequent photo-taking periods (20 minutes / 1 hour) were not the initial action that made the mother wonder about “doing it that way.”
default.q.n3-12-q65-65.explanation:
- Main point: The photographer explains that the key to capturing natural smiles from young children is to keep taking pictures continuously at first, allowing the children to become accustomed to the camera’s presence and eventually stop paying attention to the lens; the first 20 minutes of shooting serve as preparation for this.
- Translation of the question: The word “工夫” refers to what kind of technique or ingenuity?
- Translation of the choices:
1. Photographing in a familiar place so that the children do not feel stressed by an unfamiliar environment.
2. Trying to take the pictures quickly so that the children do not get bored.
3. The photographer continuing to smile while taking pictures so that the children become accustomed to the photographer.
4. Continuing to take pictures without interruption so that the children gradually become accustomed to being photographed.
default.q.n3-12-q65-65.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the photographer never explains that choosing a familiar location keeps children from feeling tense.
default.q.n3-12-q65-65.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the photographer spent a full hour taking photos and devoted the first 20 minutes to helping the child get accustomed to the situation, completely contradicting the claim that it “did not take time.”
default.q.n3-12-q65-65.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the passage does not mention that the photographer smiled while taking pictures to help the child get used to him.
default.q.n3-12-q65-65.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because the photographer explains: 「『自然な笑顔が撮れるのは、カメラに慣れて意識しなくなってからなんです。はじめの20分はそのための準備です。』」 Natural smiles can be photographed only after the children become accustomed to the camera and stop being conscious of it. The first 20 minutes are preparation for that, meaning that the photographer continues taking pictures until the children become comfortable.
default.q.n3-12-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3: The cheek with sauce on it is on the “right” from my perspective, but on the “left” from my friend’s perspective.
default.q.n3-12-q66-66.explanation:
Main point: When two people sit facing each other (向かい合って), what is “right” from one person’s point of view is “left” from the other person’s point of view. The author saw sauce on the right cheek from their own perspective and said, “You have something on your right cheek,” causing the friend to interpret it as their own right cheek and wipe the opposite cheek.
- Question translation: Why did the author say that it is difficult to accurately convey the “right” one has in mind to another person?
- Answer choices:
  1. Because the cheek with sauce is on the “right” from both the author’s and the friend’s perspectives.
  2. Because the cheek with sauce is on the “left” from both the author’s and the friend’s perspectives.
  3. Because the cheek with sauce is on the “right” from the author’s perspective but on the “left” from the friend’s perspective.
  4. Because the cheek with sauce is on the “left” from the author’s perspective but on the “right” from the friend’s perspective.
default.q.n3-12-q66-66.why.0: (a) Incorrect. If the side were "right" for both people, the friend would have wiped the correct cheek from the beginning; the passage says the friend mistakenly wiped the opposite cheek (反対側のほほをふいた) because the two people were facing each other.
default.q.n3-12-q66-66.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage clearly says that the speaker saw and pointed out the mark on the right cheek ("私から見て右だよ"), not on the left from the speaker's point of view.
default.q.n3-12-q66-66.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage says: 「私が『右のほほにソースがついているよ』と教えたら、友達は反対側のほほをふいた。『あ、そっちじゃなくて、私から見て右だよ。』」. Because they were facing each other, the cheek with sauce was on the right from the speaker's viewpoint but on the friend's left, causing the misunderstanding.
default.q.n3-12-q66-66.why.3: (d) Incorrect because this choice reverses the information in the passage: the mother has sauce on her right from the speaker’s perspective (「私から見て右だよ」), which is the friend’s left.
default.q.n3-12-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is choice 1: The explanation uses things that do not change for anyone.
default.q.n3-12-q67-67.explanation:
Main point: After analyzing relative explanations such as “the side of the heart” or “the hand used for holding chopsticks,” both of which can vary depending on a person’s position or physical condition, the author proposes finding something that does not change for anyone anywhere—something everyone uses to identify directions in the same way—such as directions (“the west cheek”).
- Question translation: The passage says, “It may have conveyed the meaning accurately.” What kind of explanation does “I” think would convey the meaning accurately?
- Answer choices:
  1. An explanation using things that do not change for anyone.
  2. An explanation widely introduced on the Internet.
  3. An explanation using words that refer to parts of the body.
  4. An explanation using things that vary from person to person.
default.q.n3-12-q67-67.why.0: (a) Correct. Evidence: 「では、誰にとっても変わらないものは何だろう。方角なら誰にとってもどんな場所でも変わらない。先日も、『西側のほほ』といえば、正しく伝わったかもしれない。」 The author argues that directions remain unchanged for everyone, so using them to describe a location conveys the meaning accurately.
default.q.n3-12-q67-67.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Explanations found online, such as "the side without the heart" or "the hand used to hold chopsticks," are rejected by the author because they change depending on one's position relative to the other person, handedness, and physical condition.
default.q.n3-12-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Even when body-part terms such as “heart” are used, the orientation is reversed when two people sit facing each other. This does not provide a basis for conveying the author's intended meaning accurately.
default.q.n3-12-q67-67.why.3: (d) Incorrect. "Things that change depending on the person" (人によって変わるもの) are precisely the cause of confusion, which is the complete opposite of what the author discusses ("誰にとっても変わらないもの").
default.q.n3-12-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is answer choice 4: “There’s some sauce stuck to your right cheek, from my point of view.”
default.q.n3-12-q68-68.explanation:
Main point: The author realizes that people do not constantly orient themselves using compass directions (east, west, south, and north) in everyday life, so saying "the west cheek" is impractical. Therefore, the most practical and accurate approach is still to use "left" or "right," while also specifying the relative position from the speaker's viewpoint ("as seen from me" - 私から見て).
- Question translation: If faced with a similar situation to the one from the previous day, what is "I" expected to say in the future in order to communicate clearly and avoid confusion?
- Answer choices:
  1. "There's sauce on your right cheek."
  2. "There's sauce on the cheek on the side where your heart is."
  3. "There's sauce on your west cheek."
  4. "There's sauce on your right cheek from my point of view."
default.q.n3-12-q68-68.why.0: (a) Incorrect. This is precisely the author's original wording, which caused the friend to wipe the opposite cheek (「私が『右のほほにソースがついているよ』と教えたら、友達は反対側のほほをふいた」) because it did not specify whose viewpoint was being used.
default.q.n3-12-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect. In paragraph 2, the author explains that expressions related to the heart are reversed when two people face each other (「向かい合っていると、相手の心臓か私の心臓かで逆になってしまう」).
default.q.n3-12-q68-68.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The author rejects this expression at the end, explaining that people do not usually pay attention to directions in daily life (「私たちはいつも方角を考えて生活してはいないので、実際にはこのような言い方はできそうにない」).
default.q.n3-12-q68-68.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage says: 「結局、相手と自分の位置関係を考えながら、『右』『左』という言葉を使う以外の方法はないだろう」. In Paragraph 1, when the author says 「私から見て右だよ」, the friend immediately understands and wipes the correct spot. Thus, specifying the relative viewpoint communicates the location most accurately.
default.q.n3-12-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 立ったり座ったりしていた人は、体がどこもあまり疲れていなかった.
default.q.n3-12-q69-69.explanation:
Main point: Paragraph 2 explains the results of a study on how the body becomes tired in different postures: people who sit continuously become tired from the neck upward and from the knees upward; people who stand continuously become tired below the knees; and people who alternate between standing and sitting experience the least fatigue throughout the body.
- Question: What can be learned from the interesting website?
- Choice 1: People who sit continuously do not get tired anywhere in their legs.
- Choice 2: People who stand continuously become tired throughout their entire body.
- Choice 3: Regardless of posture, everyone becomes tired throughout both legs.
- Choice 4: People who alternate between standing and sitting are hardly tired anywhere in their body.
default.q.n3-12-q69-69.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the person who sat the whole time became especially tired from the knees upward (「足のひざから上」が特に疲れていた), not because no part of the legs became tired.
default.q.n3-12-q69-69.why.1: (b) Incorrect because someone who stands all day feels tired mainly from the knees downward, while the area from the neck upward is not very tired (「首から上」はあまり疲れていなかった); it is not the whole body that feels tired.
default.q.n3-12-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect because each posture makes a different part tired; there is no information saying that the entire leg becomes tired in every posture.
default.q.n3-12-q69-69.why.3: (d) Correct because the passage clearly states: 「体全体があまり疲れていなかったのは、立ったり座ったりして姿勢を変えていた人だった。」 (The people whose whole bodies were not very tired were those who changed posture by alternating between standing and sitting.)
default.q.n3-12-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 社員の間でコミュニケーションが増えた.
default.q.n3-12-q70-70.explanation:
Main point: Paragraph 3 discusses a company that uses height-adjustable desks for working both standing and seated. Positive changes included fewer employees reporting illness or fatigue, more communication among employees, and shorter standing meetings.
- Question: Which change actually occurred at the company?
- Choice 1: The number of employees with declining health increased.
- Choice 2: Communication among employees increased.
- Choice 3: The number of meetings requiring lengthy discussion increased.
- Choice 4: The number of employees with good posture increased.
default.q.n3-12-q70-70.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage states that the number of people saying they were in poor health decreased (「体の調子が悪いと言う人が減り」), not increased.
default.q.n3-12-q70-70.why.1: (b) Correct because the passage clearly states: 「そのうえ、以前より社員の間でよくコミュニケーションをとるようになったそうだ。」 (“Furthermore, it seems that the employees began communicating with one another more often than before.”)
default.q.n3-12-q70-70.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage says that standing meetings generate more ideas and make meetings end earlier (「会議が早く終わることが多くなった」), not that they take more time.
default.q.n3-12-q70-70.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not mention an increase in employees with good posture.
default.q.n3-12-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 長い時間、座ったままで仕事をしている.
default.q.n3-12-q71-71.explanation:
Main point: The author hopes that their company will also replace its desks because employees currently have to sit and work for hours at a time, causing many of them to suffer from neck, shoulder, and back pain.
- Question: The author says they hope their company will also switch to this type of desk. How do employees currently work at the author's company?
- Choice 1: They alternate between working standing up and sitting down.
- Choice 2: They remain seated and work for long periods.
- Choice 3: They usually work standing up but sit during meetings.
- Choice 4: They usually work sitting down but stand during meetings.
default.q.n3-12-q71-71.why.0: (a) Incorrect because this is a work practice the author read about at another company, not one at the author’s own company.
default.q.n3-12-q71-71.why.1: (b) Correct because paragraph 1 clearly describes the author’s workplace: 「私の会社では、毎日何時間もいすに座って仕事をするので…」(At my company, we sit in chairs and work for many hours every day...).
default.q.n3-12-q71-71.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the author’s company was not simply operating normally.
default.q.n3-12-q71-71.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the company in the passage has not introduced standing desks for meetings or work.
default.q.n3-12-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 姿勢が体や仕事に与える影響.
default.q.n3-12-q72-72.explanation:
Main point: The entire passage focuses on how working posture—sitting continuously, standing continuously, or switching flexibly between the two—affects physical health (aches and fatigue) and work performance (communication and meeting duration).
- Question: What is the topic of this passage?
- Choice 1: The relationship between desk height and chair height.
- Choice 2: The relationship between health and money.
- Choice 3: The effects of posture on the body and work.
- Choice 4: The effects of employees’ opinions on the company.
default.q.n3-12-q72-72.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the article does not analyze the relationship between the height of the desk and the chair.
default.q.n3-12-q72-72.why.1: (b) Incorrect because cost is mentioned only briefly in the final sentence and is not the main theme throughout the passage.
default.q.n3-12-q72-72.why.2: (c) Correct because the passage analyzes how posture (sitting, standing, and alternating between them) affects physical fatigue (paragraph 2), as well as communication and the effectiveness of workplace meetings (paragraph 3).
default.q.n3-12-q72-72.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the author has only decided to try presenting the opinion to the company (「今度、会社に意見を出してみようと思う」). The passage does not discuss the effect of employees’ opinions on the company.
default.q.n3-12-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 2: Write your name at the reception desk before the library, then enter Room 202 by 10:45.
default.q.n3-12-q73-73.explanation:
- Key point summary: The passage requires participants to sign in at the reception desk in front of the library when they arrive at the university in order to receive the materials («大学に来たときに、 必ず図書館前の受付で名前を書いてくだい。資料をお渡しします。»). They must then enter each venue before the starting time of the program they wish to attend («各会場には各プログラムの開始時間までにお入りください。»). According to the schedule, the lecture «2-A. 『経営学入門』» starts at 10:45 and ends at 11:30 in room 202 («202 教室»). Therefore, Chu must sign in at the reception desk in front of the library and enter room 202 before 10:45.

- Question translation: Chu plans to participate only from section “2. Introduction to University Lectures” onward. If Chu wants to attend the lecture “2-A. Introduction to Business Administration,” what must Chu do?

- Answer choice translations:
1. Sign in at the reception desk in front of the library and enter room 101 before 10:00.
2. Sign in at the reception desk in front of the library and enter room 202 before 10:45.
3. There is no need to go to the reception desk in front of the library, but Chu must enter room 101 before 10:45.
4. There is no need to go to the reception desk in front of the library, but Chu must enter room 202 before 10:45.
default.q.n3-12-q73-73.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「10時までに 101 教室に入る」(enter classroom 101 by 10:00) gives the time and location for item 1 (大学紹介 入試の説明), whereas Chu wants to attend lecture 2-A, held in room 202 from 10:45.
default.q.n3-12-q73-73.why.1: (b) Correct. The instructions state: "大学に来たときに、 必ず図書館前の受付で名前を書いてくだい" (When you come to the university, you must write your name at the reception desk in front of the library), and the schedule shows that lecture 2-A takes place in Room 202 from 10:45: "10:45 - 11:30 2-A. 「経営学入門」 202 教室". This is combined with the instruction: "各会場には各プログラムの開始時間までにお入りください" (Enter each venue by the program's starting time).
default.q.n3-12-q73-73.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the notice requires people to write their names at the reception desk in front of the library ("必ず図書館前の受付で名前を書いてくだい"), not says that "there is no need to go"; also, the classroom for item 2-A is Room 202, not Room 101.
default.q.n3-12-q73-73.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The notice requires participants to write their names at the reception desk in front of the library upon arrival at the school ("必ず図書館前の受付で名前を書いてくだい"), so they cannot skip going to the reception desk.
default.q.n3-12-q74-74.verdict: The correct answer is 1: You must email the International Student Office by July 3 at the latest.
default.q.n3-12-q74-74.explanation:
- Main point: In the note (※) in item 3 (進学相談), the notice states that participants who wish to receive an individual consultation with an economics faculty member such as Professor Uehara or Professor Nakano must contact the International Student Affairs Office by email by the deadline of July 3 («先生方への相談を希望される方は、留学生課にメールでご連絡ください。 (7月3日締め切り)»). Applications cannot be made on the day itself («当日の申し込みはできません»). Therefore, if Shin wants to meet Professor Uehara, Shin must email the International Student Affairs Office no later than July 3.

- Translation of the question: Shin wants to receive advice from Professor Uehara under “3-A. Further-education counseling by the International Student Affairs Office.” How must Shin register?

- Translation of the answer choices:
1. Email the International Student Affairs Office no later than July 3.
2. Email Professor Uehara no later than July 3.
3. On the day of the event, tell the reception desk that Shin wants to receive advice from Professor Uehara.
4. On the day of the event, tell Room 101 that Shin wants to receive advice from Professor Uehara.
default.q.n3-12-q74-74.why.0: (a) Correct, because the notice clearly states: "先生方への相談を希望される方は、留学生課にメールでご連絡ください。 (7月3日締め切り)。 当日の申し込みはできません。" (Those who wish to consult with the teachers must contact the International Student Office by email by July 3.)
default.q.n3-12-q74-74.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the text asks the reader to contact the International Student Affairs Office by email (「留学生課にメールでご連絡ください」), not to contact Professor Uehara directly.
default.q.n3-12-q74-74.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage clearly states that applications cannot be made on the day of the event ("当日の申し込みはできません"), so it is impossible to register at the reception desk that day.
default.q.n3-12-q74-74.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the text clearly states that registration is not accepted on the day of the event ("当日の申し込みはできません"). Therefore, one cannot wait until that day to go to Room 101 and state one's preference.
default.q.n3-12-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 2. よやく.
default.q.n3-12-q1-1.explanation:
Meaning: "Please make a reservation for me at 10 o'clock."
- Sino-Japanese reading: 予約 (Yoyaku — reservation, appointment).
- Example: レストランを予約する。 (Make a restaurant reservation.)
default.q.n3-12-q1-1.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「ようやく」is an adverb meaning “gradually” or “finally.” The 予 in this word does not have a long-vowel reading.
default.q.n3-12-q1-1.why.1: (b) Correct: 予 (よ) combines with 約 (やく) to form 予約 (よやく: reservation, advance appointment).
default.q.n3-12-q1-1.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 約 does not have the reading「よく」.
default.q.n3-12-q1-1.why.3: (d) Incorrect: both characters have been given an incorrect long vowel; it is not 「ようよく」.
default.q.n3-12-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 4. わかかった.
default.q.n3-12-q2-2.explanation:
Meaning of the word: "(Once) young / still young."
- Kanji reading and meaning: 若 means young; its kun-reading is わか・い.
- Example: 彼女は実年齢より若く見える。 (She looks younger than her actual age.)
default.q.n3-12-q2-2.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「わるかった」is the past form of the i-adjective 悪い (わるい - AKU: bad, poor).
default.q.n3-12-q2-2.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「さむかった」 is the past form of the i-adjective 寒い (さむい—cold).
default.q.n3-12-q2-2.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「こわかった」 is the past form of the i-adjective 怖い (こわい – frightening, scary).
default.q.n3-12-q2-2.why.3: (d) Correct: 「わかかった」 is the past form of the i-adjective 「若い」 (わかい, young).
default.q.n3-12-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 1. じょうひん.
default.q.n3-12-q3-3.explanation:
Meaning: “He is an elegant / refined person, isn’t he?”
- Sino-Japanese roots: 上品 (じょうひん: elegant, refined, sophisticated). Antonym: 下品 (げひん: vulgar, crude).
- Example: 上品な言葉遣いをする。(Use refined, polite language.)
default.q.n3-12-q3-3.why.0: (a) Correct: 上 (じょう) combines with 品 (ひん) to form 上品 (じょうひん: elegant, refined).
default.q.n3-12-q3-3.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 品 retains the reading 「ひん」 in this word; it does not undergo rendaku to become 「びん」.
default.q.n3-12-q3-3.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 上 has the long-vowel reading「じょう」, not the short reading「じょ」.
default.q.n3-12-q3-3.why.3: (d) Incorrect: both 上 (missing the long vowel) and 品 (incorrect voicing) are wrong.
default.q.n3-12-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 2. たすけて.
default.q.n3-12-q4-4.explanation:
Meaning: "Yamada helped me."
- Sino-Japanese reading: 助 (JO — Kun-reading: たす・ける: to help, rescue).
- Example: 困っている人を助ける。 (Help someone in trouble.)
default.q.n3-12-q4-4.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「とどけて」is the te-form of the verb 届ける (とどける - deliver, send).
default.q.n3-12-q4-4.why.1: (b) Correct: 「たすけて」 is the te-form of the verb 助ける (たすける), meaning to rescue or help.
default.q.n3-12-q4-4.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「うけて」is the te-form of the verb 受ける (うける: to receive, take an exam or medical examination).
default.q.n3-12-q4-4.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「かたづけて」 is the te-form of the verb 片付ける (かたづける, tidy up, arrange).
default.q.n3-12-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 3. みらい.
default.q.n3-12-q5-5.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “Try thinking about the future.”
- Sino-Japanese reading: 未来 (VỊ LAI - みらい: the future).
- Distinction: 「未来」(みらい) generally refers to the broad, objective future, such as the future of humanity or society, or a futuristic world; 「将来」(しょうらい) generally refers to the more personal and immediate future, such as a person’s career or life.
- Example: 明るい未来を信じている。 (I believe in a bright future.)
default.q.n3-12-q5-5.why.0: (a) Incorrect: The reading 「しょらい」does not exist.
default.q.n3-12-q5-5.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「しょうらい」 is the reading of 将来, meaning “the future,” not of 未.
default.q.n3-12-q5-5.why.2: (c) Correct: 未 (み) combines with 来 (らい) to form 未来 (みらい: the future).
default.q.n3-12-q5-5.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 未 is read with the short sound 「み」, not the long vowel 「みい」.
default.q.n3-12-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 1. かくえき.
default.q.n3-12-q6-6.explanation:
Meaning: "This train stops at every station."
- Kanji note: 各駅 (かくえき) means each station or every station.
- Common expression: 各駅停車 (かくえきていしゃ) means a local train that stops at every station along the route.
- Example: 各駅停車の電車に乗る。 (Take a train that stops at every station.)
default.q.n3-12-q6-6.why.0: (a) Correct: 各 (かく, “each”) combines with 駅 (えき, “station”) to form 各駅 (かくえき), meaning “each station” or “all stations.”
default.q.n3-12-q6-6.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 各 is read with the unvoiced sound「かく」, not the voiced「がく」.
default.q.n3-12-q6-6.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 各 is not read as「きゃく」(that is the reading of 客 or 脚).
default.q.n3-12-q6-6.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 各 is not read as 「ぎゃく」; that is the reading of 逆.
default.q.n3-12-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 4. かった.
default.q.n3-12-q7-7.explanation:
Meaning: "Who won?"
- 勝 means "victory, win" (kun-reading: か・つ: to win, to defeat).
- Example: 試合に勝って優勝した。 (I won the match and became the champion.)
default.q.n3-12-q7-7.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「かざった」is the past form of the verb 飾る (かざる - to decorate).
default.q.n3-12-q7-7.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「おった」 is the past form of 折る (おる: to break or fold) or 居る (おる: to be, to stay).
default.q.n3-12-q7-7.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「のこった」 is the past form of the verb 残る (のこる - to remain or be left over).
default.q.n3-12-q7-7.why.3: (d) Correct: 「かった」 is the past form of the verb 勝つ (かつ), meaning to win or triumph.
default.q.n3-12-q8-8.verdict: The correct answer is 1. いんしょう.
default.q.n3-12-q8-8.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "What was your first impression of him?"
- Kanji: 印象 (いんしょう): impression.
- Common expressions: 第一印象 (だいいちいんしょう: first impression), 印象に残る (いんしょうにのこる: to leave a strong impression).
- Example: 彼の笑顔がとても印象的だった。 (His smile left a very strong impression.)
default.q.n3-12-q8-8.why.0: (a) Correct: 印 (いん) combines with 象 (しょう) to form 印象 (いんしょう, impression).
