- Example: どんな製品にも長所と欠点（＝よくないところ）の両方がある。(Every product has both strengths and weaknesses.)
default.q.n3-13-q29-29.why.0: (a) 「よくないところ」means “a bad point, weakness,” which is precisely synonymous with 「欠点」(fault, shortcoming).
default.q.n3-13-q29-29.why.1: (b) Correct: 「いいところ」 means “good point” or “strength” (長所), which is the complete opposite of 「欠点」.
default.q.n3-13-q29-29.why.2: (c) 「好きなところ」 means “a point one likes,” expressing a subjective feeling of liking; it is not equivalent to 「欠点」.
default.q.n3-13-q29-29.why.3: (d) 「好きじゃないところ」means “a part one does not like,” expressing personal dislike rather than an objective defect of an object or product.
default.q.n3-13-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 何も変えないで.
default.q.n3-13-q30-30.explanation:
- Translation: "I copied down exactly what the teacher told me without changing anything."
- Meaning: 「そのまま」usually indicates keeping something in its original state, without changing, adding to, removing, or otherwise altering it (= その状態を変えずに).
- Example: 黒板の字をそのまま（＝何も変えないで）ノートに書き写した。(I copied the writing on the blackboard into my notebook exactly as it was.)
default.q.n3-13-q30-30.why.0: (a) 「何も変えないで」 means “do not change anything; leave it exactly as it is,” which is synonymous with the adverb 「そのまま」.
default.q.n3-13-q30-30.why.1: (b) 「自分の言葉で」 means “in one’s own words,” indicating that it has been rephrased, in contrast to preserving the words exactly as 「そのまま」.
default.q.n3-13-q30-30.why.2: (c) 「急いで」 means “hurriedly” or “quickly”; it describes the speed of an action, not a state in which the content remains unchanged.
default.q.n3-13-q30-30.why.3: (d) 「すこし後で」means “a little later,” indicating when an action will take place; it is unrelated to the meaning “to keep unchanged.”
default.q.n3-13-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 4. アンケートの結果について、今日の会議で報告があった。
default.q.n3-13-q31-31.explanation:
「報告」（ほうこく）means “reporting”—presenting or notifying a supervisor, relevant person, or meeting of the results, progress, work, event, or task completed.
Example: 調査の結果を部長に報告しました。(I reported the investigation results to the department manager.)
default.q.n3-13-q31-31.why.0: The context is incorrect because a weather forecast program conveys forecast information, so 「解説をしている」 or 「伝えている」 should be used instead of 「報告」.
default.q.n3-13-q31-31.why.1: Incorrect because inviting the whole class to a museum is a proposal or invitation, so 「提案」 or 「誘い」 should be used, not 「報告」 (“report”).
default.q.n3-13-q31-31.why.2: Incorrect because expressing a wish to meet someone to apologize calls for 「連絡」, 「申し出」, or 「話」, not 「報告」.
default.q.n3-13-q31-31.why.3: This fits the context because 「報告」 is used to report the progress or results of work or research. 「アンケートの結果について報告がある」 (“There is a report on the survey results”) is a natural and standard collocation.
default.q.n3-13-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 会場は 満員で、座れない人もたくさんいた。
default.q.n3-13-q32-32.explanation:
「満員」（まんいん）means “full, packed, crowded,” and is used for means of transportation (trains and buses) or venues with limited capacity (halls, movie theaters, and stadiums) when they have reached their maximum capacity or have no room left.
Example: 満員電車に乗って通勤するのは大変だ。(Commuting on a packed train is difficult.)
default.q.n3-13-q32-32.why.0: Incorrect because when recruitment has not reached the required number of employees, use 「定員に達しない」or「人数が集まらない」, not 「満員」.
default.q.n3-13-q32-32.why.1: This is incorrect because for roads crowded with people, use 「混雑している」 or 「人が多い」, not 「満員」.
default.q.n3-13-q32-32.why.2: Incorrect because when all participants are present and ready to begin the meeting, 「全員そろった」 is used; 「参加者が満員になる」 is not appropriate.
default.q.n3-13-q32-32.why.3: This fits the context because「満員」describes a venue, room, or vehicle that is completely full to capacity. 「会場は満員」is entirely accurate when many people have no seats.
default.q.n3-13-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 牛乳に卵と砂糖を入れたら、よくかき混ぜてください。
default.q.n3-13-q33-33.explanation:
「かき混ぜる」（かきまぜる）means “to stir or mix thoroughly” by repeatedly moving a utensil such as chopsticks, a spoon, or a stick so that the ingredients blend together. It is commonly used in cooking, mixing drinks, and combining liquids or powders.
Example: スープに塩を入れて、スプーンでよくかき混ぜた。(I added salt to the soup and stirred it well with a spoon.)
default.q.n3-13-q33-33.why.0: Incorrect because when kanji and hiragana are intermingled in a sentence,「混ざっている」is used, not the action of stirring,「かき混ぜる」.
default.q.n3-13-q33-33.why.1: Correct in context because 「かき混ぜる」 means to stir or mix ingredients or liquid evenly while cooking; using it with milk, eggs, and sugar is completely appropriate.
default.q.n3-13-q33-33.why.2: Incorrect because putting an important letter among old books and accidentally throwing it away is expressed with「混ぜて」or「紛れ込ませて」, not「かき混ぜる」.
default.q.n3-13-q33-33.why.3: Incorrect because when international students from many countries study together in one class, 「集まっている」 or 「混ざっている」 is used; 「かき混ぜられている」 is not used for people.
default.q.n3-13-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 火災が 発生したときのために、みんなで避難訓練をした。
default.q.n3-13-q34-34.explanation:
「発生」(はっせい) means "arise, occur, or come about"—it is commonly used for incidents, natural phenomena, accidents, epidemics, insects, or unexpected costs that appear, such as 火災, 事故, 事件, 台風, トラブル, and 費用.
Example: 台風の影響で停電が発生した。(A power outage occurred because of the typhoon.)
default.q.n3-13-q34-34.why.0: Incorrect because a product manufactured or produced in a factory takes 「生産されている」 or 「作られている」, not 「発生」.
default.q.n3-13-q34-34.why.1: Incorrect because newly built hotels are described with 「建設されている」or 「建っている」; 「発生」is not used for constructed buildings.
default.q.n3-13-q34-34.why.2: It fits the context because 「発生」 is specifically used for incidents, accidents, and natural disasters that suddenly occur; 「火災が発生する」(a fire breaks out) is a standard collocation.
default.q.n3-13-q34-34.why.3: Incorrect because when interest or enthusiasm arises, use 「興味がわいた」 or 「興味を持った」, not 「興味が発生した」.
default.q.n3-13-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 1. あの夫妻は、どんなときでもお互いに協力し合って生きてきた。
default.q.n3-13-q35-35.explanation:
「お互いに」（おたがいに）means “one another” or “each other,” describing a reciprocal action, feeling, or interaction between two or more people or sides.
Example: 困ったときはお互いに助け合いましょう。(When we are in trouble, let’s help each other.)
default.q.n3-13-q35-35.why.0: The usage is appropriate because 「お互いに」 expresses a reciprocal action or feeling between two or more people; 「お互いに協力し合う」 ('cooperate and help one another') is a very natural and accurate expression.
default.q.n3-13-q35-35.why.1: Incorrect because when referring to people who rode in the same elevator, use 「一緒に」 or 「乗り合わせた」, not 「お互いに」.
default.q.n3-13-q35-35.why.2: Incorrect because when students are absent one after another due to colds, use 「次々に」or「それぞれ」, not 「お互いに」.
default.q.n3-13-q35-35.why.3: Incorrect because when comparing two cakes and saying that both look delicious, use 「どちらも」 or 「両方とも」; 「お互いに」 is not used for objects.
default.q.n3-14-q36-36.explanation:
- Meaning: I was so tired last night that after dinner, I fell asleep on the sofa without even turning off the lights.
- Grammar: N + も + V-ないで (emphasizes that not even N was done before V).
- Example: 昨日は忙しくて、昼ご飯も食べないでずっと働いていた。(I was so busy yesterday that I worked continuously without even eating lunch.)
default.q.n3-14-q36-36.why.0: (a) Correct. The particle 「も」 combines with the negative form 「〜ないで」 to emphasize extent, meaning “even” or “not even…”.
default.q.n3-14-q36-36.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The particle 「と」 generally indicates doing something together, listing items, a condition, or a quotation; it does not fit here as the emphasized direct object marker.
default.q.n3-14-q36-36.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「消す」 is a transitive verb and normally takes 「を」; when emphasizing the object, 「も」 can be used. 「が」 is not used with a transitive verb in this negative pattern.
default.q.n3-14-q36-36.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The particle 「で」 indicates a means, manner, or place where an action occurs, so it does not fit this position.
default.q.n3-14-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (疲れたとか仕事が多いとか).
default.q.n3-14-q37-37.explanation:
- Meaning: Yamada, who sits next to me, complains a lot. He is always saying things like he is tired or has too much work.
- Grammar: AとかBとか（言う）: "saying things like A and B"; used to list representative examples of someone's words, reasons, or complaints.
- Example: 彼はいつも「時間がない」とか「お金がない」とか文句ばかり言っている。(He is always complaining about things like not having enough time or money.)
default.q.n3-14-q37-37.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The 〜て form connects successive actions or expresses a cause or result; it is not used to list the contents of speech before 「言っている」.
default.q.n3-14-q37-37.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The structure 「〜たり〜たり」normally accompanies 「する」to list actions or states; it does not directly modify 「言っている」in this way.
default.q.n3-14-q37-37.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜し〜し」is used at the end of clauses to list reasons; it does not directly modify the verb「言う」.
default.q.n3-14-q37-37.why.3: (d) Correct. The structure 「AとかBとか言う」 lists examples of things the person commonly says or complains about (“saying things like A and B”).
default.q.n3-14-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (あまりにも).
default.q.n3-14-q38-38.explanation:
- Translation: Today I tried stopping by a newly opened bakery nearby for the first time, but it was so crowded that I had to leave without buying anything.
- Vocabulary / grammar: あまりにも (an emphatic adverbial form of 「あまりに」: excessively, far too; often followed by an unintended negative result).
- Example: その問題はあまりにも難しくて、誰にも解けなかった。(The problem was so difficult that no one could solve it.)
default.q.n3-14-q38-38.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「もっとも」(最も) means “the most” in a superlative comparison, or “however/of course,” and does not directly modify 「込んでいたので」 here.
default.q.n3-14-q38-38.why.1: (b) Incorrect.「せっかく」(折角) means “with considerable effort” or “after going to the trouble,” and commonly appears with「のに」, as in せっかく行ったのに...
default.q.n3-14-q38-38.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「ようやく」(漸く) means “finally,” after a long wait or considerable effort, so it does not fit the meaning of this sentence.
default.q.n3-14-q38-38.why.3: (d) Correct. The adverb「あまりにも」means "excessively / far too," describing a crowd so large that the speaker could not buy anything.
default.q.n3-14-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (にくらべて).
default.q.n3-14-q39-39.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: The Department of International Politics at my university has a higher proportion of international students than other departments.
- Grammar: N + に比べて (にくらべて) (compared with N).
- Kanji vocabulary: 比 (comparison) in 比べる (to compare), and 割合 (proportion, percentage).
- Example: 今年は去年に比べて、雨の日がとても多い。(Compared with last year, there have been many more rainy days this year.)
default.q.n3-14-q39-39.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「〜において」(〜に於いて) means “in, at, or within” a context, place, or field; it is not used for comparison.
default.q.n3-14-q39-39.why.1: (b) Incorrect.「〜によって」(〜に依って) means “depending on,” “because of,” “by means of,” or “due to”; it is not used to compare two objects.
default.q.n3-14-q39-39.why.2: (c) Correct. 「〜にくらべて」(〜に比べて) means “compared with...” and is used to compare one thing with another.
default.q.n3-14-q39-39.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜にしたがって」(〜に従って) means “as... changes” or “in accordance with...”; it is not used to compare the degree of something among departments.
default.q.n3-14-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (やりなおす).
default.q.n3-14-q40-40.explanation:
- Meaning: Yesterday, the sweater I had started knitting a month earlier was finished. Although I made mistakes along the way and had to knit it again several times, I was glad that I finally completed it.
- Grammar: V-stem + 直す (なおす) (do V again after making a mistake, getting confused, or being dissatisfied with the result).
- Example: 間違いが多いので、もう一度やり直してください。(There are many mistakes, so please do it again.)
default.q.n3-14-q40-40.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「やりおわった」(やり終わった) means “finished doing it,” which conflicts with the preceding 「間違えて」(made a mistake partway through).
default.q.n3-14-q40-40.why.1: (b) Correct. 「やりなおす」(やり直す) means “to do over / redo,” which fits the context perfectly: the knitting was done incorrectly halfway through, so it had to be redone several times.
default.q.n3-14-q40-40.why.2: (c) Incorrect.「やっておいた」(〜ておく) means “to do in advance” or “to prepare beforehand,” so it does not fit the context of correcting an error.
default.q.n3-14-q40-40.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「やってあった」 (〜てある) means “had been done in advance” and does not express repeatedly doing something oneself.
default.q.n3-14-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (おかげです).
default.q.n3-14-q41-41.explanation:
- Translation: Teacher: 'Congratulations on getting into university. You worked very hard.' / Student: 'Thank you, teacher. It is all thanks to your constant, careful guidance.'
- Grammar: [Plain form / N + の] + おかげで / おかげだ (thanks to..., resulting in a good outcome).
- Example: 先生方のご指導のおかげで、試験に合格できました。(Thanks to my teachers' guidance, I was able to pass the exam.)
default.q.n3-14-q41-41.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「〜ようです」is used for conjecture (“it seems/appears that...”), not to express gratitude for a favorable result.
default.q.n3-14-q41-41.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜せいです」(〜所為) is used to place blame and indicate a cause leading to a bad result (“it is because of…”).
default.q.n3-14-q41-41.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜はずです」expresses a confident inference based on logical grounds (“it should certainly be...”), so it does not fit an expression of thanks.
default.q.n3-14-q41-41.why.3: (d) Correct.「〜おかげです」(〜お陰) expresses deep gratitude for help that led to a positive result ("thanks to...").
default.q.n3-14-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (使っている).
default.q.n3-14-q42-42.explanation:
- Meaning: My grandmother is still using the vacuum cleaner she bought more than 20 years ago. She says she will not buy a new one until it becomes too broken to use.
- Grammar: まだ + V-ている (still be doing something / continue to maintain a state).
- Example: 10年前に買ったパソコンですが、今でもまだ使っています。(I bought this computer 10 years ago, but I still use it today.)
default.q.n3-14-q42-42.why.0: (a) Incorrect.「使った」 is the simple past and cannot combine with the adverb「まだ」("still...”) to express an ongoing habit.
default.q.n3-14-q42-42.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「まだ使わない」 means “still not use,” which contradicts the fact that the machine was bought 20 years ago and is serving everyday life.
default.q.n3-14-q42-42.why.2: (c) Correct. 「まだ使っている」combines 「まだ」(still) with 「〜ている」to express an action or habit that continues in the present.
default.q.n3-14-q42-42.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「使っていなかった」 is the negative past progressive (“was not using” or “had not been using”), which does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-14-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (いたします).
default.q.n3-14-q43-43.explanation:
- Meaning: Staff: 'Welcome. A party of two?' / Customer: 'Yes.' / Staff: 'This way, please. Allow me to show you to your seats.'
- Honorific language: ご + Group 3 noun + いたします (humble form used for the speaker's action toward the other person).
- Example: 会場まで私がご案内いたします。(Allow me to show you to the venue.)
default.q.n3-14-q43-43.why.0: (a) Correct. 「ご案内いたします」 is humble language formed with 「ご＋noun＋いたします」, used for an employee’s action toward a customer.
default.q.n3-14-q43-43.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「ご案内なさいます」 is respectful language used to elevate another person’s action, so it is not used for the speaker’s own action.
default.q.n3-14-q43-43.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「うかがいます」(伺います) is the humble form of「聞く/尋ねる/訪ねる」(to hear, ask, or visit), and cannot be combined with「ご案内」in this way.
default.q.n3-14-q43-43.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「いらっしゃいます」 is the respectful form of 「行く/来る/いる」; it is not used to form humble language for one’s own actions.
default.q.n3-14-q44-44.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: I love dancing and practice every day. Although many people dance better than I do, when it comes to my love of dancing, I am second to none.
- Grammar: 誰にも + V-ない (not ... anyone; completely negates the object). With 「負ける」, it becomes 「誰にも負けない」: not lose to anyone.
- Example: この秘密は誰にも言わないでください。(Please do not tell this secret to anyone.)
default.q.n3-14-q44-44.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「誰には」 is not a natural combination for expressing complete negation in Japanese.
default.q.n3-14-q44-44.why.1: (b) Correct. The pattern interrogative + 「にも」+ negative form (誰にも〜ない) creates an exhaustive negative. Combined with 「〜に負ける」, it becomes 「誰にも負けない」 (not lose to anyone).
default.q.n3-14-q44-44.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「誰かは」 (“as for someone”) refers to an unspecified person and is not used for an exhaustive negative statement.
default.q.n3-14-q44-44.why.3: (d) 「誰かも」(someone also) cannot function as the object of competition with the verb「負ける」.
default.q.n3-14-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (なるには).
default.q.n3-14-q45-45.explanation:
- Translation: To become a member of Sakura Hotel, there are two methods: "Register through the homepage" or "Register by mail."
- Grammar: V-る + には (to do V / if you want to do V—the following clause states the necessary condition, method, or means).
- Example: 日本語能力試験に合格するには、毎日の積み重ねが必要だ。(To pass the JLPT, daily accumulation of effort is necessary.)
default.q.n3-14-q45-45.why.0: (a) Correct. The structure 「V-るには」 means “in order to / if you want to do V,” and 「会員になる」 is the correct expression for “become a member.”
default.q.n3-14-q45-45.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜よりは」 means “compared with…,” and using 「する」 instead of 「なる」 is unnatural in this context.
default.q.n3-14-q45-45.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜かどうかは」 means “whether ... or not,” which does not fit a following clause presenting two ways of carrying something out.
default.q.n3-14-q45-45.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜することは」 only means “doing…,” and does not express the purpose “in order to become a member.”
default.q.n3-14-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (開こうと思ってから).
default.q.n3-14-q46-46.explanation:
- Meaning: It took more than five years from when I first decided to open my own restaurant until it actually opened, but I am very happy to have a restaurant of my own.
- Grammar: V-ようと思う (intend to do V) + 〜てから...まで (from when... until...).
- Example: 留学しようと思ってから、本格的に英語を勉強し始めた。(After deciding to study abroad, I began studying English seriously.)
default.q.n3-14-q46-46.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「〜思えば」 (the conditional 「〜ば」 form) means “if one thinks that...”; it does not form a “from... until...” time frame with 「〜まで」.
default.q.n3-14-q46-46.why.1: (b) Correct. The structure 「V-ようと思う」 (to intend to do something) combines with 「〜てから」 (since/after) to form 「開こうと思ってから...まで」 (from when I first decided to open the restaurant until...).
default.q.n3-14-q46-46.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜ようになる」 indicates a change in state or ability, and combining it with the conditional 「〜ば」 does not fit the context of a past point in time.
default.q.n3-14-q46-46.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「開くようになる」 indicates a natural change and does not express the speaker’s intention or plan to open a shop.
default.q.n3-14-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (してもらってもいい).
default.q.n3-14-q47-47.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: Maekawa: "Mr. Mori, could I also ask you to sign here on this document?" / Mori: "Oh, I forgot. I will sign it right away."
- Grammar: V-てもらってもいいですか (Could I ask you to do V for me?—a polite and courteous way to make a request).
- Example: すみません、この荷物を少し持ってもらってもいいですか。(Excuse me, could you carry this luggage for a moment?)
default.q.n3-14-q47-47.why.0: (a) Incorrect.「〜てあげてもいいですか」is used when the speaker offers to do something for the other person (“Shall I do it for you?”), whereas here Maekawa wants Mori to sign the document.
default.q.n3-14-q47-47.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜てくれたらいい」expresses the speaker’s wish (“it would be nice if you would...”); it cannot directly form a request question with 「〜ですか」.
default.q.n3-14-q47-47.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜てやる」 is a casual expression used when doing something for someone of lower status or for an animal, so it is not appropriate in workplace communication.
default.q.n3-14-q47-47.why.3: (d) Correct. The pattern 「〜てもらってもいいですか」 is a polite and tactful way to ask someone to do something for you.
default.q.n3-14-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (行かなければならないんです).
default.q.n3-14-q48-48.explanation:
- Meaning: Aoki: "Has Ms. Minami already gone home today?" / Minami: "Yes, I have to pick up my child from daycare later. Please excuse me for leaving first."
- Grammar: V-なければならない (must do V) + んです (used to explain a reason or background to the listener).
- Kanji note: 保育園 means "daycare center."
- Example: これから病院へ行かなければならないんです。(I have to go to the hospital now.)
default.q.n3-14-q48-48.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「〜ているところ」indicates an action happening right now, which conflicts with 「これから」(only now about to leave).
default.q.n3-14-q48-48.why.1: (b) Incorrect. It conflicts with 「これから」 and also incorrectly uses the ending 「ですね」, which seeks agreement and is not used when the speaker is explaining a personal matter.
default.q.n3-14-q48-48.why.2: (c) Correct. 「〜なければならない」 (must do something) combines naturally with 「〜んです」 (to explain a reason or circumstance) when Minami explains why she has to leave early.
default.q.n3-14-q48-48.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The ending 「ですね」 seeks agreement from the other person, so it is inappropriate when explaining one’s own personal reason.
default.q.n3-14-q49-49.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 3 → 4 → 1. The position of the star (★) is 4.
default.q.n3-14-q49-49.explanation:
The complete sentence: なかなか英語の単語が覚えられないので、英語の得意な友達がやっていたように何度も書いてみることにした。
Meaning: Since I could not seem to memorize English vocabulary, I decided to try writing it repeatedly, just as my friend who is good at English had done.
default.q.n3-14-q49-49.why.0: (a) 「ことに」 appears in the fourth position, after 「何度も書いてみる」, and combines with 「した」 at the end of the sentence to form 「〜ことにした」 (decide to do something).
default.q.n3-14-q49-49.why.1: (b) 「やっていた」: occupies position 1, after the subject 「英語の得意な友達が」. It is a verb in the past tense modifying 「ように」 to form a comparison or imitation clause.
default.q.n3-14-q49-49.why.2: (c) 「ように」 appears in the second position (after 「やっていた」), forming 「V-た + ように」, meaning “as / just as someone did.”
default.q.n3-14-q49-49.why.3: (d) 「何度も書いてみる」 occupies the third position (the ★ position, after 「ように」 and before 「ことに」) and describes the specific action the speaker decides to try repeatedly.
default.q.n3-14-q50-50.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 2 → 4 → 1. The star (★) is in position 4.
default.q.n3-14-q50-50.explanation:
Complete sentence: 半年前から毎週見ていた大好きなドラマがとうとう終わってしまった。
Meaning: The TV drama I loved and had been watching every week for the past six months has finally come to an end.
default.q.n3-14-q50-50.why.0: (a) 「とうとう」occupies the fourth position, after the subject 「大好きなドラマが」, and is an adverb meaning "finally," modifying the predicate 「終わってしまった」.
default.q.n3-14-q50-50.why.1: (b) 「見ていた」 occupies the second position (after the adverb 「毎週」), forming the modifying clause 「半年前から毎週見ていた」 for the noun phrase that follows.
default.q.n3-14-q50-50.why.2: (c) 「毎週」is in position 1, after「半年前から」, and is a frequency adverb that directly modifies the verb「見ていた」.
default.q.n3-14-q50-50.why.3: (d) 「大好きなドラマが」: It occupies the third position (the ★ slot), after the modifier 「半年前から毎週見ていた」, and serves as the main subject with the particle 「が」.
default.q.n3-14-q51-51.verdict: The correct order is: 4 → 2 → 1 → 3. The star (★) is in position 1.
default.q.n3-14-q51-51.explanation:
Complete sentence: 大川橋はめがねのような形をしていることから「めがね橋」とも呼ばれている。
Meaning: Because Okawa Bridge is shaped like a pair of glasses, it is also called "Megane Bridge."
default.q.n3-14-q51-51.why.0: (a) 「している」: occupies position 3, the ★ position, after 「形を」 and before 「ことから」. It appears in the fixed expression 「〜形をしている」, meaning “to have the shape or appearance of...”.
default.q.n3-14-q51-51.why.1: (b) 「形を」 occupies position 2, after the modifying phrase 「めがねのような」, and functions as the object of the verb 「している」.
default.q.n3-14-q51-51.why.2: (c) 「ことから」: It occupies the fourth position, following the plain form 「形をしている」, and is the grammar pattern 「〜ことから」, which indicates a reason or origin leading to a name or judgment.
default.q.n3-14-q51-51.why.3: (d) 「めがねのような」 occupies position 1, after 「大川橋は」, and is a comparison phrase modifying the noun 「形」 immediately after it.
default.q.n3-14-q52-52.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 1 → 4 → 3. The position of the star (★) is 4.
default.q.n3-14-q52-52.explanation:
Complete dialogue:
田中:「木村さん、仕事はどうですか。」
木村:「会社に入ってまだ少ししかたっていないのでわからないことばかりですが、毎日楽しいです。」
Translation:
Tanaka: "Kimura, how is your job?"
Kimura: "I have only been with the company for a short time, so there are many things I do not know, but I enjoy every day."
default.q.n3-14-q52-52.why.0: (a) 「ので」: Placed second, after the verb in the short form 「たっていない」, it is a conjunction indicating a cause or reason ("because only a short time has passed...").
default.q.n3-14-q52-52.why.1: (b) 「たっていない」: It appears in the first position after 「会社に入ってまだ少ししか」 and combines with 「しか + negative verb」 to express that only a short amount of time has passed.
default.q.n3-14-q52-52.why.2: (c) 「ばかり」: It appears in the fourth position, after the noun 「わからないこと」 and before 「ですが」, in the pattern 「N + ばかり」, meaning “nothing but / full of.”
default.q.n3-14-q52-52.why.3: (d) 「わからないこと」: It occupies the third position (★, after the cause clause 「〜ので」) and is a noun phrase meaning “things one does not know or understand,” functioning as the complement of 「ばかり」.
default.q.n3-14-q53-53.verdict: The correct order is: 1 → 3 → 2 → 4. The star (★) is in position 2.
default.q.n3-14-q53-53.explanation:
Complete dialogue:
(会社で)
西川:「林さん、来週のセミナーのポスター、知りませんか。さっきまであそこにあった白い段ボール箱に入ってたんですけど、気づいたら箱がなくなってて。」
林:「ああ、山下さんがどこかに持っていきましたよ。」
Translation:
(At the office)
Nishikawa: “Hayashi, do you know where the poster for next week’s seminar is? It was in the white cardboard box over there until a little while ago, but when I noticed, the box was gone.”
Hayashi: “Oh, Yamashita took it somewhere.”
default.q.n3-14-q53-53.why.0: (a) 「まで」: It appears in position 1, immediately after 「さっき」, forming the time expression 「さっきまで」 (until just now / until a moment ago).
default.q.n3-14-q53-53.why.1: (b) 「あった」: It is in position 3 (the ★ position, after 「あそこに」) and is the short past form of a verb modifying the noun 「白い段ボール箱」.
default.q.n3-14-q53-53.why.2: (c) 「あそこに」 goes in position 2, after 「さっきまで」, indicating where an object existed and pairing with the verb 「あった」.
default.q.n3-14-q53-53.why.3: (d) 「白い段ボール箱に」occupies the fourth position, following the attributive phrase 「さっきまであそこにあった」. It combines with the particle 「に」and the following verb 「入ってた」to mean “was placed in a white cardboard box.”
default.q.n3-14-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 案内されました.
default.q.n3-14-q54-54.explanation: The writer is a foreign visitor at a Japanese friend's home. After sitting and talking in the living room, the writer is shown to the next room (隣の部屋に案内されました) by the host. Since the writer is a guest and the recipient of the host's guiding action, the sentence should use the passive form 「案内されました」.
default.q.n3-14-q54-54.why.0: (a) 案内されました: The passive voice (受身) expresses that the writer, a guest, was shown to the next room by a friend or the friend’s mother; it is completely natural and accurate in context.
default.q.n3-14-q54-54.why.1: (b) 案内してあげました describes the speaker kindly showing someone the way. It does not fit because the writer is a guest visiting a friend’s house.
default.q.n3-14-q54-54.why.2: (c) 案内していました: Describes the action of guiding someone in the past, but does not show that the writer was the person being guided into the room.
default.q.n3-14-q54-54.why.3: (d) 案内させてくれました: The causative form combined with くれる means “allowed me to show the way.” This is logically incorrect because the writer was visiting a friend’s house for the first time and could not be the person asking to show the way.
default.q.n3-14-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 1. それに.
default.q.n3-14-q55-55.explanation: Before the blank, the writer gives a first impression of the tatami room: it has a pleasant, relaxing smell of dried grass (とても落ち着きました). After the blank comes another positive impression: the tatami room is cooler than the living room. Since the two clauses present successive positive impressions of the tatami room, the additive conjunction 「それに」 (moreover, in addition) is needed.
default.q.n3-14-q55-55.why.0: (a) それに: A conjunction meaning “furthermore” or “in addition,” used to add a second positive point or impression about the tatami room after the advantage mentioned in the preceding sentence.
default.q.n3-14-q55-55.why.1: (b) 一方 means “on the other hand” or “in contrast,” and is used to compare opposing aspects or different sides. It does not fit a context where information is being added in the same direction.
default.q.n3-14-q55-55.why.2: (c) つまり means "in short" or "in other words." It is used to summarize or restate the preceding idea, not to introduce a new personal impression.
default.q.n3-14-q55-55.why.3: (d) ところが means “however” or “and yet,” indicating an unexpected event. It does not fit a passage that simply lists impressions.
default.q.n3-14-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 2. この部屋.
default.q.n3-14-q56-56.explanation: In the evening, a friend took out bedding from the built-in closet in the tatami room where the two of them were spending time. Since the direct invitation “Let's sleep in this room tonight” was made at the scene while both people were in that room, the ko-series demonstrative for a place where the speaker is present must be used: 「この部屋」.
default.q.n3-14-q56-56.why.0: (a) 部屋: A noun used alone without a demonstrative makes the statement unnatural and leaves it unclear which room is meant.
default.q.n3-14-q56-56.why.1: (b) この部屋: The ko- demonstrative is used for a room where both the speaker and listener are physically present during the direct speech.
default.q.n3-14-q56-56.why.2: (c) あの部屋: The demonstrative あの- refers to a room far from both the speaker and the listener, so it is inappropriate because the two people are inside that very room.
default.q.n3-14-q56-56.why.3: (d) その部屋: The so-demonstrative refers to a room near the listener or to one in an indirect context, so it is unnatural in direct dialogue at the location.
default.q.n3-14-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 4. でしか.
default.q.n3-14-q57-57.explanation: The writer feels somewhat anxious about being invited to sleep on a futon spread over tatami because they have always slept in a bed and have never slept on a floor futon before. To express the limitation "only do V (and have never done anything else)," Japanese uses the pattern 「～しか…ない」. Combined with the location particle 「で」, it becomes 「ベッドでしか寝たことがなかった」.
default.q.n3-14-q57-57.why.0: (a) では: 「ベッドでは寝たことがなかった」 means “I had never slept in a bed,” which is the complete opposite of the context in which the writer feels anxious about sleeping on a futon on a tatami floor for the first time.
default.q.n3-14-q57-57.why.1: (b) でなら: 「ベッドでなら」 means “if it is on the bed,” but it does not form a grammatically appropriate combination with the following negative experiential expression.
default.q.n3-14-q57-57.why.2: (c) でだけ: 「だけ」expresses limitation but generally occurs with affirmative sentences. With the negative experiential expression 「寝たことがない」, the standard pattern 「しか...ない」is more natural.
default.q.n3-14-q57-57.why.3: (d) でしか: Combined with the following negative, it forms the grammar pattern '～しか…ない' (only...), expressing the idea "until now, I have only slept in bed," which explains the cause of the worry.
default.q.n3-14-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 住んでみたいです.
default.q.n3-14-q58-58.explanation: After experiencing daily life and sleeping very well in a tatami room, the writer realized the wonderful qualities of tatami. The final sentence expresses a wish arising from that experience: "I would also like to try living in a house with a tatami room." The pattern 「～てみたい」 (want to try doing something) is the most natural and accurate expression for the conclusion.
default.q.n3-14-q58-58.why.0: (a) 住むならいいです: This means “if you live there, that is fine/good,” expressing a conditional evaluation rather than the writer’s own desire.
default.q.n3-14-q58-58.why.1: (b) 住むつもりだからです includes 「～からです」 to explain a reason, so it is not suitable as the concluding sentence expressing feelings and wishes.
default.q.n3-14-q58-58.why.2: (c) 住んでみたいです: The pattern 「～てみたい」 expresses a desire to try an experience (“I would like to try living...”), making it fully appropriate as the conclusion to a reflective essay about a positive experience.
default.q.n3-14-q58-58.why.3: (d) 住もうとすることです means “the act of trying or intending to live,” which is not appropriate grammatically or pragmatically as a concluding statement.
default.q.n3-14-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 人の名前をすぐに覚えられる点 (the ability to remember people's names immediately).
default.q.n3-14-q59-59.explanation:
**Summary of the passage:**
The author ("I") says that remembering other people's names is difficult. Once, the author felt awkward when someone recognized and called out to them on the street, but the author could not remember that person's name. In contrast, the author's mother could naturally remember someone's name after talking with them briefly, even on the first meeting. The author greatly admires and envies this ability.

**Translation of the question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** What aspect of the mother does 「私」 envy?
  *(What ability of the mother does "I" envy or admire?)*
- **Choices:**
  1. Being able to remember people's names immediately
  2. Being able to quickly spot someone she knows in town
  3. Being able to quickly become friendly with someone she has just met
  4. Not becoming flustered even when she cannot immediately remember someone's name
default.q.n3-14-q59-59.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage states: 「一方、私の母は、少し話しただけの人でも、一度で名前を覚えてしまう。... 私はそんな母がとてもうらやましい。」 (My mother, on the other hand, remembers the name of someone after speaking with them only briefly... I am very envious of her). What the author admires is the mother’s ability to remember other people’s names immediately.
default.q.n3-14-q59-59.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The detail about the street concerns someone else seeing “me,” finding me, and speaking to me (「先日も町で、私を見つけて、私の名前を呼んで 話しかけてくれた人がいたのに」), not the mother’s ability to find an acquaintance.
default.q.n3-14-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage only says that the mother remembers the names of people she has spoken with briefly (「少し話しただけの人でも、一度で名前を覚えてしまう」); it does not mention becoming close to people one has just met.
default.q.n3-14-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The person who became flustered when unable to remember the name was “I” (「私はその人の名前が思い出せなくて慌ててしまった」). The mother remembered the name naturally and quickly; the passage does not say that she became flustered when she forgot it.
default.q.n3-14-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: 第一駐車場と教師用駐車場 (Parking Lot 1 and the teachers’ parking lot).
default.q.n3-14-q60-60.explanation:
**Summary:**
This is a notice from Iwamura University to students who commute by car about the parking-lot repair schedule. During construction, students are asked to park in one of the two parking lots that is not under construction; the faculty parking lot may also be used. The schedule is as follows:
- March 18–19: Construction on Parking Lot 1 (第一駐車場)
- March 20–21: Construction on the faculty parking lot (教師用駐車場)
- March 22–23: Construction on Parking Lot 2 (第二駐車場)
Students must not park in the parking lot of the supermarket "Totetsu" under any circumstances. Therefore, on March 22, when Parking Lot 2 is under construction, students may use Parking Lot 1 and the faculty parking lot.

**Translation of the question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** 3月22日に学生が利用できる駐車場はどこか。 (Which parking lots can students use on March 22?)
- 1. 第一駐車場だけ (Parking Lot 1 only)
- 2. 第一駐車場と教師用駐車場 (Parking Lot 1 and the faculty parking lot)
- 3. 第一駐車場と教師用駐車場とスーパー「東鉄」の駐車場 (Parking Lot 1, the faculty parking lot, and the supermarket "Totetsu" parking lot)
- 4. 第二駐車場だけ (Parking Lot 2 only)
default.q.n3-14-q60-60.why.0: (a) Incorrect because, in addition to parking lot 1 (第一駐車場), students are also permitted to use the teachers’ parking lot (「教師用の駐車場も利用できます」).
default.q.n3-14-q60-60.why.1: (b) Correct because March 22 is the day construction takes place in Parking Lot 2 (「3月22日(金) ~ 23日() 第二駐車場」). Therefore, students should use either of the two lots not under construction, Lot 1 or the teachers' parking lot, as instructed: 「工事期間中は、工事をしていない他の二つの駐車場のどちらかに車をとめてください(教師用の駐車場も利用できます)」.
default.q.n3-14-q60-60.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage strictly prohibits parking in the parking lot of the Totetsu supermarket: 「スーパー「東鉄」の駐車場には絶対にとめないでください」.
default.q.n3-14-q60-60.why.3: (d) Incorrect because Parking Lot 2 was under construction on March 22 (「3月22日(金) ~ 23日() 第二駐車場」), so it could not be used.
default.q.n3-14-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: 新製品発表会の当日に会場で受付をすること (Working at the reception desk at the venue on the day of the new product launch).
default.q.n3-14-q61-61.explanation:
【Summary】
This is an email from Ohnishi to a colleague, Hara, asking for help with the launch event for a new product taking place on the 24th, the week after next. Because attendance is expected to exceed the original estimate, two additional people are needed to handle reception at the venue on the day of the event. After consulting Department Manager Kurokawa, Ohnishi decides to ask Hara and Kimura for help; Kimura has already agreed. Ohnishi will explain the work in more detail next week.

【Translation of the question and answer choices】
Question: What did Ohnishi ask Hara to do?
1. Find someone to help prepare for the new product launch.
2. Work at reception at the venue on the day of the new product launch.
3. Explain the new product launch to Department Manager Kurokawa.
4. Explain the work at the new product launch to Kimura.
default.q.n3-14-q61-61.why.0: (a) Incorrect. Ohnishi was preparing for the event and needed someone to handle reception on the day itself; Ohnishi did not ask Hara to find someone to help with the preparations.
default.q.n3-14-q61-61.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states: 「当日会場で受付をしてくれる人が、あと二人必要になりました。黒川課長に相談した結果、原さんと木村さんに頼もうということになりました。忙しいとは思いますが、お願いします。」 (We need two more people to handle reception at the venue on the day. After consulting Manager Kurokawa, we decided to ask Mr. Hara and Ms. Kimura. I know you are busy, but please help.)
default.q.n3-14-q61-61.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Ohnishi personally consulted Section Chief Kurokawa (「黒川課長に相談した結果」) to ask about someone who could help, rather than asking Hara to explain it to the section chief.
default.q.n3-14-q61-61.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Kimura has already agreed to take on the task (木村さんには、もう引き受けてもらっています), and Ohnishi himself will explain the details next week (詳しいことは来週説明します); Hara is not being asked to explain them to Kimura.
default.q.n3-14-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The child is praised for having many experiences and also scolded for having many experiences.
default.q.n3-14-q62-62.explanation:
【Summary of the main point】
The passage presents the results of a survey on resilience in adult society:
- People who were often praised as children have stronger resilience than those who were praised less often.
- Among those who were often praised, people who were also scolded frequently have stronger resilience than those who were scolded less often.
- People who were rarely praised and rarely scolded have the weakest resilience.
Therefore, people who were both frequently praised and frequently scolded have the strongest resilience.

【Translation of the question】
What kind of child will develop the strongest resilience in society?

【Translation of the answer choices】
1. A child with little experience of being praised and little experience of being scolded.
2. A child with little experience of being praised but much experience of being scolded.
3. A child with much experience of being praised but little experience of being scolded.
4. A child with much experience of being praised and much experience of being scolded.
default.q.n3-14-q62-62.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage clearly states that the group with the weakest ability was the group that received the least praise and the least scolding: 「いちばんこのカが弱かったのは、『ほめられた経験も、しかられた経験も少ない人』だった。」
default.q.n3-14-q62-62.why.1: (b) Inaccurate. The passage indicates that people who receive less praise have weaker abilities than those who receive more praise, and provides no information showing that the group receiving little praise but frequent scolding is the strongest.
default.q.n3-14-q62-62.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage clearly states that among those who were often praised, people who had often been scolded possessed this ability more strongly than those who had been scolded less often: 「『ほめられた経験が多い人』の中では、『しかられた経験が多い人』が、『しかられた経験が少ない人』より、この力が強かったそうだ。」
default.q.n3-14-q62-62.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage states: 「そして、『ほめられた経験が多い人』の中では、『しかられた経験が多い人』が、『しかられた経験が少ない人』より、この力が強かったそうだ。」 (Among people with many experiences of being praised, those with many experiences of being scolded had this ability more strongly than those with few experiences of being scolded.) Combined with the idea that people who are praised often have this ability more strongly than those who are praised less often, we can infer that children who are both praised and scolded frequently have the strongest ability.
default.q.n3-14-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 4: to take the sofa currently in use to the new house.
default.q.n3-14-q63-63.explanation:
Main point: The passage begins by saying that the author’s family is preparing to move next month. Most of the furniture will be taken to the new house, but the couple has given up on taking their favorite sofa because the new house is smaller than the old one.

Question translation:
It says they "gave up," but what did the author give up?

Answer choices:
1. Moving next month.
2. Moving to a house larger than their current one.
3. Taking most of the furniture to the new house.
4. Taking the sofa they currently use to the new house.
default.q.n3-14-q63-63.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author’s family is still moving next month («わが家は来月引っ越しをします»); the plan has not been canceled.
default.q.n3-14-q63-63.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the new house is narrower than the current house, not because they are moving to a larger house («今度の家は今の家より狭いので»).
default.q.n3-14-q63-63.why.2: (c) Incorrect because most of the furniture will still be taken to the new house («ほとんどの家具は新しい家に持っていきます»); the writer is not giving this up.
default.q.n3-14-q63-63.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage directly states: «このソファは、夫も私も気に入っているので、本当は持っていきたかったです。でも、今度の家は今の家より狭いので、あきらめました。» (My husband and I both like this sofa, so we really wanted to take it with us. But the new house is smaller than our current one, so we gave up on it).
default.q.n3-14-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 3: It is possible to sit with good posture.
default.q.n3-14-q64-64.explanation:
Main point: Paragraph 2 clearly presents the couple's views and criteria for choosing a sofa: because of his back pain, the husband places the greatest importance on being able to sit with good posture, while the wife prefers a soft sofa.

Question translation:
What does the husband consider important when choosing a sofa?

Answer choices:
1. The sofa must be soft.
2. The sofa must be somewhat firm.
3. It must allow him to sit with good posture.
4. It must feel pleasant or comfortable to sit on.
default.q.n3-14-q64-64.why.0: (a) Incorrect because liking a soft sofa is the wife’s preference («私は柔らかいソファが好きです»), not a criterion valued by the husband.
default.q.n3-14-q64-64.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage only says that sofas designed to help people sit with good posture tend to be somewhat firm («そういうソファは、少し硬めのものが多い»). This is a characteristic of such sofas, not the husband's main objective.
default.q.n3-14-q64-64.why.2: (c) Correct. Direct evidence from the passage: «夫は腰が悪いので、よい姿勢で座れることが大事だと考えています。» (My husband has back problems, so he believes that being able to sit with good posture is important.)
default.q.n3-14-q64-64.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the feeling of softness/comfort when sitting (「柔らかくて気持ちがいい」) is a comment about the old sofa that suited the wife, not the husband's most important criterion.
default.q.n3-14-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 3: To live without a sofa until finding one that is truly satisfactory.
default.q.n3-14-q65-65.explanation:
Main point: Paragraph 3 explains that the author once considered buying a mediocre sofa but then stopped. The couple decides to patiently live without a sofa for a while until they find one that they genuinely like and that suits them both.

Question translation:
After moving, how does “I” plan to live?

Translation of the choices:
1. Continue using the sofa they currently have indefinitely.
2. Buy the sofa they find acceptable and use it.
3. Live without a sofa until they find one they truly like.
4. Give up buying a sofa and live without one from now on.
default.q.n3-14-q65-65.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the current sofa is not going to be taken along; the plan is to replace it with another one («ソファだけは買い替える予定です / あきらめました»).
default.q.n3-14-q65-65.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author once considered buying the sofa, which seemed acceptable, but ultimately canceled the decision: 「一度はそれを買おうかとも思いましたが、やめました」.
default.q.n3-14-q65-65.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage directly states: «やはり私たちにぴったりのソファが見つかるまで、しばらくはソファのない生活で我慢しようと思います。» (After all, I think we will put up with living without a sofa for a while, until we find one that is just right for us.)
default.q.n3-14-q65-65.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the author did not give up on buying a sofa altogether. The author merely put up with not having one for a while (「しばらくは」), until finding a suitable one (「見つかるまで」).
default.q.n3-14-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 父が中学生になって最初の誕生日の新聞のコピー.
default.q.n3-14-q66-66.explanation:
Summary: The author learned about a service that prints old newspapers and bought one as a birthday gift for their father. At first, the author planned to choose the newspaper from the day their father was born, but ultimately decided on the newspaper from the first birthday after their father entered junior high school.
Question translation: What did "I" give as a birthday gift to my father?
Translation of the choices:
1. A copy of the newspaper from the birthday in the year their father was born.
2. A copy of the newspaper from the first birthday after their father entered junior high school.
3. A copy of the newspaper from the birthday of the year their father wanted.
4. A copy of the newspaper from their father's birthday this year.
default.q.n3-14-q66-66.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author initially intended to choose a copy of the newspaper from the day their father was born, but later changed their mind («初めは父の生まれた日の新聞のコピーにしようと思いましたが... にしました»).
default.q.n3-14-q66-66.why.1: (b) Correct because the text states: 「初めは父の生まれた日の新聞のコピーにしようと思いましたが、父が中学生になって最初の誕生日の新聞にしました。」 The speaker first planned to choose a copy of the newspaper from the father’s birth date, but chose the newspaper from his first birthday after entering middle school.
default.q.n3-14-q66-66.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage does not mention the father having any wishes or requests about which year to choose.
default.q.n3-14-q66-66.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the service the author used was to reprint an old newspaper page («昔の新聞»), not this year’s birthday newspaper.
default.q.n3-14-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 1. お金持ちしか行けない高い店.
default.q.n3-14-q67-67.explanation:
Summary: When reading an old article about a fast-food restaurant opening in central Tokyo, the father recalled that as a child he thought it must be an expensive restaurant that only rich people could enter because it was located in a busy central district, even though it was actually an inexpensive, ordinary restaurant.

Question translation: What impression or image did the father have of the fast-food restaurant when he was a child?
Answer choices:
1. An expensive restaurant that only rich people could visit.
2. A restaurant found everywhere in Japan.
3. A restaurant where one could eat at a low price.
4. A restaurant that even children could easily enter.
default.q.n3-14-q67-67.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage states: 「実は安い店だったのに、父は「そんな場所にできたのだから、お金持ちしか行けない高いレストランなのだろう。」と思ってあこがれたそうです。」 (Although it was actually an inexpensive restaurant, my father thought, “Since it was opened in a place like that, it must be an expensive restaurant that only wealthy people can visit,” and apparently admired it.)
default.q.n3-14-q67-67.why.1: (b) Incorrect because fast-food restaurants were still uncommon in Japan at that time («日本ではまだ珍しかった»); they were not available everywhere.
default.q.n3-14-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the store was actually inexpensive («実は安い店だった»), but when he was young, his father did not know this and thought it was an expensive, high-class restaurant.
default.q.n3-14-q67-67.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the father thought it was an expensive place accessible only to wealthy people, so he did not think children could easily go there to eat.
default.q.n3-14-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 父の子供のころの話が聞けて、父を身近に感じたこと.
default.q.n3-14-q68-68.explanation:
Summary: Thanks to an old newspaper as a gift, the normally quiet father opened up and talked about his childhood memories. This allowed the child to learn more about the father for the first time and feel closer and more connected to him.

Question translation: The passage says, "Thanks to the old newspaper." What happened thanks to the old newspaper?
Answer choices:
1. The child learned about the society in which the father grew up.
2. The child learned for the first time that the father's childhood was different from their own.
3. The child heard about the father's childhood and felt closer to him.
4. The father remembered the child's childhood and felt nostalgic.
default.q.n3-14-q68-68.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage does not emphasize learning about society in the past. Its focus is the child’s pleasure at hearing the father talk about the past and feeling closer to him.
default.q.n3-14-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage does not mention comparing the father's childhood with the child's childhood.
default.q.n3-14-q68-68.why.2: (c) Correct because the passage states: 「父から子供時代の話を聞いたのは初めてでした。父が身近に感じられてうれしかったです。また、こんな話が聞けたらいいなと思いました。昔の新聞のおかげです。」 It was the first time I had heard about my father’s childhood. I was happy to feel closer to him, and I hoped I could hear stories like this again. It was all thanks to the old newspaper.
default.q.n3-14-q68-68.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the father is recalling and reminiscing about his own childhood (「昔の話/父の子供時代」), not the child’s childhood («「私」の子供時代»).
default.q.n3-14-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: The children go out into the schoolyard and play more actively.
default.q.n3-14-q69-69.explanation:
- Main point: Paragraph 2 explains the positive effects of the school switching to a grass field: students go outside and play more actively than when the field was bare soil, the schoolyard temperature does not rise as much in hot weather, and dry soil dust is less likely to blow into nearby homes when it is windy.
- Question translation: What change does the author say occurred when the schoolyard became a grass field?
- Answer choices:
  1. More children who see the grass field feel comfortable.
  2. Children go out to the schoolyard and play more often / more actively.
  3. In summer, the schoolyard temperature rises, making it difficult for children to play outside.
  4. Not only soil from the schoolyard but also dried grass begins to blow into the surrounding area.
default.q.n3-14-q69-69.why.0: (a) Inaccurate because the passage only says that the author found the grassy area very pleasant (とても気持ちがいい); it does not say that more children felt the same way.
default.q.n3-14-q69-69.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states:「芝生にすると、子供たちは土の校庭のときより、積極的に外で遊ぶようになる。」(When the schoolyard is converted to grass, children become more active about playing outside than when it was a dirt schoolyard.)
default.q.n3-14-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect because grass helps prevent the temperature from rising too much in hot weather (暑いときに校庭の気温を上がりにくくしたり...効果もある), rather than raising the temperature and making it difficult for children to go outside.
default.q.n3-14-q69-69.why.3: (d) Inaccurate because the grass prevents dry soil from the schoolyard from being blown by the wind into neighboring homes (校庭の乾いた土が風で近所の家に飛んでいくのを防いだりする効果もある); it does not make dry grass blow away.
default.q.n3-14-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4: Worrying about whether the grass in such a large schoolyard will grow properly.
default.q.n3-14-q70-70.explanation:
- Main point: Section 3 recounts how the author once tried growing grass in the small garden at home, but the grass withered very quickly. As a result, the author became concerned about whether grass would grow successfully when planted over a large schoolyard and decided to investigate personally.
- Question: The phrase “became concerned” appears, but what was the author concerned about?
- Answer choices:
  1. Whether it was a good idea to no longer have a dirt schoolyard.
  2. Whether the movement to cover schoolyards with grass would spread throughout Japan.
  3. Whether grass could be grown successfully in “my” home garden.
  4. Whether grass could grow successfully in a large schoolyard.
default.q.n3-14-q70-70.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author does not wonder or worry about whether losing the dirt court is good or bad.
default.q.n3-14-q70-70.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author does not express concern about whether this movement will spread in Japan.
default.q.n3-14-q70-70.why.2: (c) Incorrect because planting grass in the author’s home garden happened in the past, and the grass already withered (すぐに枯れてしまった). The concern here is about the large schoolyard of the elementary school.
default.q.n3-14-q70-70.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage says: 「あんなに広い校庭を芝生にして大丈夫なのだろうか。ちょっと心配になって、調べてみた。」 (“Would it really be okay to turn such a large schoolyard into a lawn? I became a little worried and decided to look into it.”)
default.q.n3-14-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4: Slow-growing grass does not require much time or money to maintain.
default.q.n3-14-q71-71.explanation:
- Main idea: Paragraph 4 clearly describes two types of grass: Fast-growing grass recovers easily when damaged but requires more time, money, and frequent trimming; slow-growing grass requires less time and money to maintain but is very difficult to restore when damaged. Both types need one month of rest each year, during which no one may walk on them.
- Question translation: Which of the following is correct about the characteristics of the grass?
  1. Fast-growing grass is difficult to restore when its condition deteriorates.
  2. Fast-growing grass does not need a period of rest.
  3. Slow-growing grass needs to be trimmed more frequently.
  4. Slow-growing grass does not require much time or money to maintain.
default.q.n3-14-q71-71.why.0: (a) Incorrect because when the condition worsens, the fast-growing type is easy to recover from (状態が悪くなっても直りやすい), not difficult to recover from (直りにくい).
default.q.n3-14-q71-71.why.1: (b) Incorrect because both types need a resting period of about one month each year during which no one steps on them (どちらの種類の芝生でも、1年に1か月ぐらいは誰も踏まない期間を作り、休ませる必要がある).
default.q.n3-14-q71-71.why.2: (c) Incorrect because it is the fast-growing type that must be cut repeatedly to prevent it from growing too long (長く伸びすぎないように何度も切らなければならず), not the slow-growing type.
default.q.n3-14-q71-71.why.3: (d) Correct. Evidence: 「一方、遅い種類の芝生は、世話をする時間とお金はあまりかからないが、状態が悪くなるとなかなか直らない。」 (On the other hand, slow-growing grass does not require much time or money to maintain, but once its condition deteriorates, it is difficult to restore.)
default.q.n3-14-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The author thinks taking care of the grass is difficult, so if possible, they would like to lend a hand.
default.q.n3-14-q72-72.explanation:
- Main point: The final section explains that schools that successfully maintain grassy grounds generally do so with the help of local residents. The author believes that the nearby elementary school must also be looking for volunteers and wants to help create an active, safe playground for the children.
- Question: What is "I" currently thinking about the "grassy school grounds" at the nearby elementary school?
- Answer choices:
  1. Maintaining grass is very difficult, so the author wants the school to change the grounds back to dirt.
  2. Maintaining the grass alone is very difficult, so the author wants to recruit people to help.
  3. Maintaining the grass is very difficult, so the author would like to help if possible.
  4. It is too difficult for adults alone to maintain the grass, so the author wants children to help as well.
default.q.n3-14-q72-72.why.0: (a) Inaccurate because the author wants to support care for the children so that they have a good playground, not move the school to a dirt field.
default.q.n3-14-q72-72.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author guessed that the elementary school must be looking for volunteers (「募集しているに違いない」), not that the author was recruiting someone to help them.
default.q.n3-14-q72-72.why.2: (c) Correct. Quotation: 「子供たちが元気に遊べる校庭が作れるよう、私も協力できたらいいと思っている。」 (“I think it would be good if I could also help so that a schoolyard where children can play energetically can be created.”)
default.q.n3-14-q72-72.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the author wants local residents to help the children have fun; the author does not say that the children should participate in taking care of the grass.
default.q.n3-14-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 毎朝起きるのが大変だったが、無理をしないように簡単な弁当を作っていた。
default.q.n3-14-q73-73.explanation:
Main point: Paragraph 1 describes the author's early days of making boxed lunches to take to work. Since the author was not used to getting up early and was not good at cooking, they did not overexert themselves, but simply made basic lunches from leftovers from the previous evening. The only goal at that point was to maintain the habit.

Question and answer choices:
- Question: Which of the following is true about the author's situation when they had just started making boxed lunches?
- 1. Because they were good at cooking, they got up early every morning to make elaborate boxed lunches.
- 2. Although getting up early every morning was difficult, they made simple boxed lunches so as not to overexert themselves.
- 3. To achieve better nutritional balance, they used many kinds of vegetables from the very beginning.
- 4. They set the goal of making attractive boxed lunches so that their coworkers would praise them.
default.q.n3-14-q73-73.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage clearly states that the author is not good at cooking (料理が得意ではない) and only makes a simple lunch box from the previous night’s leftovers, not an elaborate lunch box (手の込んだ弁当).
default.q.n3-14-q73-73.why.1: (b) Correct. Evidence from the passage: 「最初は毎朝早く起きるのが大変で、前の晩の残りのおかずを詰めるだけの簡単なものばかりだった。料理が得意ではないので、無理をせず「続けること」だけを目標にしていた。」 At first, getting up early every morning was difficult, so the author made simple lunch boxes by filling them with leftovers from the previous evening and set only the goal of continuing without forcing the process.
default.q.n3-14-q73-73.why.2: (c) Incorrect because paying attention to nutritional balance was a positive change that occurred after maintaining the habit for some time (毎日続けているうちに... 栄養のバランスを気にするようになった), not something done from the beginning (最初から).
default.q.n3-14-q73-73.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the author's initial goal was simply to avoid forcing themself and to keep doing it (無理をせず「続けること」だけを目標にしていた). Being praised by colleagues was a later result, not the original goal.
default.q.n3-14-q74-74.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 栄養バランスに気をつけて食べ過ぎを防げるようになり、同僚との会話も増えた。
default.q.n3-14-q74-74.explanation:
The second and third paragraphs clearly describe the positive changes after regularly making boxed lunches: in terms of health, the author pays more attention to nutritional balance and controls portion sizes to avoid overeating; in terms of communication, the boxed lunches became a topic that helped coworkers start conversations, thereby strengthening interaction at the company.

Question and answer choices:
- Question: Apart from saving money, what positive changes did regularly making boxed lunches bring to “me”?
- 1. Eating out and using convenience stores became more frequent, allowing me to eat whatever I liked.
- 2. Since my cooking skills improved, I began making boxed lunches for my coworkers.
- 3. I learned to pay attention to nutritional balance, avoided overeating, and had more conversations with my coworkers.
- 4. Having become accustomed to living alone, getting up early every morning was no longer difficult at all.
default.q.n3-14-q74-74.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage states that eating out and buying convenience-store boxed meals were former habits (以前は外食やコンビニ弁当ばかりで), not a positive change achieved after making boxed lunches.
default.q.n3-14-q74-74.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage only says that a coworker started a conversation and offered praise during the lunch break; it does not mention the author making a boxed lunch for the coworker.
default.q.n3-14-q74-74.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: 「自分で作ることで栄養のバランスを気にするようになった。また、残さないように食べる量を調整できるので、食べ過ぎることもなくなった。さらに、会社の昼休みに同僚から...声をかけられることが増え、会話のきっかけにもなっている。」 Making one’s own lunch encouraged attention to nutritional balance, made it possible to control portion sizes and avoid overeating, and created more opportunities to talk with coworkers.
default.q.n3-14-q74-74.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not mention that getting up early every morning is no longer difficult at all.
default.q.n3-14-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 2. そつぎょう.
default.q.n3-14-q1-1.explanation:
Meaning: My son will graduate next year.
・Kanji note: 卒 (graduation) + 業 (study/work) → 卒業 (そつぎょう: graduation).
・Example: 来年の三月に大学を卒業する予定です。(I plan to graduate from university next March.)
default.q.n3-14-q1-1.why.0: (a) さつきょう: both readings are incorrect: 卒 is read as そつ and 業 as ぎょう, with rendaku voicing.
default.q.n3-14-q1-1.why.1: (b) そつぎょう: Correct. 「卒業」 has the standard on-reading 「そつぎょう」.
default.q.n3-14-q1-1.why.2: (c) そつきょう: The error is in 「業」, which is read with a voiced sound as ぎょう, not きょう.
default.q.n3-14-q1-1.why.3: (d) さつぎょう: The error is in 「卒」, which is correctly read as そつ, not さつ.
default.q.n3-14-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 4. そうだん.
default.q.n3-14-q2-2.explanation:
Meaning: I discussed/studied abroad plans with my teacher.
・Kanji components: 相 (SO/SŌ) + 談 (DAN) → 相談 (そうだん: to discuss, consult, ask for advice).
・Example: 困ったときは、いつでも相談してください。(When you have a problem, please feel free to consult me anytime.)
default.q.n3-14-q2-2.why.0: (a) しょうたん: Both「相」(read as そう) and「談」(read as だん) are incorrect.
default.q.n3-14-q2-2.why.1: (b) しょうだん: The error is in 「相」, which is read そう, not しょう. 「商談 - しょうだん」 means business negotiations.
default.q.n3-14-q2-2.why.2: (c) そうたん: Incorrect because 談 is read with rendaku as だん, not たん.
default.q.n3-14-q2-2.why.3: (d) そうだん: Correct. The standard reading of 「相談」is「そうだん」.
default.q.n3-14-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 1. たしか.
default.q.n3-14-q3-3.explanation:
Meaning: I clearly remember putting it in my bag.
・Kanji note: 確 (かく) → 確か (たしか: certain, exact) / 確かに (たしかに: certainly, indeed).
・Example: 確か彼とは先月会ったはずです。(I am certain I met him last month.)
default.q.n3-14-q3-3.why.0: (a) たしか: Correct. 「確か」 is read with the kun-reading 「たしか」.
default.q.n3-14-q3-3.why.1: (b) しずか: Incorrect. 「しずか」 is the reading of the na-adjective 「静か」 (quiet, peaceful).
default.q.n3-14-q3-3.why.2: (c) たじか: Incorrect reading; there is no voiced sound change to「じ」.
default.q.n3-14-q3-3.why.3: (d) しすか: The reading is completely incorrect.
default.q.n3-14-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 2. あそぶ.
default.q.n3-14-q4-4.explanation:
Meaning: "I can hear the children playing."
・遊 means to play, as in 遊ぶ (あそぶ).
・Example: 週末は友達と公園で遊びました。(I played in the park with my friends over the weekend.)
default.q.n3-14-q4-4.why.0: (a) よぶ: Incorrect.「よぶ」is the verb「呼ぶ」(to call).
default.q.n3-14-q4-4.why.1: (b) あそぶ: Correct.「遊ぶ」(to play, have fun) is correctly read as「あそぶ」.
default.q.n3-14-q4-4.why.2: (c) まなぶ: Incorrect.「まなぶ」is the verb「学ぶ」(to learn or study).
default.q.n3-14-q4-4.why.3: (d) さけぶ: Incorrect. 「さけぶ」is the verb 「叫ぶ」, meaning “to shout” or “to yell.”
default.q.n3-14-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 3. せいふく.
default.q.n3-14-q5-5.explanation:
Meaning: Everyone at the restaurant is wearing the same uniform.
・Kanji note: 制 (regulation) + 服 (clothing) → 制服 (せいふく: uniform).
・Example: 日本の高校生は制服を着て登校します。(Japanese high school students wear uniforms to school.)
default.q.n3-14-q5-5.why.0: (a) ようふく: Incorrect. 「ようふく」 is the reading of 「洋服」(Western-style clothing).
default.q.n3-14-q5-5.why.1: (b) せいふう: The error is in 「服」, which is correctly read as ふく, not the long vowel ふう.
default.q.n3-14-q5-5.why.2: (c) せいふく: Correct. 「制服」 means “uniform” and is correctly read 「せいふく」.
default.q.n3-14-q5-5.why.3: (d) ようふう: Incorrect. 「ようふう」is the reading of 「洋風」, meaning Western style.
default.q.n3-14-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 1. かえて.
default.q.n3-14-q6-6.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Mr./Ms. Suzuki exchanged it for me.
・Kanji note: 換 → 換える (かえる: to exchange, replace, or trade) → 換えて (かえて).
・Example: 部屋の空気を換えるために窓を開けた。(I opened the window to freshen the air in the room.)
default.q.n3-14-q6-6.why.0: (a) Correct. 「換える」(KAN - to exchange, replace) takes the te-form 「かえて」.
default.q.n3-14-q6-6.why.1: (b) くわえて: Incorrect.「くわえて」is the te-form of「加える」(to add) or「咥える」(to hold in one’s mouth).
default.q.n3-14-q6-6.why.2: (c) つかまえて: Incorrect. 「つかまえて」is the te-form of 「捕まえる」(to catch, arrest).
default.q.n3-14-q6-6.why.3: (d) つたえて: Incorrect. 「つたえて」is the te-form of 「伝える」(to convey or pass on a message).

default.q.n3-14-q11-11.why.2: (c) 熱身: Incorrect because it confuses 心 (heart) with 身 (body), whose on-reading is しん in 自身/身体; Japanese does not use 熱身 for this meaning.
default.q.n3-14-q11-11.why.3: (d) 燃身: Both kanji, 燃 and 身, are incorrect.

default.q.n3-14-q12-12.why.3: (d) 帰員: Both kanji, 帰 and 員, are incorrect.
