default.q.n3-16-q37-37.explanation:
- Translation: Since the east parking lot is currently under construction, please use the south parking lot.
- Kanji-based explanation: 東側 (east side), 駐車場 (parking lot), 現在 (currently), 工事中 (under construction), 南側 (south side), 利用 (use).
- Grammar: 「N + のため(に)」 states a cause or reason in formal language, especially in public announcements. Example: 事故のため、電車が遅れています。(The train is delayed due to an accident.)
default.q.n3-16-q37-37.why.0: (a) 「ほか」(besides, other) indicates addition or exclusion; it is not used to state a cause or reason.
default.q.n3-16-q37-37.why.1: (b)「ため」following「N の」forms「〜のため(に)」, which indicates a formal cause or reason and is well suited to announcement-style writing.
default.q.n3-16-q37-37.why.2: (c) 「途中」 (“in the middle of” or “on the way”) usually combines with the particle で, as in 途中で; it is not suitable for indicating the reason leading to the following request.
default.q.n3-16-q37-37.why.3: (d) 「一方」 (on the other hand, increasingly...) expresses contrast or a one-directional trend, so it does not fit the meaning here.
default.q.n3-16-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 1. あと because it combines with a time expression in「あと + period of time」to mean “...more until...”.
default.q.n3-16-q38-38.explanation:
- Translation: Younger sister: “Can I go to the restroom for a moment?” / Older sister: “Okay. But the train will arrive in only five minutes, so hurry.”
- Vocabulary: 妹: younger sister; 姉: older sister; 電車: train; 急ぐ: hurry, act quickly.
- Grammar: 「あと + amount of time」indicates the amount of time remaining before an event occurs (“there are ... minutes left until ...”). Example: あと10分で試験が始まります。(The test will begin in 10 minutes.)
default.q.n3-16-q38-38.why.0: (a) 「あと」 combines with the time expression 「あと5分で」 to mean “only five minutes remain until...,” naturally and accurately expressing urgency.
default.q.n3-16-q38-38.why.1: (b) 「まだ」 (still/not yet), when used with time, normally takes an affirmative expression for the remaining time, such as まだ5分ある. It does not go with 「〜で来ちゃう」 in this structure.
default.q.n3-16-q38-38.why.2: (c) 「だんだん」 (“gradually”) describes a change occurring over time and does not directly precede a specific time quantity.
default.q.n3-16-q38-38.why.3: (d) 「今にも」(any moment now / about to) usually accompanies 「〜そうだ」(e.g., 今にも雨が降りそうだ), and does not combine with a specific period of time.
default.q.n3-16-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 作ってみると because the pattern 「V-てみると」describes discovering an unexpected result or fact after trying to do something.
default.q.n3-16-q39-39.explanation:
- Translation: I thought making hamburg steaks would be difficult, but when I tried, I found that it was not as difficult as I had expected.
- Sino-Japanese readings: 作る (to make, cook), 難 (difficult), 思 (to think).
- Grammar: 「V-てみると」 describes discovering or realizing a fact or unexpected result after trying something. Example: 食べてみると、とてもおいしかった。(When I tried it, it was very delicious.)
default.q.n3-16-q39-39.why.0: (a) 「作っているうちに」 (“while making it...”) describes a change that occurs during an ongoing action, so it does not fit realizing the truth after trying to make it.
default.q.n3-16-q39-39.why.1: (b) 「作ったとしても」 (“even if one made it”) expresses a concessive hypothetical, which does not fit a sentence recounting an actual experience.
default.q.n3-16-q39-39.why.2: (c) 「作ってみると」 (“when I tried making it...”) uses the pattern 「V-てみると」 to express discovering an actual fact after trying something: “it was not as difficult as I had thought.” It is completely correct.
default.q.n3-16-q39-39.why.3: (d) 「作った後で」(after finishing making it) merely indicates when the action was completed; it does not emphasize the meaning of trying something and then realizing or discovering the result.
default.q.n3-16-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 4. いただいた because it is the humble form of 「もらった」 (received from a superior).
default.q.n3-16-q40-40.explanation:
- Translation: Nakamura: "Section Chief, the souvenir box of chocolates I received from you yesterday was delicious. Thank you very much." / Section Chief: "Oh, I'm glad to hear that."
- Sino-Japanese meanings: 課長 (section chief), 昨日 (yesterday), 土産 (souvenir).
- Honorific language: 「いただく」is the humble form (kenjōgo) of 「もらう」. It is used when the speaker humbles their own act of receiving something from someone of higher status, here the 課長. Example: 先生から本をいただきました。(I received a book from my teacher.)
default.q.n3-16-q40-40.why.0: (a) 「おりました」is the humble form of「いました」(to be), so it is completely incorrect when modifying the noun お土産.
default.q.n3-16-q40-40.why.1: (b) 「まいりました」 is the humble form of 「いきました／きました」 (went/came), and is not used to mean receiving a gift.
default.q.n3-16-q40-40.why.2: (c) 「なさった」 is the respectful form of 「した」 (did), so it does not fit the meaning of receiving a souvenir.
default.q.n3-16-q40-40.why.3: (d) 「いただいた」 is the humble past form of 「もらった」 (received), used to show respect when receiving a gift from a superior.
default.q.n3-16-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 1. なんだろう because, combined with the exclamatory adverb「なんて」, it forms the exclamatory pattern「なんて…なんだろう」.
default.q.n3-16-q41-41.explanation:
- Meaning: When I met her for the first time, I thought to myself, “Wow, how can anyone be this beautiful?”
- Kanji compounds: 初 (first, initial), 彼女 (she, her), 会 (meet).
- Grammar: 「なんて + adjective/noun + なんだろう」 is an exclamatory pattern expressing surprise, admiration, or amazement (“How ...!”). Example: なんて素晴らしい景色なんだろう。(What a wonderful view!)
default.q.n3-16-q41-41.why.0: (a) 「なんだろう」combines with「なんて」to form the exclamatory structure「なんて〜なんだろう」, expressing surprise and admiration (“How can someone be so beautiful!”).
default.q.n3-16-q41-41.why.1: (b) 「だった。」simply states a past fact and does not combine with the exclamatory adverb 「なんて」at the beginning of the sentence.
default.q.n3-16-q41-41.why.2: (c)「みたいだ」means “looks like” or “seems,” expressing comparison or conjecture, and does not combine with「なんて」to form an exclamatory sentence.
default.q.n3-16-q41-41.why.3: (d) 「だったのか」 (“so it was...”) is used when realizing a past fact after suddenly understanding it; it does not form an exclamatory compliment.
default.q.n3-16-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 2. でございます, which is the formal polite form (丁寧語) of 「〜です」 used when an employee gives the name of their store.
default.q.n3-16-q42-42.explanation:
- Meaning: Employee: "Thank you for calling. Sakura Beauty Salon speaking." / Customer: "Excuse me. I would like to make an appointment for today." / Employee: "Certainly, thank you. Around what time would you like to make the appointment?"
- Character-based readings: 店員 (てんいん: employee), 美容院 (びよういん: beauty salon/hair salon), 予約 (よやく: reservation, appointment).
- Honorific language: 「〜でございます」 is the formal polite form (丁寧語) of 「〜です」. In business and service situations, it is often used when answering the phone and identifying one's company or shop. Example: はい、ABC商事でございます。(Yes, this is ABC Trading speaking.)
default.q.n3-16-q42-42.why.0: (a) 「でいらっしゃいます」 is the honorific form of 「です」. It is used when referring to the other person or a customer, not oneself or one’s own store.
default.q.n3-16-q42-42.why.1: (b) 「でございます」 is the formal polite form (丁寧語) of 「です」 and is the standard expression for an employee introducing the establishment over the phone.
default.q.n3-16-q42-42.why.2: (c) 「と申し上げます」 is the humble form of 「と言います」 and is generally used when presenting one’s opinion to someone; it is not used to introduce this store.
default.q.n3-16-q42-42.why.3: (d) 「とおっしゃいます」is the honorific form of 「と言います」, used to refer respectfully to what another person says.
default.q.n3-16-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 3. おもしろそうじゃなかった, because the pattern 「〜そうじゃなかった」 (“did not look/seem...”) expresses a direct impression after observing the class.
default.q.n3-16-q43-43.explanation:
- Translation: Nakanishi: "Kawamura, how was the trial lesson for the dance class yesterday? Did you sign up?" / Kawamura: "No. It didn't look very interesting, so I decided not to join."
- Kanji terms: 教室 (classroom, class), 見学 (observation, trial visit).
- Grammar: i-adjective (remove い) + そうじゃない / そうじゃなかった: "doesn't / didn't look..." (expressing a visual impression after observing something). Example: この料理はあまりおいしそうじゃない。(This dish doesn't look very tasty.)
default.q.n3-16-q43-43.why.0: (a) 「おもしろかったはずがない」 (“it cannot have been interesting”) is a firm conclusion based on reasoning, so it is unsuitable for describing a personal impression after a visit.
default.q.n3-16-q43-43.why.1: (b) 「おもしろくなければならなかった」 means “had to be interesting,” expressing obligation and being completely wrong in meaning.
default.q.n3-16-q43-43.why.2: (c) 「おもしろそうじゃなかった」 is the past negative form of 「おもしろそうだ」 (“looks interesting”). It accurately expresses an impression based on actually observing the class.
default.q.n3-16-q43-43.why.3: (d) 「おもしろくなかっただろう」 (It probably wasn't fun, was it?) is used to make a supposition or seek agreement from someone else, not to state the speaker's own impression.
default.q.n3-16-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 1. でしか because the location particle「で」combines with「しか…ない」to mean “can only eat there.”
default.q.n3-16-q44-44.explanation:
- Meaning: One of the pleasures of traveling is being able to enjoy dishes that can only be eaten in that particular place.
- On'yomi: 旅行 (travel), 楽 (pleasure, enjoyment), 料理 (cooking, dish).
- Grammar: 「Place + でしか + V-れない」 means "only at that place can one do V; nowhere else is it possible." Example: ここでしか買えない限定品。(A limited-edition item that can only be bought here.)
default.q.n3-16-q44-44.why.0: (a) 「でしか」combines the location particle 「で」with 「しか」and the negative potential form 「食べられない」, meaning “can eat only at that place,” so it is completely correct.
default.q.n3-16-q44-44.why.1: (b) 「だけの」 means “only belonging to...” and must directly modify a noun; it cannot precede a negative verb clause in this way.
default.q.n3-16-q44-44.why.2: (c) 「にだけ」uses the particle 「に」to indicate a point of existence or a destination, whereas an eating or drinking action requires 「で」to indicate the location where the action takes place.
default.q.n3-16-q44-44.why.3: (d) 「での」 combines the particles 「で」 and 「の」 to modify a following noun, so it cannot directly precede the verb 「食べられない」.
default.q.n3-16-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 2. にしても because the pattern「〜にしても」means “even if it is...” or “even supposing that...”.
default.q.n3-16-q45-45.explanation:
- Meaning: Apples are delicious eaten as they are, but they are also delicious made into jam.
- 食 (しょく / たべる) = eat.
- Grammar: 「N + にしても」means "even if made into N" or "even as N, ...". Example: そのままでもおいしいが、温めてスープにしてもおいしい。(It is delicious as it is, but it is also delicious warmed up and made into soup.)
default.q.n3-16-q45-45.why.0: (a) 「にするのに」 means “to make it…” or “although making it…,” expressing purpose or an unsatisfied contrast; it does not fit as an additional example that is also delicious.
default.q.n3-16-q45-45.why.1: (b) 「にしても」 means “even if it is made into ...,” expressing that it would still be delicious even when made into jam. It naturally corresponds to the preceding clause saying that it is delicious eaten as it is.
default.q.n3-16-q45-45.why.2: (c) 「になると」 indicates a natural change leading to an inevitable result (“when it becomes...”); it is not used for an intentional preparation process followed by praise.
default.q.n3-16-q45-45.why.3: (d) 「になって」indicates a natural change into another state, so it does not fit the meaning of processing an apple into jam.
default.q.n3-16-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 4. つけたまま because the transitive verb 「つける」 must be used with the object marker 「〜を」, followed by the pattern 「V-たまま」 (leaving something in its current state).
default.q.n3-16-q46-46.explanation:
- Meaning: Sometimes I leave the lights and TV on and end up sleeping until morning.
- Sino-Japanese readings: 私 (I), 電気 (light, electricity), 朝 (morning), 寝 (sleep).
- Grammar: 「V-た + まま」describes keeping something in a particular state and then performing another action. Distinguish between を + つけたまま (transitive verb) and が + ついたまま (intransitive verb). Example: 窓を開けたまま寝てしまい、風邪を引いた。(I fell asleep with the window open and caught a cold.)
default.q.n3-16-q46-46.why.0: (a) 「ついている間」 uses the intransitive verb 「つく」, so it cannot combine with the object marker 「を」 before it, and 「間」 does not express the meaning of leaving something in its current state.
default.q.n3-16-q46-46.why.1: (b) 「つけている間」 (“while it is turned on”) indicates the period during which an action takes place; it does not express leaving something in a certain state and accidentally doing something else.
default.q.n3-16-q46-46.why.2: (c) 「ついたまま」uses the intransitive verb 「つく」, which takes が, as in 電気がついたまま; it cannot take を in this sentence.
default.q.n3-16-q46-46.why.3: (d) 「つけたまま」 combines the transitive verb 「つける」, which takes を, with the pattern 「〜たまま」. It correctly means “leave the lights and television on as they are and sleep until morning.”
default.q.n3-16-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 歩きやすくて because it uses 「V-やすい」(easy to do something) in the te-form to connect the shoes’ positive features.
default.q.n3-16-q47-47.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: The shoes I bought last month are comfortable to walk in and do not make my feet tired, so I really like them.
- Sino-Japanese readings: 先月 (last month), 買 (buy), 靴 (shoes), 歩 (walk), 足 (foot), 疲 (tired), 気に入っている (like, be pleased with).
- Grammar: 「V-やすい」 (easy to do something); when connecting clauses, it becomes 「〜やすくて」. Example: このペンは書きやすくて手が疲れません。(This pen is easy to write with, so my hand does not get tired.)
default.q.n3-16-q47-47.why.0: (a) 「歩きやすくて」 is the te-form of 「歩きやすい」 (easy to walk in), linking two positive characteristics: "easy to walk in and does not make one's feet tired," clearly giving the reason the shoes are liked.
default.q.n3-16-q47-47.why.1: (b) 「歩きすぎて」 (because of walking too much) uses 「V-すぎる」 to express excessive, usually undesirable action, so it does not fit the logic of having no sore feet and being very satisfied.
default.q.n3-16-q47-47.why.2: (c) 「歩きやすかったら」 (“if they were easy to walk in”) is the hypothetical conditional form 「〜たら」. It does not fit because the speaker is commenting on the shoes actually purchased.
default.q.n3-16-q47-47.why.3: (d) 「歩きすぎたら」 (if one walks too much) is also a hypothetical conditional clause, so it does not fit the context at all.
default.q.n3-16-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 帰ってきたところだ, because it combines movement toward the speaker (〜てくる) with the pattern for having just finished something (〜たところだ).
default.q.n3-16-q48-48.explanation:
- Translation: Father: "Hello, Yamashita speaking." / Son: "Oh, hello, Dad. Is Mom home now?" / Father: "Yes, she is. She just got home from work."
- Kanji readings and meanings: 父 (father), 息子 (son), 母 (mother), 家 (home, house), 仕事 (work), 帰 (to return).
- Grammar: 「ちょうど + V-たところだ」 describes an action that has just finished. Since the action is directed toward the speaker’s location (home), 「帰ってくる」 is used.
Example: ちょうど今、家に着いたところです。(I just arrived home.)
default.q.n3-16-q48-48.why.0: (a) 「帰ってきたことがある」 uses 「V-たことがある」 to describe a past experience, so it does not combine with the adverb 「ちょうど」 (“just,” “exactly”).
default.q.n3-16-q48-48.why.1: (b) 「帰っていったことがある」has the wrong direction of movement with 「〜ていく」(moving away from the speaker) and also uses the wrong structure for expressing experience.
default.q.n3-16-q48-48.why.2: (c) 「帰ってきたところだ」 correctly uses 「帰ってくる」 for movement toward the speaker and the pattern 「ちょうど〜たところだ」 to express that the mother had just returned home from work.
default.q.n3-16-q48-48.why.3: (d) 「帰っていったところだ」 uses 「〜ていく」 to describe someone leaving and moving away from the speaker, which does not fit because the father is at home confirming that the mother has just arrived home.
default.q.n3-16-q49-49.verdict: The correct order is: 4 → 2 → 3 → 1. The position marked ★ is 3 (いい).
default.q.n3-16-q49-49.explanation:
Complete dialogue: 課長:「山田さん、資料の整理をやってもらえますか。来週の金曜まででいいですから、できるときにお願いします。」
Meaning: Section manager: “Yamada, could you organize the documents? By next Friday is fine, so please do it when you have time.”
default.q.n3-16-q49-49.why.0: (a) 「ですから」 means “therefore” or “so,” and occupies position 4 to conclude the reason clause and connect it to the gentle request 「できるときにお願いします」 that follows.
default.q.n3-16-q49-49.why.1: (b) The particle「で」follows「まで」to form the phrase「〜までで」, which combines with「いい」to create the sentence pattern「〜まででいい」(up to... is fine / only until... is necessary). It appears in the second position.
default.q.n3-16-q49-49.why.2: (c) The i-adjective「いい」 (good/acceptable) follows「までで」to form「〜まででいい」, so it goes in position 3 (the ★ slot), immediately before the conjunction「ですから」.
default.q.n3-16-q49-49.why.3: (d) The particle 「まで」 marks a time limit. Placed directly after 「来週の金曜」, it forms 「来週の金曜まで」 (“until next Friday”) and occupies the first position.
default.q.n3-16-q50-50.verdict: Correct order: 3 → 4 → 2 → 1. ★ is 2 (ということを).
default.q.n3-16-q50-50.explanation:
Complete sentence: 私は、もし自分が患者だったらどうしてほしいかということを考えながら看護師の仕事をしています。
Meaning: I work as a nurse while always considering how I would want to be treated and cared for if I were a patient.
default.q.n3-16-q50-50.why.0: (a) 「考えながら」 (“while thinking...”) uses the structure 「〜ながら」 to describe two actions occurring simultaneously. In the fourth position, it directly modifies 「看護師の仕事をしています」 at the end of the sentence.
default.q.n3-16-q50-50.why.1: (b) 「ということを」 occupies position 3, the ★ position, nominalizing the entire question clause 「〜か」 before it and functioning as the object of the verb 「考えながら」.
default.q.n3-16-q50-50.why.2: (c) 「患者だったら」 (if one were a patient) follows 「もし自分が」 to form the conditional clause 「もし自分が患者だったら」 (if I myself were a patient), occupying position 1.
default.q.n3-16-q50-50.why.3: (d) The embedded question 「どうしてほしいか」(what one wants someone else to do or how one wants to be cared for) follows the conditional clause 「患者だったら」 and occupies the second position.
default.q.n3-16-q51-51.verdict: The correct order is: 1 → 3 → 2 → 4. The position marked ★ is 2 (とき).
default.q.n3-16-q51-51.explanation:
Complete sentence: 私はエアコンの風が好きではないので、夏の夜、暑くてどうしても寝られないとき以外は自分の部屋ではエアコンを使いません。
Meaning: Because I do not like air-conditioning, I do not use it in my room on summer nights except when it is so hot that I simply cannot sleep.
default.q.n3-16-q51-51.why.0: (a) The adverb「どうしても」(no matter what) follows the te-form adjective「暑くて」to emphasize the degree. It occupies the first position and modifies the potential negative verb「寝られない」that follows.
default.q.n3-16-q51-51.why.1: (b) The noun 「とき」 (when) takes the attributive clause 「どうしても寝られない」 before it and combines with 「以外は」 after it to form 「〜とき以外は」 (except when...), occupying the third position (★ blank).
default.q.n3-16-q51-51.why.2: (c) The negative potential form 「寝られない」 (cannot sleep) follows the adverb 「どうしても」 and comes before the noun 「とき」 as an attributive phrase, occupying the second position.
default.q.n3-16-q51-51.why.3: (d) The phrase「以外は」(except for...) follows「とき」and appears in the fourth position, directly before「自分の部屋では...」, to express exclusion.
default.q.n3-16-q52-52.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 1 → 4 → 3. The ★ position is 4 (答えてくれないので).
default.q.n3-16-q52-52.explanation:
Complete sentence: 最近、田中さんは元気がない。心配だが、何があったのか聞いても答えてくれないので何もしてあげられない。
Meaning: Tanaka has not seemed very well lately. I am worried, but even when I ask what happened, he will not answer, so there is nothing I can do to help him.
default.q.n3-16-q52-52.why.0: (a) The 「〜ても」 form (“even if,” “although”) in 「聞いても」 (“even if one asks”) follows the embedded question 「何があったのか」 to form 「何があったのか聞いても」 (“even if one asks what happened”), and appears in position 2.
default.q.n3-16-q52-52.why.1: (b) The phrase 「あったのか」 combines with the question word 「何が」 before it to form the embedded question 「何があったのか」 (“what happened”), occupying position 1.
default.q.n3-16-q52-52.why.2: (c) The adverb 「何も」 (“not... anything”) occupies the fourth position and comes directly before the negative form 「してあげられない」 at the end of the sentence, forming the complete negative structure 「何もしてあげられない」 (“cannot do anything to help”).
default.q.n3-16-q52-52.why.3: (d) The pattern 「〜てくれないので」 (because someone does not do something for me) indicates a cause. It follows 「聞いても」 and occupies the third position (★) to connect to the subsequent result that help cannot be provided.
default.q.n3-16-q53-53.verdict: The correct order is: 4 → 2 → 1 → 3. The star ★ is in position 1 (私には).
default.q.n3-16-q53-53.explanation:
Complete sentence: この辺りは自然が多く、いつかこういうところに住んでみたいと思うが、近くに買い物できる場所がないので、車の運転ができない私には生活するのは大変そうだ。
Meaning: This area has abundant nature, and I think I would like to try living somewhere like this someday. However, since there is nowhere nearby to go shopping, it seems it would be difficult for someone like me who cannot drive.
default.q.n3-16-q53-53.why.0: (a) The phrase 「私には」(for me) follows the attributive clause 「車の運転ができない」to form 「車の運転ができない私には」(for someone like me who cannot drive a car), and it occupies the third position (slot ★).
default.q.n3-16-q53-53.why.1: (b) The negative potential form 「できない」 follows the phrase 「車の運転が」 and forms a predicate phrase modifying the noun 「私」 that follows, in the second position.
default.q.n3-16-q53-53.why.2: (c) The dictionary-form verb 「生活する」, meaning “to live” or “to lead a life,” occupies position 4 immediately before 「のは大変そうだ」, nominalizing the action: “living there seems difficult.”
default.q.n3-16-q53-53.why.3: (d) The noun phrase plus particle 「車の運転が」(driving a car) follows the conjunction 「ので、」and serves as the subject of the potential predicate 「できない」. It occupies position 1.
default.q.n3-16-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 3. それでも (even so, nevertheless).
default.q.n3-16-q54-54.explanation:
- **Context and flow:**
  + Previous sentence:「いつも大勢で行くから、自分一人がずっと歌うということはできません。」(Since I always go with a large group, I cannot sing by myself the whole time — expressing a limitation or slight inconvenience.)
  + Sentence with the blank:「【19】、カラオケはパーティーみたいで楽しいと思っていました。」(..., I still thought karaoke was fun, like a party — expressing a positive aspect.)
- **Analysis:** The two clauses express concession and mild contrast: although one cannot sing alone to one's heart's content, going to karaoke with a large group is still enjoyable, like a lively party. Therefore, the conjunction expressing contrast/concession is「それでも」(even so, nevertheless). Additive conjunctions such as そのうえ and また, or the adverb 特に, do not express this relationship.
default.q.n3-16-q54-54.why.0: (a) 「そのうえ」(“moreover,” “in addition”) is a conjunction that adds information in the same direction; it cannot express the contrast between “not being able to sing alone continuously” and “still enjoying it as if it were a party.”
default.q.n3-16-q54-54.why.1: (b) 「特に」(especially) is an adverb of degree used to emphasize a notable detail within a group; it does not function as a conjunction linking two contrasting sentences.
default.q.n3-16-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「それでも」 (“even so/nevertheless”) is a concessive conjunction. It fits perfectly here: although a large group cannot sing continuously, karaoke is still lively and enjoyable.
default.q.n3-16-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「また」 (“also,” “in addition”) lists or adds new information in the same direction, so it does not fit this concessive transition.
default.q.n3-16-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 思っていたからです (because I had always thought that ...).
default.q.n3-16-q55-55.explanation:
- Context and flow:
  + In the preceding sentence, the author discovers “Hitori Karaoke” and expresses extreme surprise: 「私はとても驚きました。」(I was extremely surprised.)
  + The sentence containing the blank, 「カラオケは人と一緒に楽しむものだと 【20】。」, directly explains the *reason* for the author's surprise: the author had always assumed that karaoke was something to be enjoyed together with a group of people.
- Grammar analysis:
  + To explain the reason for the preceding sentence, the sentence ending should use the causal structure 「〜からです」.
  + 「思っていた」describes an assumption or belief that had been maintained over a period of time in the past.
  + Together, they form 「思っていたからです」(Because I had always thought that...).
default.q.n3-16-q55-55.why.0: (a) 「思っていたからです」 (because I had always thought so) correctly expresses the writer’s prior state of awareness through 思っていた, while the ending 「〜からです」 explains the reason for the surprise expressed in 「私はとても驚きました」 in the previous sentence.
default.q.n3-16-q55-55.why.1: (b) 「思っていたはずです」 (must have thought) is used for an objective inference about another person's action or a situation supported by evidence; it is not used when the writer reports their own thoughts.
default.q.n3-16-q55-55.why.2: (c)「思いつづけたのです」(continued thinking) uses the explanatory ending 「〜のです」but lacks the causal connector 「から」. Also, 「思いつづけた」emphasizes the continuation of the act of thinking, which is less natural here than the state of awareness expressed by 「思っていた」.
default.q.n3-16-q55-55.why.3: (d) 「思いつづけたようです」 (“it seems that [they] continued thinking”) contains 「〜ようです」, which expresses an inference or appearance based on external observation. It is not used for the author’s own inner experience.
default.q.n3-16-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 行ってみることにしました (decided to try going).
default.q.n3-16-q56-56.explanation:
- **Context and flow:**
  + After learning that friends also went to karaoke alone, the author realized: 「一人で行ってもいいとわかって、」(After realizing that it was okay to go alone,...).
  + The immediately following action is: 「私はどきどきしながら、受付で名前を書きました。」(Feeling nervous, I wrote my name at the reception desk.)
- **Grammar analysis:**
  +「〜てみる」: try doing something new.
  +「〜ことにする」: make one's own decision to do something.
  + In the past tense: 「〜てみることにしました」(I decided to try going alone).
  + The alternatives expressing an external rule, 「ことになっている」, or the causative form, 「行かせる」, are completely unsuitable.
default.q.n3-16-q56-56.why.0: (a)「行ってみることになっています」(it has been arranged/decided that someone will try going) describes a rule or schedule set by a group or someone else, and does not express the author’s own decision.
default.q.n3-16-q56-56.why.1: (b) 「行ってみることにしました」 (“decided to try going”) combines 「〜てみる」 (“try doing…”) and 「〜ことにした」 (“decide for oneself to…”), accurately expressing the author’s decision to try going to karaoke alone.
default.q.n3-16-q56-56.why.2: (c) 「行かせてくれたことです」 (“the fact that someone let me go”) uses the causative form together with the benefactive pattern 「〜させてくれる」 and nominalization with 「〜ことです」, but the structure and meaning are completely inappropriate.
default.q.n3-16-q56-56.why.3: (d) 「行かせることができました」 means “was able to make or let someone else go.” It uses the causative potential form 「〜行かせることができる」 and describes influencing another person, not going oneself.
default.q.n3-16-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 部屋 (room).
default.q.n3-16-q57-57.explanation:
- **Text flow and context:**
  + The passage describes a sequence of actions in chronological order:
    1. Writing one’s name at reception:「受付で名前を書きました。」
    2. Entering the singing room:「そして、【22】に入り、」
    3. Practicing Japanese songs that the writer still cannot sing well:「まだ上手に歌えない日本語の歌を練習したり...」
- **Grammar analysis:**
  + After「そして」(and then), the writer enters the designated room. Since the particle「に」already follows the blank, only the simple noun「部屋」(room) is needed to form「部屋に入り」(entered the room).
  + Choices containing demonstratives, such as「そんな部屋が」(the extra particle が creates the ungrammatical sequence「がに入り」), or「こんな部屋」「あんな部屋」(which sound unnatural and overly demonstrative or exclamatory in an ordinary narrative sequence), are incorrect.
default.q.n3-16-q57-57.why.0: (a) 「部屋」 (room) combines directly with 「に入り」 to form 「部屋に入り」 (entering the room), naturally describing the next action after completing the procedure at the reception desk.
default.q.n3-16-q57-57.why.1: (b) 「そんな部屋が」 is seriously ungrammatical because inserting it would create two consecutive particles, 「そんな部屋がに入り」. In addition, the demonstrative 「そんな」 has no suitable referent.
default.q.n3-16-q57-57.why.2: (c) 「こんな部屋」(a room like this) uses the demonstrative 「こんな」 to refer to a room close to the speaker in the present or to a specific example. It is unnatural when objectively narrating a sequence of past actions.
default.q.n3-16-q57-57.why.3: (d) 「あんな部屋」 (“a room like that”) has an exclamatory or distant demonstrative nuance, referring to something far from both the speaker and the listener. It does not fit an ordinary account of entering a karaoke room.
default.q.n3-16-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 4. でも (even, even if).
default.q.n3-16-q58-58.explanation:
- **Flow and context:**
  + At first, the author thought karaoke was something people enjoyed by going in groups (「カラオケは人と一緒に楽しむものだ」).
  + However, after personally enjoying singing comfortably for two hours, the author concluded: 「カラオケは一人 【23】楽しかったです。」(Even going to karaoke alone was very enjoyable.)
  + The following sentence says: 「これからもっとカラオケに行くことが増えそうです。」(From now on, I will probably go to karaoke more often.)
- **Grammar analysis:**
  + The particle 「でも」 follows the numeral/noun 「一人」 to form 「一人でも」 (even alone / even if it is just one person), emphasizing that karaoke is enjoyable even without going with a group.
default.q.n3-16-q58-58.why.0: (a) 「だけ」 (“only”) would form 「一人だけ」 (“only I am having fun”), changing the meaning into a comparison of enjoyment between people instead of referring to the activity of going to karaoke alone.
default.q.n3-16-q58-58.why.1: (b) 「より」 (“than,” “compared with”) is used in the comparative pattern 「AよりB」 (“B is more ... than A”). It cannot form 「一人より楽しかったです」 with a logically appropriate meaning in this sentence.
default.q.n3-16-q58-58.why.2: (c) 「なら」 (if it is) introduces a condition or assumption, so it cannot be used with the predicate 「楽しかったです」, which describes an actual past experience.
default.q.n3-16-q58-58.why.3: (d) 「でも」 (even / even if) combines with 「一人」 to form 「一人でも」 (even alone), correctly expressing the author's new experience: karaoke was very enjoyable even when going alone.
default.q.n3-16-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: 優しい感じがするから (because it gives a gentle impression).
default.q.n3-16-q59-59.explanation:
- Main idea: The narrator's older sister had a daughter and gave her the hiragana name 「はるか」. At first, the narrator guessed that it might be because the child could write the name herself from an early age, but when asked, the sister replied that a hiragana name gives a gentle impression.

  1. Because the child could write it herself from an early age.
  2. Because it gives a gentle impression.
  3. Because it cannot be misread.
  4. Because it is easy for other people to remember.

default.q.n3-16-q59-59.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage quotes the older sister’s answer: 「すると、ひらがななら、優しい感じがするからという答えだった」(When asked, she answered that Hiragana gives a gentle impression).

default.q.n3-16-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The fact that the name is easy for others to remember (「覚えてもらいやすい」) is also a positive point added by the narrator (「良い点もあるだろう」), not the reason given by the older sister for choosing the name.
default.q.n3-16-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Do not wait for me; go into the concert hall first.
default.q.n3-16-q60-60.explanation:
Summary:
Mariko writes to her friend Lana to send her a concert ticket for next Friday. Because Mariko has an unexpected work commitment that day, she asks Lana to go straight to the concert hall and enter first instead of meeting at the station ticket gate as they did last time. If Mariko is late, she will email Lana.

Question translation:
What does Mariko want Lana to do next Friday?

Answer choices:
1. Wait for her at the station ticket gate.
2. Go straight to the concert hall and wait for her outside.
3. Not wait for her, but enter the concert hall first.
4. Email her if it looks as though she will be late for the concert.
default.q.n3-16-q60-60.why.0: (a) Incorrect. Meeting at the station ticket gate was for the previous concert («この前のコンサートのときは駅の改札口で待ち合わせましたが...»). This time, Mariko suddenly became busy, so they are not meeting at the station.
default.q.n3-16-q60-60.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Mariko asks Lana to go straight to the hall and go inside first («先に中に入っていてくれませんか»), not to wait outside.
default.q.n3-16-q60-60.why.2: (c) Correct. The text says: 「今回は直接会場に行って、先に中に入っていてくれませんか。」 This is equivalent to entering the venue in advance without waiting for Mariko.
default.q.n3-16-q60-60.why.3: (d) Incorrect. In the letter, Mariko says that if she seems likely to be late, she herself will email Lana (「遅れそうだったら、メールしますね」). She does not ask Lana to email her.
default.q.n3-16-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The store's mistake was sending only 3 jars of glue even though the customer ordered 5.

Nakano Stationery Store emails Teraichi to apologize for an error in yesterday's shipment: the customer ordered one box of copy paper and five bottles of glue, but the store sent only three bottles of glue. 間違いとあるが、何が間違いか。

1. コピー用紙1箱を送ってしまったこと: Sending one box of copy paper by mistake.

default.q.n3-16-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The author feels fortunate that in Japan, railways became widely available as a means of transportation before automobiles did.

- Main point: The author greatly enjoys leisurely train trips through the countryside while looking at the scenery outside. Railways were built even in sparsely populated rural areas because trains became widespread before automobiles did. The author believes that if the order had been reversed, it would now be impossible to enjoy such train trips, and feels grateful and fortunate that history unfolded this way.

- Translation of the question: What does “I” most want to say?

- Translation of the answer choices:
1. In Japan, I want many people to enjoy leisurely train trips through the countryside.
2. In Japan, it is very convenient to live even in a remote rural area because a railway runs through it.
3. In Japan, I am very happy to have been able to enjoy both car trips and train trips.
4. In Japan, it is fortunate that railways became widely used for transportation before automobiles.
default.q.n3-16-q62-62.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the reading does not mention wanting to encourage others or wanting many people to travel by train in rural areas. It only discusses the author’s personal preference.
default.q.n3-16-q62-62.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the article discusses the author’s enjoyment of the scenery while traveling by train, not the convenience of daily life for people living in rural areas.

If the order had been reversed, I could not have enjoyed traveling by rural railway as I do now. I am grateful for this history.) In other words, the author feels fortunate that railways developed before automobiles.
default.q.n3-16-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 名刺だと言われたのに、クッキーを渡されたから (Because I was told it was a business card, but was given cookies instead).

- Main point: At a party, someone greeted the author and said, "Here is my business card," but what they actually handed over was a cookie in a bag. This made the author surprised and confused, thinking, "Huh?"

default.q.n3-16-q67-67.why.2: (c) Correct because paragraph 3 clearly states: 「それに対して、努力をほめられたグループでは、90%が新しい問題にチャレンジしたのです。」 (In contrast, 90% of the group praised for their effort tried a new problem.) The 90% corresponds to most of the children (子供の多く).
default.q.n3-16-q67-67.why.3: (d) This is unsuitable because the passage only emphasizes that 90% of the children in the group praised for their effort tried the new problem. Choice (c) most directly and accurately expresses the difference stated in the passage.
default.q.n3-16-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is choice 1: The praise focuses on the child’s effort and perseverance: 「ずっと集中して頑張っていたね。本当に感心したよ。」(You stayed focused and worked hard the whole time. I’m really impressed.)
default.q.n3-16-q68-68.explanation:
• Main point: The experiment showed that praising intelligence makes children afraid of making mistakes and being seen as inadequate, so they avoid new challenges. In contrast, praising effort helps children confidently embrace new challenges. Therefore, the parenting insight the author gained is to praise the child's effort and process.

• Translation of the question: The author writes, “②I think this was an interesting experiment containing a hint about how to praise people.” What can we infer that “I” might say when praising their child in the future?

• Translation of the answer choices:
1. “You really focused and worked hard. I am truly impressed.”
2. “You did very well. You are really smart.”
3. “You did it without studying at all. You are amazing.”
4. “Even though the problem was so difficult, you finished it easily. I am surprised.”
default.q.n3-16-q68-68.why.0: (a) Correct. Through the experiment, the author realized that the effective way to praise children is to praise their effort (「努力」をほめる言葉をかけます:「よく頑張ったね」), encouraging them to take on new challenges. The sentence 「ずっと集中して頑張っていたね。本当に感心したよ。」 praises the child's effort and persistence throughout the process.
default.q.n3-16-q68-68.why.1: (b) Inappropriate because this praises innate intelligence (「頭がいいね」), a form of praise that makes children afraid of failure and inclined to choose only safe options, as demonstrated by the experiment.
default.q.n3-16-q68-68.why.2: (c) Inappropriate because this sentence praises a child for being able to do something without studying at all (「ぜんぜん勉強しなくてもできた」), which is completely contrary to encouraging and praising effort (努力).
default.q.n3-16-q68-68.why.3: (d) Not appropriate because this sentence focuses on praising how easily the child completed the task («簡単にできちゃった»), suggesting innate ability rather than valuing the process of overcoming difficulties through effort.
default.q.n3-16-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 非常に暑い日にエアコンを使うこと (using the air conditioner on extremely hot days).
default.q.n3-16-q69-69.explanation:
- Summary and explanation: The passage clearly states that on extremely hot days, people cannot do anything without air conditioning, and the heat also negatively affects their health, so most people turn on the air conditioner (エアコンのスイッチを入れる). This action is described as “unavoidable” (しかたないこと). Therefore, the “unavoidable thing” is using air conditioning on extremely hot days.
- Translation of the question: The phrase “① an unavoidable thing” appears. What is the unavoidable thing?
- Translation of the choices:
1. The average summer temperature in Japan is rising.
2. Using air conditioning on extremely hot days.
3. Having to endure the intense heat.
4. Each household having multiple air conditioners.
default.q.n3-16-q69-69.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the rise in average summer temperatures is a general weather phenomenon, not an action by people that “cannot be avoided.”
default.q.n3-16-q69-69.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because paragraph states: 「非常に暑い日はエアコンがなければ何もできない。そんな日は、ほとんどの人がエアコンのスイッチを入れる。ひどい暑さは体にも悪い影響を与えるし、①しかたないことだ。」 (On extremely hot days, it is impossible to do anything without air conditioning. On such days, most people turn it on. Severe heat also harms the body, so using air conditioning is unavoidable).
default.q.n3-16-q69-69.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the passage does not say that people had to “endure the heat” (我慢する); rather, because the heat adversely affected their health, they had to turn on the air conditioner.
default.q.n3-16-q69-69.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the fact that each household has multiple air conditioners is stated in the following sentence, 「それぞれの家に何台もエアコンがある今」, not in ①しかたないこと.
default.q.n3-16-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 4. それぞれの家で使う電気の量を少なくしてほしいと考えているから (Because the city wants each household to reduce the amount of electricity it uses).
default.q.n3-16-q70-70.explanation:
- Summary and explanation: The passage says that K City feared that if every household turned on its air conditioner at the same time, electricity consumption would increase and lead to a power shortage. Therefore, the city launched a campaign encouraging people to turn off their home air conditioners and go to shared cool locations, thereby reducing electricity consumption in individual households.
- Question translation: Why did K City call on people to "② Turn off the air conditioner at home and go somewhere cool"?
- Answer choices:
1. Because it wanted people to take care not to become ill from the heat.
2. Because it wanted people to go to places where no one had gathered because of the heat.
3. Because it wanted households to reduce the number of air conditioners in their homes.
4. Because it wanted to reduce electricity consumption in each household.
default.q.n3-16-q70-70.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the main purpose of the appeal is to save electricity, not to promote protection against heat-related illness.
default.q.n3-16-q70-70.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the city encourages people to go to cool places such as parks, libraries, and restaurants; it is not because those places are “empty due to the heat.”
default.q.n3-16-q70-70.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the city calls on people to turn off the air conditioner when going out («エアコンを止めて»), not to reduce the number of air conditioners they own («エアコンの数を減らす»).
default.q.n3-16-q70-70.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because the activity aims to 「できるだけ夏の電気の消費量を抑えようという工夫や活動が日本の各地で始まっている。」. When people gather in cool places, 「町の中で同時に使われるエアコンはずっと減る」, reducing electricity consumption in individual households.
default.q.n3-16-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 家のエアコンを止めて来たと伝えること (to say that you turned off the air conditioner at home before coming).
default.q.n3-16-q71-71.explanation:
- Summary and explanation: According to the passage, to receive a free drink or a discount at the shops listed on the map, customers must visit the shop and say that they turned off the air conditioner at home before coming («家のエアコンを止めて来たと言えば»).
- Question translation: What is necessary to receive the special offer at the shops listed on "③ Map"?
- Answer choices:
1. Visit the shop on a day so hot that nothing can be done without air conditioning.
2. Bring the map issued by City K.
3. Say that you turned off the air conditioner at home before coming.
4. Say that you do not have an air conditioner at home.
default.q.n3-16-q71-71.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the article does not require people to visit on extremely hot days in order to receive the service.
default.q.n3-16-q71-71.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the city distributes maps to all the houses (「すべての家に配っている」), but does not require customers to bring the map in order to receive the discount.
default.q.n3-16-q71-71.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because the passage clearly states: 「この地図にある店へ行って、家のエアコンを止めて来たと言えば、飲み物の無料サービスが受けられたり、商品の割引サービスが受けられたりする。」 (If you go to a shop shown on the map and say that you turned off the air conditioner at home before coming, you can receive a free drink or a discount on products.)
default.q.n3-16-q71-71.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the intended meaning is “I turned off the air conditioner at home and then came” (エアコンを止めて来た), not “there is no air conditioner at home” (エアコンがない).
default.q.n3-16-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 夏の電気使用量を抑えるための市や町の工夫 (Measures taken by cities and towns to reduce electricity consumption in summer).
default.q.n3-16-q72-72.explanation:
- Summary and explanation: The entire passage discusses the risk of summer power shortages caused by heavy air-conditioner use, then introduces ideas and activities (工夫や活動) in local communities, particularly in City K, to curb electricity consumption («電気消費量を抑える»). Increased community interaction is merely an additional positive effect («効果も出ている»).
- Question translation: What is the topic of this passage?
- Answer choices:
1. Ideas adopted by cities and towns to limit electricity consumption in summer.
2. Ideas adopted by cities and towns to increase consumer activity in summer.
3. Ideas adopted by cities and towns to help people live in harmony with nature.
4. Ideas adopted by cities and towns to promote interaction among residents.
default.q.n3-16-q72-72.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is correct because the passage consistently focuses on local initiatives, such as those in City K, to reduce summer electricity consumption by encouraging people to turn off their air conditioners at home and spend time in shared cool spaces («できるだけ夏の電気の消費量を抑えようという工夫や活動が日本の各地で始まっている»).
default.q.n3-16-q72-72.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is incorrect because the main purpose of the campaign is to save electricity, not to promote shopping or consumer activity (消費活動).
default.q.n3-16-q72-72.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because parks and temples are merely examples of cool places; the article is not intended to help residents live in nature.
default.q.n3-16-q72-72.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the increase in communication among people is merely an additional effect («コミュニケーションが盛んになるという効果も出ている»), not the original main topic.
default.q.n3-16-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 2: Discovering that they shared an interest in the same anime while working together helped the character 「私」 talk more naturally with Tanaka.
default.q.n3-16-q73-73.explanation:
- Main point: In paragraph 2, the narrator 「私」 is initially very nervous and has difficulty communicating. However, while the two of them are making a poster for the school festival, they discover that they both like the same anime. This shared interest gradually enables 「私」 to talk naturally with Tanaka.
- Question translation: What helped 「私」 talk naturally with Tanaka?
- Answer choices:
  1. Tanaka taught 「私」 how to speak well in front of a crowd.
  2. While working together, they discovered that they had a common interest.
  3. While making the cultural festival poster, 「私」 did not express any opinions and left everything to Tanaka.
  4. Tanaka invited 「私」 to work together on the cultural festival committee.
default.q.n3-16-q73-73.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage does not say that Tanaka taught 「私」 how to speak skillfully in front of a large audience.
default.q.n3-16-q73-73.why.1: (b) Correct. Paragraph 2 clearly states: 「作業を進めるうちに、私たちが同じアニメが好きだとわかり、少しずつ自然に話せるようになりました。」 (As we worked, we discovered that we both liked the same anime, and gradually became able to talk naturally).
default.q.n3-16-q73-73.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Tanaka repeatedly took the initiative to ask for the author’s opinion (「どんな絵を描きたい？」と私の意見を何度も聞いてくれました); the author did not hide their opinion or leave everything to Tanaka.
default.q.n3-16-q73-73.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Paragraph 1 only states that the author and Tanaka, a classmate, were assigned to make the poster together (同じクラスの田中君と一緒にポスターを作る係になりました); it does not say that Tanaka invited the author.
default.q.n3-16-q74-74.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The author's main message is that, in order to build good relationships with others, it is essential to care about and listen attentively to what the other person has to say.
default.q.n3-16-q74-74.explanation:
- Main point: In the final paragraph, the author summarizes the most important lesson learned through the experience with Tanaka: to become close to people and build good relationships, what matters is not forcing oneself to tell jokes or interesting stories, but showing interest in and listening attentively to what the other person shares.
- Question translation: What does the narrator most want to convey through this essay?
- Answer choices:
  1. Clearly communicating one’s own opinions to the other person is the best way to make good friends.
  2. Even if two people share interests, it is difficult to become close when their personalities are completely opposite.
  3. To build good relationships with people, it is important to be interested in and listen attentively to what they have to say.
  4. To avoid becoming tense when speaking in front of a group, one should prepare interesting topics in advance.
default.q.n3-16-q74-74.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage does not say that clearly expressing one’s opinion is the best way to make friends; its focus is on listening to the other person.
default.q.n3-16-q74-74.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Contrary to the passage, although the two people had opposite personalities (静かな私とは正反対), they ultimately became close friends through understanding and listening to each other (何でも相談できる親友).
default.q.n3-16-q74-74.why.2: (c) Correct. Paragraph 3 clearly states the central lesson the author wants to convey: 「人と親しくなるために大切なのは、無理に面白い話をすることではなく、相手の話に興味を持って耳を傾けることだと学びました。」
default.q.n3-16-q74-74.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author clearly says that the important thing is not forcing oneself to tell interesting stories (無理に面白い話をすることではなく), so this choice misses the main point.
default.q.n3-16-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (ちょくぜつ).
default.q.n3-16-q1-1.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: "I spoke directly with Section Chief Nakamura."
- Sino-Japanese reading: 直接 (CHOKUSETSU).
- Example: 詳しいことは直接会って話しましょう。(Let's meet in person and discuss the details.)
default.q.n3-16-q1-1.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 接 is pronounced せつ in this word, not voiced to ぜつ.
default.q.n3-16-q1-1.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 直 (ON-READING) is pronounced with the short sound ちょく, not the long vowel ちょう (which can be confused with 調節 - ちょうせつ: adjustment).
default.q.n3-16-q1-1.why.2: (c) Correct because 直接 is correctly read as ちょくせつ and means “directly.”
default.q.n3-16-q1-1.why.3: (d) Both kanji are misread: 直 is not read ちょう, and 接 is not read ぜつ.
default.q.n3-16-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (もえません).
default.q.n3-16-q2-2.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: "This won't catch fire right away."
- Sino-Japanese reading: 燃 (NEN — burn, catch fire).
- Example: プラスチックは燃やすと黒い煙が出ます。(Burning plastic produces black smoke.)
default.q.n3-16-q2-2.why.0: (a) Incorrect: にえません is the polite negative form of 煮える, meaning to become cooked or simmered until tender.
default.q.n3-16-q2-2.why.1: (b) Incorrect because ひえません is the polite negative form of the verb 冷える (to cool down or become cold).
default.q.n3-16-q2-2.why.2: (c) Incorrect because きえません is the polite negative form of the verb 消える, meaning “go out” or “disappear.”
default.q.n3-16-q2-2.why.3: (d) Correct because the kanji 燃 (NEN) in the verb 燃える is read as もえる (“to burn”), and its polite negative form is 燃えません (もえません).
default.q.n3-16-q3-3.explanation:
- Meaning: "Please park your car in this spot."
- Kanji reading: 位置 (position, location).
- Example: 自分の現在位置を地図で確認する。(Check your current location on a map.)
default.q.n3-16-q3-3.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 位 is read い, not と.
default.q.n3-16-q3-3.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 置 is read ち, not じ; it may be confused with 維持 - いじ (to maintain).
default.q.n3-16-q3-3.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 位 has been confused with 土 in 土地 (とち: land, a plot of land).
default.q.n3-16-q3-3.why.3: (d) Correct because 位 is read い and 置 is read ち, forming 位置 (いち: position).
default.q.n3-16-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (けいさん).
default.q.n3-16-q4-4.explanation:
- Meaning: "I've finished calculating it, so please take a look."
- 計算 means calculation.
- Example: 電卓を使って合計金額を計算する。(I use a calculator to calculate the total amount.)
default.q.n3-16-q4-4.why.0: (a) Incorrect because けいかく is the reading of 計画 (plan).
default.q.n3-16-q4-4.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 算 is pronounced さん, not voiced as ざん.
default.q.n3-16-q4-4.why.2: (c) Correct because 計 is read as けい and 算 as さん, forming 計算 (けいさん: calculation).
default.q.n3-16-q4-4.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 算 is not read as がく; it is easily confused with 額 in 金額 or with characters in words such as 計画.
default.q.n3-16-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (まわして).
default.q.n3-16-q5-5.explanation:
- Meaning: “Using the computer continuously was tiring, so I tried rotating my arm.”
- Kanji: 回 conveys the idea of turning or rotating.
- Common expression: 腕を回す (to rotate or swing one’s arm in a circular motion).
- Example: ネジを右に回して締める。(Turn the screw to the right to tighten it.)
default.q.n3-16-q5-5.why.0: (a) Correct. 回 in the verb 回す is read まわす (to turn or rotate), and its te-form is 回して (まわして).
default.q.n3-16-q5-5.why.1: (b) Incorrect because おして is the て-form of 押す (to press, to push).
default.q.n3-16-q5-5.why.2: (c) Incorrect because おろして is the te-form of 下ろす / 降ろす (to lower, put down, or let someone off).
default.q.n3-16-q5-5.why.3: (d) Incorrect because のばして is the te-form of the verb 伸ばす (to stretch out, extend).
default.q.n3-16-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (きんえん).
default.q.n3-16-q6-6.explanation:
- Meaning: "Smoking is prohibited here."
- Kanji reading: 禁煙 (no smoking, smoking prohibited).
- Example: 館内は全席禁煙となっております。(All seats inside the building are non-smoking.)
default.q.n3-16-q6-6.why.0: (a) Incorrect because it omits the ん sound in 禁; きねん is usually the reading of 記念, meaning “commemoration.”
default.q.n3-16-q6-6.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the on-reading of 禁 is きん, not き.
default.q.n3-16-q6-6.why.2: (c) Incorrect because it adds an extra n consonant, confusing it with 近年 - きんねん, meaning “recent years.”
default.q.n3-16-q6-6.why.3: (d) Correct because 禁 is read きん and 煙 is read えん; together they form 禁煙 (きんえん: no smoking).
default.q.n3-16-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (むすんで).
default.q.n3-16-q7-7.explanation:
- Meaning: "Please tie it again neatly."
- Sino-Japanese reading: 結 (KETSU: to tie, knot, or connect). Common expression: 紐・ネクタイを結ぶ (tie a shoelace / tie a necktie).
- Example: 靴のひもをしっかり結んだ。(I tied my shoelaces tightly.)
default.q.n3-16-q7-7.why.0: (a) Incorrect because たたんで is the te-form of 畳む (to fold, as clothes or bedding).
default.q.n3-16-q7-7.why.1: (b) Correct because the 結 in the verb 結ぶ is read むすぶ (to tie or fasten), and its te-form is 結んで (むすんで).
default.q.n3-16-q7-7.why.2: (c) Incorrect because つつんで is the te-form of 包む (to wrap or package gifts/things).
default.q.n3-16-q7-7.why.3: (d) Incorrect because ならんで is the te-form of the verb 並ぶ (to line up, stand in a row).
default.q.n3-16-q8-8.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (しゅじゅつ).
default.q.n3-16-q8-8.explanation:
- Meaning: “The illness will get better without surgery, so don’t worry.”
- Kanji: 手術 (しゅじゅつ): surgery, operation.
- Example: 胃の手術を受けて無事に退院した。(I underwent stomach surgery and was safely discharged from the hospital.)
default.q.n3-16-q8-8.why.0: (a) Correct because 手 (しゅ) and 術 (じゅつ) combine to form 手術 (しゅじゅつ: surgery).
default.q.n3-16-q8-8.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 手 was mistakenly read with its kun-reading て.
default.q.n3-16-q8-8.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 術 is read as じゅつ, not with the sound in しゅつ.
default.q.n3-16-q8-8.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 手 is misread as て and 術 is incorrectly read as しゅつ.
default.q.n3-16-q9-9.explanation:
Meaning: "The next target is 10 seconds."
• 秒 (びょう): second, a unit of time; 1分 = 60秒.
• Example: あと10秒で試合が終了します。(The game will end in 10 seconds.)
default.q.n3-16-q9-9.why.0: (a) The kanji「培」in 栽培 (さいばい) has the on-reading ばい (bai), not びょう.
default.q.n3-16-q9-9.why.1: (b) 「抄」, as in 抄本（しょうほん）, has the on-reading しょう (shō); it does not represent the unit of seconds.
default.q.n3-16-q9-9.why.2: (c) 「倍」, as in ２倍 (にばい), has the on-reading ばい and means “times” or “multiple,” not “second.”
default.q.n3-16-q9-9.why.3: (d) 「秒」has the on-reading びょう (byō) and denotes the unit of time “second.” 「10秒」means 10 seconds.
default.q.n3-16-q10-10.explanation:
Meaning: “The ball flew far away.”
• 飛ぶ (とぶ): to fly, to pass through the air. A Group 1 verb ending in ぶ; its past form is 飛んだ (とんだ).
• Example: 鳥が空高く飛んでいきました。(The birds flew high into the sky.)
default.q.n3-16-q10-10.why.0: (a) 「投」 (TOU) in 投げる (なげる – to throw) forms the past tense 投げた (なげた), not 投んだ.
default.q.n3-16-q10-10.why.1: (b) 「打」 in 打つ (うつ: to hit or strike) has the past form 打った (うった), not 打んだ.
default.q.n3-16-q10-10.why.2: (c) 「飛」 (PHI) in 飛ぶ (とぶ - to fly) is a Group 1 verb ending in ぶ, so its past form is 飛んだ (とんだ), which is completely correct.
default.q.n3-16-q10-10.why.3: (d) 「転んだ」is read ころんだ, the past form of 転ぶ (ころぶ: to fall), not とんだ.
default.q.n3-16-q11-11.explanation:
Meaning: “There are a lot of slopes here, aren’t there?”
• 坂道 (さかみち): slope or hill.
• Related words: 坂 (さか: slope), 上り坂 (のぼりざか: uphill slope), 下り坂 (くだりざか: downhill slope).
• Example: この坂道を上ると、きれいな海が見えます。(If you go up this slope, you can see the beautiful sea.)
default.q.n3-16-q11-11.why.0: (a) 「岩道」 (いわみち): a rocky mountain path, not read as さかみち.
default.q.n3-16-q11-11.why.1: (b) 「板道」(いたみち): a road paved with wooden planks; it does not mean a sloping road.
default.q.n3-16-q11-11.why.2: (c) 「石道」 (いしみち): a stony path; it is not read as さかみち.
default.q.n3-16-q11-11.why.3: (d) 「坂道」(さかみち): a compound of 坂 (さか - slope) and 道 (みち - road), meaning “sloping road,” which matches the question.
default.q.n3-16-q12-12.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (違います).
default.q.n3-16-q12-12.explanation:
Sentence meaning: 'Only this plate is a different color.'
• 違う (ちがう): to differ, be different, be mistaken. Polite form: 違います (ちがいます).
• Easily confused kanji with the same radical: 違, 遺, 達, 遅, 遠.

default.q.n3-16-q32-32.explanation:
「身につける (みにつける)」has two main meanings:
1. To acquire, learn, or develop knowledge, skills, or habits: 知識・技術・習慣を身につける.
2. To wear or carry on one’s person, referring to clothing and accessories: 服・時計・アクセサリーを身につける.
Example: 若いうちに外国語の能力を身につけておきたい。(I want to acquire foreign-language skills while I am still young.)
default.q.n3-16-q32-32.why.0: Incorrect because with friends, use 「たくさんの友人がいる」 (have many friends) or 「友人を作る」 (make friends); 「身につける」 is not used for people.
default.q.n3-16-q32-32.why.1: Correct because 「知識を身につける」 (to acquire or absorb knowledge) is the standard fixed expression for learning and developing knowledge and skills.
default.q.n3-16-q32-32.why.2: Incorrect because talking about nourishing the body or taking in nutrients requires「栄養をとる」or「栄養をつける」, not「栄養を身につける」.
default.q.n3-16-q32-32.why.3: Incorrect because the appropriate expression for taking a dog for a walk is 「犬を連れて」 (taking the pet along), not 「身につける」.
default.q.n3-16-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 新しい冷蔵庫は高いので先輩から中古をもらったが、問題なく使えそうだ。
default.q.n3-16-q33-33.explanation:
「中古 (ちゅうこ)」means “second-hand” or “used” and is used only for objects, equipment, property, vehicles, household appliances, houses, books, and similar items.
Example: 予算が足りないので、中古のパソコンを買うことにした。(I did not have enough money, so I decided to buy a used computer.)
default.q.n3-16-q33-33.why.0: Incorrect because 「中古」 is used only for secondhand goods; for experienced or core personnel in a company, use 「中堅 (ちゅうけん)」 or 「ベテラン」.
default.q.n3-16-q33-33.why.1: Incorrect because old or outdated information is described with 「古い」(古い情報); 「中古」is not used for information or news.
default.q.n3-16-q33-33.why.2: Correct because 「中古」 is used for previously used equipment or objects. Here, 「中古（の冷蔵庫）」 naturally and accurately means a used refrigerator.
default.q.n3-16-q33-33.why.3: Incorrect because 「中古」 is not used for feelings or relationships; to describe a friendship growing distant, use words such as 「薄れる (うすれる)」 or 「疎遠になる」.
default.q.n3-16-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 友人に映画に行こうと言われたが、用事があるので誘いを断った。
default.q.n3-16-q34-34.explanation:
「断る (ことわる)」 means:
1. To refuse or turn down (an invitation, request, proposal, or demand: 誘い・依頼・提案・要求を断る).
2. To give advance notice or ask permission in advance (断りを入れる).
Example: 急な残業が入ってしまったため、せっかくの食事の誘いを断らざるを得なかった。(Because unexpected overtime came up, I had no choice but to turn down the invitation to dinner.)
default.q.n3-16-q34-34.why.0: Incorrect because not giving up on a dream should be expressed as 「夢を諦めなかった」 (あきらめなかった) or 「夢を捨てなかった」, not 「断る」, which is not used for dreams.
default.q.n3-16-q34-34.why.1: Incorrect because denying or rejecting a rumor uses 「否定する」(ひていする), not 「断る」 with a rumor (うわさ).
default.q.n3-16-q34-34.why.2: Incorrect because leaving a company is expressed with 「会社を辞める」 (やめる) or 「退職する」, not 「会社を断る」.
default.q.n3-16-q34-34.why.3: Correct because 「誘いを断る」 (“decline an invitation”) is a completely standard and common collocation.
default.q.n3-16-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 送ってくださった資料は、本日確かに受取りました。
default.q.n3-16-q35-35.explanation:
「受取る / 受け取る (うけとる)」 means:
1. To receive or accept an object, parcel, document, money, etc. that has been handed or sent to you (手紙・荷物・給料・資料を受け取る).
2. To interpret or take something in a particular way (好意的に受け取る, 冗談として受け取る).
Example: 郵便局から配達された荷物を無事に受け取った。(I safely received the package delivered by the post office.)
default.q.n3-16-q35-35.why.0: Incorrect because when stretching out one's arms to catch and embrace a child who is running toward them, use 「抱きとめる」 (だきとめる) or 「受け止める」, not 「受取る」, which is not used for people.
default.q.n3-16-q35-35.why.1: Incorrect because accepting a homestay student into a family uses 「受け入れる」(うけいれる), not 「受取る」.
default.q.n3-16-q35-35.why.2: Correct because 「（資料・荷物などを）受取る」 is the standard expression for receiving documents or items that have been sent.
default.q.n3-16-q35-35.why.3: Incorrect because catching someone's arm when they are about to fall is expressed with 「腕を支える」 (“support the arm”) or 「つかむ」, not 「受取る」.
default.q.n3-17-q36-36.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ばかり, because it forms the grammar pattern 「〜ばかりで（は）なく〜も」 (not only... but also...).
default.q.n3-17-q36-36.explanation:
Meaning of the whole sentence: "During my study-abroad period, there were not only many enjoyable experiences but also many difficult ones, yet the year I spent studying abroad became a very valuable experience for me."
Structure:「〜ばかりで（は）なく〜も」 expresses “not only... but also...”
Example: 彼女は英語ばかりでなく、フランス語も話せる。(She can speak not only English but also French.)
default.q.n3-17-q36-36.why.0: (a) Correct. The sentence pattern 「〜ばかりで（は）なく〜も」means “not only ... but also ...”.
default.q.n3-17-q36-36.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「なんか」is generally used to introduce an example with a dismissive or minimizing nuance, so it does not form an appropriate sentence pattern here.
default.q.n3-17-q36-36.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「しか」usually occurs with a negative form, 「〜しか...ない」 (“only ...”), and cannot be combined as 「〜しかではなく」.
default.q.n3-17-q36-36.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「でも」 (even if it is...) cannot combine as 「〜でもではなく」 to express this contrastive relationship.
default.q.n3-17-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 4. にしたがって, because it expresses a change that occurs along with another change: “as ...; the more ..., the more ...”.
default.q.n3-17-q37-37.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "When I first started working at the restaurant, I was nervous every day, but as I gradually became accustomed to the job, I became able to talk with customers with a smile."
Structure: 「V-る + にしたがって」expresses a change in the latter clause that accompanies a change in the former clause (the more..., the more... / as...).
Example: 台風が近づくにしたがって、風が強くなってきた。(As the typhoon approached, the wind grew stronger.)
default.q.n3-17-q37-37.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「〜までに」 indicates a deadline (by/before), not a progressive change that leads to another result.
default.q.n3-17-q37-37.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜たびに」means “every time,” and is not used with a following clause expressing gradual change (〜ようになってきた).
default.q.n3-17-q37-37.why.2: (c) Incorrect.「〜のに対して」is used to compare two contrasting clauses.
default.q.n3-17-q37-37.why.3: (d) Correct. 「V-る + にしたがって」 indicates that as change A occurs, change B follows along with it (as one becomes accustomed to the work, one becomes more comfortable laughing and chatting).
default.q.n3-17-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 2. ようやく, because it means “at last” after a long period of waiting.
default.q.n3-17-q38-38.explanation:
Meaning of the whole sentence: "The rain that had continued falling for three days finally stopped, and today we could see the blue sky."
Related vocabulary: 青空 (blue sky).
Example: 長いトンネルを抜けて、ようやく目的地に着いた。(After passing through a long tunnel, we finally reached our destination.)
default.q.n3-17-q38-38.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「今にも」 means “at any moment” or “about to,” and is often used with 「〜そうだ」 to describe something about to happen.
default.q.n3-17-q38-38.why.1: (b) Correct.「ようやく」 means "at last" and describes an expected result achieved after a long time (three consecutive days of rain).
default.q.n3-17-q38-38.why.2: (c) Incorrect.「絶対」means “absolutely” or “certainly,” and is not used to describe an event that has already occurred as in this sentence.
default.q.n3-17-q38-38.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「あまりに」usually comes before an adjective or verb to indicate an excessive degree, and does not come before 「やんで」.
default.q.n3-17-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 便利である一方で because it expresses two parallel sides of an issue: "while it is convenient, on the other hand...".
default.q.n3-17-q39-39.explanation:
Meaning of the whole sentence: "Online shopping is convenient in one respect, but on the other hand, it is frightening not to be able to see the seller's face."
Pattern: 「〜一方で（は）」 expresses two contrasting aspects or two characteristics that coexist in parallel.
Example: 一人暮らしは自由である一方で、寂しさも感じる。(Living alone is liberating in one respect, but I also feel lonely.)
default.q.n3-17-q39-39.why.0: (a) Correct. 「〜一方で」 expresses two aspects existing simultaneously: the convenience is a positive aspect, while not being able to see the seller’s face is a concern.
default.q.n3-17-q39-39.why.1: (b) Incorrect.「〜のだから」expresses an obvious reason (“because...”), and does not create a contrastive relationship with the following clause.
default.q.n3-17-q39-39.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The word is misspelled (only 利 is used instead of 便利), and the conditional structure 「〜だとすると」 does not fit.
default.q.n3-17-q39-39.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜ように」 indicates a purpose or wish and does not fit the contrasting comparison structure in the following clause.
default.q.n3-17-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 入れ, because the transitive verb 「入れる」 forms 入れたがる by removing ます and adding 「〜たがる」 (V-stem + たがる).
default.q.n3-17-q40-40.explanation:
Meaning of the full sentence: “Babies want to put anything they can get hold of into their mouths, so be careful not to leave dangerous objects nearby.”
Structure: The transitive verb「口に入れる」(put into one's mouth) combines with the third-person desiderative form「V-stem + たがる」to become「口に入れたがる」.
default.q.n3-17-q40-40.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「入れる」is in the dictionary form and cannot combine directly with the ending 「〜たがる」.
default.q.n3-17-q40-40.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「入る」 is an intransitive verb in dictionary form, so it is unsuitable both grammatically and in terms of the required combination.
default.q.n3-17-q40-40.why.2: (c) Correct. The transitive verb 「入れる」loses ます to become 「入れ」, which combines with 「〜たがる」to form 「入れたがる」(want to put something in).
default.q.n3-17-q40-40.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「入り」 is the conjunctive form of the intransitive verb 「入る」, whereas the sentence requires the transitive verb indicating the action of putting something into the mouth.
default.q.n3-17-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 間に合いそうになくて, because it expresses an apologetic prediction: “It looks like I won’t make it in time for the appointment, so ...”.
default.q.n3-17-q41-41.explanation:
The meaning of the entire conversation:
Minami: "Hello?"
Yamashita: "Oh, hi, Minami. Sorry. I'm hurrying over to your place now, but it looks like I won't make it by the appointed time..."
Minami: "That's okay. I'll go sit and wait in a café, so take your time getting here."
Structure: 「V-stem + そうにない」expresses the negative conjecture "it doesn't look like..."; its て-form connection is 「〜そうになくて」.
Example: 雨で道が混んでいて、集合時間に間に合いそうにない。(The roads are congested because of the rain, so it doesn't look like I'll make it by the meeting time.)
default.q.n3-17-q41-41.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「〜に違いなくて」 means “certainly be on time,” which is completely opposite to the context of apologizing for being late.
default.q.n3-17-q41-41.why.1: (b) Correct. 「V-stem + そうにない」 expresses the judgment "it seems unlikely that..."; the te-form becomes 「間に合いそうになくて」 (it seems we will not make it in time, so...).
default.q.n3-17-q41-41.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜はずがない」 means “there is no way that...,” so 「間に合わないはずがなくて」 means “there is no way [someone] will not be on time,” or “will certainly be on time,” which does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-17-q41-41.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「間に合わせないといけなくて」 means “I have to make it in time”; it is not used to explain to someone that one may be late for an appointment.
default.q.n3-17-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 入るな, because danger signs use the prohibitive form 「V-る + な」 (“Do not...” ).
default.q.n3-17-q42-42.explanation:
- Full sentence meaning: “The pond near the elementary school is very deep, and it is dangerous for children to play there, so several years ago the townspeople put up a sign saying, ‘Danger! Do not enter the pond!’”
Grammar: The prohibition form uses the dictionary form of a verb + な (「V-る + な」: do not...).
Example: ここにゴミを捨てるな。(Do not throw garbage here.)
default.q.n3-17-q42-42.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「入ろう」 is the volitional form, meaning “let's enter,” so it is not used on a warning sign prohibiting entry because of danger.
default.q.n3-17-q42-42.why.1: (b) Incorrect.「入って」is the te-form used for a request or gentle command (“please come in”).
default.q.n3-17-q42-42.why.2: (c) Correct. The prohibitive form 「V-る + な」 is used to give a strong prohibition: 「池に入るな」 (Do not enter the pond!).
default.q.n3-17-q42-42.why.3: (d) Incorrect.「入りなさい」is an imperative meaning “come in,” which goes against the purpose of warning about danger.
default.q.n3-17-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 買ってしまう。 because the adverb 「つい」 is used with the pattern 「〜てしまう」 (to end up doing something unintentionally).
default.q.n3-17-q43-43.explanation:
Meaning: "I know I should try on shoes to make sure they fit before buying them, but whenever I see a pair I like online, I end up buying them impulsively."
Structure: 「つい + V-てしまう」 describes doing something unintentionally or impulsively, despite knowing one should not.
Example: ダイエット中なのに、つい甘いものを食べてしまう。(Even though I am dieting, I keep ending up eating sweets.)
default.q.n3-17-q43-43.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「〜ところだ」 indicates that someone is about to do something and is not used with the adverb 「つい」.
default.q.n3-17-q43-43.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜ことにする」expresses a deliberate decision by oneself, so it does not fit the accidental or unintentional meaning of 「つい」.
default.q.n3-17-q43-43.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜てほしい」 expresses a desire for someone else to do something for you.
default.q.n3-17-q43-43.why.3: (d) Correct. The familiar pattern 「つい + V-てしまう」 expresses accidentally or unintentionally doing something despite knowing one should not.
default.q.n3-17-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 1. だけでも because it expresses the meaning “even just today alone, I have already seen it twice.”
default.q.n3-17-q44-44.explanation:
Meaning: “Since last week, a cat has been coming to my garden frequently. Just today alone, I saw it twice, once in the morning and once in the afternoon.”
Structure: 「〜だけでも」 means “even just... / just ... alone,” and is used to give a representative example to emphasize degree or frequency.
Example: この映画は、予告編を見るだけでも感動する。(This movie is moving even if you only watch the trailer.)
default.q.n3-17-q44-44.why.0: (a) Correct. 「〜だけでも」 means "even just ..." or "just ... alone is already enough," emphasizing a high frequency by giving the example that the speaker saw it twice today alone.
default.q.n3-17-q44-44.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜までには」 indicates a deadline by which an action must be completed.
default.q.n3-17-q44-44.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜だけに」 means “precisely because..., all the more...,” so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-17-q44-44.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜までで」means “up to” or “ending at,” so it is unnatural with 「2回見た」.
default.q.n3-17-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 持たないで because it describes an accompanying state: “going outside without taking an umbrella.”
default.q.n3-17-q45-45.explanation:
Meaning of the whole sentence: "Because the weather forecast said it would be sunny today, I went out without taking an umbrella, but it suddenly started raining in the evening and I got completely soaked."
Distinction: 「V-ないで + V2」describes the state accompanying another action (doing V2 without doing V1). By contrast, 「〜なくて」is mainly used to express a cause or reason.
Example: 朝ごはんを食べないで学校へ行きました。(I went to school without eating breakfast.)
default.q.n3-17-q45-45.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「〜なくて」 expresses a cause or reason; it is not used to indicate a simultaneous state while carrying out 「出かけた」.
default.q.n3-17-q45-45.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「持てなくて」 is both the potential form and an expression of cause, so it does not convey the intended meaning.
default.q.n3-17-q45-45.why.2: (c) Correct. 「V-ないで」describes an action performed without doing the preceding action (“go out without bringing an umbrella”).
default.q.n3-17-q45-45.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「持てないで」 uses the potential form (“cannot carry”), but the context requires a deliberate action of not bringing something because of the weather forecast.
default.q.n3-17-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 入ってからのほうが because it forms the comparative structure「〜てからのほうがもっと...」, meaning “after..., it is even more...”.
default.q.n3-17-q46-46.explanation:
Full sentence meaning: “Studying for the exam is tough, but after entering university, it is even tougher.”
Structure:「〜てからのほうがもっと...」is used for comparison: the period after doing something is even more...
Example: 手術を受ける前より、受けてからのほうが痛みがひどかった。(The pain was worse after the surgery than before it.)
default.q.n3-17-q46-46.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「〜たいもの」 expresses a strong desire and is not used as the comparative clause.
default.q.n3-17-q46-46.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「入れたのは」nominalizes the act of being able to enter and does not combine naturally with the comparative「もっと」in the following clause.
default.q.n3-17-q46-46.why.2: (c) Incorrect.「入るまでより」(“compared with before entering”) duplicates the exam-preparation period stated in the preceding clause, making the sentence repetitive and meaningless.
default.q.n3-17-q46-46.why.3: (d) Correct.「〜てからのほうが」refers to the period after entering university and creates a comparison with the earlier period of studying for the entrance exam.
default.q.n3-17-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 2. がしてくると because a sensation of smell takes the particle が, as in 「においがしてくる」 (a smell begins to waft over).
default.q.n3-17-q47-47.explanation:
Meaning: “In the evening, whenever I open the window, the smell of miso soup always wafts in.”
Pattern: Sensory phenomena such as smells and sounds use the particle が: 「においがする」(there is a smell). Combined with 「〜てくる」to express movement toward the speaker, it becomes 「においがしてくる」(a smell wafts in).
Example: どこからか、いいにおいがしてくる。(A pleasant smell is wafting in from somewhere.)
default.q.n3-17-q47-47.why.0: (a) Incorrect: sensory perceptions such as smells use the particle が, as in においがする, not を.
default.q.n3-17-q47-47.why.1: (b) Correct. The phrase 「においがしてくる」 indicates that a smell wafts toward the speaker, with the particle が.
default.q.n3-17-q47-47.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The particle is wrong (が should be used instead of を), and 「している」 does not express something spreading toward the speaker.
default.q.n3-17-q47-47.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜てある」describes a deliberately prepared state resulting from human action, so it is not used for a natural sensory phenomenon.
default.q.n3-17-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 2. やってしまいたいので because it expresses a reason: “because I want to finish it completely today.”
default.q.n3-17-q48-48.explanation:
Meaning of the whole dialogue:
Aoki: “Mr. Hayashi, I’m leaving now. Aren’t you going home yet?”
Hayashi: “Yes, I’ll work a little longer and then go home. I want to finish this task completely today.”
Aoki: “I see. You’re working hard.”
Pattern: 「V-てしまう」(finish something completely) combines with「〜たい」(want to) and「ので」(because) to form「〜てしまいたいので」.
default.q.n3-17-q48-48.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The conjectural ending 「〜そう」 (“seems likely”) is not used for the speaker's own subjective intention.
default.q.n3-17-q48-48.why.1: (b) Correct. 「V-てしまう」(completion) combines with「〜たい」(want to) and「ので」(because) to form「やってしまいたいので」(because I want to finish it all).
default.q.n3-17-q48-48.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜てみてもいい」 means “it is all right to try doing ~,” which does not match the context of explaining why someone stayed to work.
default.q.n3-17-q48-48.why.3: (d) Incorrect.「〜ているところだ」indicates an action or state in progress, and the conjunction「んですが」adds a hesitant tone that is unsuitable for stating a reason.
default.q.n3-17-q49-49.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (the correct order is: 1 → 3 → 2 → 4; the ★ position is 2).
default.q.n3-17-q49-49.explanation:
・ Complete sentence: レストランAは、雑誌か何かで紹介されてからなかなか予約がとれない人気店になった。
Meaning: Since being featured in a magazine or something similar, Restaurant A has become a popular establishment where it is very difficult to get a reservation.
default.q.n3-17-q49-49.why.0: (a) 「雑誌か」(1) begins the phrase and combines with 「何か」(3) to form the noun phrase 「雑誌か何か」, meaning "a magazine or something similar."
default.q.n3-17-q49-49.why.1: (b)「で」(2) is the particle indicating a means or media channel. It follows the noun phrase「雑誌か何か」and appears at ★ (position 3).
default.q.n3-17-q49-49.why.2: (c) 「何か」 (3) occupies position 2 and combines with 「雑誌か」 (1) in the approximate expression 「Aか何か」 (“A or something”).
default.q.n3-17-q49-49.why.3: (d) 「紹介されてから」(4) occupies the fourth position and uses the 「〜てから」form (“after...”) to connect to the result clause that follows.
default.q.n3-17-q50-50.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (the correct order is: 4 → 3 → 1 → 2; the ★ position is 1).
default.q.n3-17-q50-50.explanation:
Complete sentence: A:「わあ、夕日がきれいですね。」 B:「本当にすばらしいですね。こんなにきれいな夕日は見たことがありません。」
Meaning: A: "Wow, the sunset is beautiful, isn't it?" - B: "It really is wonderful. I've never seen a sunset this beautiful before."
default.q.n3-17-q50-50.why.0: (a) 「夕日は」 (1) is the main noun modified by 「こんなにきれいな」 and is made the topic with the particle 「は」. It appears at ★ (position 3).
default.q.n3-17-q50-50.why.1: (b) 「見たことが」 (2) occupies the fourth position and is directly followed by 「ありません」 at the end of the sentence to form the experiential pattern 「〜たことがありません」 (“have never seen or done something”).
default.q.n3-17-q50-50.why.2: (c) 「きれいな」(3) is a na-adjective in the second position, modified by the adverb 「こんなに」(4) and modifying the noun 「夕日は」(1).
default.q.n3-17-q50-50.why.3: (d) 「こんなに」(4) is an adverb indicating degree (“this much/so”), placed first to modify the adjective 「きれいな」(3).

default.q.n3-17-q51-51.why.1: (b) 「どちらが」(2) occupies the first position and serves as the subject with the particle 「が」in the subordinate clause 「どちらが勝っても」.
default.q.n3-17-q51-51.why.2: (c) 「おかしくない」(3) occupies the ★ position, combining with 「勝っても」(4) to form 「〜てもおかしくない」(it would not be surprising even if...), which modifies the noun 「試合」.
default.q.n3-17-q51-51.why.3: (d) 「勝っても」 (4) occupies position 2. It is the 「〜ても」 conditional form of the verb 「勝つ」 and combines with 「おかしくない」 (3).

default.q.n3-17-q52-52.explanation:
