default.q.n3-17-q52-52.why.1: (b) 「子供の」 (2) occupies the ★ position (the third position), with the particle 「の」 replacing 「が」 as the subject of the relative clause 「興味がある」.

default.q.n3-17-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 2. すると.
default.q.n3-17-q54-54.explanation:
Before the blank is the sentence:「食べ終わって話していたとき、掃除の時間を知らせる放送が流れました。」(When we had finished eating and were talking, an announcement notifying us that it was time to clean up came over the speaker.) The next sentence is:「＿＿、予想外のことが起きました。子供たちが教室の前に机といすを運び始めたのです。」(Just then/As a result, something unexpected happened. The children began carrying the desks and chairs to the front of the classroom.)
The conjunction「すると」describes an event that occurs immediately after a preceding action or event in chronological order, often leading to an unexpected development or new discovery. Therefore,「すると」is the most appropriate answer.
default.q.n3-17-q54-54.why.0: (a) 「つまり」means "in other words / in summary" and is used to explain or summarize the preceding idea, not to introduce what happens next in the story.
default.q.n3-17-q54-54.why.1: (b) 「すると」 means “immediately afterward” or “then,” linking an event that occurs right after the preceding event. It is natural and correct here, following the announcement over the loudspeaker.
default.q.n3-17-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「結局」 means “in the end” or “ultimately,” referring to the final result after a long process; it does not fit a situation at the present moment.
default.q.n3-17-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「例えば」means “for example” and is used to introduce an illustrative example, so it is not suitable for continuing a sequence of actions.
default.q.n3-17-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 驚きました.
default.q.n3-17-q55-55.explanation:
The subject of the passage is the author (first person 「私」). Immediately after this sentence, the author explains the reason: 「私の小学校では掃除は掃除の会社の人がしていたので、子供が掃除するのを見たのは初めてだったのです。」(At my elementary school, cleaning was done by employees of a cleaning company, so it was the first time I had seen children clean.)
Therefore, 「これを見て、とても＿＿」(Seeing this, I was very...) requires a verb directly expressing the writer's own past emotion or state, namely 「驚きました」. The conjectural form (ようです) and passive form (驚かれました) are both inappropriate because the first-person subject is describing their own feelings.
default.q.n3-17-q55-55.why.0: (a) 「驚きました」 directly describes the author’s own past emotional state—“I was very surprised”—when witnessing the event, so it is completely correct.
default.q.n3-17-q55-55.why.1: (b) 「驚かれました」is passive or honorific language, and is not used to describe the writer’s own feelings.
default.q.n3-17-q55-55.why.2: (c) 「驚いたようです」means “seems to have been surprised” or “appears surprised,” expressing an inference about another person’s feelings in the third person. It is not used for one’s own emotions.
default.q.n3-17-q55-55.why.3: (d) 「驚かれたようです。」combines the passive/honorific form with the conjectural expression 「〜ようです」, making it incorrect in both point of view and nuance.
default.q.n3-17-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 3. その.
default.q.n3-17-q56-56.explanation:
In paragraph 1, the author writes:「先週、日本の小学校を訪問しました。小学校で最初に思ったのは、子供がたくさんいるのにごみが落ちていないということでした。」(Last week, I visited an elementary school in Japan. The first thing I thought at the school was that, although there were many children, not a single piece of trash had been dropped.)
In paragraph 3, the author refers back to this:「私は、これが＿＿学校にごみが落ちていなかった理由だと思います。」(I think this was the reason that there was no trash at that school.)
The demonstrative 「その」is used in written language to refer back to a specific object or place mentioned in the preceding passage—in this case, the Japanese elementary school the author had just visited.
default.q.n3-17-q56-56.why.0: (a) 「ある」 refers to some unspecified school, which is inappropriate because this refers to the specific school that was just visited.
default.q.n3-17-q56-56.why.1: (b) 「あらゆる」 means “every” or “all kinds of,” so it is unsuitable because the author is explaining a specific phenomenon witnessed at the school they visited.
default.q.n3-17-q56-56.why.2: (c) 「その」is a textual demonstrative that replaces a noun mentioned earlier (“that school”), making the sentence cohesive and grammatically correct.
default.q.n3-17-q56-56.why.3: (d) 「私の」means "my school", which is incorrect because the author's overseas school had dedicated cleaning staff; it is not the school being described as having no litter.
default.q.n3-17-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 4. なら.
default.q.n3-17-q57-57.explanation:
The author recalls that, as a child, they did not care about litter in the classroom, but would pick up litter at home and always wanted to keep their room clean. From this, the author infers the following psychological tendency:「きっと、自分や自分の知っている人が掃除した場所＿＿大切に使うのでしょう。」(People probably use and take better care of a place if they themselves or someone they know cleaned it.)
The particle 「なら」 introduces a hypothetical or limited topic/condition (“if it is …” / “when it comes to …”), making it a perfect fit with the predicate 「大切に使う」that follows.
default.q.n3-17-q57-57.why.0: (a) 「などに」 indicates examples combined with a direction or location, so it does not connect naturally with the predicate phrase 「大切に使う」.
default.q.n3-17-q57-57.why.1: (b) 「よりは」 is used in comparative structures ("rather than..."), so it does not fit because this sentence has no contrasting comparison.
default.q.n3-17-q57-57.why.2: (c) 「でも」 expresses concession (“even if” or “even...”), which conflicts with the logic here because taking care of a place one has cleaned oneself is natural, not an exceptional or paradoxical case.
default.q.n3-17-q57-57.why.3: (d) 「なら」introduces a topic or limited condition meaning “if it is...” or “in the case of....” It correctly expresses the idea that if it is a place one has cleaned oneself, one will appreciate and take care of it.
default.q.n3-17-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 身についていいと思います.
default.q.n3-17-q58-58.explanation:
The previous sentence concludes:「「掃除の時間」は学校がきれいになるだけではありません。」(“Cleaning time” does not merely make the school clean.)
The following sentence continues by presenting a greater benefit of this activity:「みんなで使う場所をきれいに使う習慣が＿＿。」
The structure「〜ていい」(it is good that…) combined with「〜と思います」(I think that…) forms「身についていいと思います」, expressing the author's positive view: “I think it is good that the habit of keeping shared spaces clean becomes established.”
default.q.n3-17-q58-58.why.0: (a) 「身についてもいいです」expresses permission or minimal acceptance (“it is okay if it becomes a habit”), so it does not fit the article’s purpose of praising the activity and presenting its positive benefits.
default.q.n3-17-q58-58.why.1: (b) 「身についていいだけです」means “it is only good when it becomes a habit,” but the sentence is incomplete and fails to express the writer’s thoughts or feelings.
default.q.n3-17-q58-58.why.2: (c) 「身についていいと思います」naturally and completely expresses the writer’s opinion: developing the habit of maintaining public cleanliness is a very good thing.
default.q.n3-17-q58-58.why.3: (d) 「身についてもいいと思うだけです」 means “I only think it would be fine if it became a habit,” conveying a half-hearted attitude that does not fit the positive tone of the passage.

What kind of trip is referred to by the phrase "①a trip like this"?

1. A trip for which nothing was reserved in advance.
2. A trip to stay at a hot-spring inn with a friend.
3. A trip for which information was gathered about three months in advance.
4. A trip that was not carefully planned.

At the end of this trip, what did “I” think about traveling?

default.q.n3-17-q65-65.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author enjoyed the trip and felt that even the failures became good memories. The author thought, 「たまにはこんな旅行でもいい」 (a trip like this is fine once in a while), not that they never wanted to travel again.
default.q.n3-17-q65-65.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author has no intention whatsoever of giving up traveling.
default.q.n3-17-q65-65.why.2: (c) Correct because the conclusion states: 「今回の旅行はいつもとは少し違いましたが、楽しかったです。失敗もいい思い出になりました。いつものような旅行のほうが安心ですが、たまにはこんな旅行でもいいと思いました」 (This trip was somewhat different from usual, but it was fun. The failures also became good memories. Traveling as usual feels more reassuring, but I think a trip like this is fine once in a while.)
default.q.n3-17-q65-65.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the author normally always plans trips carefully in advance (ふだん、私は旅行の三か月くらい前から情報を集めてしっかり計画を立てます), rather than only occasionally planning a trip.
default.q.n3-17-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 3: This town has an abundance of leaves, and even elderly people can gather them easily and without difficulty.
default.q.n3-17-q66-66.explanation:
Main point: A town official learned that Japanese restaurants in the city had difficulty finding attractive leaves for food presentation, while this rural town was 85% forest, with abundant leaves that were lightweight and easy to collect—making the work well suited to older people.

Question translation:
Why does the author say, "This work is a perfect fit for this town"?

Answer choices:
1. Because the town has many Japanese restaurants that serve dishes decorated with attractive leaves.
2. Because many older people in the town want to sell leaves in the city.
3. Because the town has countless leaves that older people can also easily collect.
4. Because the town has many forests and has collected attractive leaves for sale since long ago.
default.q.n3-17-q66-66.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because restaurants serving Japanese food needed decorative leaves in the city (「都会の店では、このような葉がなかなか手に入らなかった」), not because this town had many Japanese restaurants.
default.q.n3-17-q66-66.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the business idea originated with a town hall employee («ある田舎の町の役所の人が...思いついた»), not with elderly people who had already wanted to sell leaves.
default.q.n3-17-q66-66.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because it directly quotes the passage: «葉はいくらでもあるし、軽くて簡単に集められる。お年寄りが多いこの町にぴったりの仕事だったのだ» (There were plenty of leaves, and they were light and easy to collect, so it was the perfect job for a town with many elderly people).
default.q.n3-17-q66-66.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because this was a new business idea conceived by a municipal employee (「売ることを思いついた」), not work that local residents had been doing since long ago (「昔から...」).
default.q.n3-17-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 2: Older people stay healthier because they actively work while using both their minds and bodies.
default.q.n3-17-q67-67.explanation:
Main idea: Elderly people borrowed computers to select orders, went into the mountains themselves to gather leaves and earn income, exercised both their minds and bodies, and became happier, more energetic, and healthier. As a result, the number of people who needed to visit the hospital decreased significantly.

Translation of the question:
The passage says, “The number of people visiting the hospital decreased.” What does the author believe was the reason?

Translation of the choices:
1. Elderly people searched for information on computers and cured their own illnesses.
2. Elderly people exercised both their minds and bodies and became increasingly active in their work.
3. Elderly people became too busy with work to have time to see a doctor.
4. As their income increased, elderly people spent more money on health care.
default.q.n3-17-q67-67.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the computers provided by the committee are used only to view and receive orders («パソコンを使い、多くの注文の中からやりたいものを選んで»), not to look up information for self-treatment.
default.q.n3-17-q67-67.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because the passage says: «皆、頭や体を使うようになり、「忙しくて病気になる暇がない。」と笑っている。そして、本当に町では、病院に通う人が減ったのだそうだ、この仕事のおかげで、元気で過ごせるお年寄りも多いのだろう» (Everyone uses both their minds and bodies; thanks to this work, many elderly people are able to stay healthy, and the number of people going to the hospital has decreased).
default.q.n3-17-q67-67.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because 「忙しくて病気になる暇がない」 (I am so busy I have no time to get sick) is a humorous remark showing good health and energy, not a statement that they are too busy to go to the hospital.
default.q.n3-17-q67-67.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage only mentions that the harvested leaves can immediately be turned into money («すぐお金になる»); it does not mention using that money for healthcare expenses.
default.q.n3-17-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The town created new jobs using available local resources and successfully collaborated with older residents.
default.q.n3-17-q68-68.explanation:
Main point: The town used its existing natural resources—85% of its area is forest—to create a new type of work suited to older people. Its successful cooperation between the local government and residents led to major success.

Question translation:
What kind of town is this?

Answer choices:
1. A town that succeeded because it used its resources to create a new product based on ideas from older people.
2. A town that succeeded by devising new work using its resources and cooperating with older people.
3. A town where older people began a new industry by using the small amount of land outside the forested area.
4. A town where older people made a film themselves to help make the town famous.
default.q.n3-17-q68-68.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the idea of selling forest leaves was conceived by a town-office employee («役所の人が...思いついた»), not by an elderly person.
default.q.n3-17-q68-68.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because the passage says that a municipal employee made use of leaves from the forest covering 85% of the town’s area («町の85%もある森林の葉を商品として売ることを思いついた»), working with elderly residents to collect them («お年寄りに集めてもらい...大成功»), resulting in great success.
default.q.n3-17-q68-68.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the town makes use of the forest area, which accounts for as much as 85% of the town (“町の85%もある森林の葉”), not the small amount of land outside the forest (“森林以外の少ない土地”).
default.q.n3-17-q68-68.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the town's success gradually became well known and was eventually made into a film («次第に有名になり、今では映画にもなっている»); the elderly people did not make a film themselves for publicity.
default.q.n3-17-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The group met once a month, with the same members each time, for a total of three meetings together.
default.q.n3-17-q69-69.explanation:
- Main point: The opening paragraph introduces the rules and organization of experiential classes at Mizukawa Elementary School: the class is held once a month, for a total of three sessions; each group consists of one baby, a parent, two sixth-grade students, and the same members remain together throughout the sessions.
- Question: ① How is the class conducted?
- Answer choices:
  1. Once a month, with the same group members each time, for a total of three sessions together.
  2. Three times a month, with the same group members each time, for a total of three sessions together.
  3. Once a month, with different group members each time, for a total of three sessions together.
  4. Three times a month, with different group members each time, for a total of three sessions together.
default.q.n3-17-q69-69.why.0: (a) Correct. Paragraph 1 states: 「授業は月に1回、全部で3回行われる。一人の赤ちゃんとその親と生徒二人がグループを作る。各グループのメンバーは毎回変わらない。」 (The class is held once a month, three times in total. One baby, the baby's parent, and two students form a group. The members of each group do not change from one session to the next.)
default.q.n3-17-q69-69.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage clearly states 「月に1回」 (once a month), not 「月に3回」 (three times a month).
default.q.n3-17-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the article says 「各グループのメンバーは毎回変わらない」 (the members of each group do not change each time), not 「毎回違うメンバー」 (different members each time).
default.q.n3-17-q69-69.why.3: (d) Incorrect because both pieces of information, 「月に3回」 and 「毎回違うメンバー」, contradict the content of the passage.
default.q.n3-17-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 4. At first, the student only watched, but gradually began actively approaching and interacting with the baby.
default.q.n3-17-q70-70.explanation:
- Main point: The passage describes changes in the students’ attitudes and actions during their first class. At first, they are hesitant and anxious, only watching the baby and talking to the baby’s mother, but after a while they become more open and proactively touch and try holding the baby.
- Question translation: What were the students like during the first class?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. They only watched the baby throughout the class and looked anxious.
  2. They were completely unable to do what they had learned before class and were very confused.
  3. They actively interacted with the baby from the beginning and were very lively.
  4. At first they only watched, but gradually they began interacting with the baby on their own.
default.q.n3-17-q70-70.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage says 「初めは...聞いているだけだったが、しばらくすると...赤ちゃんに触ったり、抱いてみたりする生徒も出てきて」; the students did not spend the entire session merely watching the baby (「ずっと赤ちゃんを見ているだけ」).
default.q.n3-17-q70-70.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage contains no information that the student could not do what they had learned or was having trouble («全然できなくて、とても困っていた»).
default.q.n3-17-q70-70.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the students initially appeared worried and only listened and asked questions («初めは...聞いているだけだった»); they were not active and enthusiastic from the beginning («初めから積極的に»).
default.q.n3-17-q70-70.why.3: (d) Correct: Passage 3 clearly states: 「初めは、赤ちゃんを見ながら、お母さんに赤ちゃんの名前や一日の生活について聞いているだけだったが、しばらくすると...赤ちゃんに触ったり、抱いてみたりする生徒も出てきて、だんだんにぎやかになった。」 (At first, they merely looked at the baby while asking the mother about the baby’s name and daily routine, but after a while, some students began touching or trying to hold the baby, and things gradually became lively).
default.q.n3-17-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is 3. The student is surprised because the baby has grown much bigger and moves around much more.
default.q.n3-17-q71-71.explanation:
- Main point: From the second lesson onward, the students eagerly looked forward to seeing the baby again, and each time they were surprised by how much the baby had grown and how actively the baby moved after a month apart.
- Question translation: What were the students surprised by②?
- Answer choices:
  1. When they tried touching the baby, they found that the baby was very soft.
  2. When they tried to make the baby laugh, the baby started crying instead.
  3. The baby had grown and was moving more.
  4. The baby smiled more often and had become cuter.
default.q.n3-17-q71-71.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the detail that the baby was soft and seemed as if it might break («柔らかくてこわれそうだった») is an impression after the lesson near the end, not the reason the students were surprised each time they encountered it on the second visit.
default.q.n3-17-q71-71.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the incident of trying to make the baby laugh but making the baby cry instead («笑わせようとして泣かれてしまう») occurred in the first lesson, not as the reason for the surprise in the second lesson.
default.q.n3-17-q71-71.why.2: (c) Correct. Immediately after underlined part ②, the passage explains: 「そして、会うたびに②びっくりしていた。1か月見ない間に、赤ちゃんはとても大きくなり、よく動くようになっていたのだ。」 (And they were surprised every time they met. During the month they had not seen the baby, it had grown much larger and had begun moving much more.)
default.q.n3-17-q71-71.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not say that the reason for the surprise was that the baby laughed more.
default.q.n3-17-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 1: It seems that the students developed respect for life and gratitude toward their parents.
default.q.n3-17-q72-72.explanation:
- Main point: The original purpose of the lesson (stated in paragraph 1) was to foster an appreciation for the value of life and gratitude toward one's parents. The students' sincere thoughts and feelings after the lesson (feeling that they needed to protect the baby's small life and understanding the hardships their parents had gone through to raise them) demonstrated that this purpose had been conveyed very effectively.
- Question translation: The author says, "It seems that the purpose of the lesson was fully conveyed ③." Why did the author feel this way?
- Answer choices:
  1. Because the students seemed to have developed an appreciation for the value of life and feelings of gratitude toward their parents.
  2. Because the students seemed to realize that even a child like themselves could take care of a baby.
  3. Because the students seemed to realize the importance of putting their thoughts into words.
  4. Because the students seemed to develop a desire to raise a baby themselves.
default.q.n3-17-q72-72.why.0: (a) Correct: Paragraph 1 states the objective: 「命を大切にする心や親に感謝する気持ちを育てることが目的」. The final paragraph quotes the students’ reactions, such as 「守ってあげなきゃと思った」 (feeling that they needed to protect the baby—valuing life) and 「私のお父さん、お母さんも大変だったんだろうな」 (understanding how hard things must have been for their parents—feeling gratitude toward them), showing that the lesson’s objectives were achieved.
default.q.n3-17-q72-72.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage does not mention the students realizing that they could take care of a baby themselves («赤ちゃんの世話ができることに気づいた»).
default.q.n3-17-q72-72.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage does not mention awareness of the importance of expressing one’s thoughts aloud («声に出して言うことの大切さ»).
default.q.n3-17-q72-72.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the student's impression does not mention that the students themselves want to raise a baby («自分も赤ちゃんを育てたい»).
default.q.n3-17-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 3. The author decided to establish shopping rules after buying many unnecessary things and realizing that this was a waste of money.
default.q.n3-17-q73-73.explanation:
- Question: Why did the author decide to establish rules for shopping?
- Answer choices:
  1. Because the online shopping sale had ended.
  2. Because the author’s family gave them many things they did not want.
  3. Because the author had bought unnecessary things and realized they were wasting money.
  4. Because the room had become crowded and there was no space for new furniture.
- Main point: In Section 1, the author says that they used to buy things whenever they saw a sale announcement, without thinking about whether they needed them. This caused the room to fill with clothes and other items that had never been used. After realizing they were wasting money, the author reflected on their behavior and established new shopping rules.
default.q.n3-17-q73-73.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage does not say that the online shopping sale ended; rather, the author used to buy things indiscriminately whenever they saw a sale notification.
default.q.n3-17-q73-73.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage does not mention being given unwanted items by one's family at all.
default.q.n3-17-q73-73.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: 「その結果、部屋には一度も使っていない洋服や雑貨がたくさん増えてしまい、お金の無駄遣いにも気づいて反省しました。そこで、先月から買い物のルールを一つ決めました。」 (As a result, my room filled with many clothes and miscellaneous goods that I had never used even once. I realized that I had been wasting money and reflected on it. So, starting last month, I established one shopping rule.)
default.q.n3-17-q73-73.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage only mentions unused clothing and miscellaneous goods (洋服や雑貨); it does not say that the room was too cramped to store furniture (家具).
default.q.n3-17-q74-74.verdict: The correct answer is 2. Thanks to the rule they established, the author no longer wastes money and can live comfortably while keeping only the things they truly like.
default.q.n3-17-q74-74.explanation:
- Question: How did the author’s life change as a result of the rule they established?
- Answer choices:
  1. They worked more to buy the things they wanted.
  2. They stopped wasting money and came to value the things they truly liked.
  3. They spent more time shopping and came to hate shopping.
  4. They stopped using online shopping services altogether.
- Main point: At the end, the author states that since adopting the three-day waiting rule, wasteful spending has decreased, they now live surrounded only by things they genuinely like, and life has become extremely comfortable and pleasant.
default.q.n3-17-q74-74.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage does not mention the author having to work more in order to buy the things they wanted.
default.q.n3-17-q74-74.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states: 「このルールを始めてから、無駄な出費が減っただけでなく、本当に気に入った大切な物だけに囲まれて暮らせるようになり、生活がとても快適になりました。」 Since starting this rule, not only have unnecessary expenses decreased, but the author has also been able to live surrounded only by truly cherished belongings, making life much more comfortable.
default.q.n3-17-q74-74.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage does not say that the author dislikes shopping because it takes too much time; waiting three days helps the author think things through more carefully.
default.q.n3-17-q74-74.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage only says that the author applies a three-day waiting rule before deciding to buy something; it does not say that they completely stopped buying things online (全く使わない).
default.q.n3-17-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (きたない).
default.q.n3-17-q1-1.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: It is so dirty here. Let's go somewhere else.
・Kanji meaning: 汚 means dirty or polluted.
・Example: 部屋が汚いので、掃除してください。 (The room is dirty, so please clean it.)
default.q.n3-17-q1-1.why.0: (a) せまい (狭い) means “narrow” or “cramped”; it is not the reading of 汚い.
default.q.n3-17-q1-1.why.1: (b) くさい (臭い): means smelly or foul-smelling; it is not the reading of 汚い.
default.q.n3-17-q1-1.why.2: (c) きたない (汚い): Correct. 「汚」 in the adjective 「汚い」 is read きたない, meaning dirty or filthy.
default.q.n3-17-q1-1.why.3: (d) うるさい (煩い) means noisy or troublesome; it is not the reading of 汚い.
default.q.n3-17-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (しょうひん).
default.q.n3-17-q2-2.explanation:
Meaning: I will check whether the product has any scratches.
・Kanji components: 商 + 品.
・Example: 新しい商品を開発する。 (Develop a new product.)
default.q.n3-17-q2-2.why.0: (a) しょひん: Incorrect on-reading of 商; it requires the long vowel しょう, not the short sound しょ.
default.q.n3-17-q2-2.why.1: (b) しょうひん: Correct. 「商」(しょう) + 「品」(ひん) forms「商品」(しょうひん), meaning “goods” or “commercial product.”
default.q.n3-17-q2-2.why.2: (c) せいひん is the reading of 「製品」, meaning a manufactured product; 商 is not read せい.
default.q.n3-17-q2-2.why.3: (d) せひん: The reading violates the rules for on-readings.
default.q.n3-17-q3-3.explanation:
Meaning: The food or drink is still not cold or cool enough, so please wait a little longer.
・Sino-Japanese reading: 冷 (REI — cold, cool).
・Example: ビールがよく冷えている。 (The beer is nicely chilled.)
default.q.n3-17-q3-3.why.0: (a) もえて (燃えて): the te-form of the verb 燃える (to burn, blaze).
default.q.n3-17-q3-3.why.1: (b) ひえて (冷えて): Correct. The verb 「冷える」 (ひえる: to become cold or cool down) takes the te-form ひえて.
default.q.n3-17-q3-3.why.2: (c) にえて (煮えて): The te-form of the verb 煮える, meaning “to be cooked through” or “to be well boiled.”
default.q.n3-17-q3-3.why.3: (d) うえて (飢えて/植えて): the te-form of the verbs 飢える (to be hungry/starved) or 植える (to plant).
default.q.n3-17-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (そうたい).
default.q.n3-17-q4-4.explanation:
Meaning: I left work early because I was not feeling well.
・早 (early) + 退 (leave) = leaving early.
・Example: 体調が悪いため、早退させていただきます。 (I am not feeling well, so please allow me to leave early.)
default.q.n3-17-q4-4.why.0: (a) そうてい: This is the reading of「想定」(assumption, projection); the character「退」here is read たい, not てい.
default.q.n3-17-q4-4.why.1: (b) ぞうたい: the initial sound is incorrect; the on-reading of 「早」is そう (voiceless), not ぞう.
default.q.n3-17-q4-4.why.2: (c) そうたい: Correct. 「早」 (EARLY) is read そう and 「退」 (WITHDRAW) is read たい, forming そうたい, meaning leaving early (before the scheduled time).
default.q.n3-17-q4-4.why.3: (d) ぞうてい: This is the reading of 「贈呈」, meaning “to present” or “to give as a gift.”
default.q.n3-17-q5-5.explanation:
Meaning: Underline the important words.
・下 means "below" and 線 means "line."
・Example: 下線部を適切な言葉に直してください。 (Please correct the underlined part using the appropriate words.)
default.q.n3-17-q5-5.why.0: (a) げぜん: both on-readings are wrong; 下 is read as か here, and 線 as せん, not with a voiced ぜん sound.
default.q.n3-17-q5-5.why.1: (b) かぜん: The on-reading of 線 is せん; it does not undergo voicing to become ぜん.
default.q.n3-17-q5-5.why.2: (c) げせん: The character 「下」 in this word uses the on-reading か (下線 かせん), not げ. The reading げ appears in 下品 げひん and 下車 げしゃ.
default.q.n3-17-q5-5.why.3: (d) かせん is correct: 「下」 (か) + 「線」 (せん) is read as かせん and means an underline.
default.q.n3-17-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (ころんだ).
default.q.n3-17-q6-6.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Apparently, I broke it when I fell.
・Sino-Japanese reading: 転 (TEN — roll, fall, change).
・Example: 雪道で滑って転んだ。 (I slipped and fell on a snowy road.)
default.q.n3-17-q6-6.why.0: (a) はこんだ (運んだ): the ta-form of the verb 運ぶ (to transport, carry).
default.q.n3-17-q6-6.why.1: (b) ふんだ (踏んだ): the ta-form of the verb 踏む (to step on, tread on).
default.q.n3-17-q6-6.why.2: (c) ころんだ (転んだ): Correct. The ta-form of the verb 「転ぶ」 (ころぶ), meaning to fall, tumble, or roll, is ころんだ.
default.q.n3-17-q6-6.why.3: (d) つつんだ (包んだ): the ta-form of 包む (to wrap, to包).
default.q.n3-17-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (しゅよう).
default.q.n3-17-q7-7.explanation:
Meaning: Today's lecture has two main topics.
・主 (main) + 要 (important).
・Example: 主要なメンバーが集まって会議を行った。 (The key members gathered to hold a meeting.)
default.q.n3-17-q7-7.why.0: (a) しゅよう: Correct. 「主」(しゅ) +「要」(よう) forms「主要」(しゅよう: main, primary, major).
default.q.n3-17-q7-7.why.1: (b) じゅよう is the reading of 「需要」(demand) or 「受容」(acceptance); 「主」 is not read じゅ.
default.q.n3-17-q7-7.why.2: (c) しゅよ: Incorrect On-reading of 「要」; it must have the long vowel よう, not the short sound よ.
default.q.n3-17-q7-7.why.3: (d) じゅよ is the reading of 「授与」, meaning “presentation,” “conferral,” or “granting.”
default.q.n3-17-q8-8.explanation:
Meaning: Even now, I still sometimes think about things from the past.
・Kanji components: 過 (past) + 去 (gone).

default.q.n3-17-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 終わり.
default.q.n3-17-q29-29.explanation:
Meaning: "Today's experiment is over / This is the end."
- おしまい (noun/interjection): the end, finished, over (＝ 終わり).
- 実験 (じっけん): experiment.
- Example: これで今日の授業はおしまい（＝終わり）です。(This concludes today's class.)
default.q.n3-17-q29-29.why.0: (a) 「終わり」(ending, completion) is synonymous with the more casual expression「おしまい」(finished, over, the end).
default.q.n3-17-q29-29.why.1: (b) 「初めて」 means “for the first time,” indicating a beginning or first experience, which is opposite to an ending.
default.q.n3-17-q29-29.why.2: (c)「簡単」(simple, easy) describes the level of difficulty and does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-17-q29-29.why.3: (d) 「成功」means “success,” referring to an achieved result; it does not mean ending or stopping.
default.q.n3-17-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 明るすぎて.
default.q.n3-17-q30-30.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: “The glare is so strong that I cannot clearly read the writing on the sign.”
- 眩しい / まぶしい: glaring, dazzling (because the light is too strong ＝ 明るすぎる).
- 看板 (かんばん): sign, signboard, advertising board.
- Example: 太陽の光がまぶしくて（＝明るすぎて）、目が開けられない。(The sunlight is so dazzling（＝too bright）that I cannot open my eyes.)
default.q.n3-17-q30-30.why.0: (a) 「小さすぎて」means "too small," so it does not explain the feeling of dazzling brightness in the eyes.
default.q.n3-17-q30-30.why.1: (b) 「暗すぎて」 means “too dark,” which is the opposite of the eyes being dazzled by bright light.
default.q.n3-17-q30-30.why.2: (c) 「稼すぎて」(making too much money) comes from the verb「稼ぐ」(to earn money), so it is completely wrong in meaning in the context of observing the sign.
default.q.n3-17-q30-30.why.3: (d) 「明るすぎて」 (“too bright”) is synonymous with 「まぶしくて」 (“dazzling, glaring”); the adjective まぶしい/眩しい is used when light is too strong for the eyes.
default.q.n3-17-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 3 because "分類" (classification) is the appropriate term for classifying library books by subject matter.
default.q.n3-17-q31-31.explanation: "分類" means dividing and arranging things or objects into groups according to their characteristics, types, or specific criteria, such as sorting garbage, documents, or books. Example: ごみを燃えるごみと燃えないごみに分類する (Sort garbage into burnable and non-burnable garbage).
default.q.n3-17-q31-31.why.0: Incorrect because when dividing the year into seasons, 分かれている (be divided into) is used, not 分類 (classify objects by type).
default.q.n3-17-q31-31.why.1: Incorrect because when a payment is divided into multiple installments, 「分割して」(pay in installments, divide into payments) or 「分けて」should be used.
default.q.n3-17-q31-31.why.2: Correct because 「分類」 means categorizing objects according to groups or content, and it forms a natural expression in 「内容によって分類され」 (“be classified according to content”).
default.q.n3-17-q31-31.why.3: Incorrect because when separating the sidewalk from the roadway, use「分離されている」(separated),「分かれている」, or「区別されている」.
default.q.n3-17-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 4 because “引き受ける” is correctly used to mean accepting or taking responsibility for a task (仕事を引き受ける).
default.q.n3-17-q32-32.explanation: "引き受ける" means to take on or accept a job, responsibility, or assigned/requested task, or to commit to shouldering it. Example: 忙しいが、頼まれた以上はその仕事を引き受けることにした (Although I am busy, since I was asked to do it, I decided to take on the job).
default.q.n3-17-q32-32.why.0: Incorrect because accepting, listening to, and following someone else’s advice should be expressed with「受け入れて」(accept) or「聞いて」.
default.q.n3-17-q32-32.why.1: Incorrect because adopting, incorporating, or carrying on characteristics of other countries’ cuisines is expressed with 「取り入れている」(incorporating) or 「受け継いでいる」(carrying on).
default.q.n3-17-q32-32.why.2: Incorrect because catching a cold from someone else is expressed with 「うつされた」 (風邪をうつされた) or 「もらった」, not 「引き受ける」.
default.q.n3-17-q32-32.why.3: Correct because "仕事を引き受ける" is a standard expression meaning to accept responsibility for and carry out an assigned task.
default.q.n3-17-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 2 because "滞在" describes staying at a hotel for a period of time (ホテルに滞在する).
default.q.n3-17-q33-33.explanation: 「滞在」 (staying) refers to temporarily living or remaining in a place (such as a hotel, city, or foreign country) for a certain period for purposes such as business, travel, or study. Example: パリに2週間滞在する予定です (I plan to stay in Paris for two weeks).
default.q.n3-17-q33-33.why.0: Incorrect because birds and animals living in or temporarily stopping at a lake are described with「生息している」(inhabit) or「いる」.
default.q.n3-17-q33-33.why.1: Correct because 「滞在する」 is the precise word for a person staying at a hotel for a period of time (ホテルに滞在していた).
default.q.n3-17-q33-33.why.2: Incorrect because when a means of transportation, such as a bus, temporarily stops at a stop, use "停車していた" or "止まっていた".
default.q.n3-17-q33-33.why.3: Because this refers to waiting briefly in a café for the rain to stop, use 「雨宿りする」 (take shelter from the rain) or 「過ごす」 / 「いる」, not a long-term-stay term such as 「滞在」.
default.q.n3-17-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 1 because "どきどき" describes nervous excitement, with the heart pounding from tension (緊張で胸がどきどきした).
default.q.n3-17-q34-34.explanation: 「どきどき」is an onomatopoeic/mimetic adverb describing a heart beating rapidly and strongly because of nervousness, tension, anxiety, excitement, or fear. Example: 合格発表を見る前は、緊張で胸がどきどきしていた (Before checking the results, my heart was pounding with nervousness).
default.q.n3-17-q34-34.why.0: Correct because "胸がどきどきする" is a fixed expression meaning that one's heart is beating fast, describing nervousness or anxiety caused by being in front of a crowd.
default.q.n3-17-q34-34.why.1: Incorrect because the ticking of a clock in a quiet room is expressed with onomatopoeia such as 「カチカチ」, 「コチコチ」, or 「チクタク」.
default.q.n3-17-q34-34.why.2: Incorrect because trembling violently from the cold is expressed with the onomatopoeia 「ぶるぶる」 or 「がたがた」, as in 「体がぶるぶる震える」.
default.q.n3-17-q34-34.why.3: Incorrect because for a sign shaking or swaying violently in strong wind, use "がたがた", "ぐらぐら", or "ゆらゆら".
default.q.n3-17-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 2 because "かれる" (枯れる) is correctly used when plants or flowers wither from a lack of water (花がかれてしまった).
default.q.n3-17-q35-35.explanation: "かれる" (usually written 枯れる) means for plants, flowers, or leaves to dry up, wither, or die from lack of water or age. It can also mean to run dry, when written 涸れる, or to become hoarse, as in 声が枯れる. Example: 秋になると、木の葉が枯れて落ちる (When autumn comes, the leaves wither and fall.)
default.q.n3-17-q35-35.why.0: Incorrect because when meat becomes burnt from being cooked over high heat, use 「焦げてしまった」 (こげてしまった), not 「かれる」.
default.q.n3-17-q35-35.why.1: Correct because 「花がかれる」(a flower withers and dries up) is the standard collocation using 「枯れる」when plants lose water and wither.
default.q.n3-17-q35-35.why.2: Incorrect because for old machinery that is damaged or malfunctioning, use「壊れて」(こわれて),「故障して」, or「がたがきて」.
default.q.n3-17-q35-35.why.3: Incorrect because snow and ice melting and disappearing as the weather warms is expressed with「溶けた」(とけた) or「消えた」, not「かれる」.
default.q.n3-18-q36-36.explanation:
Meaning: "He became famous as a novelist, but ordinarily he works as a doctor at a small hospital."
- Grammar pattern: 「N + として」means "as / in the capacity of / in the role of N" and indicates a status, position, or capacity.
- Vocabulary & kanji readings: 小説家: novelist; 医者: doctor.
- Example: 彼は留学生として日本へ来ました。(He came to Japan as an exchange student.)
default.q.n3-18-q36-36.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜について」 means “about” a topic or issue and is not used to indicate a person's status or role.
default.q.n3-18-q36-36.why.1: (b) Correct because「N として」means “as N” or “in the capacity of N,” and is used to specify a status or role (famous as a novelist).
default.q.n3-18-q36-36.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜にしたがって」 means "as... changes/according to..." or "in accordance with...," which does not fit this context.
default.q.n3-18-q36-36.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「〜と比べて」 means “compared with...,” and is used to contrast two things.
default.q.n3-18-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (としたら).
default.q.n3-18-q37-37.explanation:
Meaning: "Last week, during a company interview, I was asked, 'If you were to represent yourself with a color, what color would you be?' and I answered orange. That is because orange has an image of being 'healthy' and 'full of energy.'"
- Grammar pattern: 「もし〜としたら」 (or とすれば / とすると) introduces a supposition or hypothetical situation ("if we suppose that...").
- Vocabulary and kanji: 面接 (DIỆN TIẾP - interview), 表す (BIỂU - express, represent), 健康 (KIỆN KHANG - health).
- Example: もし生まれ変われるとしたら、鳥になりたい。(If I could be reborn, I would like to become a bird.)
default.q.n3-18-q37-37.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜ことから」 indicates a cause, origin, or basis for a judgment (“because of / based on the fact that...”), and does not combine with 「もし」 to form a hypothetical question.
default.q.n3-18-q37-37.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「〜という点で」 means “in the respect that...” or “from the standpoint of...,” and is used to state an aspect for evaluation.
default.q.n3-18-q37-37.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜ように」 means "so that / as / like..." and is not used with 「もし」 to form a hypothetical condition.
default.q.n3-18-q37-37.why.3: (d) Correct because the structure 「もし〜としたら」 sets up an imaginary assumption (“if we suppose that…”).
default.q.n3-18-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (どうしても).
default.q.n3-18-q38-38.explanation:
- Sentence translation: "Last night, just before going to bed, I suddenly craved yogurt so badly that I could not resist it. Even though it was midnight, I ended up running to the convenience store to buy some."
- Adverb: 「どうしても」 used with a desire form (〜たい) means "no matter what / desperately want to..." and expresses a powerful urge.
- Vocabulary and related kanji: 夜中 (よなか - midnight).
- Example: 理由はどうしても言えません。(I cannot tell you the reason no matter what.)
default.q.n3-18-q38-38.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「どうか」is commonly used for earnest requests or pleas ("please..."), or in questions meaning "whether or not."
default.q.n3-18-q38-38.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「せっかく」 means “after taking the trouble to do something” and is usually accompanied by regret or advice to make use of the opportunity.
default.q.n3-18-q38-38.why.2: (c) Correct because 「どうしても」 combined with 「〜たい」 expresses an intense, irresistible desire ("want to by all means" or "really want to no matter what").
default.q.n3-18-q38-38.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「きっと」 means “surely” and is used for making a confident judgment or expressing strong belief. It is not used to describe one’s own appetite.
default.q.n3-18-q39-39.explanation:
Meaning: “Since you only have to mix the ingredients together and bake them, anyone can make this cake successfully and deliciously.”
- Grammar pattern: 「V-る + だけだ / だけだから」means “all you have to do is...” or “you only need to...,” emphasizing simplicity and ease.
- Vocabulary: 材料 (ingredients), 混ぜる (mix, stir), 失敗 (failure).
- Example: パスポートを見せるだけでいいです。(You only need to show your passport.)
default.q.n3-18-q39-39.why.0: (a) Correct because 「V-る + だけだ」means "just do... / all one has to do is...". Combined with 「から」, it means "because all you have to do is mix the ingredients and bake them...".
default.q.n3-18-q39-39.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「V-る + ことだ」 gives advice (“you should/must do...”), not an explanation of how simple an operation is.
default.q.n3-18-q39-39.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜せいだ」 means “because of...” and usually indicates a bad or negative result, whereas the following clause describes a positive result (“tasty and not spoiled”).
default.q.n3-18-q39-39.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「〜ときだ」means “it is when...” or “it is the time when...,” and does not express a logical cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.n3-18-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (行われます).
default.q.n3-18-q40-40.explanation:
Meaning: "In my town, a summer festival is held every year on the last Sunday of August."
- Grammar: Since the subject is an event or festival, 「夏祭りが」, the verb 「行う」 (to conduct, hold) must be changed to the passive form 「行われる」, meaning “is held.”
- Vocabulary: 夏祭り (summer festival), 行う (to conduct, hold).
- Example: 来月、東京で国際会議が行われます。(An international conference will be held in Tokyo next month.)
default.q.n3-18-q40-40.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「行います」is active voice, requiring a person or organization as the subject and taking the object pattern 「〜を行う」.
default.q.n3-18-q40-40.why.1: (b) Incorrect because「行わせます」is the causative form (“make or allow someone to organize”).
default.q.n3-18-q40-40.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「行っています」 is the active progressive form (“is organizing”).
default.q.n3-18-q40-40.why.3: (d) Correct because the subject is the event「夏祭りが」, so the verb must be in the passive form「行われます」(the festival is held).
default.q.n3-18-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (お待ちください).
default.q.n3-18-q41-41.explanation:
Customer: “Excuse me. Do you have these shoes in a size larger?”
Staff member: “Oh, yes. I will go check, so please wait a moment.”
- Honorific language: 「お + V(stem without ます) + ください」 is a respectful form used to make a polite request to the other person (such as a customer), meaning “please...”.
- Vocabulary: 確認 (confirmation/checking), 少々 (a little, a moment).
- Example: こちらにお名前とお電話番号をお書きください。 (Please write your name and telephone number here.)
default.q.n3-18-q41-41.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「お待ちしております」 is humble language describing the speaker’s own action (“we are waiting for you”), so it is not used to ask a customer to wait.
default.q.n3-18-q41-41.why.1: (b) Correct because「お＋V (ます-stem)＋ください」is the standard honorific language pattern for politely asking or requesting something from a customer (“Please wait”).
default.q.n3-18-q41-41.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「お待ちできます」forms the potential incorrectly as honorific language and is not used to make a request of someone else.
default.q.n3-18-q41-41.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「お待ちしましょう」 means “I/we will wait” or “Shall I/we wait?”, which is the opposite of asking the customer to wait.
default.q.n3-18-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (申します).
default.q.n3-18-q42-42.explanation:
Translation:
Employee at Construction Company X: “Yes, you’ve reached the Sales Department of Construction Company X.”
Nakada: “Hello, this is Nakada from ABC Bank. Could you please put me through to Mr./Ms. Yamaishi?”
- Honorific language: 「〜と申します」 is the humble form of 「言う」, used when stating one’s name or introducing oneself in polite or business communication (“my name is ...” / “I am called ...”).
- Vocabulary and kanji: 建設 (construction), 営業部 (Sales Department).
- Example: 初めまして。タナカと申します。よろしくお願いいたします。(Nice to meet you. My name is Tanaka. I look forward to working with you.)
default.q.n3-18-q42-42.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜とございます」 is ungrammatical; the polite form of a noun is 「〜でございます」.
default.q.n3-18-q42-42.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「いたします」is the humble form of 「します」and is not used to state one’s name with the particle 「と」.
default.q.n3-18-q42-42.why.2: (c) Correct because 「〜と申します」 is the standard humble form used to give one's own name (“My name is…”).
default.q.n3-18-q42-42.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「申し上げます」 is humble language meaning “to say/express to the other person” (as in お礼を申し上げます), and is not used in the name-introduction pattern 「〜と申し上げます」.
default.q.n3-18-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (持っていくことになっている).
default.q.n3-18-q43-43.explanation:
Translation: "At the high school my son attends, bread and drinks are also available for purchase at lunchtime, but basically everyone is required to bring a packed lunch."
- Grammar pattern: 「V-る / V-ない + ことになっている」 expresses a predetermined rule, regulation, or general custom ("it is established that...").
- Vocabulary and Sino-Japanese readings: 通う (to attend regularly), 基本的 (fundamental, basic), 全員 (everyone), 弁当 (packed lunch).
- Example: 法律で20歳未満はお酒を飲んではいけないことになっている。(By law, people under 20 are not allowed to drink alcohol.)
default.q.n3-18-q43-43.why.0: (a) Incorrect because「V-た + ばかりだ」means “have just done something” and is not used to express a general rule for a group.
default.q.n3-18-q43-43.why.1: (b) Correct because 「V-る + ことになっている」 is used for general rules or regulations established by an organization ("it is stipulated that one must bring it").
default.q.n3-18-q43-43.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜たい」expresses a personal desire and does not fit the collective subject 「全員が」(the entire school).
default.q.n3-18-q43-43.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「〜つもりだ」 expresses the speaker’s personal intention and cannot naturally be used with the collective subject 「全員が」 in the context of school regulations.
default.q.n3-18-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (寝られないと).
default.q.n3-18-q44-44.explanation:
Meaning: "Taking a nap feels very good, but if I cannot sleep at night, it is very troublesome, so I always get up after sleeping for only about 15 minutes."
- Grammar: 「V-ない + と + 困る」 expresses a hypothetical negative condition ("if ..., it will be troublesome/difficult"). Here, the negative potential form 「寝られない」 combines with 「と」 to form 「寝られないと」 (if I cannot sleep).
- Vocabulary and Sino-Japanese reading: 昼寝 (ひるね: nap), 気持ちがいい (pleasant, comfortable).
- Example: 早く寝ないと、明日朝起きられなくて困るよ。(If you do not go to bed early, you will have trouble getting up tomorrow morning.)
default.q.n3-18-q44-44.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜なくて」connects clauses or gives a reason (“because I did not sleep...”), and does not form a hypothetical conditional clause with 「困る」.
default.q.n3-18-q44-44.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「寝られると思って」 means “thinking that one would be able to sleep, so ...,” which has the opposite meaning and does not connect logically with 「困る」.
default.q.n3-18-q44-44.why.2: (c) Correct because 「寝られないと」combines the negative potential form 「寝られない」(cannot sleep) with the conditional particle 「と」(“if one cannot sleep at night, it is very troublesome”).
default.q.n3-18-q44-44.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜と思うと」means “just when one thinks…” or “as soon as one thinks…,” which does not fit the sentence.
default.q.n3-18-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (利用したくても).
default.q.n3-18-q45-45.explanation:
Translation: "Because City A has few preschools, it has become a serious problem that some people want to use childcare services but are unable to do so."
- Grammar: 「V-たくても + (negative potential form)」means “even though someone really wants to do V, they cannot,” expressing helplessness in the face of circumstances.
- Vocabulary and kanji readings: 保育園 (HOIKUEN - nursery school, preschool), 利用 (RIYO - use), 問題 (MONDAI - problem).
- Example: 忙しくて、旅行に行きたくても行けません。(I am too busy, so even though I want to travel, I cannot go.)
default.q.n3-18-q45-45.why.0: (a) Correct because 「V-たくても」 means “even if one wants to..., (it is impossible),” and combined with 「利用できない」, it means “even if one wants to send a child to or use the daycare center, it cannot be used.”
default.q.n3-18-q45-45.why.1: (b) 「〜そうになって」 means “almost...” or “looked as if ... was about to happen,” which does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-18-q45-45.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「利用しているのに」 means “although [someone] is using it,” directly contradicting the following clause, “cannot use it” (利用できない).
default.q.n3-18-q45-45.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「〜できたら」means “if one can do something” and does not create a contrastive relationship with the following clause.
default.q.n3-18-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (予約しておくよ).
default.q.n3-18-q46-46.explanation:
Meaning:
Wife: “Hey, I’m going out to do a little shopping. Could you reserve the restaurant we’re going to tonight?”
Husband: “Sure, I’ll make the reservation. Would 7:00 p.m. work?”
Wife: “Yes, thank you.”
- Grammar pattern: 「V-ておく」means to do something in advance or prepare something for later.
- Vocabulary: 予約 (reservation; advance booking).
- Example: パーティーの前に飲み物を買っておきます。(I will buy drinks in advance for the party.)
default.q.n3-18-q46-46.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜してね」 is a request or reminder for the listener to do something, whereas here the husband is agreeing to do it himself.
default.q.n3-18-q46-46.why.1: (b) Correct because 「V-ておく」 means doing something in advance as preparation; the husband says, “I’ll make the reservation in advance” (予約しておくよ).
default.q.n3-18-q46-46.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜ようよ」is used to invite someone to do something together (“Let’s order it”), which does not fit accepting a request to help one’s wife.
default.q.n3-18-q46-46.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「V-てある」 describes a state that has already been completed and left in place (“has already been placed”), whereas the husband has just been asked and is about to place it.
default.q.n3-18-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (食べてもよさそうだ).
default.q.n3-18-q47-47.explanation:
Dialogue meaning:
Child: "Dad, can I eat this tomato yet? Look, it has turned red."
Father: "Yes. It looks like it is ready to eat, doesn't it?"
- Grammar: 「V-てもいい」 (it is okay to do...) combined with the visual-evidence conjectural ending 「〜そうだ」 becomes 「〜てもよさそうだ」, meaning "it looks like it is okay to... / it looks like it is ready to..."
- Vocabulary and related kanji: 畑 (はたけ - field, vegetable garden).
- Example: 雨もやんだし、そろそろ出かけてもよさそうだ。(The rain has stopped, so it looks like it is about time to go out.)
default.q.n3-18-q47-47.why.0: (a) Incorrect because「食べやすいそうだ」means “I hear that it is easy to eat” (the hearsay form), which does not fit the context of directly observing tomatoes growing on the plant.
default.q.n3-18-q47-47.why.1: (b) 「食べていそうだ」means “seems to be eating,” which is unsuitable when the subject is a tomato.
default.q.n3-18-q47-47.why.2: (c) 「食べたがるそうだ」 means “I hear that someone wants to eat,” which does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-18-q47-47.why.3: (d) Correct because 「V-てもいい」 (“it is okay to eat”) combines with the visual conjecture 「〜そうだ」 to form 「〜てもよさそうだ」, meaning “it looks like it is ready to eat.”
default.q.n3-18-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (行ってしまいましょうか).
default.q.n3-18-q48-48.explanation:
Minami: "Yamashita still hasn't arrived. He isn't answering his mobile phone either. What should we do now?"
Nakagawa: "If we wait any longer, we won't make it on time either. Shall we just go ahead?"
Minami: "You're right. Let's go."
- Grammar pattern: 「V-てしまう + ましょうか」 → 「V-てしまいましょうか」 is used to make a decisive proposal or invitation to take an action ("Shall we just go ahead and ...?").
- Vocabulary: 携帯 (mobile phone), 間に合う (to be on time).
- Example: 時間がないから、タクシーに乗ってしまいましょうか。(We don't have much time, so shall we just take a taxi?)
default.q.n3-18-q48-48.why.0: (a) Correct because 「V-てしまいましょうか」 makes a firm suggestion to do something together (“Shall we just go ahead and leave first?”).
default.q.n3-18-q48-48.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「〜のでしょう」 expresses a supposition or request for confirmation (“I suppose it will leave, right?”); it is not used to invite someone or propose an action.
default.q.n3-18-q48-48.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜てしまいましたか」 is a past-tense question (“Did you accidentally go off already?”), which does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-18-q48-48.why.3: (d) Incorrect because「〜てしまっていました」is a past form meaning “had already gone,” which does not fit a suggestion about a subsequent action.
default.q.n3-18-q49-49.verdict: The correct order is: 4 → 2 → 3 → 1. The ★ position (the third blank) is answer choice 3 (なかなか).
default.q.n3-18-q49-49.explanation:
Complete sentence: この写真の鳥はとても珍しくて、この鳥の研究をしている専門家でもなかなか見る機会がないそうだ。
Meaning: The bird in this photograph is extremely rare, and apparently even experts who study this species rarely get a chance to see it.
default.q.n3-18-q49-49.why.0: (a) 「見る機会がない」 appears in the fourth position (the final slot) and combines with the hearsay structure 「〜そうだ」 at the end of the sentence to form 「見る機会がないそうだ」 (“I hear that there is no opportunity to see it”).
default.q.n3-18-q49-49.why.1: (b) 「専門家でも」occupies the second position and serves as the subject with the meaning "even if one is an expert"; it is modified by the preceding clause 「この鳥の研究をしている」.
default.q.n3-18-q49-49.why.2: (c) 「なかなか」 appears in third position, marked with ★. It is an adverb meaning “not easily / no matter how hard one tries,” and is used with the negative form 「〜ない」 afterward (「なかなか見る機会がない」).
default.q.n3-18-q49-49.why.3: (d) 「研究をしている」 is in position 1, following 「この鳥の」 to form the modifying clause 「この鳥の研究をしている」, which modifies the noun 「専門家」 immediately afterward.
default.q.n3-18-q50-50.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 1 → 4 → 2. The ★ position (the third blank) is answer choice 4 (大学時代).
default.q.n3-18-q50-50.explanation:
Complete sentence: 春から大学生になる娘には、勉強以外にも大学時代にしかできない経験をいろいろしてほしい。
Meaning: I want my daughter, who will become a university student in the spring, to have many experiences that are only possible during university, in addition to studying.
default.q.n3-18-q50-50.why.0: (a) 「にも」 occupies the second position and follows 「勉強以外」 to form 「勉強以外にも」, meaning “besides studying, also...”.
default.q.n3-18-q50-50.why.1: (b) 「にしか」 appears in position 4. It follows the time noun 「大学時代」 and combines with the negative potential verb 「できない」 in the pattern 「〜にしか…できない」 (“can only be done in/during...” ).
default.q.n3-18-q50-50.why.2: (c) 「勉強以外」is in position 1, serving as the noun phrase before the particle「にも」to introduce additional information.
default.q.n3-18-q50-50.why.3: (d) 「大学時代」 is in the third position (the ★ position). It is a noun indicating a period of time and is followed by the particle 「にしか」 to modify 「できない経験」.
default.q.n3-18-q51-51.verdict: The correct order is: 4 → 3 → 2 → 1. The star ★ is in the third position, occupied by choice 2 (という).
default.q.n3-18-q51-51.explanation:
Complete sentence: 土曜日は買い物をしたり友人と食事をしたりし、日曜日はどこにも出かけずに家で過ごすというのが私の好きな週末の過ごし方だ。
Translation: On Saturdays, I go shopping or eat out with friends, while on Sundays I stay home without going anywhere. That is my favorite way to spend the weekend.
default.q.n3-18-q51-51.why.0: (a) 「のが」 appears in position 4. The nominalizing particle 「の」 plus the subject particle 「が」 turns everything before it into the subject of the predicate 「私の好きな週末の過ごし方だ」.
default.q.n3-18-q51-51.why.1: (b) 「という」 occupies the third position (the ★ position) and defines or introduces the content of the nominalizer 「の」 that follows, according to the structure 「V-dictionary form + というの」.
default.q.n3-18-q51-51.why.2: (c) 「家で過ごす」 occupies position 2 and is the main action predicate for Sunday (“spend the day at home”), following the manner adverb 「どこにも出かけずに」 and preceding 「という」.
default.q.n3-18-q51-51.why.3: (d) 「どこにも出かけずに」 is in position 1 and expresses the state of “not going anywhere and then...” by using 「V-ずに」 (equivalent to ないで) to modify the following action 「家で過ごす」.
default.q.n3-18-q52-52.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 3 → 1 → 4. The ★ blank (the third blank) is choice 1 (待っているんです).
default.q.n3-18-q52-52.explanation:
Complete dialogue:
客: 「すみません 15分ぐらい前に案内をお願いして、しばらくここで待てって言われたから待っているんですけど。まだですか。」
店員: 「大変申し訳ありません。」
Meaning:
Customer: “Excuse me. About 15 minutes ago, I asked to be shown to a table, and I was told to wait here for a while, so I have been waiting... Is it still not ready?”
Staff member: “I am terribly sorry.”
default.q.n3-18-q52-52.why.0: (a) 「待っているんです」 occupies the third position (the ★ position). It is the main predicate expressing the state of waiting, followed by an explanation with 「〜んです」 and then the connective particle 「けど」.
default.q.n3-18-q52-52.why.1: (b) 「言われた」 is in the first position and is the passive form of 言う, following the quoted instruction 「待てって」 (was told to wait...).
default.q.n3-18-q52-52.why.2: (c) 「から」occupies the second position and is a conjunction meaning “because.” It connects the passive clause 「言われた」with the following action 「待っているんです」.
default.q.n3-18-q52-52.why.3: (d) 「けど」 is in the fourth position, functioning as a connective particle with a hesitant tone, expressing a complaint or transition before the question 「。まだですか。」.
default.q.n3-18-q53-53.verdict: The correct order is: 1 → 4 → 3 → 2. The ★ blank (the third blank) is choice 3 (と思うようになって).
default.q.n3-18-q53-53.explanation:
Complete sentence: 歴史を勉強すればするほどもっと学びたいと思うようになって歴史学科への進学を決めた。
Meaning: The more I studied history, the more I wanted to learn, so I decided to continue my education in the Department of History.
default.q.n3-18-q53-53.why.0: (a) 「勉強すればするほど」 appears in the first position, takes 「歴史を」 as its object at the beginning of the sentence, and uses the grammar pattern 「〜ば〜ほど」, meaning “the more one studies, the more...”
default.q.n3-18-q53-53.why.1: (b) 「歴史学科への」 occupies the fourth position. It consists of a noun phrase naming a major combined with the particle 「への」, modifying the noun 「進学」 immediately afterward (entering the history department for further study).
default.q.n3-18-q53-53.why.2: (c) 「と思うようになって」occupies the third position, marked by the star ★. It follows the expression of desire 「もっと学びたい」in the pattern「〜と思うようになる」(gradually come to think that...), and its te-form connects it to the decision in the following clause.
default.q.n3-18-q53-53.why.3: (d) 「もっと学びたい」 occupies the second position. It is the result clause expressing a desire ("want to study even more"), following the conditional clause 「勉強すればするほど」 and preceding the quotative particle 「と」.
default.q.n3-18-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 3. けれども.
default.q.n3-18-q54-54.explanation: Before the blank, the author says that in Japan, wherever you go, people greet one another and then talk about the weather. After the blank, the author says that people in their home country rarely talk about the weather, so they do not understand why Japanese people do so. The two clauses express opposition and contrast, so the conjunction 「けれども」 (however, but) is the correct choice.
default.q.n3-18-q54-54.why.0: (a) 「そのうえ」 (moreover, in addition) adds information in the same direction; it does not express the contrast between Japanese people often talking about the weather and people in the author’s country not doing so.
default.q.n3-18-q54-54.why.1: (b) 「つまり」(in other words / in short) explains or summarizes the preceding idea, so it does not fit a context involving a contrastive shift.
default.q.n3-18-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「けれども」(however, but) is a conjunction expressing contrast. It connects the fact that everyone in Japan talks about the weather with the fact that people in the author’s country rarely do so.
default.q.n3-18-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「すると」 (“then,” “immediately afterward”) indicates an action or result that follows directly from an event; it does not express contrast.
default.q.n3-18-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 言ってしまいました.
default.q.n3-18-q55-55.explanation: Previously, the author thought that talking about the weather was optional and did not bring it up proactively. However, one winter morning, when meeting a Japanese friend, the author unconsciously blurted out 「寒いね」 (“It’s cold, isn’t it?”). The pattern 「〜てしまう」expresses an action that happens unintentionally or slips out naturally, which fits very well with the adverb 「自然に」.
default.q.n3-18-q55-55.why.0: (a) 「言われていました」 is the past progressive passive form (was said), which is inappropriate because the subject here is the author herself saying the greeting.
default.q.n3-18-q55-55.why.1: (b) 「言ってもらいました」 means “had someone say it for me / received the favor of being told,” expressing help received from another person; the agent and meaning are incorrect here.
default.q.n3-18-q55-55.why.2: (c) 「言わせてみました」incorrectly combines the causative with てみる (try making or forcing someone to speak), which does not fit the first-person narrative context.
default.q.n3-18-q55-55.why.3: (d) 「言ってしまいました」 combines the verb 言う with the grammar pattern 「〜てしまう」, indicating an unintentional action or something blurted out against one's intention. It fits perfectly with the adverb 「自然に」 (naturally).
default.q.n3-18-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 広がって.
default.q.n3-18-q56-56.explanation: After beginning with a discussion of the weather, the conversation between the author and their friend expanded to topics such as delicious winter food and winter clothing. The 「〜て」 form in 「広がって」 connects the two clauses, expressing an event that led to the feeling 「おもしろいと思いました」 (I thought it was interesting).
default.q.n3-18-q56-56.why.0: (a) 「広がって」is the te-form, used to connect clauses describing the progression of events and the cause leading to a feeling or judgment: the conversation about the weather expanded to related topics, and the author found it interesting.
default.q.n3-18-q56-56.why.1: (b) 「広がるより」 expresses a comparison (“rather than expanding”), so it does not fit the grammar or logic of the sentence.
default.q.n3-18-q56-56.why.2: (c) 「広がるように」 expresses a purpose (“so that it spreads”) or a wish; it is not used to report an event that has already occurred.
default.q.n3-18-q56-56.why.3: (d) 「広がったそうで」 expresses hearsay (“I hear that it spread”), whereas this is a firsthand experience directly experienced by the author.
default.q.n3-18-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 持つのかもしれません.
default.q.n3-18-q57-57.explanation: The preceding sentence explains that Japan has four seasons, temperatures change considerably, and the weather changes frequently. The conjunction 「そのため」(for that reason) leads to the author's inference that this may be why many Japanese people pay close attention to the weather. The pattern 「〜のかもしれません」(it may be that...) expresses a modest, natural inference or conclusion.
default.q.n3-18-q57-57.why.0: (a) 「持ったはずがありません」 (“there is no way [they] had concern”) is strongly negative and contradicts the cause-and-effect reasoning of the passage.
default.q.n3-18-q57-57.why.1: (b) 「持ちたがりません」 indicates that a third person does not want to be concerned, contradicting the author’s statement that Japanese people are very concerned about the weather.
default.q.n3-18-q57-57.why.2: (c) 「持つのかもしれません」 uses the conjectural pattern 「〜のかもしれない」 (may be / might be) to present a reasonable explanatory supposition.
default.q.n3-18-q57-57.why.3: (d) 「持とうとしません」 (“does not intend to hold” or “refuses to care”) is completely inconsistent with the contextual meaning.
default.q.n3-18-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 2. これ.
default.q.n3-18-q58-58.explanation: In the preceding sentence, the author has just arrived at a new realization: «天気の話は誰とでもしやすいこと» (talking about the weather is easy with anyone). In the following sentence, the demonstrative 「これ」 directly refers to this realization as one of the reasons many people often talk about the weather.
default.q.n3-18-q58-58.why.0: (a) 「どれ」is an interrogative pronoun meaning “which one,” and cannot replace the event just mentioned as a demonstrative pronoun.
default.q.n3-18-q58-58.why.1: (b) 「これ」is a demonstrative pronoun used in written or argumentative language to directly refer to the statement or point the writer has just presented in the preceding sentence («天気の話は誰とでもしやすいこと»).
default.q.n3-18-q58-58.why.2: (c) 「あれら」 is a plural demonstrative pronoun in group A (those over there, far from the speaker's mental or physical space). It is not used for an understanding that has just been reached.
default.q.n3-18-q58-58.why.3: (d) 「それら」 is a plural demonstrative pronoun (“those things”), whereas the preceding sentence refers to a single idea or matter («天気の話は誰とでもしやすいこと»).
default.q.n3-18-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3: An email from the office will arrive at 10:00 announcing whether there will be an afternoon class.
default.q.n3-18-q59-59.explanation:
- **Main point**: An email from Oyama University’s office announces that heavy snow has stopped public transportation, so the morning classes and morning club activities are canceled. Regarding the afternoon classes, the university will send an email at 10:00 announcing whether they will be held, depending on whether public transportation resumes before 10:00.
- **Translation of the question**: What can be understood from this email?
- **Translation of the choices**:
  1. Today’s morning classes will begin at 10:00.
  2. All club activities, both morning and afternoon, will be canceled today.
  3. Whether today’s afternoon classes will be held will be announced by email from the office at 10:00.
  4. If an email from the office arrives at 10:00, today’s afternoon classes will be held.
default.q.n3-18-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage clearly states 「午前の授業は行われません」 (the morning classes will not be held), not that they will start at 10:00.
default.q.n3-18-q59-59.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the notice only asks that club activities be canceled during the morning (「午前中は中止してください」); it does not require cancellation for the entire afternoon.
default.q.n3-18-q59-59.why.2: (c) Correct, as directly quoted from the passage: 「授業を行うかどうか10時にメールでお知らせしますので、必ず確認してください。」 (We will notify you by email at 10:00 whether the class will be held, so be sure to check), with the sender listed as 「大山大学　事務室」.
default.q.n3-18-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the email at 10:00 is intended to announce whether the class will be held (「授業を行うかどうか」); receiving an email does not necessarily mean that there will be a class.
default.q.n3-18-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The author acknowledges that phones are convenient but dislikes living constantly preoccupied with them, so they currently have no intention of using one.
default.q.n3-18-q60-60.explanation:
**Main point:** The author acknowledges that mobile phones are convenient, but when they used one in the past, they always felt that they had to answer it regardless of when or where it rang. Disliking that restrictive feeling, the author stopped using one and felt more at ease. Although occasionally not having a phone is inconvenient, the author still wants to continue living without one.

**Translation of the question:**
What does the author think about mobile phones?

**Translation of the answer choices:**
1. Some people say they are convenient, but the author does not think so and currently has no intention of using one.
2. The author thinks they are convenient but dislikes a life in which they always have to worry about and pay attention to their phone, so they currently have no intention of using one.
3. They are convenient to use, and since service fees have recently become cheaper, the author intends to use one again.
4. The author did not want to use one in the first place, but not having one is inconvenient, so they intend to use one again.
default.q.n3-18-q60-60.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because when someone says that using a phone is convenient, the author admits 「それは私もよくわかっている」 (I understand that very well too), rather than saying that they do not think phones are convenient.
default.q.n3-18-q60-60.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because the passage states that the author knows phones are convenient (「それは私もよくわかっている」), but in the past 「いつどこにいても電話に出なければいけない気がして、それが嫌で持つのをやめてしまった」 (they felt they had to answer the phone anytime and anywhere, disliked that, and stopped carrying one), and still chooses not to use one now (「それでも、私は今のままでいいと思っている」).
default.q.n3-18-q60-60.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because although the fee is cheaper, the author states 「私は今のままでいいと思っている」 (“I think things are fine as they are now”) and does not intend to use it again (もう一度持つつもりだ).
default.q.n3-18-q60-60.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the author used a mobile phone in the past (「私も以前、携帯電話を持っていた」). Although not having one is somewhat inconvenient now, the author still wants to continue living without one and has no intention of using one again.
default.q.n3-18-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The president of the beverage company thought that people would welcome and enjoy a vending machine that could also sell hot drinks.
default.q.n3-18-q61-61.explanation:
- Main point summary: The passage explains how modern vending machines came to offer both hot and cold drinks. One winter day, the director of a beverage company saw truck drivers drinking cold beverages bought from a vending machine and looking extremely cold. He wanted people to be able to enjoy hot drinks in winter, and after nearly 10 years of research, the versatile vending machines we know today were created.
- Question translation: Why were vending machines like those used today created?
- Answer choice translations:
1. Because the director of a beverage company bought a cold drink from a vending machine in winter and felt sorry for the customers.
2. Because the director of a beverage company thought vending machines selling cold drinks would be convenient.
3. Because the truck drivers requested vending machines that sold hot drinks.
4. Because the director of a beverage company thought everyone would be delighted if vending machines could sell hot drinks as well as cold drinks.
default.q.n3-18-q61-61.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the people who bought and drank the cold beverages were truck drivers, not the director buying one for himself: 「トラックの運転手たちが自動販売機で買ったジュースを飲んでいた」.
default.q.n3-18-q61-61.why.1: (b) Incorrect because vending machines could already sell cold items in their early days (「最初のころの自動販売機は、冷たい物しか売ることができなかった」). What he aimed to do was add hot items for sale in winter.
default.q.n3-18-q61-61.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the truck drivers did not directly say anything to or ask anything of the company president. Rather, after seeing them shivering, the president came up with the idea (「それを見た飲料会社の社長が、冬には温かい物を飲んでほしいと考えた」).
default.q.n3-18-q61-61.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage directly states: 「みんなとても寒そうだったので、それを見た飲料会社の社長が、冬には温かい物を飲んでほしいと考えた。それから10年近くかけて作られたのが、今の販売機なのだそうだ。」 (Everyone looked very cold, so the president of a beverage company thought that he wanted people to be able to drink something warm in winter. The vending machines used today were apparently developed over the following ten years.)
default.q.n3-18-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Park-san needs to prepare a list of the companies participating in the information session by around 11 o’clock.
default.q.n3-18-q62-62.explanation:
**Main point of the passage:** On the evening of December 1, Section Chief Kuroda left a note for Park-san (which Park-san read on the morning of December 2), praising the report from the previous week's presentation for being clear and easy to understand. After reading this note, what does Park-san need to do?

2. Rewrite the report from the presentation to make it easier to understand before the afternoon meeting.
