default.q.n3-2-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 4. どちらかというと.
default.q.n3-2-q39-39.explanation:
Meaning: Tanaka: "I hear you watch a lot of movies, right? Do you watch them at the theater?" — Yamashita: "I do go to the theater, but if I had to choose, I watch DVDs at home more often."
• Expression: どちらかというと (if I had to say or choose; comparatively speaking between two options).
• Example: 肉と魚、どちらかというと魚のほうが好きです。(Between meat and fish, if I had to choose, I prefer fish.)
default.q.n3-2-q39-39.why.0: (a) 確かに: an adverb meaning “indeed, certainly,” used to confirm a fact, not to compare tendencies between two choices.
default.q.n3-2-q39-39.why.1: (b) まるで means “just like” or “as if,” and is commonly followed by 「〜ようだ / 〜みたいだ」 for comparison.
default.q.n3-2-q39-39.why.2: (c) 必ずしも means “not necessarily” or “not always” and must be followed by a negative form such as 「〜とは限らない / 〜ない」 at the end of the sentence.
default.q.n3-2-q39-39.why.3: (d) どちらかというと: an adverb meaning “if I had to choose between the two” or “rather,” used to compare two possibilities, going to the theater and watching at home, and indicate which tendency is stronger.
default.q.n3-2-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 2. うちに.
default.q.n3-2-q40-40.explanation:
Meaning: If you peel boiled potatoes after they are cooked, the skins come off more cleanly. After boiling them, peel them while they are still hot.
• Structure: A-い / A-な / V-る / V-ている / V-ない + うちに (while/in the meantime; take the opportunity to do something before the situation changes).
• Example: スープが温かいうちに召し上がってください。(Please enjoy the soup while it is still warm.)
default.q.n3-2-q40-40.why.0: (a) のに means “although” or “in order to,” so it does not fit the meaning of the cooking instructions.
default.q.n3-2-q40-40.why.1: (b) うちに: The grammar pattern「〜うちに」means “while / before the state changes”;「熱いうちに」means “while the potatoes are still hot.”
default.q.n3-2-q40-40.why.2: (c) ことで: means "by doing" or "because of," indicating a method or cause; it does not combine with the adjective 「熱い」 here.
default.q.n3-2-q40-40.why.3: (d) とすると means “assuming that” or “if we suppose that,” so it does not fit a sentence giving instructions for an action.
default.q.n3-2-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ばかり.
default.q.n3-2-q41-41.explanation:
Meaning: I only ate a little while ago, but my stomach is already starting to feel hungry.
• Structure: V-た + ばかり (having just finished doing V, according to the speaker's subjective perception).
• Example: さっき起きたばかりなのに、もう眠くなってきた。(I just woke up a little while ago, but I am already getting sleepy.)
default.q.n3-2-q41-41.why.0: (a) せい means “because of” or “due to,” usually indicating a negative cause, and is used in patterns such as 「〜せいで / せいか」; 「食べたせいなのに」 does not fit this context.
default.q.n3-2-q41-41.why.1: (b) とき means “when/at the time,” but it does not naturally combine with 「〜ときなのに」 to express a contrast involving something that has just happened.
default.q.n3-2-q41-41.why.2: (c) よう: Means “seems like” or “like,” expressing a supposition or comparison; it is not appropriate when talking about one’s own action of eating a meal.
default.q.n3-2-q41-41.why.3: (d) ばかり: The grammar pattern 「Vた + ばかり」 means “have just done something.” Combined with 「なのに」, 「食べたばかりなのに」 means “even though I have just eaten,” expressing surprise at something contrary to expectations.
default.q.n3-2-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 1. したくて.
default.q.n3-2-q42-42.explanation:
Meaning: When I was in elementary school, I absolutely loved playing video games. Because I wanted to play games at home as soon as possible, I ran all the way home from school every day.
• Structure: V-たくて (because one wants to do V; the て-form of the desire expression indicates a reason or cause).
• Example: 喉が渇いて、早く水が飲みたくてたまらなかった。(I was so thirsty that I desperately wanted to drink water.)
default.q.n3-2-q42-42.why.0: (a) したくて: The 〜て-form of the i-adjective 「したい」 (want to do) expresses a cause or reason: "because I really wanted to play a game at home soon..." The particle 「が」 is appropriate for the object of the desire expressed by 「〜たい」.
default.q.n3-2-q42-42.why.1: (b) したくても means "even if one wants to do it," expressing concession; this contradicts the enthusiastic act of running home in the following clause.
default.q.n3-2-q42-42.why.2: (c) するためで: 「ために」is used to express purpose. 「〜ためで」cannot connect a purpose clause to an action in this way; moreover, with 「する」, the preceding particle should be 「を」rather than 「が」.
default.q.n3-2-q42-42.why.3: (d) するためでも: Means “even for the purpose of doing ...,” which does not fit a context expressing the direct cause that prompted the action.
default.q.n3-2-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 2. あげたら.
default.q.n3-2-q43-43.explanation:
Meaning: I am thinking about what birthday present to choose for my younger brother. I wonder what I could give him that would make him happy.
• Giving and receiving: あげる (I give something to someone else) >< くれる (someone else gives something to me).
• Example: 友達の結婚祝いに何をあげたらいいか迷っている。(I am wondering what would be a good wedding present to give my friend.)
default.q.n3-2-q43-43.why.0: (a) くれたら: The verb 「くれる」 is used when someone else gives something to the speaker or someone on the speaker's side; it is not used when the speaker gives something to their younger brother.
default.q.n3-2-q43-43.why.1: (b) あげたら: The verb あげる is used when the speaker gives something to someone else. Combined with 〜たら, it forms a hypothetical condition: “If I gave someone something, they would be happy, wouldn’t they?”
default.q.n3-2-q43-43.why.2: (c) くれるから: The direction of the action is incorrect (「くれる」 is used), and the connective meaning is also incorrect (「〜から」 indicates a reason, not a hypothetical condition).
default.q.n3-2-q43-43.why.3: (d) あげるから:「〜から」indicates a cause or reason, so it does not fit a hypothetical question with「〜だろうか」.
default.q.n3-2-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 持ってく.
default.q.n3-2-q44-44.explanation:
Meaning: A: “Could you lend me the novel I borrowed last time one more time?” B: “Sure. I'll bring it to school tomorrow.”
• Colloquial grammar: V-ていく → V-てく (to take or bring something away from the speaker to another place).
• Example: 明日のピクニックにお弁当を持ってくね。(I'll bring a boxed lunch to tomorrow's picnic.)
default.q.n3-2-q44-44.why.0: (a) 持っとく is a shortened form of 「持っておく」(to keep or prepare something in advance), and does not describe carrying an object from home to school.
default.q.n3-2-q44-44.why.1: (b) 持ってる is the contracted form of 「持っている」 (to have / be holding), describing a state of possession rather than the action of carrying something away.
default.q.n3-2-q44-44.why.2: (c) 持ってく: A shortened spoken form of「持っていく」(take something to another location), appropriate because B will take the books to school tomorrow.
default.q.n3-2-q44-44.why.3: (d) 持っちゃう is the contracted form of 「持ってしまう」 (to end up taking or carrying everything), expressing regret or complete accomplishment, so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-2-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 晴れるといい.
default.q.n3-2-q45-45.explanation:
Meaning: A: “I’m really looking forward to the mountain climb the week after next.” B: “Yes, I hope the weather will be sunny that day.”
• Pattern: V-る / V-ない + といいね (I hope… / It would be nice if…; expressing a wish for the future).
• Example: 明日の試験、合格できるといいね。(I hope you pass tomorrow’s exam.)
default.q.n3-2-q45-45.why.0: (a) 晴れてきた describes a change of state happening before one’s eyes (“it has started to clear up”); it is not used for an event in the week after next (再来週).
default.q.n3-2-q45-45.why.1: (b) 晴れるといい: The pattern 「Vるといい(ね)」 expresses hope or a wish for a future event (“I hope the weather will be clear/sunny”).
default.q.n3-2-q45-45.why.2: (c) 晴れるんだ: This is used to explain or assert a fact, so it sounds unnatural when talking about a weather forecast for two weeks later in a context of anticipation.
default.q.n3-2-q45-45.why.3: (d) 晴れてよかった is used to express relief that something good happened in the past (“It’s a relief that the weather cleared up”), so it is not used for the future.
default.q.n3-2-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ご参加になれます.
default.q.n3-2-q46-46.explanation:
Meaning: On September 30, a lecture by children’s manga author Sakamoto Midori will be held. Anyone who lives in the city may attend free of charge.
• Honorific language: ご + Sino-Japanese noun stem + になれます (the respectful potential form of a Group 3 verb: “you may/can…”).
• Example: こちらのラウンジは、会員の方ならどなたでもご利用になれます。(Any member may use this lounge.)
default.q.n3-2-q46-46.why.0: (a) ご参加になれます: the potential form of the respectful honorific pattern 「ご〜になる」 (ご参加になる → ご参加になれる). It respectfully refers to the residents’ action: “you will be able to participate.”
default.q.n3-2-q46-46.why.1: (b) 参加いたします: 「〜いたす」 is humble form, used to humble the speaker’s own action; it is not used for the actions of residents or readers.
default.q.n3-2-q46-46.why.2: (c) ご参加になっています is the honorific progressive form (“is participating”); it does not express ability (“can participate”).
default.q.n3-2-q46-46.why.3: (d) 参加できます is the ordinary potential form and is moderately polite, but in a formal announcement on a city website addressed to residents, the honorific expression 「ご参加になれます」 is the most accurate and polite choice.
default.q.n3-2-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 見えなくなってしまった.
default.q.n3-2-q47-47.explanation:
Meaning: In the past, I could see the sea from the company window, but after a high-rise building was constructed next door, I can no longer see it.
• Pattern: V-なくなる + てしまう (come to be unable to do something, expressing regret about the change of state).
• Example: 視力が落ちて、遠くの文字が見えなくなってしまった。(My eyesight deteriorated, and now I can no longer see distant writing clearly.)
default.q.n3-2-q47-47.why.0: (a) 見えなくてよくなった: Means “it became fine not to have to see it anymore,” expressing a positive feeling, so it is unsuitable when the view of the sea has been lost.
default.q.n3-2-q47-47.why.1: (b) 見られたかもしれない: Means “might have been able to see it,” expressing a past conjecture, which does not fit the reality that the view was blocked by a building.
default.q.n3-2-q47-47.why.2: (c) 見えなくなってしまった combines 「見えなくなる」 (“become no longer visible”) with 「〜てしまう」, expressing regret over an unwanted event, and fits the context perfectly.
default.q.n3-2-q47-47.why.3: (d) 見られるようにならない means "cannot become visible," which sounds awkward and does not match the tense in a sentence describing a change that has already occurred.
default.q.n3-2-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 飲んだほうがいいでしょうか.
default.q.n3-2-q48-48.explanation:
Meaning: Doctor: “Please take this medicine for five days.” — Patient: “I understand. Even if my fever has gone down, should I still take it?” — Doctor: “Yes. Be sure to take it for the full five days.”
• Structure: V-た + ほうがいいでしょうか (Should I V? — used when asking someone for advice or an opinion).
• Example: 明日、傘を持って行ったほうがいいでしょうか。(Should I take an umbrella with me tomorrow?)
default.q.n3-2-q48-48.why.0: (a) 飲んではいけませんか means “Am I not allowed to take the medicine?” If the question were phrased that way, the doctor's reply, “Yes, be sure to take it for all five days,” would be contradictory.
default.q.n3-2-q48-48.why.1: (b) 飲んでいないんでしょうか means “Could it be that you have not taken it?” and is completely meaningless in a context where a patient is asking for advice about taking medicine in the future.
default.q.n3-2-q48-48.why.2: (c) 飲んでみようと思いますか means “Are you planning to try drinking it, doctor?”, so the person performing the action is completely wrong.
default.q.n3-2-q48-48.why.3: (d) 飲んだほうがいいでしょうか: the sentence pattern 「〜たほうがいいでしょうか」 politely asks for advice (“Should I take it?”), fitting the doctor's instruction, “Yes. Be sure to take it for all five days.”
default.q.n3-2-q49-49.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (去年の夏に). The correct order is: 1 → 3 → 4 → 2 (★ falls in the third position, corresponding to choice 4).
default.q.n3-2-q49-49.explanation:
Complete sentence: 今年の夏も暑いが、異常な暑さだった去年の夏に比べるとずっと涼しく感じる。

Meaning: This summer is hot too, but it feels much cooler than last summer, which was abnormally hot.
default.q.n3-2-q49-49.why.0: (a) 「異常な」, a na-adjective, occupies position 1 and directly modifies the noun 「暑さ」 to form 「異常な暑さ」 (“abnormal heat”).
default.q.n3-2-q49-49.why.1: (b) 「比べると」 occupies the fourth position and combines with the particle 「に」 in piece (4) to form the comparison pattern 「〜に比べると」 (compared with ...).
default.q.n3-2-q49-49.why.2: (c) 「暑さだった」 is in the second position and, together with fragment (1), forms the attributive clause 「異常な暑さだった」 modifying the noun 「去年の夏」 in fragment (4).
default.q.n3-2-q49-49.why.3: (d) 「去年の夏に」 occupies position 3 (the ★ slot), receives the preceding modifying clause, and uses the particle 「に」 to connect with 「比べると」 in fragment (2).
default.q.n3-2-q50-50.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (大変な). The correct order is: 3 → 4 → 2 → 1 (★ falls in position 3, corresponding to answer choice 2).
default.q.n3-2-q50-50.explanation:
Complete sentence: 初めてアルバイトをして、お金を稼ぐことがどれだけ大変なことかわかった。

Meaning: It was my first time working part-time, and I learned how difficult it is to earn money.
default.q.n3-2-q50-50.why.0: (a) 「ことか」appears in the fourth position. It follows the adjective「大変な」and combines with the adverb「どれだけ」to form the exclamatory structure「どれだけ〜ことか」(how...; to what extent...).
default.q.n3-2-q50-50.why.1: (b) 「大変な」 (na-adjective) goes in position 3 (the ★ slot), modifying 「ことか」 to emphasize how difficult it was in the pattern 「どれだけ大変なことか」.
default.q.n3-2-q50-50.why.2: (c) 「ことが」 is in the first position and follows 「お金を稼ぐ」, nominalizing the verb phrase to form the subject 「お金を稼ぐことが」 (earning money).
default.q.n3-2-q50-50.why.3: (d) 「どれだけ」 is in the second position and is an adverb of degree used with the exclamatory pattern 「どれだけ〜ことか」.
default.q.n3-2-q51-51.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (ので). The correct order is: 4 → 2 → 1 → 3 (★ falls in position 3, corresponding to answer choice 1).
default.q.n3-2-q51-51.explanation:
Complete sentence: 今日、昼食の後、図書館へ行って本を読んでいたら、いつのまにか外が暗くなっていたので驚いた。

Meaning: Today, after lunch, I went to the library and was reading a book when I was surprised to find that it had somehow become dark outside.
default.q.n3-2-q51-51.why.0: (a) 「ので」 occupies the third position (the ★ slot) and connects the cause 「外が暗くなっていた」 with the result 「驚いた」.
default.q.n3-2-q51-51.why.1: (b) 「外が暗くなっていた」is in the second position. It is a clause describing a change of state (it had become dark outside), modified by the adverb「いつのまにか」.
default.q.n3-2-q51-51.why.2: (c) 「驚いた」 appears in the fourth position at the end of the sentence and is the main predicate expressing surprise.
default.q.n3-2-q51-51.why.3: (d) 「いつのまにか」 is placed in position 1. It is an adverb meaning “before one realizes it” and modifies the action or state in fragment (2).
default.q.n3-2-q52-52.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (だけ). The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 3 → 1 (★ falls in position 3, corresponding to answer choice 3).
default.q.n3-2-q52-52.explanation:
Complete sentence: このチーズケーキの作り方は材料を混ぜて冷やすだけだから、誰でも簡単に作れると思う。

Meaning: This cheesecake is made simply by mixing the ingredients and chilling them, so I think anyone can make it easily.
default.q.n3-2-q52-52.why.0: (a) 「だから」 occupies position 4 and follows the particle 「だけ」 to state a cause or reason (“because it is only ~, ...”).
default.q.n3-2-q52-52.why.1: (b) 「作り方は」 is in position 1 and combines with the beginning of the sentence to form the subject 「このチーズケーキの作り方は」 (the way to make this cheesecake).
default.q.n3-2-q52-52.why.2: (c) 「だけ」is in position 3 (the ★ slot), following the verb「冷やす」to express the simple limitation “just...” or “only...”.
default.q.n3-2-q52-52.why.3: (d) 「材料を混ぜて冷やす」 is in position 2 and serves as the predicate listing the successive steps for the subject 「作り方は」.
default.q.n3-2-q53-53.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (中止にならないんだけど). The correct order is: 3 → 2 → 4 → 1 (★ falls in position 3, corresponding to choice 4).
default.q.n3-2-q53-53.explanation:
Complete passage: A「『あさってのサッカーの試合、応援に行くね。天気予報では曇りと言っていたけど、雨だったら中止になる？』</br> B「ありがとう。もし雨が降ったとしても試合は中止にならないんだけど、雨が降ったら、応援には無理して来なくてもいいよ。」

Meaning:
A: "I’ll go cheer for you at the soccer game the day after tomorrow. The weather forecast said it would be cloudy, but will the game be canceled if it rains?"
B: "Thanks. Even if it does rain, the game won’t be canceled, but if it rains, you don’t have to force yourself to come and cheer."
default.q.n3-2-q53-53.why.0: (a) 「雨が降ったら」 appears in the fourth position. It is the conditional clause “if it rains,” placed immediately before the main clause 「応援には無理して来なくてもいいよ」.
default.q.n3-2-q53-53.why.1: (b) 「試合は」 is in the second position and functions as the subject of the predicate 「中止にならない」 in fragment (4).
default.q.n3-2-q53-53.why.2: (c) 「雨が降ったとしても」(1) is in the first position. Together with 「もし」 at the beginning of the sentence, it forms the concessive hypothetical pattern 「もし〜としても」 (even if / supposing that ...).
default.q.n3-2-q53-53.why.3: (d) 「中止にならないんだけど」 goes in the third position (the ★ slot), using the contrastive ending 「〜んだけど」 to explain the situation before giving advice in the following clause.
default.q.n3-2-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 2. それでも.
default.q.n3-2-q54-54.explanation: The previous sentence presents a difficult situation and the speaker’s reluctance: "その日は晴れていましたが、バスを降りたらとても寒くて、私は暖かいところにいたいと思いました" (It was sunny that day, but it was very cold when I got off the bus, and I wanted to stay somewhere warm). The next sentence describes an action: "...せっかく来たのだからと思って、スキーの練習を始めました" (Thinking that I had come all this way, I began practicing skiing). To connect the desire to stay somewhere warm because it was so cold with the decision to go skiing anyway, a contrastive or concessive conjunction meaning “even so” or “nevertheless” is needed: 「それでも」.
default.q.n3-2-q54-54.why.0: (a) 「例えば」(for example): Used to introduce a specific example illustrating the preceding sentence; it cannot express a concessive relationship between two sentences.
default.q.n3-2-q54-54.why.1: (b) 「それでも」 (“even so / nevertheless”): A conjunction expressing concession, used when an action is still carried out despite the preceding difficult circumstances. It fits the development of the passage very well.
default.q.n3-2-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「実は」 (actually, in fact) is used to reveal an unexpected fact or provide an explanation, so it does not fit this context.
default.q.n3-2-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「また」(also, in addition): adds information in the same direction and does not express contrast.
default.q.n3-2-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 滑れるようになりました.
default.q.n3-2-q55-55.explanation: The passage describes the writer learning to ski: at first, they could not ski and found it difficult, but after half a day of practice, their ability improved ("they fell less often"). The structure 「V-れるようになる」expresses a change in ability, from being unable to do something to becoming able to do it. Therefore, 「滑れるようになりました」(became able to ski) is the most accurate choice. The choices containing てあげる, てくれる, and てもらう describe giving or receiving an action with another person, so they do not fit the author's own change in ability.
default.q.n3-2-q55-55.why.0: (a) 「滑れるようになりました」(I became able to ski): the pattern 「V-れるようになる」expresses a change in the author's ability after half a day of practice, so it is completely correct.
default.q.n3-2-q55-55.why.1: (b) 「滑れるようにしてあげました」 (“made it possible for someone to ski”) uses 「~てあげる」 to describe an action benefiting someone else, so it is inappropriate when talking about the writer’s own improvement.
default.q.n3-2-q55-55.why.2: (c) 「滑ってくれました」(someone skated for me): The structure「~てくれる」is used when someone performs an action for the speaker, which does not fit the context of practicing by oneself.
default.q.n3-2-q55-55.why.3: (d) 「滑ってもらえました」 (“someone slid for me”): the structure「~てもらう」is used when receiving an action from another person, so it does not fit the meaning.
default.q.n3-2-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 4. あの.
default.q.n3-2-q56-56.explanation: In the text, when the writer wants to refer back to a past event or memory that both the writer and reader already know well (here, the ski trip described in detail earlier in the passage), the demonstrative from the あ-series is used, specifically 「あの」(that, that ... back then). The phrase「あのスキー旅行」means “that ski trip” or “that ski trip we took back then.”
default.q.n3-2-q56-56.why.0: (a) 「あの広告の」(of that advertisement): If inserted, it would mean “remembering that advertisement’s trip,” which is incorrect because the author is recalling their own trip.
default.q.n3-2-q56-56.why.1: (b) 「ああいう」 (“that kind of”) indicates a similar type or quality and is not used to identify a specific event from one’s memories.
default.q.n3-2-q56-56.why.2: (c) 「ある」 (“a certain...,” “some...”): Used when referring to an unspecified thing or event; it is unsuitable here because this is a specific trip described in detail.
default.q.n3-2-q56-56.why.3: (d) 「あの」 (“that”): A demonstrative from the あ-series used to modify a noun referring to a specific past memory or experience known to both the writer and the reader.
default.q.n3-2-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 3. わかりました.
default.q.n3-2-q57-57.explanation: The preceding clause is a condition or premise: 「自分でもスキーをしてみて」(After trying skiing myself). The writer summarizes an understanding or realization gained from that personal experience. Because it is a direct realization reached through a past experience, the affirmative past form 「わかりました」(I realized / I came to understand) is used.
default.q.n3-2-q57-57.why.0: (a) 「わかっていきます」 (“will gradually come to understand”) describes an ongoing change in the future, so it does not fit because the author understood after completing the experience.
default.q.n3-2-q57-57.why.1: (b) 「わかるのでしょう」 (“I wonder if [they] will understand”) expresses a conjecture; it is not used to assert the writer's own understanding.
default.q.n3-2-q57-57.why.2: (c) 「わかりました」(I realized or understood): The affirmative past form naturally and accurately expresses that the writer understood the reason after experiencing it personally.
default.q.n3-2-q57-57.why.3: (d) 「わかったそうです」 means "I hear that they understood." It is a structure for reporting information from another person and is not used for the speaker's direct perception.
default.q.n3-2-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Review the materials once more this week.

Question: What is John being asked to do in this email?

default.q.n3-2-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 予約した本を借りることと、本を返すことと、本の予約をすること (checking out reserved books, returning books, and making book reservations).

While Midori Library is closed for renovations (April 1–September 30), it operates a special counter on the third floor of Mizumori Station building. What can you do at the special counter in the station building?

**Translation of the choices:**
1. Borrow reserved books, return books, read books, and reserve books.
2. Borrow reserved books, return books, and read books.
3. Borrow reserved books, return books, and reserve books.
4. Only borrow reserved books and return books.
default.q.n3-2-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage clearly states 「本や新聞を読む場所はありません」 (“There is no place to read books or newspapers”), so books cannot be read at the special counter.
default.q.n3-2-q59-59.why.1: (b) Incorrect. This choice includes reading books, even though there is no place for that: 「本や新聞を読む場所はありません」. It also leaves out the activity of reserving books at the counter.

default.q.n3-2-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect. This choice uses 「だけ」 (“only”), but in addition to borrowing and returning books, users can also reserve books at the counter (「なお、本の予約は、インターネットでの予約が便利ですが、特別窓口でも可能です」).
default.q.n3-2-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 記事で紹介されていた靴下は、洗濯ができて、繰り返して使えること (The socks introduced in the article can be washed and reused many times).
default.q.n3-2-q60-60.explanation:
Summary of the main point: When the author sees the title "Socks Made from Paper," they assume the socks will be used once and thrown away like paper cups. However, the article explains that the socks are made from a special, durable paper fiber that is water-resistant, washable, and reusable many times. This difference between reality and the author's initial assumption is what surprises them.

Question translation:
The passage says, "Contrary to my expectations, it was surprising." What surprised the author?

Answer choices:
1. There are paper socks that are used once and thrown away like paper cups.
2. The socks introduced in the article can be washed and reused many times.
3. The socks introduced in the article absorb sweat well and dry quickly.
4. There are socks for people who wear shoes for long periods.
default.q.n3-2-q60-60.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the idea that it would be used once and then thrown away like a paper cup was only the author's initial assumption after seeing the title (「一度使ったら捨ててしまう物なのだろうと思った」); it was not the surprising discovery made after reading the article.
default.q.n3-2-q60-60.why.1: (b) Correct. default.q.n3-2-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Once the most painful area has improved, the patient begins to feel pain in another location.
default.q.n3-2-q61-61.explanation:
**Summary of the main point:**
The passage explains why, when a patient's pain improves in one area, pain may begin to appear in another area. The patient may actually have had injuries in multiple locations from the beginning, but the human body can perceive only the strongest pain at any given time. Therefore, once the most painful area improves or heals, the patient begins to perceive the pain in the next location.

**Translation of the question:**
Why does the patient say, “The other area has started to hurt again. This time, it seems that something is wrong there”?

**Translation of the answer choices:**
1. Because when one painful area gradually heals, people may begin to feel several pains at the same time.
2. Because when one painful area heals, the next painful area may become more severe.
3. Because even when several areas hurt, patients may sometimes tell the doctor about only one area at a time.
4. Because when the painful area improves, people begin to feel pain in another location.
default.q.n3-2-q61-61.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the reading states 「人の体は、同じときに一つの痛みしか感じない」 (the human body can feel only one pain at a time), which contradicts the idea of feeling multiple pains simultaneously (複数の痛みを感じる).
default.q.n3-2-q61-61.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage does not say that the next location had become worse (もっと悪くなる). Rather, some parts had already been bad from the beginning (最初から悪いところがいくつかあった), and the speaker only noticed them now.
default.q.n3-2-q61-61.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage explains the body's mechanism for sensing pain; it does not say that patients intentionally report or communicate each location one by one (一つずつしか伝えない).
default.q.n3-2-q61-61.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage provides the following evidence: 「人の体は、同じときに一つの痛みしか感じない。そのときにいちばん強い痛みだけを感じるのである。この患者は、最も悪かったところが治ってきたので、次の痛みを感じるようになってきたと考えられる。」 (The human body feels only one pain at a time—the strongest pain at that moment. Since the patient's worst injury had begun to heal, it is thought that they had begun to feel the next pain elsewhere.)
default.q.n3-2-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 2: It gives an example of how “I” and my younger sister have opposite attitudes toward things they dislike or tasks they do not want to do.
default.q.n3-2-q62-62.explanation:
**Summary of the relevant passage:**
The passage begins by contrasting two sisters: although their faces look very similar, their attitudes toward things they dislike or find unpleasant are completely opposite (嫌いな物や嫌なことに対する姿勢は逆です). The author first gives the example of eating food they dislike (the narrator eats it last, while the younger sister eats it first), then introduces another example (もう一つ例があります) involving their summer vacation homework. Therefore, '① example' illustrates their contrasting attitudes toward things they dislike.

**Question and answer choices:**
*Question:* The word '① example' refers to an example of what?
1. The narrator and the younger sister are alike not only in appearance but also in personality.
2. The narrator and the younger sister have opposite attitudes toward things they dislike or tasks they do not want to do.
3. The narrator and the younger sister cooperate and help each other with their summer vacation homework.
4. Every year during summer vacation, the narrator and the younger sister are both scolded by their parents.
default.q.n3-2-q62-62.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage only says that the two sisters look very much alike (顔はとても似ていると言われますが); their attitudes toward things they dislike are opposite, and it never says that their personalities are alike.
default.q.n3-2-q62-62.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage says: 「私と妹は、顔はとても似ていると言われますが、嫌いな物や嫌なことに対する姿勢は 逆です。例えば、食事で苦手な物があったとき、私は最後に食べますが、妹は最初に食べて しまいます。 もう一つ①例があります。」 -> 'Here is another example' introduces the second piece of evidence for their opposite attitudes toward things they dislike.
default.q.n3-2-q62-62.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage never says that the two sisters worked together on their summer homework; each used a completely opposite approach.
default.q.n3-2-q62-62.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage says that in previous years only “I” was scolded by my parents for leaving the task until the last minute (「毎年、私だけ両親にしかられました」), not that both people were scolded every year.
default.q.n3-2-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 2: Both I and my younger sister dislike the summer vacation homework every year.
default.q.n3-2-q63-63.explanation:
**Summary of the relevant passage:**
The author gives two examples to illustrate attitudes toward “things one dislikes” (嫌なこと): the first is food one dislikes eating (苦手な物), and the second is being assigned a large amount of summer homework (宿題がたくさん出ました). Both sisters dislike summer homework and see it as something unpleasant (嫌なこと), but they deal with it in opposite ways: the younger sister wants to finish it immediately because she dislikes it, just as one eats disliked food first, while “I” keeps putting it off and ends up rushing to finish it just before the deadline, just as one leaves disliked food until the end.

**Question and answer choices:**
*Question:* What did “I” and the younger sister think about their summer vacation homework every year?
1. Both “I” and the younger sister liked it.
2. Both “I” and the younger sister disliked it.
3. “I” liked it, but the younger sister disliked it.
4. “I” disliked it, but the younger sister liked it.
default.q.n3-2-q63-63.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the summer homework is given as the second example of 「嫌なことに対する姿勢」 (one’s attitude toward things one dislikes doing), so both people dislike summer homework.
default.q.n3-2-q63-63.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states 「嫌いな物や嫌なことに対する姿勢は 逆です」 and gives 「もう一つ例」 involving summer homework. The younger sister does it immediately to get rid of something she dislikes, like eating an unpleasant dish first, whereas “I” puts it off until the end, like leaving the unpleasant dish for last. Both regard summer homework as 「嫌なこと」.
default.q.n3-2-q63-63.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the speaker put off doing the homework until just before the end of the vacation because they disliked or were reluctant to do it, not because they liked summer homework.
default.q.n3-2-q63-63.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the younger sister finished her homework at the very beginning of the vacation not because she liked homework, but because she habitually wants to get unpleasant tasks over with immediately.
default.q.n3-2-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The younger sister was scolded because she wrote things she had never actually done or experienced in her essay, “Memories of This Summer Vacation” (fabricating the content).
default.q.n3-2-q64-64.explanation:
**Relevant part of the passage:**
Every year, the younger sister finished all her homework as soon as the vacation began and was praised by her parents. One year, however, one of the assignments was an essay titled “Memories of This Summer Vacation.” Because she completed all her homework at the beginning of the vacation, before any actual summer experiences had taken place, what she wrote in the essay was fabricated—a lie (うそ). On the final day of the vacation, her mother discovered that the essay was untrue, scolded her, and made her rewrite it.

**Question and answer choices:**
*Question:* The passage says, “② the younger sister was also scolded.” Why was she scolded?
1. Because she did not start her homework until a few days before the summer vacation ended.
2. Because she wrote an essay for “Memories of This Summer Vacation” that was exactly the same as “my” essay.
3. Because she wrote about things in “Memories of This Summer Vacation” that she had not actually done or experienced.
4. Because she did not write “Memories of This Summer Vacation” until the final day of the summer vacation.
default.q.n3-2-q64-64.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the person who panicked and started doing the homework only a few days before summer vacation ended was "I" (「私は夏休みが終わる数日前になって慌ててやり始めました」), not the younger sister.
default.q.n3-2-q64-64.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage does not mention the younger sister copying or writing an essay similar to “mine.”
default.q.n3-2-q64-64.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: 「その年も、妹は夏休みが始まって すぐに、すべての宿題をやってしまいました。... その中に「今年の夏休みの思い出」という作文の宿題があったことに、気が ついていなかったのです。夏休みの最後の日、母は作文の内容がうそであることに気づいて、 書き直させました。」 Since she finished the assignment at the beginning of summer vacation, before she had any memories to write about, the essay was fabricated (うそ / describing something that had not actually happened).
default.q.n3-2-q64-64.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the younger sister wrote and completed the essay at the beginning of the summer vacation along with all her other assignments, rather than waiting until the final day.
default.q.n3-2-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 1. カラスが文字を読めないと意味がない方法だから (Because this method would be meaningless if crows could not read characters).

default.q.n3-2-q65-65.why.1: (b) DOES NOT MATCH: The passage does not mention that everyone could come up with this method as a reason for thinking it was a joke.

default.q.n3-2-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 4. カラスをよく見る人が増えて、カラスが危険を感じたから (Because more people began watching the crows closely, making the crows feel threatened).

default.q.n3-2-q66-66.why.0: (a) Does not match. The fact that the warehouse became dirty because crows made a mess is the reason people tried to drive the crows away, not a reason for the crows to leave because the warehouse was dirty.
default.q.n3-2-q66-66.why.1: (b) DOES NOT FIT: The passage explains that crows are frightened not because they see the paper themselves, but because of people’s reaction after seeing the paper and then looking at the crows.
default.q.n3-2-q66-66.why.2: (c) DOES NOT MATCH: The people who came to look at the crows were passersby who noticed the strange piece of paper, not researchers who came to observe the crows.

default.q.n3-2-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 「カラス侵入禁止」と書かれた紙を見たら、近くにいるカラスを観察したくなる。 (When people see a sign saying “No crows allowed,” they will want to observe the crows nearby.)
default.q.n3-2-q67-67.explanation:

  2. People would try to think of ways to keep crows out of places where they were not wanted.

default.q.n3-2-q67-67.why.0: (a) DOES NOT MATCH: The passage does not mention people wanting to seek out places that are featured as famous destinations in the news.
default.q.n3-2-q67-67.why.1: (b) DOES NOT MATCH: This concerns a research institute trying to solve the crow problem, not predicting how passersby would react to the posted notice.
default.q.n3-2-q67-67.why.2: (c) DOES NOT MATCH / CONTRADICTS: When people see the paper, they do not become afraid of the crows and avoid them; on the contrary, they look at and observe the crows more closely.
default.q.n3-2-q67-67.why.3: (d) QUOTE: The passage states: 「まず、そこを通って紙を見た人が不思議に思って、近くにいるカラスをよく見る。」 The author concludes: 「この研究者がカラスの行動だけでなく、人間の行動についても、しっかり③予想できていたのだろうと感心した。」 (The researcher had anticipated that people would find the paper strange and pay close attention to the crows.)
default.q.n3-2-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The restaurant has very few dishes made with common types of fish and many dishes made with unusual types of fish.

1. It had many dishes made with both common and unusual fish.

default.q.n3-2-q68-68.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage clearly states 「よく知られた魚を使った料理はほとんどなく」 (“there are hardly any dishes using familiar, commonly eaten fish”), so it cannot be said that there are many dishes of both types.
default.q.n3-2-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the information is completely opposite to the passage: ordinary fish dishes are actually very few, while there are many unusual fish dishes whose names the speaker has never heard.

default.q.n3-2-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The decline in Japan’s fish catch prompted a movement to increase the number of people eating underused fish.

default.q.n3-2-q69-69.why.0: (a) Correct, as shown by the passage: 「日本では、魚がとれる量が減り続けていて、多いときの半分以下になっている。…そこで、未利用魚を食べる人を増やそうという動きが広がってきた。」 (In Japan, the amount of fish caught continues to decline and has fallen to less than half its peak level... default.q.n3-2-q69-69.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage only says that the amount of fish caught is continuing to decrease (魚がとれる量が減り続けていて) and that Japanese people usually eat about 80 species; it does not say that the number of fish species they eat is decreasing.
default.q.n3-2-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage does not mention that if many people ate underused fish, other types of fish would no longer sell.

default.q.n3-2-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Because the parents wanted "me" to understand both how delicious the fish was and the significance of eating underused fish.
default.q.n3-2-q70-70.explanation:
- Main idea: The restaurant considers it important to help people learn about the deliciousness and significance of eating underused fish. The author agrees and realizes that their parents share the same view, which is why they invited the author to eat there.
- Translation of the question: Why did the parents take the author to the restaurant?
- Translation of the answer choices:
1. Because they wanted the author to learn about the deliciousness and significance of eating underused fish.
2. Because they wanted both to eat underused fish and to hear the author talk about underused fish.
3. Because they wanted to show the author that there were many other delicious kinds of fish besides underused fish.
4. Because they knew the author was interested in underused fish.

  + Thursday (18:00–20:00): marked 「バスケットボール」, with no restriction and within the desired 16:00–20:00 period. Anh Nguyen can play then.
  + Friday (14:00–16:00): basketball is available, but this is outside the desired 16:00–20:00 period. From 16:00 to 20:00 on Friday, volleyball (バレーボール) is scheduled.

- 2. Tuesday or Thursday
- 3. Thursday or Friday
- 4. Thursday
default.q.n3-2-q73-73.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the ★ on Tuesday is reserved for elementary and junior high school students, while basketball on Friday is available only from 14:00 to 16:00, outside the 16:00–20:00 period.
default.q.n3-2-q73-73.why.1: (b) Incorrect because Tuesday from 16:00 to 18:00 is marked 「★バスケットボール」. According to the note 「★ の時間は小学生と中学生だけが利用可能です」, a university student such as Nguyen cannot use it.
default.q.n3-2-q73-73.why.2: (c) Incorrect because on Friday, the 16:00–20:00 time slot is for volleyball (バレーボール). Basketball takes place from 14:00 to 16:00, so it does not fit the required time slot.
default.q.n3-2-q73-73.why.3: (d) Correct because according to the September schedule, Thursday's 18:00–20:00 slot offers 「バスケットボール」 for all participants and falls within the 16:00–20:00 period. Tuesday is restricted by the ★ mark to elementary and junior high school students, while Friday basketball is available only from 14:00 to 16:00.

default.q.n3-2-q15-15.explanation:
Sentence translation: The scenery viewed from the mountaintop was beautiful, so I was deeply moved / impressed.

default.q.n3-2-q15-15.why.0: (a) 拝見 (haiken): the humble form of 見る (to see, look at), used when the speaker looks at the other person’s belongings or documents respectfully; it is not used to describe feelings toward scenery.
default.q.n3-2-q15-15.why.1: (b) 歓迎 (welcome): to warmly welcome someone (e.g., 新入生を歓迎する); it is not used for a personal feeling when admiring a view.

default.q.n3-2-q16-16.explanation:

- Sino-Japanese reading: 中古 (used, secondhand), 後半 (latter half), 中年 (middle age), 後期 (latter period).
- Example: 予算が少ないので、中古のパソコンを買った。(My budget was small, so I bought a used computer.)
default.q.n3-2-q16-16.why.0: (a) 後半 (the second half, latter half) refers to the second half of a game, film, century, and so on; it is not used with 車 to mean a used car.
default.q.n3-2-q16-16.why.1: (b) 中年 (middle age): middle-aged, referring to a person; it is not used to modify or describe the nature of an object or vehicle.
default.q.n3-2-q16-16.why.2: (c) 中古: used, secondhand.「中古の車 / 中古車」means a used car, one that has previously been owned.
default.q.n3-2-q16-16.why.3: (d) 後期 means “the latter period” or “the second term” (e.g., 後期高齢者, 後期試験), not “old belongings.”
default.q.n3-2-q17-17.explanation:
Sentence meaning: I made a list of the things I need to take on next week’s trip.
- Katakana vocabulary: リスト (list), スケジュール (schedule), カタログ (catalog), プログラム (program).
- Example: 買い物に行く前に、買う物のリストを作っておく。(I make a list of what to buy before going shopping.)
default.q.n3-2-q17-17.why.0: (a) スケジュール (schedule): a timetable or schedule of activities arranged over time; it is not used for a list of objects.
default.q.n3-2-q17-17.why.1: (b) リスト: means “list.”「持っていく物のリスト」means a list of things to take along, or a packing list.
default.q.n3-2-q17-17.why.2: (c) カタログ: a product catalog containing pictures and price lists; it is not a list of personal belongings.
default.q.n3-2-q17-17.why.3: (d) プログラム: a performance program, event program, or software program; it is not used to list belongings.
default.q.n3-2-q18-18.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (くやしかった).
default.q.n3-2-q18-18.explanation:
Sentence translation: I was really frustrated about losing last time, but I won this time, so I am truly happy.
- Vocabulary: 悔しい (frustrating, bitterly disappointing after losing), 貧しい (poor), 緩い (loose, gently sloping), ずるい (sly, unfair).
- Example: あと1点で合格できたのに、落ちてしまって本当に悔しい。(I needed just one more point to pass, but I failed, which is really frustrating.)
default.q.n3-2-q18-18.why.0: (a) くやしかった (from 悔しい—regretful, frustrated, resentful after a defeat): describes deep frustration and regret over losing the previous match, perfectly fitting the following clause, “so I was very happy to win this time.”
default.q.n3-2-q18-18.why.1: (b) まずしかった (from 貧しい - poor, impoverished): it describes poor economic conditions and is not used for the feeling of losing a match.
default.q.n3-2-q18-18.why.2: (c) ゆるかった (from 緩い: loose, gently sloping, mild) describes loose clothing, a loose fastening, or a gentle slope; it is not used for one’s mood.
default.q.n3-2-q18-18.why.3: (d) ずるかった (from ずるい — cunning, deceitful, sly): describes dishonest character or behavior and is not used to express personal feelings after losing.
default.q.n3-2-q19-19.explanation:
Translation: How far is it from here to the city hall?
- Sino-Japanese terms: 距離 (distance), 途中 (on the way, midway), 徒歩 (on foot), 方向 (direction).
- Example: 駅までの距離を地図で調べる。(I checked the distance to the station on a map.)
default.q.n3-2-q19-19.why.0: (a) 途中 (on the way, midway) means being in the middle of a journey (for example, 学校に行く途中で), and it cannot be combined with 「どのくらい」 to ask about the length of a route.
default.q.n3-2-q19-19.why.1: (b) 徒歩 means walking or on foot (e.g., 徒歩5分, a 5-minute walk); it does not form 「〜までの徒歩はどのくらい」 to ask about distance.
default.q.n3-2-q19-19.why.2: (c) 方向 (direction): direction, orientation (e.g., 駅の方向); it is not used with 「どのくらい」 to ask about distance.
default.q.n3-2-q19-19.why.3: (d) 距離: spatial distance or length. The pattern 「〜までの距離はどのくらいですか」 is the standard way to ask how far it is from one place to another.
default.q.n3-2-q20-20.explanation:
Translation: After taking a shower, use this towel to dry yourself.
- Kanji-related verbs: 拭く means to wipe, 干す means to dry, 張る means to stretch or hang, and 直す means to fix or adjust.
- Example: 汗をかいたので、ハンカチで顔をふいた。(I was sweating, so I wiped my face with a handkerchief.)
default.q.n3-2-q20-20.why.0: (a) ほして comes from 干す (“to hang out or dry”), as in 洗濯物を干す; it is not used for wiping one’s body with a towel.
default.q.n3-2-q20-20.why.1: (b) ふいて (from 拭く - wipe): Used to wipe a surface or the body with a towel or cloth. 「タオルで体をふく」 means “wipe one’s body with a towel.”
default.q.n3-2-q20-20.why.2: (c) 張って (from 張る: to stretch, put up, or spread out): used for stretching a tarp or pitching a tent, not for wiping oneself with a towel.
default.q.n3-2-q20-20.why.3: (d) 直して (from 直す, to repair or adjust): used for repairing something broken or adjusting clothing, not for drying someone’s body.
default.q.n3-2-q21-21.explanation:
Sentence translation: Because the delivery was late, I was complained at by the customer.
- Vocabulary: 文句 (complaint, grumbling), 失礼 (rudeness), 命令 (command), 否定 (negation).
- Fixed expressions: 文句を言う (to complain), 文句を言われる (to be complained at, be criticized).
- Example: いつも文句ばかり言っていないで、自分でやってみなさい。(Stop complaining all the time and try doing it yourself.)
default.q.n3-2-q21-21.why.0: (a) 失礼 (rudeness, discourtesy): it means impoliteness or discourtesy (e.g., 失礼な態度), and does not form「失礼を言われる」with the meaning "to be complained about."
default.q.n3-2-q21-21.why.1: (b) 命令 (command): an instruction or order (e.g., 命令を下す), which does not fit the context of a customer being angry about a delayed delivery.
default.q.n3-2-q21-21.why.2: (c) 否定 means “denial” or “negation” (e.g., 意見を否定する); it is not used in the phrase 「否定を言われる」.
default.q.n3-2-q21-21.why.3: (d) 文句: A complaint, grievance, or grumbling. The fixed expressions 「文句を言う / 文句を言われる」 mean “complain / have someone complain to you.”
default.q.n3-2-q22-22.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (思いついた).
default.q.n3-2-q22-22.explanation:
- Sentence translation: Is there anyone who can think of a good way to solve this problem?
- Common expression: アイデア／方法を思いつく (to think of an idea / method).
- Sino-Japanese readings: 解決 (solution), 思いつく (to think of), 引き受ける (to take on), 知り合う (to get acquainted), 取り替える (to replace).
- Example: いいアイデアを思いついたので、みんなに提案した。(I thought of a good idea, so I suggested it to everyone.)
default.q.n3-2-q22-22.why.0: (a) 思いついた (from 思いつく: think of, come up with): Commonly used with 「方法 / アイデアを思いつく」, meaning to come up with a solution or idea.
default.q.n3-2-q22-22.why.1: (b) 引き受けた (from 引き受ける – to accept or take on a task/responsibility): Used with work or a position (e.g., 仕事を引き受ける), not with 「方法を引き受ける」.
default.q.n3-2-q22-22.why.2: (c) 知り合った (from 知り合う, “to become acquainted”): used for relationships between people (e.g., パーティーで知り合った), not with a word referring to a method.
default.q.n3-2-q22-22.why.3: (d) 取り替えた (from 取り替える: to exchange, replace) means replacing something old with something new or changing one thing for another (e.g., 電池を取り替える); it does not fit the context of thinking of a solution.
default.q.n3-2-q23-23.explanation:
Translation: The road from my house to the station is uphill, so walking to the station is exhausting.
- Related compounds: 坂道 (SAKA-MICHI - uphill road), 通り道 (TŌRI-MICHI - passageway, route), 片道 (KATA-MICHI - one-way trip), 近道 (CHIKA-MICHI - shortcut).
- Example: 自転車で急な坂道を上るのは大変だ。(It is hard to cycle up a steep hill.)
default.q.n3-2-q23-23.why.0: (a) 坂道 (さかみち — sloping road): a road with an incline. Walking on a sloping road takes a lot of effort and makes you tired (疲れます), which fits the context perfectly.
default.q.n3-2-q23-23.why.1: (b) 通り道 (a route or passageway): a road or path that passes through a particular location; it is not the direct cause of becoming tired while walking.
default.q.n3-2-q23-23.why.2: (c) 片道 (one-way): a one-way route or one-way ticket (opposite of 往復, round trip); it is not used to describe tiring terrain.
default.q.n3-2-q23-23.why.3: (d) 近道 (shortcut): A shortcut reduces the distance or time needed, so it does not fit the reason why walking made the person tired.
default.q.n3-2-q24-24.explanation:
Sentence meaning: This restaurant is very popular, and there is always a long line of people waiting for it to open in front of the entrance.
- Kanji readings: 列 (れつ — line), 帯 (たい — band, belt), 線 (せん — line), 壁 (へき — wall).
- Fixed expressions: 列ができる (a line forms), 列に並ぶ (to line up).
- Example: 有名なラーメン屋の前に長い列ができていた。(There was a long line in front of the famous ramen restaurant.)
default.q.n3-2-q24-24.why.0: (a) 帯: obi belt, kimono sash, narrow strip; it is not used to mean a line of people waiting.
default.q.n3-2-q24-24.why.1: (b) 線: line, marked line, wire or route (e.g., 白い線); it is not used for a line of people waiting.
default.q.n3-2-q24-24.why.2: (c) 列 (line, row): a line or row of people.「人の（長い）列ができる」means that a long line of people waiting forms.
default.q.n3-2-q24-24.why.3: (d) 壁: a wall or barrier that separates things; it is not used to describe a line of people waiting.
default.q.n3-2-q25-25.explanation:
Sentence meaning: To write the report later, I recorded the experimental results in my notebook.
- Vocabulary: 記録 (record), 申請 (application), 予報 (forecast), 通知 (notification).
- Example: 毎日の体重をノートに記録している。(I record my weight in a notebook every day.)
default.q.n3-2-q25-25.why.0: (a) 申請 (しんせい): to submit an application or register for an administrative procedure (e.g., ビザの申請); it is not used for writing experimental results in a notebook.
default.q.n3-2-q25-25.why.1: (b) 記録 (record): Writing information or data down in a notebook or on a device. 「ノートに記録する」 means to record the results in a notebook.
default.q.n3-2-q25-25.why.2: (c) 予報 (forecast): a prediction of how something will develop in advance (e.g., 天気予報); it is not used for recording results that have already occurred.
default.q.n3-2-q25-25.why.3: (d) 通知 (つうち): a notification informing someone of news or a result (e.g., 合格通知); it is not used for the act of making one's own notes in a notebook.
default.q.n3-2-q26-26.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (大変だった).
default.q.n3-2-q26-26.explanation:
Meaning: "That job was truly very hard for me."
- 苦労 means hardship, difficulty, or struggle (＝大変).
- Example: 彼は若いころに苦労した。(He went through many hardships when he was young.)
default.q.n3-2-q26-26.why.0: (a) 危険だった (was dangerous) is not synonymous with 苦労した (had a difficult or arduous time).
default.q.n3-2-q26-26.why.1: (b) 大変だった (very difficult or demanding) is synonymous with 苦労した (went through a lot of difficulty).
default.q.n3-2-q26-26.why.2: (c) つまらない (“boring”) describes a tedious feeling and is not synonymous with being tiring or difficult.
default.q.n3-2-q26-26.why.3: (d) やりたくなかった (did not want to do it) describes a personal feeling or desire and is not equivalent to the meaning of hardship.
default.q.n3-2-q27-27.explanation:
Meaning: "Honda and Sato quietly/surreptitiously left the room."
- そっと: gently, quietly, without making a sound or attracting attention (＝静かに / 誰にも気づかれないように).
- Example: 赤ちゃんが寝ているので、そっとドアを閉めた。(The baby was sleeping, so I quietly closed the door.)
default.q.n3-2-q27-27.why.0: (a) 静かに (quietly, gently) is synonymous with the adverb そっと (gently, without making a sound).
default.q.n3-2-q27-27.why.1: (b) にぎやかに (lively, noisy) has a meaning completely opposite to そっと.
default.q.n3-2-q27-27.why.2: (c) 急いで (hurriedly, in a rush) describes the speed of movement, not moving quietly or gently.
default.q.n3-2-q27-27.why.3: (d) 二人で (the two of them together) indicates the number of people performing the action, not the manner in which it is performed.
default.q.n3-2-q28-28.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (早く帰った).
default.q.n3-2-q28-28.explanation:
Meaning: "I heard that Tanaka went home early yesterday."
- 早退: leaving before the end of work or school (＝予定より早く帰ること).
- Example: 熱があったので、会社を早退した。(I had a fever, so I left work early.)
default.q.n3-2-q28-28.why.0: (a) 早く起きた (woke up early) is unrelated to returning early from work or school.
default.q.n3-2-q28-28.why.1: (b) 早く来た (came early) expresses the opposite direction of action from 早退 (leave early).
default.q.n3-2-q28-28.why.2: (c) 早く寝た (went to bed early) only means going to bed early in the evening, so it does not have the correct meaning.
default.q.n3-2-q28-28.why.3: (d) 早く帰った (went home early) is synonymous with 早退した (left early before the scheduled time).
default.q.n3-2-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (過ぎました).
default.q.n3-2-q29-29.explanation:
Meaning: 'About a week has passed since I came here.'
- たつ (経つ): (of time) to pass (＝時間が過ぎる).
- Example: 日本に来てからもう3年が経ちました。(Three years have already passed since I came to Japan.)
default.q.n3-2-q29-29.why.0: (a) 待ちました (waited; the verb 待つ) does not mean that time has passed.
default.q.n3-2-q29-29.why.1: (b) 続けました (continued; from the verb 続ける) is not equivalent to 経つ when talking about the passage of time.
default.q.n3-2-q29-29.why.2: (c) 休みました means “rested” or “took a break” and is completely different in meaning; it comes from the verb 休む.
default.q.n3-2-q29-29.why.3: (d) 過ぎました (“has passed,” from the verb 過ぎる) is synonymous with (時間が)たつ/経つ (“time passes”).
default.q.n3-2-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (いろいろな).
default.q.n3-2-q30-30.explanation:
Sentence meaning: This restaurant offers a wide variety of dishes.
- さまざま (様々): diverse, various, many different kinds (＝いろいろ).
- Example: 世界にはさまざまな文化がある。(There are many different cultures in the world.)
default.q.n3-2-q30-30.why.0: (a) きれいな (beautiful, clean) describes outward beauty or cleanliness, not variety.
default.q.n3-2-q30-30.why.1: (b) 有名な (famous) describes reputation, not a rich variety of types.
default.q.n3-2-q30-30.why.2: (c) いろいろな (many kinds, diverse) is synonymous with さまざまな (varied, diverse).
default.q.n3-2-q30-30.why.3: (d) 特別な means “special, unusual, unique,” and is not synonymous with “many varieties.”
default.q.n3-2-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 3 because 「人口が減少する」 (the population decreases) is a completely correct and natural collocation.
default.q.n3-2-q31-31.explanation:
【減少（げんしょう）】: a decrease or decline in a measurable quantity, volume, or degree (commonly used for statistics such as 人口 - population, 収入 - income, 犯罪件数 - number of crimes).
- It is not used for one’s spirits or vitality (use 元気がなくなる), temperature (use 気温が下がる), or prices (use 値段が下がる/安くなる).
- Example: 若者の読書時間が年々減少している。(The amount of time young people spend reading is decreasing year by year.)
default.q.n3-2-q31-31.why.0: Incorrect because 「元気」 (energy, vitality) describes an emotional or physical state and is not used with 減少. Expressions such as 「元気がなくなる」 or 「元気が落ちている」 are used instead.
default.q.n3-2-q31-31.why.1: Incorrect because 「気温」(temperature) is used with 「下がる」or 「低下する」, not 減少.
default.q.n3-2-q31-31.why.2: Correct because 「人口が減少する」 (the population decreases) is the standard expression for indicating a reduction in the number of people according to statistical data.
default.q.n3-2-q31-31.why.3: Incorrect, because 「値段」 (price) normally goes with 「下がる」, 「安くなる」, or 「値下がりする」, not 減少.
default.q.n3-2-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 4 because 「重大な発表」 is the precise expression for an important announcement concerning a significant event with a major impact.
default.q.n3-2-q32-32.explanation:
【重大（じゅうだい）】(na-adjective): important, serious,重大; having a major impact on or determining the future or outcome. Common examples include 重大な発表 (an important announcement), 重大な問題 (a serious problem), and 重大な責任 (a heavy responsibility).
- Not used for facial expressions (use 真剣な顔 / 深刻な顔), personal keepsakes (use 大切な / 大事な), or life experiences (use 貴重な / 大切な).
- Example: この決定は今後の会社経営において重大な意味を持つ。(This decision has major significance for the future management of the company.)
default.q.n3-2-q32-32.why.0: Incorrect because a serious, attentive facial expression while listening to a lecture should be expressed as 「真剣な顔」 or 「まじめな顔」, not 「重大な顔」.
default.q.n3-2-q32-32.why.1: Incorrect because a precious, personally important keepsake from a family member is described with 「大切な」, 「大事な」, or 「貴重な」, not 「重大な」.
default.q.n3-2-q32-32.why.2: Incorrect because a valuable experience gained for oneself is expressed as「貴重な経験」or「大切な経験」, not「重大な経験」.
default.q.n3-2-q32-32.why.3: Correct because 「重大な発表」 (a major announcement) is a natural collocation describing an announcement of great importance from the director.
default.q.n3-2-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 2 because 「資料がばらばらになる」 accurately describes the documents falling apart and being scattered all over the floor.
default.q.n3-2-q33-33.explanation:
【ばらばら】(adverb / na-adjective): scattered, separate, disorganized, or dispersed, with people or things no longer forming a unified whole.
- Commonly used for objects scattered after falling (資料がばらばらになる), people living apart (家族がばらばらに暮らす), or inconsistent opinions (意見がばらばらだ).
- Not used for spilled liquids (use こぼれる), softened melted ice cream (use 溶ける/どろどろになる), or escaping air (use 逃げる).
- Example: 卒業後、クラスメートはばらばらになってしまった。(After graduation, the classmates all went their separate ways.)
default.q.n3-2-q33-33.why.0: Incorrect because ice cream becoming soft and runny from not being refrigerated is expressed with「溶けてしまった」or「どろどろになってしまった」, not ばらばら.
default.q.n3-2-q33-33.why.1: Correct because when the documents fell to the floor, the pages came loose and became scattered everywhere, so「資料がばらばらになってしまった」is completely accurate.
default.q.n3-2-q33-33.why.2: Incorrect because when warm air escapes from a room and causes it to become cold, 「逃げてしまった」 or 「冷めてしまった」 should be used, not ばらばら.
default.q.n3-2-q33-33.why.3: Incorrect because for liquid fruit juice that has spilled out, use 「こぼれてしまった」; liquids are not described with ばらばら.
default.q.n3-2-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 1 because 「じゃがいもの皮をむく」 is the standard expression for peeling a potato.
default.q.n3-2-q34-34.explanation:
【皮（かわ）】: skin, or the thin, soft outer covering of fruits and vegetables such as bananas, oranges, apples, and potatoes.
- Common expression: 「皮をむく」 (peel, remove the skin).
- Distinguish it from 殻 (から: a hard shell, such as an eggshell, crab shell, or seashell), 表紙 (ひょうし: a book or textbook cover), and カバー/表面 (a protective cover or the surface of a machine).
- Example: りんごの皮をナイフできれいにむいた。(I neatly peeled the apple with a knife.)
default.q.n3-2-q34-34.why.0: Correct because 「じゃがいもの皮」 means the skin of a potato, and 「皮をむく」 (peel the skin) is completely accurate usage.
default.q.n3-2-q34-34.why.1: Incorrect because the exterior or surface of a laptop is expressed with 「表面」, 「カバー」, or 「ボディ」, not 「皮」.
default.q.n3-2-q34-34.why.2: Incorrect because the hard outer shell of an egg is 「殻（から）」(卵の殻), not 「皮」.
default.q.n3-2-q34-34.why.3: Incorrect. For the outer cover of a book or textbook, use「表紙（ひょうし）」or「カバー」, not「皮」.
default.q.n3-2-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 3 because 「デザートをオーダーする」 is the correct expression for ordering dessert at a restaurant.
default.q.n3-2-q35-35.explanation:
【オーダー】(noun / suru-verb - from the English word "order"): ordering food or drinks at a restaurant or diner (注文する), or ordering something custom-made (オーダーメイド).
- Common expressions: オーダーを取る (take a customer's order), オーダーを通す (send the order to the kitchen), デザート/料理をオーダーする (order dessert/a dish).
- Not used for a doctor's medical instructions (use 指導/アドバイス), a request to clean the house (use 頼む/言いつける), or expectations in competition (use 求める/期待する).
- Example: 店員が私たちのテーブルへオーダーを取りに来た。(The server came to our table to take our order.)
default.q.n3-2-q35-35.why.0: Incorrect because advice or instructions from a doctor to exercise should be expressed with 「指導された」, 「アドバイスされた」, or 「勧められた」, not オーダー.
default.q.n3-2-q35-35.why.1: Incorrect. When a mother tells or asks her younger sister to clean the room, use「頼んだ」or「言いつけた」, not オーダー.
default.q.n3-2-q35-35.why.2: Correct because 「デザートをオーダーする」means ordering dessert after a meal at a restaurant, which is the appropriate context for ordering food.
default.q.n3-2-q35-35.why.3: Incorrect because expressing a wish or expectation that athletes win the tournament requires 「求めた」, 「期待した」, or 「頼んだ」, not オーダー.
default.q.n3-20-q36-36.verdict: The correct answer is 4. のほかに.

Meaning: At the library in Town A, they have magazines and CDs in addition to books.

default.q.n3-20-q36-36.why.0: (a) 「～によって」 means “depending on,” “by,” or “by means of”; it is not used to list an additional object as in this sentence.

default.q.n3-20-q36-36.why.3: (d) 「～のほかに」 means “besides ~”; combined with the particle 「も」 in the following clause, it expresses that besides books, there are also magazines and CDs.

default.q.n3-20-q37-37.explanation:
Meaning:
A: "Hello. I just arrived at the station. Where are you?"
B: "Well, do you know a bookstore called 'Kimura Pukku'?"
A: "Yes."
B: "I'm there."
- Pattern: `N1 + って + N2` is the casual conversational form of `N1 + という + N2` (N2 is called N1).
- Example: 田中さんって人から電話があったよ。(I got a call from someone named Tanaka.)
default.q.n3-20-q37-37.why.0: (a) 「～と」cannot be placed directly before a noun to identify it; grammatically correct forms are「～という」or「～といった」.
default.q.n3-20-q37-37.why.1: (b) 「～って」 is the informal spoken form of「～という」, used to name or identify something:「～って本屋」 (a bookstore called ~).
default.q.n3-20-q37-37.why.2: (c) 「～だって」 is commonly used to quote something heard (“they say that...”) or to mean “even” or “even if”; it is not used to identify the noun that follows.
default.q.n3-20-q37-37.why.3: (d) 「～なんか」 is commonly used to give an example with a dismissive or modest nuance (“things such as ...”); it is not used to name a store.
default.q.n3-20-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 大変か.
default.q.n3-20-q38-38.explanation:
Translation: It was not until I got my first part-time job that I realized how hard it is to earn money.
- On’yomi and vocabulary: 稼ぐ (かせぐ — GIÁ: to earn money).
- Grammar: `Question word (どれだけ / どんなに / 何...) + plain form + か + verb (わかる / 知る...)` forms an embedded question expressing degree.
- Example: 親のありがたさがどれだけ大きいか、一人暮らしをして初めて分かった。(It was only after living alone that I realized how much my parents mean to me.)
default.q.n3-20-q38-38.why.0: (a) The interrogative structure 「どれだけ + na-adjective + か + わかった」 expresses degree (“how difficult it was”).
default.q.n3-20-q38-38.why.1: (b) 「～だと」 is used when reporting an affirmative statement and cannot directly combine with the degree question word 「どれだけ」 before it.
default.q.n3-20-q38-38.why.2: (c) 「～かどうか」 means “whether or not” and is used for yes/no questions; it does not combine with the degree interrogative 「どれだけ」.
default.q.n3-20-q38-38.why.3: (d) 「～なのが」nominalizes a clause, but it does not form an embedded question expressing the degree of compatibility with「どれだけ」.
default.q.n3-20-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 3. せいで.
default.q.n3-20-q39-39.explanation:
Meaning: This morning, because my alarm clock did not ring, I overslept by a full hour.
- Vocabulary and kanji roots: 目覚まし時計 (めざましどけい: alarm clock), 鳴る (なる — to ring, sound), 寝坊する (ねぼうする — to oversleep, get up late).
- Grammar: `V/A/N-修飾型 + せいで`: “because of” or “due to,” used for a cause leading to a negative result.
- Example: 電車が遅れたせいで、面接に遅刻してしまった。(Because the train was late, I ended up being late for the interview.)
default.q.n3-20-q39-39.why.0: (a) 「～はずで」 generally expresses a well-founded supposition (“should be,” “is expected to be”); it is not used to indicate the direct cause of an unfavorable result that has already occurred.
default.q.n3-20-q39-39.why.1: (b) 「～一方で」expresses two contrasting or parallel aspects of something (“on the other hand / while...”), not a cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.n3-20-q39-39.why.2: (c) 「～せいで」 means “because of / due to ...” and indicates a cause that leads to a negative or undesirable result (oversleeping by one hour).
default.q.n3-20-q39-39.why.3: (d) 「～場合」 means “in the case of / when,” and is used for a hypothetical situation, not to indicate the cause of an event that occurred in the past.
default.q.n3-20-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 行くんだったら.
default.q.n3-20-q40-40.explanation:
Meaning:
Husband: "I'm going to the convenience store for a moment."
Wife: "Okay, go ahead. Oh, if you're going to the convenience store, could you bring back some milk?"
- Grammar: `V-る + んだったら / のなら`: "If you are going to..." or "If that's what you're doing..." Used to respond to information or an intention from the other speaker before making a request or suggestion.

default.q.n3-20-q40-40.why.0: (a) 「～ば」 is not used when the following clause expresses volition, a request, or a favor (買ってきて), when the verb in the preceding clause is a volitional action.
default.q.n3-20-q40-40.why.1: (b) 「～行っていたら」expresses a hypothetical situation in which someone was there or had already gone in the past, so it does not fit when the listener has only just prepared to go.
default.q.n3-20-q40-40.why.2: (c) 「～とすると」 is used for a theoretical assumption or inference (“assuming that…”); it does not accompany a request or exhortation.
default.q.n3-20-q40-40.why.3: (d) 「～んだったら」(the colloquial form of のなら) is used when taking information or an intention from the other person as the basis for making a request, suggestion, or judgment.
default.q.n3-20-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 習いはじめた.
default.q.n3-20-q41-41.explanation:
Meaning: My child only started learning piano yesterday, but because the piano lessons are far from home, I am worried about letting my child go alone.

default.q.n3-20-q41-41.why.1: (b) 「～つづけた」 means “continued doing V throughout,” so it does not fit the time marker 「昨日から」, which indicates a newly started action.
default.q.n3-20-q41-41.why.2: (c) 「～習わせたかった」 means “wanted to have (someone, such as one's child) study,” expressing a past desire rather than indicating that the activity actually began.
default.q.n3-20-q41-41.why.3: (d) 「～習わせてほしかった」 means “wanted someone to let [the child] take lessons,” which has the wrong subject and does not fit the context of the family deciding on its own to have the child study.
default.q.n3-20-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 2. ございます.
default.q.n3-20-q42-42.explanation:
Translation:
Customer: "Excuse me, where is the restroom?"

default.q.n3-20-q42-42.why.1: (b) 「ございます」 is the formal polite form (丁寧語) of 「あります」, used to indicate the location or existence of something such as 「お手洗い」.
default.q.n3-20-q42-42.why.2: (c) 「いたします」 is the humble form of 「します」 and is not used to indicate existence or location.
default.q.n3-20-q42-42.why.3: (d) 「いらっしゃいます」 is the honorific form of 「います / 行きます / 来ます」 and is used for another person’s action or state, not for an object.
default.q.n3-20-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 2. しないように.
default.q.n3-20-q43-43.explanation:
Translation: Because the doctor told me, “You still have a slight fever, so don’t overexert yourself,” I stayed home from school yesterday.

  - 無理をする (むりをする): to overwork oneself, to push oneself too hard.

default.q.n3-20-q43-43.why.1: (b) 「V-ない + ように(言う / 言われる)」 is used to report or quote advice, requests, or instructions: "be careful not to overexert yourself."
default.q.n3-20-q43-43.why.2: (c) 「～しなかったのに」 means “even though someone did not do it,” expressing contrast or regret; it does not fit an instruction or reminder.
default.q.n3-20-q43-43.why.3: (d) 「～していませんが」 means “although [someone] is not doing ~”; it is not a pattern for giving advice or commands.
default.q.n3-20-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ぐらいしか.
default.q.n3-20-q44-44.explanation:
Meaning: Because I did so much shopping, I have only about 500 yen left in my wallet.

default.q.n3-20-q44-44.why.1: (b) 「～でしか」usually accompanies a method, means, or exclusive location (“only by/at ...”); it does not directly follow an amount of money to indicate that only a small amount remains.
default.q.n3-20-q44-44.why.2: (c) 「～ぐらいは」usually indicates a minimum acceptable level and is used with an affirmative statement expressing a positive or acceptable meaning; it does not combine with the negative predicate 「残っていない」.
default.q.n3-20-q44-44.why.3: (d) 「～ぐらいしか」 combines 「ぐらい」 (approximately) with 「しか...ない」 (only, no more than), indicating that only a very small amount remains (about 500 yen).
default.q.n3-20-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 1. になるまで.

Translation: "Next, add oil to the pan and heat it until it reaches 170 degrees."

Meaning: My dream is to build a car that people all over the world will love.

default.q.n3-20-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 話し合ってみるつもりです.

default.q.n3-20-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 信じてしまいそうだ.

The painting he made looks exactly like a photograph. If someone showed it to me and told me it was a photograph, I would probably believe it completely.

default.q.n3-20-q48-48.why.3: (d) 「V-てしまいそうだ」 combines 「～てしまう」 (to accidentally do something) with 「～そうだ」 (seems/about to), indicating that the speaker is highly likely to mistake it for a real photograph.
