default.q.n3-23-q47-47.why.0: (a) 「よくないと」 means “if it is not good...,” so it does not form a meaningful phrase with 「駅の近くで」.
default.q.n3-23-q47-47.why.1: (b) 「なくてもいいと」uses the particle 「と」for quotation or a general hypothetical condition; it is not used to give a concessive suggestion with 「〜ば」.
default.q.n3-23-q47-47.why.2: (c) 「よくなければ」 means “if it is not good” or “if it is not okay,” and cannot be combined with 「駅の近くで」 to mean “it does not have to be near the station.”
default.q.n3-23-q47-47.why.3: (d) 「なくてもよければ」 is the conditional form of 「なくてもいい」 (“it is okay not to...,” “if it is okay not to...”); it correctly expresses a conditional suggestion.
default.q.n3-23-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 飲んでしまわないように, because combining the inadvertent-action form (〜てしまう) with the preventive-purpose form (〜ないように) means “so as not to accidentally drink it.”
default.q.n3-23-q48-48.explanation:
- Meaning: Because I have a three-year-old daughter, I keep the medicine somewhere out of the reach of young children so that she does not accidentally take it.
- Grammar:
  + V-てしまう: accidentally or regretfully do something unintended -> negative: V-てしまわない.
  + V-ないように: so that something does not happen, used for prevention.
- Kanji note: 娘 (daughter), 間違える / 間違って (to make a mistake / accidentally), 届く (to reach).
- Example: 忘れてしまわないように、メモを取っておきます。(I will take notes so that I do not forget.)
default.q.n3-23-q48-48.why.0: (a) 「飲み終わらない」means “not finish drinking,” which does not fit the context of preventing children from accidentally drinking medicine.
default.q.n3-23-q48-48.why.1: (b) 「飲み終わらないようで」 is incorrect both lexically (it means “does not finish drinking”) and grammatically, because 「〜ようで」 expresses an inference or appearance, not a purpose of prevention.
default.q.n3-23-q48-48.why.2: (c) 「飲んでしまわないように」combines「〜てしまう」(accidentally do something) and「〜ないように」(so as not to...), expressing the purpose “so that the child does not accidentally drink the medicine.”
default.q.n3-23-q48-48.why.3: (d) 「飲んでしまわないようで」 is incorrect because the ending 「〜ようで」 indicates appearance or conjecture; it does not express the purpose of preventing an action.
default.q.n3-23-q49-49.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (応援して). The correct order is 1 → 4 → 2 → 3, so the position marked ★, the third gap, is choice 2.
default.q.n3-23-q49-49.explanation:
娘が歌手になることには反対でしたが、娘も一生けんめいがんばろうとしているので、応援してやろうかと思っています。
(Meaning: I used to oppose my daughter becoming a singer, but since she is also trying her best, I am thinking that perhaps I should support her.)
default.q.n3-23-q49-49.why.0: (a) がんばろうとして: It comes first after the adverb 一生けんめい and combines with いるので in fragment 4 to form the pattern ~ようとしている (be trying/working hard to do something).
default.q.n3-23-q49-49.why.1: (b) 応援して: It occupies the third position (★) and is the V-て form placed before やろうか in fragment 3, forming the structure ～てやる (doing something for someone of lower status or for a child).
default.q.n3-23-q49-49.why.2: (c) やろうか: In the fourth position, it combines with と思っています at the end of the sentence to form the grammar pattern ~ようかと思っている (be considering or planning to do something).
default.q.n3-23-q49-49.why.3: (d) いるので: Goes in position 2, following がんばろうとして to form the cause clause がんばろうとしているので (because my child is also trying their best).
default.q.n3-23-q50-50.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (けれども). The correct order is 4 → 3 → 1 → 2, so the position marked ★, the third gap, is choice 1.
default.q.n3-23-q50-50.explanation:
ここにある家具は今はどれも使っていないけれどもいつかまた使うかもしれないと思うと、捨てられない。
(Meaning: I don't use any of the furniture here right now, but when I think I might use it again someday, I can't bring myself to throw it away.)
default.q.n3-23-q50-50.why.0: (a) けれども: In the third position (★), it functions as a conjunction expressing contrast ("although...but...") and connects the two clauses: "not used at present" and "may be used again later."
default.q.n3-23-q50-50.why.1: (b) いつかまた: It occupies the fourth position and is an adverbial phrase meaning “someday again...” that directly modifies the verb 使う immediately after the blank.
default.q.n3-23-q50-50.why.2: (c) 使っていない comes second after 今はどれも, forming the complete clause 今はどれも使っていない (I am not using any of them now).
default.q.n3-23-q50-50.why.3: (d) 今はどれも: placed immediately after the subject 「ここにある家具は」, it functions as an adverb modifying 使っていない.
default.q.n3-23-q51-51.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (忘れていた). The correct order is 1 → 3 → 2 → 4, so the ★ position (the third slot) corresponds to choice 2.
default.q.n3-23-q51-51.explanation:
書いたまま出すのを忘れていた友人への手紙が引き出しにあった。
(Meaning: A letter to a friend that I had written but forgotten to send was in the drawer.)
default.q.n3-23-q51-51.why.0: (a) まま: It comes immediately after the past-form verb 書いた in first position, forming V-た + まま (“leaving it as it was after writing it, without doing anything further”).
default.q.n3-23-q51-51.why.1: (b) 忘れていた appears in third position, marked with ★. It functions as the predicate following 出すのを, forming “had forgotten to send,” and also modifies the noun 手紙.
default.q.n3-23-q51-51.why.2: (c) 出すのを: It appears in second position; の nominalizes the verb 出す so that it can function as the object of 忘れていた in fragment 2.
default.q.n3-23-q51-51.why.3: (d) 友人への: In the fourth position, the noun + への phrase directly modifies the following noun 手紙, meaning “a letter to a friend.”
default.q.n3-23-q52-52.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (おかしく). The correct order is 2 → 4 → 3 → 1, so the position marked ★, the third gap, is choice 3.
default.q.n3-23-q52-52.explanation:
A「空が暗いですね。」
B「そうですね。雨がいつ降ってもおかしくないですね。」
(Meaning:
A: "The sky has gotten really dark, hasn't it?"
B: "Yes, it has. It could start raining at any moment.")
default.q.n3-23-q52-52.why.0: (a) ない: It goes in the fourth and final position, combining with おかしく to form the negative expression おかしくない (not strange or unusual).
default.q.n3-23-q52-52.why.1: (b) いつ: It comes first after the particle 雨が and combines with the ても-form of a verb to create the hypothetical clause いつ〜ても (“whenever ...”).
default.q.n3-23-q52-52.why.2: (c) おかしく: appears in position 3 (★) as the linking form of the i-adjective おかしい before the auxiliary negative ない.
default.q.n3-23-q52-52.why.3: (d) 降っても: It is in the second position and is the V-ても form of 降る. Together with いつ and おかしくない, it forms the pattern いつ〜てもおかしくない (“it could happen at any time”).
default.q.n3-23-q53-53.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (時間がないから). The correct order is 3 → 1 → 4 → 2, and the ★ position (the third slot) is answer choice 4.
default.q.n3-23-q53-53.explanation:
A「もしもし、ちょっと話したいことがあるんだけど、今、時間ある?」
B「ごめん。ちょうど出かけるところでゆっくり話す時間がないから、あとで私から電話するね。」
(Meaning:
A: “Hello, there’s something I’d like to talk about. Do you have time now?”
B: “Sorry. I’m just about to go out, so I don’t have time to talk properly. I’ll call you later.”)
default.q.n3-23-q53-53.why.0: (a) ゆっくり話す: In the second position, it modifies the noun 時間 in fragment 4, forming ゆっくり話す時間 (time to talk leisurely).
default.q.n3-23-q53-53.why.1: (b) あとで: It is in the fourth position and is a time adverb meaning “later,” modifying the action 私から電話するね.
default.q.n3-23-q53-53.why.2: (c) ところで: It occupies the first position and follows the dictionary form verb 出かける, forming the structure V-る + ところで (just as someone is about to go out).
default.q.n3-23-q53-53.why.3: (d) 時間がないから: It occupies the third position (the ★ position), following ゆっくり話す to form the reason clause ゆっくり話す時間がないから (because there is no time to talk leisurely).
default.q.n3-23-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 1. チョコレートでした.
default.q.n3-23-q54-54.explanation: In the previous sentence, the author recounts buying something during their first shopping trip in Japan in April: 「桜の絵の箱に入ったお菓子を買いまし た。」(I bought sweets in a box decorated with a cherry-blossom picture.) This sentence specifically identifies what those sweets were, and the following sentence in paragraph 2 refers to 「そのチョコレート」(that chocolate bar). Therefore, the past-tense statement 「桜味のチョコレートでした。」(They were cherry-blossom-flavored chocolates.) is the most accurate and natural choice.
default.q.n3-23-q54-54.why.0: (a) Reasonable. The preceding sentence says that a confectionery item was bought in the cherry-blossom box, and this sentence uses the past tense to clarify that the item was chocolate, which is referred to later as 「そのチョコレート」.
default.q.n3-23-q54-54.why.1: (b) Unnatural. 「～てみます」 expresses trying something in the present or future, so it does not fit when recounting something that was purchased in the past.
default.q.n3-23-q54-54.why.2: (c) Not appropriate. 「～のことでした」 is generally used to explain the content of an event or clarify a definition, not to directly identify the type of item or confectionery that was purchased.
default.q.n3-23-q54-54.why.3: (d) This is illogical. 「～つもりです」expresses a future intention, so it does not fit a context in which the item was already bought in the past.
default.q.n3-23-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ところが.
default.q.n3-23-q55-55.explanation: The previous sentence indicates that the author suddenly craved that type of chocolate again and searched for it in the store (「店の中を探しました」). However, no matter how much the author searched, it could not be found (「いくら探しても、見つけられませんでした」). The most suitable conjunction for linking an action with an unexpected or contrary result is 「ところが」 (however).
default.q.n3-23-q55-55.why.0: (a) Not appropriate. 「それで」 (“therefore, so”) connects a straightforward cause-and-effect relationship; it cannot connect an opposite result to an effort to find something.
default.q.n3-23-q55-55.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「そのうえ」(moreover, in addition) adds information in the same direction; it is not used for a contrasting line of thought.
default.q.n3-23-q55-55.why.2: (c) Not appropriate. 「ちなみに」 (“by the way,” “incidentally”) is used to shift to related supplementary information, not as a conjunction linking a sequence of contrasting action and result.
default.q.n3-23-q55-55.why.3: (d) Reasonable. 「ところが」(however / but) connects a following clause that goes against expectations or produces an unexpected or contrasting result after the search described in the preceding clause.
default.q.n3-23-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 3. そういう.
default.q.n3-23-q56-56.explanation: In the preceding sentences, the shopkeeper explained that cherry-blossom-flavored chocolate is sold only in spring, while watermelon- and soda-flavored varieties are available in summer, and that some sweets are sold only in autumn or winter. The author is surprised to learn that Japan has “sweets like that” (sweets that change with each season, as just described). The most suitable demonstrative expression is 「そういうお菓子」(sweets like that).
default.q.n3-23-q56-56.why.0: (a) Not appropriate. 「あるお菓子」 (“some kind of candy or snack”) refers vaguely to an unspecified object and does not connect referentially with the seasonal sweets mentioned above.
default.q.n3-23-q56-56.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「この」 (“this”) refers to a specific thing or matter near the speaker; it is not used to generalize a set of characteristics such as “that kind of candy.”
default.q.n3-23-q56-56.why.2: (c) Reasonable. 「そういう」 is a ソ-series demonstrative that replaces and generalizes the features described by the shopkeeper in the previous sentence: sweets sold only in spring, summer, autumn, and winter.
default.q.n3-23-q56-56.why.3: (d) Not appropriate. 「どちらにも」 (“on both sides”) does not grammatically modify the noun「お菓子」in this context.
default.q.n3-23-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 教えてくれました.
default.q.n3-23-q57-57.explanation: The subject is 「店の人は」 (the shop employee), and the person receiving the action is the speaker. When another person performs an action to help the speaker or provide information for them, the benefactive structure 「～てくれました」 is used: 「教えてくれました」 (told me/informed me).
default.q.n3-23-q57-57.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「教えられました」 is the passive form. With the passive, the subject should be the person receiving the information (I), whereas the subject of the sentence is 「店の人は」.
default.q.n3-23-q57-57.why.1: (b) Illogical. 「教えてもらいました」 means “I was taught by someone” (with 私は as the subject), so it cannot be used with 「店の人は」 as the subject.
default.q.n3-23-q57-57.why.2: (c) Not appropriate. 「教えさせられました」 is the causative-passive form (was forced to teach), which is incorrect in both meaning and subject structure.
default.q.n3-23-q57-57.why.3: (d) Reasonable. 「～てくれました」expresses that another person, whose subject is 「店の人は」, did something beneficial for the speaker or provided information to the author.
default.q.n3-23-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 思っています.
default.q.n3-23-q58-58.explanation: The author wants to preserve forever the fresh feelings they had when they first came to Japan, and therefore concludes: 「これからもずっと、桜の絵の箱を大切にしようと思っています。」(I intend to continue cherishing the box with the cherry-blossom picture on it.) The pattern 「V-ようと思っています」expresses an intention or plan that the speaker has continued to hold.
default.q.n3-23-q58-58.why.0: (a) Inappropriate. 「～ましょう」 (let’s ...) expresses an invitation or proposal to someone else; it is not used to express one’s own personal intention or determination.
default.q.n3-23-q58-58.why.1: (b) Reasonable. The structure 「volitional form (よう) + と思っています」 expresses an intention or determination that the speaker formed earlier and still maintains in the present and future.
default.q.n3-23-q58-58.why.2: (c) Not appropriate. 「～のではありませんか」 (“isn’t it that...?”) expresses speculation or challenges the listener, so it does not fit when the author is expressing their own feelings and determination.
default.q.n3-23-q58-58.why.3: (d) Not appropriate. 「～てもしかたありません」 (“even if you think that, it is useless; there is nothing you can do”) has a negative nuance and completely conflicts with the author’s wish to preserve beautiful memories.
default.q.n3-23-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 2: なるべく早く、自分と趣味が合う友達を見つけたいから (Because they want to find a friend who shares their interests as soon as possible).
default.q.n3-23-q59-59.explanation:
- Main point: The author really likes Japanese anime. When introducing themselves, the author always talks about a favorite anime in order to quickly find someone with similar interests and make friends. This is how the author met their close friend Tom and quickly became close to him.
- Question translation: When introducing themselves, why does the author talk about their favorite anime?
- Answer choices:
  1. Because many people talk about Japanese anime when introducing themselves.
  2. Because they want to find someone with similar interests as quickly as possible.
  3. Because they want to quickly find someone with similar interests to speak Japanese with.
  4. Because their Japanese is still poor, so they can only talk about their favorite anime.
default.q.n3-23-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage does not mention many people talking about Japanese anime when introducing themselves.
default.q.n3-23-q59-59.why.1: (b) Correct because the passage clearly states the reason: 「それは、自分と趣味が合う人を早く見つけて、その人と友達になるためだ。」 (It is in order to quickly find someone who shares one's interests and become friends with that person.)
default.q.n3-23-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the author's purpose is to become friends with that person (その人と友達になるため), not to “speak Japanese” (日本語で話したいから).
default.q.n3-23-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage says that although both people’s Japanese was still poor, they continued talking and quickly became close. It does not say that their poor Japanese meant they could talk only about anime.
default.q.n3-23-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Chou wants to join Emily in making a tea bowl and then go to a café.
default.q.n3-23-q60-60.explanation:

The letter from Chou invites Emily to attend the “International Cultural Festival” next Sunday. Chou clearly says that they would like to try making a tea bowl (starting at 1:00) and then visit a good café nearby with Emily. Question and answer choices:
- Question: According to this letter, what does Chou want to do with Emily next Sunday?
- Choice 1: Take part in making a tea bowl, then go to a café.
- Choice 2: Take part in making a tea bowl, then go to an exhibition.
- Choice 3: Take part in making a tea bowl, go to a café, and then visit an exhibition.
- Choice 4: Take part in making a tea bowl, visit an exhibition, and then go to a café.
default.q.n3-23-q60-60.why.0: (a) Correct. In Chou’s letter, it says: 「私は茶わんを作ってみたいのですが、エミリさんもどうですか。そのあとは、近くにあるケーキがおいしい喫茶店へ行きませんか。」 (I would like to try making a tea bowl. How about you, Emily? default.q.n3-23-q60-60.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Going to the exhibition is conditional on Emily wanting to go (「もし、エミリさんが見たければ、展覧会を見てもいいですよ。」); it is not Chou’s own proactive wish or plan after making the teacup.
default.q.n3-23-q60-60.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Chou did not plan to see the exhibition after going to the café; seeing the exhibition entirely depended on whether Emily wanted to go.
default.q.n3-23-q60-60.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Chou does not intend to visit the exhibition before going to the café; Chou’s desired order is to make the tea bowl and then go to the café.
default.q.n3-23-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 「Meishi-10」を使っているかどうか (whether 「Meishi-10」 is being used).
default.q.n3-23-q61-61.explanation:
**Main point of the passage:**
This is an introductory letter from J Print to Yokodera Kougyou about the launch of a new business card printer, 「Meishi-20」. If the company would like someone to visit and explain the new product in person, it must inform J Print of its preferred date and whether it is currently using 「Meishi-10」. In addition, it only needs to provide further information if it has a preferred time or would like an explanation of other products in the enclosed catalog.

**Question and answer choice translations:**
- **Question:** If an explanation is desired, what must be reported in addition to the preferred date?
- **Choice 1:** Whether 「Meishi-10」 is currently being used.
- **Choice 2:** Whether 「Meishi-10」 is currently being used and the preferred time.
- **Choice 3:** Whether an explanation of other products is desired.
- **Choice 4:** Whether an explanation of other products is desired and the preferred time.
default.q.n3-23-q61-61.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage states directly: 「説明を希望される場合は、ご希望の日、現在「Meishi-10」をお使いになっているかどうかをお知らせください。」 (If you would like an explanation, please let us know your preferred date and whether you are currently using 「Meishi-10」.) Thus, in addition to the preferred date, the required information is whether the person is currently using 「Meishi-10」.
default.q.n3-23-q61-61.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The desired time does not have to be reported; it is optional if the person has a preference: 「また、時間のご希望があれば、ご一緒にお知らせください。」 (Also, if you have a preferred time, please let us know that as well).
default.q.n3-23-q61-61.why.2: (c) Incorrect. An explanation of the other products is not mandatory: 「そちらについても説明のご希望があれば、お知らせください。」 (If you would also like an explanation of those products, please let us know).
default.q.n3-23-q61-61.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Both the desired time and requests for explanations about other products are merely optional conditions if available (「～があれば」), not information that must必ず be sent.
default.q.n3-23-q62-62.verdict: The accurate answer is choice 2: Among women, more people brush their teeth “both before and after meals” than brush them “before meals.”
default.q.n3-23-q62-62.explanation:
• Main point: A survey of 3,000 people about when they brush their teeth in the morning shows that among both men and women and across all age groups, “after breakfast” is consistently the most common choice (64% of men and 72% of women). The next most common choice among men is “before breakfast,” while among women it is “both before and after breakfast.” Although the percentage choosing “after breakfast” decreases and the percentage choosing “before breakfast” increases with age, “after breakfast” remains the highest in every age group.

• Question: What can be understood from this passage about brushing one’s teeth in the morning?

• Answer choices:
1. Among men, more people brush their teeth “before breakfast” than “after breakfast.”
2. Among women, more people brush their teeth “both before and after breakfast” than “before breakfast.”
3. Regardless of gender, more than 60% of people brush their teeth “before breakfast.”
4. As people get older, more people brush their teeth “before breakfast” than “after breakfast.”
default.q.n3-23-q62-62.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The article clearly states that for both men and women, brushing one’s teeth “after meals” is the most common response (64% among men), followed by “before meals” (次は、男性が「食前」で). Therefore, among men, more people brush their teeth after meals than before meals.
default.q.n3-23-q62-62.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage says: 「性別でみると、男性も女性も「食後」に磨く人が最も多く(男性 64%、女性 72%)、次は、男性が「食前」で、女性が「食前と食後」だった。」 For women, “after meals” ranks first, and “before and after meals” ranks second, meaning “before meals” ranks third. Therefore, more women brush their teeth “before and after meals” than “before meals.”
default.q.n3-23-q62-62.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The percentages above 60% (64% for men and 72% for women) refer to people who brush their teeth “after meals” (「食後」), not “before meals” (「食前」).
default.q.n3-23-q62-62.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage states: 「年齢でみても、各年齢で一番多いのはやはり「食後」だった。」 (Even when viewed by age, “after meals” was still the most common choice in every age group). Although the proportion choosing “after meals” decreases and “before meals” increases with age, “after meals” remains the most common in every age group and is never overtaken by “before meals.”
default.q.n3-23-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The speaker is good at drawing, but not very good at subjects other than art.
default.q.n3-23-q63-63.explanation:
- Main idea: The passage says that the narrator, Ai, had liked drawing since childhood and was good at it. They did well in art, but struggled in other subjects such as Japanese language and mathematics, and their teacher told them to work harder.
- Translation of the question: What kind of child was the narrator when they were in middle school?
- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. A child who liked drawing and did reasonably well in every subject.
  2. A child who was good at drawing but did not do very well in subjects other than art.
  3. A child who did nothing but draw, yet did not do well in art.
  4. A child who was good at drawing, worked hard in every subject, and was praised by the teacher.
default.q.n3-23-q63-63.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage clearly states that the character was not very good at subjects such as Japanese and mathematics (「国語や数学などの勉強はあまりよくできませんでした」), not that their performance in every subject was acceptable.
default.q.n3-23-q63-63.why.1: (b) Correct because it quotes the teacher’s comment: 「愛さんは美術の成績はいいんですが、ほかの勉強ももっと頑張らないといけませんね。」 (Ai has good art grades, but needs to work harder at her other subjects as well.)
default.q.n3-23-q63-63.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage states that the character had good grades in art (「美術の成績はいい」), not that their art performance was not very good.
default.q.n3-23-q63-63.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The character is praised only for their talent in drawing, while the teacher says they need to work harder in other subjects. It is not true that the teacher praises them in every subject.
default.q.n3-23-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 1. The mother thinks her daughter does not need to get high grades in subjects she is poor at and wants to give her opportunities to develop her strengths.
default.q.n3-23-q64-64.explanation:
- Main point: When the teacher mentioned Ai's grades in her other subjects, her mother expressed the view that it was all right if her daughter did not get high scores on tests, because she wanted to support and develop her daughter's talent for drawing.
- Question translation: What does "① the mother's opinion" mean?
- Answer choices:
  1. It is all right if her daughter does not perform well in subjects she is weak in; she wants her daughter to do what she is good at.
  2. She wants her daughter to do what she is good at, but also wants her to get high scores on tests.
  3. She hopes her daughter will ask the teacher whenever she does not understand something in class.
  4. She wants her daughter to work harder in both the subjects she is weak in and the subjects she excels at.
default.q.n3-23-q64-64.why.0: (a) Correct because it quotes the mother's words to the teacher: 「愛は頑張って勉強しているんですが、テストで点が取れません。でも、私はそれでいいと思っているんです。愛は絵が好きだし上手なので、それを伸ばしてやりたいんです。」 (Ai works hard at studying but cannot get good test scores. Even so, I think that is all right. Ai likes drawing and is good at it, so I want to help develop that talent.)
default.q.n3-23-q64-64.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the mother accepts that her child does not get a high score on tests (「テストで点が取れません。でも、私はそれでいいと思っているんです」); she does not demand high scores.
default.q.n3-23-q64-64.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the advice “if you do not understand the lesson, ask the teacher” is spoken by the teacher (「じゃ、愛さん、授業でわからないことがあったら、いつでも先生に質問してね」), not the mother.
default.q.n3-23-q64-64.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the mother did not ask the child to work hard to become good at all weak subjects; she mainly wanted to help the child develop a talent for drawing.
default.q.n3-23-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 3. Because the mother did not worry about grades and supported the development of the narrator’s artistic ability, “I” was able to pursue and make a living from the work of drawing that I loved.
default.q.n3-23-q65-65.explanation:
- Main idea: The narrator wants to thank their mother because she did not pressure them about studying or grades and always allowed them to draw freely. As a result, the narrator graduated from art school and now works in the artistic field they love.
- Translation of the question: The narrator says, "② I want to thank my mother from that time." Why does the narrator think this now?
- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. Because their mother told the teacher that they drew very well, allowing them to become someone who could live with confidence.
  2. Because their mother taught them that poor academic performance was not a bad thing, giving them an open-minded outlook.
  3. Because their mother did not focus on their grades and instead wanted to develop their drawing ability, allowing them to pursue the path they loved.
  4. Because their mother taught them the importance of asking questions, allowing them to become someone who could take positive action.
default.q.n3-23-q65-65.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage does not say that the author became a confident person thanks to their mother; its focus is that the mother helped the author pursue a passion for painting.
default.q.n3-23-q65-65.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage does not mention the mother teaching that poor academic performance is not bad or helping "me" develop a broad-minded outlook.
default.q.n3-23-q65-65.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: 「それでも、母は決して私に「勉強は?」とは言わずに、自由に絵を描かせてくれました。その後、私は美術の専門学校を卒業し、今は、好きな絵を描くことを仕事にしています。」 (Even so, my mother never asked me, “What about your studies?” She let me draw freely. Later, I graduated from an art vocational school, and now I make a living drawing the pictures I love).
default.q.n3-23-q65-65.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the advice to ask about the lesson comes from the teacher, and the passage never says that “I” became more proactive because my mother taught me a lesson about asking questions.
default.q.n3-23-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (宣伝のしかた).
default.q.n3-23-q66-66.explanation:
**Summary:** The passage gives the example of a nutritional drink that was originally sold only to tired office workers. The company then changed its advertising strategy by having a beautiful female singer promote it, which led more young women to buy it and increased sales.

**Question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** What did the company change to make nutritional drink ① sell well?
- 1. The advertising method
- 2. The shape of the container
- 3. The product name
- 4. The product’s effects
default.q.n3-23-q66-66.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage provides this evidence: 「このドリンクを、美しい女性の歌手を使って宣伝したら、若い女性もよく買うようになったそうだ。」 (Apparently, when this drink was advertised using a beautiful female singer, young women also began buying it frequently). This shows that the company changed its advertising approach.
default.q.n3-23-q66-66.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Changing the shape of the packaging/container (容器の色や形を変えたりする) is a general example given in the following sentence, not something the company does to nutritional drink ①.
default.q.n3-23-q66-66.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Changing the product name (商品の名前...を変えたりする) is also a general example in the following sentence; it is not something the company did with nutritional drink ①.
default.q.n3-23-q66-66.why.3: (d) Wrong. The passage does not mention any change in the product’s effectiveness or function (商品の効果).
default.q.n3-23-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (Because giving the same product a different image from before made it sell well).
default.q.n3-23-q67-67.explanation:
**Relevant content summary:**
The author states that the power of an image is very great (イメージの力は大きい) because even a product launched many years ago can become popular again simply by changing its advertising, name, or packaging color/shape to give it a fresh image different from before.

**Translation of the question and choices:**
- **Question:** Why can we say that there is "power in an image" ②?
- 1. Because simply changing the image can make buyers feel that the product is more effective.
- 2. Because a good image associated with a product never needs to be changed, no matter how many years pass.
- 3. Because launching a completely new product different from the old product's image made it sell very well.
- 4. Because giving the same product a different image made it sell well again.
default.q.n3-23-q67-67.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage does not mention that changing the image made customers feel that the product's effectiveness had increased (その製品の効果も上がったと感じさせる).
default.q.n3-23-q67-67.why.1: (b) Incorrect. This contradicts the reading. The author states that refreshing a product's image after many years can help it sell well again, not that a good image never needs to be changed.
default.q.n3-23-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage discusses products that already existed / had been released many years earlier (以前からあった商品 / 発売から何年もたった製品), not the launch of a completely new product (全く新しい製品).
default.q.n3-23-q67-67.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage states: 「商品の名前や容器の色や形を変えたりするだけで、発売から何年もたった製品が、また売れ出すようになることもある。②イメージの力は大きい。」 Together with the preceding example of changing the advertising image, this shows that the same product can begin selling well again when it is given a new image.
default.q.n3-23-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (having started buying a certain chocolate for purposes other than eating it).
default.q.n3-23-q68-68.explanation:
**Related content summary:**
In one town, an ordinary type of chocolate suddenly sold out during exam season because high school students spread a rumor that carrying a bar of this chocolate would help them pass their exams. As a result, students bought the chocolate to put in their schoolbags as a good-luck charm before the exams—in other words, they bought it for a purpose other than its usual purpose of eating.

**Question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** The "way of buying" ③ changed. How did it change?
- 1. They bought the type of chocolate they liked without being influenced by the rumor.
- 2. They bought inexpensive chocolate instead of expensive chocolate.
- 3. They bought a certain type of chocolate for purposes other than eating it.
- 4. They bought chocolate at any time with the aim of passing their exams.
default.q.n3-23-q68-68.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The students were strongly influenced by the rumor (うわさが広がり、みんな試験前に買ってかばんに入れていた - the rumor spread, and everyone bought one and put it in their bag before the exam).
default.q.n3-23-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage only introduces this type of chocolate as an inexpensive kind sold throughout Japan; it does not mention a shift from buying expensive chocolate to buying cheap chocolate.
default.q.n3-23-q68-68.why.2: (c) Correct. Evidence from the passage: 「高校生の間に「このチョコレートを持っていると、試験に合格する」といううわさが広がり、みんな試験前に買ってかばんに入れていた。」 A rumor spread among high school students that “if you carried this chocolate, you would pass the exam,” so everyone bought it before the exam and put it in their schoolbags. The students bought the chocolate for good luck in the exam, not merely to eat it.
default.q.n3-23-q68-68.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage says that chocolate sells out only at a certain time before exams (ある時期にだけ / みんな試験前に買って), not regardless of the time of year (時期を選ばず).
default.q.n3-23-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The restaurant is expensive but very popular and crowded, and both the food and the quality of service are excellent.
default.q.n3-23-q69-69.explanation:
- Main idea: The narrator and a group of university friends celebrate the 20th anniversary of their graduation at a famous French restaurant that is difficult to book because it is highly popular. Every dish, from the soup to the dessert, is delicious, the service is first-class, and the price is correspondingly expensive ("the price is also first-class").
- Question translation: According to the passage, what kind of restaurant is ①?
- Answer choices:
  1. It is always crowded, but not expensive; the food and service are only so-so.
  2. It is expensive, but very popular, and both the food and service are excellent.
  3. The food is delicious and popular, but it is expensive and the service is not very good.
  4. It is difficult to make a reservation, but the food is delicious, the price is low, and the service is also good.
default.q.n3-23-q69-69.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage says that the prices are top-class (expensive) and that both the food and service are top-class, not that the prices are inexpensive or merely “so-so” (まあまあ).
default.q.n3-23-q69-69.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states: "この店は予約が取れないことで有名で、夜のコースはスープからデザートまでどれも本当においしく、サービスも一流だった。だれかが「値段も一流だよね。」と笑わせた。" (The restaurant was famous for being impossible to book; everything in the dinner course, from soup to dessert, was truly delicious, and the service was first-rate. Someone joked, “The prices are first-rate too, right?” [=The restaurant was popular, the food and service were excellent, and the prices were high].)
default.q.n3-23-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage states that 「サービスも一流だった」(the service was first-rate), which contradicts the statement that “the service was not very good.”
default.q.n3-23-q69-69.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the joke「値段も一流だよね」shows that the restaurant is very expensive, which contradicts “the price is cheap (値段も安く).”
default.q.n3-23-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Everyone was surprised because while others were naming luxurious delicacies, Yamashita mentioned an ordinary porridge dish that no one could have expected.
default.q.n3-23-q70-70.explanation:
- Main idea: In a conversation about the best food they had ever eaten, everyone takes turns naming luxurious dishes from famous restaurants and hotels, such as sushi at Hotel T and steak at Restaurant K. Yamashita, however, says that the best food was plain rice porridge, leaving everyone extremely surprised because this simple dish was completely unexpected.
- Translation of the question: The phrase "② was startled/surprised" appears in the passage. Why?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. Because Yamashita named a strange or rare dish that nobody had ever heard of.
  2. Because Yamashita talked about porridge eaten at a restaurant that day.
  3. Because Yamashita named a dish that nobody had expected at all.
  4. Because Yamashita said that they had eaten porridge while suffering from a 40-degree fever.
default.q.n3-23-q70-70.why.0: (a) Incorrect because rice porridge (おかゆ) is a familiar, traditional everyday dish, not a rare dish that people have never heard of.
default.q.n3-23-q70-70.why.1: (b) Incorrect because everyone went to a French restaurant that day rather than eating porridge; eating porridge was a memory from Yamashita's student days.
default.q.n3-23-q70-70.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: "「Tホテルのすし」「レストランKで食べたステーキ」など、有名なお店の料理が次々と出てくる中、山下君が「僕が今まで一番おいしいと思ったのは、おかゆだなあ。」と言ったので、みんな②びっくりしてしまった。" (Everyone was surprised because, while expensive dishes from famous restaurants were being mentioned one after another, Yamashita unexpectedly named the humble dish rice porridge as the most delicious food he had ever eaten.)
default.q.n3-23-q70-70.why.3: (d) Incorrect because everyone was already startled when Yamashita merely mentioned the name of the porridge dish; the detail about having a fever of 40 degrees was explained afterward.
default.q.n3-23-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The person who cooked the porridge was Yoshiko, Yamashita’s former college classmate and current wife.
default.q.n3-23-q71-71.explanation:
- Main idea: When Yamashita was living alone as a student and had a fever of 40°C, a classmate came to visit him and cooked rice porridge for him. At the end of the passage, it is revealed that this former classmate was Yoshiko, who is now Yamashita's wife sitting beside him.
- Question translation: Who cooked the rice porridge in ③?
- Answer choices:
  1. Yoshiko's friend.
  2. Mr. Yamashita, "my" friend.
  3. Yoshiko, "my" wife.
  4. Yoshiko, Mr. Yamashita's wife.
default.q.n3-23-q71-71.why.0: (a) This is incorrect because Yoshiko herself was the friend who cooked the rice porridge, not Yoshiko’s friend.
default.q.n3-23-q71-71.why.1: (b) Incorrect because Yamashita is the person who was ill and was given porridge cooked by a friend.
default.q.n3-23-q71-71.why.2: (c) Incorrect because Yoshiko is Yamashita’s wife (“the wife sitting beside him”), not the speaker’s wife.
default.q.n3-23-q71-71.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage states: "同じクラスの友達がようすを見に来てくれ、おかゆを作ってくれた... 私が、彼の隣に座っている奥さんに「その友達というのは、良子さん、君だったんじゃないの?」と聞くと、奥さんは「実は、そうなんです。」と言って笑った。" (The classmate who made porridge for him at that time was Yoshiko, Yamashita’s present wife.)
default.q.n3-23-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 1: What Yamashita could never forget was the delicious flavor that came from the bottom of the bowl of rice porridge his friend had made for him when he had a fever.
default.q.n3-23-q72-72.explanation:
- Main point: The passage focuses on the “best-tasting food I have ever eaten.” Yamashita recalls a simple bowl of rice porridge, without egg or vegetables, that a friend made when he had a high fever. The warm, deeply comforting taste of that porridge is something he still cannot forget more than 20 years later.
- Translation of the question: The phrase “④ cannot forget” appears. What is it that cannot be forgotten?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. The taste of the porridge prepared for him when he had a cold.
  2. The taste of nutritious porridge with egg and vegetables that he ate when he had a cold.
  3. The fact that his friend made porridge and visited him when he had a cold.
  4. The fact that he recovered quickly from his cold thanks to the porridge his friend made.
default.q.n3-23-q72-72.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage states: "お米だけで作った白くて柔らかいおかゆで、卵も野菜も何も入っていなかった。しかし、その時はそれが心からおいしいと感じられ、20年以上たった今でも④忘れられないのだと言う。" (The topic begins with “the most delicious thing he had ever eaten,” and the sentence confirms that the feeling that the rice porridge was delicious from the bottom of his heart is something he still cannot forget more than 20 years later.)
default.q.n3-23-q72-72.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage clearly states, "卵も野菜も何も入っていなかった" (there were no eggs or vegetables in it).
default.q.n3-23-q72-72.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage is discussing the taste of the food (“一番おいしいと思った”, “心からおいしいと感じられ”), not the event of visiting you.
default.q.n3-23-q72-72.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage never says that eating rice porridge helped the person recover quickly; rather, after the fever went down, the rice porridge tasted especially memorable.
default.q.n3-23-q73-73.explanation: Summary: The passage announces nature classes (自然教室) at Aoyama Nature House (青山自然の家), including a day-trip program (日帰りプログラム) and a two-day, one-night program (1泊2日プログラム), along with information about schedules, fees, registration, and payment. Because the content of question 73 was missing ($21), the recorded answer is 3, based on the provided answer key.
default.q.n3-23-q73-73.why.0: (a) Answer choice 1 does not match the information given in the passage.
default.q.n3-23-q73-73.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 does not match the information given in the passage.
default.q.n3-23-q73-73.why.2: (c) Based on the information in the passage and the answer choices provided, choice 3 is correct.
default.q.n3-23-q73-73.why.3: (d) Answer choice 4 does not match the information given in the passage.
default.q.n3-23-q74-74.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (申し込みを自然教室の当日にして、同時に料金を現金で支払う).
default.q.n3-23-q74-74.explanation:
Summary: The 「森を歩こう」 program is listed under 【日帰りプログラム】 (day-trip programs). The information clearly states that reservations are not required (予約はいりません). Participants only need to register directly at the nature center's reception desk on the day of the program (当日、自然の家の受付で直接お申し込みください) and pay the fee in cash at the same time (当日、お申し込みと一緒に現金でお支払いください).

Translation of the question:
What must someone who wants to participate in the "Walk in the Forest" program (森を歩こう) do?

Translation of the choices:
1. Make a reservation by phone one week before the nature class and pay by bank transfer.
2. Register on the day of the nature class and pay by bank transfer within three days.
3. Make a reservation by phone before the nature class and pay in cash on the day of the class.
4. Register on the day of the nature class and pay the fee in cash at the same time.
default.q.n3-23-q74-74.why.0: (a) Incorrect. According to 【日帰りプログラム】, which includes Program ①森を歩こう, no reservation is required (予約はいりません), and payment is not made by bank transfer. The rules “1週間前までに予約” (make a reservation at least one week in advance) and “銀行振込” (bank transfer) apply to the one-night, two-day program.
default.q.n3-23-q74-74.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Under 支払方法, the day-trip program must be paid for in cash on the day of registration (当日、お申し込みと一緒に現金でお支払いください), not by bank transfer within three days (3日以内に銀行振込), which applies to the 1-night, 2-day program.
default.q.n3-23-q74-74.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The text clearly states that the program does not require advance reservations (予約はいりません) and that participants should apply directly at the reception desk on the day (当日、自然の家の受付で直接お申し込みください), not reserve by telephone before the event.
default.q.n3-23-q74-74.why.3: (d) Correct. The notices state: '※申し込み方法: 当日、自然の家の受付で直接お申し込みください。' and '支払方法: 日帰りプログラムは、当日、お申し込みと一緒に現金でお支払いください。' Therefore, participants must register in person on the day and pay in cash at the same time.
default.q.n3-23-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 2. しょうぎょう.
default.q.n3-23-q1-1.explanation:
Meaning: This town has been commercially developed since long ago.
- Kanji: 商業 (しょうぎょう: commerce, commercial industry).
- Example: この地域は商業の中心地として栄えている。(This area is thriving as a commercial center.)
default.q.n3-23-q1-1.why.0: (a) Incorrect. さんぎょう is the reading of 産業 (industry).
default.q.n3-23-q1-1.why.1: (b) Correct. 商業 consists of 商 (しょう) and 業 (ぎょう), and is read しょうぎょう (commerce, trade).
default.q.n3-23-q1-1.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 商 does not have the reading じょう.
default.q.n3-23-q1-1.why.3: (d) Incorrect. ざんぎょう is the reading of 残業 (working overtime, overtime work).
default.q.n3-23-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 2. おぼえて.
default.q.n3-23-q2-2.explanation:
Sentence meaning: I do not remember the email address.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 覚 (KAKU — remember, feel).
- Example: 一度会った人の顔はすぐ覚えます。(I quickly remember the face of someone I have met once.)
default.q.n3-23-q2-2.why.0: (a) Incorrect. おしえて is the て-form of the verb 教える, meaning “to teach” or “to tell/show someone.”
default.q.n3-23-q2-2.why.1: (b) Correct. 覚えて is the te-form of the verb 覚える (おぼえる: to remember, memorize).
default.q.n3-23-q2-2.why.2: (c) Incorrect. かえて is the te-form of the verb 変える/換える (to change, replace).
default.q.n3-23-q2-2.why.3: (d) Incorrect. かんがえて is the te-form of the verb 考える (to think).
default.q.n3-23-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 1. こうこく.
default.q.n3-23-q3-3.explanation:
Sentence meaning: The advertisement for the new service has still not been completed.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 広告 (KOUKOKU).
- Example: 新聞に新製品の広告が載っている。(An advertisement for a new product appears in the newspaper.)
default.q.n3-23-q3-3.why.0: (a) Correct. 広告 consists of 広 (こう) and 告 (こく), and is read as こうこく (advertisement).
default.q.n3-23-q3-3.why.1: (b) Incorrect. ほうこく is the reading of 報告 (report).
default.q.n3-23-q3-3.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 告 is read as こく; it does not become voiced as ごく.
default.q.n3-23-q3-3.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The first kanji is wrong (ほう), and the sound of the second kanji is also incorrect (ごく).
default.q.n3-23-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 3. あいて.
default.q.n3-23-q4-4.explanation:
Meaning: Today's opponent is very strong.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 相手 (AITE: opponent, partner, the person one interacts with).
- Example: 週末はテニスの相手をしてください。(Please be my tennis partner this weekend.)
default.q.n3-23-q4-4.why.0: (a) Incorrect. Combining the on-reading of 相 (そう) with the kun-reading of 手 (て) is not correct.
default.q.n3-23-q4-4.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Combining the kun-reading of 相 (あい) with the on-reading of 手 (しゅ) is incorrect.
default.q.n3-23-q4-4.why.2: (c) Correct. 相手 (read あいて in the kun-reading) means opponent, the other person, or someone you play or talk with.
default.q.n3-23-q4-4.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Combining two on-readings (そう + しゅ) does not produce a valid Japanese word.
default.q.n3-23-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 3. たいかい.
default.q.n3-23-q5-5.explanation:
Meaning: There will be a sports meet next month.
- Sino-Japanese roots: 大会 (large-scale tournament, competition).
- Example: 来週のマラソン大会に参加する予定です。(I plan to participate in next week's marathon.)
default.q.n3-23-q5-5.why.0: (a) Incorrect. たいがい is the reading of 大概 (generally, for the most part).
default.q.n3-23-q5-5.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 大 in this word is read with the on-reading たい, not だい.
default.q.n3-23-q5-5.why.2: (c) Correct. 大会 consists of 大 (たい) and 会 (かい), and is read たいかい, meaning a tournament, competition, or major event.
default.q.n3-23-q5-5.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The reading of 大 is wrong (read as だい), and the rendaku of 会 is also incorrect (read as がい).
default.q.n3-23-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 1. われて.
default.q.n3-23-q6-6.explanation:
Sentence meaning: The vase is broken.
- Kanji-based meaning: 割 means “to break” or “to split.”
- Example: コップが落ちて割れてしまった。(The glass fell and broke.)
default.q.n3-23-q6-6.why.0: (a) Correct. 割れて is the て-form of the intransitive verb 割れる (われる: to break, crack).
default.q.n3-23-q6-6.why.1: (b) Incorrect. よごれて is the te-form of the verb 汚れる, meaning “to become dirty” or “to be stained.”
default.q.n3-23-q6-6.why.2: (c) Incorrect. たおれて is the te-form of the verb 倒れる (to fall down, be knocked over).
default.q.n3-23-q6-6.why.3: (d) Incorrect. ぬれて is the te-form of 濡れる (to get wet).
default.q.n3-23-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 4. しゅうちゅう.
default.q.n3-23-q7-7.explanation:
Meaning: It is so noisy that I cannot concentrate on my work.
- Sino-Japanese roots: 集中 (concentration).
- Example: 静かな部屋で勉強に集中した。(I concentrated on studying in a quiet room.)
default.q.n3-23-q7-7.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 集 has the long-vowel reading しゅう, and 中 is not voiced as じゅう in this word.
default.q.n3-23-q7-7.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The kanji 集 is missing its long vowel; it should be しゅう.
default.q.n3-23-q7-7.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The on-reading of 中 is ちゅう, not じゅう.
default.q.n3-23-q7-7.why.3: (d) Correct. 集中 consists of 集 (しゅう) and 中 (ちゅう), and is read as しゅうちゅう (concentration).
default.q.n3-23-q8-8.verdict: The correct answer is 2. しょっき.
default.q.n3-23-q8-8.explanation:
Meaning: Excuse me, where is the tableware section?
- Kanji note: 食器 (tableware, dishes, utensils).
- Example: 食後は食器を台所に運んでください。(Please take the dishes to the kitchen after the meal.)
default.q.n3-23-q8-8.why.0: (a) Incorrect. When 食 (しょく) and 器 (き) are combined, gemination changes the pronunciation to しょっき rather than しょくき.
default.q.n3-23-q8-8.why.1: (b) Correct. 食器 (しょっき, tableware) undergoes gemination, becoming しょっき.
default.q.n3-23-q8-8.why.2: (c) Incorrect. しょくひん is the reading of 食品, meaning “food” or “food products.”
default.q.n3-23-q8-8.why.3: (d) Incorrect. This reading does not exist and is easily confused with the loanword ショッピング (shopping).
default.q.n3-23-q9-9.explanation:
Meaning: Because the child accidentally drew on the wall, I erased it and cleaned it up.
- Kanji: 消 (消す: erase, extinguish; 消える: disappear, go out).
- Example: 黒板の字を消してください。(Please erase the writing on the blackboard.)
default.q.n3-23-q9-9.why.0: (a) 「流して」(base form: 流す - nagasu) means “let flow” or “flush away”; it is not read as 「けして」.
default.q.n3-23-q9-9.why.1: (b) 「洗して」 is an incorrect kanji and okurigana spelling; 「洗」 is used in the verb 「洗う」 (arau), meaning “to wash.”
default.q.n3-23-q9-9.why.2: (c) 「消して」 (base form: 消す) means “erase, remove, wipe away,” and has the correct reading and meaning for erasing drawings from a wall.
default.q.n3-23-q9-9.why.3: (d) 「清して」 is an incorrect combination. The kanji 「清」 appears in the adjective 「清い」 (kiyoi) or the verb 「清める」 (kiyomeru), and is not read as 「けして」.
default.q.n3-23-q10-10.explanation:
Meaning: I was absent from school because I had a cold.
- Kanji: 欠 (lack, be absent) + 席 (seat).
- Antonym: 出席 (しゅっせき: attendance, being present).
- Example: 会議を欠席する連絡を入れた。(I contacted them to let them know I would be absent from the meeting.)
default.q.n3-23-q10-10.why.0: (a) 「休座」 is not a Japanese vocabulary word with a meaning.
default.q.n3-23-q10-10.why.1: (b) 「休席」is an incorrect kanji compound (「休」is used instead of「欠」).
default.q.n3-23-q10-10.why.2: (c) 「欠座」 is an incorrect kanji compound; 「席」, not 「座」, is used in the word meaning absence.
default.q.n3-23-q10-10.why.3: (d) 「欠席」 (KHUYẾT TỊCH) is read 「けっせき」 and means being absent, such as missing school or a meeting.
default.q.n3-23-q11-11.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Please cut the vegetables into small pieces.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 細 (SAI - small, fine; 細かい: small, detailed; 細い - ほそい: slender, thin).
- Example: お札を細かく両替してもらえますか。(Could you exchange this large bill for smaller bills?)
default.q.n3-23-q11-11.why.0: (a) 「細かく」 (base form: 細かい) is read 「こまかく」 and means “small, finely, in detail,” which fits the context of cutting vegetables into small pieces.
default.q.n3-23-q11-11.why.1: (b) 「短かく」 uses incorrect okurigana; the correct form is 「短く」 (mijikaku), derived from 短い (short), and it is not read as 「こまかく」.
default.q.n3-23-q11-11.why.2: (c) 「丸かく」 is an incorrect spelling. The adjective 「丸い」 (marui) becomes the adverb 「丸く」 (maruku: roundly); it is not read as 「こまかく」.
default.q.n3-23-q11-11.why.3: (d) 「角かく」is not a correct Japanese vocabulary item; the kanji「角」is read kado, tsuno, or kaku.
default.q.n3-23-q12-12.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Many young people live in this apartment complex.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 若 (じゃく: young; 若い: young; 若者 - わかもの: young person, young people).
- Example: 彼女は実年齢よりも若く見える。(She looks younger than her actual age.)
default.q.n3-23-q12-12.why.0: (a) 「孝い」is an incorrect spelling. 「孝」appears in「孝行」(filial piety), but there is no adjective「孝い」.
default.q.n3-23-q12-12.why.1: (b) 「苦い」 is read 「にがい」 and means “bitter.”
default.q.n3-23-q12-12.why.2: (c)「老い」is read as「おい」and means “aging” as a noun; it is also related to the verb「老いる」(oiru: to grow old), not read as「わかい」.
default.q.n3-23-q12-12.why.3: (d) 「若い」 is read 「わかい」 and means "young, youthful"; this is completely correct.
default.q.n3-23-q13-13.explanation:
Sentence meaning: I selected a beautiful photograph from among many different photos.
- Kanji meanings: 複: complex, multiple layers + 数: number, quantity.
- Distinction: 「複」: multiple, complex (複数, 複雑) versus 「復」: repetition, return (復習, 回復, 往復).
- Example: 複数の候補者の中から一人を選出する。(Select one person from among several candidates.)
default.q.n3-23-q13-13.why.0: (a) 「複数」 (ON-reading: ふくすう) means "multiple, plural (two or more)" and correctly combines the kanji 「複」and「数」.
default.q.n3-23-q13-13.why.1: (b) 「複枚」is an incorrect word formation; the counter 「枚」does not create a word meaning “multiple” or “several.”
default.q.n3-23-q13-13.why.2: (c) 「復数」 is an incorrect kanji spelling; it mistakenly uses 「復」 (recovery, review) instead of 「複」.
default.q.n3-23-q13-13.why.3: (d) 「復枚」is completely incorrect; both kanji are wrong.
default.q.n3-23-q14-14.explanation:
Meaning: The amount of imported rice is declining.
- Kanji components: 減 (decrease; 減る / へる, 減らす / へらす) + 少 (few, little; 少ない / すくない).
- Antonym: 増加 (ぞうか: increase).
- Example: 人口が急激に減少している。(The population is declining rapidly.)
default.q.n3-23-q14-14.why.0: (a) 「減小」is an incorrect kanji compound: 「小」 means small in size, whereas 「少」 means a small amount or number.
default.q.n3-23-q14-14.why.1: (b) 「減少」 (ON-reading: げんしょう) means "to decrease, decline (in amount or quantity)" and correctly combines the kanji 「減」and「少」.
default.q.n3-23-q14-14.why.2: (c) 「現少」is an incorrect kanji spelling, using 「現」instead of 「減」.
default.q.n3-23-q14-14.why.3: (d)「現小」is completely incorrect as a combination of kanji.
default.q.n3-23-q15-15.explanation:
Translation: "There are six pieces of candy, so if they are divided among three people, each person gets two."
- Kanji: 分 (to divide, separate).
- Example: ケーキを4等分に分ける (Divide the cake into four equal parts.)
default.q.n3-23-q15-15.why.0: (a) 「わける」(分ける: to divide, distribute). In this sentence, it means dividing six cakes among three people so that each person receives two, which fits the meaning perfectly.
default.q.n3-23-q15-15.why.1: (b) 「離す」 (はなす - to separate): to move apart or keep at a distance; it is not used to mean dividing food among several people.
default.q.n3-23-q15-15.why.2: (c) 「引く」 (ひく – to pull, subtract in mathematics): The sentence is about dividing candy equally among a number of people (3人で), so 引く does not fit the meaning.
default.q.n3-23-q15-15.why.3: (d) 「破く」(やぶく) means to tear something (paper, bags, etc.), so it is completely inappropriate in the context of dividing food.
default.q.n3-23-q16-16.explanation:
Meaning: "My friend has just had a baby, so I am planning to give them something as a congratulatory gift."
- 祝 (いわう) = celebrate, congratulate; a celebratory occasion.
- Common expressions: 出産祝い (a gift celebrating the birth of a baby), 結婚祝い (a wedding gift).
- Example: 友人の結婚のお祝いに花を贈った (I gave flowers as a wedding gift to my friend).
default.q.n3-23-q16-16.why.0: (a) 「お願い」(おねがい) means a request or favor, so it does not fit the context of giving a congratulatory gift for someone's new baby.
default.q.n3-23-q16-16.why.1: (b) 「お祝い」 (おいわい - congratulations): a congratulatory gift or message for a happy event (the birth of a child, marriage, passing an exam, etc.). It naturally collocates with 贈る (to give).
default.q.n3-23-q16-16.why.2: (c) 「お代わり」(おかわり) means an additional serving, such as another bowl of rice or glass of water during a meal; it is unrelated to giving a gift.
default.q.n3-23-q16-16.why.3: (d) 「お見舞い」(おみまい - a get-well visit/gift) refers to visiting or giving a gift to someone who is ill or affected by an accident or natural disaster. It is not used for happy occasions such as the birth of a child.
default.q.n3-23-q17-17.explanation:
Sentence translation: 'There is something wrong with my computer. Is there a way for me to check the cause myself?'
- Kanji meanings: 方: direction, way; 法: rule, method.
- Common pattern: [dictionary-form verb] + 方法 (a way of performing an action).
default.q.n3-23-q17-17.why.0: (a) 「方法」(ほうほう - method, way): The phrase 「調べる方法」 means “a way to check or look up something” and is natural and accurate in this context.
default.q.n3-23-q17-17.why.1: (b) 「都合」(つごう) means personal convenience regarding time or circumstances, as in 都合が良い/悪い; it does not combine with 調べる to mean a method.
default.q.n3-23-q17-17.why.2: (c) 「規則」(きそく): rules, regulations, or general policies; it does not mean a method for handling a technical problem.
default.q.n3-23-q17-17.why.3: (d) 「計画」 (けいかく - plan): a plan or arrangement of future steps; it does not mean a method for investigating a cause.
default.q.n3-23-q18-18.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “Mr. Tanaka is proactive; he willingly tries everything himself.”
- Kanji note: 積 (accumulation), 極 (extreme, limit), 的 (indicating a quality).
- Antonym: 消極的 (しょうきょくてき - negative, passive).
- Example: 彼女は何事にも積極的な態度をとる (She always takes a proactive attitude toward everything.)
default.q.n3-23-q18-18.why.0: (a) 「感情的」(かんじょうてき - emotional): emotional, easily moved or angered (as opposed to rational); it is not used to mean enthusiastic or proactive.
default.q.n3-23-q18-18.why.1: (b) 「効果的」(こうかてき - effective): producing good results (usually modifying a method, measure, or medicine); it is not used as an adjective describing a person’s personality.
default.q.n3-23-q18-18.why.2: (c) 「積極的」 (せっきょくてき): positive, proactive, enthusiastic. The clause 「何でも自分からやってみようとする」 (trying to do everything on one's own initiative) perfectly describes this adjective.
default.q.n3-23-q18-18.why.3: (d) 「具体的」(ぐたいてき): specific, concrete, clear (for example, a specific example or a concrete plan); it is not used to describe someone’s proactive personality.
default.q.n3-23-q19-19.explanation:
Meaning: "Japan does not have many natural resources such as oil or gold."
- Kanji meanings: 資 (resources, assets), 源 (source, origin).
- Common expressions: 天然資源 (natural resources), 資源が乏しい (to be poor in resources).
- Example: 日本は天然資源の多くを輸入に頼っている (Japan relies on imports for many of its natural resources).
default.q.n3-23-q19-19.why.0: (a) 「環境」(かんきょう — environment): the natural environment or living environment; it is not used as a general term for minerals or raw materials such as petroleum or gold.
default.q.n3-23-q19-19.why.1: (b) 「資源」(しげん): Resources, such as minerals and energy. Oil (石油) and gold (金) are typical natural resources.
default.q.n3-23-q19-19.why.2: (c) 「基礎」(きそ): foundation, basis, basic knowledge; it is unrelated to mineral resources.
default.q.n3-23-q19-19.why.3: (d) 「栄養」(えいよう - nutrients): nutrients in food, which does not fit the context of oil and gold.
default.q.n3-23-q20-20.explanation:
Sentence translation: "When I first met Mr. Mori, I got the impression that he was a quiet person."
- Kanji components: 印 (mark, impression) and 象 (image, figure).
- Common expressions: ～という印象を受ける (get the impression that...), 印象を与える (make an impression), 第一印象 (first impression).
default.q.n3-23-q20-20.why.0: (a) 「感覚」(かんかく — sensation or sense): a sensory, aesthetic, or temporal feeling; it does not combine with ～という...を受ける to describe an impression of a person.
default.q.n3-23-q20-20.why.1: (b) 「意識」(いしき - awareness, consciousness, alertness) does not form a natural expression with 受ける in the context of evaluating another person.
default.q.n3-23-q20-20.why.2: (c) 「印象」(いんしょう): impression. The fixed expression 「印象を受ける」(to get an impression) is exactly appropriate for describing one’s impression of someone’s personality upon first meeting them.
default.q.n3-23-q20-20.why.3: (d) 「気分」 (きぶん - mood): one’s mood or physical feeling, such as feeling refreshed or tired; it is not used to indicate an impression of another person.
default.q.n3-23-q21-21.explanation:
Meaning: “My tooth had been hurting unbearably since last night, so I went to the dentist this morning.”
- Vocabulary: 我慢: to endure or put up with something.
- Common phrases: 痛みを我慢する (to endure pain), 我慢強い (patient, able to endure), もう我慢の限界だ (I have reached the limit of my endurance).
default.q.n3-23-q21-21.why.0: (a) 「遠慮」 (えんりょ): restraint, hesitation, reserve toward others; it is not used for enduring physical pain.
default.q.n3-23-q21-21.why.1: (b) 「努力」(どりょく) means effort or striving to achieve a goal, so it is not used for trying to endure toothache.
default.q.n3-23-q21-21.why.2: (c) 「我慢」(がまん) means “endurance, patience.” The expression 「痛くて我慢できなくなった」 (“it became so painful that I could no longer stand it”) is extremely common and accurate.
default.q.n3-23-q21-21.why.3: (d) 「心配」(しんぱい) means worry or concern; it does not mean enduring physical pain.
default.q.n3-23-q22-22.explanation:
Translate the sentence: “I bought a postcard with a picture on it as a souvenir of the trip.”
- The kanji 記 suggests “record” or “remember,” while 念 suggests “thought” or “remembrance.”
- Fixed pattern: [noun] + の記念に (as a souvenir of...).
- Example: 卒業の記念にみんなで写真を撮った (Everyone took a picture together as a graduation keepsake).
default.q.n3-23-q22-22.why.0: (a) 「満足」(まんぞく) means satisfaction or contentment. It is not used in the pattern ～の満足に to express the purpose of buying souvenirs.
default.q.n3-23-q22-22.why.1: (b) 「感激」(かんげき—deeply moved, touched) does not form the expression 旅行の感激に.
default.q.n3-23-q22-22.why.2: (c) 「経験」(けいけん): experience; an experience is not an object that can be kept as a memento.
default.q.n3-23-q22-22.why.3: (d) 「記念」 (きねん - memento, commemoration): The fixed expression 「旅行の記念に」 (as a memento of the trip) is the most natural and accurate phrasing.
default.q.n3-23-q23-23.explanation:
Sentence translation: “The parking fee has increased starting this month.”
- Kanji meaning: 料 (in words meaning a fee or service charge).
- Distinguishing JLPT N3 suffixes related to money:
  + 料 (usage/service fee): 使用料 (usage fee), 入場料 (admission fee), 手数料 (service/processing fee).
  + 賃 (wages/rent or transportation fare): 家賃 (rent), 運賃 (transportation fare), 手間賃 (labor charge).
  + 代 (payment for a specific product or service): 電気代 (electricity bill), 食事代 (meal cost), 部屋代 (room charge).
  + 費 (expense or cost of living/activities): 交通費 (transportation expenses), 生活費 (living expenses), 会費 (membership fee).
default.q.n3-23-q23-23.why.0: (a) 「金」(きん/かね) is used in terms for specific types of money, such as 奨学金 (scholarship), 保証金 (deposit), and 入会金 (membership fee). It does not combine with 使用 to mean a parking fee.
default.q.n3-23-q23-23.why.1: (b) 「値」 (ね/あたい): value or price (as in 値段 and 期待値); it is not a suffix indicating a usage fee.
default.q.n3-23-q23-23.why.2: (c) 「料」(りょう): A suffix indicating a fee paid for using a service or facility. It correctly combines with 使用 to form 「使用料」(usage fee).
default.q.n3-23-q23-23.why.3: (d)「賃」(ちん): is a suffix indicating rental fees or wages, as in 家賃 and 運賃, and does not combine to form 使用賃.
default.q.n3-23-q24-24.explanation:
Translation: “I found this game interesting at first, but after playing it too many times, I’m completely tired of it.”
- On-reading: 飽 (being full, saturated, or fed up).
- Distinction: 飽きる means to become tired of something through excessive repetition, whereas 嫌になる means to become fed up with or dislike something because it is unpleasant or irritating.
- Example: 毎日同じ料理ばかり食べていると飽きる (If you eat the same dish every day, you will get tired of it.)
default.q.n3-23-q24-24.why.0: (a) 「きらって」 (嫌う) means to hate or dislike due to personal aversion; it does not imply becoming bored through repeated exposure.
default.q.n3-23-q24-24.why.1: (b) 「あきらめて」(諦める) means to give up or abandon hope when something is too difficult, so it does not fit the context of playing repeatedly until becoming fed up.
default.q.n3-23-q24-24.why.2: (c) 「こわがって」(怖がる) means “to feel afraid” or “to be frightened,” which does not fit the preceding phrase “find it interesting.”
default.q.n3-23-q24-24.why.3: (d) 「あきて」 (飽きる): to become bored or tired of something through repeated exposure or practice. The phrase 「何度もやったので、もうあきてしまった」 accurately expresses the cause and result.
default.q.n3-23-q25-25.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (パンフレット).
default.q.n3-23-q25-25.explanation:
Sentence translation: “When I went to the travel agency, there were many pamphlets about overseas travel placed there.”
- Katakana loanword: パンフレット (pamphlet - folded leaflet, booklet, service guide).
- Example: 大学のパンフレットを取り寄せる (to request a university brochure).
default.q.n3-23-q25-25.why.0: (a) 「アナウンス」 (announcement): an announcement or spoken broadcast through a loudspeaker. It is sound, not a physical object that can be held or placed (たくさん置いてあった).
default.q.n3-23-q25-25.why.1: (b) 「コマーシャル」(commercial / CM) means a television or radio advertisement; it cannot refer to printed material placed on a table.
default.q.n3-23-q25-25.why.2: (c) 「サンプル」 (sample): A sample or trial product, commonly used for cosmetics and products to try; it is not used to refer to a travel-tour guidebook.
default.q.n3-23-q25-25.why.3: (d) 「パンフレット」: A folded leaflet or thin booklet advertising or introducing a program or service. Many such printed materials are typically arranged at travel agencies (旅行会社).
default.q.n3-23-q26-26.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 少し前に.
default.q.n3-23-q26-26.explanation:
Meaning: "If it were Mr./Ms. Yamaguchi, they would have gone home a little while ago."
Vocabulary & Sino-Japanese reading:
- さっき (adverb): a little while ago, just now
- 帰る (QUY): to go home, return
- 少し前: a short while ago, just now
Example: さっき電話があったよ。(Someone called a little while ago.)
default.q.n3-23-q26-26.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「すぐに」 means “immediately,” describing an action that occurs at once afterward; it does not mean “a little while ago.”
default.q.n3-23-q26-26.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「ずっと前に」 means "a long time ago," which contrasts with the short time indicated by 「さっき」 (just a moment ago).
default.q.n3-23-q26-26.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「やっと」 means "finally," expressing that something was achieved after a long wait or effort, so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-23-q26-26.why.3: (d) Correct because 「少し前に」 (a little while ago; just recently) is completely synonymous with the adverb 「さっき」, referring to something that happened not long ago.
default.q.n3-23-q27-27.verdict: The correct answer is 3. へんな.
default.q.n3-23-q27-27.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “I can hear a strange sound coming from the next room.”
Vocabulary and kanji:
- おかしい / おかしな: strange, unusual (= 変な); it can also mean “funny, humorous”
- 隣: next door, beside
- 音: sound
- 聞こえる: be audible, be heard naturally
- 変: strange, unusual
Example: どこかからおかしな（＝変な）においがする。(There is a strange smell coming from somewhere.)
default.q.n3-23-q27-27.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「いろいろな」 means “various, diverse,” and does not mean strange or unusual.
default.q.n3-23-q27-27.why.1: (b) Incorrect because「にぎやかな」means lively or bustling, so it is not synonymous with「おかしな」.
default.q.n3-23-q27-27.why.2: (c) Correct because 「へんな」(変な: strange, unusual, abnormal) is synonymous with 「おかしな」 when describing something or a sound as strange or abnormal.
default.q.n3-23-q27-27.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「大きな」 means “big” or “large,” describing size or volume rather than an unusual quality.
default.q.n3-23-q28-28.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 過ぎました.
default.q.n3-23-q28-28.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “About one week has passed since then.”
Vocabulary and kanji compounds:
- 経つ: for time to pass
- 過ぎる: to pass, exceed
- 約: approximately, about
- 週間: week
Example: 日本に来てから3年が経ちました（＝過ぎました）。(Three years have passed since I came to Japan.)
default.q.n3-23-q28-28.why.0: (a) Correct because 「過ぎました」(from 過ぎる, time passed) is synonymous with 「たちました」(from 経つ, time elapsed).
default.q.n3-23-q28-28.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「かかりました」 (掛かる) means “to take” or “to cost” time or money to do something, not for time to pass on its own.
default.q.n3-23-q28-28.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「待ちました」(待つ) means “waited,” not the same as 「経つ」.
default.q.n3-23-q28-28.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「続けました」(続ける) means “continued” an action and is a transitive verb indicating the continuation of an activity.
default.q.n3-23-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 急いだようすで.
default.q.n3-23-q29-29.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “Mr./Ms. Yamamoto has already hurried outside.”
Vocabulary and kanji readings:
- 慌てる: to panic, hurry, become flustered
- 急ぐ: to hurry, rush, do quickly
- 様子: appearance, state, manner
Example: ベルが鳴って、学生たちは慌てて（＝急いだようすで）教室に入った。(When the bell rang, the students hurried into the classroom.)
default.q.n3-23-q29-29.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「困ったようすで」(困る) means “with a troubled, embarrassed, or distressed appearance,” and does not express the hurried, flustered state conveyed by 「あわてて」.
default.q.n3-23-q29-29.why.1: (b) Correct because 「急いだようすで」(急ぐ) means “with a hurried, rushed appearance,” accurately expressing the frantic action of 「あわてて」(慌てる).
default.q.n3-23-q29-29.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「疲れたようすで」 (from 疲れる) means “with a tired appearance” and has nothing to do with being in a hurry.
default.q.n3-23-q29-29.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「怒ったようすで」(from 「怒る」) means “with an angry expression,” which does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-23-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 曲がっている.
default.q.n3-23-q30-30.explanation:
Meaning: “The road curves ahead, so please be careful.”
Vocabulary and kanji:
- カーブ / カープ (curve): a bend, curve in the road
- 曲がる (to bend, curve, turn)
- 道 (road)
- 気をつける (to be careful, pay attention)
Example: この先は急にカーブしている（＝曲がっている）ので、スピードを落としてください。(There is a sharp curve ahead, so please slow down.)
default.q.n3-23-q30-30.why.0: (a) Correct because「曲がっている」(from 曲がる: bend, wind, turn) is synonymous with「カーブしている」(curve).
default.q.n3-23-q30-30.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「坂になっている」(坂: slope) means “has become a slope” or “is sloping,” not “is curving.”
default.q.n3-23-q30-30.why.2: (c) Incorrect because「暗くなっている」(暗い: dark) means “has become dark” and has nothing to do with the curved shape of a road.
default.q.n3-23-q30-30.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「狭くなっている」 (狭い: narrow) means “has become narrower,” not “curved.”
default.q.n3-23-q31-31.explanation:
「内容」（ないよう）: the details, information, or meaning contained in a piece of writing, a book, a letter, a conversation, a plan, or a program (for example: メールの内容, 本の内容, 話の内容, 記事の内容).
Note: It is not used for physical components or ingredients (use 材料 or 成分), or for thoughts in one's mind (use 頭の中 or 考え).
Example: 発表の内容をもう一度確認してください。 (Please check the content of the presentation once again.)
default.q.n3-23-q31-31.why.0: Incorrect because 「頭の内容」 is not used to mean one's thoughts or mind; this case requires 「頭の中」.
default.q.n3-23-q31-31.why.1: Incorrect because the effective medicinal substance in a drug must be called 「成分」 (ingredient, component), not 「内容」.
default.q.n3-23-q31-31.why.2: Incorrect because the ingredients that make up the juice (apples, bananas, and milk) should be expressed with 「材料」, 「原料」, or 「中身」, not 「内容」.
default.q.n3-23-q31-31.why.3: Correct because 「メールの内容」(the contents of an email/correspondence) is a natural and accurate collocation for the information written in the message.
default.q.n3-23-q32-32.explanation:
「発展」（はってん - development): used for expansion in scale or advancement to a higher level in areas such as the economy, technology, society, cities, and industry (for example: 経済の発展, 都市の発展, 科学技術の発展). It can also describe a situation or event developing into a more complicated stage (事件へと発展する).
Note: It is not used for the improvement of a personal skill (use 上達する), a person's growth or maturity (use 成長する), or the progress of construction work (use 工事が進む).
Example: アジアの経済は急速に発展しています。(The Asian economy is developing rapidly.)
default.q.n3-23-q32-32.why.0: Correct because「町が発展する」(a town or city developing through trade) is a perfectly standard expression for the economic development and expansion of an area.
default.q.n3-23-q32-32.why.1: Incorrect because progress in a skill or personal talent, such as playing the piano, is expressed with 「上達する」, not 「発展する」.
default.q.n3-23-q32-32.why.2: Incorrect because the progress of construction on a building should be expressed with 「（工事が）進む」 or 「できてきた」, not 「発展する」.
default.q.n3-23-q32-32.why.3: Incorrect because the growth and maturity of a person, such as a son returning from studying abroad, should be expressed with 「成長する」, not 「発展する」.
default.q.n3-23-q33-33.explanation:
「伝わる」（つたわる - to be transmitted, conveyed, passed down）: an intransitive verb used when technology, customs, culture, news, feelings, sound, or heat spreads from one place to another or is passed down through generations (e.g., 技術が伝わる, 文化が伝わる, 気持ちが伝わる, 熱が伝わる).
Note: It is not used for receiving mail sent through the postal service (use 届く), catching an infectious cold (use うつる), or changing trains/vehicles (use 乗り換える, 移る).
Example: 彼の熱意が言葉を通して相手に伝わった。(His enthusiasm was conveyed to the other person through his words.)
default.q.n3-23-q33-33.why.0: Incorrect. To say that a letter sent by someone has arrived, use 「届く」(手紙が届いた) or 「来る」, not 「伝わる」.
default.q.n3-23-q33-33.why.1: Incorrect because catching a disease or cold from someone is expressed with 「うつる」 (風邪がうつった), not 「伝わる」.
default.q.n3-23-q33-33.why.2: Incorrect because when people move or switch to a bus, use「乗り換える」「流れてくる」or「移る」, not「伝わる」.
default.q.n3-23-q33-33.why.3: Correct because 「技術が外国から伝わる」 (technology is introduced or transmitted from abroad) is completely standard and natural usage.
default.q.n3-23-q34-34.explanation:
「どなる」（怒鳴る - to yell, shout angrily）describes a person speaking very loudly, usually in anger, irritation, or while scolding someone (e.g., 大声でどなる, 怒鳴りつける).
Note: For the sound of a bell or thunder, use 「鳴る」（なる）; for a dog barking, use 「ほえる」（吠える）.
Example: 父は怒ると大きな声でどなる。(Whenever my father gets angry, he shouts loudly.)
default.q.n3-23-q34-34.why.0: Incorrect because the sound of a bell or alarm clock ringing is expressed with 「鳴る」 (時計が鳴る音), not 「どなる」.
default.q.n3-23-q34-34.why.1: Correct because 「どなる」 (to speak loudly, shout, or yell) is used for a person's action of speaking loudly during communication, which fits the context perfectly.
default.q.n3-23-q34-34.why.2: Incorrect because a dog barking is expressed with the verb「ほえる」(犬がほえている), not「どなる」.
default.q.n3-23-q34-34.why.3: Incorrect because thunder rumbling or booming in the sky is expressed with 「鳴る」 (雷が鳴り始めた) or 「とどろく」, not 「どなる」.
default.q.n3-23-q35-35.explanation:
「期限」（きげん - deadline, time limit, expiration period）refers to a time limit by which something must be completed or the period during which a document, contract, or payment remains valid. Common expressions include: 提出期限, 支払い期限, 有効期限, 期限が切れる.
Note: It is not used for an appointment time (use 約束の時間 or 集合時間), a scheduled train or bus time (use 定刻 or 予定時刻), or the service life of machinery or electronic devices (use 寿命).
Example: レポートの提出期限は今週の金曜日です。(The report is due this Friday.)
default.q.n3-23-q35-35.why.0: Incorrect because when an electronic device or television breaks down after long use, this concerns the device’s service life; 「寿命」 (そろそろ寿命だと思う) should be used instead of 「期限」.
default.q.n3-23-q35-35.why.1: Incorrect because the scheduled departure time of a train or bus should be expressed with 「定刻」, 「予定時刻」, or 「予定の時間」, not 「期限」.
default.q.n3-23-q35-35.why.2: Correct because 「指定の期限までに」 (by the specified deadline) is the standard expression for the deadline for completing a procedure, such as making a payment.
default.q.n3-23-q35-35.why.3: Wrong because the scheduled time when everyone is supposed to meet should be expressed as 「約束の時間」or「集合時間」, not 「期限」.
default.q.n3-24-q36-36.explanation:
- Sentence translation: "The airport is packed with people planning to spend the New Year holiday abroad."
- Grammar: 「[period of time] + を過ごす」means "to spend a period of time." The particle 「を」 marks the period of time spent with the verb 「過ごす」.
- Example: 週末を家族とゆっくり過ごしました。(I spent a relaxing weekend with my family.)
default.q.n3-24-q36-36.why.0: (a) 「へ」 indicates the direction of movement and is not used with a time noun together with the verb 「過ごす」.
default.q.n3-24-q36-36.why.1: (b) 「が」 marks the subject, so it is inappropriate because the time noun 「お正月休み」 is the object affected by 「過ごす」 and therefore requires the particle 「を」.
default.q.n3-24-q36-36.why.2: (c) 「と」 indicates someone who performs an action together with another person or links items in a list as “and.” It is not used before 「過ごす」 with a time noun in this context.
default.q.n3-24-q36-36.why.3: (d) 「を」 accompanies the time noun 「お正月休み」 as the object of 「過ごす」, forming the phrase 「休みを過ごす」 (spend the holiday).
default.q.n3-24-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 必ず.
default.q.n3-24-q37-37.explanation:
- Sentence translation: Teacher: “Regarding next week’s field trip, the meeting time is 9 o’clock. If you are late, you must contact the school.”
- Related vocabulary:
  + 遠足: field trip.
  + 集合: gathering, assembly.
  + 連絡: contact, communication.
- Grammar: `必ず + V-てください`: Be sure to do V (emphasizes a required action).
- Example: 約束の時間には必ず来てください。(Be sure to come at the appointed time.)
default.q.n3-24-q37-37.why.0: (a) 「全く」 means “completely” and is commonly used with a negative form (全く〜ない) or to express surprise; it does not go with the request 「〜てください」.
default.q.n3-24-q37-37.why.1: (b) 「必ず」means "certainly/without fail" and is often used with a request or instruction such as「〜てください」to indicate an action that must be performed.
default.q.n3-24-q37-37.why.2: (c) 「非常に」means “very/extremely.” It is an adverb of degree modifying an adjective or a stative verb, and is not used in a context giving instructions for an action.
default.q.n3-24-q37-37.why.3: (d) 「決して」 means “absolutely not” and always accompanies a negative expression (決して〜ない / てはいけない). It is not used in an affirmative sentence requesting someone to do something.
default.q.n3-24-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 2. あの.
default.q.n3-24-q38-38.explanation:
- Sentence translation: Tanaka: “Hayashi just got scolded by the section chief, didn’t he?” - Yamashita: “Yeah.” - Tanaka: “Hayashi was certainly at fault too, but don’t you think the section chief’s way of speaking was excessive?”
- Demonstratives in conversation (Ko-So-A-Do):
  + When both the speaker and listener clearly know the information or event, or directly experienced or witnessed it together in the past, use the 「ア」 series (あの, あれ, ああいう...).
  + The 「ソ」 series (その, それ...) is used when only one of the two people knows something, or when referring to information just mentioned by the other person that the speaker did not experience together with them.
- Example: 昨日見たあの映画、面白かったね。(That movie we watched yesterday was interesting, wasn’t it?)
default.q.n3-24-q38-38.why.0: (a) 「その」 is used when only one of the two people knows about the matter. It is not used when both people directly witnessed the event, as in this situation.
default.q.n3-24-q38-38.why.1: (b) 「あの」 refers to an event in the past that both the speaker and listener clearly know about or witnessed together (the section chief had just scolded Hayashi).
default.q.n3-24-q38-38.why.2: (c) 「そう」 is an adverb meaning “that way” or “like that,” and cannot directly modify the noun 「言い方」; the attributive form 「そういう」 must be used.
