default.q.n3-25-q19-19.verdict: The correct answer is 1. リサイクル.
default.q.n3-25-q19-19.explanation:
Meaning: If cans and plastic bottles are recycled instead of being thrown away, the amount of waste will decrease.
- Katakana loanwords:
  + リサイクル (recycle): to recycle waste or used items.
  + キャンセル (cancel): to cancel an appointment, order, or ticket.
  + カット (cut): to cut costs, cut hair, or cut a scene from a film.
  + チェンジ (change): to change or renew.
- Example: 古い紙をリサイクルしてトイレットペーパーを作る。(Recycle old paper to make toilet paper.)
default.q.n3-25-q19-19.why.0: (a) リサイクル (recycle): recycling waste. Recycling cans and plastic bottles 「リサイクルすれば」 helps reduce waste, so this is completely correct.
default.q.n3-25-q19-19.why.1: (b) キャンセル (cancel): to cancel an appointment, service, or contract; it is not used with garbage or canned goods.
default.q.n3-25-q19-19.why.2: (c) カット (cut): to cut or reduce something (such as costs or length); it does not describe recycling waste materials.
default.q.n3-25-q19-19.why.3: (d) チェンジ (change) means changing a person or state, so it does not fit the context of waste processing.
default.q.n3-25-q20-20.verdict: The correct answer is 4. うわさ (rumor).
default.q.n3-25-q20-20.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: 'I heard a rumor that Mr. Hayashi is getting married soon, but I don't know whether it is really true.'
- Vocabulary and Sino-Japanese readings:
  + 噂 (うわさ): rumor (噂を聞く: hear a rumor, 噂が広まる: a rumor spreads).
  + 文句 (もんく): complaint, grumbling (文句を言う).
  + 宣伝 (せんでん): advertising, promotion.
  + 嘘 (うそ): lie, falsehood.
- Example: 彼についての変な噂を聞いた。(I heard a strange rumor about him.)
default.q.n3-25-q20-20.why.0: (a) 文句 (もんく): complaint, grumbling; it commonly occurs in 「文句を言う」 and is inappropriate for hearing that someone has gotten married.
default.q.n3-25-q20-20.why.1: (b) 宣伝 (せんでん) means promotion or advertising of a product or marketing information; it is not used for someone's personal marriage announcement.
default.q.n3-25-q20-20.why.2: (c) うそ (嘘): a lie; using 「うそを聞いた」 (heard a lie) would contradict the following clause 「本当かどうかはわからない」 (I do not know whether it is true).
default.q.n3-25-q20-20.why.3: (d) うわさ (噂): Rumor. It naturally and accurately combines with 「うわさを聞いたが、本当かどうかはわからない」(I heard a rumor, but I do not know whether it is true).
default.q.n3-25-q21-21.verdict: The correct answer is 4. おもに (mainly, mostly).
default.q.n3-25-q21-21.explanation:
Meaning: “The participants in this presentation are mainly students, but there are also a few homemakers and company employees.”
- Important adverbs:
  + 主に (おもに): mainly, mostly (often used with a clause describing the small remainder).
  + すべて (全て): all, everything.
  + 必ず (かならず): surely, without fail.
  + 十分 (じゅうぶん): sufficiently, enough.
- Example: この雑誌の読者は主に若い女性です。(The readers of this magazine are mainly young women.)
default.q.n3-25-q21-21.why.0: (a) かならず (必ず): certainly, without fail. It expresses inevitability or a promise/assertion, and is not used to indicate the proportion of participants.
default.q.n3-25-q21-21.why.1: (b) すべて (全て): “all, everything”; if it meant “everyone,” it would directly contradict the following clause 「ほかに...も少しいた」 (“there were also a few other people”).
default.q.n3-25-q21-21.why.2: (c) じゆうぶん (十分): sufficient, satisfactory (in amount or degree); it cannot be used as an adverb modifying “mainly students.”
default.q.n3-25-q21-21.why.3: (d) おもに (主に - mainly): mainly, for the most part. It contrasts perfectly with 「ほかに...少しいた」(there were a few others), making the sentence complete and accurate.
default.q.n3-25-q22-22.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 不安 (anxiety, uneasiness).
default.q.n3-25-q22-22.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “At first, I was very worried about whether I would be able to handle such an important job.”
- Vocabulary:
  + 不安 (ふあん): anxiety, unease, worry.
  + 無理 (むり): impossible, too difficult (in this context, it would need to be used as 「無理だと思った」).
  + 退屈 (たいくつ): boring, tedious.
  + 苦手 (にがて): poor at, not good with, uncomfortable doing.
- Example: 初めての一人暮らしで、とても不安だった。(I was very anxious when I first lived alone.)
default.q.n3-25-q22-22.why.0: (a) 不安 (ふあん - anxiety): a feeling of worry or unease; it follows the interrogative clause 「～できるかどうか」(whether one can do something or not), fitting both the meaning and emotional nuance precisely.
default.q.n3-25-q22-22.why.1: (b) 無理 (むり - impossible, too difficult) does not directly fit the structure 「～できるかどうか...無理だった」; if used here, it would be 「無理だと思った」.
default.q.n3-25-q22-22.why.2: (c) 退屈 (たいくつ): bored or having nothing to do; it does not fit the context of accepting an important assignment.
default.q.n3-25-q22-22.why.3: (d) 苦手 (にがて): poor at, not good at, not fond of; it commonly appears in「～が苦手だ」and does not connect logically with「～できるかどうか...苦手だった」.
default.q.n3-25-q23-23.verdict: The correct answer is 2. なるべく (as much as possible, as...as one can).
default.q.n3-25-q23-23.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "When you are busy or your schedule is inconvenient, please contact us as soon as possible."
- Important adverbs:
  + なるべく: as much as possible within one's ability (なるべく早く: as soon as possible).
  + ずいぶん (随分): quite, considerably (beyond the ordinary degree).
  + きっと: surely, certainly (used for an inference or expectation).
  + 早速 (さっそく): immediately, right away (indicating that an action is performed at once).
- Example: なるべく早く返信をいただけますと幸いです。(I would appreciate it if you could reply as soon as possible.)
default.q.n3-25-q23-23.why.0: (a) ずいぶん (随分) means “quite” or “very,” indicating a surprisingly high degree; it is not used to ask someone to do something “as quickly as possible.”
default.q.n3-25-q23-23.why.1: (b) なるべく (成るべく): as much as possible; it forms the phrase 「なるべく早く」 (“as soon as possible”) naturally and accurately with the request 「連絡してください」.
default.q.n3-25-q23-23.why.2: (c) きっと: certainly; used in statements of supposition or firm requests such as 「きっと来てください」, but it does not naturally combine as 「きっと早く連絡してください」.
default.q.n3-25-q23-23.why.3: (d) さっそく (早速): right away, immediately; it is used when the subject takes action promptly and is not combined as 「さっそく早く」when making a request.
default.q.n3-25-q24-24.verdict: The correct answer is 4. とじて (close one's eyes).
default.q.n3-25-q24-24.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: “During the entire meeting, Mr. Yamada kept closing his eyes, so I thought he was sleeping.”
- Vocabulary and expressions:
  + 目を閉じる (めをとじる): to close one’s eyes. (Opposite: 目を開ける, to open one’s eyes.)
  + 目を止める (めをとめる): to pay attention to, take notice of.
  + やめる: to quit, stop doing something.
  + 下げる (さげる): to lower something, such as one’s head.
- Example: 静かに目を閉じて音楽を聴いた。(I quietly closed my eyes and listened to music.)
default.q.n3-25-q24-24.why.0: (a) とめる (止める/留める): to stop, hold back; 「目を留める」 means to pay attention to or keep an eye on something, not to close one's eyes and sleep.
default.q.n3-25-q24-24.why.1: (b) やめる (辞める/止める): to quit, stop doing something; there is no expression「目をやめる」.
default.q.n3-25-q24-24.why.2: (c) さげる (下げる) means “lower” or “bow”; 「目をさげる」is not used for closing one’s eyes or sleeping.
default.q.n3-25-q24-24.why.3: (d) とじる (閉じる - to close): It is used for closing one's eyes or closing/folding a book; 「目を閉じる」 (“close one's eyes”) fits perfectly with 「寝ているのかと思った」 (“I thought [they] were sleeping”).
default.q.n3-25-q25-25.verdict: The correct answer is 3. たたんで (folding, folding up).
default.q.n3-25-q25-25.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “I carefully folded the sweater and put it away in a drawer.”
- Verbs and kanji:
  + 畳む (たたむ): fold, fold up (clothes, umbrellas, blankets, mats, etc.).
  + 締める (しめる): tighten (a tie, seat belt), screw tight (a bolt).
  + 曲げる (まげる): bend, curve (a metal bar, stick, etc.).
  + 結ぶ (むすぶ): tie, knot (shoelaces, rope, etc.).
- Example: 洗濯物をきれいにたたんで引き出しに入れた。(I folded the laundry neatly and put it in the drawer.)
default.q.n3-25-q25-25.why.0: (a) 締める (しめる) means to tie, fasten, tighten, or shut firmly, as with a tie or belt. It is not used for neatly folding a sweater for storage.
default.q.n3-25-q25-25.why.1: (b) 曲げる (まげる): to bend or curve a hard object or long item; it is not used for soft fabric clothing.
default.q.n3-25-q25-25.why.2: (c) たたむ (畳む — emphasis): to fold, fold up (clothes, fabric, umbrellas). It correctly combines with 「セーターをきちんとたたむ」 (fold the sweater neatly) before putting it in the drawer.
default.q.n3-25-q25-25.why.3: (d) 結ぶ (むすぶ: to tie, to knot) is used for shoelaces, hair, or string; it does not mean folding clothes.
default.q.n3-25-q26-26.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (大きさ) because the loanword 「サイズ」 (size) means dimensions or magnitude and is synonymous with 「大きさ」.
default.q.n3-25-q26-26.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "Is there a plate that is the same size as this one?"
- サイズ (size): size, dimensions = 大きさ (おおきさ).
- Sino-Japanese reading: 大 (だい).
- Example: この靴はサイズ（＝大きさ）がちょうどいい。(These shoes are just the right size.)
default.q.n3-25-q26-26.why.0: (a) 大きさ: size, dimensions. It is completely synonymous with and precisely replaces the loanword 「サイズ」 (size).
default.q.n3-25-q26-26.why.1: (b) 値段 (ねだん): price, cost. It is not synonymous with size.
default.q.n3-25-q26-26.why.2: (c) 色 (いろ): color. It is not synonymous with size.
default.q.n3-25-q26-26.why.3: (d) 形 (かたち): shape, form. It is not synonymous with size.
default.q.n3-25-q27-27.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (たのみましたか) because 「注文する」 (order food or goods) is synonymous with 「頼む」 (たのむ: order food or goods).
default.q.n3-25-q27-27.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: "Have you ordered the salad yet?"
- 注文する (ちゅうもんする): to order, to place an order = 頼む (たのむ).
- Example: レストランで料理を注文した（＝頼んだ）。(I ordered a dish at a restaurant.)
default.q.n3-25-q27-27.why.0: (a) 作りましたか means “Did you make or prepare it?” It is not synonymous with ordering a dish.
default.q.n3-25-q27-27.why.1: (b) たのみましたか (Lai - 頼みましたか): Have you ordered it? / Have you placed your order? It directly means the same as 「注文しましたか」 in a restaurant context.
default.q.n3-25-q27-27.why.2: (c) 食べましたか (たべましたか): Have you eaten? This is completely different in meaning from ordering food.
default.q.n3-25-q27-27.why.3: (d) はこびましたか (運びましたか) means “Did you carry/move/transport it?” It does not mean “Did you place an order?”
default.q.n3-25-q28-28.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (チェックして) because 「たしかめる」(to confirm, check again) is synonymous with the loanword 「チェックする」(to check).
default.q.n3-25-q28-28.explanation:
Meaning: “Sorry, could you check it one more time for me?”
- 確かめる (たしかめる): to check or make sure; equivalent to チェックする and 確認する.
- Example: 出かける前に鍵をかけたか確かめる（＝チェックする）。(I check whether I locked the door before going out.)
default.q.n3-25-q28-28.why.0: (a) コピーして (copy): to copy or photocopy a document. It does not mean to check or confirm.
default.q.n3-25-q28-28.why.1: (b) メモして (memo): to make a brief note or write something down. It does not mean to check or confirm.
default.q.n3-25-q28-28.why.2: (c) メールして means “send an email/message.” It does not mean “check.”
default.q.n3-25-q28-28.why.3: (d) チェックして (check): to check, review. It is a direct synonym of 「確かめて」(たしかめて: to confirm, check again).
default.q.n3-25-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (さいきん) because 「このごろ」(these days, recently) is synonymous with 「さいきん」(最近 - recently).
default.q.n3-25-q29-29.explanation:
Sentence: "Yamada-san looks busy these days, doesn't he/she?"
- このごろ (この頃): these days, recently = 最近 (さいきん: recently).
- Note: Both 「このごろ」 and 「最近」 refer to the recent past and are commonly used to describe a current condition or trend.
- Example: このごろ（＝最近）寒くなってきましたね。(It has been getting cold lately, hasn't it?)
default.q.n3-25-q29-29.why.0: (a) ずっと: all the time, continuously, or much more; it expresses continuous duration or a clearly greater degree, and is not synonymous with “recently.”
default.q.n3-25-q29-29.why.1: (b) いつも: always, all the time. It indicates a constant habit or frequency and is not synonymous with “these days.”
default.q.n3-25-q29-29.why.2: (c) まだ: still, not yet. It indicates an incomplete or ongoing state, not a recent time period.
default.q.n3-25-q29-29.why.3: (d) さいきん (最近): “recently” or “these days.” It is exactly synonymous with 「このごろ」.
default.q.n3-25-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (話して) because 「しゃべる」(to talk) is synonymous with 「話す」(はなす: to talk).
default.q.n3-25-q30-30.explanation:
Meaning: “All I have seen that child do up to now is talk nonstop.”
- しゃべる: to talk, speak, chat = 話す (はなす — to speak).
- Grammar: ～ばかりいる (to do nothing but ~; to keep ~ing).
- Example: 彼は授業中ずっとしゃべって（＝話して）いる。(He keeps talking throughout class.)
default.q.n3-25-q30-30.why.0: (a) 騒いで (さわいで): to make noise, to cause a commotion. It implies disorderly or noisy behavior and is not synonymous with simply talking, 「しゃべる」.
default.q.n3-25-q30-30.why.1: (b) 話して ( - はなして): to speak, to talk. A direct synonym of 「しゃべって」 (しゃべる: to talk, to chatter).
default.q.n3-25-q30-30.why.2: (c) 答えて (こたえて): answer, respond. It refers to responding to a question, not to speaking in general.
default.q.n3-25-q30-30.why.3: (d) 遊んで (あそんで) means “play,” so it differs in meaning from “talk.”
default.q.n3-25-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 3: ここに新しい空港が建設される予定です。
default.q.n3-25-q31-31.explanation:
「建設（けんせつ）」means "construction" and is used for large-scale buildings, infrastructure, or projects, such as buildings, airports, dams, expressways, and bridges. For small objects, use 「作る/組み立てる」; for installing equipment or furniture, use 「設置する」; and for building ships, use 「造る/造船する」。
Example: 市の郊外に新しい高速道路を建設している。(A new expressway is being constructed in the suburbs of the city.)
default.q.n3-25-q31-31.why.0: 本棚 is ordinary furniture, so use 作った or 組み立てた, not 建設, which is used for large-scale structures.
default.q.n3-25-q31-31.why.1: A ベンチ (bench) is a small outdoor amenity, so 「設置された」 (installed) or 「置かれた」 (placed) should be used instead of 建設.
default.q.n3-25-q31-31.why.2: 建設 (けんせつ, construction) is used for large-scale infrastructure, and combines correctly with 空港 (airport): 空港が建設される (an airport is constructed).
default.q.n3-25-q31-31.why.3: A ship (船) is a means of transportation, so building or manufacturing ships is expressed with 造っている (or 製造している / 作っている), not 建設.
default.q.n3-25-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 専門学校でいろいろな技術を身につけて、いい会社に入りたい。
default.q.n3-25-q32-32.explanation:
「身につける（みにつける）」has two main meanings:
1. To wear or put an object (jewelry, clothing, or an accessory) on one’s body.
2. To acquire, develop, or master knowledge or skills (such as 「技術」「知識」「習慣」).
Example: 留学を通して、実用的な英会話力を身につけた。(Through studying abroad, I acquired practical English conversation skills.)
default.q.n3-25-q32-32.why.0: 希望 (hope, aspiration) is used with verbs such as 持つ or 抱く (希望を持っている: to have hope), not 身につける.
default.q.n3-25-q32-32.why.1: 尊敬 (respect) combines with verbs such as 集める (尊敬を集めた: earned respect) or 得る; it does not combine with 身につける.
default.q.n3-25-q32-32.why.2: 身につける means to acquire, develop, and master a skill or knowledge, and it combines naturally with 技術 (technique, skill): 技術を身につける.
default.q.n3-25-q32-32.why.3: 顔と名前 (one's face and name) takes 覚える (to memorize, remember), not 身につける.
default.q.n3-25-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 1: この二つの洗剤を混ぜると危険なガスが発生するので、気をつけてください。
default.q.n3-25-q33-33.explanation:
「発生（はっせい）」means "to occur, arise, or be generated." It is used when phenomena, accidents, problems, natural disasters, gases, bacteria, insects, and similar things appear or arise, as in ガス/煙が発生する, 事故/事件が発生する, and 台風/地震が発生する. It is not used for people graduating from a school (use 「輩出」), newly opened stores (use 「できる/開店する」), or flowers blooming (use 「咲く」).
Example: 大雨の影響で各地で土砂崩れが発生した。(Because of the heavy rain, landslides occurred in many places.)
default.q.n3-25-q33-33.why.0: 発生する (to arise, be generated) is correctly used for gases, phenomena, or incidents produced by a reaction or event; here, ガスが発生する (gas is generated) is a perfectly natural collocation.
default.q.n3-25-q33-33.why.1: For researchers who graduated from a university, 輩出している (produce or turn out talented people), 出ている, or 育っている should be used; 発生 is not appropriate.
default.q.n3-25-q33-33.why.2: For a store opening or appearing, use できた (or 開店した / 増えた), not 発生.
default.q.n3-25-q33-33.why.3: For a flower growing or blooming on a plant, use 咲きます (to bloom) or つきます, not 発生.
default.q.n3-25-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 2: ロープを強くにぎっていたせいで、手が赤くなってしまった。
default.q.n3-25-q34-34.explanation:
「握る（にぎる）」means "grasp, grip, squeeze, or mold by hand" (as with rice), describing the action of enclosing or tightly holding something with the whole hand and fingers. Examples include 手/ロープ/ハンドルを握る, おにぎりを握る, and 秘密/弱みを握る. It is not used for tying a cord (use 「結ぶ/しばる」), picking something up with chopsticks (use 「つかむ/はさむ」), or fastening paper with a staple (use 「留める/とめる」).
Example: 彼は緊張のあまり、マイクを強く握りしめていた。(He was so nervous that he was gripping the microphone tightly.)
default.q.n3-25-q34-34.why.0: When tying a bag with rope or cord, use 結んで (tie) or しばって, not にぎる.
default.q.n3-25-q34-34.why.1: にぎる (to grasp tightly) describes using one’s hand to hold an object firmly. In this case, ロープをにぎる (“to grasp the rope tightly”) is completely correct.
default.q.n3-25-q34-34.why.2: For picking up food with chopsticks, use つかみにくい (difficult to pick up) or はさみにくい, not にぎる (to grasp in one’s hand).
default.q.n3-25-q34-34.why.3: When using a clip to hold documents together, use とめた (clipped/secured), not にぎった (gripped).
default.q.n3-25-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 朝から熱があって体がだるかったので、会社を休みました。
default.q.n3-25-q35-35.explanation:
「だるい（怠い）」is an i-adjective meaning “sluggish, tired, exhausted, or heavy,” describing a physical sensation or the feeling in one's limbs when ill, feverish, sleep-deprived, or overexerted. It commonly occurs in expressions such as 「体がだるい」「足がだるい」「手足がだるい」. It is not used to describe regret or disappointment (use 「残念/がっかり」), the weather (use 「曇っている」), or a stuffy room or oppressive atmosphere (use 「息苦しい/蒸し暑い」).
Example: 昨日の長距離マラソンのせいで、今日は全身がだるい。(Because of yesterday's long-distance marathon, my whole body feels exhausted today.)

default.q.n3-26-q51-51.explanation:
Complete sentence:
川名寺は桜がきれいなことで有名ですが、桜だけでなく秋の景色もすばらしいです。

Meaning:
Kawana Temple is famous for its beautiful cherry blossoms, but not only the cherry blossoms—the autumn scenery is also wonderful.
default.q.n3-26-q51-51.why.0: (a) Fragment 1 (桜だけでなく) occupies the fourth position, following the contrastive conjunction 「有名ですが」 to form 「AだけでなくBも」 (not only A but also B), which connects to 「秋の景色もすばらしいです」.
default.q.n3-26-q51-51.why.1: (b) Fragment 2 (ことで) occupies the second position. Following the adjective 「きれいな」, it nominalizes the clause and indicates the cause or reason in the pattern 「～ことで有名」 (famous for/because of...).
default.q.n3-26-q51-51.why.2: (c) Fragment 3 (有名ですが) appears in third place (the ★ position), completing 「～ことで有名ですが」(famous for..., but...) and transitioning to the next idea.
default.q.n3-26-q51-51.why.3: (d) Fragment 4 (きれいな) comes first immediately after 「桜が」, modifying it to form 「桜がきれいな」 before 「ことで」.
default.q.n3-26-q52-52.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 4 → 1 → 2. The star ★ marks answer choice 1 (チャレンジして).
default.q.n3-26-q52-52.explanation:
Complete sentence:
父はいつも、「何もしないでいるよりチャレンジして失敗するほうがいい。」と言っている。

Meaning:
My father always says, "It is better to challenge yourself and fail than to sit around doing nothing."
default.q.n3-26-q52-52.why.0: (a) Fragment 1 (チャレンジして) goes in the third position (the ★ position); it is the first action in the sequence 「チャレンジして失敗する」 after the comparison clause 「～より」.
default.q.n3-26-q52-52.why.1: (b) Fragment 2 (失敗する) belongs in position 4 and combines with 「ほうがいい」that follows to form the pattern 「～ほうがいい」, meaning “it is better to...”.
default.q.n3-26-q52-52.why.2: (c) Fragment 3 (しないで) comes first, directly after「何も」, forming the negative phrase「何もしないで」(without doing anything).
default.q.n3-26-q52-52.why.3: (d) Fragment 4 (いるより) comes second and follows 「しないで」, forming the state-maintaining pattern 「～ないでいる」together with the comparative particle 「より」(compared with continuing to do nothing).
default.q.n3-26-q53-53.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 1 → 4 → 3. The star ★ position is answer choice 4 (まで).
default.q.n3-26-q53-53.explanation:
Complete dialogue:
「ねえ、来近の日曜日、北町の美術館に行かない?」
B「いいね。あ、私、そこの割引券を持ってるよ。その割引券一枚で三人まで二割引になるんだ。」

Meaning:
A: “Hey, do you want to go to the Kitamachi Museum of Art next Sunday?”
B: “Sounds good. Oh, I have a discount coupon for that place. With just one coupon, up to three people can get 20% off.”
default.q.n3-26-q53-53.why.0: (a) Fragment 1 (三人) belongs in position 2. It follows the means phrase 「その割引券一枚で」and combines with 「まで」to indicate the maximum number of people who can receive the discount.
default.q.n3-26-q53-53.why.1: (b) Fragment 2 (割引券一枚で) occupies position 1 immediately after the demonstrative 「その」, forming 「その割引券一枚で」 (“with just that one discount coupon”).
default.q.n3-26-q53-53.why.2: (c) Fragment 3 (二割引) comes fourth, before 「になるんだ」, forming the predicate 「二割引になるんだ」 (“become 20% off / be discounted by 20%”).
default.q.n3-26-q53-53.why.3: (d) Part 4 (まで) occupies the third position (★), immediately following the numeral 「三人」 to form 「三人まで」, expressing the maximum limit: “up to three people.”
default.q.n3-26-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 4. それ.
default.q.n3-26-q54-54.explanation: Before the blank, the author describes two things that surprised them: the toilet lid opened automatically (自動的にトイレのふたが開いて、びっくりしました) and the seat was warm (座るところが温かかったので、またびっくりしました). Next, the author adds that when they stood up, the water flushed automatically and the lid closed by itself. Therefore, 「びっくりしたのはそれだけではありません」(Those were not the only things that surprised me) uses the demonstrative pronoun 「それ」 to refer to the surprising things already mentioned, leading into the next surprise.
default.q.n3-26-q54-54.why.0: (a) 「水」 (water): The meaning does not fit because the author is talking about unexpected events, not comparing water with other things.
default.q.n3-26-q54-54.why.1: (b) 「トイレ」 (“restroom/toilet”): Inappropriate because the story concerns the features of restrooms, not a comparison between a restroom and another place.
default.q.n3-26-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「その家」 (“that house”): It does not fit the context because what causes surprise is the toilet’s features, not the entire house.
default.q.n3-26-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「それ」 (that / those things): Exactly correct. The demonstrative 「それ」 refers to the unexpected features listed earlier, such as the automatically opening lid and the heated seat, forming the familiar expression 「それだけではありません」 (That is not all / It does not stop there).
default.q.n3-26-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 思いました.
default.q.n3-26-q55-55.explanation: The passage begins by recounting a past experience (冬休みにホームステイをした家でトイレを使ったときのことです). When the author used the toilet at that time, they wondered whether it was really necessary to be that way (思いました). Later, after hearing the elderly woman’s explanation, their opinion changed (考えが変わりました). Therefore, the simple past form 「思いました」 is the most appropriate.
default.q.n3-26-q55-55.why.0: (a) 「思っています」 describes an ongoing state of thought continuing into the present, which conflicts with the author having changed their mind immediately afterward (考えが変わりました).
default.q.n3-26-q55-55.why.1: (b) 「思いました」is correct because the story recounts a thought held at the time of an event in the past.
default.q.n3-26-q55-55.why.2: (c) 「思ったところです」expresses an action that has just occurred at the present moment; it is not used to narrate a sequence of past events.
default.q.n3-26-q55-55.why.3: (d) 「思います」 expresses a thought in the present, so it does not fit a narrative describing a past experience.
default.q.n3-26-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 座れるのだそうです.
default.q.n3-26-q56-56.explanation: The passage quotes the grandmother in the homestay family (おばあさんは... と言っていました). She explains that suddenly sitting on a cold seat is bad for one’s health, whereas if the seat is warm, “it is said that one can sit down without worry” (安心して座れるのだそうです). The verb should be in the potential form 「座れる」, and the quoted-speech ending should be 「〜のだそうです」 to match the grandmother’s reported statement.
default.q.n3-26-q56-56.why.0: (a) 「座ってしまうからです」: The structure 「〜てしまう」 (“accidentally” or “completely”) does not fit this reassuring context, and the form used to report the old woman’s words is missing.
default.q.n3-26-q56-56.why.1: (b) 「座るからです」: It lacks the potential form (座れる) and the sentence ending used to convey indirect information (〜そうだ) in this context.
default.q.n3-26-q56-56.why.2: (c) 「座れることだそうです」 uses 「ことだそうです」 to mean “I hear that it is the matter of being able to sit,” creating an awkward and unnatural sentence for expressing relief about being able to sit.
default.q.n3-26-q56-56.why.3: (d) 「座れるのだそうです」uses the potential form 「座れる」(can sit) together with the explanatory and hearsay pattern 「〜のだそうです」(“I hear that...”), accurately conveying the old woman’s explanation.
default.q.n3-26-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 3. しかし.
default.q.n3-26-q57-57.explanation: In the preceding sentence, the author talks about himself: "Even if the seat is cold, I do not mind, and opening and closing the lid is not difficult either" (私は、座るところが冷たくても気にならないし、ふたの開閉も大変ではありません). The following sentence talks about elderly people: "...for older people, it is probably not a simple matter" (お年寄りには簡単なことではないでしょう). This is a contrastive relationship between the two clauses, so the contrastive conjunction 「しかし」(However / But) is required.
default.q.n3-26-q57-57.why.0: (a) 「なぜなら」 is used to explain the cause or reason for the preceding sentence, so it is inappropriate because the following sentence is not the reason for the preceding one.
default.q.n3-26-q57-57.why.1: (b) 「ちなみに」 is used to add incidental or supplementary information, so it does not express a contrast between two subjects.
default.q.n3-26-q57-57.why.2: (c) 「しかし」: A conjunction indicating a clear contrast or opposition between the young person (the author) and the elderly person.
default.q.n3-26-q57-57.why.3: (d) 「また」is used to add information in the same direction, so it does not fit a contrastive context.
default.q.n3-26-q58-58.explanation: The verb at the end of the sentence is the passive form 「作られた」(was made / was manufactured). In a direct passive sentence involving an object, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence and takes 「が」: [object] が + [passive verb] (こういうトイレが作られた = toilets like this were made). Therefore, the particle to fill in is 「が」.
default.q.n3-26-q58-58.why.0: (a) 「が」: Used with the subject 「こういうトイレ」 to mark what is affected in the passive sentence 「作られた」 (was made/created); it is completely correct.
default.q.n3-26-q58-58.why.1: (b) 「に」usually marks the agent performing an action in a passive sentence or indicates direction. It is not used as the particle marking the thing created in this position.
default.q.n3-26-q58-58.why.2: (c) 「で」usually indicates a place, means, or material; it cannot serve as the subject marker of the passive in this sentence.
default.q.n3-26-q58-58.why.3: (d) 「から」indicates a starting point or original material, so it does not form a natural sentence structure in this position.
default.q.n3-26-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: Confirm the meeting schedule and make contact when the sample component arrives.
default.q.n3-26-q59-59.explanation:
- Main point summary: In an email, Noguchi informs Yamada about a meeting to discuss components for a new product, scheduled for December 11, and asks Yamada to confirm the meeting schedule (ご確認ください). Noguchi also says that component samples have been sent by mail and asks Yamada to let them know when they arrive (届きましたらお知らせください). Therefore, Yamada needs to confirm the meeting schedule and notify Noguchi when the component samples arrive.
- Translation of the question: After reading this email, what does Yamada need to do?
- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. Confirm the meeting schedule and contact Noguchi when the new product arrives.
  2. Confirm the meeting schedule and contact Noguchi when the component samples arrive.
  3. Confirm what was decided at the meeting and contact Noguchi when the new product arrives.
  4. Confirm what was decided at the meeting and contact Noguchi when the component samples arrive.
default.q.n3-26-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the sender asks to be notified when the component sample (部品のサンプル) arrives, not when the new product (新製品) arrives.
default.q.n3-26-q59-59.why.1: (b) Correct. Evidence from the email includes:「新製品に使用する部品についての会議日程が、以下のように決まりました。ご確認ください。」(requesting confirmation of the meeting schedule) and「なお、部品のサンブルを郵送しましたので、届きましたらお知らせください。」(requesting notification when the component samples arrive).
default.q.n3-26-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the meeting has not yet taken place (it is scheduled for December 11), so this is not confirmation of content decided at the meeting (会議で決まった内容). In addition, what was sent was a component sample, not a new product (新製品).
default.q.n3-26-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the meeting has not yet taken place, so Yamada needs to confirm the schedule for the upcoming meeting (会議日程), not the content decided at the meeting (会議で決まった内容).
default.q.n3-26-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Midori Park has a large lawn, and many people visit on holidays.
default.q.n3-26-q60-60.explanation:
- Main point: The passage introduces Midori Park in Maruyama City. It is the largest park in the city, with more than half of its area covered by lawns and many famous cherry trees for hanami. The park has two ponds, one large and one small, as well as many long-established native plants. Although it is in the city center, the park is very quiet and offers the relaxing feeling of a picnic in the suburbs, so it attracts many visitors on holidays.

- Question translation: What can we understand about Midori Park from this passage?
- Answer choices:
  1. It has a large lawn and attracts many visitors on holidays.
  2. It has two large ponds and two small ponds.
  3. It collects rare trees and grasses that are seldom found in Maruyama City.
  4. It is located in the suburbs and people can have picnics there.
default.q.n3-26-q60-60.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage explicitly states 「公園の半分以上が芝生になっていて」 (more than half of the park is covered with grass, equivalent to 広い芝生) and 「休日には多くの人びとが公岡（公園）に来る」 (many people come to the park on holidays, equivalent to 休日には大勢の人が来る).
default.q.n3-26-q60-60.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage says 「大小の二つの池があり」, meaning there are only two ponds in total—one large and one small—not two of each type (二つずつ).
default.q.n3-26-q60-60.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage says 「この土地に昔からある木や草が植えられている」(trees and plants that have existed in this area since long ago are planted), which is the opposite of gathering rare plants from Maruyama City.
default.q.n3-26-q60-60.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage says 「市の中心部にあるのに静かで、郊外へピクニックに出かけたような気分になれる」 (although it is in the city center, it is quiet and makes one feel as if one had gone on a picnic to the suburbs). Therefore, the park is in the city center, not in the suburbs (郊外にあって).
default.q.n3-26-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (一つのことばは、さまざまな内容を持っている) because the passage states that the same utterance or word can contain different content and meanings depending on the situation.
default.q.n3-26-q61-61.explanation:
* Main point: The author bought the most popular electric-train toy as a gift for a niece or nephew because the child had once said, “I like electric trains,” but the child was not very happy because the gift was not the type of electric train they liked. The author then realized that although people may all say “I like electric trains,” some like only a particular type, some like watching trains run, and some like every kind of train. This shows that the same expression or word can have many different connotations and meanings.

* Question translation:
The passage says, “The meaning expressed by words is not limited to just one.” What does this mean?

* Answer choices:
1. A word can express only one thing.
2. A word can convey many different meanings.
3. There are many different ways to express what one wants to communicate.
4. Many different words are needed to communicate what one wants to say.
default.q.n3-26-q61-61.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is completely contrary to the passage’s claim: 「一つのことしか表せない」 means “can express only one thing,” whereas the passage says 「ことばが表す意味は一つではない」, “the meaning expressed by words is not limited to one.”
default.q.n3-26-q61-61.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct, as supported by the passage: 「電車が好き」と言っても、ある決まった電車だけが好きだという子や、走っている電車を見るのが好きだという子もいる。もちろん、電車なら何でもいい子もいる。「電車が好き」にも、いろいろある。ことばが表す意味は一つではないのだ。 (The same statement, "I like trains," can have many different meanings or implications.)
default.q.n3-26-q61-61.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the passage analyzes how "the same word or expression can have several different meanings," not how "different expressions can be used to convey the same content."
default.q.n3-26-q61-61.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage never mentions needing many words to convey what one wants to say.
default.q.n3-26-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Taking the express train from Tagawa Station to Muraguchi Station will get you there 5 minutes earlier than before.
default.q.n3-26-q62-62.explanation:
**Main point of the passage:**
An announcement from Nanzan Railway about changes to the Tamura Line schedule beginning January 5, 2013, with three specific changes:
1. The first train departing from Tagawa Station will leave 15 minutes earlier, at 5:30 a.m.
2. On weekdays, the number of express trains (急行) will increase between 7:00 and 9:00 a.m., departing every 10 minutes between Tagawa Station and Muraguchi Station.
3. Travel time between Tagawa Station and Muraguchi Station will be reduced: express trains by 5 minutes and local trains stopping at every station by 3 minutes.

**Translation of the question and choices:**
- **Question:** What can be learned from this announcement about the new schedule of the Tamura Line?
- **Choice 1:** The first train leaves Tagawa Station at 5:15 a.m.
- **Choice 2:** On weekdays, express trains run every 10 minutes from the first train to the last train.
- **Choice 3:** If you take an express train from Tagawa Station to Muraguchi Station, you will arrive 5 minutes earlier than before.
- **Choice 4:** Beginning February 1, the Tamura Line schedule will change and become more convenient than before.
default.q.n3-26-q62-62.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage says 「始発電車の発車が15分早くなり 午前5時30分になります」, meaning the first train departs 15 minutes earlier, at 5:30 a.m. (previously 5:45), not at 5:15 a.m.
default.q.n3-26-q62-62.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage clearly states: 「平日午前7時から9時の間の急行の数が増え、田川駅と村口駅を10分間隔で発車します」, meaning that express trains run at 10-minute intervals only between 7:00 and 9:00 a.m. on weekdays, not from the first train to the last train (始発から終電まで).
default.q.n3-26-q62-62.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: 「田川駅と村口駅の間の乗車時間は、これまでより、急行は5分、各駅停車は3分短くなります。」 (Travel time between Tagawa Station and Muraguchi Station will be reduced by 5 minutes for express trains compared with before), meaning that taking an express train will get you there 5 minutes earlier than before.
default.q.n3-26-q62-62.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The new timetable takes effect on January 5, 2013 (「2013年1月5日から、田村線...のダイヤが新しくなります」), not February 1 (2月1日).
default.q.n3-26-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The author wants to return to the hotel to rest because they are exhausted after skiing.
default.q.n3-26-q63-63.explanation:
- **Main idea**: The author was skiing for the first time and was exhausted by the afternoon of the first day. Therefore, the author decided to return to the hotel alone ahead of the others to rest and wait for the friends.
- **Question translation**: It says that the author "returned to the hotel alone ahead of the others." Why?
- **Answer choices**:
  1. Because the author wanted to rest at the hotel.
  2. Because the friends were waiting at the hotel.
  3. Because the author wanted to walk alone in the snowy mountains.
  4. Because the author had already planned to listen to an explanation about the snowy mountains.
default.q.n3-26-q63-63.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage states: 「私はスキーが初めてだったので、1日目の午後には疲れてしまった。そこで、私は一人で①先にホテルに戻って、友達を待つことにした。」 (Because it was my first time skiing, I was exhausted by the afternoon of the first day. So I decided to return to the hotel alone ahead of my friends and wait for them.)
default.q.n3-26-q63-63.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage says that the author went to the hotel first to wait for a friend (友達を待つことにした), not that the friends were already waiting at the hotel.
default.q.n3-26-q63-63.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The author sees the poster and learns about the snow-mountain walking tour only after returning to the hotel (ホテルに戻ると、ロビーに...).
default.q.n3-26-q63-63.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author returned to the hotel because they were tired, then happened to notice the poster and asked the front desk staff about it; they had not planned to receive an explanation in advance.
default.q.n3-26-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The clothes and gloves are for skiing, while the shoes are waterproof boots, not ski boots.
default.q.n3-26-q64-64.explanation:
- Main idea: The receptionist explains that people walking on a snowy mountain should wear ski clothing and gloves, and waterproof boots that keep snow out. They should not wear ski boots because they are difficult to walk in.

  1. Ski clothing and gloves, with ski boots that keep snow and water out.
  2. Ski clothing and gloves, with boots that keep snow and water out but are not ski boots.
  3. Everyday clothing and gloves, with ski boots that keep snow and water out.
  4. Everyday clothing and gloves, with boots that keep snow and water out but are not ski boots.
default.q.n3-26-q64-64.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage clearly states that ski boots are not used because they are difficult to walk in: 「スキー用のブーツは歩きにくいので、だめだそうだ」.
default.q.n3-26-q64-64.why.1: (b) Correct. default.q.n3-26-q64-64.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The clothing and gloves must be for skiing (スキー用), not for everyday use (日常用), and ski boots may not be worn for walking.
default.q.n3-26-q64-64.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The clothes and gloves must be specialized for skiing (スキー用の服と手袋), not ordinary everyday items.
default.q.n3-26-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Although the author could not ski very much, they fully enjoyed walking around and exploring the snowy mountains.
default.q.n3-26-q65-65.explanation:
- Main point: Although the author did not get to ski much and did not improve, walking through the snowy mountains with a guide, enjoying the beautiful natural scenery and animal tracks, provided an unexpectedly enjoyable experience, making the author feel that coming back again would be wonderful.

- Answer choices:
  1. Because the author could not only enjoy skiing but also see animals in the snowy mountains.
  2. Although the author did not get to enjoy skiing much, they were able to see animals in the snowy mountains.
  3. Because the author not only improved at skiing but also enjoyed walking through the snowy mountains.
  4. Although the author did not get to ski much, they were able to enjoy walking through the snowy mountains.
default.q.n3-26-q65-65.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The author was not able to ski much (あまり滑れなかった) and only saw tracks or feeding marks, not the animal itself.
default.q.n3-26-q65-65.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage only mentions seeing animal footprints and traces of feeding (動物の足跡や、えさを食べた跡なども見つけた); the author did not directly see the animals.
default.q.n3-26-q65-65.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The author clearly states that their skiing did not improve because they were unable to ski much (スキーは上手にならなかった).
default.q.n3-26-q65-65.why.3: (d) Correct. Evidence from the passage: 「今回はあまり滑れなかったので、スキーは上手にならなかったが、ほかにこんな楽しみがあるなら、②また来てもいいと思った。」 (Although I did not become better at skiing because I did not ski much this time, I thought I would be willing to come again if there were another enjoyable activity like this [walking in the snowy mountains]).
default.q.n3-26-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3: The person opens their wallet and buys the item because its low price makes them happy and eager to purchase it.
default.q.n3-26-q66-66.explanation:
Main point:
The author observes that many people who complain that they cannot keep their rooms tidy actually have a shopping habit: whenever they see a sale sign, they eagerly enter the store, and when they see something cheap, they open their wallets and buy it immediately without considering whether they need it. As a result, their rooms become filled with possessions.

Question translation:
There is the expression “①財布を開く” (to open one’s wallet / spend money to buy something). Why do they do this?

Answer choices:
1. Because there is still room to store things in the room.
2. Because they feel awkward entering a store and leaving without buying anything.
3. Because the low price makes them happy and want to buy it.
4. Because they think it is definitely something they need.
default.q.n3-26-q66-66.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage does not mention buying something because there was space left in the room; instead, the result was that the room became overcrowded with excess belongings.
default.q.n3-26-q66-66.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the passage does not mention feeling guilty or embarrassed about leaving the shop without buying anything.
default.q.n3-26-q66-66.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct, as directly quoted from the passage: 「「セール」や「割引」の看板を見つけると、喜んで、つい店に入ってしまう。そして、安くなっているのを見ると、それが必要かどうか深く考えず、①財布を開く。」 (When people see a "Sale" or "Discount" sign, they are delighted and end up entering the store. Then, when they see that something is cheaper, they open their wallets without thinking carefully about whether they need it).
default.q.n3-26-q66-66.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the author says they “did not think deeply about whether it was necessary” (それが必要かどうか深く考えず), not that they were certain it was necessary.
default.q.n3-26-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3: The advice is to think carefully about whether the item is necessary, whether one already has something similar, and whether there is room to store it.
default.q.n3-26-q67-67.explanation:
Summary:
The author offers three steps to consider before deciding to buy something:
1. Think about whether the item is truly necessary.
2. If it is necessary, consider whether you already have something similar.
3. If you do not, consider whether you have a place to store it at home. If you have nowhere to put it, give up on buying it. Only buy it if, after considering all of this carefully, you still feel that it is necessary.

Question translation:
Which of the following is appropriate regarding 「②アドバイス」 (the advice) about shopping?

Answer choices:
1. If you have a place to store it, buy it even if you already own something similar.
2. If you think the item is necessary, buy it immediately without considering anything else.
3. Carefully consider whether you need it, whether you already have something similar, and whether you have a place to store it.
4. Carefully consider whether you already have something similar, whether you have a place to store it, and whether it is genuinely inexpensive.
default.q.n3-26-q67-67.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because, according to the passage, only when there is no similar item (持っていなければ) should one consider whether there is space to store it; it does not mean buying another item despite already having a similar one.
default.q.n3-26-q67-67.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is incorrect because even after deciding that the item is necessary, the buyer must consider two more factors (whether they already own something similar and whether they have room to store it), rather than buying it immediately without further thought.
default.q.n3-26-q67-67.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because it fully quotes the three pieces of advice in the passage: 「買う前に、まず、必要かどうかを考える。必要だと思ったら、次に、同じような物を持っていないかどうかを考える。持っていなければ、最後に、それをしまう場所があるかどうかを考える。場所がなければ、あきらめる。そこまで考えて、必要だったら、買えばいい。」
default.q.n3-26-q67-67.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the criterion "whether it is really cheap" (本当に安いか) is not part of the author's advice. The author recommends considering necessity, duplication, and storage space.
default.q.n3-26-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4: People troubled by cleaning their rooms should be careful about the upcoming sales.
default.q.n3-26-q68-68.explanation:
Main point:
The author concludes that if people keep buying unnecessary items or things they have nowhere to store simply because they are cheap, a cluttered room is inevitable. With sales season about to begin at many department stores, the author warns people who are struggling to tidy their rooms to exercise restraint.

Question translation:
Which option is most appropriate for filling in the blank ( 　)?

Answer choices:
1. People who are bad at cleaning their rooms should enjoy shopping too.
2. People who like shopping should check the prices carefully before buying.
3. People who want to buy cheap items should hurry to the stores.
4. People who are struggling to clean their rooms should be careful.
default.q.n3-26-q68-68.why.0: (a) Answer choice 1 is incorrect because the passage advises people who are bad at tidying to be careful and restrained when shopping, rather than encouraging them to enjoy shopping.
default.q.n3-26-q68-68.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is incorrect because the article is intended to help people who are poor at tidying think about its necessity and where to store things, not to advise people who like shopping to compare prices.
default.q.n3-26-q68-68.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because it completely contradicts the author's warning not to buy things indiscriminately just because they are cheap.
default.q.n3-26-q68-68.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct based on the concluding logic: 「安いからといって、必要のない物やしまう場所のない物を次々と買えば、部屋が片付かないのは当然だ。 もうすぐ、あちこちのデパートでセールが始まるが、（部屋の整理に悩んでいる人は、気をつけよう）。」 The author warns people who are struggling to organize their rooms to be careful when facing upcoming department-store sales.
default.q.n3-26-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 棚を重ねて使って育てるから (Because they are grown by stacking multiple shelves on top of one another).
default.q.n3-26-q69-69.explanation:
- Main point of the passage: The author explains that at a vegetable factory, many shelves are stacked in multiple levels from top to bottom, with vegetables grown on each shelf. As a result, the factory can produce more vegetables on the same floor area than can be grown in an ordinary field.
- Question translation: The passage says that "many vegetables can be produced." Why is that?
- Answer choices:
  1. Because the shelves are stacked on top of one another for growing the vegetables.
  2. Because electric light is used for growing them.
  3. Because they are grown in a large area.
  4. Because they are grown inside a building.
default.q.n3-26-q69-69.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage states: 「屋内に上下に何段も棚を重ねて作り、そこで野菜を育てます。それぞれの棚で野菜が作れるので、同じ広さの場所でも畑より①多くの野菜を生産することができます。」 (By stacking many shelves vertically and growing vegetables on each shelf, more vegetables can be produced in the same amount of space than in a field.)
default.q.n3-26-q69-69.why.1: (b) Incorrect because using electric light (電気の光) helps plants photosynthesize indoors; it does not explain why more vegetables can be produced in the same area than in a field.
default.q.n3-26-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage clearly states “even in places of the same area” (同じ広さの場所でも), not “because the growing area is large” (広い場所).
default.q.n3-26-q69-69.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Growing plants indoors (建物の中) is merely the location or environment. The factor that produces a much higher yield per unit of area is making use of vertical space by stacking multiple shelves (棚を重ねて).
default.q.n3-26-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 野菜がよく育つように、エアコンで適当な温度にする。 (To help the vegetables grow well, set the temperature appropriately using the air conditioner.)
default.q.n3-26-q70-70.explanation:
- Main point: The passage gives the example of people creating a growing environment for vegetables by actively controlling temperature, humidity, and lighting duration. This allows the vegetables to grow well without depending on the natural weather outside; for example, summer vegetables can be grown even in winter.
- Question translation: The passage says that "people can also create an environment." What is an example of how they do this?
- Answer choices:
  1. Using air conditioning to adjust the temperature so that the vegetables grow well.
  2. Designing the height of the shelves so that insects do not eat the vegetables.
  3. Arranging the shelves so that sunlight shines effectively on the vegetables.
  4. Keeping the temperature constant so that the vegetable growers can work more easily.
default.q.n3-26-q70-70.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage states: 「例えば、工場では温度や湿度、野菜が光を浴びる時間も決められるので、外の天気に影響されずに野菜が育ちます。」, and paragraph 4 mentions using air conditioning: 「電気やエアコンを長時間つけておく必要があるので」. Adjusting the temperature with air conditioning so that vegetables grow well is a representative example of humans creating an artificial living environment for vegetables.
default.q.n3-26-q70-70.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Insect prevention is achieved through the enclosed factory, where insects are unlikely to enter (工場は虫などが入りにくい). The shelf height (棚の高さ) is adjusted so that workers can work comfortably without back pain (仕事がしやすい高さ).
default.q.n3-26-q70-70.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The factory grows vegetables using electric light (電気の光で野菜を育てる), not sunlight (太陽の光).
default.q.n3-26-q70-70.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Adjusting the temperature and environment is intended to support the vegetables' growth, allowing summer vegetables to be grown outdoors even in the cold winter. It is not intended to make the growers' work easier.
default.q.n3-26-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 安心して食べられるが、作るのにお金がかかる。 (It can be eaten with peace of mind, but it costs money to produce.)
default.q.n3-26-q71-71.explanation:
- Main point: The author points out both the advantages and disadvantages of factory-grown vegetables: the advantage is that no pesticides are needed, making them safe to eat, but the major disadvantage is the high cost of building the factory and paying for the electricity needed for air conditioning and lighting.
- Question translation: What does the author say about factory-grown vegetables?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. They are cheaper to grow than field crops but contain fewer nutrients.
  2. They can be grown regardless of the season, but not many can be grown at one time.
  3. They can be eaten with confidence, but they are expensive to produce.
  4. There are many varieties, but they do not taste very good.
default.q.n3-26-q71-71.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage says that factory-grown vegetables require substantial construction costs and electricity costs (建設費がかかります、電気代もかかります), so they are not cheaper than field-grown vegetables. It also says that some varieties are more nutritious than vegetables grown in fields (畑で育った野菜より栄養があるものもある).
default.q.n3-26-q71-71.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage states that the factory can produce many vegetables in the same area (多くの野菜を生産することができます), not that it cannot grow many at the same time.
default.q.n3-26-q71-71.why.2: (c) Correct. Regarding food safety, the passage says: 「農薬を使う必要がありません。ですから、工場で作られた野菜は安心して食べられます。」 Regarding high production costs, it says: 「まず、工場を作るのにかなりの建設費がかかります。そして、野菜を作るには、電気やエアコンを長時間つけておく必要があるので、電気代もかかります。」
default.q.n3-26-q71-71.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The article clearly states that the number of vegetable varieties that can currently be grown in the factory is still small (作れる野菜の種類もまだ少ない), not large.
default.q.n3-26-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 問題はあるがいい点も多く、将来は工場での野菜の生産を増やしていく必要がある。 (Although there are problems, there are also many good points, and vegetable production in factories needs to be increased in the future.)
default.q.n3-26-q72-72.explanation:
- Main point of the passage: The author states that although plant factories still face issues involving cost and the number of varieties, the relevant parties are researching ways to overcome them. For a mountainous country with little arable land such as Japan, expanding vegetable production through plant factories will be necessary in the future.
- Question translation: What does the author think about plant factories?
- Answer choices:
  1. Since research takes time, vegetable production in open fields should be increased beyond its previous level.
  2. Although plant factories have advantages, they face many problems, so new techniques for growing vegetables outside factories must be developed.
  3. They have problems but also many advantages, so vegetable production in plant factories should be increased in the future.
  4. Since the problems currently being researched have been solved, plant factories should be built immediately.
default.q.n3-26-q72-72.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage emphasizes that production using vegetable factories (野菜工場を利用した作物の生産も増やしていかなければならない) must increase in the future, not production in open fields.
default.q.n3-26-q72-72.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The author says that the parties involved are researching new technology to solve the vegetable factory's problems (このような問題を解決するための新しい技術の研究), not searching for technology outside the factory.
default.q.n3-26-q72-72.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage notes several advantages of plant factories and concludes: 「日本のように山が多く、利用できる土地が少ない国では、今後、野菜工場を利用した作物の生産も増やしていかなければならないでしょう。」 (In a mountainous country with little usable land, such as Japan, production of crops using plant factories will need to increase in the future.)
default.q.n3-26-q72-72.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author says that new research is currently being conducted and may take time, 「研究を行っています。時間がかかるかもしれませんが」. It is not yet a resolved issue that can immediately lead to large-scale construction.
default.q.n3-26-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The cup has a slightly irregular shape, but the author bought it because it felt pleasant and comfortable to hold.
default.q.n3-26-q73-73.explanation:
- Main point: When the author visited a pottery shop, the owner offered warm tea and talked about pottery-making and the history of the town. There, the author found a handmade teacup (湯呑み). Although its shape was slightly irregular, it felt very comfortable to hold, so the author decided to buy it as a personal souvenir.
- Question translation: Which of the following is consistent with the passage about the teacup the author bought this time?
- Answer choices:
1. The author bought an item made by a famous artisan at the request of friends.
2. The author made it by hand while the shop owner taught them how to make it.
3. The author bought it because its shape was slightly irregular but it felt very pleasant to hold.
4. The author bought it because it had a picture of the town's history on it and its shape was beautiful.
default.q.n3-26-q73-73.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The author traveled alone and decided to buy the cup as a souvenir for themselves (自分へのお土産として買うことにしました), not because a friend asked them to buy something made by a famous artisan.
default.q.n3-26-q73-73.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The shop owner simply talks kindly about how ceramics are made and the history of the town (器の作り方や町の歴史について優しく教えてくれました); the author does not make a cup personally.
default.q.n3-26-q73-73.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: 「そこで見つけた手作りの湯呑みは、形が少し不揃いでしたが、手に持ったときの感触がとても心地よく、自分へのお土産として買うことにしました。」 The handmade teacup I found there was slightly irregular in shape, but it felt very pleasant to hold, so I decided to buy it as a souvenir for myself.
default.q.n3-26-q73-73.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage only says that the owner talked about the town's history; it does not mention historical paintings on the cups. In addition, the cups are slightly uneven in shape (形が少し不揃い), not beautifully shaped.
default.q.n3-26-q74-74.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The author realized that taking a leisurely trip around a town and interacting with local residents can also be wonderful, rather than simply visiting as many attractions as possible.
default.q.n3-26-q74-74.explanation:
- Main point: The author used to think that a truly fulfilling trip meant visiting as many famous tourist attractions as possible. However, after taking a leisurely trip to a pottery town, talking with local residents, and enjoying the atmosphere, the author realized that slow travel involving meaningful interaction can also be wonderful.
- Translation of the question: How did the author's view change through this trip?
- Translation of the answer choices:
1. The author began to think that the best trip was one in which they visited as many famous tourist attractions as possible with friends.
2. The author began to realize that, in addition to visiting many tourist attractions, taking a leisurely trip in a town and interacting with local residents could also be wonderful.
3. The author began to believe that the most important thing when traveling was simply staying quietly in a hotel and doing nothing.
4. The author realized that making a trip fulfilling required creating a very detailed plan before departure.
default.q.n3-26-q74-74.why.0: (a) Incorrect. In the past, the author would usually plan trips to many places, but on this trip the author traveled alone and changed their view of the meaning of travel.
default.q.n3-26-q74-74.why.1: (b) Correct. The evidence is quoted from the reading: 「これまで私は、たくさんの場所を訪れることが充実した旅行だと思っていました。しかし、一つの町でゆっくりと地元の人と触れ合い、その土地の空気を感じる旅も素晴らしいと気づきました。」 (I used to think that a fulfilling trip meant visiting many places. However, I realized that a leisurely journey spent interacting with local people in one town and experiencing the atmosphere of that place can also be wonderful.)
default.q.n3-26-q74-74.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage does not say that "staying in the hotel and doing nothing is the most important thing"; the author still goes out, observes a pottery workshop, and enters a shop to talk with local people.
default.q.n3-26-q74-74.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Making detailed plans to visit many places was the author's old habit (普段の旅行では...計画を立てることが多い); on this trip, the author chose to take things easy and realized the value of experiencing things at a slower pace, rather than concluding that more detailed planning was necessary.
default.q.n3-26-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (みじかすぎて).
default.q.n3-26-q1-1.explanation:
Meaning: This cord is too short, so it is difficult to use.
• Kanji: 短 — on-reading: タン; kun-reading: みじか・い.
• Example: スカート丈が短すぎる。(The skirt is too short.)
default.q.n3-26-q1-1.why.0: (a) よわすぎて: Incorrect; this is the te-form of 弱すぎる (too weak), derived from 弱い (weak, poor).
default.q.n3-26-q1-1.why.1: (b) みじかすぎて: Correct. The kanji「短」in the i-adjective「短い」is read with its kun-reading, みじか(い), meaning short.
default.q.n3-26-q1-1.why.2: (c) ほそすぎて is incorrect; it is the te-form of 細すぎる (細: ほそい - thin, slender, narrow).
default.q.n3-26-q1-1.why.3: (d) かたすぎて is incorrect; it is the te-form of 固すぎる / 堅すぎる / 硬すぎる (かたい: hard, solid).
default.q.n3-26-q2-2.explanation:
Sentence translation: “That person does not listen to other people’s opinions at all.”
• Kanji: 他 (other) + 人 (person) = 他人 (たにん: another person, outsider).
• Example: 他人の迷惑にならないように気をつけてください。(Please be careful not to inconvenience other people.)
default.q.n3-26-q2-2.why.0: (a) ちにん: Incorrect reading; 「他」 is not read as 「ち」.
default.q.n3-26-q2-2.why.1: (b) たじん: Incorrect reading of 「人」 in this compound; when combined with 他, it is read にん.
default.q.n3-26-q2-2.why.2: (c) たにん: Correct. 「他人」 consists of 「他」 (た) and 「人」 (にん), is read 「たにん」, and means another person or an outsider.
default.q.n3-26-q2-2.why.3: (d) ちじん: Incorrect; this is the reading of 「知人」(ちじん - acquaintance).
default.q.n3-26-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (しめした).
default.q.n3-26-q3-3.explanation:
Sentence meaning: I represented the changes in the population with a graph.
• Kanji: 示 (し: indicate) — on-readings: ジ/シ, kun-reading: しめ・す (indicate, show, represent).
• Example: 調査の結果をグラフで示した。(I presented the survey results in a graph.)
default.q.n3-26-q3-3.why.0: (a) うつした: Wrong. This is the past-tense reading of 写す / 映す / 移す (うつす: to photograph, reflect, or transfer).
default.q.n3-26-q3-3.why.1: (b) さした: Incorrect. This is the past-form reading of 指す, 差す, or 刺す（さす: to point, hold an umbrella, or stab）.
default.q.n3-26-q3-3.why.2: (c) あらわした: Incorrect; this is the past-tense reading of 表す / 現す / 著す (あらわす: to express, appear, or write a book).
default.q.n3-26-q3-3.why.3: (d) Correct: the verb「示す」has the kun-reading「しめす」, and its past form is「示した」(しめした).
default.q.n3-26-q4-4.explanation:
Sentence translation: Mr. Tanaka is a surgeon.
• Kanji: 外 (gai) + 科 (ka) = 外科 (げか: surgery, surgical department).
• Note: 「外」 is normally read with the on-reading ガイ (as in 外国 and 外部), but in 「外科」 it is read as ゲ, a Go-on reading. Similarly, 内科 is read ないか.
• Example: けがをしたので外科で診てもらった。(I was injured, so I went to the surgical department for an examination.)
default.q.n3-26-q4-4.why.0: (a) がいか: Incorrect. Although「外」can be read as「がい」, the technical term「外科」is read「げか」.
default.q.n3-26-q4-4.why.1: (b) げか: Correct. 「外科」 (surgery, surgical department) has the special on-reading 「げか」.
default.q.n3-26-q4-4.why.2: (c) げいか: Incorrect; 外 does not have the reading 「げい」.
default.q.n3-26-q4-4.why.3: (d) がか: Incorrect; this is the reading of 「画家」(painter).
default.q.n3-26-q5-5.explanation:
Translation: Ms. Sato's smile is beautiful/charming.
• Kanji: 笑 (laughter) + 顔 (face) = 笑顔 (えがお: smile, smiling expression).
• Example: 彼女はいつも笑顔を絶やさない。(She always keeps a bright smile on her face.)
default.q.n3-26-q5-5.why.0: (a) えがお: Correct. 「笑顔」 combines 「笑」 (え) and 「顔」 (かお, which becomes がえる through rendaku).
default.q.n3-26-q5-5.why.1: (b) えかお: Incorrect because the rendaku sound change is missing in 「顔」.
default.q.n3-26-q5-5.why.2: (c) わらがお is incorrect. Although the verb is 「笑う」 (わらう), the noun 「笑顔」 is read 「えがお」.
default.q.n3-26-q5-5.why.3: (d) わらかお: Both the reading of 「笑」and the voicing of 「顔」are incorrect.
default.q.n3-26-q6-6.explanation:
Meaning: Please call again after 5 o'clock.
• Kanji: 以 (DĨ) + 降 (HÀNG/GIÁNG) = 以降 (いこう: after that point in time, from then on).
• Distinction: 「以後」(いご) and 「以降」(いこう) both refer to a time after a certain point, but 「以降」is often used with a specific time or date in the past or future.
• Example: 明日以降の予定を教えてください。(Please tell me your schedule from tomorrow onward.)
default.q.n3-26-q6-6.why.0: (a) いこ: Incorrect because the long vowel 「う」 is missing from 「降」(こう).
default.q.n3-26-q6-6.why.1: (b) いごう: Incorrect reading of 「降」; it should be こう, not ごう.
default.q.n3-26-q6-6.why.2: (c) いこう: correct. 「以降」consists of 「以」(い) and 「降」(こう), and is read 「いこう」.
default.q.n3-26-q6-6.why.3: (d) いご: Incorrect; this is the reading of 「以後」(いご).
default.q.n3-26-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (おうだん).
default.q.n3-26-q7-7.explanation:
Translation: When crossing the road, please watch out carefully for traffic.
• Kanji: 横 (across) + 断 (cut off) = 横断 (おうだん: cross, go across).
• Related vocabulary: 横断歩道 (おうだんほどう: pedestrian crossing).
• Example: 信号を守って道路を横断しましょう。(Let’s obey the traffic signals when crossing the road.)
default.q.n3-26-q7-7.why.0: (a) おうだん: correct. 「横断」consists of 「横」(おう) and 「断」(だん), and is read 「おうだん」.
default.q.n3-26-q7-7.why.1: (b) よこだん is incorrect because it combines the kun-reading 「よこ」 with the on-reading 「だん」. The word uses two on-readings: おうだん.
default.q.n3-26-q7-7.why.2: (c) おうたん: Incorrect because the「断」in this word is read with the voiced sound「だん」, not「たん」.
default.q.n3-26-q7-7.why.3: (d) よこたん: Incorrect; both the on- and kun-readings are wrong, and a voiced sound is missing.
default.q.n3-26-q8-8.explanation:
Meaning: Start when I give you the signal.
• Kanji: 合 (together) + 図 (diagram) = 合図 (あいず: signal, cue, command).

default.q.n3-26-q28-28.why.0: (a) 「入れられて」 (the passive form of 入れる) means “be put in” or “be placed in”; it does not mean stealing the ball.
default.q.n3-26-q28-28.why.1: (b) 「止められて」 (the passive form of 止める) means “to be stopped” or “to be blocked,” not “to have the ball taken away.”
default.q.n3-26-q28-28.why.2: (c) 「打たれて」 (the passive form of 打つ) means “to be hit / to be struck by something thrown,” so the meaning is incorrect.
default.q.n3-26-q28-28.why.3: (d) 「取られて」is the passive form of 取る and means “be taken away” or “be robbed,” synonymous with 「うばわれて」, the passive form of 奪う.
default.q.n3-26-q29-29.explanation:
- Sentence translation: The meeting has already started, so please go inside quietly.
• そっと: quietly, gently, stealthily; doing something silently so as not to attract attention or disturb others (= 静かに, こっそり).
• Example: 赤ちゃんが起きないように、ドアをそっと閉めた。 (I gently closed the door so that the baby would not wake up.)
default.q.n3-26-q29-29.why.0: (a) 「後ろから」 means “from behind,” indicating a position or direction of movement; it does not express acting gently or quietly.
default.q.n3-26-q29-29.why.1: (b) 「急いで」 means “hurriedly” or “in haste,” not “quietly” or “stealthily.”
default.q.n3-26-q29-29.why.2: (c) 「静かに」 means “quietly,” “softly,” or “gently,” and is synonymous with the adverb 「そっと」.
default.q.n3-26-q29-29.why.3: (d) 「一人ずつ」 means “one person at a time” and indicates quantity or order, not a gentle action.
default.q.n3-26-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (明るすぎて).
default.q.n3-26-q30-30.explanation:
Translation: The glare is so bright that I can't see the writing on the poster clearly.
• 眩しい / 目映い (まぶしい - HUYỄN): dazzling, glaring (because the light is too strong = 光が強くて / 明るすぎて).
• Example: 夏の強い日差しがまぶしい。 (The intense summer sunlight is dazzling.)
default.q.n3-26-q30-30.why.0: (a) 「明るすぎて」 means “too bright” or “so bright that it is glaring,” and is synonymous with the adjective 「まぶしくて」 (眩しい, painfully bright).
default.q.n3-26-q30-30.why.1: (b) 「遠すぎて」 means “too far,” referring to distance, not dazzling brightness.
