default.q.n3-27-q25-25.why.0: (a) ケース (case): a box or hard container for storing things; a hard case of this type is not used for a motorcycle parked outdoors.
default.q.n3-27-q25-25.why.1: (b) カバー (cover): a tarp or protective cover; 「バイクにカバーをかける」 means covering a motorcycle with a tarp to protect it from rain and sunlight.
default.q.n3-27-q25-25.why.2: (c) マスク (mask): a face mask or protective mask; it is used for people, not to cover a motorcycle.
default.q.n3-27-q25-25.why.3: (d) ラップ (wrap): plastic wrap used to cover and preserve food; it is not used for a motorcycle.
default.q.n3-27-q26-26.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (同じところ).
default.q.n3-27-q26-26.explanation:
Sentence translation: There is something in common among these methods.
- 共通点 (きょうつうてん - KYŌTSŪTEN): common point, similarity (= 同じところ).
- Example: 2人の意見には多くの共通点がある。(The two people's opinions have many similarities.)
default.q.n3-27-q26-26.why.0: (a) 「悪いところ」 means a bad point or an area that is not good; it is not synonymous with 「共通点」.
default.q.n3-27-q26-26.why.1: (b) 「いいところ」 means “good point” or “strength”; it is not synonymous with 「共通点」.
default.q.n3-27-q26-26.why.2: (c) 「違うところ」means “a point of difference,” the opposite of「共通点」(a common point).
default.q.n3-27-q26-26.why.3: (d) 「同じところ」 means “similar point” or “point in common,” exactly matching 「共通点」.
default.q.n3-27-q27-27.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (片付けた).
default.q.n3-27-q27-27.explanation:
Translation: Everyone organized the materials together.
- 整理する (せいりする): to organize, tidy up, put in order (= 片付ける).
- Example: 机の上をきれいに整理してください。(Please tidy up the desk neatly.)
default.q.n3-27-q27-27.why.0: (a) 「数えた」 (かぞえた) means “counted,” not organized or tidied up the documents.
default.q.n3-27-q27-27.why.1: (b) 「片付けた」 (かたづけた) means “cleaned up” or “put in order,” and is synonymous with 「整理した」 in the context of organizing documents.
default.q.n3-27-q27-27.why.2: (c) 「運んだ」 (はこんだ) means “carried” or “transported,” not organized or tidied up.
default.q.n3-27-q27-27.why.3: (d) 「探した」(さがした) means “searched for,” which does not fit the context of processing documents that already exist.
default.q.n3-27-q28-28.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (かならず).
default.q.n3-27-q28-28.explanation:
Meaning: I think Mr. Tanaka will definitely come.
- 絶対に (ぜったいに): absolutely, definitely, without fail (= 必ず - かならず).
- Example: この約束は絶対に守ります。(I will definitely keep this promise.)
default.q.n3-27-q28-28.why.0: (a) 「すぐに」 means “immediately,” indicating when an action is performed, not the degree of certainty or affirmation.
default.q.n3-27-q28-28.why.1: (b) 「たぶん」 means “probably” or “perhaps,” expressing uncertainty, which is opposite to the definite meaning of 「ぜったいに」.
default.q.n3-27-q28-28.why.2: (c) 「かならず」 means “certainly/definitely” and is synonymous with 「ぜったいに」, expressing a firm assertion.
default.q.n3-27-q28-28.why.3: (d) 「あとから」means “afterward” or “later,” indicating chronological order rather than certainty.
default.q.n3-27-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (だれにも話さないで).
default.q.n3-27-q29-29.explanation:
Translation: Please keep this a secret.
- 内緒（ないしょ）means a secret or private matter; 「ないしょにする」means to keep something secret and not tell anyone (= だれにも話さない / 秘密にする).
- Example: これは2人だけの内緒だよ。(This is a secret just between the two of us.)
default.q.n3-27-q29-29.why.0: (a) 「だれにも話さないで」 means “don’t tell anyone,” exactly synonymous with 「ないしょにして」 (“keep it secret”).
default.q.n3-27-q29-29.why.1: (b) 「いろいろな人に話して」 means “tell many people,” which is the complete opposite of keeping something secret.
default.q.n3-27-q29-29.why.2: (c) 「早く忘れて」 means “Forget it quickly,” and does not mean to keep something secret from others.
default.q.n3-27-q29-29.why.3: (d) 「忘れないで」means “don’t forget,” not “keep it a secret.”
default.q.n3-27-q30-30.explanation:
Sentence translation: “Of all the songs on this CD, this is the one I like best.”
- 気に入る (きにいる - KÍ NHẬP): to like, be pleased with, suit one's taste; 「気に入っている」 = to like, be fond of (= 好きな).
- Example: このデザインがとても気に入っています。(I really like this design.)
default.q.n3-27-q30-30.why.0: (a) 「人気がある」means “popular” or “liked by many people.” It refers to the preference of the general public, not the speaker's personal preference.
default.q.n3-27-q30-30.why.1: (b) 「よく覚えている」means “remember very clearly.” It describes memory, not preference.
default.q.n3-27-q30-30.why.2: (c) 「好きな」 means “to like,” and is synonymous with 「気に入っている」 (to like, to be pleased with).
default.q.n3-27-q30-30.why.3: (d) 「楽しい」 means “fun” or “enjoyable,” describing a cheerful feeling; it is not synonymous with 「気に入っている」, which expresses liking or satisfaction.
default.q.n3-27-q31-31.explanation:
「緊張（きんちょう）」means psychological tension, nervousness, or anxiety in an important situation or in front of a crowd. It can also refer to strained or highly confrontational relations, such as diplomatic relations or security situations. Common expressions: 緊張が解ける (one's tension is eased), 緊張感 (a sense of tension).
Example: 面接の前は誰でも緊張するものだ。(Everyone gets nervous before an interview.)
default.q.n3-27-q31-31.why.0: "胸が緊張した" is inappropriate in this context. When someone is delighted or excited to see snow for the first time, they would say "胸がわくわくした" or "胸が高鳴った"; 緊張 refers to tension or nervousness, not joyful excitement.
default.q.n3-27-q31-31.why.1: "計画が緊張している" is an incorrect collocation. To describe a tightly packed summer vacation plan or schedule, use "詰まっている" or "ぎっしりだ", not "緊張".
default.q.n3-27-q31-31.why.2: "使い方が緊張していて" is incorrect. To describe a computer as complicated or difficult to use, use "複雑で." 緊張 refers to a person's psychological state or a tense situation, not the characteristics of how an object or machine is used.
default.q.n3-27-q31-31.why.3: "テレビのインタビューを受けて、とても緊張した。" is correct; "緊張する" accurately describes the tension and nervousness someone feels when being interviewed on television.
default.q.n3-27-q32-32.explanation: 「暗記（あんき）」means to memorize something by heart, remembering the exact wording, vocabulary, figures, formulas, poems, and so on, usually for study or exams. It differs from 「覚える」, which means to remember in general, such as remembering a person, event, or feeling. Example: 英単語を1日10個暗記することにしている。(I have decided to memorize 10 English words a day.)
default.q.n3-27-q32-32.why.0: "景色を暗記しておきたい" is incorrect. To remember and preserve the image of beautiful scenery in one’s mind, use "覚えておきたい" or "目に焼き付けておきたい". "暗記" is used only for memorizing texts, words, figures, and similar material.
default.q.n3-27-q32-32.why.1: "文を暗記しています" is correct; "暗記する" combines perfectly naturally with memorizing each sentence in a textbook.
default.q.n3-27-q32-32.why.2: "田中さんを暗記していますか" is incorrect; when asking whether someone remembers an old acquaintance, use "覚えていますか". 暗記 is not used with a person as its object.
default.q.n3-27-q32-32.why.3: “暗記していません” is incorrect. Remembering or forgetting where belongings are kept concerns memory of everyday events, so 「覚えていません」 must be used instead of 「暗記」, which means memorizing study material.
default.q.n3-27-q33-33.explanation: 「訪問（ほうもん）」means to visit or call on a person, place, organization, company, or school for a specific purpose, often in a formal, polite, or business context. Example: 明日、取引先の会社を訪問する予定です。(I am scheduled to visit our business partner's company tomorrow.)
default.q.n3-27-q33-33.why.0: "会社を訪問しました" is correct; 「訪問する」 is appropriately used when a job seeker visits or meets a senior's company for job-hunting purposes (就職活動).
default.q.n3-27-q33-33.why.1: “手紙が訪問しました” is incorrect. When a letter arrives somewhere, use “届きました” or “来ました.” 訪問 describes a person intentionally going to a place and is not used for objects such as letters.
default.q.n3-27-q33-33.why.2: "海を訪問しています" is incorrect; going to the beach for family recreation and relaxation on the weekend should be expressed as "海に行っています" or "海を訪れています". "訪問" has a formal, businesslike or visit-oriented nuance and sounds unnatural here.
default.q.n3-27-q33-33.why.3: "チャンスが訪問しました" is incorrect. When an opportunity comes along, use "チャンスが訪れました (おとずれました)" or "チャンスが巡ってきました". "訪問" is not used as the predicate of an abstract noun such as “opportunity.”
default.q.n3-27-q34-34.explanation: 「翻訳（ほんやく）」means translating written text from one language into another (unlike 通訳, which means interpreting spoken language). It is not used for explaining something, changing its reading, or rephrasing it in different words within the same language. Example: 彼女は日本の小説を英語に翻訳している。(She is translating a Japanese novel into English.)
default.q.n3-27-q34-34.why.0: “漢字をひらがなに翻訳する” is incorrect. Converting kanji into hiragana within the same language uses “直す,” “書き換える,” or “振り仮名を振る”; “翻訳” means translation between different languages.
default.q.n3-27-q34-34.why.1: "短くわかりやすい文章に翻訳する" is incorrect; rewriting a long passage as short, easy-to-understand sentences in the same language is expressed with "書き直す", "言い換える", or "要約する" (to summarize), not "翻訳".
default.q.n3-27-q34-34.why.2: "十以上の言語に翻訳されている" is correct; "翻訳される" accurately expresses that a literary work, such as a novel, is translated into more than ten different languages worldwide.
default.q.n3-27-q34-34.why.3: 「ほかのことばに翻訳すれば」 is incorrect. Explaining the meaning of a word using different words in the same language requires 「言い換えれば」 (“in other words”), not 「翻訳」 (“translate”).
default.q.n3-28-q36-36.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: "Next week, the company president will be going on a business trip to Japan, so I will go along as an interpreter."
- Structure: `Noun + として`: as... / in the role of...
- Example: 彼は留学生として日本へ来ました。(He came to Japan as an international student.)
default.q.n3-28-q36-36.why.0: (a) Grammatically correct: the structure 「N + として」indicates a person's or thing's status, position, or role ('as an interpreter').
default.q.n3-28-q36-36.why.1: (b) This is grammatically incorrect: 「〜にして」 is generally used to emphasize a special time or stage, or to combine two qualities; it is not used to indicate a role or status.
default.q.n3-28-q36-36.why.2: (c) Grammatically incorrect: 「〜とまで」 means “to the extent that...” and does not fit the context of taking on a role.
default.q.n3-28-q36-36.why.3: (d) Grammatically incorrect: 「〜にまで」 means “as far as” or “to the extent of,” and is not used to indicate a capacity or position held.
default.q.n3-28-q37-37.explanation:
- Meaning: “The coins we commonly use every day come in many round shapes.”
- Pattern: `Noun (shape, color, characteristic) + をしている`: to have or possess a particular characteristic or shape.
- Example: その犬は長くて白い毛をしている。(That dog has long, white fur.)
default.q.n3-28-q37-37.why.0: (a) Grammatical error: 「〜のしている」does not form a sentence pattern for describing an object’s shape or external characteristics.
default.q.n3-28-q37-37.why.1: (b) Grammatically incorrect: the particle 「も」 (“also”) does not form a fixed phrase describing appearance or characteristics.
default.q.n3-28-q37-37.why.2: (c) Grammatically correct: The pattern 「〜をしている」 describes the shape, color, appearance, or characteristic of a person or thing (丸い形をしている: “has a round shape”).
default.q.n3-28-q37-37.why.3: (d) Grammatically incorrect: The particle 「で」indicates a means, manner, location, or cause, and does not combine with 「している」to describe a shape.
default.q.n3-28-q38-38.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: “Some people easily decide to get pets for reasons such as ‘they are cute’ or ‘I feel lonely when I am alone,’ but I think strong determination is also necessary to continue caring for them until the end.”
- Structure: `A (とか) B + などという + noun`: Lists representative examples with a slightly dismissive nuance (“for reasons such as…”).
- Example: 忙しいなどという理由で約束を破ってはいけない。(You must not break a promise for a reason such as being busy.)
default.q.n3-28-q38-38.why.0: (a) Grammatically incorrect: When いう (to say/call) introduces quoted content, it requires the quotation particle 「と」, not the object particle 「を」 in the pattern 「〜という理由」.
default.q.n3-28-q38-38.why.1: (b) Grammatically correct: The pattern 「〜などという理由で」combines 「など」(giving a representative example) with 「と」(the quotation particle used with いう), meaning “for reasons such as...”.
default.q.n3-28-q38-38.why.2: (c) Grammatically incorrect. 「こと」 nominalizes a clause, but the preceding part is already a direct quotation followed by 「とか」, and the quotation particle 「と」 is missing before 「いう」.
default.q.n3-28-q38-38.why.3: (d) Grammatically incorrect: the combination「ことと」does not sound natural after a list of quoted impressions「〜とか〜」and before「いう理由」.
default.q.n3-28-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (いるなら).
default.q.n3-28-q39-39.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: “Child: ‘Mom, is there anything to eat?’ — Mom: ‘If you’re hungry, there are some doughnuts.’”
- Structure: `V-ている + なら`: If someone is in the state of doing... (「なら」takes up information from the conversation partner and offers a suitable suggestion or guidance).
- Example: 時間があるなら、一緒にお茶でも飲みませんか。(If you have time, would you like to have tea together?)
default.q.n3-28-q39-39.why.0: (a) Grammatically incorrect: 「〜ても」 means “even if ...,” making the sentence illogical: “Even if the child is hungry, there are donuts.”
default.q.n3-28-q39-39.why.1: (b) Grammatically incorrect. The conditional pattern 「〜と」is used for inevitable natural laws or habitual results, not for suggestions, proposals, or advice directed at the listener.
default.q.n3-28-q39-39.why.2: (c) Incorrect in meaning: 「〜けど」 means “but” or “although,” which does not fit the context of responding to a child’s question with a suggestion for a dish.
default.q.n3-28-q39-39.why.3: (d) Grammatically correct:「〜なら」introduces an assumption or condition based on the other person’s situation or information (“If you’re hungry, there are donuts here”).
default.q.n3-28-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (にくらべて).
default.q.n3-28-q40-40.explanation:
- Meaning: "The laptop being released this time is considerably lighter than previous products, so it is very convenient to carry around."
- Pattern: `Noun + に比べて / にくらべて`: compared with ...
- Related Sino-Japanese readings: 発売 (release, sale), 比 (comparison).
- Example: 今年の夏は、去年に比べてとても暑い。(This summer is much hotter than last summer.)
default.q.n3-28-q40-40.why.0: (a) Grammatically incorrect: 「〜にしたがって」means 'along with / the more..., the more...', expressing a correlated change over time; it is not used to compare two static objects.
default.q.n3-28-q40-40.why.1: (b) Grammatically correct: 「〜にくらべて」(に比べて) means “compared with…” and is used to compare differences in qualities or degree between two things (“it is much lighter compared with those up to now”).
default.q.n3-28-q40-40.why.2: (c) Grammatically incorrect: 「〜の一方で」 means “on the other hand” or “in contrast,” and is used to present two contrasting aspects of something.
default.q.n3-28-q40-40.why.3: (d) Incorrect grammar: 「〜のことで」 means “about the matter of...,” and is not used in a comparison structure.
default.q.n3-28-q41-41.explanation:
- Meaning of the sentence: "Team Leader: 'Yamada, have you sent the materials for tomorrow's meeting to the department manager yet?' — Yamada: 'Yes, I have. I just took them over a moment ago.'"
- Pattern: `V-た + ところだ`: to have just finished doing something. Distinguish between `持って行く` (to take something to another place) and `持って来る` (to bring something here).
- Example: たった今、荷物を送ったところです。(I have just sent the package.)
default.q.n3-28-q41-41.why.0: (a) Incorrect in both grammar and direction of movement: 「V-るところ」 describes something that is about to happen, contrary to “it has already been delivered” and “just a moment ago.” Also, 「来る」 describes movement toward the speaker, rather than taking something somewhere else.
default.q.n3-28-q41-41.why.1: (b) Grammatically correct: 「持って行く」 describes taking the documents to the manager, and combining the past form 「行った」 with 「〜ところ」 creates 「V-たところだ」, meaning that something was completed very recently, which fits 「ついさっき」 and 「届けました」.
default.q.n3-28-q41-41.why.2: (c) Grammatically incorrect: 「持って行くところ」means "be about to take it," which conflicts with the fact that it has already been delivered (届けました) and with the recent timing (ついさっき).
default.q.n3-28-q41-41.why.3: (d) The direction of movement is incorrect: 「持って来た」means “brought here,” toward the speaker’s current location, so it does not fit bringing documents from one’s own location to the manager’s office.
default.q.n3-28-q42-42.explanation:
- Meaning: "Company representative: 'That concludes my explanation. Does anyone have any questions?' - Student: 'Yes, may I ask two questions?'"
- Structure: `V-(さ)せてください`: Please allow me to V / May I V.
- Example: 気分が悪いので、少し休ませてください。(I am not feeling well, so please let me rest for a while.)
default.q.n3-28-q42-42.why.0: (a) Grammatically incorrect. 「質問してください」 asks the other person to ask a question (“Please ask a question”), so it is not used when the speaker is asking permission to ask something.
default.q.n3-28-q42-42.why.1: (b) Grammatically correct: The causative combined with てください, 「V-(さ)せてください」, is used to ask someone to allow the speaker to perform an action (“Please let me ask two questions”).
default.q.n3-28-q42-42.why.2: (c) Inappropriate for the context: 「やってください」 uses the verb 「やる」, which has a casual, lowering tone and is unsuitable for a formal company presentation.
default.q.n3-28-q42-42.why.3: (d) Incorrect grammar: 「されて」is the passive or respectful form used for another person’s action. It is not used for one’s own action when asking permission.
default.q.n3-28-q43-43.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: "Senior: 'You're late again. Last time, the teacher told you not to be late for practice from now on, didn't they?' - Nishida: 'Yes, I'm truly sorry.'"
- Structure: `V-る + な`: imperative prohibition form (Do not V). In indirect quotations: `〜（する）なと言われる / って言われる` (be told not to do something).
- Example: 医者に、お酒を飲むなと言われました。(I was told by the doctor not to drink alcohol.)
default.q.n3-28-q43-43.why.0: (a) Grammatically correct: The prohibitive form 「V-る + な」 (do not do something) is indirectly quoted in 「〜するなって言われた」(I was told not to be late).
default.q.n3-28-q43-43.why.1: (b) Incorrect in meaning: 「するよ」 is a sentence ending used to announce or assert something, so interpreting it as "Be late, okay?" is completely inconsistent with the teacher's stern reminder.
default.q.n3-28-q43-43.why.2: (c) Incorrect in meaning: 「するね」 is used to express agreement or a mild intention, so it does not fit a warning forbidding someone from being late.
default.q.n3-28-q43-43.why.3: (d) Incorrect in meaning: 「するんだ」is used to emphasize a mild command or explain a reason. It would mean "have to go late," which is completely opposite to the context.
default.q.n3-28-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (さしあげる).
default.q.n3-28-q44-44.explanation:
- Meaning: "We have prepared a gift for our teacher and are planning to give it to him on the last day of class."
- Honorific language: `さしあげる` (差し上げる) is the humble form of `あげる` (give), used when giving something to someone of higher status.
- Example: お世話になった先輩に記念品を差し上げました。(I gave a commemorative gift to the senior colleague who had helped me.)
default.q.n3-28-q44-44.why.0: (a) Incorrect honorific usage: 「くださる」is the respectful form of 「くれる」(someone of higher status gives something to the speaker), whereas here the subject “we” is giving a present to the teacher.
default.q.n3-28-q44-44.why.1: (b) Incorrect honorific usage: 「なさる」is the respectful form of 「する」(to do), not a verb meaning “to give a gift,” and it is not used for the speaker's own action.
default.q.n3-28-q44-44.why.2: (c) Correct honorific usage: 「さしあげる」 is the humble form (謙譲語) of 「あげる」, used when the speaker gives something to a person of higher status, such as a teacher.
default.q.n3-28-q44-44.why.3: (d) Incorrect honorific language: 「いただく」 is the humble form of 「もらう」 (“to receive from someone”). If 「いただく」 were used, it would need to be preceded by 「から/に」 and mean receiving a gift. Here, the speaker is preparing a gift to give to the teacher.
default.q.n3-28-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (ようなことを).
default.q.n3-28-q45-45.explanation:
- Meaning: “It was truly unavoidable at the time, but I still feel sorry that I accidentally said things that made him angry.”
- Structure: `V (plain form) + ような + noun (こと/もの)`: something/something like..., used to give an example or describe a similar quality.
- Example: 人を傷つけるようなことを言ってはいけません。(You must not say things that hurt people.)
default.q.n3-28-q45-45.why.0: (a) Grammatically incorrect: The dictionary-form verb 「怒らせる」 cannot directly combine with 「そうな」; it must be changed to the stem form 「怒らせそうな」. In addition, the substitute pronoun 「の」 is not appropriate for referring to abstract speech content.
default.q.n3-28-q45-45.why.1: (b) Incorrect in context: Although 「怒らせるような」 is grammatically correct, when used with the verb 「言う」, the noun 「こと」 (words or things said) is more natural than the object-substitution pronoun 「の」.
default.q.n3-28-q45-45.why.2: (c) Grammatically incorrect: 「そう」expressing an appearance or prediction must follow the verb stem with ます removed (怒らせそうな); it cannot follow the dictionary form「怒らせる」.
default.q.n3-28-q45-45.why.3: (d) Grammatically correct: the plain form of the verb 「怒らせる」 modifies 「ようなこと」 (“things such as making him angry”), which functions as the object before 「言ってしまって」.
default.q.n3-28-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (だけでよければ).
default.q.n3-28-q46-46.explanation:
- Meaning of the sentence: "Yamashita: 'Tanaka, could you come and clean the research room tomorrow?' — Tanaka: 'I have plans in the afternoon. If morning only is acceptable, I can do it.'"
- Structure: `Noun + だけでよければ`: If just N is acceptable / If N alone will do (a humble way to state the limit of what one can offer).
- Example: 私の日本語でよければ、手伝いますよ。(If my Japanese is good enough, I'll help you.)
default.q.n3-28-q46-46.why.0: (a) Incorrect word choice: 「ばかり」means “nothing but” or “all,” and is not used to restrict something to the sole time period that satisfies a condition, as「だけ」is.
default.q.n3-28-q46-46.why.1: (b) Grammatically incorrect: The combination of 「ばかり」 as a limiting expression and 「〜ても」 (“even if...”) does not express a condition agreed upon with the other person.
default.q.n3-28-q46-46.why.2: (c) This is grammatically correct: 「〜だけでよければ」is a common expression meaning “if just... is acceptable,” used when the speaker can meet only a limited part of the request (in this case, being available only in the morning).
default.q.n3-28-q46-46.why.3: (d) Incorrect grammar: The concessive ending 「〜ても」 (“even if...”) is not used to establish a condition for agreeing to a request.
default.q.n3-28-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (お目にかかる).
default.q.n3-28-q47-47.explanation:
- Meaning of the dialogue: “Yamaguchi: ‘Professor Nakagawa!’ — Professor Nakagawa: ‘Oh, Yamaguchi. What a coincidence.’ — Yamaguchi: ‘Yes. I never expected to see you at this party.’”
- Honorific language: `お目にかかる`: the humble form of `会う` (to meet someone of higher status). Pattern: `[person of higher status] に お目にかかる`.
- Distinction: `拝見する` is the humble form of `見る` (to look at or read an object, letter, or document); `ご覧になる` is the respectful form of `見る`.
- Example: いつか社長にお目にかかりたいと思っております。(I sincerely hope to meet the company president someday.)
default.q.n3-28-q47-47.why.0: (a) Incorrect honorific. 「お見えになる」 is the respectful form of 「来る / いる」 (“to come / be present”) and describes the other person’s action; it does not take the particle 「に」 to indicate the speaker’s act of meeting someone.
default.q.n3-28-q47-47.why.1: (b) Incorrect honorific usage: 「拝見する」 is the humble form of 「見る」 (to look at or view documents or objects), and is not used for meeting a person.
default.q.n3-28-q47-47.why.2: (c) Correct honorific usage: 「お目にかかる」is the humble form (謙譲語) of 「会う」(to meet). It is used with 「先生に」(meet the teacher) to show respect for the teacher.
default.q.n3-28-q47-47.why.3: (d) Incorrect honorific usage: 「ご覧になる」 is the respectful form of 「見る」 (to look at, watch). It is not used for meeting someone and is not used for one's own actions.
default.q.n3-28-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (しないようになった).
default.q.n3-28-q48-48.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: “My daughter was physically weak when she was young, but since she started elementary school, she has gradually stopped catching colds or developing fevers.”
- Pattern: V-ない + ようになる: come to no longer do something or no longer experience something (expressing a gradual change in a state or habit over time).
- Example: 薬を飲んでから、夜よく眠れるようになりました。(Since taking the medicine, I have come to sleep well at night.)
default.q.n3-28-q48-48.why.0: (a) Grammatically incorrect: 「〜ことになった」 indicates a result or rule decided by others or by external circumstances. It is not used for a natural physical or health-related change.
default.q.n3-28-q48-48.why.1: (b) Grammatically correct: 「〜ようになる」 (negative form: 〜ないようになる) is used with the adverb 「だんだん」 (gradually) to express a natural change over time in a physical condition or state (“gradually stopped catching colds and fevers so often”).
default.q.n3-28-q48-48.why.2: (c) Grammatically incorrect: 「〜ことにした」 expresses a deliberate human decision (“decided not to…”), so it is not used for becoming sick or feverish, which is beyond one’s control.
default.q.n3-28-q48-48.why.3: (d) Incorrect in context: 「〜ようにした」expresses an effort to carry out an action ('tried not to...'), whereas becoming healthier and getting sick less often is a natural process of physical recovery after growing up.

default.q.n3-28-q49-49.explanation:

default.q.n3-28-q49-49.why.1: (b) It is a noun followed by the particle は, serving as the subject of the negative predicate 「ない」 at the end of the sentence, after the modifying i-adjective 「おもしろい」 (4).
default.q.n3-28-q49-49.why.2: (c) The demonstrative pronoun comes first among the four slots (immediately after 「わたしは、」) and serves as the object of comparison directly before the particle 「ほど」 (1).

default.q.n3-28-q50-50.why.1: (b) It follows the modifying phrase「19世紀の」to form「19世紀の画家たち」and is followed by the particle に to connect to 「よって」(1).

default.q.n3-28-q51-51.explanation:
Complete sentence: 昨日のパーティ－は、友だちと話していたら、ほとんど何も食べないうちに終わってしまって、あとでおなかがすいてしまった。

default.q.n3-28-q51-51.why.1: (b) It follows the adverb 「ほとんど」 and is used with the negative verb 「食べない」 (4), forming 「ほとんど何も食べない」 (hardly eat anything).
default.q.n3-28-q51-51.why.2: (c) In position 3 (the ★ slot), it follows the negative-form verb 「食べない」 (4) to form 「～ないうちに」 (“while not yet...,” “before one has a chance to...”).
default.q.n3-28-q51-51.why.3: (d) The verb in the negative form follows the object 「何も」(2) and comes immediately before 「うちに」(3), creating the meaning "before I had a chance to eat anything."

default.q.n3-28-q52-52.explanation:
Complete sentence: 夏休みに行われた会社での実習は、わたしにとって、企業で働くというのがどういうことか考えるいい機会になった。

default.q.n3-28-q52-52.why.1: (b) The particle phrase nominalizes the action 「働く」 in fragment (3), making it the subject or topic of the following interrogative clause 「どういうことか」 in fragment (4).
default.q.n3-28-q52-52.why.2: (c) A dictionary-form verb comes first (after 「企業で」) and combines with 「というのが」(2) to form the topic “working at a company.”

default.q.n3-28-q53-53.explanation:
Complete sentence: 母は「風邪をひかないのは、毎朝しているジョギングのおかげだ。」とよく言っている。
Meaning: My mother often says, "I don't catch colds because I jog every morning."

default.q.n3-28-q53-53.why.1: (b) The verb in the ている-form follows the adverb 「毎朝」(4) to form 「毎朝している」, which modifies the noun 「ジョギング」(1).
default.q.n3-28-q53-53.why.2: (c) It appears in the fourth position, at the end of the quoted sentence, and combines with the preceding noun to form the pattern expressing a cause that leads to a favorable result: 「～のおかげだ」(it is thanks to...).
default.q.n3-28-q53-53.why.3: (d) The adverb of frequency goes first among the four blanks, after 「風邪をひかないのは、」, and modifies the verb 「している」(2).
default.q.n3-28-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 1. そこで.
default.q.n3-28-q54-54.explanation: In the preceding sentence, the author expresses the wish to choose a Japanese song that everyone could understand because the classmates came from different countries (「みんながわかる日本語で歌いたいと思いました」). To address and fulfill this wish, the author then decides to sing a Japanese anime song (「日本のアニメの歌を歌うことにしました」). Therefore, the most appropriate conjunction linking the reason or purpose to the action taken is 「そこで」 (therefore, so, as a result). The other conjunctions express contrast or a change of topic and do not fit the logic of the passage.
default.q.n3-28-q54-54.why.0: (a) Correct. 「そこで」 means "therefore" or "so" and connects the preceding situation or desire (to sing a Japanese song that everyone would understand) to a specific solution (deciding to sing an anime song).
default.q.n3-28-q54-54.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「それでも」 means “even so” or “nevertheless,” expressing contrast or concession, so it does not fit a cause-and-solution sequence.
default.q.n3-28-q54-54.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「ところで」 means “by the way” or “incidentally” and is used to shift to another topic; it is not used to connect actions involved in resolving the issue just mentioned.
default.q.n3-28-q54-54.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「ところが」 means “however” or “but,” and is used when an unexpected result contradicts a prediction; that does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-28-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 歌い出したからです.
default.q.n3-28-q55-55.explanation: In the previous sentence, the author worries that people may not know the song they chose, but immediately states that "there was no need to worry" (「その必要はありませんでした」). The sentence at position 55 explains why there was no need to worry: "because when I began singing, everyone began singing along" (「わたしが歌い始めたら、みんながいっしょに歌い出したからです」). Therefore, the cause-and-reason structure 「〜からです」 is the correct answer. 「〜せいです」 is not used because it expresses blame or a negative result.
default.q.n3-28-q55-55.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「〜せい」 indicates a cause leading to a negative consequence or assigns blame, whereas the whole class singing along is a fun, positive experience.
default.q.n3-28-q55-55.why.1: (b) Correct. 「〜からだ／からです」 explains the reason for the statement in the previous sentence (“there is no need to worry”). The author need not worry because everyone joined in singing.
default.q.n3-28-q55-55.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜だけ」 means “only...,” making the sentence mean “only sing together,” and it does not explain the reason for the preceding sentence.
default.q.n3-28-q55-55.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜ことだ／ことです」 is used to give advice or report a fact; it is not used to end an explanation of a reason.
default.q.n3-28-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 同じアニメ.
default.q.n3-28-q56-56.explanation: The previous passage included the sentence: "It seems that everyone had also watched that anime in their own countries" (「みんなも自分の国でそのアニメを見ていたそうです」). During karaoke, the author and the others realized that everyone had watched "the same anime" (「同じアニメ」). This shared point of interest became a bridge that helped them start talking more about anime and grow closer. Therefore, 「同じアニメ」is the completely correct choice according to the flow of the passage.
default.q.n3-28-q56-56.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「自分のアニメ」 means “one’s own anime,” which does not fit because this is a Japanese anime that everyone watches together.
default.q.n3-28-q56-56.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「みんなのアニメ」 means “everyone's anime,” which is unnatural and does not express watching the same work together.
default.q.n3-28-q56-56.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「違う国のアニメ」 means “anime from different countries,” which contradicts the context that everyone watched the same anime.
default.q.n3-28-q56-56.why.3: (d) Correct. 「同じアニメ」means "the same anime series." The preceding passage says that everyone had watched that anime in their own countries (「そのアニメを見ていた」), so discovering that they had all watched the same anime prompted them to start talking more openly.
default.q.n3-28-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 親しくなることができたのです.
default.q.n3-28-q57-57.explanation: The previous passage says that after the karaoke outing, they became more open with each other and 「今はほかのいろいろな話もできる友だちになれました」 (they have now become friends who can talk about many different things). Therefore, becoming closer than before was an actual result achieved in the past thanks to Japanese anime. The past potential form combined with the explanatory ending 「〜ことができたのです」 (were able to become closer) expresses this meaning precisely.
default.q.n3-28-q57-57.why.0: (a) Correct. 「〜ことができたのです」 combines the past potential form with 「〜のです」 to assert and explain an actual result: thanks to anime, the author was able to become closer to five friends.
default.q.n3-28-q57-57.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜てほしい」 expresses a desire for someone else to do something for the speaker; it is not used to describe a change in the speaker's own relationship.
default.q.n3-28-q57-57.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜そうだった」 expresses an inference such as “seemed” or “looked as if it almost happened,” which does not fit because the author confirms that they are now close friends.
default.q.n3-28-q57-57.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜てみたい」 expresses the desire “to try doing something,” so it is unsuitable for describing a result that already occurred and was achieved in the past.
default.q.n3-28-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 3. ものだったのだと思っています.
default.q.n3-28-q58-58.explanation: The concluding sentence begins with “As for myself now...” (「今は日本のアニメは自分にとって...」). This is the ending of an essay and expresses the author’s present feelings and deeper understanding after the experiences described above. Therefore, the sentence should end with 「〜と思っています」(“I think that...”), which expresses the author’s own thoughts. The other choices indicate asking the reader (「〜ますか」), reporting secondhand information (「〜そうです」), or making an uncertain guess (「〜かもしれません」), so they do not fit the reflective essay style.
default.q.n3-28-q58-58.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「〜と思いますか」 is an interrogative question directed at the reader and is not used to end an essay presenting the author's personal thoughts.
default.q.n3-28-q58-58.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜そうです」 conveys information heard from someone else (“I hear that...”), and is not used to express the author's own thoughts, as indicated by 「自分にとって」.
default.q.n3-28-q58-58.why.2: (c) Correct. The sentence ending 「〜と思っています」accurately expresses the author’s current thoughts or awareness (“now I think...”), while 「〜のだ」emphasizes the author’s impression and conclusion.
default.q.n3-28-q58-58.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜かもしれません」expresses an uncertain guess (“might...”), so it does not fit the author's concluding statement of firm, deeply considered insight.
default.q.n3-28-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 3: パーティーの相談をするためにレストランに行ける日 (the day when they can go to the restaurant to discuss the party).

  3. パーティーの相談をするためにレストランに行ける日: The date when he can go to the restaurant to discuss the party.

default.q.n3-28-q59-59.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because the passage states: 「一度お料理、お飲み物の内容について、ご相談したいので、申し訳ございませんが、こちらにいらっしゃれる日を知らせていただけないでしょうか」 (We would like to discuss the menu and drinks, so could you please let us know a day when you can come to the restaurant?). Therefore, the first thing that must be reported (まず) is the date of the visit for discussing the arrangements.
default.q.n3-28-q59-59.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the final number of guests only needs to be reported by three days before the party (「3日前までに」); it does not need to be reported immediately at the outset.
default.q.n3-28-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 4: たくさんかんで食べる (chew thoroughly while eating).

Main point of the passage: To protect and strengthen the teeth, in addition to limiting sweets and brushing after meals, it is important to chew more often so that the jaw muscles and teeth become stronger. default.q.n3-28-q60-60.why.0: (a) Incorrect because not eating too many sweets is mentioned merely as an obvious important measure for protecting one’s teeth (「甘いものを食べすぎないことや、食後の歯磨きが大切なのはもちろん」), not as a specific action the author says they have recently been taking.
default.q.n3-28-q60-60.why.1: (b) Incorrect because brushing one's teeth after eating is common knowledge mentioned as an obviously important practice, not something the author has recently started doing to strengthen their teeth.

default.q.n3-28-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (A short speech takes more time to prepare than a long one.).
default.q.n3-28-q62-62.explanation:
- Main point: The passage describes a conversation between a student and a politician. When the student assumes that a long speech must take a great deal of time to prepare, the politician denies this and explains that if he could speak for as long as he wanted, he could do so immediately, but if he had to give a concise five-minute speech, he would need two weeks of preparation. The politician is emphasizing that a short, concise speech is more difficult and takes more preparation time than a long speech.

- Question:
この政治家が言いたいことはどれか。
(What is this politician trying to say?)

- Answer choices:
  1. 短いスピーチのほうが、長いものより準備に時間がかかる。
     (A short speech takes more time to prepare than a long one.)
  2. 短いスピーチなら、準備をしなくてもすぐにできる。
     (If it is a short speech, it can be given immediately without preparation.)
  3. スピーチが長ければ長いほど、準備に長い時間がかかる。
     (The longer the speech, the more time it takes to prepare.)
  4. スピーチの準備時間が長ければ長いほど、人を感動させられる。
     (The more time spent preparing a speech, the more it can move people.)
default.q.n3-28-q62-62.why.0: (a) Correct. The politician says: 「いくら話してもいいのなら、今すぐでもできますが、5分のスピーチを頼まれたら、準備に２週間はかかるでしょう」 (If I can speak for as long as I like, I can do it right now, but if I am asked to give a five-minute speech, it will take two weeks to prepare). This shows the politician’s view that a short speech takes more preparation than a long one.
default.q.n3-28-q62-62.why.1: (b) Incorrect. This contradicts the passage. The politician says that a five-minute speech would take two weeks to prepare (「5分のスピーチを頼まれたら、準備に２週間はかかるでしょう」), whereas being able to speak immediately without preparation applies only when there is no time limit (「いくら話してもいいのなら、今すぐでもできますが」).
default.q.n3-28-q62-62.why.2: (c) Incorrect. This is the student’s initial assumption (「今日は長いスピーチでしたから、きっと長く準備をされたんでしょうね」), but the politician rejects it with 「そういうことではありません」 and explains that the short speech took more time to prepare.
default.q.n3-28-q62-62.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage only mentions that the student was moved after hearing the politician’s speech. The politician never states or proposes a rule that the longer the preparation, the more moved people will be.
default.q.n3-28-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The number of people who answered that they eat fish dishes at home “more often” increased by more than the number who answered “less often” compared with one year earlier.
default.q.n3-28-q63-63.explanation:
- Relevant summary: A survey of about 1,000 people found that 27.0% had increased the amount of fish they ate at home compared with one year earlier, clearly more than the 15.0% who had decreased it. In addition, “good for one's health” was the most common impression at 82.7%, followed by “delicious” at 72.1%.
- Question: According to this passage, what can be learned from survey ①?
- Choices:
  1. Recently, Japanese people have been eating more meat dishes instead of fish dishes.
  2. More people said that eating fish at home had “increased” than said it had “decreased” compared with one year earlier.
  3. More people had the impression that fish was “delicious” than thought it was “good for their health.”
  4. Compared with one year earlier, awareness that fish is “good for one's health” has spread more widely than awareness that meat is.
default.q.n3-28-q63-63.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage begins by questioning this belief ("It is said that Japanese people have stopped eating much fish and have begun eating meat, but is that really the case?") and the actual survey results show that Japanese people are tending to eat fish again.
default.q.n3-28-q63-63.why.1: (b) Correct because the passage directly cites the survey results: "それによると、1年前に比べて自宅で魚料理を食べることが増えた人は27.0％で、減ったと答えた人（15.0％）よりかなり多い。" (The proportion of people who ate more fish was 27.0%, considerably higher than the 15.0% who said they ate less.)
default.q.n3-28-q63-63.why.2: (c) Incorrect because according to the survey, “good for your health” ranked highest at 82.7%, followed by “delicious” at 72.1% (「魚料理のイメージは「体にいい」が82.7％で、最も多かった。...その次は、「おいしい（72.1％）」だった。」), not the other way around.
default.q.n3-28-q63-63.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage only speculates that awareness of the health benefits of fish is spreading ("魚は健康にいいという知識が広がっているからだろう"). It does not compare fish with meat or compare the extent of the spread with that of one year earlier.
default.q.n3-28-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The older one gets, the more one gradually comes to enjoy eating fish.
default.q.n3-28-q64-64.explanation:
- Relevant summary: Before looking at the survey, the author expressed their initial thought: "I used to think that the older people got, the more they liked fish, but apparently that is not the case (②そうではないらしい)." Therefore, the demonstrative "そう" directly replaces the preceding clause: "年をとればとるほど、魚が好きになる" (the older people get, the more they like fish).
- Translation of the question: In the phrase ②「そうではない」 (apparently that is not the case), what does "そう" (that way) refer to?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. The older people get, the more they gradually come to like fish.
  2. Young people do not like eating fish very much.
  3. Young people like fish more than older people do.
  4. Whether people like or dislike fish has nothing to do with age.
default.q.n3-28-q64-64.why.0: (a) Correct, because the demonstrative "そう" refers to the author’s immediately preceding thought: "私は、年をとればとるほど、魚が好きになると思っていたが、②そうではないらしい。" The structure "年をとればとるほど" means “as one gets older, increasingly,” equivalent to "年をとると次第に".
default.q.n3-28-q64-64.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the idea that “young people do not like eating fish” is not what 「そう」 indicates in this context.
default.q.n3-28-q64-64.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the author's earlier assumption was not that young people preferred fish to older people; the author thought that older people would prefer fish.
default.q.n3-28-q64-64.why.3: (d) Incorrect because this is not the content replaced by the demonstrative "そう" (which refers to the author's initial thoughts).
default.q.n3-28-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 4: An increase in the number of people eating fish (the renewed trend of Japanese people eating fish).
default.q.n3-28-q65-65.explanation:
- Main topic: The article begins by questioning whether Japanese people really eat less fish and more meat, then presents survey data showing that the proportion of people who eat fish has increased (27.0% > 15.0%) and that people of many age groups, including younger people, like fish. It concludes: "These results show that Japanese people have recently started eating fish again..." Therefore, the overall topic is the increase in the number of people who eat fish.
- Question translation: What is the topic of the entire passage?
- Answer choices:
  1. Young people eating meat dishes.
  2. The relationship between liking meat and age.
  3. Young people disliking fish dishes.
  4. The increase in the number of people who eat fish.
default.q.n3-28-q65-65.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the article focuses on analyzing the habit of eating fish dishes, not on young people eating meat dishes.
default.q.n3-28-q65-65.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the survey in the passage concerns fish dishes, such as the proportion of people who eat fish and the age at which people find fish tasty. It does not discuss the relationship between age and liking meat.
default.q.n3-28-q65-65.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the conclusion states that many young people also like fish (“若い人にも魚好きが多い”), which contradicts the claim that they “hate fish dishes.”
default.q.n3-28-q65-65.why.3: (d) Correct. Throughout the passage, the author uses survey data to show that people in Japan have recently started eating more fish again (「この結果から、日本人は最近また、魚を食べるようになってきていて...」). Therefore, the main topic is the increase in the number of people eating fish.
default.q.n3-28-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4: The writer remembers a beloved cherry tree and often talked and read books around its trunk.
default.q.n3-28-q66-66.explanation:
The passage describes the author's childhood memories in the town where they once lived. There was a small shrine with a huge cherry tree that the author loved very much, and they often talked with friends or read books beside it.

Question and answer choices:
*Question:* What memory does the writer have of cherry tree ①?
1. It stood at a large shrine in the town where the writer once lived, and the writer often played beneath its blossoms when they were in full bloom.
2. Twenty years ago, it was not yet a large tree, but it bloomed beautifully every year.
3. Because it was exceptionally beautiful, many people came to see it throughout the year, making the area lively.
4. It was a favorite tree, and the writer often spent time talking and reading around its trunk.
default.q.n3-28-q66-66.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage states that the shrine in the old town was a small shrine (「小さな神社」), not a large shrine (「大きな神社」).
default.q.n3-28-q66-66.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage states that the cherry tree was already a large tree from the author's childhood (「大きな桜の木が１本あった」), not that it was not yet large 20 years ago.
default.q.n3-28-q66-66.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage says that many people came from far away to view the flowers in spring (「春には毎年美しい花を咲かせるので、遠いところからも多くの人が花見に来ていた」), not throughout the year (「一年中」).
default.q.n3-28-q66-66.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage states: 「わたしは、その桜の木が大好きで、よく木のそばで、友達とおしゃべりをしたり、本を読んだりした。」 (I loved that cherry tree and often talked with friends or read books beside it).
default.q.n3-28-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: The reason for putting a rope around the cherry tree.
default.q.n3-28-q67-67.explanation:
**Main point:**
When the author revisited the temple, they saw that a rope had been placed around the cherry tree to keep people away. When the author asked the cleaner why the tree had been surrounded by a rope (その理由), the cleaner explained that the tree’s roots had been trampled so often that the tree had nearly withered and died.

**Question and answer choices:**
*Question:* The phrase “that reason ②” appears in the passage. What is it the reason for?
1. The reason flower-viewing visitors no longer came to the temple.
2. The reason a rope was placed around the cherry tree.
3. The reason the cherry tree nearly withered and died.
4. The reason the temple grounds were cleaned.
default.q.n3-28-q67-67.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage only describes the situation at the time the author arrived: there were not many flower viewers. The question 「その理由」 does not ask why people did not come to the temple.
default.q.n3-28-q67-67.why.1: (b) Correct. The preceding sentence states: 「桜の木の周りはロープで囲まれ、近くに行くことができなくなっていた。神社を掃除していた人に、②その理由を聞くと...」 The demonstrative 「その」 refers to the immediately preceding situation: the area around the cherry tree had been roped off, making it impossible to approach.
default.q.n3-28-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The fact that the cherry tree was nearly dying (「桜が枯れそうになったから」) explains why a barrier was put up; the question 「その理由」asks for the reason why the barrier was placed around the tree.
default.q.n3-28-q67-67.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author encountered someone cleaning the shrine and asked why a rope had been tied around the tree, not why that person was sweeping the shrine grounds.
default.q.n3-28-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4: The writer is disappointed that the tree is no longer as it used to be, but hopes that one day it will bloom brilliantly again.
default.q.n3-28-q68-68.explanation:
**Main point:**
When the author returned to see the cherry tree after more than 20 years, they were disappointed that its blossoms were no longer as magnificent as before and that a rope barrier had been placed around the trunk because its roots had been trampled. Although they regretted not being able to approach it, they still hoped that the tree would recover soon and continue producing beautiful blossoms in the years to come.

**Question and answer choices:**
*Question:* What did the writer think when they saw the cherry tree’s current condition?
1. They regretted not being able to approach it, but accepted it because the area needed to be cleaned up.
2. They felt sorry that a rope barrier had been put up, but accepted it because it was necessary to compact the soil.
3. They were astonished that not a single flower had bloomed, but hoped the tree would recover soon.
4. They were disappointed that it was different from the past, but hoped that someday it would once again produce beautiful blossoms to admire.
default.q.n3-28-q68-68.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The reason it is impossible to get close is the protective rope around the tree roots, not that it is for cleaning (「掃除のため」).
default.q.n3-28-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Being stepped on causes the soil to become compacted, preventing the roots from getting enough air; this weakens the plants. The ropes are put up to prevent this, not “to make the soil compact” (「土を固くするため」).
default.q.n3-28-q68-68.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage states that the cherry tree “was not blooming as beautifully as it did in the past” (「昔ほど美しく咲いていなくて」), not that it had no blossoms at all (「少しも咲いていない」).
default.q.n3-28-q68-68.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage says: 「桜は、昔ほど美しく咲いていなくて、がっかりした。」 (I was disappointed that the cherry blossoms were not blooming as beautifully as they used to) and 「木のそばに行けなかったのは残念だったが、早く元気になって、また美しい花を咲かせてほしい。」 (Although it was unfortunate that I could not go near the tree, I hope it recovers soon and blooms beautiful flowers again).
default.q.n3-28-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 「そういう人」 refers to people who quit immediately after starting jogging (after just two or three days).
default.q.n3-28-q69-69.explanation:
- Main point: In the sentence 「せっかくジョギングを始めても、2 日か３日でやめてしまう人がいます。①そういう人は、走る楽しみを見つけられないまま、走ることは苦しいものだと思ってしまうのです。」, the demonstrative expression 「そういう人」 directly refers to the people mentioned in the previous sentence: those who make the effort to start jogging but quit after only two or three days.
- Question translation: Who does ①「そういう人」 (people like that) refer to?
- Answer choices:
  1. People who have just started jogging.
  2. People who start jogging and quit right away.
  3. People who think jogging is difficult.
  4. People who are able to enjoy jogging.
default.q.n3-28-q69-69.why.0: (a) Incorrect. This choice refers to “someone who has just started jogging,” whereas the previous sentence specifically describes someone who starts but gives up after two or three days (2 日か３日でやめてしまう人).
default.q.n3-28-q69-69.why.1: (b) Correct. The preceding sentence states: 「せっかくジョギングを始めても、2 日か３日でやめてしまう人がいます。」(Some people make the effort to start jogging but quit after only two or three days.) The demonstrative pronoun 「そういう人」 directly refers to these people.
default.q.n3-28-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect. “Thinking that running is difficult” is the consequence or interpretation explained in the following clause, 「走ることは苦しいものだと思ってしまう」. It is not what the demonstrative expression 「そういう人」refers to from the preceding sentence.
default.q.n3-28-q69-69.why.3: (d) Incorrect. This is completely contrary to the passage, which says that this person “could not find the enjoyment in running” (走る楽しみを見つけられないまま).
default.q.n3-28-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The next goal is slightly higher than the previous one.
default.q.n3-28-q70-70.explanation:
- Main point: The author says that the joy of running comes from gradually raising one’s goal (走る楽しみは、目標を少しずつ高くしていくことで生まれます). After achieving the set goal, setting the "next goal" (次の目標) means continuing by raising the goal slightly higher than before.
- Question translation: What kind of goal is ②「次の目標」(the next goal)?
- Answer choices:
  1. A goal of running as hard and fast as possible.
  2. A goal of running as hard as possible over a long distance.
  3. A goal that is slightly higher than before.
  4. A goal that is much higher than before.
default.q.n3-28-q70-70.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage does not advise setting a goal of running as fast as possible. It emphasizes gradually raising the goal (「少しずつ高くしていく」) and making a manageable plan.
default.q.n3-28-q70-70.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage does not mention setting the excessive goal of pushing oneself to run a very long distance.
default.q.n3-28-q70-70.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: 「走る楽しみは、目標を少しずつ高くしていくことで生まれます。」 and 「目標のとおり走れたら、②次の目標を決める。」 Once someone has run according to the target, setting the next target means raising it slightly higher than before (少しずつ).
default.q.n3-28-q70-70.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「かなり」(quite a lot, very high) conflicts with 「少しずつ」(little by little) stated in the passage.
default.q.n3-28-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is 4: First run 2 km at nearly walking speed, gradually increase the speed, and then gradually increase the distance.
default.q.n3-28-q71-71.explanation:
- Main point: The author recommends a suitable plan for beginners: during the first month, run 2 km at a pace of 10 minutes per kilometer (almost walking), then gradually increase the pace to 8 and 7 minutes per kilometer. In the following months, gradually increase the distance, first running 2 km without worrying about time and then increasing it to 3 km.
- Question translation: What kind of plan is considered suitable for ③people who are planning to start running?
- Answer choices:
  1. First run 1 km in 7 minutes, then gradually increase the speed until you can run 1 km in 5 minutes.
  2. First run 2 km in 10 minutes, then gradually increase the distance until you can run a marathon.
  3. First run 1 km without worrying about time, then gradually increase the distance until you can run 3 km.
  4. First run 2 km at a walking pace, then gradually increase the speed and lengthen the distance step by step.
default.q.n3-28-q71-71.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage recommends starting at a pace of 1 km in about 10 minutes (almost walking), not immediately at a pace of 1 km in 7 minutes.
default.q.n3-28-q71-71.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage says 「1 キロ10分程度の速さ」 (a pace of about 10 minutes per kilometer, meaning about 20 minutes for 2 km). The choice saying “run 2 km in 10 minutes” is too fast and misinterprets the figures.
default.q.n3-28-q71-71.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The instructions say to run 2 km at about 10 minutes per kilometer during the first month, and only in the following month to run 2 km without worrying about the time it takes (かかる時間を気にしないで 2 キロを走り). It does not say to begin by running 1 km without paying attention to the time.
default.q.n3-28-q71-71.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage states: 「まず、最初の１か月は、とにかく2 キロを、1 キロ10分程度の速さで走ることから始めます。これは、走るより歩くのに近い速さです。」, 「次第に、１キロを8分、7分とスピードを上げていきます。」, and 「少しずつ距離を延ばしていきます。」 The entire training plan matches choice 4 perfectly.
default.q.n3-28-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 2: How to enjoy jogging (ジョギングの楽しみ方).
default.q.n3-28-q72-72.explanation:
- Main point summary: The passage begins by defining jogging as a sport practiced for enjoyment, analyzes why beginners easily lose motivation, and presents a step-by-step method of setting plans and goals to find enjoyment in jogging (「このように、目標を決め、計画を立てて走ることで、ジョギングを楽しむことができるのです。」). Therefore, the overall theme is "How to enjoy jogging."
- Question translation: What is the theme of this entire passage?
- Answer choices:
  1. The rules of jogging.
  2. How to enjoy jogging.
  3. The importance of running.
  4. The difficulty of running.
default.q.n3-28-q72-72.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage does not mention the rules or regulations of running competitions.
default.q.n3-28-q72-72.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage begins: 「ジョギングは、走ることを楽しむスポーツです。」 and concludes: 「このように、目標を決め、計画を立てて走ることで、ジョギングを楽しむことができるのです。」 Throughout the passage, the author explains how setting realistic goals and making a plan can help people enjoy jogging.
default.q.n3-28-q72-72.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage does not focus on the importance or benefits of jogging for health or daily life.
default.q.n3-28-q72-72.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author only mentions the initial difficulty beginners experience in order to offer a solution that helps them enjoy running; the main topic is not the difficulty of running itself.
default.q.n3-28-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3 (1,200円) because the day of use is Sunday (a day off/weekend), the location is a sports field (運動場), and the user is not a resident of Wakaba City.
default.q.n3-28-q73-73.explanation:
Summary: Chan wants to play soccer with his friends at the sports park’s athletic field (運動場) in Wakaba City on Sunday, February 11, from 10:00 to 14:00. Neither Chan nor his friends are residents of Wakaba City (わかば市民ではない), so the nonresident Sunday rate for using the athletic field is 1,200 yen per hour.

Translation of the question: Chan wants to play soccer with his friends at the sports park’s athletic field in Wakaba City. He wants to use it on Sunday, February 11, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. If neither Chan nor his friends is a resident of Wakaba City, how much is the fee per hour?
Translation of the choices:
1. 800 yen
2. 1,000 yen
3. 1,200 yen
4. 1,400 yen
default.q.n3-28-q73-73.why.0: (a) 800円 is the price for Wakaba city residents using the stadium on Sundays or holidays (or the weekday price for another category), and does not apply to nonresidents using it on a Sunday.
default.q.n3-28-q73-73.why.1: (b) 1,000円 is the price for people from outside the city using the stadium on a weekday (平日), which does not match the actual date, Sunday, February 11 (2月11日の日曜日).
default.q.n3-28-q73-73.why.2: (c) According to the fee table, for the sports field (運動場), on Sunday (日曜日), when the applicant is not a Wakaba City resident (わかば市民ではない), the usage fee is 1,200円 per hour.
default.q.n3-28-q73-73.why.3: (d) 1,400円 is a fee higher than the stated rate for the stadium (usually the weekend fee for using the 体育館 by people from outside the city), not the fee for the athletic field (運動場).
default.q.n3-28-q74-74.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2 because the rules clearly state that the person registering must be at least 18 years old.
default.q.n3-28-q74-74.explanation:
Summary: The instructions for registering to use Wakaba City Sports Park state that reservations are accepted from one month in advance by phone or online; registrants must be at least 18 years old; the fee must be paid at the counter before or on the day of use; and Wakaba residents who wish to receive the discounted rate must bring proof of residence when paying.

Question translation: When registering to use Wakaba City Sports Park, what must be done?
Answer choices:
1. Register one month before the date of use.
2. A person aged 18 or older must register.
3. Pay the fee at the time of registration.
4. Bring proof of address when registering.
default.q.n3-28-q74-74.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the article says 「申し込みの受付は、利用日の1か月前から」, meaning applications begin to be accepted “from one month before the usage date” (1か月前から), not that the application deadline is “one month before” (1か月前までに).
default.q.n3-28-q74-74.why.1: (b) Matches the quotation in the passage exactly: 「なお、申し込みは18歳以上の方がしてください」 (“In addition, applicants must be at least 18 years old”).
default.q.n3-28-q74-74.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because 「利用当日までに受付でお支払いください」means payment must be made at the reception desk by the day of use at the latest. It is not required at the time of application (申し込みのとき).
default.q.n3-28-q74-74.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because according to the passage, 「わかば市民は割引料金で利用できますので... 料金を支払われるときに住所を証明できるものをお持ちください」, proof of address must be presented when paying in order to receive the resident discount. It is not required when applying (申し込みのとき), nor is it mandatory for everyone.
default.q.n3-28-q1-1.explanation:
Sentence meaning: I hear that this summer is the hottest summer in the past 10 years.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 過去 (かこ).
- Example: 過去の失敗を教訓にして前へ進む。(Use past failures as lessons and move forward.)
default.q.n3-28-q1-1.why.0: (a) かきょ: The on-reading of 去 is incorrect in this compound (去 is read as こ in 過去).
default.q.n3-28-q1-1.why.1: (b) かこう: The long vowel is incorrectly added; 過 has only the short on-reading か.
default.q.n3-28-q1-1.why.2: (c) かこ: Correct answer; 過去 is read as かこ and means "the past."
default.q.n3-28-q1-1.why.3: (d) かきょう: The on-readings of both kanji are incorrect.
default.q.n3-28-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (とうちゃく).
default.q.n3-28-q2-2.explanation:
Meaning: We will arrive at Tokyo Station in five minutes.
- 到着 (とうちゃく): arrival, reaching a destination.
- Example: 飛行機は予定通りに目的地へ到着した。(The airplane arrived at its destination as scheduled.)
default.q.n3-28-q2-2.why.0: (a) とうつく: Confuses the on-reading「とう」of 到 with the kun-reading「つく」of the verb 着く.

default.q.n3-28-q13-13.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 券: ticket, voucher (けん).

default.q.n3-28-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 4: ほかに約束があったので、パーティーの誘いを断りました。

default.q.n3-28-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 仕事が残っているけど、そろそろ12時なので昼休みにしよう。

default.q.n3-29-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 1. なんか.
