default.q.n3-29-q41-41.why.0: (a) Correct. 「〜なんか」is the colloquial form of「〜など」, used to make a light suggestion or give a casual example in spoken language:「〜なんかどう？」.
default.q.n3-29-q41-41.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「ばかり」(nothing but, only) is not used in the suggestion pattern「これ〜どう」.
default.q.n3-29-q41-41.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「へ」 is a particle indicating the direction of movement, so it does not fit the grammar here.
default.q.n3-29-q41-41.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The particle 「に」 cannot stand alone to form a natural structure for giving an example or suggestion, such as 「なんか」.
default.q.n3-29-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 欲しがっている.
default.q.n3-29-q42-42.explanation:
- Meaning: “Mom: ‘Is the child who bought candy earlier Takeru?’ — Child: ‘No, it isn’t. It is the child over there crying and asking for candy.’”
- Kanji meanings: 菓子 (snacks, sweets), 買 (buy), 子 (child), 泣 (cry).
- Example: 弟は新しいおもちゃを欲しがっている。(My younger brother is insisting that he wants a new toy.)
default.q.n3-29-q42-42.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「欲しい」is used directly only for the first person’s feelings and takes the particle が; it is not used directly with を to modify a third person’s action.
default.q.n3-29-q42-42.why.1: (b) Correct. The structure 「〜欲しがる」 expresses a third person’s desire based on outward behavior, while 「〜ている」 describes a specific action in progress.
default.q.n3-29-q42-42.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「欲しそうな」(seeming to want) does not naturally combine with the particle「お菓子を」to modify the specific action of crying and asking for candy.
default.q.n3-29-q42-42.why.3: (d) Incorrect.「欲しがってみる」(to try wanting something) does not make sense in Japanese.
default.q.n3-29-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 3. うかがっても.
default.q.n3-29-q43-43.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: “Student: ‘Excuse me, teacher. There is something I would like to ask your advice about. May I come to your office after class?’ — Teacher: ‘Of course. That's fine.’”
- Sino-Japanese readings: 学生 (student), 先生 (teacher), 相談 (consultation, discussion), 授業 (class), 後 (after), 研究室 (research room, office).
- Example: 明日、先生のお宅にうかがってもよろしいでしょうか。(Would it be all right if I visited your home tomorrow?)
default.q.n3-29-q43-43.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「来られる」 is the respectful form of 来る, used for a superior's action (the teacher), not for a student's action.
default.q.n3-29-q43-43.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「いらっしゃる」 is the honorific form of 行く/来る and is used for someone of higher status, not for the student's own action.
default.q.n3-29-q43-43.why.2: (c) Correct. 「うかがう」(伺う) is the humble form (謙譲語) of 「行く/訪ねる」(to go/visit), appropriately used when a student visits a teacher.
default.q.n3-29-q43-43.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「行かれる」is the honorific form of 行く and is not used for the speaker’s own action as a student.
default.q.n3-29-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 4. みたらどうでしょう.
default.q.n3-29-q44-44.explanation:
Meaning:
A: "I've had a headache since yesterday. Do you know of any good hospitals?"
B: "Let me see. How about trying ABC Hospital?"
- Kanji notes: 昨日 means "yesterday"; 頭 means "head"; 痛 means "pain"; 病院 means "hospital"; 知 means "to know."
- Example: 一度専門のお医者さんに診てもらったらどうでしょう。(Why don't you have a specialist examine you?)
default.q.n3-29-q44-44.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「〜みさせてください」 (please let me try…) is used when the speaker asks permission to do something, not when advising someone else.
default.q.n3-29-q44-44.why.1: (b) Incorrect.「〜みてもいいでしょうか」(May I try doing it?) is used to ask permission for one's own action.
default.q.n3-29-q44-44.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「みさせてほしいのですが」 (I would like to be allowed to try...) is used to ask permission for oneself, so it is inappropriate here.
default.q.n3-29-q44-44.why.3: (d) Correct. The sentence pattern「〜てみたらどうでしょう(か)」is used to give advice or make a suggestion politely and considerately.
default.q.n3-29-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 4. だけで.
default.q.n3-29-q45-45.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: “This confectionery is made only from flour, eggs, and sugar. It does not use butter or cow’s milk at all.”
- 菓子 means confectionery, 小麦粉 means wheat flour, 卵 means egg, 砂糖 means sugar, 使 means use, and 牛乳 means cow’s milk.
- Example: この料理は野菜と塩だけでできています。(This dish is made only from vegetables and salt.)
default.q.n3-29-q45-45.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「ほどが」 is wrong both in expressing degree and in the use of the particle before 「できています」.
default.q.n3-29-q45-45.why.1: (b) Wrong. 「ほどで」indicates degree or approximate extent; it is not used to list the materials that make up an object.
default.q.n3-29-q45-45.why.2: (c) Wrong. The particle 「が」does not combine with 「できています」in the pattern describing the material or ingredients from which a product is made.
default.q.n3-29-q45-45.why.3: (d) Correct. This combines the limiting adverb「だけ」(only) with the particle「で」in the structure「〜（原料）でできている」(made from a particular material).
default.q.n3-29-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 2. までには.
default.q.n3-29-q46-46.explanation:
- Meaning: "A: Excuse me, where is Mr. Yamada?" - "B: Mr. Yamada is in a meeting, but I think the meeting will end before 11:30."
- Key vocabulary: 会社 (company), 会議 (meeting), 時半 (half past the hour), 終 (end), 思 (think).
- Example: レポートは明日の午前中までには提出してください。(Please submit the report by tomorrow morning.)
default.q.n3-29-q46-46.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「までは」is used for an action or state that continues until a certain point; it does not combine with an endpoint verb such as 「終わる」.
default.q.n3-29-q46-46.why.1: (b) Correct.「までに」sets a deadline by which a punctual action such as「終わる」must be completed;「は」emphasizes the estimated time.
default.q.n3-29-q46-46.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「までも」means “even” or “as far as,” and does not indicate a deadline or end point in time.
default.q.n3-29-q46-46.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「までにも」 is not a standard limiting structure in this context.
default.q.n3-29-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 3. ようなら.
default.q.n3-29-q47-47.explanation:
- Meaning of the sentence: "Younger sister: 'I'm going out to dinner with a friend today, and then I'll come home.' - Older brother: 'Got it. If it looks like you'll be later than 9, I'll come pick you up, so remember to call.'"
- Kanji readings and meanings: 妹 (いもうと; younger sister), 友 (とも; friend), 晩 (ばん; evening), 飯 (めし; meal, rice), 兄 (あに; older brother), 時 (じ; time), 過 (か; exceed, pass), 迎 (むか; pick up, welcome), 電話 (でんわ; telephone, call).
- Example: 雨が降るようなら、試合は中止になります。(If it looks like it will rain, the game will be canceled.)
default.q.n3-29-q47-47.why.0: (a) Incorrect.「らしい」does not combine directly with「なら」(this violates the grammar rule).
default.q.n3-29-q47-47.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「らしいのに」(although it seems to be...) expresses contrast or concession, so it does not fit a following clause that gives a condition for going to pick someone up.
default.q.n3-29-q47-47.why.2: (c) Correct. The structure 「V plain form + ようなら」 (“if it seems that / if it is the case that...”) presents a hypothetical situation that may occur.
default.q.n3-29-q47-47.why.3: (d) Incorrect.「ようなのに」(although it seems that...) expresses concession or contrast and does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-29-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 話しかけないほうがよさそうだな.
default.q.n3-29-q48-48.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: "Younger brother: 'Do you know where Dad is?' - Older brother: 'He was in his room a little while ago, but he looked very busy.' - Younger brother: 'I see. In that case, it seems better not to talk to him right now. I want to discuss my plans for further education with him.'"
- Sino-Japanese readings: 父 (ふ: father), 部屋 (へや: room), 忙 (ぼう: busy), 今 (いま: now), 話 (はなし: talk), 進学 (しんがく: continuing one's education), 相談 (そうだん: discussion, consultation).
- Example: 疲れているときは、無理をしないほうがよさそうだ。(When you are tired, it seems better not to push yourself too hard.)
default.q.n3-29-q48-48.why.0: (a) Correct. The advice/judgment structure 「〜ないほうがいい」 (“should not...”) changes into the conjectural form 「〜ないほうがよさそうだ」 (“it seems better not to...” ).
default.q.n3-29-q48-48.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「話しかけなくてもよさそう」 (“it seems that it is okay not to start a conversation”) means that talking is unnecessary, which is the opposite of the younger sibling’s desire to discuss the matter (相談).
default.q.n3-29-q48-48.why.2: (c) Incorrect.「〜いいそうだ」is the hearsay form (it is said to be good), whereas the conjectural form of「いい」must be「よさそう」.
default.q.n3-29-q48-48.why.3: (d) Incorrect. It is unsuitable both in meaning for the context and in the form used for reported speech.
default.q.n3-29-q49-49.verdict: Correct order: 3 → 4 → 2 → 1. The correct answer is 2 (the ★ position is 練習に来ないで).
default.q.n3-29-q49-49.explanation:
Complete sentence: A「来週、試合なのにちっとも練習に来ないで何をやっていたんですか。」 B「すみません。」
Meaning: A: "The match is next week, yet you haven't come to practice at all. What on earth have you been doing?" — B: "I'm sorry."
default.q.n3-29-q49-49.why.0: (a) 「何をやっていた」: It occupies the fourth position and comes directly before the sentence ending「んですか」to form a questioning, reproachful expression: 「何をやっていたんですか」(What were you doing?).
default.q.n3-29-q49-49.why.1: (b) 「練習に来ないで」: Belongs in position 3 (the ★ slot), following the negative adverb 「ちっとも」to form 「ちっとも練習に来ないで」(without coming to practice at all...).
default.q.n3-29-q49-49.why.2: (c) 「なのに」: It appears in the first position, following the noun 「試合」, and expresses a contrastive concessive relationship: “even though the match is next week.”
default.q.n3-29-q49-49.why.3: (d) 「ちっとも」: It occupies the second position and is an adverb meaning “not at all,” modifying the negative phrase「練習に来ないで」that follows.
default.q.n3-29-q50-50.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 1 → 4 → 2. The correct answer is 4 (が fits in the ★ blank).
default.q.n3-29-q50-50.explanation:
Complete sentence: あの美術館は曜日によって閉まる時間が違うから窓口で確認したほうがいいよ。
Meaning: That art museum closes at different times depending on the day of the week, so you should check at the ticket counter.
default.q.n3-29-q50-50.why.0: (a) 「閉まる時間」 is in the second position and is a noun phrase functioning as the subject of the predicate 「違う」.
default.q.n3-29-q50-50.why.1: (b) 「違うから」 is in the fourth position. It is a predicate expressing difference, followed by 「から」 (“because”), linking it to the advice 「窓口で確認したほうがいいよ」.
default.q.n3-29-q50-50.why.2: (c) 「によって」 is in position 1, directly after the noun 「曜日」, forming the structure 「Nによって」(depending on N).
default.q.n3-29-q50-50.why.3: (d) 「が」occupies the third position (the ★ slot) as the subject particle after「閉まる時間」, forming the predicate「違う」(閉まる時間が違う).
default.q.n3-29-q51-51.verdict: The correct order is: 1 → 4 → 2 → 3. The correct answer is 2 (the ★ is 大変).
default.q.n3-29-q51-51.explanation:
Complete sentence: 自分で野菜を作ってみて、おいしい野菜を育てること[が] [どんなに] [大変] [ことか] わかりました。
Meaning: After trying to grow vegetables myself, I realized just how difficult it is to grow delicious vegetables.
default.q.n3-29-q51-51.why.0: (a) 「ことが」: In position 1, it nominalizes the verb phrase 「おいしい野菜を育てる」as 「育てること」, which serves as the subject with the particle 「が」.
default.q.n3-29-q51-51.why.1: (b) 「大変」: It is in the third position (★), a na-adjective expressing difficulty or hardship, functioning as the predicate in the exclamatory structure 「どんなに～ことか」.
default.q.n3-29-q51-51.why.2: (c) 「ことか」: Occupying the fourth position, it combines with 「どんなに」 before it to form the exclamatory degree pattern 「どんなに～ことか」 (how very; to what extent) before the verb 「わかりました」.
default.q.n3-29-q51-51.why.3: (d) 「どんなに」: It appears in the second position as the adverb introducing the exclamatory pattern 「どんなに～ことか」.
default.q.n3-29-q52-52.verdict: Correct order: 4 → 2 → 1 → 3. The correct answer is 1 (the ★ position is  の).
default.q.n3-29-q52-52.explanation:
Complete sentence: A「今度のさよならパーティーで、みんなで歌う歌は、これでいいですか」 B「すみません。この歌は好きなんですが、少しむずかしいですからほかのにしてほしいです。」
Meaning: A: "Is this song suitable for everyone to sing at the upcoming farewell party?" B: "I'm sorry. I like this song, but it's a little difficult, so I'd like you to choose another one."
default.q.n3-29-q52-52.why.0: (a) 「 の」: It appears in position 3 (the ★ gap), replacing the noun 歌 (song), and combines with 「ほか」to form 「ほかの」(another song / something else).
default.q.n3-29-q52-52.why.1: (b) 「ほか」comes in position 2 and is a noun meaning “other”; combined with「の」, it forms「ほかの」.
default.q.n3-29-q52-52.why.2: (c) 「に」: In the fourth position, it follows the noun 「ほかの」to form the choice pattern 「～にする」(choose or switch to something else), together with 「～してほしい」(want someone to do something).
default.q.n3-29-q52-52.why.3: (d) 「から」: It occupies the first position and is a conjunction expressing a reason. It follows the polite predicate「むずかしいです」and connects it to the suggestion that follows (because it is difficult...).
default.q.n3-29-q53-53.verdict: The correct order is: 1 → 4 → 3 → 2. The correct answer is 3 (the ★ position is やらせて).
default.q.n3-29-q53-53.explanation:
Complete sentence: 最近、子どもがピアノを習いたいと言いだした。わたしは、子どもがしたいと思うことはやらせてやりたいと思っている。
Meaning: Recently, my child started saying that they wanted to learn the piano. I want to let my child do whatever they want to do.
default.q.n3-29-q53-53.why.0: (a) 「したい」 is in the first position, following the subject 「子どもが」 and combining with 「と思うことは」 to form 「子どもがしたいと思うことは」 (“the things the child wants to do”).
default.q.n3-29-q53-53.why.1: (b) 「やりたい」: It occupies the fourth position and combines with the te-form causative 「やらせて」 before it to form 「やらせてやりたい」 (“want to let my child do it / want to give my child the opportunity to do it”), followed by 「と思っている」.
default.q.n3-29-q53-53.why.2: (c) 「やらせて」: It occupies the third position (the ★ slot), is the -te form of the causative 「やる」(to let someone do something), and combines with 「～てやる」(to do something for someone) to form 「やらせてやる」.
default.q.n3-29-q53-53.why.3: (d) 「と思うことは」 occupies the second position, following 「したい」 to form a nominalized clause functioning as the object: 「したいと思うことは」 (as for the things you think you want to do...).
default.q.n3-29-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 3. わかってきました.
default.q.n3-29-q54-54.explanation: In the previous sentence, the author describes their initial question after arriving in Japan: "最初は、人が多くて大変なのに、なぜみんなが電車を使おうとするのか不思議でした" (At first, I wondered why everyone tried to use trains even though they were so crowded and inconvenient). The conjunction "しかし" (however), together with the time expression "東京に来て3か月たって" (three months after coming to Tokyo), indicates a change in understanding from the past to the present. The grammar pattern V-てくる describes a gradual change or development from the past up to the present point ("I gradually came to understand" / "I began to understand"), so "わかってきました" is the most appropriate answer.
default.q.n3-29-q54-54.why.0: (a) 「わかってくるほず（はず）です」means “will surely gradually come to understand,” which does not fit the writer’s account of their own actual experience after living there for three months.
default.q.n3-29-q54-54.why.1: (b) 「わかっていくそうです」 conveys hearsay about an ongoing future change. It is not used to describe the author's own realization from the past up to the present.
default.q.n3-29-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「わかってきました」 combines with the 〜てくる structure to express a gradual change in understanding from the past to the present ("I gradually came to understand"), which fits the author's context and experience exactly.
default.q.n3-29-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「わかっていったようです」uses ~ていく and the conjectural form ようです, giving an outside observer’s impression. It is unnatural when describing the speaker’s own understanding.
default.q.n3-29-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 4. それから.
default.q.n3-29-q55-55.explanation: The passage explains why people prefer traveling by train in Tokyo. The author begins with the conjunction "まず" (first / to begin with) to introduce the first advantage: a network of many lines and more than 600 convenient stations reaching all over the city. The blank 【20】 begins the next sentence, which introduces a second advantage: trains are rarely late and run at very short intervals. Therefore, the additive sequencing conjunction "それから" (in addition / besides that) is the most appropriate choice.
default.q.n3-29-q55-55.why.0: (a) 「したがって」 is a conjunction expressing a cause-and-effect relationship (“therefore” or “consequently”). It is inappropriate because the following sentence adds an independent advantage rather than a result arising from the previous sentence.
default.q.n3-29-q55-55.why.1: (b) 「つまり」 is used to summarize or rephrase the preceding sentence (“in other words”); it does not fit a context in which another advantage is being added.
default.q.n3-29-q55-55.why.2: (c) 「たとえば」 introduces an illustrative example (for example). It is inappropriate here because trains being rarely delayed and arriving quickly is not an example of having many stations.
default.q.n3-29-q55-55.why.3: (d) 「それから」 is a conjunction used to add information or continue a list (in addition, furthermore). It follows 「まず」 (first) in the preceding sentence to add the second advantage of Tokyo's railway system.
default.q.n3-29-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 3. こういう電車.
default.q.n3-29-q56-56.explanation: In the preceding sentences, the author lists a number of convenient features of Tokyo's train system (many lines, many stations that make it possible to go anywhere, punctuality, and one train every 3 minutes). The phrase "こういう電車なら" (If trains are this convenient...) uses the demonstrative "こういう" to generalize all the features and advantages just described, leading to the conclusion that it is understandable that everyone would want to use them.
default.q.n3-29-q56-56.why.0: (a) 「ある電車」 means “a certain train” or “some train,” without specifying which one. It is unsuitable for summarizing the superior features of the Tokyo trains described in the preceding sentences.
default.q.n3-29-q56-56.why.1: (b) 「そこの電車」 usually indicates a location (“the train over there”), so it is unnatural when referring to the type or characteristics of an electric train.
default.q.n3-29-q56-56.why.2: (c) 「こういう電車」 means "trains like this"—convenient, with an extensive network, few delays, and frequent services—so it accurately refers to all the features of trains mentioned immediately beforehand.
default.q.n3-29-q56-56.why.3: (d) 「どちらかの電車」means “one of the two trains,” which does not fit because the context contains no choice between two specific subjects.
default.q.n3-29-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 2. なぜなのか.
default.q.n3-29-q57-57.explanation: The author presents a paradox: trains arrive continuously, so there should be no need to hurry, yet everyone in the station moves very quickly. The phrase "わたしは、これがなぜなのかわかりません" means “I do not understand why this is so” or “I do not understand the reason for this.” The interrogative なぜ (why), combined with the embedded-question marker なのか, forms an indirect question expressing the author’s puzzlement about the phenomenon being observed.
default.q.n3-29-q57-57.why.0: (a) 「答えなのか」 means “whether it is the answer,” which does not fit the context, where the author is wondering about the reason for everyone's hurried actions.
default.q.n3-29-q57-57.why.1: (b) 「なぜなのか」 combines the question word なぜ (“why”) with the embedded-question expression なのか, forming the phrase “the reason why.” This fits the context of wondering why people remain hurried even though trains arrive one after another.
default.q.n3-29-q57-57.why.2: (c) 「理由なのか」 means “could it be the reason?”, which does not correctly express the question of identifying the cause. (If 理由 is used, it should be written as 「その理由がわかりません」.)
default.q.n3-29-q57-57.why.3: (d) 「だれなのか」 means “who someone is,” so it is incorrect because the author is wondering about the cause of a behavioral phenomenon, not asking about someone’s identity.
default.q.n3-29-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 1. なるのでしょうか.
default.q.n3-29-q58-58.explanation: The author has been in Japan for only three months and does not yet understand why everyone is in such a hurry. The hypothetical clause 「日本に長く住んでいたら」(If I lived in Japan for a long time...) presents a future situation. The author wonders whether they, too, will eventually become as hurried as everyone else (「わたしも同じようになるのでしょうか」). The following sentence, 「留学生活が終わるころには、答えがわかるのかもしれません」(Perhaps I will know the answer by the time my study-abroad life ends), directly continues this self-questioning. Therefore, the self-questioning ending 「なるのでしょうか」is the correct answer.
default.q.n3-29-q58-58.why.0: (a) 「なるのでしょうか」 uses the interrogative ending 「のでしょうか」 to express wondering or asking oneself, as in “Will it become that way?” It expresses uncertainty about the future while imagining “if I live in Japan for a long time,” which fits the following sentence: “Perhaps I will know the answer someday.”
default.q.n3-29-q58-58.why.1: (b) 「なったでしょう」 is the past-tense conjectural form, meaning “they probably became that way.” It does not fit a supposition about the future of someone who has been in Japan for only three months.
default.q.n3-29-q58-58.why.2: (c) 「なってしまうのです」 emphatically asserts an unintended result (“it will surely end up becoming that way”), so it cannot express the questioning uncertainty needed to connect with the following sentence.
default.q.n3-29-q58-58.why.3: (d) 「なってしまいました。」 is in the past tense, meaning “it ended up becoming that way.” This is factually incorrect because the author has only been in Japan for 3 months and still does not understand that behavior.
default.q.n3-29-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Explaining the malfunction to the repair technician.
default.q.n3-29-q59-59.explanation:
Main point:
Teacher Shimoda left Nakamura a note explaining that the printer was malfunctioning because printed pages were getting stained with ink, and that a repair technician was scheduled to arrive at 10:00. Since the teacher would be teaching, Nakamura was asked to take the technician to the printer when they arrived, show them the sample page with the printing error that had been left there, and explain the problem. After the repair was complete, Nakamura was to prepare enough materials for the afternoon seminar.

Question translation:
What must Nakamura do when the repair technician arrives?

Answer choices:
1. Go to the classroom to call Teacher Shimoda.
2. Put the printed page next to the printer.
3. Explain the malfunction to the repair technician.
4. Ask the repair technician to print the materials for the seminar.
default.q.n3-29-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect because Shimoda is teaching at that time and asks Nakamura to take the technician to the printer; he does not ask Nakamura to call the teacher from the classroom.
default.q.n3-29-q59-59.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the defective sample printout had already been placed by the teacher at the printer (「実際に印刷した紙がプリンターのところに置いてありますから」); Nakamura was not the one who did this.
default.q.n3-29-q59-59.why.2: (c) Correct because the passage says: 「実際に印刷した紙がプリンターのところに置いてありますから、それを修理の人に見せて説明してください。」 (“The actual printed paper is placed by the printer, so show it to the repair person and explain the situation.”)
default.q.n3-29-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect because after the repair, Nakamura must prepare the seminar materials in advance (quote: 「修理がすんだら、午後のゼミの資料を人数分用意しておいてください」), not ask the repair technician to print them.
default.q.n3-29-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3: Reply by July 8 and pay for the commemorative gift by July 31.
default.q.n3-29-q60-60.explanation:
- Main point: An email to students announces a farewell party for Professor Kawashima. For people who cannot attend, the email gives two important deadlines:
1. Reply by July 8 to say whether they will attend or not (7月8日 (金) までに参加するかどうかを返信してください).
2. Those who cannot attend only need to pay for the commemorative gift during July (参加できない人は、記念品代だけを7月中に払ってください — that is, by July 31).

- Question translation: After reading this email, what must a person who cannot attend do?
- Answer choices:
1. They do not need to reply, but must pay for the commemorative gift by July 31.
2. They do not need to reply, but must pay for the commemorative gift on August 10.
3. They must reply by July 8 and pay for the commemorative gift by July 31.
4. They must reply by July 8 and pay for the commemorative gift on August 10.
default.q.n3-29-q60-60.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the notice asks recipients to reply by July 8 (Friday) stating whether they will participate or not: "7月8日 (金) までに参加するかどうかを返信してください". Therefore, even those who will not participate must reply.
default.q.n3-29-q60-60.why.1: (b) Incorrect because even those who are not participating must send a reply by July 8 and pay for the souvenir during July (7月中), rather than wait until August 10.
default.q.n3-29-q60-60.why.2: (c) Correct because the passage says: “7月8日 (金) までに参加するかどうかを返信してください” (reply by July 8 whether you will participate) and “参加できない人は、記念品代だけを7月中に払ってください” (those who cannot participate need only pay for the commemorative gift during July, that is, by July 31).
default.q.n3-29-q60-60.why.3: (d) Incorrect because people who are not participating must pay for the souvenir during July (7月中に), whereas August 10 is the day of the party, when payment is collected directly at the venue from participants.
default.q.n3-29-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The hotel did not throw away the document; it kept it, which allowed the author to find it again.
default.q.n3-29-q61-61.explanation:
• **Question:**
The passage says it was “a happy event.” What kind of event was it?

• **Answer choices:**
1. The company’s difficult problem was finally resolved.
2. The hotel staff cleaned up and organized the author’s documents.
3. The hotel did not throw away the documents but kept them for the author.
4. The author was able to stay one more night in that room.

• **Summary and analysis:**
The author was on a business trip to Hiroshima. While packing to check out, the author accidentally threw important documents into the trash and then returned to Tokyo. The next morning, after discovering what had happened and anxiously calling the hotel, the author was helped when the hotel quickly found the documents. The reason was that the hotel had a policy of keeping the room’s trash for one additional night even after the guest had checked out. The author was deeply impressed by this considerate customer service and extremely happy. Therefore, the “happy event” refers to the hotel keeping the documents instead of throwing them away immediately by retaining the room’s trash for one more night.
default.q.n3-29-q61-61.why.0: (a) Option 1 is incorrect: Solving the company’s difficult problem merely brought a feeling of relief (ほっとして) beforehand; it was not the “pleasant thing” (うれしいこと) emphasized by the author at the end about the hotel’s service.
default.q.n3-29-q61-61.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect: The author organized their own luggage and accidentally threw away the documents (荷物を整理したとき、間違えて重要な書類を捨ててしまった); the hotel staff did not organize it for them.
default.q.n3-29-q61-61.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct. The passage states: 「そのホテルでは、客がチェックアウトしたあとも部屋のゴミはもう一泊させるのだそうだ。客のことをよく考えたサービスだと感心し、本当にうれしかった。」 This corresponds to the hotel keeping the customer's documents instead of throwing them away.
default.q.n3-29-q61-61.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect: the passage says to “let the garbage stay in the room for one more night” (部屋のゴミはもう一泊させる), not that the author is allowed to stay in the room for another night.
default.q.n3-29-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Even people who are already adults can express what they feel through music or painting with a “childlike spirit.”
default.q.n3-29-q62-62.explanation:
**Main point of the passage:** The author recalls the innocent associations and feelings of childhood—seeing animals in the clouds and hearing music in the sounds of wind and rain—and points out that most people lose this “childlike spirit” as they grow up. According to the author, an artist is someone who preserves this “childlike spirit” and knows how to express these sensations through music or painting.

**Question translation:** 
What kind of person does the writer consider to be an artist?

**Answer choices:**
1. Someone who, even after growing up, can remember experiences from childhood.
2. Someone who, even after growing up, can convey childhood experiences through music or painting.
3. Someone who has lost almost all of their “childlike spirit” after growing up.
4. Someone who, even after growing up, can express through music or painting what they perceive with their “childlike spirit.”
default.q.n3-29-q62-62.why.0: (a) Incorrect: The passage only says, "Please try to remember your childhood" (子どものころのことを思い出してみてください) as a prompt for reflection; it does not claim that artists are people recalling their childhood experiences.
default.q.n3-29-q62-62.why.1: (b) Incorrect: The author discusses using a childlike spirit to perceive and express the present, not conveying "experiences or memories from childhood" (子どものころの経験).
default.q.n3-29-q62-62.why.2: (c) Incorrect: The passage states that "many people lose the childlike spirit when they grow up" (多くの人が、大人になると、そのように感じる「子どもの心」をなくしてしまいます) — this is a characteristic of ordinary adults in general, contrasted with artists.
default.q.n3-29-q62-62.why.3: (d) Correct. The final sentence provides the evidence: 「『子どもの心』を持ち続け、それによって感じたものを音楽や絵で表すことのできる人が、芸術家なのではないでしょうか。」 (Isn't an artist someone who continues to possess a “child's heart” and can express through music or painting what they feel through it?) This completely matches the content of choice 4.
default.q.n3-29-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 子どものころ、自分が住んでいた家 (the house where I lived when I was a child).
default.q.n3-29-q63-63.explanation:
• Main point: While out walking, the author suddenly smells a familiar floral scent and naturally remembers a house where they once lived. Immediately afterward, the author uses the demonstrative「①それは」to describe that house in detail: a country house with a large garden where the author lived with their grandparents as a child.
• Question translation: What does ①「それ」(that) refer to?
• Answer choices:
1. The house with flowers in bloom that could be seen along the walking route.
2. The house that closely resembled the one where the author once lived.
3. The house where the author lived as a child.
4. Akiko's house, where the author used to play as a child.
default.q.n3-29-q63-63.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author only smelled the faint scent of flowers while walking; they did not see a house with blooming flowers.
default.q.n3-29-q63-63.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「それ」 directly replaces the house where the author once lived, not another house that merely looks similar.
default.q.n3-29-q63-63.why.2: (c) Correct. The preceding sentence and the sentence containing the underlined word state: 「昔住んでいた家のことを思い出しました。① それは、田舎の、広い庭がある家でした、祖父と祖母も一緒に住んでいて、にぎやかな毎日でした。」 (I remembered the house where I used to live. It was a house in the countryside with a large garden, where I lived together with my grandparents...). Therefore, 「それ」 refers to the house where the author lived in childhood.
default.q.n3-29-q63-63.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage clearly states that Akiko is the girl next door (「隣の家の明子ちやん」), while "それ" refers to the author's own family's house.
default.q.n3-29-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 友達と一緒に山や川で遊んだ (played with friends in the mountains and by the river).
default.q.n3-29-q64-64.explanation:
• Main point: When recalling beautiful childhood memories in the countryside, the author remembers living with their grandparents and often inviting their neighbor Akiko to play on the mountain behind the house and by the nearby river. These are the "nostalgic memories" (なつかしい思い出).
• Question translation: The phrase ②「なつかしい思い出」(nostalgic memories) appears. What kind of memories does the author mean?
• Answer choices:
1. Frequently going to the neighbor's large garden.
2. The grandparents often coming to visit.
3. Looking at flowers with Akiko in the garden.
4. Playing with a friend on the mountain and by the river.
default.q.n3-29-q64-64.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the spacious garden belongs to the author’s house (「田舎の、広い庭がある家でした」), not the neighbor’s house.
default.q.n3-29-q64-64.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author's grandparents lived together with the author (「祖父と祖母も一緒に住んでいて」), rather than visiting occasionally.
default.q.n3-29-q64-64.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the author does not mention viewing flowers in the garden with a friend in this passage.
default.q.n3-29-q64-64.why.3: (d) Correct. The sentence immediately before the underlined part states: 「隣の家の明子ちやんという女の子と、家の裏にある山に行ったり、近くの川に行ったりして、よく一緒に遊びました。②なつかしい思い出です。」 (I often played with Akiko, the girl next door, going to the mountain behind our house or the nearby river. They are truly cherished memories).
default.q.n3-29-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 昔住んでいた家の庭に咲いていたのと同じ花の香りがしたから (Because it smelled like the same kind of flower that had bloomed in the garden of the house where the author used to live).
default.q.n3-29-q65-65.explanation:
• Main idea: The author wonders why they suddenly remembered their old house while out for a walk. After returning home and looking at old photographs, the author remembers that many small white flowers used to bloom in the garden of the house in spring, and that those flowers gave off exactly the same fragrance as the scent the author had noticed on today’s walk.
• Translation of the question: Why does the writer think they remembered the house they used to live in while out for a walk?
• Translation of the answer choices:
1. Because they smelled a fragrance like that of flowers that once bloomed in the garden of the house they used to live in.
2. Because they saw white flowers like those that once bloomed in the garden of the house they used to live in.
3. Because they smelled a fragrance like that of flowers that once bloomed on a road near the house they used to live in.
4. Because they saw white flowers like those that once bloomed on a road near the house they used to live in.
default.q.n3-29-q65-65.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage concludes: 「そして、昔住んでいた家の庭には、春になると、白くて小さな、かわいい花がたくさん咲いていたことを思い出しました。その花は、今日道を歩いていたときの、あの花と同じ香りだったのです。」 (Then I remembered that, in spring, many small, white, lovely flowers used to bloom in the garden of the house where I once lived. Those flowers had the same scent as the flowers I encountered while walking today).
default.q.n3-29-q65-65.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author realized it by smelling a familiar scent (「知っている香り」「同じ香り」); the author did not see white flowers while walking.
default.q.n3-29-q65-65.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the flower bloomed in the garden of the old house (「昔住んでいた家の庭には」), not on a road near the house.
default.q.n3-29-q65-65.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the flowers bloomed in the garden of the old home, and the scent—not seeing the flowers—was what brought back the memories.
default.q.n3-29-q66-66.explanation:
Main point: Immediately before the demonstrative expression「このこと」, the passage describes a change in how children play: in the past, children often played outdoors with friends, but now they mainly stay indoors alone watching TV or playing games.

Question: What does “this” (このこと) refer to?
Answer choices:
1. The fact that parks and play areas for children in town are increasing.
2. The fact that children used to play outside the home frequently.
3. The fact that children today have shifted to playing alone indoors.
4. The fact that children’s physical strength has declined compared with the past.
default.q.n3-29-q66-66.why.0: (a) Incorrect. Passage 1 states that parks and recreational spaces are decreasing, not increasing: 「公園や空き地が少しずつ消えられてきた」「室外で子供の遊ぶ場所が減少した」.
default.q.n3-29-q66-66.why.1: (b) Incorrect because children playing outdoors in the past is merely a comparison with the past, not the thing (“this”) that directly led to the two negative effects in the present.
default.q.n3-29-q66-66.why.2: (c) Correct. The preceding sentence states: 「昔は子どもは外で遊ぶことが多かったが、今は一人で室内でテレビを見たり、ゲームをしたりすることが多い。」 (Children today have shifted to staying alone indoors to watch TV and play games.)
default.q.n3-29-q66-66.why.3: (d) Incorrect because declining physical strength is one of the two effects explained afterward (「一つ目は『体力』への影響である」), not the content referred to by 「このこと」.
default.q.n3-29-q67-67.explanation:
Main point: The passage identifies two major negative effects on children caused by the habit of staying indoors to play video games or watch TV: (1) declining basic physical fitness due to fewer opportunities for outdoor exercise, and (2) poorer ability to make friends and communicate because they spend more time alone.

Question translation: “What changes in children does the author mention in this passage?”
Answer choices:
1. They spend less time playing alone outdoors, and their physical fitness declines.
2. They spend more time playing without moving their bodies, and their physical fitness declines.
3. They have learned how to socialize and make friends well by playing with friends.
4. They have learned how to socialize and make friends well from television and video games.
default.q.n3-29-q67-67.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage says that children nowadays stay indoors alone (「一人で室内で」). It attributes their declining physical fitness to reduced outdoor exercise, not to less time playing alone outdoors.
default.q.n3-29-q67-67.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states: 「走る、跳ぶ、投げるなどの基礎的な体力は昔より落ちている。外で体を動かして遊ぶ機会が減ったことが、最大の原因だと考えられている。」 The decrease in opportunities to play and exercise outdoors has caused physical fitness to decline.
default.q.n3-29-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage describes learning how to communicate while playing with friends as something that happened in the past (「昔は、近所の子どもが一緒に外で遊び...付き合い方を学習した」), while the number of children who currently fail to build good relationships is increasing.
default.q.n3-29-q67-67.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage never claims that watching TV or playing games helps people learn to communicate well. On the contrary, staying alone in one's room weakens relationships between people.
default.q.n3-29-q68-68.explanation:
Main point: The passage analyzes how urbanization has eliminated play spaces, causing children to play alone indoors, which leads to two negative consequences: declining physical fitness and weaker social relationships. The author’s main message appears in the concluding sentence: even as cities continue to develop, we must not forget these negative effects on children.

Question: “What is the author trying to say most strongly in this passage?”
Answer choices:
1. We must pay attention to the negative effects that urban development is having on children.
2. We must not forget that a lack of urban development would also have negative effects on children.
3. Because urban development is having negative effects on children, it would be better to return cities to their pre-development state.
4. Even though urban development may have negative effects on children, cities should continue to develop.
default.q.n3-29-q68-68.why.0: (a) Correct. The concluding sentence states: 「これからも日本の町は発展していくだろうが、それが子供に与える影響も忘れてはいけない。」 (Although Japanese towns will probably continue to develop, we must not forget the negative effects of urban development on children).
default.q.n3-29-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the article discusses the negative effects of the town’s development, not “when the town does not develop” (「町が発展しない場合」).
default.q.n3-29-q68-68.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the author never suggests returning the town to its pre-development state (「町を発展する前の状態に戻したほうがいい」).
default.q.n3-29-q68-68.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the main point of the passage is not to encourage the town to develop regardless of the consequences, but to remind readers to consider the impact on children.
default.q.n3-29-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The number of people working in agriculture has decreased sharply, and more than half of them are elderly.
default.q.n3-29-q69-69.explanation:
• Summary: The demonstrative expression 「この状態」(this situation) refers to the circumstances described in the two preceding sentences: the number of farmers in Japan has fallen to less than one-third of the level 40 years ago, and more than 60% of them are aged 65 or older.
• Question translation: What situation does the expression "this situation (①)" refer to?
• Answer choices:
1. The number of farmers has declined sharply, and more than half have become elderly.
2. The number of farmers has declined sharply, and more than half have become young people.
3. The number of farmers has declined slightly, and the proportion of elderly people is increasing.
4. The number of farmers has declined slightly, and the proportion of young people is increasing.
default.q.n3-29-q69-69.why.0: (a) Correct. The sentence before the demonstrative states: 「40年前に比べると、その数は3分の1 以下に減っている。そして、農業をしている人の60%以上は65歳以上のお年寄りだ。」 (Compared with 40 years ago, the number has fallen to less than one-third [a sharp decrease], and more than 60% [over half] of people working in agriculture are elderly people aged 65 or older).
default.q.n3-29-q69-69.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage states that over 60% are elderly people (お年寄り), not young people (若者).
default.q.n3-29-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage says that the number of farmers has fallen to one-third or less (3分の1以下に減っている), which is a very large decrease (大きく減った), not a slight decrease (少し減った).
default.q.n3-29-q69-69.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The number of farmers decreased sharply, not slightly (少し減った), and farmers are mainly elderly people, rather than the proportion of young people increasing.
default.q.n3-29-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Teaching people with no experience, starting with the fundamentals of agriculture.
default.q.n3-29-q70-70.explanation:
• Summary: The passage lists three ideas or improvements (工夫) introduced by Aozora Company:
  1. Paying fixed monthly wages by growing various kinds of vegetables throughout the year to offset fluctuations.
  2. Giving employees days off on a rotating schedule so everyone could get enough rest.
  3. Having experienced workers teach farming from the basics to people who had never farmed before.
Answer choice 4 accurately describes the third idea.
• Question translation: The phrase "several ideas or improvements (②)" refers to what kind of idea, for example?
• Answer choices:
1. How to pay monthly wages even though some months are busier than others.
2. Trying to continue growing only one type of vegetable throughout the year.
3. How to let all employees take Saturdays and Sundays off.
4. Teaching the basics of agriculture to people with no experience.
default.q.n3-29-q70-70.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage states that the company pays the same fixed salary every month: 「毎月同じ給料が払えるようにする」, not that the amount varies from month to month.
default.q.n3-29-q70-70.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage states that the company grows many kinds of vegetables throughout the year: 「一年中いろいろな種類の野菜を作る」. It does not grow only one kind of vegetable (一種類の野菜).
default.q.n3-29-q70-70.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage says that employees take days off on different days and take turns: 「社員はみんな違う日に休みを取る... 順番に休みを取る」, not that everyone takes Saturday and Sunday off together.
default.q.n3-29-q70-70.why.3: (d) Correct. The third improvement is described as: 「第三の工夫は『農業を数える（教える）こと』。土に触ったことが全然ないような人には、経験者が農業を一からきちんと教える。」 The third improvement is “teaching farming.” Experienced people carefully teach farming from the basics to those who have never touched soil before.
default.q.n3-29-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Because Aozora created a favorable, comfortable working environment for its employees.
default.q.n3-29-q71-71.explanation:
• Summary: Through innovative improvements, including fixed salaries, rotating days off, and thorough training, Aozora has created a convenient, easy-to-work-in environment for young people (若者も働きやすい環境を作っている). This is why many young people who want to try working in agriculture join the company every year.
• Question translation: The passage says that many young people who want to try agriculture join Aozora every year (③). Why?
• Answer choices:
1. Because Aozora allows employees to take many days off.
2. Because Aozora teaches employees how to manage a company.
3. Because Aozora preserves traditional agricultural methods.
4. Because Aozora creates an easy-to-work-in environment.
default.q.n3-29-q71-71.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage says that there are not very many days off, but everyone can rest properly (「それほど多くはないが、みんながきちんと休める」), not that they can take many days off (たくさん取ることができる).
default.q.n3-29-q71-71.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The company teaches agricultural skills from the very beginning (「農業を一からきちんと教える」), not methods of managing a company (会社経営の方法).
default.q.n3-29-q71-71.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The company introduced unprecedented innovations (「今までにないいくつかの工夫」), rather than preserving traditional agricultural methods from the distant past (昔からのやり方を守っている).
default.q.n3-29-q71-71.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage gives the reason: 「『あおぞら』では今までにないいくつかの工夫によって、若者も働きやすい環境を作っている。... このような工夫は若者にも伝わり、③『あおぞら』には毎年農業にチャレンジしたいという若者が大勢入ってきて...」 (At Aozora, several unprecedented innovations have created an environment in which young people can work comfortably. These innovations have reached young people as well, so every year many young people who want to take on the challenge of agriculture join the company.)
default.q.n3-29-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 2: Agriculture from now on (agriculture in the future).
default.q.n3-29-q72-72.explanation:
• Summary: The passage discusses the aging population and decline of the agricultural workforce in Japan, then introduces a new solution: operating agriculture as a business, as in Aozora Company, with policies designed to attract young people. The passage concludes that this is a promising new form of agriculture for the future (これからの農業 / 新しい農業の形).
• Translation of the question: What is the overall topic of this passage?
• Translation of the choices:
1. Older people and agriculture.
2. Agriculture from now on (agriculture in the future).
3. Family-scale agriculture.
4. Agriculture learned from experienced people.
default.q.n3-29-q72-72.why.0: (a) Incorrect. “Older people and agriculture” is only part of the situation described in the opening passage, not the overarching topic of the entire text.
default.q.n3-29-q72-72.why.1: (b) Correct. The opening sentence establishes the topic, and the conclusion states: 「①この状態を変えようと、最近いろいろな農業のやり方が考えられているそうだ。... そして、それは新しい農業の形として期待されている。」 The entire passage discusses new directions and the future of agriculture.
default.q.n3-29-q72-72.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The article emphasizes changing from family-based farming to corporate farming: 「これまでのように家族で農業をするのではなく、多くの人が働く『会社』の形で農業をする」.
default.q.n3-29-q72-72.why.3: (d) Incorrect. “Learning farming from experienced people” is only one of three small initiatives by Aozora, not the subject of the entire article.
default.q.n3-29-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (② 新幹線で行く丸山スキー場 4日間).
default.q.n3-29-q73-73.explanation:
- Translation of the question: Lin wants to go skiing. Since she has no ski equipment, she wants a trip where she can borrow equipment free of charge. She also strongly wants to stay at a hot-spring inn (onsen ryokan). Which trip best suits Lin's wishes?
- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. ① Four-day Hokkaido ski trip by plane
  2. ② Four-day trip to Maruyama Ski Resort by Shinkansen
  3. ③ Three-day trip to Hanamiyama Ski Resort by bus
  4. ④ Kawaguchi Lake ice-skating day trip by bus
- Analysis and comparison:
  + Wish 1: To go skiing (スキーをしたい) -> Tour ④ is an ice-skating day (スケートの日), so it is not suitable.
  + Wish 2: To borrow ski equipment free of charge (無料で用具を借りられる) -> Tour ① charges a rental fee (スキー用具の貸出は有料です), so it is eliminated.
  + Wish 3: To stay at a hot-spring inn (温泉旅館に泊まりたい) -> Tour ③ uses a business hotel (ビジネスホテル利用), so it is eliminated.
  + Tour ② meets all the requirements: skiing, staying at a hot-spring inn (お泊まりは温泉旅館です), and borrowing ski equipment free of charge (スキー用具が無料で借りられます).
default.q.n3-29-q73-73.why.0: (a) Incorrect because Tour ① charges a fee for renting ski equipment (「スキー用具の貸出は有料です」), so it does not meet Lin's requirement for free rental.
default.q.n3-29-q73-73.why.1: (b) Correct because tour ② includes 「お泊まりは温泉旅館です」(“You will stay at a hot-spring inn”) and 「スキー用具が無料で借りられます」(“Ski equipment can be borrowed free of charge”), matching all of Lin’s wishes.
default.q.n3-29-q73-73.why.2: (c) Incorrect because tour ③ stays at a business hotel, not a hot-spring inn (「ビジネスホテル利用」).
default.q.n3-29-q73-73.why.3: (d) Incorrect because Tour ④ is a day trip for ice skating (「スケートの日」「日帰り旅行」), not skiing, and it does not include an overnight stay.
default.q.n3-29-q74-74.explanation:

- Answer choices:
  1. February 18
  2. February 20
  3. February 22
  4. February 25
- Analysis and comparison:
  + Kim’s tour departure date: February 25.
  + Payment method: Pay directly at the travel agency (旅行社で直接お支払い).
  + Relevant rule: 「旅行社で直接お支払いされる場合、出発の三日前までにお願いします。」(If paying directly at the travel agency, please pay no later than three days before departure.)
  + Calculation: 25 - 3 = 22 → The payment deadline is February 22 (2月22日).
default.q.n3-29-q74-74.why.0: (a) Incorrect because February 18 is one week before the departure date (25 - 7 = 18), making it the application deadline (「お申し込みは...出発日の一週間前まで」), not the payment deadline.
default.q.n3-29-q74-74.why.1: (b) Incorrect because February 20 is five days before the departure date (25 - 5 = 20), which is the payment deadline for payment through a bank or convenience store (「銀行またはコンビニの場合、出発の5日前まで」).
default.q.n3-29-q74-74.why.2: (c) Correct, as stated in the passage: 「旅行社で直接お支払いされる場合、出発の三日前までにお願いします。」 Since the trip departs on February 25, payment is due three days beforehand, on February 22 (25 - 3 = 22).
default.q.n3-29-q74-74.why.3: (d) Incorrect because February 25 is the actual departure date (出発日), whereas the rules require payment three days before departure.
default.q.n3-29-q1-1.explanation:
Translation: Where is the capital of Japan?
- Sino-Japanese reading: 首都 (SHUTO) = capital.
- 首 (SHU) has the on-reading しゅ, and 都 (TO) has the on-reading と (short sound).
- Example: ベトナムの首都はハノイです。 (The capital of Vietnam is Hanoi.)
default.q.n3-29-q1-1.why.0: (a) Incorrect: The long vowel 「とう」 is unnecessary in 「都」 (the on-reading of 都 is と or つ; this word does not contain the long vowel とう).
default.q.n3-29-q1-1.why.1: (b) Incorrect: the long vowel 「しゅう」is added unnecessarily to 「首」.
default.q.n3-29-q1-1.why.2: (c) Correct: 「首都」 (capital city) is read 「しゅと」. Both 「首」 (しゅ) and 「都」 (と) have short vowels, with no long vowel.
default.q.n3-29-q1-1.why.3: (d) Incorrect: Both long vowels 「しゅう」 and 「とう」 are added unnecessarily.
default.q.n3-29-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (ちきゅう).
default.q.n3-29-q2-2.explanation:
Translation: The Earth revolves around the Sun.
- Kanji: 地球（ちきゅう） means Earth or the globe.
- 地 is read as ち in 地球, and 球 is read as きゅう.
- Example: 私たちは地球という惑星に住んでいる。 (We live on a planet called Earth.)
default.q.n3-29-q2-2.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「地」 in this word has the on-reading 「ち」; reading it as 「じ」 is incorrect.
default.q.n3-29-q2-2.why.1: (b) Correct: 「地球」 is correctly read as 「ちきゅう」; 「地」 is read as 「ち」 and 「球」 as 「きゅう」.
default.q.n3-29-q2-2.why.2: (c) Incorrect: The sound of 「地」 is wrong (it should be じ), and the long vowel in 「球」 is missing (きゅ instead of きゅう).
default.q.n3-29-q2-2.why.3: (d) Incorrect: The long vowel in 「球」is missing (きゅ instead of きゅう).
default.q.n3-29-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (おくれて).
default.q.n3-29-q3-3.explanation:
Translation: That clock is running slow.
- Sino-Japanese character: 遅 (in 遅れる（おくれる）: to be late; for a clock, to run slow).
- Note: A slow clock is described as 時計が遅れる; a fast clock is described as 時計が進む（すすむ）.
- Example: 電車が10分遅れている。 (The train is 10 minutes late.)
default.q.n3-29-q3-3.why.0: (a) Incorrect:「こわれて」is the reading of「壊れて」(broken).
default.q.n3-29-q3-3.why.1: (b) Correct: 「遅れて」 is the te-form of 「遅れる」 (to be late, delayed, or slow), correctly read as 「おくれて」.
default.q.n3-29-q3-3.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「たおれて」is the reading of 「倒れて」(to fall, collapse).
default.q.n3-29-q3-3.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「よごれて」 is the reading of 「汚れて」 (become dirty).
default.q.n3-29-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (きょうりょく).
default.q.n3-29-q4-4.explanation:
Translation: If the two of them work together, the work will probably be finished soon.
- 協力 (きょうりょく) means cooperation or working together.
- 協 is read きょう; 力 is read りょく.
- Example: 皆さんのご協力をお願いします。 (We ask for everyone’s cooperation.)
default.q.n3-29-q4-4.why.0: (a) Incorrect: The long vowel in 「協」is missing (きょ instead of きょう).
default.q.n3-29-q4-4.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「どりょく」 is the reading of 「努力」, meaning “effort” or “endeavor.”
default.q.n3-29-q4-4.why.2: (c) Correct: 「協力」 is correctly read 「きょうりょく」; 「協」 is read 「きょう」 and 「力」 is read 「りょく」.
default.q.n3-29-q4-4.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「どうりょく」 is the reading of 「動力」 (power, motive force), or it confuses the sound of the kanji 協.
default.q.n3-29-q5-5.explanation:
Meaning: I applied for my university's scholarship.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 応募 (ỨNG MỘ) = おうぼ: to apply, enter, or register.
- 応 (ỨNG) is read おう; 募 (MỘ) is read ぼ (a short sound).
- Example: アルバイトの募集に応募した。 (I applied for a part-time job.)
default.q.n3-29-q5-5.why.0: (a) Correct: 「応募」 is correctly read as 「おうぼ」; 「応」 is read as 「おう」 and 「募」 as 「ぼ」 (a short vowel).
default.q.n3-29-q5-5.why.1: (b) Incorrect: the 「ぼ」sound of 「募」was mistakenly read as 「も」.
default.q.n3-29-q5-5.why.2: (c) Incorrect: It adds a long vowel to「募」(ぼう instead of ぼ; 「横暴」is read おうぼう).
default.q.n3-29-q5-5.why.3: (d) Incorrect: The sound is confused, and an extra long vowel is added to 「募」, making it 「もう」.
default.q.n3-29-q6-6.explanation:
Translation: I answered the child’s question.
- Kanji: 疑問（ぎもん）means a question, doubt, or uncertainty.
- 疑 is read as ぎ (voiced reading), and 問 is read as もん.
- Example: その説明にはいくつか疑問が残る。 (Several questions remain about that explanation.)
default.q.n3-29-q6-6.why.0: (a) Incorrect: The sound of 「疑」 is misread as 「く」; 疑 is read ぎ, while くもん is the reading of 苦悶 or 公文.
default.q.n3-29-q6-6.why.1: (b) Incorrect: The voicing mark is missing from 「疑」 (き instead of ぎ).
default.q.n3-29-q6-6.why.2: (c) Incorrect: The kanji 「疑」 has been incorrectly changed to 「ぐ」 (the reading ぐもん belongs to 愚問).
default.q.n3-29-q6-6.why.3: (d) Correct: 「疑問」 is correctly read 「ぎもん」; 「疑」 has the voiced reading 「ぎ」 and 「問」 is read 「もん」.
default.q.n3-29-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (はっぴょう).
default.q.n3-29-q7-7.explanation:
Sentence meaning: The exam results have been announced.
- 発表 (はっぴょう) = announcement, publication, presentation.
- In this word, 発 (はつ) is pronounced はっ (with a geminate consonant), and 表 (ひょう) changes to ぴょう (with voicing assimilation).
- Example: 明日、研究の成果を発表します。 (Tomorrow, I will present/announce the results of my research.)
default.q.n3-29-q7-7.why.0: (a) Incorrect: the sound change to the handakuten form has not been applied to「表」. After the sokuon, はつ + ひょう becomes はっぴょう.
default.q.n3-29-q7-7.why.1: (b) Correct: 「発表」 (Hatsu Hyō) is correctly read 「はっぴょう」, combining the geminate consonant 「っ」 with the semi-voiced sound 「ぴょう」.
default.q.n3-29-q7-7.why.2: (c) Incorrect: The sound change to ひょ is missing, and the long vowel is missing (it should be ぴょう).
default.q.n3-29-q7-7.why.3: (d) Incorrect: The long vowel in 「表」is missing (ぴょ instead of ぴょう).
default.q.n3-29-q8-8.explanation:
Translation: The vocabulary list is on the adjacent page.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 単語 (TANGO) = たんご: vocabulary word, single word.
- 単 (TAN) is read as たん; 語 (GO) is read as ご.
- Example: 毎日新しい単語を10個覚える。 (I memorize 10 new vocabulary words every day.)
default.q.n3-29-q8-8.why.0: (a) Incorrect: The kanji 「単」 was mistaken for 「げい」.
default.q.n3-29-q8-8.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「けいご」is the reading of 「敬語」(honorific language) or 「警護」(guarding/protection).
default.q.n3-29-q8-8.why.2: (c) Incorrect:「だんご」is the reading of「団子」(dango), or an incorrect voiced reading of「単」.
default.q.n3-29-q8-8.why.3: (d) Correct: 「単語」 is correctly read 「たんご」; 「単」 is read 「たん」 (unvoiced) and 「語」 is read 「ご」.
default.q.n3-29-q9-9.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 解決: resolve (a problem).
default.q.n3-29-q9-9.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "Everyone discussed the issue together and solved it."
- Sino-Japanese reading: 解決 (resolution, solution).
- Example: この問題はすぐに解決できます。(This problem can be solved right away.)
default.q.n3-29-q9-9.why.0: (a) The kanji 改 is incorrect; the correct word requires 解.

default.q.n3-29-q9-9.why.2: (c) Correct because 解決 means solving or satisfactorily dealing with a problem.

Meaning: "Yamaguchi showed me around Tokyo."

Meaning: "I jog every day for my health."
- Kanji reading: 健康 (health).
- Example: 健康のために野菜をたくさん食べています。(I eat lots of vegetables for my health.)

default.q.n3-29-q11-11.why.2: (c) Incorrect kanji: 庫 (as in 冷蔵庫, “storage”) is being confused with 康 (as in “health and well-being”).
default.q.n3-29-q11-11.why.3: (d) Both 建 and 庫 are incorrect; they do not form a meaningful word.
default.q.n3-29-q12-12.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 気温: air temperature, outdoor temperature.
default.q.n3-29-q12-12.explanation:
Meaning: “The air temperature has been very high this summer.”
- Sino-Japanese term: 気温 (air temperature).
- Distinctions: 気温 (きおん — air temperature), 体温 (たいおん — body temperature), 水温 (すいおん — water temperature).

default.q.n3-29-q12-12.why.1: (b) Correct because 気温 is read as きおん and means “air temperature.”
default.q.n3-29-q12-12.why.2: (c) The kanji 湯 (THANG, as in hot water お湯) is incorrect; there is no compound 気湯.
default.q.n3-29-q12-12.why.3: (d) Incorrect kanji: 混 (mixing, confused); there is no compound 気混.
default.q.n3-29-q13-13.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 痛い: painful.

Meaning: "I took medicine because I had a headache."
- Kanji reading: 痛 (つう — pain).

default.q.n3-29-q13-13.why.3: (d) The kanji 症 appears in words such as 症状 (symptoms) and 重症 (a serious condition); there is no i-adjective 症い.
default.q.n3-29-q14-14.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 大量: a large quantity, in large numbers.

Meaning: This shirt is mass-produced at the factory.
- Kanji reading: 大量 (TAI-RYŌ).
- Distinction: 大量 (たいりょう - a large quantity, mass production) vs. 多量 (たりょう - a large amount, contrasted with 微量/少量).
