default.q.n3-29-q14-14.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 料 has no compound word 大料.
default.q.n3-29-q15-15.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: "Some users are also dissatisfied because this mobile phone is difficult to press the buttons on."
- On'yomi-based vocabulary: 不満 (dissatisfaction), 関心 (interest), 目標 (goal), 我慢 (patience, endurance).
- Common expression: 「不満を持つ」 (to feel dissatisfied, to have a grievance).
- Example: サービスの悪さに不満を持つ客が多い。(Many customers are dissatisfied with the poor quality of the service.)
default.q.n3-29-q15-15.why.0: (a) 関心 (interest, concern) commonly occurs in 「関心を持つ」, meaning to be interested in or pay attention to an issue. It does not fit a complaint that a button is difficult to use.
default.q.n3-29-q15-15.why.1: (b) 不満 (dissatisfaction, discontent) combines with 「不満を持つ」, meaning to have dissatisfaction or discontent about something, and fits the context perfectly.
default.q.n3-29-q15-15.why.2: (c) 目標 (goal) is used with 「目標を持つ」, meaning to have a goal to work toward; it does not fit criticism of a product.
default.q.n3-29-q15-15.why.3: (d) 我慢 (patience, endurance) is a noun/verb referring to patiently enduring something, and is not used in the expression 「我慢を持つ」in this context.
default.q.n3-29-q16-16.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (ぶらぶら).
default.q.n3-29-q16-16.explanation:
Meaning: “While I was wandering around town, I happened to run into Mr. Yamamoto.”
- Expression: 「ぶらぶらする / ぶらぶら歩く」(stroll casually, wander around without a particular purpose).
- Example: 週末は特に予定もなく、近所をぶらぶらした。(I had no particular plans over the weekend, so I just wandered around the neighborhood.)
default.q.n3-29-q16-16.why.0: (a) ぐらぐら describes shaking or wobbling (as with an earthquake or a loose tooth), or water boiling vigorously; it is not used for walking around town.
default.q.n3-29-q16-16.why.1: (b) がらがら describes an empty state, such as a nearly empty bus, or a loud/hoarse sound; it does not combine with going for a walk.
default.q.n3-29-q16-16.why.2: (c) ばらぼら has no meaning in Japanese; only 「ばらばら」 exists, meaning scattered or separate.
default.q.n3-29-q16-16.why.3: (d) ぶらぶら combines with 「街をぶらぶらする」 to describe strolling casually or wandering around town without a specific destination. This choice is completely appropriate.
default.q.n3-29-q17-17.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: “Those who wish to attend the seminar should fill in their address, full name, and preferred date on the application form.”
- Kanji compounds: 申込書 (application form), 証明書 (certificate), 領収書 (receipt), 参考書 (reference book).
- Expression: 「申込書に記入する / 書く」 (fill in / write on an application form).
- Example: 大会の申込書は締め切りまでに提出してください。(Please submit the tournament application form by the deadline.)
default.q.n3-29-q17-17.why.0: (a) 証明書 (certificate) is a document confirming personal information or qualifications, not a form to fill out when registering for an event.
default.q.n3-29-q17-17.why.1: (b) 領収書 (receipt): a document confirming that payment has been received; it is not used to register for a seminar.
default.q.n3-29-q17-17.why.2: (c) 申込書 (an application form) is a form for entering information to register for a seminar or course, so this is completely correct.
default.q.n3-29-q17-17.why.3: (d) 参考書 (a reference book) is study material used for learning and reference; it is not a form for writing one's address and name.
default.q.n3-29-q18-18.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: “This calculation is very complicated, so it takes a long time even when using a calculator.”
- Kanji readings and meanings: 複雑 (complicated), 意外 (unexpected), 重大 (serious, significant), 正常 (normal).
- Antonym: 複雑 (complicated) >< 単純 (simple).
- Example: 複雑な問題を分かりやすく説明するのは難しい。(It is difficult to explain a complicated problem in an easy-to-understand way.)
default.q.n3-29-q18-18.why.0: (a) 意外 (unexpected; contrary to expectations) describes something surprising, such as 意外な結果; it is not used to describe the troublesome nature of a calculation.
default.q.n3-29-q18-18.why.1: (b) 重大 (“serious,” “重大”) is used for major problems, responsibilities, or events (e.g., 重大な問題), not for calculations.
default.q.n3-29-q18-18.why.2: (c) 複雑 means “complex” or “complicated.” It describes a calculation involving many intertwined steps or factors, as in 「複雑な計算」, reasonably explaining why even a computer takes time.
default.q.n3-29-q18-18.why.3: (d) 正常 (normal, functioning properly) describes a machine or system operating without unusual errors, so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-29-q19-19.explanation:
Meaning: "A large river runs through this town."
- Verbs: 流れる (to flow), 沈む (to sink, set), 浮く (to float), 零れる (to spill or overflow).
- Example: 町の中心を美しい川が流れている。(A beautiful river flows through the center of the town.)
default.q.n3-29-q19-19.why.0: (a) 流れて (流れる: to flow) combines with 「川が流れている」 to mean that the river is flowing through the town, which is completely accurate and natural.
default.q.n3-29-q19-19.why.1: (b) しずんで (沈む: to sink, to set) is used for an object sinking in water or for the sun setting, not for a river.
default.q.n3-29-q19-19.why.2: (c) 浮いて, from 浮く “to float,” is used for an object floating on water or another surface, not to describe a river.
default.q.n3-29-q19-19.why.3: (d) こぼれて (零れる: to spill, overflow) is used when liquid in a container spills or overflows; it is not used for a natural river.
default.q.n3-29-q20-20.explanation:
Meaning: "This orange is from the United States (imported from the United States)."
- Word-forming suffixes:
  + [Place name] + 産 (さん): origin of agricultural, marine, or naturally occurring mineral products (e.g., アメリカ産のオレンジ, 青森産のりんご).
  + [Place name / manufacturer] + 製 (せい): industrially manufactured or processed goods, machinery (e.g., 日本製のカメラ, アメリカ製の車).
- Example: この店では国産とアメリカ産の牛肉を販売している。(This store sells both domestically produced Japanese beef and beef from the United States.)
default.q.n3-29-q20-20.why.0: (a) 産 (さん) is a suffix attached to the name of a region or country to indicate the origin of agricultural, marine, or mineral products (「アメリカ産」 = oranges from the United States).
default.q.n3-29-q20-20.why.1: (b) 製 (せい) is a suffix indicating where industrial products or machines were manufactured or processed (e.g., アメリカ製 = an industrial product made in America). It is not used for fresh fruit.
default.q.n3-29-q20-20.why.2: (c) 作 (taku / さく) is a suffix indicating an artistic or literary work created by someone, as in ゴッホの作; it is not attached to a country name to refer to agricultural products.
default.q.n3-29-q20-20.why.3: (d) 品 (ひん) is a suffix indicating a type of product (e.g., 輸入品, 高級品); it does not directly follow a country name to indicate the origin of fresh fruit.
default.q.n3-29-q21-21.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (インタビュー).
default.q.n3-29-q21-21.explanation:
Meaning: "I interviewed the champion athlete and then wrote an article."
- Common katakana loanword expressions:
  + インタビューをする: conduct an interview.
  + スピーチをする: give a speech in front of an audience.
  + コミュニケーションをとる: communicate, exchange information.
- Example: 記者は金メダルを獲得した選手にインタビューをした。(The reporter interviewed the athlete who won the gold medal.)
default.q.n3-29-q21-21.why.0: (a) スピーチ (speech) is used in the phrase 「スピーチをする」, meaning to give a speech oneself. It is not used in the structure 「選手にスピーチをする」 to collect material for a newspaper article.
default.q.n3-29-q21-21.why.1: (b) インタビュー (interview) correctly combines in the structure 「〜にインタビューをする」, meaning to interview someone in order to gather information for an article.
default.q.n3-29-q21-21.why.2: (c) メッセージ (message: a text, note, or message) commonly occurs with 「メッセージを送る / 伝える」; 「メッセージをする」 is unnatural in this sentence.
default.q.n3-29-q21-21.why.3: (d) コミュニケーション (communication) usually combines with 「コミュニケーションをとる」. It does not take the particle に or refer to writing an article in this context.
default.q.n3-29-q22-22.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "Because everyone insisted on defending their own opinions, the meeting went on without ending."
- On'yomi: 主張 (assertion, defending one's position), 命令 (order), 返信 (reply), 注文 (order, request).
- Expression: 「意見を主張する」 (to assert or defend one's opinion).
- Example: 彼は会議で自分の権利を強く主張した。(He strongly asserted his rights at the meeting.)
default.q.n3-29-q22-22.why.0: (a) 命令 means an order given by a superior to a subordinate, so 「自分の意見を命令する」 is not used.
default.q.n3-29-q22-22.why.1: (b) 返信 (a reply to correspondence) is used for responding to a message or letter (e.g., メールに返信する), not for expressing an opinion in a meeting.
default.q.n3-29-q22-22.why.2: (c) 主張 (assert, insist on, defend an opinion) forms 「意見を主張する」, meaning to insist on one's viewpoint, which explains why the meeting lasted so long.
default.q.n3-29-q22-22.why.3: (d) 注文 (to order food or goods) is used when ordering a dish or purchasing merchandise; it does not combine with 「自分の意見」.
default.q.n3-29-q23-23.explanation:
Meaning: "The documents and books are arranged very neatly. What a clean and attractive room."
- Sino-Japanese readings: 整理 (organize neatly), 準備 (preparation), 世話 (care), 選択 (selection).
- Expression: 「整理整頓 (せいりせいとん)」 (cleaning up and putting things in order).
- Example: 机の上をきれいに整理してください。(Please tidy up the desk.)
default.q.n3-29-q23-23.why.0: (a) 準備 means preparing belongings or supplies in advance for an event, such as 「旅行の準備」. It is not used to describe the state of a room being neatly organized.
default.q.n3-29-q23-23.why.1: (b) 世話 (care, help) is used for people, animals, or plants (e.g., 子どもの世話), not for books or documents.
default.q.n3-29-q23-23.why.2: (c) 選択 means choosing between alternatives (e.g., 進路を選択する); it is not used for cleaning a room.
default.q.n3-29-q23-23.why.3: (d) 整理 (organizing, putting in order) forms 「きちんと整理されている」, meaning that something has been tidied up and arranged neatly, making the room clean and pleasant.
default.q.n3-29-q24-24.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (からから).
default.q.n3-29-q24-24.explanation:
Meaning: “I haven’t had anything to drink since this morning, so my throat is extremely dry.”
- Common mimetic expressions in the JLPT:
  + のどがからから: one’s throat is parched.
  + お腹がぺこぺこ: one’s stomach is growling with hunger.
  + 頭がふらふら: one’s head is dizzy; feeling unsteady.
  + 英語がぺらぺら: speaking English fluently.
- Example: 運動した後はのどがからからになる。(Your throat becomes parched after exercising.)
default.q.n3-29-q24-24.why.0: (a) ぺらぺら describes speaking a foreign language fluently (e.g., 英語がぺらぺら), or talking rapidly and nonstop. It is not used for being thirsty.
default.q.n3-29-q24-24.why.1: (b) からから describes a dry or parched condition; 「のどがからから」is a common expression meaning that one's throat is dry from lack of water.
default.q.n3-29-q24-24.why.2: (c) ふらふら describes being dizzy, staggering, or unsteady from fatigue or dizziness (e.g., 頭がふらふらする).
default.q.n3-29-q24-24.why.3: (d) ぺこぺこ describes a rumbling, extremely hungry stomach (e.g., お腹がぺこぺこ) or obsequious bowing.
default.q.n3-29-q25-25.explanation:
Meaning: "I am saving money for the future."
- Verbs: 貯める (to save money), 乗せる (to put on or load), 重ねる (to pile up or repeat), 加える (to add).
- Phrase: 「お金を貯める」 (to save money), synonymous with 「貯金する」.
- Example: 車を買うために、毎月少しずつお金をためています。(I save a little money every month to buy a car.)
default.q.n3-29-q25-25.why.0: (a) ためて (貯める: save, accumulate) forms 「お金を貯める」, meaning to save or accumulate money for the future, so it is the correct answer.
default.q.n3-29-q25-25.why.1: (b) のせて (乗せる/載せる: to give someone a ride, load onto a vehicle, post) does not combine with money to express the meaning of saving.
default.q.n3-29-q25-25.why.2: (c) かさねて (重ねる: to pile up, accumulate, or repeat) commonly goes with experience (「経験を重ねる」) or effort (「努力を重ねる」). 「お金を重ねる」 is not used to mean saving money.
default.q.n3-29-q25-25.why.3: (d) くわえて (加える: to add, to include) is used in the structure of adding A to B, e.g., スープに塩を加える; it cannot stand alone to mean saving money.
default.q.n3-29-q26-26.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (仕事に行って).
default.q.n3-29-q26-26.explanation:
・Translation: I commute to work with my wife.
・Vocabulary: 「通勤」（つうきん）means traveling from home to one’s workplace every day and is synonymous with 「仕事に行く」.
・Related terms: 「通学」（つうがく: commuting to school), 「通院」（つういん: making regular visits to a hospital or clinic).
・Example: 毎朝、電車で通勤しています。(I commute to work by train every morning.)
default.q.n3-29-q26-26.why.0: (a) Correct. 「通勤する」(つうきんする) means “commute to work,” synonymous with 「仕事に行く」 (“go to work”).
default.q.n3-29-q26-26.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「勉強に行って」 means “go to study,” which does not fit the meaning of 「通勤」, commuting to work.
default.q.n3-29-q26-26.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「買い物に行って」means going shopping, which does not fit the meaning of 「通勤」.
default.q.n3-29-q26-26.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「散歩に行って」 means going for a walk, which does not fit the meaning of 「通勤」.
default.q.n3-29-q27-27.explanation:
・Translation: I had a very frightening experience.
・Vocabulary: The i-adjective 「おそろしい」（恐ろしい）describes fear of something dreadful or terrifying, and is synonymous with 「こわい」（怖い/恐い）.
・Example: 昨夜、おそろしい夢を見て目が覚めた。(Last night, I woke up after having a very frightening dream.)
default.q.n3-29-q27-27.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「たのしい」(楽しい) means “fun” or “enjoyable,” the opposite of the fear expressed by 「おそろしい」.
default.q.n3-29-q27-27.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「うれしい」 (嬉しい) means happy or delighted and is not synonymous with 「おそろしい」.
default.q.n3-29-q27-27.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「はずかしい」（恥ずかしい）means embarrassed or ashamed, which does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-29-q27-27.why.3: (d) Correct. 「おそろしい」（恐ろしい - KHỦNG）means frightening or terrifying, and is synonymous with 「こわい」（怖い/恐い - frightening, afraid）.
default.q.n3-29-q28-28.explanation:
・ Translation: I explained the reason and circumstances clearly to my teacher.
・ Vocabulary: The noun 「わけ」（訳）when used independently means reason, cause, or circumstances, and is equivalent to 「理由」（りゆう）or 「事情」（じじょう）.
・ Example: 遅刻したわけを説明してください。(Please explain why you were late.)
default.q.n3-29-q28-28.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「アイディア」 means an idea or suggestion and is not synonymous with 「わけ」.
default.q.n3-29-q28-28.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「ルール」(rule) means a rule or regulation, so it is not appropriate.
default.q.n3-29-q28-28.why.2: (c) Correct. 「わけ」（訳 - DỊCH）means a reason, cause, or circumstances leading to an event, and is synonymous with 「理由」（りゆう - LÝ DO）.
default.q.n3-29-q28-28.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「秘密」 (ひみつ) means “secret” and is not synonymous with 「わけ」.
default.q.n3-29-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (少なくなった).
default.q.n3-29-q29-29.explanation:
・ Translation: Recently, I feel that the amount of water in this river has decreased.
・ Vocabulary: The verb 「減る」（へる）describes a decrease in quantity or degree, meaning “decrease” or “become less,” equivalent to 「少なくなった」. Its antonym is 「増える」（ふえる / 「多くなった」）.
・ Example: 最近、体重が2キロ減った。(I have lost 2 kg recently.)
default.q.n3-29-q29-29.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「多くなった」 (多くなる) means “to become more” or “to increase,” which is the opposite of 「減る」.
default.q.n3-29-q29-29.why.1: (b) Correct. 「ヘった」(減った) means “decreased” or “became less,” synonymous with 「少なくなった」(少なくなる).
default.q.n3-29-q29-29.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「きれいになった」 (きれいになる) means to become cleaner or more beautiful; it does not mean that the amount of water decreased.
default.q.n3-29-q29-29.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「きたなくなった」（汚くなった）means “became dirtier,” and is not synonymous with 「減る」.
default.q.n3-29-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (もう一度やった).
default.q.n3-29-q30-30.explanation:
・ Sentence translation: Because the experiment did not go smoothly, I started over from the beginning.
・ Grammar / Vocabulary: The suffix 「〜直す」(なおす) attaches to the verb stem (V without ます) and means to do the action again in order to improve or correct it (e.g., 書き直す - rewrite, 考え直す - reconsider). Therefore, 「やり直す」means the same as 「もう一度やる」.
・ Example: 間違いが多いので、最初からやり直してください。(There are many mistakes, so please start over from the beginning.)
default.q.n3-29-q30-30.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「やり方を調べた」means looking up or learning how to do something, not doing it again.
default.q.n3-29-q30-30.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「やり方を教わった」 means “was taught how to do it by someone else,” which does not fit.
default.q.n3-29-q30-30.why.2: (c) Correct. 「やりなおした」（やり直した）means doing something again after it was unsuccessful, and is synonymous with 「もう一度やった」.
default.q.n3-29-q30-30.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「やるのを途中でやめた」means to stop doing something halfway through, not to do it again.
default.q.n3-29-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (階段でころんでけがをした)。
default.q.n3-29-q31-31.explanation:
「ころぶ (転ぶ)」 is a godan intransitive verb meaning “to fall, take a fall, slip and fall.” It is generally used when a standing or moving person or object loses balance and falls to the ground.
- Standard usage: 「道／階段／雪道で転ぶ」(fall on a road/stairs/a snowy road), 「転んでひざをすりむく」(fall and scrape one’s knee).
- Distinction: Use 「倒れる」 for trees or buildings collapsing; use 「転がる / 横になる」 for rolling over or lying down.
- Example: 滑りやすいので、転ばないように気をつけて歩いてください。(The ground is slippery, so please walk carefully to avoid falling.)
default.q.n3-29-q31-31.why.0: Incorrect because lying back, collapsing onto the bed, or rolling around to rest should be expressed with 「横になる」「倒れ込む」 or 「転がる (ころがる)」. 「ころぶ」 means to fall while walking or standing.
default.q.n3-29-q31-31.why.1: Incorrect. When a plan falls through or goes awry, use 「つぶれる」, 「だめになる」, or 「狂う」, not 「ころぶ」.
default.q.n3-29-q31-31.why.2: Incorrect, because trees knocked down or flattened by a typhoon must be described with the verb「倒れる (たおれる)」.
default.q.n3-29-q31-31.why.3: Correct because「ころぶ (転ぶ)」is the appropriate verb for tripping and falling on stairs (階段で転ぶ).
default.q.n3-29-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (「この書類、30部コピーしておいて」と秘書に指示した)。
default.q.n3-29-q32-32.explanation:
「指示 (しじ)」 is a noun and a Group 3 verb (指示する), meaning “instruction, guidance, or an order” to do something. It is commonly used when a supervisor, authority figure, or person in charge assigns work or gives directions to subordinates or colleagues.
- Standard usage: 「指示を出す／与える」(give instructions), 「指示に従う」(follow instructions), 「部下／秘書に指示する」(give instructions to a subordinate/secretary).
- Example: 現場のリーダーの指示に従って作業を進めてください。(Please proceed with the work according to the on-site leader’s instructions.)
default.q.n3-29-q32-32.why.0: Correct because「指示する (しじする)」means to instruct, order, or assign a task from a superior to a subordinate; here, the task is assigned to the secretary to photocopy the documents.
default.q.n3-29-q32-32.why.1: Incorrect because when asking a teacher to check one's work, one must use a polite request such as 「頼んだ」 or 「お願いした」. 「指示した」 means “instructed” and cannot be used for a student instructing a teacher or superior.
default.q.n3-29-q32-32.why.2: Incorrect because inviting friends to see a movie requires 「誘った (さそった)」 or 「提案した」, not the commanding expression 「指示した」.
default.q.n3-29-q32-32.why.3: Incorrect. To ask a staff member where the restroom is, use 「尋ねた (たずねた)」 or 「聞いた」.
default.q.n3-29-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (国に帰る友人を空港まで見送った)。
default.q.n3-29-q33-33.explanation:
「見送る (みおくる)」 is a godan transitive verb with two main meanings:
1. To see someone off (at a train station, airport, or doorway, watching as they leave).
2. To postpone, put off, or refrain from carrying out a plan or project (commonly used in 「採用を見送る」: postpone hiring, and 「計画を見送る」: put a plan on hold).
- Standard usage: 「空港／駅で人を見送る」 (see someone off at the airport/station), 「見送りに行く」 (go to see someone off).
- Example: 出発する母を駅の改札口で見送った。 (I saw my mother off at the station ticket gate.)
default.q.n3-29-q33-33.why.0: Incorrect because sending an email requires 「送信する」 or 「送る」, not 「見送る」.
default.q.n3-29-q33-33.why.1: Incorrect because flipping through or skimming a few pages requires 「めくってみた」, 「目を通してみた」, or 「読んでみた」.
default.q.n3-29-q33-33.why.2: Incorrect because looking at the scenery outside a train window requires 「眺める (ながめる)」 or 「見る」.
default.q.n3-29-q33-33.why.3: Correct because 「見送る (みおくる)」 is appropriately used to mean seeing someone off when they go far away, here seeing a friend off at the airport before returning home.
default.q.n3-29-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (近所の公園にはいろいろな花が植えてある)。
default.q.n3-29-q34-34.explanation:
「植える (うえる)」is a Group 2 transitive verb meaning "to plant" (trees, flowers, vegetables, and so on, putting their roots into the soil so they can grow) or, figuratively, to implant or instill an idea or feeling.
- Standard usage: 「木／花／野菜／苗を植える」(to plant a tree/flower/vegetables/seedlings), 「庭に桜を植える」(to plant cherry trees in the garden).
- Example: 春になったら、庭にトマトときゅうりの苗を植えるつもりです。(When spring comes, I plan to plant tomato and cucumber seedlings in the garden.)
default.q.n3-29-q34-34.why.0: Correct because 「植える (うえる)」 means “to plant” (trees, flowers, and other plants), and it fits the context of flowers being planted in a park (花が植えてある).
default.q.n3-29-q34-34.why.1: Incorrect. To put strawberries on a cake or cover it with cream, use「のせた」,「飾った（かざった）」, or「トッピングした」.
default.q.n3-29-q34-34.why.2: Incorrect. To fill in land or dump soil into the sea to reclaim land for an airport, 「埋めて (うめて)」 from 「埋め立てる (うめたてる)」 must be used.
default.q.n3-29-q34-34.why.3: Incorrect because installing or erecting a streetlight pole should be expressed with 「設置した」, 「立てた」, or 「取り付けた」.
default.q.n3-29-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (小川さんは正直な人で、決してうそは言いません)。
default.q.n3-29-q35-35.explanation:
「正直 (しょうじき)」is a na-adjective and adverb (正直に / 正直言って), meaning "honest, truthful, straightforward" (describing someone who does not deceive others and speaks the truth), or "to be honest..."
- Standard usage: 「正直な人」(an honest person), 「正直に言う／答える」(to say / answer honestly), 「正直なところ／正直言って」(to be honest / honestly speaking).
- Example: 自分のミスを正直に上司に報告した。(I honestly reported my mistake to my supervisor.)
default.q.n3-29-q35-35.why.0: Correct because 「正直な人 (しょうじきなひと)」 means a truthful, honest person who never lies, so it is completely accurate in meaning.
default.q.n3-29-q35-35.why.1: Incorrect because the standard, accurate expressions for how to use a product are 「正しい使い方 (ただしいつかいかた)」 or 「適切な使い方」.
default.q.n3-29-q35-35.why.2: Incorrect. For a true story, as opposed to a fabricated story, 「本当の話 (ほんとうのはなし)」 must be used, not 「正直な話」.
default.q.n3-29-q35-35.why.3: Incorrect. For an exact distance, use 「正確な距離 (せいかくなきょり)」, not 「正直な距離」.
default.q.n3-3-q36-36.verdict: The correct answer is 2. に, because in the grammar pattern 「〜に〜てほしい」(want someone to do something), the person who performs the action is marked by the particle に.
default.q.n3-3-q36-36.explanation:
Translation: “I opened a bakery because I wanted many people to eat the bread I made myself.”
Grammar: N に V-てほしい: to want N to do V (the person who performs the action is marked by に).
Example: 先生に日本語を教えてほしいです。(I want my teacher to teach me Japanese.)
default.q.n3-3-q36-36.why.0: (a) は is a topic particle. It is not used to mark the person who is wanted to perform an action in the pattern 「〜に〜てほしい」.
default.q.n3-3-q36-36.why.1: (b) に: Grammatically correct in 「[person] に V-てほしい」, indicating the person whom the speaker wants to perform the action (the speaker wants several people to eat).
default.q.n3-3-q36-36.why.2: (c) まで means “as far as” or “until,” so it does not fit the context of wanting someone to do something.
default.q.n3-3-q36-36.why.3: (d) なら is a particle expressing a hypothetical condition (“if” / “if it is”), and it does not combine with てほしい to indicate the object of this action.
default.q.n3-3-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 3. のことで, used to introduce the topic or matter the speaker wants to discuss (the presentation next week).
default.q.n3-3-q37-37.explanation:
Sentence translation:
Student: "Excuse me, Sensei. Do you have a moment now? I would like to discuss next week's presentation with you."
Teacher: "Sure."
Grammar: N のことで: regarding N; about N (often used when opening a consultation or discussion: Nのことで相談する / 話がある).
Example: 就職のことで、両親と話し合いました。(I discussed finding a job with my parents.)
default.q.n3-3-q37-37.why.0: (a) にとって means “for” or “from the standpoint of,” used to evaluate something from N’s perspective. It is not used to introduce a topic for discussion or ask for advice.
default.q.n3-3-q37-37.why.1: (b) によると means “according to...” as a source of information and is usually followed by そうだ or ということだ. It is not appropriate here.
default.q.n3-3-q37-37.why.2: (c) のことで: Correct structure. 「N のことで（相談する）」 means “to consult about N” or “regarding N” (equivalent to N について), used when discussing a specific topic.
default.q.n3-3-q37-37.why.3: (d) のほか means “besides...” (〜のほかに), which does not fit the meaning of the context.
default.q.n3-3-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ぐらいで, because 「1時間」 indicates an approximate duration, so 「ぐらい」 is used for “about,” together with the particle 「で」 to indicate the time required to complete the action.
default.q.n3-3-q38-38.explanation:
Meaning: “I usually take more than two hours to do my homework, but today it looks like I’ll finish in only about an hour.”
Grammar and distinction:
- ごろ indicates an approximate point in time, for example 3時ごろ (around 3 o’clock), while ぐらい indicates an approximate duration, for example 1時間ぐらい (about one hour).

default.q.n3-3-q38-38.why.0: (a) ごろに: 「ごろ」only goes with a specific point in time (such as 1時ごろ—around 1 o’clock), not a duration such as 1時間; also, 「に」does not indicate a time limit for completion.
default.q.n3-3-q38-38.why.1: (b) ごろで: 「ごろ」 is used only with points in time, not with durations such as 1時間.
default.q.n3-3-q38-38.why.2: (c) ぐらいに: 「ぐらい」 correctly indicates an approximate duration, but the particle 「に」 marks the point in time when an action occurs; it does not indicate a time limit for completion. で is required.
default.q.n3-3-q38-38.why.3: (d) ぐらいで: Correct because 「1時間ぐらい」(about one hour) combined with 「で」indicates the amount of time needed to finish the assignment.
default.q.n3-3-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 3. さっき, meaning “just now / a little while ago,” which fits well with the structure expressing an action that has just occurred, 「〜たばかり」.
default.q.n3-3-q39-39.explanation:
Translation:
Son: "Mom, I'm hungry."
Mother: "What? We just finished eating a moment ago. Are you hungry already?"
Vocabulary: さっき (a moment ago, earlier) is an adverb referring to the recent past and naturally combines with 〜たばかり (have just done something).
Example: さっき電話があったよ。(There was a phone call a moment ago.)
default.q.n3-3-q39-39.why.0: (a) そろそろ means “soon” or “it is about time,” indicating an action that will happen in the near future; it is not used for an action that has already occurred.
default.q.n3-3-q39-39.why.1: (b) だんだん: Means “gradually / little by little,” indicating a continuing change over time, so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-3-q39-39.why.2: (c) さっき: Means “just now / a little while ago,” referring to a short time earlier and fitting the context of having just finished eating.
default.q.n3-3-q39-39.why.3: (d) ずっと: Means “throughout / for a long time” or “far more,” so it does not fit the context of having just finished eating.

default.q.n3-3-q40-40.why.0: (a) 入れたまま: Grammatically correct because it uses the transitive verb 「入れる」, which fits the object marked by 「〜を」at the beginning of the sentence, together with 「V-たまま」to describe leaving the receipt in the pocket while washing the clothes.
default.q.n3-3-q40-40.why.1: (b) 入ったまま: 「入る」 is an intransitive verb and takes が, so it does not fit the object 「大事なレシートを」 at the beginning of the sentence.

default.q.n3-3-q41-41.explanation:

A: "If we hurry, we might still catch the 9 o'clock train. Shall we run?"

default.q.n3-3-q41-41.why.2: (c) 走らなきゃ: A shortened form of「走らなければ（いけない）」meaning “must run,” which contradicts the following clause, “we probably won't make it in time.”
default.q.n3-3-q41-41.why.3: (d) 走っちゃって: This is a contracted form of 「走ってしまって」, indicating an accidentally performed or completed action, so it does not fit a hypothetical context.

Translation: “I usually shop online, but I do not buy clothes online because I want to try them on in person before buying them.”

- V-てから: after finishing V, then perform the next action.

default.q.n3-3-q44-44.explanation:
Translation:
A: "It has gradually gotten colder lately, hasn’t it?"
B: "Yes. It’s especially freezing today."
Grammar:

- V-ていく: A change that continues from the present toward the future.

default.q.n3-3-q46-46.explanation:
Sentence translation:
Student: “Excuse me. Could you lend me a pen?”

Distinction:

- 借りてもいいですか: Asking for permission to borrow a pen (you perform 借りる).

default.q.n3-3-q54-54.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜そうです」 (“I hear that...”) is used to relay information heard from someone else, not to describe the writer’s own experience.
default.q.n3-3-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 2. でも.
default.q.n3-3-q55-55.explanation: The preceding sentence describes anxiety before the trip:「日本人の家に泊まるのは初めてだったので、行く前は少し不安な気持ちもありました。」(Since it was my first time staying at a Japanese person's house, I also felt a little anxious before going.) The following sentence describes an enjoyable actual experience:「行ってみたらとても楽しかったです。」(But when I actually went, it was very enjoyable.) The two sentences express contrasting emotional states (anxiety before going >< great enjoyment after arriving), so the contrastive conjunction「でも」(but/however) is needed.
default.q.n3-3-q55-55.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「それで」(therefore, so) expresses a straightforward cause-and-effect relationship, with the result arising from the preceding cause. It does not connect two contrasting clauses.
default.q.n3-3-q55-55.why.1: (b) Correct. 「でも」 (“but/however”) is a conjunction expressing contrast between the worry before leaving and the actual cheerful feelings after arriving.
default.q.n3-3-q55-55.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「実は」(actually, to tell the truth) introduces a newly revealed fact or unexpected information; it does not function as a contrastive conjunction here.
default.q.n3-3-q55-55.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「また」(also, furthermore) adds information in the same direction, so it does not fit the contrast between the two sentences.
default.q.n3-3-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 3. しか.
default.q.n3-3-q56-56.explanation: The passage describes the writer's mother growing many vegetables and everyone cooking with them. Immediately after the blank, the writer says: 「家で育てた野菜を食べたのは初めてでしたが、とてもおいしかったです。」(It was my first time eating vegetables grown at home, but they were very delicious.) This shows that until then, the writer had eaten only vegetables bought at stores and had never eaten homegrown vegetables. The grammar pattern 「〜しか + negative verb」(〜しか…ない) means “only,” producing the sentence: 「私は、お店で売られている野菜しか食べたことがありませんでした。」(I had eaten only vegetables sold at stores.)
default.q.n3-3-q56-56.why.0: (a) Incorrect. If the particle 「は」were used, the sentence would become 「野菜は食べたことがありませんでした」(As for vegetables, I had never eaten them), which completely contradicts the fact that the author still ate vegetables bought at the store.
default.q.n3-3-q56-56.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「などを」with the negative expression 「〜食べたことがありませんでした」means “had never eaten things such as vegetables from the store,” and does not express the contrast between store-bought vegetables and home-grown vegetables.
default.q.n3-3-q56-56.why.2: (c) Correct. The grammar pattern 「〜しか + V-negative」 (〜しか…ない) means “only.” The sentence means “Until now, I have eaten only vegetables sold at stores,” which fits perfectly and logically with the following sentence: “This is the first time I have eaten vegetables grown at home.”
default.q.n3-3-q56-56.why.3: (d) Incorrect. When 「だけ」is used directly with the negative form「〜食べたことがありませんでした」, it means "the only vegetables I had never eaten were those sold at the store," which is completely opposite to the writer's meaning: in fact, the writer only ate vegetables bought at the store.
default.q.n3-3-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 育ててみることにしました.
default.q.n3-3-q57-57.explanation: The previous sentence says that after hearing the writer mention having no garden for growing vegetables, the mother explained how to grow vegetables indoors: 「それを聞いていたお母さんが、家の中でも育てることができる野菜について教えてくれました。」. The sentence immediately after the blank states the current result: 「今、2種類の野菜を育てています。」(I am currently growing two types of vegetables.) Therefore, the blank should express the writer's past decision: “I decided to try growing vegetables too.” The pattern 「〜てみることにしました」(decided to try doing something) is the most appropriate answer.
default.q.n3-3-q57-57.why.0: (a) Incorrect.「〜てほしい」(want someone to do something) expresses a desire for another person's action; it is not used for the subject's own action, as in 私も.
default.q.n3-3-q57-57.why.1: (b) Incorrect.「〜てもいい」(it is all right to...) expresses permission or asking for permission; it is not used to express one's own decision to do something.
default.q.n3-3-q57-57.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜ようとする」(to intend or attempt to do something) expresses an intention to do something or an attempt that is often unfinished, unsuccessful, or interrupted by another event. It does not fit a sentence that states that the speaker is actually growing two types of vegetables.
default.q.n3-3-q57-57.why.3: (d) Correct. 「〜ことにする」 (decide to do something) combines with 「〜てみる」 (try doing something) to form 「〜てみることにしました」 (decided to try growing). It describes a past personal decision, leading to the following statement that the speaker is now growing two kinds of vegetables.
default.q.n3-3-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Imagawa advises Miguel to choose Midorino because it takes only 15 minutes by train to Kita Station, where the company is located, and there are many convenience stores there for everyday needs.
default.q.n3-3-q58-58.explanation:
【Summary of the passage's main points】:
Imagawa replies by email to Miguel's request for advice about where to live. Miguel says he would like to be able to walk to work, but Imagawa explains that the area around the company consists almost entirely of office buildings, with very few rental apartments. Therefore, Imagawa suggests that Miguel move to Midorino, where Imagawa used to live. Although Miguel would have to commute by train, it takes only 15 minutes from Midorino Station to Kita Station, where the company is located, and Midorino has many shops that are convenient for daily life.

【Translation of the question】:
What advice did Imagawa give Miguel about where to live?

【Translation of the answer choices】:
1. How about choosing a place that is more convenient for commuting rather than one that is convenient for daily life?
2. If you want to walk to the company, how about choosing Midorino?
3. How about choosing Midorino because you can take a 15-minute train ride to Kita Station and there are also many shops?
4. Since there are many convenient shops, how about choosing a place near Kitazono Station?
default.q.n3-3-q58-58.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because Imagawa does not compare or advise Miguel to prioritize employment over daily-life convenience. Midorino is recommended as convenient both for commuting to work (15 minutes by train) and for daily life (many stores).
default.q.n3-3-q58-58.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the passage clearly says that Miguel wants to walk to the company («会社まで歩いて行きたい»), but if he lives in Midorino, he will have to commute by train («電車通勤になりますが») instead of walking.
default.q.n3-3-q58-58.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because it accurately quotes the passage: 「電車通勤になりますが、私が以前住んでいた緑野という町はいいですよ。緑野駅から会社のある北駅まで電車で15分だし、いろいろなお店があって便利です。」 (Although I would commute by train, Midorino, the town where I used to live, is nice. It takes 15 minutes by train from Midorino Station to Kita Station, where the company is located, and there are many shops, making it convenient.)
default.q.n3-3-q58-58.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because Imagawa introduces a trip from Midorino Station (「緑野駅」) to Kita Station (「北駅」); there is no place or station called Kitazono Station (「北園駅」).
default.q.n3-3-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (ほかの人が「いいこと」 だと思わないことも「いいこと」 だと思える人).
default.q.n3-3-q59-59.explanation:
【Main point summary】
In the past, the narrator thought Maki was lucky because she often talked about good things. Recently, however, when their train stopped and they had to walk several kilometers home, the narrator felt annoyed and frustrated, while Maki cheerfully said, "We can walk through a town we don't know." Through this experience, the narrator realized that Maki does not simply encounter more good luck than other people. Rather, because of her personality, she can enjoy and regard as "good things" even situations that others find troublesome.

【Question and answer choices】
Question: What has the narrator recently begun to think Maki is like?
1. Someone who is lucky and encounters nothing but "good things."
2. Someone who can regard anything experienced together with the narrator as a "good thing."
3. Someone who can share in the joy of "good things" that happen to other people.
4. Someone who can regard as "good things" even things that other people would not consider good.
default.q.n3-3-q59-59.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because it describes the author's former belief (「マキは運がいいのだと思っていた」), whereas the author has recently realized that this is not the case (「しかし、最近、そうではないと気づいた」).
default.q.n3-3-q59-59.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is incorrect because the passage never says that Maki regards only experiences shared with “me” as good. Rather, Maki always views everything happening around her positively.
default.q.n3-3-q59-59.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the passage does not say that Maki knows how to share in or congratulate other people's “good things.”
default.q.n3-3-q59-59.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct, as shown by the passage: 「嫌だなと思っている私に、 マキは 『知らない町を歩できるね。』とうれしそうに言った。 こんなことでも、マキは楽しめてしまうのだ。 今まで私が聞いた話も、マキだから『いいこと』だと感じたのだろうと思う。」 While the narrator feels unpleasant about having to walk a long distance, Maki happily enjoys it, showing that Maki can perceive as good even things other people would not consider good.
default.q.n3-3-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 小会議室をキャンセルする (cancel the small conference room).
default.q.n3-3-q60-60.explanation:
- Main points of the passage:
Section manager Haraguchi leaves a note for Min, saying that they have to leave early because their child has a fever. The note clearly specifies when each task should be done:
1. Cancel the small meeting room reserved for this afternoon's discussion: Do it IMMEDIATELY after returning to the desk (「席に戻ったら、すぐお願いします」).
2. Confirm the meeting schedule and prepare the meeting room: Do this tomorrow morning (「明日の朝、 最初に確認して、そのあとに会議室の準備をしましょう」).
3. Print 8 sets of documents: Do this today (「今日中に8人分印刷しておいてください」).
Therefore, the first thing Min must do (まず) after reading the note is cancel the small meeting room.

- Translation of the question:
After reading this note, what must Min do first?

- Translation of the choices:
1. Confirm the meeting schedule with the section manager.
2. Cancel the small meeting room.
3. Prepare the meeting room.
4. Print 8 copies of the meeting documents.
default.q.n3-3-q60-60.why.0: (a) Incorrect. According to the note, confirming the meeting proceedings has been postponed until tomorrow morning (「会議の進行については、 明日の朝、 最初に確認して...」), not listed as the first thing to do upon returning to one's desk.
default.q.n3-3-q60-60.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states: 「午後の話し合いのために手約していた小公議はキャンセルして くれますか。 席に戻ったら、すぐお願いします。」 (The department manager asks Min to immediately cancel the small meeting room reserved for the afternoon discussion upon returning to their seat).
default.q.n3-3-q60-60.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The meeting room will be prepared tomorrow morning after the meeting procedure has been confirmed (「そのあとに会議室の準備をしましょう」), not immediately.
default.q.n3-3-q60-60.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Printing eight sets of materials is requested to be completed by the end of today (「今日中に8人分印刷しておいてください」), not as something to do first (まず) immediately upon returning to the desk.
default.q.n3-3-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The restaurant uses warm colors to give customers a positive impression of both the food and the time they spend there.
default.q.n3-3-q61-61.explanation:
Main point of the passage:
The passage explains two psychological effects of warm colors (暖色) used by family restaurants in Japan: (1) They stimulate the appetite and make food look more appetizing; (2) They make people perceive time as longer than it really is, helping customers feel relaxed and comfortable even during a short stay. Thus, warm colors are used to give customers a positive impression of both the food and their overall experience at the restaurant.

Translation of the question:
Why do family restaurants in Japan use many warm colors?

Translation of the answer choices:
1. To avoid spending much money on heating the restaurant.
2. To give customers a positive impression of the restaurant’s food and the time they spend there.
3. To make the restaurant look stylish and attractive and encourage customers to enter.
4. To make customers stay longer and order more dishes.
default.q.n3-3-q61-61.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage does not mention the restaurant’s heating costs (暖房).
default.q.n3-3-q61-61.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage identifies two benefits: warm colors make food look more appetizing («暖色には食欲を感じさせる効果があるので、 暖色に囲まれていると、 料理がおいしそう に見える»), and they make customers feel relaxed even during a short stay («時間を実際より長く感じさせる効果もある。 客は、 店にいた時間が短くても、 ゆっくりできたように感じるのだ»). In other words, they create a positive impression of both the food and the time spent at the restaurant.
default.q.n3-3-q61-61.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage does not mention making the café stylish or fashionable (おしゃれ) to attract customers inside.
default.q.n3-3-q61-61.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The effect of warm colors is to make customers feel relaxed, as if they had stayed longer even when their actual time in the shop was short (店にいた時間が短くても、 ゆっくりできたように感じる), not to keep them seated for a long time so they will order more dishes.
default.q.n3-3-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 3. The speaker has trouble because they are asked to bring a traditional dish from home but cannot cook their specialty in Japan due to a lack of ingredients.
default.q.n3-3-q62-62.explanation:
Summary: When the author was asked to bring a hometown dish to an international student exchange gathering, they had a signature dish but could not make it because the ingredients were unavailable in Japan, leaving them in an awkward situation.

Translation of the question:
The author says, "Something rather awkward happened." Why did "I" have difficulty?

Translation of the choices:
1. Because they were told to bring an ordinary seasoning that is rarely used.
2. Because they had no specialty dish but were asked to cook a hometown dish and bring it.
3. Because they were asked to cook a hometown dish and bring it, but could not make their specialty dish in Japan.
4. Because they did not know how to make fried rice but were asked to bring fried rice.
default.q.n3-3-q62-62.why.0: (a) Incorrect because bringing the seasoning happened before coming to Japan; it was not the reason “I” felt confused last month when accepting the invitation to the exchange event.
default.q.n3-3-q62-62.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the speaker does have a dish they are good at making (私にも得意な料理はある), rather than having no specialty dish at all.
default.q.n3-3-q62-62.why.2: (c) Correct, as shown by the original sentence: 「ある留学生交流会に、 国の料理を何か作ってきてほしいと言われたのです。 私にも得意な料理はあるのですが、日本では買えない材料を使うので作れません。」 (The speaker was asked to prepare a dish from their home country for an international student gathering, but could not make their specialty because it used ingredients unavailable in Japan.)
default.q.n3-3-q62-62.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the person asked her to cook a dish from her home country (国の料理), not fried rice (チャーハン).
default.q.n3-3-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 1. The special fried rice is made with ingredients bought in Japan (meat and eggs), then seasoned with spices brought from the author's homeland.
default.q.n3-3-q63-63.explanation:
Summary: The author uses ingredients available in Japan (meat and eggs) to make ordinary fried rice, then sprinkles it with seasoning brought from their mother's homeland, creating special fried rice with the flavor of home.

Question translation:
What kind of fried rice is the "special fried rice"?

Choice translations:
1. Fried rice made with ingredients sold in Japan and sprinkled with seasoning from the author's homeland.
2. Fried rice made with ingredients sold in Japan and sprinkled with Japanese seasoning.
3. Fried rice made with ingredients brought from the author's homeland and sprinkled with seasoning from the author's homeland.
4. Fried rice made with ingredients brought from the author's homeland and sprinkled with Japanese seasoning.
default.q.n3-3-q63-63.why.0: (a) Correct, as shown in the passage: 「私は、 肉と卵を使ってチャーハンを作り、 香辛料をかけてみました。 すると、 日本によくある普通のチャーハンが、 私の国らしい味と箸りの特別なチャーハンになったのです。」 (I made fried rice with the meat and eggs commonly used in Japan and sprinkled it with the spice my mother had brought from my country.)
default.q.n3-3-q63-63.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the seasoning being sprinkled is the author's hometown's powdered spice (粉の香辛料 / あの香辛料), not a Japanese seasoning.
default.q.n3-3-q63-63.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the ingredients for fried rice, such as meat and eggs, are ordinary ingredients in Japan, not ingredients brought from one's home country.
default.q.n3-3-q63-63.why.3: (d) Incorrect because both the ingredients and the seasoning for the fried rice are described incorrectly compared with the passage.
default.q.n3-3-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The narrator wants to ask why their mother had predicted that the flavors of their hometown would be useful in Japan.
default.q.n3-3-q64-64.explanation:
Summary: Before the author went abroad to study, their mother gave them seasoning and said it "might come in handy." When the seasoning helped the author solve the problem of cooking food from home in Japan, the author wondered whether their mother had anticipated this and decided to call and ask why.

Question translation:
The sentence "I think I'll ask my mother" can be understood as meaning that the author will ask their mother what?

Choice translations:
1. Why she thought the seasoning from home would be useful in Japan.
2. What dish the seasoning from home should be used to cook.
3. Whether she had predicted that the author would study abroad in Japan.
4. What food she thought the author should bring to the next international student gathering.
default.q.n3-3-q64-64.why.0: (a) Correct because the passage connects paragraph 1, in which the mother gives the speaker a seasoning and says 「役に立つかもしれない」 (it might be useful), with the final paragraph, in which the seasoning actually proves useful and the speaker wonders: 「あのとき、母はこういうことを予想していたのでしょうか。明日電話するので、母に聞いてみようと思います。」 The speaker wants to ask how the mother knew the seasoning would be useful.
default.q.n3-3-q64-64.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author found a way to use the seasoning and succeeded, so there was no need to ask how to use it.
default.q.n3-3-q64-64.why.2: (c) Incorrect because studying abroad in Japan is a concrete plan that had already been made, not something the mother predicted.
default.q.n3-3-q64-64.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the交流 event ended successfully, and the passage makes no mention of a subsequent event.
default.q.n3-3-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 4: A foreign fashion company uses plastic waste collected from the sea by fishermen to produce clothing and shoes.
default.q.n3-3-q65-65.explanation:
- Summary: Paragraph 2 clearly states that a foreign fashion company collaborates with fishermen so that, when fishing, the fishermen bring the waste they collect back to the port. The company then collects the waste at the port, sorts it, turns the recyclable plastic into textile fibers, makes clothes and shoes from them, and sells the products.
- Translation of the question: Which of the following is true about what the "foreign fashion company" is doing?
  1. Going out to sea with the fishermen to collect waste.
  2. Receiving waste from the fishermen at the port and taking it somewhere else.
  3. Helping the fishermen make clothes and shoes from waste and then selling them.
  4. Using the plastic waste collected by the fishermen at sea to produce clothes and shoes.
default.q.n3-3-q65-65.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the company did not go out to sea to collect garbage with the fishermen; instead, it coordinated with them so that they would collect garbage caught in their nets while fishing and bring it back to the port.
default.q.n3-3-q65-65.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the company collects waste at the port, sorts it, and recycles it into clothing fibers; it does not simply receive the waste and take it somewhere else.
default.q.n3-3-q65-65.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the company directly recycles plastic waste into fibers and then manufactures and sells clothing and shoes, rather than helping fishermen produce these items themselves.
default.q.n3-3-q65-65.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage states: 「まず、 漁師たち、つまり魚をとって生活している人たちに組んで、魚をとるときに[一]緒にとれるごみを、港に持ち帰ってもらう。 そして、 会社がそのごみを回収、 分[別]し、 その中のプラスチックを繊[維]に変え、服や靴にして売るというリサイクル活動である。」 The company works with fishermen, who bring ashore the waste caught while fishing; the company then collects and sorts it, turns the plastic into fiber, and sells it as clothing and shoes.
default.q.n3-3-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The fishermen participated because they could clean the sea and reduce waste without having to pay out of their own pockets.
default.q.n3-3-q66-66.explanation:
- Content summary: Paragraph 3 explains why the fishermen participate: In the past, when they collected trash, they usually threw it back into the sea because bringing it to port would incur a waste-disposal fee. Thanks to this fashion company's collection activity, the fishermen can clean up the sea without paying the disposal costs themselves.
- Question translation: Why did the fishermen participate in the activity organized by the "foreign fashion company"?
- Answer choices:
  1. Because they can build cooperative relationships with other fishermen.
  2. Because they can reduce the amount of trash in the sea without spending their own money.
  3. Because they can reduce the costs of fishing.
  4. Because the sea will be cleaned up if they each contribute only a small amount of money.
default.q.n3-3-q66-66.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage does not mention building or developing cooperative relationships among the fishermen.
default.q.n3-3-q66-66.why.1: (b) Correct. Evidence from the passage: 「実は、 以前、漁師たちはごみがとれても海に戻していた。 [港]に持ち帰ると捨てるのにお[金]がかかるからだ、この活動は、漁師にとっても、 自分のお金を使わずに海をきれいにで[きる]良さがあるのだ。」 (In the past, fishermen returned the trash they collected to the sea because bringing it back to the port and disposing of it cost money. This activity is also beneficial to fishermen because it lets them clean the sea without spending their own money).
default.q.n3-3-q66-66.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage refers to the cost of disposing of garbage (捨てるのにお金がかかる), not the cost of catching fish (魚をとるためにかかっていたお金).
default.q.n3-3-q66-66.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the activity does not require fishermen to spend their own money (自分のお金を使わずに); it does not mean that they spend a small amount.
default.q.n3-3-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The author believes that the product is certain to sell well in Japan because more and more people are interested in environmental issues and the product design is not bad either.
default.q.n3-3-q67-67.explanation:
- Summary of the main point: In paragraph 1, the author points out that the number of consumers concerned about the environmental harm caused by plastic waste is increasing. In the final paragraph, the author says that these recycled clothing and footwear products have reasonably good designs and that, as consumers' environmental awareness continues to grow, they will certainly be widely accepted in Japan.
- Translation of the question: What does the author think about the clothing and footwear from the “foreign fashion company” that have begun to be sold in Japan?
- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. Since the number of people interested in foreign fashion is increasing, they will probably sell well.
  2. Since the number of people concerned about environmental issues is increasing and the designs are not bad, they will probably sell well.
  3. Since the number of people choosing products based on attractive design is increasing, they will probably sell well even if they are expensive.
  4. Since the product designs do not suit Japanese consumers, they probably will not sell much.
default.q.n3-3-q67-67.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the change in consumer awareness refers to concern about environmental issues (このような問題に関心を持つ企業や消費者は、日本でも海外でも増えている), not concern about foreign fashion.
default.q.n3-3-q67-67.why.1: (b) Correct. Evidence from the passage: Paragraph 1 states 「このような問題（プラスチックごみ問題）に関心を持つ企業や消費者は、日本でも海外でも増えている。」, and the final paragraph says 「デザインも悪くない。 消費者の意識が変 化している今、日本でもきっと受け入れられるだろう。」 (Consumer awareness is changing—they are becoming more concerned about the environment—and the design is not bad, so it will surely be accepted in Japan.)
default.q.n3-3-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage does not mention high prices (値段が高くても) or consumers buying products simply because of their attractive design.
default.q.n3-3-q67-67.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the author says that the product’s design is not bad either (デザインも悪くない) and is confident that it will be well received (きっと受け入れられるだろう), which contradicts the claim that the design is unsuitable and difficult to sell.
default.q.n3-3-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 誰も住んでいない壊れた古民家がたくさんあった。
default.q.n3-3-q68-68.explanation:
- Main point: Paragraph 2 states that before K came to live there 30 years ago, Village T had many old houses that were damaged and abandoned.
- Question translation: What was Village T like before K came to live there?
- Answer choices:
  1. It had many old houses that were almost undamaged but unoccupied.
  2. It had many old houses that had been renovated to make them easier to live in but were unoccupied.

default.q.n3-3-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Activity ① (花や木の世話 - taking care of flowers and trees).
default.q.n3-3-q72-72.explanation:
- Summary of the main points:
The notice recruits volunteers for four activities at Higashiyama Park beginning in April. Kou has three requirements: (1) the activity takes place in the morning (午前中—from 9:00 to 11:00), (2) the location is outside the office (事務所以外), and (3) participation is possible every week (毎週).

  • Activity ② (ホームページ作り): Every Tuesday, 9:00–11:00, but held at the office (公園の事務所で) → does not satisfy the requirement of being outside the office.
  • Activity ③ (公園の緑): Every Thursday, but held in the afternoon (14:00–16:00) → does not satisfy the morning requirement.
  • Activity ④ (公園の案内): Held in the morning (9:00–11:00), in the park, but only once a month on the second Sunday (毎月第2日曜日) → does not satisfy the weekly requirement.

- Translation of the question:
“Kou wants to participate in one of the activities in the park. He wants an activity that takes place in the morning, outside the office, and can be attended every week. Which activity meets Kou’s wishes?”

- Translation of the answer choices:
1. Activity ① (Taking care of flowers and trees)
2. Activity ② (Creating a website)
3. Activity ③ (Cleaning / Park greenery)
4. Activity ④ (Guiding visitors around the park)
default.q.n3-3-q72-72.why.0: (a) Evidence from Activity ①: 「毎週 火曜日 9時~11時」「園内で、 花や木の世話をします。」 This activity takes place in the morning (9:00–11:00), on the park grounds rather than in an office (園内で), and regularly every week (毎週 火曜日), fully satisfying all of Kou's requests.
default.q.n3-3-q72-72.why.1: (b) Activity ② is unsuitable because it takes place at the park office:「公園の事務所で、ホームページの記事を書きます。」, whereas the activity must take place outside the office (事務所以外).
default.q.n3-3-q72-72.why.2: (c) Activity ③ is not suitable because it takes place in the afternoon: 「毎週木曜日 14時-16時」, which conflicts with the condition that activities take place in the morning (午前中).
default.q.n3-3-q72-72.why.3: (d) Activity ④ is unsuitable because it takes place only once a month, on the second Sunday: 「毎月第2日曜日 9時~11時」, which conflicts with the requirement to participate weekly (毎週).
default.q.n3-3-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 説明会に参加するために、参加希望日の前日までに電話で連絡しなければならない (To attend the information session, one must contact them by telephone no later than the day before the desired attendance date.)
