default.q.n3-3-q33-33.why.2: The wrong word is used. A bird perching on a branch should be expressed with 「止まっています」 (from 止まる), not 落ち着く.
default.q.n3-3-q33-33.why.3: Used appropriately in context. 「気持ちが落ち着く」 (to feel calm, relieved, or relaxed) is a very common and completely correct expression.
default.q.n3-3-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 今日は疲れているので、朝までぐっすり眠れそうだ。
default.q.n3-3-q34-34.explanation:
「ぐっすり」 is an adverb meaning “soundly, deeply,” and is used almost exclusively with 眠る (to sleep) or 寝る (to sleep) in expressions such as 「ぐっすり眠る / ぐっすり寝る」.
Example: 昨夜はぐっすり眠れたので、今朝は気分がとてもいい。(I slept very soundly last night, so I feel great this morning.)
default.q.n3-3-q34-34.why.0: The wrong word is used. For eating a lot or eating freely, do not use ぐっすり; use 「たくさん食べて」 or 「お腹いっぱい食べて」.
default.q.n3-3-q34-34.why.1: The wrong word is used. Studying hard and seriously should be expressed with 「一生懸命」, 「しっかり」, or 「みっちり」, not ぐっすり.
default.q.n3-3-q34-34.why.2: The usage fits the context. 「ぐっすり眠る/寝る」is a fixed, very common expression describing sleeping deeply and soundly.
default.q.n3-3-q34-34.why.3: The word is incorrect. For chatting happily and comfortably, use 「たくさん」, 「ゆっくり」, or 「心ゆくまで」, not ぐっすり.
default.q.n3-3-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 森さんはおとなしい性格で、 自分の意見はあまり言いません。
default.q.n3-3-q35-35.explanation:
「性格」（せいかく）means personality or character and refers to a person's characteristic psychological qualities (such as 性格がいい/悪い, 明るい性格, おとなしい性格). It is not used for an object's performance or for talent or culture.
Example: 兄と弟は性格が全く違っている。(The older and younger brothers have completely different personalities.)
default.q.n3-3-q35-35.why.0: The word is incorrect. Japanese cultural features, customs, or ancient traditions should be expressed with 「文化」 (culture) or 「伝統」 (tradition), not 性格 (human personality).
default.q.n3-3-q35-35.why.1: Used appropriately in context. 「おとなしい性格」 (a gentle, quiet personality) is exactly the right expression for describing someone's personality.
default.q.n3-3-q35-35.why.2: The word is incorrect. 「性能」(performance, capabilities) must be used for the features or performance of cars and machines; 性格 is not used for objects.
default.q.n3-3-q35-35.why.3: The word is used incorrectly. A musical aptitude or talent that needs to be developed should be expressed with 「才能」 (talent) or 「素質」 (aptitude), not 性格.
default.q.n3-30-q36-36.verdict: The correct answer is 2. って.
default.q.n3-30-q36-36.explanation:
Meaning: A: "Mr. Tanaka is working part-time today too, isn't he?" B: "He said he isn't working today."
• Grammar: 「〜って」 is the casual spoken form of the quotation particle 「〜と」. It follows the plain form (普通形) and is used to report speech, information, or thoughts.
• Example: 田中さんは明日休むって言ってたよ。 (Mr. Tanaka said he would be off tomorrow.)
default.q.n3-30-q36-36.why.0: (a) を: Incorrect because the particle 「を」is not used to quote direct or indirect speech after a predicate clause.
default.q.n3-30-q36-36.why.1: (b) って: Correct because 「って」is an informal spoken quotation particle that replaces 「と」(「ないって言っていました」=「ないと言っていました」).
default.q.n3-30-q36-36.why.2: (c) のを: Incorrect because the nominalizer 「のを」is not used to introduce quoted content in this indirect-quotation structure.
default.q.n3-30-q36-36.why.3: (d) だ: Incorrect because an -i adjective or the negative form「ない」cannot be directly followed by「だ」, and the quoting particle「と」/「って」is also missing before「言っていました」.
default.q.n3-30-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 3. たびに.
default.q.n3-30-q37-37.explanation:
Meaning: Every time I met Mr. Yamada, I always thought he was a truly wonderful person.
• Grammar: 「V-る / Nの + たびに」: every time / whenever someone does something, ... Emphasizes a regular, repeated occurrence and is often used with 「いつも」.
• Kanji readings: 会 (meeting), 山田 (Yamada), 人 (person).
• Example: この写真を見るたびに、楽しかった旅行を思い出す。 (Every time I look at this photo, I remember the enjoyable trip.)
default.q.n3-30-q37-37.why.0: (a) うちに: Incorrect because「〜うちに」means "while/during the time that..." and is not used to express a repeated rule together with「いつも」.
default.q.n3-30-q37-37.why.1: (b) はじめに: Incorrect because it means “first/at the beginning” and does not form the grammar pattern 「Vる + はじめに」 to indicate a repeated action.
default.q.n3-30-q37-37.why.2: (c) たびに: Correct because the structure 「V-る / Nの + たびに」 means "each time" or "whenever," describing an event in which B occurs every time A happens. It fits well with the adverb 「いつも」 (always).
default.q.n3-30-q37-37.why.3: (d) だけに: Incorrect because the pattern 「〜だけに」 expresses a corresponding cause (“precisely because..., all the more...”), which does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-30-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 4. いつの間にか.
default.q.n3-30-q38-38.explanation:
Meaning: I was so absorbed in reading that, before I knew it, five hours had passed.
• Vocabulary: 「いつの間にか」 (before one knows it; without realizing when), describing a change or the passage of time that one does not notice, often combined with the regretful or unintended 「〜てしまう」.
• Kanji readings: 読 (to read), 間 (interval; period of time), 経 (to pass).
• Example: 夢中でゲームをしていたら、いつの間にか朝になっていた。 (I was so absorbed in playing games that it was morning before I knew it.)
default.q.n3-30-q38-38.why.0: (a) そろそろ: Incorrect because 「そろそろ」 means “soon” or “about to do something,” referring to an action that will occur in the near future, not to time that has already passed in the past.
default.q.n3-30-q38-38.why.1: (b) だんだん: Incorrect because 「だんだん」describes gradual change by degree (gradually, little by little). It is not used for time passing rapidly without the speaker noticing.
default.q.n3-30-q38-38.why.2: (c) ようやく: Incorrect because「ようやく」means “finally,” describing an outcome achieved after a long period of effort or anticipation, with a positive nuance.
default.q.n3-30-q38-38.why.3: (d) いつの間にか: Correct because 「いつの間にか」 means “before one realizes it / somehow,” describing time passing unnoticed, which fits 「五時間も経ってしまった」 perfectly.
default.q.n3-30-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 会う.
default.q.n3-30-q39-39.explanation:
Sentence meaning: I am meeting a friend at Tokyo Station at 7 o'clock today, so I am about to leave.
• Grammar: 「V-る / V-ない + ことになっている」 expresses a rule, custom, or plan/schedule that has been decided or arranged in advance.
• Sino-Japanese readings: 会 (HỘI - meet), 駅 (DỊCH - station), 友 (HỮU - friend), 出 (XUẤT - go out).
• Example: 明日、先生と研究室で相談することになっている。 (I am scheduled to consult with my teacher in the laboratory tomorrow.)
default.q.n3-30-q39-39.why.0: (a) 会おう: Incorrect because the volitional form 「〜よう」 does not combine with 「ことになっている」.
default.q.n3-30-q39-39.why.1: (b) 会う: Correct because the dictionary form (V-る) combines with 「ことになっている」 to express a scheduled or prearranged plan (“it is arranged that I will meet you”).
default.q.n3-30-q39-39.why.2: (c) 会った: Incorrect because the past form 「〜た」does not combine with 「ことになっている」to indicate a future plan or appointment.
default.q.n3-30-q39-39.why.3: (d) 会って: incorrect because the te-form 「〜て」cannot directly modify the noun 「こと」.
default.q.n3-30-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 1. やめる.
default.q.n3-30-q40-40.explanation:
Meaning: My doctor told me to quit smoking, but I still have not been able to quit.
• Grammar: 「V-る / V-ない + ように言われる」: to be told or asked by someone to do or not do something (an indirect command or piece of advice).
• Kanji notes: 医者 means "doctor"; 言 means "to say."
• Example: 先生からもっと本を読むように言われた。 (My teacher advised me to read more books.)
default.q.n3-30-q40-40.why.0: (a) やめる: Correct because the dictionary form (V-る) combines with 「ように言われている」to express advice or a request to perform an action (“the doctor told me to quit smoking”).
default.q.n3-30-q40-40.why.1: (b) やめた is incorrect because the past form「〜た」does not combine with「ように言う／言われる」in a pattern for conveying a request or advice.
default.q.n3-30-q40-40.why.2: (c) やめない: Incorrect in meaning because「たばこをやめないように」means "to be told not to quit smoking," which is completely contrary to the logic of the context.
default.q.n3-30-q40-40.why.3: (d) やめ is incorrect because the verb stem formed by removing ます cannot directly precede 「ように言われる」.
default.q.n3-30-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 3. あいだ.
default.q.n3-30-q41-41.explanation:
Meaning: Throughout Mr. Yamada’s lecture, everyone listened attentively.
• Grammar: Difference between 「間」 and 「間に」:
 - 「A 間 B」: During the entire period A, action B continues throughout the period from beginning to end (here, everyone listened attentively for the whole lecture).
 - 「A 間に B」: During period A, action B occurs at a particular moment or as an interruption.
• Kanji readings: 講演 (lecture), 熱心 (enthusiastic, earnest), 聞 (to listen).
• Example: 夏休みの間、ずっと祖母の家に滞在していた。 (I stayed at my grandmother’s house throughout the summer vacation.)
default.q.n3-30-q41-41.why.0: (a) あいだと: Incorrect because the grammatical combination of the particle 「あいだと」 does not exist.
default.q.n3-30-q41-41.why.1: (b) あいだに: Incorrect because 「〜あいだに」is used when the following action is momentary or short, whereas the following clause here is 「聞いていた」, a continuous action lasting throughout the speech.
default.q.n3-30-q41-41.why.2: (c) あいだ: Correct because the structure 「Nの + 間（あいだ）」 indicates that the action in the following clause continues throughout the entire period during which event N takes place, from beginning to end.
default.q.n3-30-q41-41.why.3: (d) あいだで: Incorrect because「〜の間で」usually indicates a range of relationships between people or a spatial range; it does not indicate the duration of an event.
default.q.n3-30-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ございます.
default.q.n3-30-q42-42.explanation:
Meaning: A: “Where is the counter that sells school bags?” B: “It is on the fifth floor.”
• Honorific language: 「ございます」 is the formal polite form (丁寧語) of 「あります」, the verb indicating the existence or location of an object, and of 「〜です」. It is commonly used in customer service when directing customers to a location or introducing an item.
• Kanji readings: 場 (place), 階 (floor).
• Example: お手洗いはあちらの右手にございます。 (The restroom is over there on the right.)
default.q.n3-30-q42-42.why.0: (a) ございます: Correct because 「ございます」is the formal polite form (丁寧語) of 「あります」, the verb indicating the existence or location of an object, and is used when staff politely tell a customer where the counter is.
default.q.n3-30-q42-42.why.1: (b) いらっしゃいます: Incorrect because 「いらっしゃいます」 is the honorific language (尊敬語) form of 「いる/行く/来る」. It is used for respected people, not for places or sales counters.
default.q.n3-30-q42-42.why.2: (c) いる: Incorrect because 「いる」 is normally used only for people and animals, not objects or shop counters, and it also lacks the required level of politeness.
default.q.n3-30-q42-42.why.3: (d) おります: Incorrect because 「おります」 is the humble form (謙譲語) of 「いる」. It is used for oneself or someone on one's side, not for objects or locations.
default.q.n3-30-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 4. だけに.
default.q.n3-30-q43-43.explanation:
Meaning: A: "Why don't we eat something?" - B: "I'll order spaghetti and coffee." - C: "I'm not hungry, so I'll just order coffee."
• Grammar: 「N + にする」expresses a decision or choice, often when ordering at a restaurant or café. To limit the choice, use 「N + だけにする」(choose only N).
• Kanji: 喫茶店 (きっさてん - coffee shop, café).
• Example: 今日はあまり時間がないので、簡単なランチだけにします。 (I don't have much time today, so I'll just have a simple lunch.)
default.q.n3-30-q43-43.why.0: (a) だけ: Wrong because 「コーヒーだけする」is missing the particle 「に」in the pattern for choosing something, 「〜にする」.
default.q.n3-30-q43-43.why.1: (b) だけで: Incorrect because 「だけで」 indicates a means, method, or condition ('only by...'); it does not combine with 「する」 to create a pattern for choosing dishes.
default.q.n3-30-q43-43.why.2: (c) だけを is incorrect because 「〜をする」 does not mean deciding which dish to choose; that meaning requires the construction 「〜にする」.
default.q.n3-30-q43-43.why.3: (d) だけに: Correct because the adverb 「だけ」(only) combines with the choice pattern 「N + にする」to form 「N + だけにする」, meaning “choose/order only N.”
default.q.n3-30-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ようになってから.
default.q.n3-30-q44-44.explanation:
Meaning: After studying Japanese and becoming able to speak it to some extent, Japanese lessons became much more enjoyable.
• Grammar: 「V-potential + ようになる」 indicates a change in ability or habit over time (“become able to ...”). Combined with 「〜てから」, it means “since after ...”.
• Kanji readings and meanings: 勉強 (study), 程度 (degree, extent), 話 (speech, talk), 授業 (class, lesson).
• Example: 自転車に乗れるようになってから、行動範囲が広がった。 (Since I became able to ride a bicycle, the range of places I go has expanded.)
default.q.n3-30-q44-44.why.0: (a) ことができるまで: Incorrect because 「ことができる」 is not used with a verb already in the potential form, 話せる, and 「〜まで」 (until) does not indicate the point when a positive change begins in the following clause.
default.q.n3-30-q44-44.why.1: (b) ことができてから: Incorrect because 「話せる」 is already the potential form, so the 「〜ことができる」 construction would be redundant.
default.q.n3-30-q44-44.why.2: (c) ようになるまで: Semantically incorrect because 「〜ようになるまで」means “until one becomes able to...,” implying that after being able to speak, studying would no longer be enjoyable, which contradicts the emotional flow of the sentence.
default.q.n3-30-q44-44.why.3: (d) ようになってから: Correct because 「V-potential + ようになる」 describes a change in ability from being unable to do something to being able to do it, while 「〜てから」 indicates the point in time after which the class became enjoyable.
default.q.n3-30-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 2. あるのかについて.
default.q.n3-30-q45-45.explanation:
Meaning: I want to know exactly how effective Company A's product is for back pain.
• Grammar:
 - An indirect question with an interrogative: `[interrogative] + plain form + か / のか`.
 - 「N / V plain form + の + について」: about N / about doing V.
• Kanji readings and meanings: 商品 (product), 腰 (waist, lower back), 痛 (pain), 効果 (effectiveness), 詳 (detailed), 知 (to know).
• Example: この薬がどのくらい効くのかについて、先生に質問した。 (I asked the doctor how effective this medicine is.)
default.q.n3-30-q45-45.why.0: (a) あるのかによって: Incorrect because 「〜によって」 means “depending on...,” which does not fit the following clause 「詳しく知りたい」 (want to know in detail).
default.q.n3-30-q45-45.why.1: (b) あるのかについて: Correct because when used with the question phrase 「どのくらい」(to what extent), the embedded question form 「〜のか」is required, followed by 「について」(about) to specify the subject being investigated.
default.q.n3-30-q45-45.why.2: (c) あるのかどうかによって: Incorrect because「のかどうか」is used for an yes-or-no question without a question word, whereas「どのくらい」is already present here. In addition,「によって」does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-30-q45-45.why.3: (d) あるのかどうかについて: Incorrect because 「どのくらい」 already asks about degree or extent, so it cannot be combined with 「〜かどうか」 (whether or not).
default.q.n3-30-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 濃くなりすぎて.
default.q.n3-30-q46-46.explanation:
Meaning: Yesterday, my younger sister and I made soup together, but because we used the wrong amount of salt, the soup became too strong and salty.
• Grammar:
 - Remove い from an -i adjective and add 「くなる」: become... (an intransitive change of state, used with が).
 - Adjective stem / masu-form without ます + 「すぎる」: do something excessively / become too...
   Here: 「濃く」 + 「なりすぎる」 → 「濃くなりすぎていました」.
• Kanji readings: 妹 (いもうと - younger sister), 作 (つくる - make, cook), 塩 (しお - salt), 量 (りょう - amount), 間違 (まちがい - mistake), 味 (あじ - taste), 濃 (こい - strong, salty).
• Example: 唐辛子を入れすぎて、スープが辛くなりすぎてしまった。 (I added too much chili pepper, so the soup became excessively spicy.)
default.q.n3-30-q46-46.why.0: (a) 濃くなりやすくなって: Incorrect because 「〜やすい」means “easy to ...” or “likely to ...,” describing a tendency or inherent characteristic. It does not express a consequence caused by a specific mistake, such as adding the wrong amount of salt.
default.q.n3-30-q46-46.why.1: (b) 濃くしやすくなって: Incorrect both in the meaning of 「〜やすい」 and in particle usage. With 「味が」, the intransitive expression 「濃くなる」 must be used, not the transitive verb 「濃くする」.
default.q.n3-30-q46-46.why.2: (c) 濃くなりすぎて: Correct. 「濃くなる」 (become strong) combines with 「〜すぎる」 (too much) to form 「濃くなりすぎる」. With the particle 「味が」, it expresses that the soup has become too salty or too strong because too much salt was added.
default.q.n3-30-q46-46.why.3: (d) 濃くしすぎて: Incorrect particle usage because 「濃くする」 is a transitive verb and requires the particle 「を」 (味を濃くしすぎる), whereas the question uses 「味が」.
default.q.n3-30-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 1. させないでください.
default.q.n3-30-q47-47.explanation:
Meaning: A: "Where is my wallet?" - B: "Huh? Really?" - A: "Oh, I found it, I found it!" - B: "Honestly, don’t scare me like that! But what a relief."
• Grammar:
 - 「びっくりさせる」: to startle or frighten someone (causative form).
 - 「V-ないでください」: please don’t do V → 「びっくりさせないでください」: please don’t scare me again.
• Kanji readings and meanings: 財布 (wallet), 本当 (really, true).
• Example: 急に後ろから大声を出して、びっくりさせないでよ。 (Don’t suddenly shout loudly from behind and scare me like that.)
default.q.n3-30-q47-47.why.0: (a) させないでください: Correct because the negative causative form 「V-(さ)せないでください」 (please don't make me...) combines with 「びっくりする」 to form 「びっくりさせないでくださいよ」, expressing a mild, affectionate reproach: “Don't scare me like that!”
default.q.n3-30-q47-47.why.1: (b) させてください: Incorrect because this is a causative request for permission (“please let me startle you”), which makes no sense in this context.
default.q.n3-30-q47-47.why.2: (c) させないことにしてください: Incorrect because the structure 「〜ことにする」 expresses a deliberate decision, not an immediate exclamatory utterance in conversation.
default.q.n3-30-q47-47.why.3: (d) させることにしてください: Incorrect in both meaning and conversational nuance.
default.q.n3-30-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 行けばいいのだろうが.
default.q.n3-30-q48-48.explanation:
Meaning: I have had a terrible toothache since this morning. I know I should go to the dentist right away, but I really do not want to go.
• Grammar: 「V-ばいいのだろうが」 expresses awareness that doing something would be best, while indicating that psychological reasons such as embarrassment, fear, or laziness make the speaker unwilling to do it.
• Sino-Japanese readings: 今朝 (this morning), 歯 (tooth), 痛 (pain), 歯医者 (dentist), 行 (to go).
• Example: 早く寝ればいいのだろうが、つい夜更かししてしまう。 (I know I should go to bed early, but I end up staying up late.)
default.q.n3-30-q48-48.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 行かなくてもいいのだろうが means “although I probably do not have to go,” which conflicts with the fact that the tooth is causing severe pain and with the following phrase 「行きたくない」.
default.q.n3-30-q48-48.why.1: (b) 行かなくてもいいようだが: Incorrect because the conjectural expression 「ようだが」 (“it seems that”) and the negative expression 「行かなくてもいい」 (“it is not necessary to go”) do not fit the context of severe toothache.
default.q.n3-30-q48-48.why.2: (c) 行けばいいのだろうが: Correct because the pattern 「V-ばいいのだろうが / のだろうけれど」 expresses awareness of what one should rationally do (“I know I should go see a doctor, but...”), showing the speaker’s internal conflict as they are afraid or reluctant to go 「行きたくない」.
default.q.n3-30-q48-48.why.3: (d) 行ければいいようだが: Incorrect because 「行ければ」(if it were possible to go) combined with 「ようだが」does not express the conflict between the speaker’s reason and emotions.
default.q.n3-30-q49-49.verdict: The correct order is: 1 → 4 → 3 → 2. The star ★ position is answer choice 3 (まだ).
default.q.n3-30-q49-49.explanation:
- Complete dialogue:
A 「じゃあ、 あしたはコンサート会場の入り口に5時に集まりませんか。 」
B 「コンサートは7時からですから、そんなに早く行ってもまだ開いていないと思いますよ。」
- Translation:
A: “Then, shall we meet at the entrance to the concert venue at 5 tomorrow?”
B: “The concert starts at 7, so I don’t think the venue will be open yet even if we go that early.”
default.q.n3-30-q49-49.why.0: (a) 早く: An adverb indicating time or degree, placed before the verb 行っても to mean “go early enough to that extent.”
default.q.n3-30-q49-49.why.1: (b) 開いていない: The verb is in the negative form, indicating that it is not open, and comes before と思います to complete the predicate 「開いていないと思いますよ」.
default.q.n3-30-q49-49.why.2: (c) まだ: An adverb expressing the state of "still not," forming「まだ開いていない」(it is still not open) before 開いていない, in the position marked by ★.
default.q.n3-30-q49-49.why.3: (d) 行っても is the concessive conditional form 「〜ても」, meaning “even if...” or “although...,” connecting the clause “even if you go early...”.
default.q.n3-30-q50-50.verdict: The correct order is: 4 → 2 → 1 → 3. The star ★ is in position 1 (すこし).
default.q.n3-30-q50-50.explanation:
- Complete dialogue:
学生: 「田中先生はいらっしゃいますか。 」
秘書: 「今、ほかの学生と話していらっしゃいますから、すこし待ってください。」
- Translation:
Student: “Is Professor Tanaka here?”
Secretary: “He is speaking with another student now, so please wait a moment.”
default.q.n3-30-q50-50.why.0: (a) すこし: An adverb indicating a small amount or short period (“a little”). It comes before 待ってください to mean “please wait a moment” and occupies the ★ position.
default.q.n3-30-q50-50.why.1: (b) から: This linking particle indicates a reason or cause ('because...') and follows the polite form いらっしゃいます to connect it to the explanatory clause.
default.q.n3-30-q50-50.why.2: (c) 待って: The te-form of the verb combines with ください at the end of the sentence to form the polite request pattern 「〜てください」(please wait).
default.q.n3-30-q50-50.why.3: (d) いらっしゃいます: This is the respectful form of います and combines with the preceding 話して to form the honorific structure 「〜ていらっしゃいます」(is talking).
default.q.n3-30-q51-51.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 1 → 2 → 4. The starred position ★ is answer choice 2 (と思って).
default.q.n3-30-q51-51.explanation:
- Complete sentence: 父も私も、今日はかさがなくても大丈夫だろうと思って出かけたが、雨に降られてしまった。
- Meaning: Both my father and I thought we would be fine going out without an umbrella today, but we ended up getting caught in the rain.
default.q.n3-30-q51-51.why.0: (a) だろう: an auxiliary expressing supposition (“probably…”). It follows the noun or adjective 大丈夫 to form the judgment 「大丈夫だろう」.
default.q.n3-30-q51-51.why.1: (b) と思って: The pattern 「〜と思って」 (thinking that...) quotes the preceding thought and connects it to the action 出かけた that follows. It belongs in the position marked ★.
default.q.n3-30-q51-51.why.2: (c) 大丈夫: a na-adjective/noun. It follows 「かさがなくても」to form the phrase “it is okay even without an umbrella.”
default.q.n3-30-q51-51.why.3: (d) 出かけた is the main verb of the preceding clause and comes directly before the conjunction が, which expresses contrast with the following clause.
default.q.n3-30-q52-52.verdict: The correct order is: 1 → 3 → 2 → 4. The ★ position is choice 2 (ライオンの).
default.q.n3-30-q52-52.explanation:
- Complete sentence: 昨日動物園に行ったら、 先月生まれたばかりのライオンの赤ちゃんを見ることができました。
- Meaning: When I went to the zoo yesterday, I was able to see a lion cub that had just been born the previous month.
default.q.n3-30-q52-52.why.0: (a) 生まれた: The past-tense verb follows the time expression 先月 and combines with ばかりの to form 「先月生まれたばかり」 (was just born last month).
default.q.n3-30-q52-52.why.1: (b) ライオンの: The noun plus the particle の comes before 赤ちゃん to form an attributive phrase (“a lion cub” / “a baby lion”), occupying the position marked by ★.
default.q.n3-30-q52-52.why.2: (c) ばかりの: The grammar pattern 「Vた + ばかりの + N」 means “having just done something...” and modifies the noun phrase 「ライオンの赤ちゃん」 that follows.
default.q.n3-30-q52-52.why.3: (d) 赤ちゃんを: A noun followed by the object particle を, functioning as the direct object of the potential expression 「見ることができました」at the end of the sentence.
default.q.n3-30-q53-53.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 1 → 3. The star ★ is in position 4 (ような).
default.q.n3-30-q53-53.explanation:
- Complete dialogue:
ジョン: 「この 『りかい』という言葉はどういう意味ですか。」
アリ: 「ああ、確か 『わかる』というような意味だったと思うんですけど。」
- Meaning:
John: “What does the word 『りかい』 (understanding) mean?”
Ali: “Oh, I think it had a meaning something like 『わかる』 (to understand/know).”
default.q.n3-30-q53-53.why.0: (a) 意味だった: It follows ような to modify the noun 意味 ("a meaning like..."), and is in the past form before the quotation particle と in と思う.
default.q.n3-30-q53-53.why.1: (b) という: Placed after the quoted expression 『わかる』 to form a phrase defining or explaining its meaning.
default.q.n3-30-q53-53.why.2: (c) と思う: A verb expressing a personal judgment or thought ("I think that..."). Placed directly before んですけど, it creates a tactful, softened way of speaking.
default.q.n3-30-q53-53.why.3: (d) ような: Combines with という to form the pattern 「〜というような + N」 (something like...), appears before 意味だった, and occupies the starred position ★.
default.q.n3-30-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (ところがあるのです).
default.q.n3-30-q54-54.explanation:
- The passage begins by saying that people would usually refuse to believe and laugh at the idea of a vending machine that could talk: 「ほとんどの人は、自動販売機がしゃべるはずはないと言って、笑うでしょう。」 (Most people would laugh and say that a vending machine could not possibly talk.)
- The next sentence introduces an unexpected fact that contrasts with this assumption and leads into the passage: in reality, there is such a machine.
- Therefore, the contrastive conjunction 「ところが」 (however; indicating that what actually happens is contrary to the usual expectation) is needed at position 19-a, together with the explanatory/emphatic pattern 「～のです」 (here, 「あるのです」) at position 19-b.
default.q.n3-30-q54-54.why.0: (a) 「ところが～あるのです」: Grammatically and contextually appropriate. 「ところが」 (“however”) is used when an unexpected fact contrary to what people thought in the previous sentence occurs, while 「～のです」 asserts the point and introduces an explanation or account of the fact.
default.q.n3-30-q54-54.why.1: (b) 「なぜなら～あるからです」: This is inappropriate. The pattern 「なぜなら～から」 explains a reason (“the reason is that …”), but this sentence does not serve as the reason why everyone laughed in the preceding sentence.
default.q.n3-30-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「でも～あるでしょうか」 is unsuitable. The sentence ending 「～でしょうか」 expresses a question or doubt (“could it be…?”), whereas the author wants to assert that the machine exists and continue the narrative.
default.q.n3-30-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「たとえば～あるとしましょう」: Incorrect. 「たとえば～としましょう」 means “let us suppose that…,” and is used for an imagined hypothetical situation, not to introduce a real event.
default.q.n3-30-q55-55.explanation:
- The previous sentence introduces the vending machine: 「わたしの家の近所には一台の自動販売機があります。」 (There is a vending machine near my house.)
- The sentence containing the blank continues describing that specific machine: "It looks like an ordinary drink vending machine, but [this machine] can talk."
- The demonstrative 「この」 refers to an object mentioned in the immediately preceding sentence, creating a clear connection between the sentences.
default.q.n3-30-q55-55.why.0: (a) 「ある」: Not appropriate. 「ある」 before a noun means “a certain” (e.g., ある日) and is used for an unidentified object, whereas the machine was already specifically identified in the preceding sentence.
default.q.n3-30-q55-55.why.1: (b) 「一台」: Not appropriate. 「一台」is a counter for quantity; when it directly modifies a noun, it must be followed by 「一台の」. Since 「一台の」has already been used in the previous sentence, a demonstrative linking expression is needed here.
default.q.n3-30-q55-55.why.2: (c) 「この」: Grammatically and contextually appropriate. The demonstrative「この」refers to the vending machine near the house that was just mentioned in the previous sentence (“this vending machine”).
default.q.n3-30-q55-55.why.3: (d) 「ふつうの」: Not appropriate. The previous clause already contains 「ふつうの飲み物の自動販売機に見えますが」(it looks like an ordinary vending machine, but...), so repeating 「ふつうの」in the following clause would be redundant and create a contradictory meaning.
default.q.n3-30-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (言っている).
default.q.n3-30-q56-56.explanation:
- Sentence structure: 「[recipient] に、『[spoken content]』と言う」 (say something to someone). Here, the vending machine is the subject performing the act of speaking, saying 「お疲れさまでした。」 to the person who bought a drink (飲み物を買った人に).
- Since the author witnessed this scene, the progressive form 「言っている」 is used together with nominalization in 「のを見たことがあります」 (“I have seen the vending machine saying...”).
default.q.n3-30-q56-56.why.0: (a) 「言っている」: Grammatically and contextually appropriate. The machine is the speaker addressing the customer who bought a drink (飲み物を買った人に saying 「お疲れさまでした」), and the progressive form in 「言っているのを見た」 describes witnessing that scene in progress.
default.q.n3-30-q56-56.why.1: (b) 「言って帰る」: Not appropriate. The machine remains fixed in one place, so it cannot perform the action “say something and then go home” (帰る).
default.q.n3-30-q56-56.why.2: (c) 「言われている」: Inappropriate. The passive form 「言われている」 does not fit the context, in which the server actively speaks to the customer using the pattern 「[buyer] に...と言う」.
default.q.n3-30-q56-56.why.3: (d) 「言われて帰る」: This is inappropriate. Similarly, a machine cannot perform the action 「帰る」.
default.q.n3-30-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (ですから).
default.q.n3-30-q57-57.explanation:
- The passage explains the author's impression:
  + Previous sentence: 「わたしがよく見るアニメの中では、機械も人間と同じようにしゃべったり、歩いたりしています。」 (In the anime I often watch, machines talk and walk just like humans.)
  + Following sentence: Being spoken to by a vending machine makes the author feel as though they are in the world of an anime.
- The two sentences have a cause-and-effect relationship (because machines talk like humans in anime, being spoken to by a real machine makes the author feel as though they have entered an anime), so the most appropriate conjunction is 「ですから」 (therefore / for that reason).
default.q.n3-30-q57-57.why.0: (a) 「一方」: Not appropriate. 「一方」means “on the other hand” or “in contrast,” and is used to compare two parallel aspects rather than express a cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.n3-30-q57-57.why.1: (b) 「ですから」: Grammatically and contextually appropriate. 「ですから」 (therefore / so) expresses a cause-and-effect relationship: because machines talk like people in anime, the vending machine speaking to the author made them feel as if they were in an anime world.
default.q.n3-30-q57-57.why.2: (c) 「それなのに」: Incorrect. 「それなのに」 means “even so / despite that” and is used when the following clause contrasts with the expectation or logic of the preceding clause.
default.q.n3-30-q57-57.why.3: (d) 「そのうえ」: Not suitable. 「そのうえ」means “moreover/in addition,” and is used to add information in the same direction, not simply to indicate a conclusion drawn from the preceding sentence.
default.q.n3-30-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (おどろかない).
default.q.n3-30-q58-58.explanation:
- The opening of the article introduces the topic: 「最近びっくりしたこと」 (Something that surprised me recently).
- In paragraph 3, the author writes: 「最初はとてもびっくりしました。」 (At first, I was very surprised).
- At the end, the author says that they are now used to vending machines talking to them: 「今は、自動販売機が「いってらっしゃい」と話しかけてくるのにも慣れて...」.
- Therefore, the concluding sentence contrasts with the initial surprise: even if vending machines that can walk were invented in the future, the author probably "would no longer be surprised" (おどろかないかもしれません).
default.q.n3-30-q58-58.why.0: (a) 「信じない」: Not appropriate. 「信じない」(not believe) does not fit the logic of the passage, because the author has witnessed technological development and has become accustomed to it, rather than being skeptical or unable to believe it.
default.q.n3-30-q58-58.why.1: (b) 「言い返さない」: inappropriate. 「言い返さない」 (not respond or talk back) does not fit the psychological reaction of accepting something unfamiliar.
default.q.n3-30-q58-58.why.2: (c) 「しゃべらない」: Inappropriate. 「しゃべらない」 (not to talk) does not fit the meaning of this context.
default.q.n3-30-q58-58.why.3: (d) 「おどろかない」: This is grammatically and contextually appropriate. 「おどろかない」(not be surprised) forms a clear correspondence with the topic 「びっくりしたこと」and the earlier sentence 「最初はとてもびっくりしました」, showing that the author has become accustomed to it and will no longer be surprised.
default.q.n3-30-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 道を歩きながら、タバコを吸ってはいけない (You must not smoke while walking).
default.q.n3-30-q59-59.explanation:
- Main point summary: The city of Asahi introduced three new prohibitions: (1) throwing trash anywhere other than designated places such as trash bins, (2) smoking while walking, and (3) parking bicycles outside designated areas. Violators may also be fined in some cases.

**Question translation:**
Which of the following statements about these rules is correct?

**Answer choices:**
1. Trash may not be thrown anywhere except at one's own home.
2. Smoking while walking along the street is prohibited.
3. Bicycles may not be ridden outside designated areas.
4. Everyone who does not follow the rules must pay a fine.
default.q.n3-30-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the rule only prohibits throwing garbage anywhere other than designated places such as trash cans (「ゴミ箱などの決められた場所以外にゴミを捨てること」). It does not prohibit throwing garbage outside one’s home if there is a designated place or trash can there.
default.q.n3-30-q59-59.why.1: (b) Correct because the passage clearly states that the second prohibited act is:「②　歩きながらタバコを吸うこと」 (smoking while walking).
default.q.n3-30-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the rule prohibits parking bicycles outside designated areas (「指定の場所以外に自転車をとめること」), not riding bicycles (「走ってはいけない」).
default.q.n3-30-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the text only says that some people may be fined (「守らなかった場合は、お金を払わされることもあるそうだ」), not that everyone who violates the rule must pay (「全員」).
default.q.n3-30-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The important thing when choosing a hospital is to have one’s own standards and genuinely feel that the hospital is good for oneself.
default.q.n3-30-q60-60.explanation:
- Main point: The passage discusses what makes a good hospital and how to find one. The author points out that each person has different criteria and that there are many ways to gather information, but the essential point is that the final decision must be one's own. To choose a hospital that makes one feel secure and confident, it is important to have a firm "measuring stick for choosing a good hospital" («いい病院を選ぶための物差しを、自分の中にしっかり持っていることが重要だ»).
- Question translation: According to the passage, what is important when choosing a hospital?
- Answer choices:
  1. The doctors at the hospital listen carefully.
  2. The hospital has many new, state-of-the-art machines.
  3. The hospital has been recommended in books, newspapers, or magazines.
  4. You yourself are certain that the hospital is good.
default.q.n3-30-q60-60.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the doctor's willingness to listen carefully is merely an example illustrating differences in people's perspectives («医師がよく話を聞いてくれる、最新の機械があるかどうかと。人によって考えは様々だ»), not the main point the author wishes to emphasize.
default.q.n3-30-q60-60.why.1: (b) Incorrect because having new machinery is only one example of each individual's personal criteria («最新の機械があるかどうかと»), not the conclusion about what matters when making a choice.
default.q.n3-30-q60-60.why.2: (c) Incorrect because books, newspapers, and magazines are merely ways to look up reference information («人に聞いたり、本や雑誌、インターネットなどで調べたり、いくらでも方法はある»), not criteria for making a decision.
default.q.n3-30-q60-60.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage states: 「しかし、最終的に選ぶのは自分である。いい病院を選ぶための物差しを、自分の中にしっかり持っていることが重要だ。」 The final choice is one’s own, and it is important to have a firm personal standard for choosing a good hospital. This, together with 「結局、自分にとって安心できる病院がいい病院だと言えるだろう」, supports the answer.
default.q.n3-30-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (文房具の説明にいつ来られるかと聞くこと).
default.q.n3-30-q61-61.explanation:
**Main point:**
Suzuki, who is in charge of stationery at Kawamura Department Store, emails Wada of the Sales Department at Nihon Note to say that Suzuki has looked at the stationery catalogue sent the previous day. Since Suzuki would like to hear Wada explain and introduce the products in person, Suzuki invites Wada to visit and asks Wada to let them know a convenient date.

**Question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** What is the purpose of Suzuki's email to Wada?
- **1.** To ask Wada to send a stationery catalogue.
- **2.** To ask Wada to look at a stationery catalogue.
- **3.** To ask when Wada can come and explain the stationery products.
- **4.** To ask when Suzuki should go and explain the stationery products.
default.q.n3-30-q61-61.why.0: (a) Incorrect because Suzuki had already received and looked at the catalog (「先日送っていただきました『新学期向け文房具』のカタログを拝見しました」); the letter was not being sent to request the catalog.
default.q.n3-30-q61-61.why.1: (b) Incorrect because Suzuki is the person who looks at the catalogue sent by Wada; Suzuki does not ask Wada to look at it.
default.q.n3-30-q61-61.why.2: (c) Correct because the letter says: 「ぜひ一度、お話をうかがいたいので、こちらに来ていただけますでしょうか。ご都合のよい日をお知らせください。」 (I would very much like to hear from you in person, so would you be able to come here? Please let me know a convenient date).
default.q.n3-30-q61-61.why.3: (d) Incorrect because Suzuki invites Wada to come to Suzuki’s location (「こちらに来ていただけますでしょうか」), rather than asking when Suzuki should go to Wada’s location (「行ったらいいか」).
default.q.n3-30-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 2: Applicants had to choose one of two themes—“Peace” or “The Environment”—and submit a painting.
default.q.n3-30-q62-62.explanation:
**Main points:**
The Kawada Museum of Art is celebrating its 10th anniversary and issuing two types of commemorative stamps. The museum is selecting paintings to print on the stamps under two themes, «Peace» and «Environment». Applicants must choose one of the two themes. The drawing paper must be the specified size (20x25cm), but any drawing tool or medium may be used.

**Question translation:**
What must applicants do?

**Answer choices:**
1. Draw a picture on the theme «Peace and Environment» and submit it.
2. Choose one of the two themes, draw a picture, and submit it.
3. Draw a picture on paper of any size and submit it.
4. Draw a picture using the specified type of paint and submit it.
default.q.n3-30-q62-62.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the article clearly says 「どちらかを選んで応募してください」(please choose one of the two topics and apply), not to draw a picture combining both topics, 「平和と環境」.
default.q.n3-30-q62-62.why.1: (b) Correct because it is quoted directly from the passage: 「テーマは「平和」と「環境」の二つです。どちらかを選んで応募してください。」(There are two themes, “Peace” and “Environment.” Choose one of them and apply.)
default.q.n3-30-q62-62.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage clearly says「紙は指定の大きさ(20X25cm)のものを使ってください」(please use paper of the specified size, 20X25 cm), so any size (好きな大きさ) is not allowed.
default.q.n3-30-q62-62.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage says 「絵の具、色えんぴつなど、何を使ってかいてもかまいません」 (“you may use paints, colored pencils, or anything else to draw”), so a specified type of paint (決められた絵の具) is not required.
default.q.n3-30-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3: Whenever there is a special occasion, the author usually buys flowers at this shop.
default.q.n3-30-q63-63.explanation:
**Main idea:**
The author shares childhood memories connected with the flower shop near home, especially going there with their mother to buy flowers for special occasions such as family birthdays or visits from guests.

**Question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** The sentence ① says, “Memories of the flower shop are connected with childhood memories.” What kind of memory is this?
- **Choice 1:** The flower shop opened when I started elementary school.
- **Choice 2:** When I graduated from elementary school, I bought flowers at this shop with my teacher.
- **Choice 3:** Whenever there was a special occasion, I often bought flowers at this shop.
- **Choice 4:** Because I liked the florist very much, I often bought flowers at this shop.
default.q.n3-30-q63-63.why.0: (a) Option 1 is incorrect because the passage says the shop opened before the author entered elementary school (「この店がオープンしたのは、わたしがまだ小学校に入る前だった」), not when the author started elementary school.
default.q.n3-30-q63-63.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because when the author graduated from elementary school, the author and classmates bought flowers for their homeroom teacher (「担任の先生に花束をおくることになった」), rather than going shopping with the teacher.
default.q.n3-30-q63-63.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because the passage states: 「家族の誕生日や家にお客さんが来る時などには、母と一緒にこの店で花を買っていた。」 (On occasions such as family birthdays or when guests came to the house, I would buy flowers at this shop with my mother)—that is, the author usually bought flowers there with their mother when there was a special occasion (特別なことがある時).
default.q.n3-30-q63-63.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the author buys flowers for family birthdays or when guests come to the house. The passage does not say that the author often buys flowers because they “really like the florist.”
default.q.n3-30-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4: Although the speaker had very little money, they made an excessive request to the florist by asking for a very large bouquet.
default.q.n3-30-q64-64.explanation:
**Main point:** When they graduated from elementary school, the whole class wanted to give their teacher a very large bouquet, but they had collected only a small amount of pocket money. Therefore, the children felt both nervous and anxious as they boldly asked the florist to make a very large bouquet with their limited funds.

**Translation of the question and choices:**
- **Question:** In sentence ②, “We were both nervous...,” why were the children nervous?
- **Choice 1:** Because they made an excessive request to the florist at a shop that was about to close.
- **Choice 2:** Because they made an excessive request to the man, who looked displeased.
- **Choice 3:** Because the shop did not have many flowers, yet they made an excessive request to the florist.
- **Choice 4:** Because they had only a small amount of money, yet they made an excessive request to the florist.
default.q.n3-30-q64-64.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the nervous memory of making flowers took place at elementary school graduation in the past, whereas the flower shop’s closure happened recently (「最近、近所の花屋が閉店した」).
default.q.n3-30-q64-64.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the passage clearly states that the uncle did not look displeased (「おじさんは嫌な顔もしないで」).
default.q.n3-30-q64-64.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the passage does not mention that there were not many flowers in the shop.
default.q.n3-30-q64-64.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because the passage states: 「しかし、小学生のおこづかいの中集まったお金は少しだけだった。それで、②わたしたちはどきどきしながら、「大好きな先生にあげるから、できるだけ大きい花束を作ってください」とお願いした。」 (However, the amount collected from the elementary school students' pocket money was small. So, nervously, we asked, “We are giving it to our beloved teacher, so please make the largest bouquet possible”).
default.q.n3-30-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: Deep gratitude toward the flower seller who created warm and wonderful memories.
default.q.n3-30-q65-65.explanation:
**Main point:** When a long-established flower shop near the author's home closes, the author recalls fond childhood memories connected with the shop and expresses sincere appreciation and gratitude to the kind uncle who ran it for more than 30 years.

**Question and choice translations:**
- **Question:** What does the writer most want to convey in this essay?
- **Choice 1:** Gratitude toward the teacher who helped them greatly during elementary school.
- **Choice 2:** Gratitude toward the uncle who ran the flower shop and created wonderful memories.
- **Choice 3:** Sadness that the flower shop they loved has closed.
- **Choice 4:** The inconvenience caused by the closure of the flower shop near their home.
default.q.n3-30-q65-65.why.0: (a) Answer choice 1 is incorrect because giving flowers to the teacher is only a childhood memory illustrating the flower seller’s kindness, not the main message the author wants to convey.
default.q.n3-30-q65-65.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because the passage concludes: 「30年以上もきれいな花束を作り続け、あたたかい思い出を作ってくれたおじさんに、「ありがとう、お疲れ様でした。」と言いたい。」 (I want to say, “Thank you. You have worked so hard,” to the man who continued making beautiful bouquets for more than 30 years and created warm memories).
default.q.n3-30-q65-65.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the author focuses on expressing gratitude and appreciation to the flower shop owner rather than merely describing the sadness of the shop closing.
default.q.n3-30-q65-65.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage never mentions feeling “inconvenienced” (不便) when the flower shop is closed.
default.q.n3-30-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 1. いらなくなった物から新しい物を作ること (making new things from items that are no longer needed).
default.q.n3-30-q66-66.explanation:
- Main idea: Paragraph 1 defines "recycling" (リサイクル) as breaking down or transforming things that are no longer needed into other objects (for example, using newspapers that have been read to produce toilet paper).
- Question translation: In this passage, what does the author say recycling is?
- Answer choices:
1. Making new things from things that are no longer needed.
2. Destroying things that are no longer needed and throwing them away.
3. Not damaging objects and reducing the amount of waste.
4. Not throwing things away but using them again in the same form.
default.q.n3-30-q66-66.why.0: (a) Correct. Quotation:「リサイクルとは、いらない物を壊して、別の物に作り変えることだ。」(Recycling means breaking down unwanted things and transforming them into different objects.)
default.q.n3-30-q66-66.why.1: (b) Incorrect because recycling is not throwing something away (捨てる), but transforming it into another object (別の物に作り変える).
default.q.n3-30-q66-66.why.2: (c) Incorrect because recycling involves changing or breaking down objects (いらない物を壊して), whereas “without breaking the object” (物を壊さないで) describes reuse (再使用).
default.q.n3-30-q66-66.why.3: (d) Incorrect because "using something again exactly as it is" (そのままもう一度使う) is the definition of reuse (再使用: ものを壊さないで、何度も使う), not recycling (リサイクル).
default.q.n3-30-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 再使用する物は丈夫に作られている (Items intended for reuse are made to be strong and durable).
default.q.n3-30-q67-67.explanation:
- Main point: Paragraph 2 introduces the method of "reuse" (再使用), explaining that reusable plastic bottles are made thick and sturdy (丈夫 / 少し厚くしっかりと作られている) so they can be used many times.
- Question translation: What does the passage say about reusing plastic bottles?
- Answer choices:
1. Reuse costs absolutely nothing.
2. Reused items cannot be recycled.
3. The only reusable item is a plastic bottle.
4. Items intended for reuse are made very sturdy and durable.
default.q.n3-30-q67-67.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage clearly states that, depending on the situation, reuse may consume more money and energy (場合によっては再使用の方がお金やエネルギーを使う); it does not say that reuse costs nothing.
default.q.n3-30-q67-67.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage does not mention at all that reusable items cannot be recycled.
default.q.n3-30-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect because plastic bottles are merely one illustrative example (例えば、飲んだ後のペットボトルを...); the passage does not say that only plastic bottles can be reused.
default.q.n3-30-q67-67.why.3: (d) Correct. The quotation states: 「再使用するペットボトルは何回も使えるように、少し厚くしっかりと作られている。」 (Reusable plastic bottles are made slightly thicker and sturdier so that they can be used many times; 「しっかりと作られている」 is synonymous with 「丈夫に作られている」).
default.q.n3-30-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 3. リサイクルと再使用では、どちらが環境にいいか簡単には決められない (It is not easy to determine whether recycling or reuse is better for the environment).
default.q.n3-30-q68-68.explanation:
- Main point: Paragraph 3 compares recycling and reuse, explaining that people used to think reuse was better, but closer examination shows that, depending on the circumstances, reuse can require more money and energy. Therefore, it is not possible to simply say which option is better for the environment.
- Question translation: In this passage, what does the author say when comparing recycling and reuse?
- Answer choices:
1. Recycling is better for the environment than reuse because it does not consume energy.
2. Reuse reduces waste and has fewer negative effects on the environment than recycling.
3. It is not easy to determine which is better for the environment, recycling or reuse.
4. Both recycling and reuse cause environmental problems, so it is better to stop doing them.
default.q.n3-30-q68-68.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage does not state that recycling uses less energy than reuse; the energy consumption of both depends on the circumstances.
default.q.n3-30-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect because this was an earlier belief (以前は...と考えられていた), whereas actual research shows that, depending on the situation, reuse can cost more money and energy.
default.q.n3-30-q68-68.why.2: (c) Correct. Quotation: 「最近はどちらの方が環境にいいとは単純には言えなくなっている。」 (“Recently, it has become impossible to simply say which option is better for the environment.”) 「単純には言えない」 is synonymous with 「簡単には決められない」.
default.q.n3-30-q68-68.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not contain any advice to stop (中止したほうがいい) these two methods.
default.q.n3-30-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 森さんも会社をやめてそば屋を開いた人の一人である。
default.q.n3-30-q69-69.explanation:
- Main idea: The passage begins by stating that recently, many people have left companies where they worked for a long time to open Japanese soba restaurants, and Mr. Mori is one of them. Therefore, “one of them” (その一人) refers to people who left their companies to open soba restaurants.
- Question translation: The sentence says, “①Mr. Mori is also one of them.” What does this mean?
- Answer choices:
1. Mr. Mori is also one of the people who left their companies to open soba restaurants.
2. Mr. Mori is also one of the people who opened soba restaurants in April this year.
3. Mr. Mori is also one of the people who opened a restaurant with his wife.
4. Mr. Mori is also one of the people who opened a restaurant near Nakamura Station.
default.q.n3-30-q69-69.why.0: (a) 「最近、長い間働いた会社をやめて、日本そば屋を始める人が増えているそうだ。…森さんもその一人だ」: The demonstrative expression 「その一人」 directly refers to the group mentioned in the previous sentence: people who quit companies where they had worked for a long time and opened Japanese soba restaurants.
default.q.n3-30-q69-69.why.1: The point “April of this year” is simply the time when Mr. and Mrs. Mori opened the restaurant; it is not the referent of 「その一人」.
default.q.n3-30-q69-69.why.2: (c) The detail that “the married couple opened a restaurant” is specific to Mr. Mori’s family and is not the content replaced by the demonstrative pronoun.
default.q.n3-30-q69-69.why.3: (d) “Opening a restaurant near Nakamura Station” refers to Mr. Mori’s own restaurant location, not the group of people mentioned in the trend in the previous sentence.
default.q.n3-30-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 3. そばは、ほかの料理に比べると簡単にできるし、外食の中で人気があるから。
default.q.n3-30-q70-70.explanation:
- Main idea: Paragraph 2 explains why many people open soba restaurants: compared with other restaurants, soba uses fewer types of ingredients and is not too difficult to prepare; also, as more people have recently become health-conscious, healthy soba has become a popular choice when eating out.
- Question translation: There is a statement that "②Many people open soba restaurants." What reason does the author give?
- Answer choices:
1. Because the number of people being laid off from companies where they had worked for many years has recently increased.
2. Because opening a soba restaurant will definitely increase one's income compared with working as a company employee.
3. Because soba is easier to prepare than other dishes and is popular when eating out.
4. Because soba is cheaper than tempura or sushi, so many people eat it.
default.q.n3-30-q70-70.why.0: (a) The passage only says that everyone quit voluntarily (会社をやめて); it does not mention being forced to leave or being fired (やめさせられる).
default.q.n3-30-q70-70.why.1: (b) Passage 1 clearly states that actual income decreased (収入は減った); it does not say that income definitely increased.
default.q.n3-30-q70-70.why.2: (c) 「そば屋は、てんぷら屋やすし屋…に比べると、あつかう材料の種類も少なく、作り方もそれほど難しくない。また、最近は健康に気をつける人が増え、外食の時にそばのような体にいい食べ物を選ぶ人も多くなっているからだ」: Soba restaurants use fewer kinds of ingredients, their preparation is not especially difficult, and soba is healthy, so many people choose it when eating out.
default.q.n3-30-q70-70.why.3: The passage does not mention the factor of “a lower price” (値段が安い) at all.
default.q.n3-30-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is 4. The requirement to remain smiling at the store no matter what happens.
default.q.n3-30-q71-71.explanation:
- Main point: Immediately after saying "That sounds tough," the wife explains the reason using a cause-explanation pattern: "Because even if I argue with my husband, I still have to keep smiling at the shop (にこにこしていなければなりませんから)." In other words, she has to keep smiling at the shop no matter what happens.
- Translation of the question: In the statement "③That sounds tough," what is tough?
- Translation of the choices:
1. Having to keep making delicious soba with the same flavor.
2. Having to start preparing to open the shop at 6 a.m.
3. Having to research how to make delicious soba every night.
4. Having to keep smiling at the shop no matter what happens.
default.q.n3-30-q71-71.why.0: (a) Preserving soba’s original flavor is the professional challenge mentioned by the author in paragraph 3, not what the wife explains as the reason for her statement.
default.q.n3-30-q71-71.why.1: (b) Preparing from 6:00 a.m. is Mr. Mori’s work, mentioned in the previous sentence; it is not the reason his wife says, “That must be hard.”
default.q.n3-30-q71-71.why.2: (c) Researching how to make soba noodles every evening is Mr. Mori’s work, not what his wife is talking about.
default.q.n3-30-q71-71.why.3: (d) 「『大変ですよ。夫とけんかをしても、店ではにこにこしていなければなりませんから』と、奥さんが笑う」: The wife explains that the work is demanding because even if she argues with her husband, she still has to smile at customers while in the shop (she must keep smiling regardless of what happens - 笑顔).
default.q.n3-30-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 毎日疲れるし、おいしいそばを作るのは大変だが、やってよかった。
default.q.n3-30-q72-72.explanation:
- Main point: Although his income has decreased and making soba and running the restaurant are demanding, requiring early preparation and nighttime research, Mr. Mori is very happy when customers compliment him and says that he feels fortunate and believes opening the restaurant was the right decision (やってよかったと思っています).
- Question: What does Mr. Mori currently say about opening the soba restaurant?
- Answer choices:
1. Every day is enjoyable, but his income has decreased, so he wishes he had not opened it.
2. He has become busier and argues more with his wife, so he wishes he had not opened it.
3. Nothing is particularly difficult, so opening the restaurant was a good decision.
4. Every day is exhausting and making delicious soba is difficult, but opening the restaurant was a good decision.
default.q.n3-30-q72-72.why.0: (a) Paragraph 1 clearly quotes Mori saying 「今はやってよかったと思っています」(Now I think opening the shop was a good decision), which is the opposite of “I should not have done it” (やらないほうがよかった).
default.q.n3-30-q72-72.why.1: (b) The passage does not say that marital arguments increased or that Mr. Mori was satisfied with his decision; it does not say that he thought, “I should not have done it.”
default.q.n3-30-q72-72.why.2: (c) The passage shows that making soba is difficult and demanding (preparing from 6 a.m., doing research at night, and maintaining the flavor are all challenging), so saying that it is "not demanding or difficult at all" is incorrect.
default.q.n3-30-q72-72.why.3: (d) 「『収入は減ったけど、今はやってよかったと思っています』と、森さんは言う」「お客さんの『おいしかったよ』という言葉を聞くと、疲れも消えるんですよ」: Although the work is demanding and tiring, Mori says that opening the restaurant was the right decision (やってよかった).
default.q.n3-30-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 参加費と昼食 (participation fee and lunch).
default.q.n3-30-q73-73.explanation:
- Main point: The notice for the digital camera class (デジタルカメラ教室) clearly states what participants need to bring: postcards will be provided free of charge by the organizers (はがきはこちらで用意します(無料)); participants who have a camera should bring it, while those who do not have one can borrow one (お持ちの方は、ご持参ください。持っていない方には、お貸しします). However, all participants must bring the 500-yen participation fee to pay on the day (参加費 一人500円(当日お支払いください)) and must bring their own lunch (昼食はご持参ください).
- Question translation: According to this notice, what must participants bring?
- Answer choices:
  1. The participation fee and postcards
  2. The participation fee and lunch
  3. Lunch only
  4. The participation fee only
default.q.n3-30-q73-73.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the postcards (はがき) are prepared free of charge by the organizers (※はがきはこちらで用意します(無料)); participants are not required to bring one.
default.q.n3-30-q73-73.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because the passage clearly states that the participation fee must be paid on the day: 「●参加費 一人500円(当日お支払いください)」, and that participants must bring their own lunch: 「●その他 ... 昼食はご持参ください」. These are therefore the two things participants must bring or prepare.
default.q.n3-30-q73-73.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because, in addition to lunch (昼食), participants are also required to bring the 500-yen participation fee and pay it on the day ("●参加費 一人500円(当日お支払いください)").
default.q.n3-30-q73-73.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because, in addition to the participation fee (参加費), participants are required to bring their own lunch (“昼食はご持参ください”).
default.q.n3-30-q74-74.verdict: The correct answer is 1. デジタルカメラ教室への参加を申し込みます。①中川市大田2-5-1 ②小林花子　小林一郎(6年生) ③031-849-8713 ④カメラを借ります
default.q.n3-30-q74-74.explanation:
- Main idea: The passage explains the requirements and information to be entered on the application postcard. Elementary school students in fifth grade or above who wish to participate must be accompanied by an adult family member (小学生は家族の大人の方がいっしょに参加してください). When applying as a family, the full names of everyone and the elementary school student’s grade must be provided (②氏名(小学生も学年も) / ※家族でお申し込みの場合は、全員お書きください). If an applicant wishes to borrow a digital camera, this must be indicated in section ④ (④デジタルカメラの貸し出しを希望するかどうか). Ichiro, a sixth-grade student, wants to borrow a camera, so his postcard must include the name of the accompanying adult (Kobayashi Hanako), his own name and grade (Kobayashi Ichiro (Grade 6)), his address, telephone number, and a clear indication that he wants to borrow a camera.
- Translation of the question: Kobayashi Ichiro, a sixth-grade elementary school student, wants to participate in this class. Since he does not have a digital camera, he plans to borrow one from the photography studio. Which application postcard is filled out correctly?
- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. Application for the digital camera class / ① Address / ② Kobayashi Hanako, Kobayashi Ichiro (Grade 6) / ③ Telephone number / ④ Borrow a camera
  2. Application for the digital camera class / ① Address / ② Kobayashi Hanako, Kobayashi Ichiro (Grade 6) / ③ Telephone number (Section ④, borrowing a camera, is missing)
  3. Application for the digital camera class / ① Address / ② Kobayashi Hanako, one child (Grade 6) / ③ Telephone number / ④ Borrow a camera (The student’s full name is not provided)
  4. Application for the digital camera class / ① Address / ② Kobayashi Ichiro (Grade 6) / ③ Telephone number (The accompanying adult and section ④ are missing)
default.q.n3-30-q74-74.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is correct because the instructions require elementary school students to participate with an adult family member ("小学生は家族の大人の方がいっしょに参加してください"). When applying as a family, everyone's name and the student's grade must be entered ("※家族でお申し込みの場合は、全員お書きください", "②氏名(小学生も学年も)"), and those wishing to borrow a camera must indicate this in item ④ ("④デジタルカメラの貸し出しを希望するかどうか"). Postcard 1 includes the adult's full name (小林花子), the student's name and grade (小林一郎(6年生)), and a request to borrow a camera (④カメラを借ります).
default.q.n3-30-q74-74.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is incorrect because it omits item ④, which indicates the desire to borrow a camera. Ichiro does not have a camera and wants to borrow one from the studio (「④デジタルカメラの貸し出しを希望するかどうかお申し込みください」).
default.q.n3-30-q74-74.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because item ② gives only the general description 「子ども一名(6年生)」 instead of the student’s full name, as required by 「②氏名(小学生も学年も)」.
default.q.n3-30-q74-74.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because elementary school students must be accompanied by an adult family member and all participants’ names must be written down («小学生は家族の大人の方がいっしょに参加してください», «※家族でお申し込みの場合は、全員お書きください»). However, the postcard lists only Ichiro’s name and leaves item ④, borrowing a camera, blank as well.
default.q.n3-30-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 1. つつんで because the verb 「包む」 (to wrap, cover) has the kun'yomi reading つつむ, which changes to つつんで in the te-form.
default.q.n3-30-q1-1.explanation:
Meaning: The present was wrapped in beautiful paper.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 包 (BAO — to wrap, enclose).
- Example: 割れ物をタオルで包んで箱に入れた。(I wrapped the fragile item in a towel and put it in a box.)
default.q.n3-30-q1-1.why.0: (a) Correct. The verb 「包む」 (つつむ: to wrap or bundle) forms its te-form as 「包んで」 (つつんで).
default.q.n3-30-q1-1.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The character「包」is read with the sound「つ」in both the initial and medial positions; it does not undergo voicing to「づ」.
default.q.n3-30-q1-1.why.2: (c) Incorrect.「包」in this verb is read with the short sound「つつむ」; it does not contain a long vowel「う」.
default.q.n3-30-q1-1.why.3: (d) Incorrect. This choice is wrong both because it adds the long vowel 「う」 and because it uses the voiced pronunciation 「づ」.
default.q.n3-30-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 4. とくい because the kanji compound 「得意」 consists of 得 (とく) and 意 (い), and is correctly read とくい.
default.q.n3-30-q2-2.explanation:
Meaning: He is very good at dancing.
- Kanji reading: 得意 (good at, one's forte).
- Example: 彼女は料理が得意です。(She is very good at cooking.)
default.q.n3-30-q2-2.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「得」 is read with a short vowel and has the sound in 「とく」; it does not have the voiced sound 「ど」 or a long 「お/う」 sound.
default.q.n3-30-q2-2.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「得」 is pronounced with the short sound 「とく」; it does not have the long vowel 「お」.
default.q.n3-30-q2-2.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「得」is read 「とく」; it does not undergo voicing to become 「どく」.
default.q.n3-30-q2-2.why.3: (d) Correct. 「得意」 has the correct on-reading とくい and describes a strong point or being good at something.
default.q.n3-30-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 1. はっけん because when 「発」(はつ) is combined with 「見」(けん), the sound changes to the geminated form はっけん.
default.q.n3-30-q3-3.explanation:
Meaning: A new star has been discovered.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 発見 (HAKKEN — discovery, discovering).
- Example: 新種のカエルが発見された。(A new species of frog was discovered.)
default.q.n3-30-q3-3.why.0: (a) Correct. When 「発」 (はつ) comes before the /k/ sound of 「見」 (けん), it produces the geminate sound 「はっけん」.
default.q.n3-30-q3-3.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The small pause marker 「っ」 is missing; 「はけん」 is the reading of 「派遣」, meaning dispatch or assignment.
default.q.n3-30-q3-3.why.2: (c) Incorrect. In this compound word, 「つ」must change to the geminate sound 「っ」; it cannot remain 「はつけん」.
default.q.n3-30-q3-3.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「発」is not read as「ばつ」in this word.
default.q.n3-30-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 4. あらわして because the kanji 「表」 in the verb 「表す」has the kun-reading あらわす, whose te-form is あらわして.
default.q.n3-30-q4-4.explanation:
Meaning: This graph shows changes in population.
- Sino-Japanese roots: 表 (BIỂU - to express, display, represent).
- Example: 言葉で気持ちを表すのは難しい。(It is difficult to express feelings in words.)
default.q.n3-30-q4-4.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「しめして」 is the te-form of 「示す」 (to indicate, show).
default.q.n3-30-q4-4.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「ふやして」is the te-form of the verb 「増やす」, meaning “to increase something.”
default.q.n3-30-q4-4.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「うごかして」 is the te-form of the verb 「動かす」 (to move or operate).
default.q.n3-30-q4-4.why.3: (d) Correct. The verb 「表す」 (to express or represent) is read あらわす, and its te-form is あらわして.
default.q.n3-30-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 1. けん because the kanji 「件」has the on-reading けん and means “an incident” or “a matter.”
default.q.n3-30-q5-5.explanation:
Meaning: There was a phone call from Mr. Yamada about next week's meeting.
- Kanji: 件 (matter, issue, case).
- Example: その件については後でお話しします。(I will discuss that matter with you later.)
default.q.n3-30-q5-5.why.0: (a) Correct. The kanji 「件」 has the on-reading けん and indicates the matter or issue being discussed.
default.q.n3-30-q5-5.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「あん」 is the reading of 「案」 (plan, proposal, draft).
default.q.n3-30-q5-5.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「ほう」is the reading of kanji such as 「方」, 「報」, and 「法」...
default.q.n3-30-q5-5.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「よう」is the reading of kanji such as 「用」, 「様」, and 「要」...
default.q.n3-30-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 2. つうきん because the kanji 「通」 is read つう and 「勤」 is read きん, forming 「通勤」 (つうきん).
default.q.n3-30-q6-6.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Commuting to work takes a great deal of time.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 通勤 (commuting to work).

default.q.n3-4-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 続けられている, in the passive pattern 「N は 〜 によって V-(ら)れる」 (is maintained by someone).
default.q.n3-4-q44-44.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “This summer festival has been maintained by people living in this town since more than 100 years ago.”
- N3 grammar: 「N は 〜 によって V-passive」(something is carried out or created by a particular agent).
- Example: この寺は有名な建築家によって建てられました。(This temple was built by a famous architect.)
default.q.n3-4-q44-44.why.0: (a) 1. 続けてもらえる: The benefactive form (V-てもらう) cannot combine with a thing as its subject and an agent marked by 「〜によって」 in this context.
default.q.n3-4-q44-44.why.1: (b) 2. 続けさせられる: The causative-passive form means “be forced to continue” and has a negative nuance, which does not fit the context of preserving a festival tradition.
default.q.n3-4-q44-44.why.2: (c) 3. 続けられている: Correct because the passive structure「〜によって V-られる」(be maintained or continued by...) describes a festival tradition preserved by the townspeople for over 100 years.
default.q.n3-4-q44-44.why.3: (d) 4. 続けてくれている expresses someone continuing to do something as a favor for the speaker. It is not used when an inanimate thing is the subject with 「によって」.
default.q.n3-4-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 買ったの, using the casual information-seeking structure 「V-た + の?」.
default.q.n3-4-q45-45.explanation:
Translation:
A: “These cookies are delicious. Where did you buy them?”
B: “At Sakura Shopping Center.”
- Grammar: The plain form +「の？」is used in casual spoken language to ask for a reason or additional information.
- Example: その可愛いかばん、どこで買ったの？(Where did you buy that cute bag?)
default.q.n3-4-q45-45.why.0: (a) 1. 買ったの: Correct because the sentence-final form 「〜の?」 is used in casual conversation after a question word (どこで/とこで) to seek detailed information (“Where did you buy it?”).
default.q.n3-4-q45-45.why.1: (b) 2. 買ったよね: The sentence ending 「〜よね」 seeks agreement or confirmation about something the speaker already knows; it is not used immediately after a question word.
default.q.n3-4-q45-45.why.2: (c) 3. 買ったことある: The structure 「〜たことがある」 asks about past experience ("have you ever bought one?"), so it is not suitable for asking about the origin of the cake being eaten.
default.q.n3-4-q45-45.why.3: (d) 4. 買ったんじゃない: The structure 「〜んじゃない?」 expresses an affirmative conjecture (“didn’t you buy it at…?”), so it is not used with an interrogative word to ask for new information.
default.q.n3-4-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 3. しておいてください because it combines 「〜ままにする」(keep something in its current state) with 「〜ておいてください」(please do something in advance/keep something ready).
default.q.n3-4-q46-46.explanation:
Translation:
A: “Everyone, thank you for your hard work in the meeting. This meeting room will be used again later, so please leave the air conditioner on.”
B: “Yes, understood.”
- N3 grammar: 「〜ままにする」(leave something in its current state) + 「〜ておく」(do something in advance for a later purpose).
- Example: ドアは開けたままにしておいてください。(Please leave the door open.)
default.q.n3-4-q46-46.why.0: (a) 1. していませんか: This is an interrogative sentence meaning “aren’t you doing...?” It does not fit the context of making a polite request, to which B responds 「はい、わかりました」.
default.q.n3-4-q46-46.why.1: (b) 2. なっていませんか: uses the intransitive verb 「なる」 in an interrogative form, so it is not suitable for asking the other person to perform an action.
default.q.n3-4-q46-46.why.2: (c) 3. しておいてください: Correct because 「つけたままにする」 (“leave it switched on”) combines with 「〜ておいてください」 (“please do/leave it in preparation for later”) to form a polite request appropriate to the context.
default.q.n3-4-q46-46.why.3: (d) 4. なっておいてください: 「なる」is an intransitive verb and does not combine with the active request pattern 「〜ておいてください」to ask someone to maintain an object in a state caused by human action.
default.q.n3-4-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 悪いことではない, used with the structure 「必ずしも 〜 ではない」, meaning “not necessarily” or “not always the case.”
default.q.n3-4-q47-47.explanation:
Translation: "The magazine I read yesterday said, 'Forgetting is not necessarily a bad thing.'"
- N3 grammar: 「必ずしも 〜 ではない / わけではない / とは限らない」(not necessarily..., it does not always mean..., not certain to...).
- Example: 高いものが必ずしも良いものだとは限らない。(Expensive things are not necessarily good.)
default.q.n3-4-q47-47.why.0: (a) 1. 悪いことなのだ: This is an affirmative form, whereas 「必ずしも」must be accompanied by a negative clause.
default.q.n3-4-q47-47.why.1: (b) 2. 悪いことではない: Correct because 「必ずしも 〜 ではない」 means “not necessarily...” or “not always...,” expressing partial negation.
default.q.n3-4-q47-47.why.2: (c) 3. 悪いことのはずだ: The strongly affirmative judgment ending「〜はずだ」cannot be combined with「必ずしも」.
default.q.n3-4-q47-47.why.3: (d) 4. 悪いことかもしれない: The conjectural ending 「〜かもしれない」 does not form a standard grammatical pairing with 「必ずしも」.
default.q.n3-4-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 3. なさいますか because it is the respectful form (尊敬語) of the verb 「する」.
default.q.n3-4-q48-48.explanation:
Dialogue translation:
Student: “Teacher, do you play any sports on weekdays?”
Teacher: “Yes, I do. I sometimes play golf.”
- Honorific language: The verb「する」becomes the respectful form「なさる (なさいます)」and the humble form「いたす (いたします)」.
- Example: 週末は何をなさいますか。(What will you do this weekend?)
default.q.n3-4-q48-48.why.0: (a) 1. いたしますか: 「いたす」is the 謙譲語 (humble form) of 「する」. It is used only for the speaker's own actions, not for the teacher's actions.
default.q.n3-4-q48-48.why.1: (b) 2. まいりますか: 「まいる」is the humble form (謙譲語) of「行く/来る」, so it is incorrect both in terms of honorific type and meaning when used with「スポーツを〜」.
default.q.n3-4-q48-48.why.2: (c) 3. なさいますか: Correct because 「なさる」 (polite form 「なさいます」) is the respectful form (尊敬語) of 「する」, used to show respect for the teacher's sporting activity.
default.q.n3-4-q48-48.why.3: (d) 4. いらっしゃいますか: 「いらっしゃる」is the respectful form of 行く, 来る, and いる. It cannot replace する in the phrase 「スポーツをする」.

Complete sentence: 朝、近所のパン屋の前を通ると、パンの焼けるいいにおいがする。

default.q.n3-4-q51-51.explanation:
Complete dialogue: 森田「西山さん、新しいアルバイトはどうですか。」 西山「始めたばかりなので覚えなければいけないことが多くて大変ですが、楽しいです。」

default.q.n3-4-q51-51.why.1: (b) 「覚えなければいけない」comes second and is a relative clause modifying the noun 「こと」(things that must be memorized).

default.q.n3-4-q52-52.explanation:
Complete sentence: 初めて登山をしたとき、山の上からの景色を見て、「なんてきれいな眺めなんだろう」と感動した。

Complete dialogue: 田中「ねえ、知ってる? 営業課の山下さん、来月受付の林さんと結婚するんだって。」 石川「え、そうなんだ。知らなかった。」

default.q.n3-4-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 話しかけてくれました.
default.q.n3-4-q54-54.explanation:
Quoted sentence from the passage: 「私が行くと、林さんはいつも【19】。それで、私たちはだんだん仲がよくなりました。」
The subject of the clause is 「林さんは」(Mr./Ms. Hayashi), and the person receiving the action of initiating a conversation (話しかける) is the author (私). When someone does something kind or friendly for us, we use the structure 「〜てくれる / 〜てくれました」. Therefore, 「話しかけてくれました」 (Hayashi always spoke to me first) is correct both grammatically and in terms of the emotional flow, explaining why the two gradually became close in the following sentence.
default.q.n3-4-q54-54.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「〜ていました」 simply describes an action in progress in the past; it does not express Mr. Hayashi's active and enthusiastic attitude toward the author, which would explain why the two became closer.
default.q.n3-4-q54-54.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜てあげました」 is used when the speaker does something for another person; it is not used when another person (Uncle Hayashi) does something for the speaker (the author).
default.q.n3-4-q54-54.why.2: (c) Correct. 「〜てくれました」is used when another person (Mr. Hayashi) performs an action that benefits the speaker or shows friendliness toward the speaker (the author), fitting the structure 「林さんは（私に）〜てくれました」.
default.q.n3-4-q54-54.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜てもらいました」 requires the subject to be the recipient (「私は林さんに…」), whereas the subject of this clause is「林さんは」.
default.q.n3-4-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 4. それから.
default.q.n3-4-q55-55.explanation: The passage lists things the two people usually talk about when the café has few customers: different types of coffee, the difficulties of living in Japan, and advice from Dr. Hayashi. Next, the author adds another shared interest: movies (「映画の話もよくします」—"We also often talk about movies"). To connect and add another item to the same list, the most suitable conjunction is「それから」(in addition, besides that, and then).
default.q.n3-4-q55-55.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「確かに」 means “indeed” or “that is true,” and is used to confirm an obvious fact or show agreement; it is not used to introduce a new topic of conversation.
default.q.n3-4-q55-55.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「ところが」 means “however,” expressing contrast or an unexpected result contrary to expectations. It does not fit a flow that simply adds information.
default.q.n3-4-q55-55.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「例えば」 means "for example" and introduces an illustrative example of the preceding statement. Watching movies is not an example of Hayashi giving life advice.
default.q.n3-4-q55-55.why.3: (d) Correct. 「それから」means “in addition,” “besides,” or “and then,” connecting and adding a new idea or activity to the series of topics the two people usually share.
default.q.n3-4-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 2. のような.
default.q.n3-4-q56-56.explanation: Sentence meaning: "I never imagined that I could have a friend like Mr. Hayashi in Japan." The next sentence clearly explains this: 「こんなに年上の友達ができたのは初めてでしたが…」(It was the first time I had made a friend so much older than me, but...). The structure 「N1 のような N2」(an N2 like N1) is the standard structure for modifying the noun 「友達」, forming the phrase 「林さんのような友達」(a friend like Mr. Hayashi).
default.q.n3-4-q56-56.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「〜にも」means “also...”; inserting it would not create a grammatically appropriate modifier for the following noun 「友達」.
default.q.n3-4-q56-56.why.1: (b) Correct. The structure 「N1 + のような + N2」 means "N2 like N1"; here, 「林さんのような友達」 means "a friend like Mr. Hayashi," which fits the following phrase 「こんなに年上の友達」 (such an older friend).
default.q.n3-4-q56-56.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜にだけ」 means “only for/to...” and cannot directly modify the following noun 「友達」.
default.q.n3-4-q56-56.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜のほかに」 means "besides..."; using it here would mean "a friend besides Mr. Hayashi," which does not fit the passage's emphasis on becoming friends with one special person like him.
default.q.n3-4-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 会えて.
default.q.n3-4-q57-57.explanation: The pattern 「V-て + よかった / よかったです」 expresses happiness, relief, or satisfaction about something that happened or an action that was completed ("I'm glad / it was fortunate that..."). The verb 「会う」 (to meet) changes to the potential form 「会える」 (can meet), and then to the te-form 「会えて」. The entire sentence 「日本で林さんに会えてよかったです。」 means "I am very happy / fortunate that I was able to meet Mr. or Ms. Hayashi in Japan," bringing the meaningful passage to a close.
default.q.n3-4-q57-57.why.0: (a) Correct. The potential-form verb in the te-form, 「会えて」, combines with 「〜てよかった」 (it was good/lucky that...), forming 「会えてよかったです」 (I am glad I was able to meet Mr. Hayashi).
default.q.n3-4-q57-57.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「会うから」(because I will meet someone) expresses a reason and does not combine with「よかったです」to form an expression of satisfaction or gratitude about something that happened.
default.q.n3-4-q57-57.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「会えるのが」nominalizes the action, but it does not form the standard complete sentence pattern expressing satisfaction at the end, 「〜てよかったです」.
default.q.n3-4-q57-57.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「会っても」(even if I meet them) expresses a hypothetical concessive condition (“even if...”), which does not fit the context of expressing happiness or satisfaction.
default.q.n3-4-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Nomura wants to announce that whether the department-head meeting will be postponed will be communicated at 3:00 p.m. tomorrow.

default.q.n3-4-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 1: One must register both for participation and practice at the International Student Center by May 7, then arrive at the venue at 10:00 on the 29th.
