- Kanji meanings: 友達 (friend), 誘う (to invite), 夏休み (summer vacation), 海外旅行 (travel abroad), 家族 (family), 楽しみ (something to look forward to).
- Example: 秘密だから、彼としか話したことがありません。(It is a secret, so I have only talked about it with him.)
default.q.n3-6-q38-38.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「家族だけで」 means “the family alone does something,” and when combined with the negative 「行ったことがない」, it does not express “having only ever traveled with one’s family.”
default.q.n3-6-q38-38.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「だけが」 functions as a subject particle and is not suitable for modifying an action involving going somewhere with someone.
default.q.n3-6-q38-38.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜となら」 means “if it is with...,” which does not fit the context of recalling a past experience.
default.q.n3-6-q38-38.why.3: (d) Correct because 「家族と」 (with one's family) combined with 「〜しか...ない」 (only) forms 「家族としか行ったことがない」, meaning "I have only ever gone with my family" (I have never gone with anyone else).
default.q.n3-6-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (できれば).
default.q.n3-6-q39-39.explanation:
- Translation:
Staff member: 'How do you like this apartment? It takes about 15 minutes to walk from the station, but the room is spacious and very clean.'
Customer: 'Oh, the room looks nice, but it is a little far from the station. If possible, I would prefer somewhere a little closer……'
- Adverb: できれば / できたら: if possible, if it can be arranged (used to make a request or express a gentle preference).
- Kanji vocabulary: 店員 (shop or restaurant staff), 歩く (to walk), 部屋 (room), 遠い (far), 近い (near).
- Example: できれば、今週中にお返事をいただきたいです。(If possible, I would like to receive your reply by the end of this week.)
default.q.n3-6-q39-39.why.0: (a) Correct because 「できれば」 means “if possible” or “if you can,” and expresses a wish politely and gently.
default.q.n3-6-q39-39.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「別に」 means “nothing in particular” or “not especially” and is usually used with the negative 「別に〜ない」.
default.q.n3-6-q39-39.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「せっかく」means “with considerable effort” or “rarely having the opportunity”; it does not express a personal wish in this context.
default.q.n3-6-q39-39.why.3: (d) Incorrect because「確かに」means “indeed” or “that is true” and is used to affirm or agree with the preceding opinion.
default.q.n3-6-q40-40.explanation:
- Meaning: While I was out for a walk, it suddenly started raining, so I hurriedly ran into a nearby café.
- Grammar: V-ます stem + だす: to suddenly begin doing something or for something to suddenly occur (often used for natural phenomena or sudden actions).
- Kanji readings and meanings: 散歩中 (while out walking), 急 (sudden), 降る (to fall, as rain), 慌てる (to panic, hurry), 喫茶店 (café).
- Example: 赤ちゃんが急に泣きだした。(The baby suddenly burst into tears.)
default.q.n3-6-q40-40.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜だす」 does not combine with the dictionary form (V-る).
default.q.n3-6-q40-40.why.1: (b) Correct because the pattern 「V (ます-stem) + だす」describes an action or event that suddenly begins (「降りだす」: it suddenly starts raining).
default.q.n3-6-q40-40.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜だす」 does not combine with the te-form of a verb (V-て).
default.q.n3-6-q40-40.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「〜だす」 does not combine with the ta-form (V-た).
default.q.n3-6-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (呼ばれるまで).
default.q.n3-6-q41-41.explanation:
- **Translation**: Receptionist: "Please wait in front of the examination room until your name is called."
- **Grammar**:
  + Passive form (受身形): 呼ぶ → 呼ばれる (to be called).
  + V-る / V-ない + まで: until..., indicating the time limit up to which the following action continues.
- **Related vocabulary**: 受付 (うけつけ - reception desk), 名前 (なまえ - name), 診察室 (しんさつしつ - examination room), 待つ (まつ - to wait).
- **Example**: バスが来るまで、ここで待っていましょう。(Let's wait here until the bus comes.)
default.q.n3-6-q41-41.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「呼ぶ」 is active (“someone calls”), whereas the subject 「お名前が」 requires the passive form. Also, 「〜と」 does not go with a following request or command.
default.q.n3-6-q41-41.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the verb 「呼ぶ」 has not been changed to the passive form 「呼ばれる」, which fits with the particle 「が」 and the noun 「お名前」.
default.q.n3-6-q41-41.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the conjunction 「〜と」cannot be used when the following clause expresses volition, a request, or a command such as 「お待ちください」.
default.q.n3-6-q41-41.why.3: (d) Correct because「お名前が呼ばれる」is the passive form (your name is called), which combines with「〜まで」(until...) to mean “please wait until your name is called.”
default.q.n3-6-q42-42.explanation:
- Meaning: This morning, my train was delayed, so I ended up being late for work.
- Grammar: V/A/N (plain form; N + の; na-adjective + な) + せいで: because of/due to... (indicates a cause that produces a negative result, often conveying blame or regret).
- Vocabulary: 今朝 (this morning), 電車 (train), 遅れる (to be late), 会社 (company/workplace), 遅刻 (being late).
- Example: 目覚まし時計が鳴らなかったせいで、寝坊してしまった。(Because my alarm clock did not ring, I overslept.)
default.q.n3-6-q42-42.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜間に」 means “while / during,” and is not used to indicate a cause leading to a negative result.
default.q.n3-6-q42-42.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「〜点で」 means “in terms of...” or “from the standpoint of...” and is used when evaluating or analyzing a specific aspect.
default.q.n3-6-q42-42.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜たびに」means “every time” or “whenever,” so it does not fit the cause of a single event that happened this morning.
default.q.n3-6-q42-42.why.3: (d) Correct because「V / A / N + の + せいで」means “because of” or “due to” and indicates a cause leading to a bad or undesirable result (in this case, being late for work).
default.q.n3-6-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (読んでおかなければならない).
default.q.n3-6-q43-43.explanation:
- Meaning: I was supposed to read up to page 30 of the textbook before class tomorrow, but I still have not read any of it.
- Grammar:
  + V-ておく: do something in advance to prepare for a future time or purpose.
  + V-なければならない: must do something.
  + Combined: V-ておかなければならない: must do something in advance / must have something prepared.
- Kanji readings: 明日 (あした - tomorrow), 授業 (じゅぎょう - class), 全然 (ぜんぜん - not at all), 読む (よむ - read).
- Example: 旅行に行く前に、ホテルの予約をしておかなければならない。(I must reserve a hotel before going on a trip.)
default.q.n3-6-q43-43.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜てはいけない」means prohibition (“must not do...”); this is the exact opposite of needing to prepare the lesson beforehand.
default.q.n3-6-q43-43.why.1: (b) Correct because the combined structure 「V-ておく」(do something in advance / prepare beforehand) and 「〜なければならない」(must do) forms 「〜読んでおかなければならない」(must read in advance), which fits the context of preparing for class.
default.q.n3-6-q43-43.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜ことにしてはいけない」means “must not decide to do ...,” which does not fit the meaning.
default.q.n3-6-q43-43.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「〜ことにしなければならない」awkwardly means “must decide to read...,” and it is unnatural and lacks the preparatory meaning expressed by 「〜ておく」.
default.q.n3-6-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (眠れなかつた).
default.q.n3-6-q44-44.explanation:
- Meaning: "Last night, I was so distracted by the howling wind that I could not sleep at all."
- Grammar:
  + 少しも / ぜんぜん / ちっとも + V-ない: Not ... even a little (emphasizing complete negation).
  + Potential form: 眠る (to sleep) → 眠れる (can sleep) → 眠れない / 眠れなかった (cannot / could not sleep).
- Related kanji readings: 昨日の夜 (— last night), 風 (— wind), 音 (— sound), 気になる (— to be concerned or worried), 眠る (— to sleep).
- Example: 心配事があって、昨夜は少しも眠れなかった。(I had something to worry about, so I could not sleep at all last night.)
default.q.n3-6-q44-44.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜たかった」 is the affirmative desiderative form (“wanted to sleep”), so it cannot be used with the negative adverb 「少しも」.
default.q.n3-6-q44-44.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「〜ようとした」 means “intended to” or “tried to sleep,” and it cannot be combined with 「少しも」 in an affirmative sentence.
default.q.n3-6-q44-44.why.2: (c) Correct because 「少しも + V-ない」means 'not even a little,' and with the past negative potential form 「眠れなかった」it expresses being unable to sleep at all.
default.q.n3-6-q44-44.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「〜なくなった」 means “came to no longer sleep,” describing a change in habit or state. It does not describe being unable to sleep because of last night's wind.
default.q.n3-6-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (開くことだ).
default.q.n3-6-q45-45.explanation:
- Meaning: My dream is to open my own pastry shop someday.
- Grammar: 私の夢 / 目標 / 趣味 は + V-る + ことだ: My dream / goal / hobby is to...
- Kanji readings: 私 ( - I, me), 夢 ( - dream), 自分 ( - oneself, one's own), 開く ( - open a shop).
- Example: 私の目標は、今年中にN3に合格することです。(My goal is to pass N3 this year.)
default.q.n3-6-q45-45.why.0: (a) Incorrect because when the subject is 「私の夢は」(My dream is...), the predicate should end with a noun or the nominalized structure 「〜ことだ」, not 「〜と思う」.
default.q.n3-6-q45-45.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「〜たいと思う」 (“to think that one wants to...”) is used to express the speaker’s own thoughts or desires and does not fit the structure with the subject 「私の夢は...」.
default.q.n3-6-q45-45.why.2: (c) Correct because the standard pattern for defining a dream or goal is 「私の夢は + V-る + ことだ」(My dream is to open my own pastry shop).
default.q.n3-6-q45-45.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the dictionary form (V-る) is used before nominalized 「ことだ」, not the desiderative form 「〜たいことだ」in this structure.
default.q.n3-6-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (やみそうにない).
default.q.n3-6-q46-46.explanation:
- Meaning:
Wife: "It doesn't look like the rain is going to stop anytime soon, does it? Why don't we just not go out today?"
Husband: "Yeah, you're right."
- Grammar: 全然 + V-ます (ます removed) + そうにない / そうもない: there is no sign that ... will happen at all / is highly unlikely to ... (a prediction based on the observable situation).
- Kanji readings and meanings: 妻 (wife), 雨 (rain), 全然 (completely, not at all), 出かける (to go out), 夫 (husband).
- Example: 仕事が山ほどあって、今日は早く帰れそうにない。(I have a mountain of work, so it looks like I won't be able to go home early today.)
default.q.n3-6-q46-46.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜はずがない」 means “cannot possibly...”; combined with 「やまない」, it creates a double negative meaning “it is certain to stop,” which contradicts the suggestion to stay home.
default.q.n3-6-q46-46.why.1: (b) Correct because 「全然 + V (ます-stem) + そうにない」 means “does not look at all as if ...,” describing that there is no sign that the rain will stop soon.
default.q.n3-6-q46-46.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜に違いない」 means “it must certainly clear up,” which is contrary to the decision not to go outside anymore.
default.q.n3-6-q46-46.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「〜てもしかたない」 means “even if it clears up, it will be of no use / there is nothing that can be done,” which does not fit the meaning.
default.q.n3-6-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (できるらしい).
default.q.n3-6-q47-47.explanation:
- Meaning:
A: “I heard from a senior that a new café is apparently going to open in front of the station soon.”
B: “Really? That’s something to look forward to.”
- Grammar: Plain form + らしい: “I hear that ...,” “apparently ...” Used to relay information heard from someone else or a well-founded inference.
- Example: 天気予報によると、明日は雨が降るらしい。(According to the weather forecast, it is apparently going to rain tomorrow.)
default.q.n3-6-q47-47.why.0: (a) The preceding phrase 「先輩に聞いたんだけど」 (“I heard from a senior that ...”) indicates received information, so it naturally takes 「〜らしい」 (“I hear that / apparently”) to pass on what was heard.
default.q.n3-6-q47-47.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「〜てほしい」 expresses a desire for someone else to do something for oneself; it is not used to report information one has heard.
default.q.n3-6-q47-47.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜ことがある」means “there are times when…” or “sometimes,” and is not used to express something that is about to happen in the near future.
default.q.n3-6-q47-47.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「〜たほうがいい」 is a sentence pattern used to give advice (“you should do …”), which does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-6-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (してもらえますか).
default.q.n3-6-q48-48.explanation:
- Translation:
Barber: “Is this length all right?”
Customer: “Could you cut it a little shorter, please?”
Barber: “Yes, I understand.”
- Grammar:
  + i-adjective: A-い → A-くする (to make something become...; a transitive construction acting on an object).
  + V-てもらえますか / V-ていただけますか: “Could you please do V for me?” (a polite request).
- Vocabulary: 長さ (length), 短い (short).
- Example: すみません、写真を撮ってもらえますか。(Excuse me, could you take a picture for me?)
default.q.n3-6-q48-48.why.0: (a) Incorrect because「〜てあげますか」is used when the speaker does something for the other person, not when asking the other person to serve the speaker.
default.q.n3-6-q48-48.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「なる」 is an intransitive verb, and 「〜てあげる」 means doing something for someone else; neither expresses asking a hairdresser to cut one's hair.
default.q.n3-6-q48-48.why.2: (c) Correct because 「短くする」 (to cut/make shorter) combines with the polite request pattern 「〜てもらえますか」 (could you do this for me?) to appropriately ask the hairdresser to make it shorter.
default.q.n3-6-q48-48.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「短くなる」 is an intransitive verb (become shorter), so it cannot combine with 「〜てもらう」 when requesting an action performed by a worker.
default.q.n3-6-q49-49.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 2 → 4 → 1. The ★ position is answer choice 4 (目の疲れ).
default.q.n3-6-q49-49.explanation:
Complete sentence: パソコンや携帯電話の見すぎによる目の疲れが原因で、頭が痛くなることもあるそうだ。
Meaning: Apparently, eye strain caused by looking at computers and mobile phones too much can also cause headaches.
default.q.n3-6-q49-49.why.0: (a) [1. が]: It follows the noun「目の疲れ」to form「目の疲れが原因で」(with eye strain as the cause / due to eye strain), appearing in the fourth position.
default.q.n3-6-q49-49.why.1: (b) [2. による]: It modifies the noun 「目の疲れ」 that follows in the structure 「N1 + による + N2」 (N2 caused by N1), forming 「見すぎによる目の疲れ」 and occupying the second position.
default.q.n3-6-q49-49.why.2: (c) [3. 見すぎ]: Combined with the preceding noun phrase 「パソコンや携帯電話の」, it forms 「パソコンや携帯電話の見すぎ」 (looking at computers and mobile phones too much) and occupies the first position.
default.q.n3-6-q49-49.why.3: (d) [4. 目の疲れ]: The noun is modified by「見すぎによる」and followed by the particle「が」, placing it at ★ (position 3).
default.q.n3-6-q50-50.verdict: Correct order: 2 → 3 → 1 → 4. Choice 1 is placed at ★ (上手に弾けない).
default.q.n3-6-q50-50.explanation:
Complete passage: 私は子供の時、ピアノを習っていたが、３年でやめてしまった。何回練習してもなかなか上手に弾けない曲があって、いやになってしまったのだ。
Meaning: When I was a child, I took piano lessons, but I quit after three years. There were some pieces I could not play well no matter how many times I practiced, and I eventually became discouraged.
default.q.n3-6-q50-50.why.0: (a) [1. 上手に弾けない]: It follows the adverb 「なかなか」 to express “cannot play well no matter how hard one tries,” and modifies the noun 「曲」 that follows. It occupies the ★ position (the third position).
default.q.n3-6-q50-50.why.1: (b) [2. 練習しても]: It follows「何回」to form「何回～ても」(no matter how many times...), occupying the first position.
default.q.n3-6-q50-50.why.2: (c) [3. なかなか]: This adverb commonly occurs with the negative form 「～ない」to express 'cannot... despite trying' or 'it takes a long time to...'. It is in the second position, modifying 「上手に弾けない」.
default.q.n3-6-q50-50.why.3: (d) [4. 曲があって]: The noun 「曲」 is modified by the preceding phrase 「なかなか上手に弾けない」 and takes the 「～て」 form to connect to the following clause expressing the reason for becoming discouraged, occupying the fourth position.
default.q.n3-6-q51-51.verdict: Correct order: 4 → 2 → 1 → 3. The ★ position is answer choice 1 (失敗をしてしまった).
default.q.n3-6-q51-51.explanation:
Complete sentence: 失敗をすることは誰にでもある。大切なのはどうして失敗をしてしまったのか考えて、同じ失敗を繰り返さないようにすることだ。
Meaning: “Everyone makes mistakes. What matters is thinking about why you made the mistake and making sure not to repeat it.”
default.q.n3-6-q51-51.why.0: (a) [1. 失敗をしてしまった]: The verb follows the question word 「どうして」and comes directly before 「のか」to form the indirect question 「どうして失敗をしてしまったのか」(why one ended up failing). It is in position ★ (the third position).
default.q.n3-6-q51-51.why.1: (b) [2. どうして]: This question word means “why,” introduces an indirect interrogative clause with 「～のか」, and occupies position 2.
default.q.n3-6-q51-51.why.2: (c) [3. のか]: An interrogative particle used in the embedded question「～のか考えて」(think about why...), appearing in the fourth position before the verb「考えて」.
default.q.n3-6-q51-51.why.3: (d) [4. のは]: It follows the adjective 「大切な」 and nominalizes it to form the subject 「大切なのは」 (“what is important is ...”). This corresponds to the sentence-final structure 「～ことだ」 and belongs in position 1.
default.q.n3-6-q52-52.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 3 → 1. The ★ is in position 3 (とか).
default.q.n3-6-q52-52.explanation:
Complete dialogue: （教室で）
南「西川さんの誕生日に、何かプレゼントをあげない？」
森「いいね。スポーツが好きだと言っていたからタオルとかいいんじゃない？」
Meaning: (In the classroom)
Minami: “How about giving Nishikawa some kind of present for their birthday?”
Mori: “Sounds good. They said they like sports, so wouldn't something like a sports towel be suitable?”
default.q.n3-6-q52-52.why.0: (a) [1. いいんじゃない]: This pattern is used to offer a suggestion or proposal, 「～いいんじゃない？」 (“Wouldn’t ... be a good idea?”), and appears in the fourth position before the question mark.
default.q.n3-6-q52-52.why.1: (b) [2. から]: It comes immediately after the clause 「スポーツが好きだと言っていた」to indicate the reason (because he said he liked sports...), in position 1.
default.q.n3-6-q52-52.why.2: (c) [3. とか]: This particle follows the noun 「タオル」to give a representative example, 「タオルとか」(such as towels), and occupies the ★ position (third position).
default.q.n3-6-q52-52.why.3: (d) [4. タオル]: This noun suggests a gift, comes after「から」and directly before the listing particle「とか」, occupying the second position.
default.q.n3-6-q53-53.verdict: Correct order: 1 → 3 → 4 → 2. Choice 4 is placed at ★ (山下花子先生に).
default.q.n3-6-q53-53.explanation:
Complete sentence: （講演会で）
司会者「本日は、鳥の専門家でいらっしゃる山下花子先生に都会で見ることができる様々な鳥について、お話をしていただきます。」
Meaning: (At a lecture)
MC: 'Today, we will hear from Ms. Hanako Yamashita, an expert on birds, about the various birds that can be seen in urban areas.'
default.q.n3-6-q53-53.why.0: (a) [1. 専門家で]: Following 「鳥の」, it forms 「鳥の専門家で」 (“being an expert on birds”) and uses the connective form 「で」 to link to the honorific 「いらっしゃる」, so it occupies position 1.
default.q.n3-6-q53-53.why.1: (b) [2. 都会で]: This location phrase comes immediately before 「見ることができる」 to form the modifying clause 「都会で見ることができる様々な鳥」 (various birds that can be seen in the city), occupying the fourth position.
default.q.n3-6-q53-53.why.2: (c) [3. いらっしゃる]: The honorific form of「である」, combined with「専門家で」to form the attributive phrase「専門家でいらっしゃる」modifying the noun「山下花子先生」, in the second position.
default.q.n3-6-q53-53.why.3: (d) [4. 山下花子先生に]: A noun referring to a person is modified by the honorific phrase before it, and the particle 「に」 marks the person who performs the action in the pattern 「～に...お話をしていただきます」 (“have someone give a talk/share something”), so it is in position ★ (the third position).
default.q.n3-6-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 1. でも.
default.q.n3-6-q54-54.explanation: Paragraph 1 ends with the author sharing that, although the work was sometimes difficult, everyone’s help enabled them to “continue working” (続けることができました). In paragraph 2, the author shifts to saying that “studies became busy from this semester, so I quit my part-time job last month” (今学期から勉強が忙しくなって、先月アルバイトを辞めました). This is a contrast between “continuing to work” and “having to quit work,” so the most appropriate conjunction at the beginning of the sentence is 「でも」 (“but” or “however”).
default.q.n3-6-q54-54.why.0: (a) 「でも」 (but, however): It is appropriate because it indicates a contrast between continuing to work because everyone helped in the previous passage and having to take time off because of studying in this passage.
default.q.n3-6-q54-54.why.1: (b) 「だから」(therefore, so) expresses a straightforward cause-and-effect relationship. It is inappropriate because taking time off work is not a result of being helped by everyone.
default.q.n3-6-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「すると」(then, immediately afterward): Indicates that an action follows immediately after another action or a new discovery. It is not used to connect two contrasting clauses when changing the direction of a passage.
default.q.n3-6-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「そのうえ」 (moreover, in addition): Used to add information in the same direction, so it does not fit a context involving a contrastive transition.
default.q.n3-6-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 書かれていた.
default.q.n3-6-q55-55.explanation: Earlier, the sentence says: “The store manager told me that all of the coworkers at the shop had written messages” (店長は、店の仲間全員がメッセージを書いたと教えてくれました). When the author looks at the card and describes its contents—“What was written on the card was many words of thanks and encouragement” (カードに書かれていたのは、たくさんの感謝の言葉や応援の言葉でした)—the past progressive passive form of 書く, 「書かれていた」, is both objective and appropriate for expressing the state in which the written messages remained on the card.
default.q.n3-6-q55-55.why.0: (a) 「書いておいた」 (“had written it in advance”): The 〜ておく form describes an action prepared in advance by the subject, so it is inappropriate for describing the content of the card from the recipient’s perspective.
default.q.n3-6-q55-55.why.1: (b) 「書きたかった」 (wanted to write): This expresses the speaker’s own desire in the past, so it does not fit because this is a message written by the author’s colleagues.
default.q.n3-6-q55-55.why.2: (c) 「書かれていた」(was written/recorded): The passive form combined with the past progressive (〜ていた) describes the state of the content being written on the card, so it is completely accurate.
default.q.n3-6-q55-55.why.3: (d) 「書いてほしかった」 (“I wanted [someone] to write it for me”): Expresses a desire for another person to do something for the speaker. It does not fit the context, in which the author is reading messages already written on a card.
default.q.n3-6-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 大学.
default.q.n3-6-q56-56.explanation: The author is an international student (留学生). In paragraph 1, the author says, 'I worked part-time at a restaurant near the university' (大学の近くのレストランでアルバイトをしていました). In paragraph 2, the author quit the job to focus on studying because school became busy (今学期から勉強が忙しくなって). Paragraph 3 describes the author hanging the card in their room and looking at it every day before going to university (大学に行く前に必ず見ています) for motivation. Therefore, directly inserting the noun 「大学」 is the most accurate and natural choice.
default.q.n3-6-q56-56.why.0: (a) 「そこ」(that place): This demonstrative pronoun is unnatural here because no specific location was mentioned in the preceding sentence to serve as its referent.
default.q.n3-6-q56-56.why.1: (b) 「大学」 (university): This noun refers to the place where the author studies every day. 「大学に行く前に」 (“before going to university”) naturally and accurately describes a daily routine.
default.q.n3-6-q56-56.why.2: (c) 「その大学」 (that university): 「その」 refers to a specific university previously mentioned outside the immediate context; it is unnatural when talking about attending one's own university every day.
default.q.n3-6-q56-56.why.3: (d) 「そういうところ」 (places like that): a general expression referring to a type of place, so it is completely unsuitable for describing a daily school-going habit.
default.q.n3-6-q57-57.verdict: The provided answer is 2; however, the grammatically most accurate answer with the structure「どんなに〜ても」must be 4. 頑張ることができそうです.
default.q.n3-6-q57-57.explanation: The grammar pattern 「どんなに + [て-form] も」 means “no matter how...” or “however...”. The following clause often expresses the speaker’s ability, determination, or positive expectation. When the author looks at the card and feels encouraged (カードを見ると、元気が出ます), they want to say: “No matter how difficult studying becomes, I feel that I can keep trying” (どんなに勉強が大変になっても、頑張ることができそうです). Choice 2 ends with 「〜からです」 (because...), which gives a reason and therefore cannot follow the concessive clause 「どんなに〜ても」.
default.q.n3-6-q57-57.why.0: (a) 「頑張っているのです」: The present progressive combined with 「〜のです」 explains a present fact, so it is incompatible with the future concessive hypothetical structure 「どんなに〜ても」 (“no matter how …”).
default.q.n3-6-q57-57.why.1: (b) 「頑張ることができるからです」: The ending 「〜からです」explains the reason for the preceding sentence; it does not form an appropriate grammar structure after the concessive clause 「どんなに〜ても」.
default.q.n3-6-q57-57.why.2: (c) 「頑張っているみたいです」 expresses an inference based on observing a state currently in progress. It is not suitable for expressing the speaker's attitude or ability in response to a difficult future supposition.
default.q.n3-6-q57-57.why.3: (d) 「頑張ることができそうです」: Used with 「どんなに〜ても」, this means “no matter how difficult studying is, I feel that I can still do my best.” It expresses confidence and determination after seeing the encouraging card.
default.q.n3-6-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Guests can rent their preferred yukata and obi from the hotel at a specially discounted rate.
default.q.n3-6-q58-58.explanation:
Summary:
This is a flyer from Iwanaka Hotel for guests staying on August 11 and 12 about the Iwanakamura Summer Festival at Iwanaka Park. The hotel provides a shuttle bus between the hotel and the festival venue, which takes about 5 minutes. In particular, the hotel offers yukata and obi rentals in the style of the guest's choice at a special price of 2,000 yen per day, with free dressing assistance for guests who do not know how to put them on. In addition, guests wearing a yukata receive one free drink at any stall inside the festival area.

Translation of the question:
Which of the following is true about the service that guests staying at Iwanaka Hotel on the day of the summer festival can receive from the hotel?

Translation of the choices:
1. If they wear a yukata, they can use the hotel bus to go to the summer festival venue.
2. They can have one free drink at the hotel restaurant.
3. They can rent a yukata and the obi of their choice from the hotel at a special price.
4. If they pay an additional 2,000 yen on top of the yukata and obi rental fee, a hotel staff member will help them put them on.
default.q.n3-6-q58-58.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the shuttle bus between the hotel and the festival venue is a service for all hotel guests; the passage never says that passengers must wear yukata.
default.q.n3-6-q58-58.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the free-drink offer for wearing a yukata is available at any shop inside the festival venue (「会場内のどの店でも」), not at the hotel restaurant.
default.q.n3-6-q58-58.why.2: (c) Correct because it is quoted directly from the text: 「ホテルでは、お好きな浴衣と帯を特別料金【1 日 2,000円】でお貸しします(浴衣の着方がわからない方は、お手伝いいたします)。」 (At the hotel, we rent the yukata and obi of your choice at the special rate of 【2,000 yen per day】).
default.q.n3-6-q58-58.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 2,000 yen per day is the price for renting the complete yukata and obi set. Assistance with putting on the yukata is an included service for people who do not know how to wear it, not an additional 2,000-yen charge.
default.q.n3-6-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The author’s long-forgotten dream of becoming a teacher has become a reality.
default.q.n3-6-q59-59.explanation:
**Summary:**
The author has just returned home from studying in the United States and has accepted a position teaching mathematics at a university beginning in April. While cleaning the room in the old family home before starting work, the author happened to find an elementary-school essay titled “My Dream,” in which the author had written about wanting to become a teacher. Although the author had completely forgotten about it, realizing that this childhood dream had now come true made the author determined to do their very best.

**Question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** The author says 「頑張ろう」(I will do my best). Why did the author think this?
- 1. Because the forgotten dream of studying in the United States had come true.
- 2. Because the forgotten dream of becoming a teacher had come true.
- 3. Because the author had successfully studied in the United States, just as they had always wished since childhood.
- 4. Because the author had become a teacher, just as they had always wished since childhood.
default.q.n3-6-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the dream written about in the childhood essay was to become a teacher (先生になりたい), not to study abroad in the United States (アメリカに留学したい).
default.q.n3-6-q59-59.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states: 「そこには、先生になりたいと書いてあった。そんなことはすっかり忘れていたが、...子供のころの夢が本当になったのだし、頑張ろうと思う。」 (It said there that I wanted to become a teacher. I had completely forgotten about that, but... since my childhood dream had come true, I decided to do my best.)
default.q.n3-6-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage states that the author had completely forgotten this dream (そんなことはすっかり忘れていた), not that they had always wanted it since childhood (ずっと行きたいと思い続けていた). In addition, the dream in the passage is to become a teacher, not to study abroad.
default.q.n3-6-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the phrase “something I had always wanted since childhood” (ずっと...思い続けていた) directly contradicts the sentence in the passage: 「そんなことはすっかり忘れていた」 (“I had completely forgotten about it”).
default.q.n3-6-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 1: ２６日までに学校で招待券を受け取っておく。
default.q.n3-6-q60-60.explanation:
Main points:
An email from Kawano Japanese Language School announces complimentary tickets to a baseball game on Saturday, February 27 (doors open at 1:00 p.m.; the game starts at 2:00 p.m.).
- Students who have not received a ticket must pick one up at the office by Friday the 26th.
- Students who are not confident about going alone can go with Nakagawa-sensei: they should meet at the school at noon on the 27th and can receive their tickets from the teacher that day.
- Students going on their own do not need to meet at the school or the baseball stadium, which means they must pick up their tickets at the school office by the 26th.

Translation of the question:
According to this email, what must a student who plans to go to the baseball stadium alone do?

Translation of the answer choices:
1. Pick up the complimentary ticket at school before the 26th.
2. Pick up the complimentary ticket at school before the 26th, then meet in front of the baseball stadium at 1:00 p.m. on the day of the game.
3. Go to school at noon on the day of the game and receive the complimentary ticket from Nakagawa-sensei.
4. Go to the baseball stadium at 1:00 p.m. on the day of the game and receive the complimentary ticket from Nakagawa-sensei.
default.q.n3-6-q60-60.why.0: (a) Correct. The general rule states: 「まだ招待券を受け取っていない人は、２６日(金)までに事務室に取りに来てください」. For those going independently, it says: 「自分で行く人は、学校にも野球場にも集合する必要はありません」. Therefore, students who are not going with Mr. Nakagawa on the game day must come to school to collect their tickets before the 26th.
default.q.n3-6-q60-60.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage states 「自分で行く人は、学校にも野球場にも集合する必要はありません」 (people who go on their own do not need to assemble either at the school or at the baseball stadium), so there is no requirement to gather at the stadium at 1 p.m.
default.q.n3-6-q60-60.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Meeting at the school at noon to receive tickets from Mr. Nakagawa is intended only for those who want to go with him (「一緒に行きたい人は、12 時に学校に集合してください。その場合、招待券は当日、中川先生からもらってもいいです」); it does not apply to people going on their own.
default.q.n3-6-q60-60.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage does not mention that people going on their own will receive tickets from Mr. Nakagawa at the baseball field at 1:00 p.m.; nor do they need to gather together.
default.q.n3-6-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The experiment demonstrated that some fish can recognize that the image reflected in a mirror is themselves.
default.q.n3-6-q61-61.explanation:
**Main idea of the passage:** The passage introduces an interesting experiment: after a fish had a mark put on its face and was shown a mirror, it rubbed itself against sand to remove the mark and then looked at the mirror again to check. This experiment shows that, in addition to intelligent animals such as monkeys, some fish can recognize that the image in the mirror is themselves.

**Question and choices:**
- **Question:** What did this experiment reveal about fish?
- **1.** Some fish look in a mirror and then put a mark on themselves.
- **2.** Some fish can recognize that the fish in the mirror is themselves.
- **3.** Some fish immediately want to swim toward a mirror when they realize it is a mirror.
- **4.** Some fish try to clean a mirror when they see that it is dirty.
default.q.n3-6-q61-61.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the researcher smeared dirt on the fish’s face, and the fish tried to rub the dirt off (汚れを落とす); the fish did not smear itself.
default.q.n3-6-q61-61.why.1: (b) Correct because the text clearly states: 「鏡の中にいる自分を見て、それが自分自身だとわかるのは、サルなどの頭のいい動物だけだと考えられていた。しかし、魚にもそれができるものがいるのだと、この研究者は言っている。」 (People had believed that only intelligent animals such as apes could look at themselves in a mirror and recognize that it was themselves, but the researcher says that some fish can do this as well.)
default.q.n3-6-q61-61.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage contains no information saying that the fish immediately swam in front of the mirror whenever it noticed its reflection.
default.q.n3-6-q61-61.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the fish cleans the dirt stuck to its own face (自分の顔についた汚れを落とし), not a dirty mirror.
default.q.n3-6-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The author decided to stop driving because they themselves felt anxious and uncertain about whether they could continue driving safely.
default.q.n3-6-q62-62.explanation:
• Main idea: The 70-year-old author had been confident in their driving ability. However, after hearing that a friend of the same age had crashed into a garage wall, the author began to worry about whether it was safe to continue driving at that age, so they decided to stop driving and sell their car.

• Translation of the question and answer choices:
- *Question*: The passage says「①連転をやめることにして」(decided to stop driving). Why did the author make that decision?
- *Choice 1*: Although confident in their driving, they had crashed into a wall themselves.
- *Choice 2*: Because they also began to worry about whether they could continue driving safely. (CORRECT)
- *Choice 3*: Because they had always felt insecure about their driving ability since they were young.
- *Choice 4*: Because their wife advised them to stop driving.
default.q.n3-6-q62-62.why.0: (a) Incorrect: The passage says that the person who crashed into the garage wall was the author’s 70-year-old friend (「私と同じ 70 歳の友人が、自宅の車庫の壁に車をぶつけてしまった」), not the author.
default.q.n3-6-q62-62.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states: 「私は運転に自信があったが、その話を聞いて、安全に運転が続けられるか不安になってきた。それで、①連転をやめることにして、車を売った。」 The narrator had been confident in their driving, but after hearing the story, became worried about whether they could continue driving safely and therefore decided to stop driving.
default.q.n3-6-q62-62.why.2: (c) Incorrect: The author was originally very confident in their driving ability (「私は運転に自信があった」), rather than being anxious since childhood.
default.q.n3-6-q62-62.why.3: (d) Incorrect: The passage does not say that the author's wife advised him to give up driving; the author himself felt uneasy after hearing his friend's story.
default.q.n3-6-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The problem the author encountered was that walking uphill home while carrying groceries from the supermarket was not as easy as initially expected.
default.q.n3-6-q63-63.explanation:
• **Main point**: The author's house is on a hill, so after selling the car, the author has to walk down to the supermarket below the slope to shop. At first, the author thought walking would be a convenient way to exercise, but carrying the shopping home uphill turned out to be much harder than expected.

• **Question and answer choices**:
- *Question*: What does 「②困ったこと」 (the troublesome problem) refer to?
- *Choice 1*: Having to go shopping at the supermarket with their spouse every day.
- *Choice 2*: Having to shop at a supermarket farther away than before.
- *Choice 3*: Lacking exercise because shopping no longer provides an opportunity to exercise.
- *Choice 4*: Carrying the shopping home from the supermarket is not as easy as expected. (CORRECT)
default.q.n3-6-q63-63.why.0: (a) Incorrect: Going shopping at the supermarket every day with his wife is a long-standing habit that has continued as before (「毎日の買い物はこれまでと変わらず、二人で坂の下のスーパーまで行く」), not a new problem that arose after giving up the car.
default.q.n3-6-q63-63.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The couple still goes to the supermarket at the foot of the hill as before; there is no information saying they have to go to a more distant supermarket.
default.q.n3-6-q63-63.why.2: (c) Incorrect. At first, the author thought that walking would count as exercise (「初めは、運動にもなるし、スーパーまで歩けばいいと考えていた」), and did not say that they lacked exercise or were unable to exercise.
default.q.n3-6-q63-63.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage states: 「初めは、運動にもなるし、スーパーまで歩けばいいと考えていた。しかし、車を使わず荷物を持って板を上がって帰るのは、思ったより大変だったのだ。」 (At first, I thought walking to the supermarket would also count as exercise. However, carrying the groceries uphill without using a car was much harder than expected—it was not as easy as anticipated.)
default.q.n3-6-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The author is very satisfied with the delivered product and believes that, from now on, if this delivery service is used, there will be no need to move house again.
default.q.n3-6-q64-64.explanation:
• **Main point**: While the author and his wife were considering moving because carrying groceries up the hill was so difficult, they discovered the supermarket’s online ordering service with home delivery. After trying it with meat and vegetables and finding the deliveries high quality and convenient, the author realized that they would no longer need to move if they used the service from then on.

• **Question and answer choices**:
- *Question*: After using the supermarket’s service, what does “I” now think about moving?
- *Choice 1*: Since carrying purchased items home is difficult, perhaps we should move closer to the supermarket.
- *Choice 2*: Since delivery costs money, perhaps we should move closer to the supermarket.
- *Choice 3*: I am very satisfied with the delivered goods, so if we use this service from now on, we will no longer need to move. (CORRECT)
- *Choice 4*: Some of the delivered items were unsatisfactory, but if we use this service, perhaps we still will not need to move.
default.q.n3-6-q64-64.why.0: (a) Incorrect: Since home delivery solved the problem of carrying the purchases, the author no longer considered moving closer to the supermarket (「いい方法が見つかった。これで引っ越しをしなくてもよさそうである」).
default.q.n3-6-q64-64.why.1: (b) Incorrect because although delivery costs money, the author values convenience more (「配達料はかかるが、便利さのほうが重要だ」), and this solution means the author does not need to move.
default.q.n3-6-q64-64.why.2: (c) Correct: The text says, 「翌日届いた品物はどれもとても良かった。... いい方法が見つかった。これで引っ越しをしなくてもよさそうである。」 (Every item delivered the next day was very good... A good solution had been found. It seemed that moving house would no longer be necessary).
default.q.n3-6-q64-64.why.3: (d) Incorrect: The passage clearly states that all the delivered items were very good (「翌日届いた品物はどれもとても良かった」), so there was no item the person was dissatisfied with.
default.q.n3-6-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Both bringing the child along and having only the parents go (and leaving the child behind) are difficult.
default.q.n3-6-q65-65.explanation:
- Summary and evidence: The author explains why many people who enjoy music, films, or painting sometimes have to refrain from going when their children are young: on the one hand, they cannot bring the children because they may make noise, and on the other hand, it is not easy to have someone else look after them (子供は、騒いでしまう心配があるので連れて行けないし、人に預けることも簡単ではないからです).

default.q.n3-6-q65-65.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage never mentions a lack of places near one’s home to enjoy art or movies.
default.q.n3-6-q65-65.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the passage does not say that the reason was having no time because of taking care of the children.
default.q.n3-6-q65-65.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because paragraph 1 clearly explains: 「子供は、騒いでしまう心配があるので連れて行けないし、人に預けることも簡単ではないからです。」 (They cannot bring their children because they are worried the children may make noise, and it is not easy to leave them with someone else.) default.q.n3-6-q65-65.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage does not mention children's costs or ticket prices at all.
default.q.n3-6-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The movie theater adjusts the brightness and volume so that children will not be frightened or startled.
default.q.n3-6-q66-66.explanation:
- Summary and supporting evidence: To allow parents and children to enjoy entertainment together, some movie theaters have introduced practical measures: keeping the screening room slightly lit throughout the movie so children will not become frightened and cry in the dark, and keeping the volume from becoming too loud so children will not be startled (ある映画館では、映面の間も会場を少し明るくしておくそうです。暗いと、怖がって泣いてしまう子供がいるからです。大きな音を聞くと、びつくりする子供もいるので、音も大きすぎないようにしてあります).
- **Question translation**: The passage says that there are “initiatives that allow parents and children to enjoy themselves together.” What are some movie theaters doing?

  1. Preparing special seats where parents and children can talk while watching the movie.
  2. Increasing the movie's volume so the noise made by children will not be noticed.
  3. Choosing movies that both adults and children will enjoy watching.
  4. Adjusting the lighting and volume so that children will not become frightened or startled.
default.q.n3-6-q66-66.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the article does not mention preparing special seats for watching a movie while talking.
default.q.n3-6-q66-66.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the movie theater adjusted the sound so that it would not be too loud (音も大きすぎないようにしてあります), which is the exact opposite of turning the movie volume up.
default.q.n3-6-q66-66.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the passage does not mention selecting film content for both adults and children.
default.q.n3-6-q66-66.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because the text clearly states: 「ある映画館では、映面の間も会場を少し明るくしておくそうです。暗いと、怖がって泣いてしまう子供がいるからです。大きな音を聞くと、びつくりする子供もいるので、音も大きすぎないようにしてあります。」 (At one movie theater, the auditorium is kept slightly lit throughout the film because some children become frightened and cry when it is dark; the sound is also kept from being too loud because some children are startled by loud noises).
default.q.n3-6-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 1: In Japan, an environment where parents with young children can also enjoy music and films is gradually being developed.
default.q.n3-6-q67-67.explanation:
- Summary and supporting evidence: The passage as a whole explains that parents with young children once had to put up with being unable to go to movies or concerts, but recently in Japan more places have begun offering childcare or making adjustments to sound and lighting, allowing families with young children to go out and enjoy themselves with peace of mind (このように、最近は、小さな子供がいる人が安心して、出かけて楽しめる場所が増えてきています).

default.q.n3-6-q67-67.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage focuses on entertainment environments for people with young children, not on an increase in the number of children attending cultural or artistic events.
default.q.n3-6-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The company decided to make shoes for elderly people after receiving an inquiry or request for advice from the manager of a nursing home.
default.q.n3-6-q68-68.explanation:
Summary: The company initially produced only indoor slippers. However, after a nursing home administrator explained that elderly residents often fell at the facility and that their footwear might be the cause, the company decided to begin researching and producing safe shoes for older people.
- Question: Why did the shoe company decide to make shoes for older people?
- Choice:
1. Because it received many letters from older people asking for better shoes.
2. Because older people stopped wearing indoor slippers and switched to shoes.
3. Because a nursing home administrator consulted them about a footwear-related problem.
4. Because a survey of older people's walking habits revealed a problem with their shoes.
default.q.n3-6-q68-68.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the 20,000 thank-you letters received were a later result of the company’s successful product sales (1年に２万通も感謝の手紙がくる), not the reason the company began making shoes.
default.q.n3-6-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage does not mention elderly people stopping wearing slippers indoors and switching to shoes.
default.q.n3-6-q68-68.why.2: (c) Correct because the passage explicitly gives the reason: 「お年寄りのための介護施設(注)の経営者から、こんな相談をされた。『施設内でお年寄りがよく転ぶので 、困っているんです 。... 靴に問題がありそうなんです。』それて、お年寄りのための安全な靴を作ることにしたそうだ。」
default.q.n3-6-q68-68.why.3: (d) Incorrect because surveying the walking styles of 500 elderly people (社長はまず、約５００人のお年寄りの足を観察して、歩き方を調査することにした) was an action taken after deciding to make shoes, not the initial reason for making the decision.
default.q.n3-6-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 4: When reviewing the survey results, the company realized that as people age, the shape and size of their left and right feet can change differently.
default.q.n3-6-q69-69.explanation:
Summary: After shoes for older people initially failed to sell well, the company reviewed the survey results and discovered that many elderly people had weakness in one leg or changes in foot shape, causing the sizes of their left and right feet to differ.
- Question translation: The passage says that they decided to review the survey results. What, for example, did they come to understand?
- Answer choice:
1. Some elderly people are very prone to falling.
2. Some elderly people think that shoes are expensive.
3. As people grow older, some have fewer opportunities to wear shoes.
4. As people grow older, the shapes of their left and right feet can change differently.
default.q.n3-6-q69-69.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the fact that elderly people often fall was stated by the nursing-home manager at the beginning, not newly discovered when reviewing the investigation results.
default.q.n3-6-q69-69.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage does not mention elderly people complaining that the shoes were expensive.
default.q.n3-6-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage does not mention older people having fewer opportunities to wear shoes.
default.q.n3-6-q69-69.why.3: (d) Correct because the text clearly states the result after the investigation: 「すると、あることがわかった。お年寄りの中には年をとって片方の足だけが悪くなったり、足の形が変わってしまい左右の足の大きさが違ってきたりして、困っている人が少なくない。」
default.q.n3-6-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 「そんなこと」refers to selling shoes individually, one shoe at a time, instead of selling them as a pair as usual.
default.q.n3-6-q70-70.explanation:
Summary: After learning that many elderly people have feet of different sizes or need only one shoe, the manager decided to allow shoes to be sold individually. A veteran in the shoe industry objected that doing this (selling individual shoes) would make the business unprofitable, but the manager went ahead anyway.
- Question translation: What does「そんなこと」(such a thing) refer to?
- Answer choices:
1. Spending a great deal of money on research.
2. Selling only pairs of shoes whose left and right shoes are the same size.
3. Producing only one type of shoe, namely "shoes for elderly people."
4. Selling shoes individually, one shoe at a time.
default.q.n3-6-q70-70.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage does not mention being opposed by a senior colleague because the investigation cost too much money.
default.q.n3-6-q70-70.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the company does not simply sell shoes with equal sizes for both feet; it solves the problem of unequal sizes by selling individual shoes.
default.q.n3-6-q70-70.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「そんなこと」does not refer to making shoes exclusively for elderly people; it refers to the new sales method mentioned in the immediately preceding sentence.
default.q.n3-6-q70-70.why.3: (d) Correct because immediately before the demonstrative expression 「そんなこと」 is the sentence 「そこで、「お年奇りのための靴」を片方でも買えるようにした。」, and the following sentence confirms that this was 「この新しい販売方法」 (the method of selling shoes individually).
default.q.n3-6-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The company’s policy is to give wholehearted consideration to people facing difficulties and create and sell products that meet their needs.
default.q.n3-6-q71-71.explanation:
Summary: The company's success (selling more than 180,000 pairs a year and receiving 20,000 thank-you letters) stems from its wholehearted commitment to people in difficult situations: developing good products and selling them in the most suitable way so they reach those who truly need them.
- Question translation: 「このような会社」(a company like this) is mentioned. What kind of company is it?
- Answer choices:
1. A company that wholeheartedly considers people in difficult situations when developing and selling products.
2. A company that trusts its own good products and continues selling them even when they do not sell.
3. A company that seeks out things no one else does and carries them out despite opposition from those around it.
4. A company made up only of employees who deeply understand customers and continue creating good products.
default.q.n3-6-q71-71.why.0: (a) Correct because the preceding sentence clearly states the company’s attitude: 「困っている人の問題を解決するためにいいものを作り、今までの靴の売り方とは全く違った売り方で、それが必要な人のところに届けようとしたのである。」
default.q.n3-6-q71-71.why.1: (b) Incorrect because when the product initially sold poorly, the company proactively reviewed the survey results to improve its sales approach rather than stubbornly continuing to sell it.
default.q.n3-6-q71-71.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the core objective is to solve customers’ difficulties, not to do something others do not do merely to stand out despite opposition.
default.q.n3-6-q71-71.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not mention a criterion of using only staff who understand customers.
default.q.n3-6-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (cafeteria ③ - カフェ南川) because during the vacation, cafeterias ① and ② are closed, while cafeteria ④ does not allow students, so Tim can only go to café ③ at 1:00 p.m. on weekdays.
default.q.n3-6-q72-72.explanation:
- Main point: According to the rules in the notice, during weekdays in the university vacation period (大学の休暇期間中の平日), Cafeteria ① (Marukawa) and Cafeteria ② (Asahana) are both closed (①と②は休み). Café ③ (Minamikawa) and Cafeteria ④ (Hanamaru) are open from 11:00 to 14:00 (③と④は平日 11 時～14 時に営業します). However, Cafeteria ④ is exclusively for faculty and university staff, so students may not use it (教師や大学で働く関係者のための食堂です。学生は利用できません). Since Tim is a student who wants to eat at 13:00 on a weekday during the vacation, the only place he can go is Café ③.

- Question translation: Today is a weekday during the university vacation. Tim plans to eat at a university cafeteria or café at 13:00. Which cafeteria or café can Tim, a student, use?

- Answer choices:
1. Cafeterias ① and ② and Café ③.
2. Cafeterias ① and ②.
3. Café ③ and Cafeteria ④.
4. Café ③.
default.q.n3-6-q72-72.why.0: (a) Incorrect because both cafeteria ① (丸川食堂) and ② (朝花食堂) are closed during the vacation period according to the notice: 「※大学の休暇期間中の営業について: ①と②は休み」.
default.q.n3-6-q72-72.why.1: (b) Incorrect because both cafeterias ① and ② are closed during the school vacation (「①と②は休み」).
default.q.n3-6-q72-72.why.2: (c) Incorrect because although cafeteria ④ is open on weekdays during the vacation (11:00–14:00), students are not allowed to use it: 「教師や大学で働く関係者のための食堂です。学生は利用できません」. Tim is a student.
default.q.n3-6-q72-72.why.3: (d) Correct. The rule states: 「※大学の休暇期間中の営業について: ③と④は平日 11 時～14 時に営業します」. Café ③ allows students to enter, unlike cafeteria ④ (「学生は利用できません」), so Tim can go to café ③ at 1 p.m. on a weekday during the university vacation.
default.q.n3-6-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 2 because the party is held at cafeteria ② on Saturday (October 23), so the food order must be at least 2,500 yen per person.
default.q.n3-6-q73-73.explanation:
- Main points: Rules for holding a party in Cafeteria ② at Marukawa University:
1. Applicant: For ①–③, students may apply themselves (「※①～③は学生が申し込めます」).
2. Food cost: For ①–③, the cost is at least 2,000 yen per person; on Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays, it is at least 2,500 yen per person (「●①～③では一人 2０００円以上(土曜、日曜、祝日は、2,5００円以上)」).
3. Minimum number of people: Cafeteria ② accepts reservations for 40 or more people (「②は４０人...から予約受付をします」).
4. End time: Parties at ①–③ must end by 20:00 (「●①～③は 20 時まで...終えてください」).
Since student Ou wants to hold a party in Cafeteria ② on Saturday, October 23 (土曜日), the correct point to note is that the food must cost at least 2,500 yen per person.

- Translation of the question: Ou, a student at Marukawa University, wants to hold a class party in Cafeteria ② on Saturday, October 23. It has been confirmed that Cafeteria ② can be used for the party on October 23, but which of the following is correct regarding what must be kept in mind?

- Translation of the answer choices:
1. Students cannot apply.
2. The food must cost at least 2,500 yen per person.
3. The minimum number of people for a reservation is 20.
4. The party must end before 21:00.
default.q.n3-6-q73-73.why.0: (a) Incorrect because students are fully allowed to register for the party at cafeteria ②; the passage clearly states: 「※①～③は学生が申し込めますが、④は教師か事務所の人の申し込みが必要です」.
default.q.n3-6-q73-73.why.1: (b) Correct. Under 「►料理について」, the passage states: 「●①～③では一人 2０００円以上(土曜、日曜、祝日は、2,5００円以上)」. Since October 23 was a Saturday (土), the order at cafeteria ② must be at least 2,500 yen per person.
default.q.n3-6-q73-73.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the minimum number of people required to make a reservation at cafeteria ② is 40, not 20: 「●①は 18 人、②は４０人、③と④は２０人から予約受付をします」.
default.q.n3-6-q73-73.why.3: (d) Incorrect because events at venues ①～③ must end by 20:00; only ④ ends at 21:00: 「●①～③は 20 時まで、④は 21 時までに終えてください」.
default.q.n3-6-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 3. ふくしゅう.
default.q.n3-6-q1-1.explanation:
Meaning: Because I review every day, I have been doing much better.
- Kanji meanings: 復 (restore, repeat) + 習 (study, practice) → reviewing previously learned material.
- Related/contrasting terms: 予習 (よしゅう - preparing in advance), 練習 (れんしゅう - practice, training).
- Example: 授業の前に必ず予習し、終わったら復習する。(I always prepare before class and review after it ends.)
default.q.n3-6-q1-1.why.0: (a) ふうしゅう is an incorrect reading of「復」; its standard on-reading is「ふく」, without a long vowel「ふう」.
default.q.n3-6-q1-1.why.1: (b) れんしゅう: This is the reading of 「練習」, meaning practice; 「復」 is not read 「れん」.
default.q.n3-6-q1-1.why.2: (c) ふくしゅう: Correct.「復習」(review) is formed from「復」(ふく) and「習」(しゅう).
default.q.n3-6-q1-1.why.3: (d) れいしゅう: Incorrect reading; this vocabulary word does not exist.
default.q.n3-6-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 3. こがた.
default.q.n3-6-q2-2.explanation:
Meaning: I want a small radio.
- Kanji components: 小 (しょう: small) + 型 (がた: type, size, model) ➝ small-sized, compact.
- Related words: 大型 (おおがた: large-sized), 中型 (ちゅうがた: medium-sized).
- Note: When 型 (かた) follows 小 (こ), its pronunciation changes through rendaku to がた.
- Example: 小型カメラを買いました。(I bought a compact camera.)
default.q.n3-6-q2-2.why.0: (a) こかた: Incorrect reading because「型」(かた) changes to「がた」when it follows「小」(こ).
default.q.n3-6-q2-2.why.1: (b) しょうがた: An incorrect reading of 「小」. In words indicating size such as 小型 and 小型車, it is read with the kun-reading 「こ」, not the on-reading 「しょう」.
default.q.n3-6-q2-2.why.2: (c) こがた: Correct. 「小型」 (small-sized, small type) is read as 「こがた」.
default.q.n3-6-q2-2.why.3: (d) しょうかた: Both the reading of 「小」 (しょう) and the rendaku of 「型」 (かた) are incorrect.
default.q.n3-6-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 4. うたがって.
default.q.n3-6-q3-3.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Even without any reason, you must not doubt other people.
- The kanji 疑 means doubt or suspicion.
- Related vocabulary: 疑う (verb: to doubt), 疑問 (question, doubt), 容疑者 (suspect).
- Example: 彼の言葉を疑う余地はない。(There is no reason to doubt his words.)
default.q.n3-6-q3-3.why.0: (a) きらって: The te-form of the verb 「嫌う」 (きらう – to hate).
default.q.n3-6-q3-3.why.1: (b) こわがって: The te-form of the verb「怖がる」(こわがる - to be afraid, to feel apprehensive).
default.q.n3-6-q3-3.why.2: (c) しかって: The te-form of the verb「叱る」(しかる: to scold, reprimand).
default.q.n3-6-q3-3.why.3: (d) うたがって: Correct. The verb 「疑う」(うたがう), meaning to doubt or suspect, becomes 「疑って」 in the te-form.
default.q.n3-6-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ほそく.
default.q.n3-6-q4-4.explanation:
Meaning: From this point on, the road becomes narrower.
- Kanji: 細 (fine, thin, narrow).
- Antonym: 太い (ふとい: thick, fat, wide).
- Distinction:「細い」(ほそい: thin or slender) differs from「狭い」(せまい: narrow or cramped in terms of space).
- Example: 彼女は足が細くて長いです。(Her legs are slender and long.)
default.q.n3-6-q4-4.why.0: (a) ひろく: The adverbial form of the i-adjective 「広い」(ひろい - spacious, wide).
default.q.n3-6-q4-4.why.1: (b) ふとく: The adverbial form of the adjective 「太い」(ふとい: thick, fat, wide).
default.q.n3-6-q4-4.why.2: (c) せまく: The adverbial form of the i-adjective 「狭い」(せまい - narrow, cramped).
default.q.n3-6-q4-4.why.3: (d) ほそく: Correct. The i-adjective「細い」(ほそい) changes to「細く」(ほそく) when used adverbially.
default.q.n3-6-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 1. たいいん.
default.q.n3-6-q5-5.explanation:
Sentence meaning: I hear that Mr./Ms. Kawai will be discharged from the hospital tomorrow.
- Kanji components: 退 (to withdraw, leave) + 院 (hospital) → discharge from the hospital.
- Antonym: 入院 (にゅういん: hospitalization, admission to a hospital).
- Related words: 退社 (たいしゃ: leaving a company, finishing work), 退学 (たいがく: leaving school, dropping out).
- Example: 来週の月曜日に退院できることになった。(It has been decided that I can leave the hospital next Monday.)
default.q.n3-6-q5-5.why.0: (a) たいいん: Correct. 「退院」 (TAIIN – leaving the hospital) combines the on-readings of 「退」 (たい) and 「院」 (いん).
default.q.n3-6-q5-5.why.1: (b) たんいん: The reading of 「退」 is incorrect; it has been confused with the 「たん」 reading in 単位 / たんい.
default.q.n3-6-q5-5.why.2: (c) だいいん: The reading incorrectly voices 「たい」as「だい」; the on-reading of 「退」is the unvoiced 「たい」.
default.q.n3-6-q5-5.why.3: (d) だんいん: Incorrect reading, easily confused with 団員 / だんいん (団員).
default.q.n3-6-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 2. ふうふ.
default.q.n3-6-q6-6.explanation:
Sentence meaning: My spouse and I will attend the party together.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 夫 (husband) + 婦 (wife) → married couple.
- Note on vowel length: 「夫」is read with a long vowel as「ふう」, while「婦」is read with the short sound「ふ」→「ふうふ」.
- Example: あの夫婦はいつも仲がいい。(That married couple is always on good terms.)
default.q.n3-6-q6-6.why.0: (a) ふうふう: Incorrect because the long vowel in「婦」is unnecessary;「婦」is read briefly as「ふ」.
default.q.n3-6-q6-6.why.1: (b) ふうふ: Correct. 「夫婦」(married couple) is correctly read as 「ふうふ」(夫/ふう + 婦/ふ).
default.q.n3-6-q6-6.why.2: (c) ふふう: Incorrect because the long vowel is placed on the second character instead of the first.
default.q.n3-6-q6-6.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the long vowel is missing in 「夫」, whose on-reading is 「ふう」.
default.q.n3-6-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 2. るす.
default.q.n3-6-q7-7.explanation:
Meaning: It seems that someone came while I was away from home.
- Kanji note: 留守 originally combines 留 (to stay or remain) and 守 (to guard or look after). It developed from the idea of staying behind to watch the house while someone else was away, and now means being away from home or having no one at home.
- Related words: 留守番 (looking after the house while someone is away), 留守番電話 (answering machine / voicemail).
- Example: 一人暮らしなので、昼間はいつも留守にしています。(I live alone, so I am always away from home during the day.)
default.q.n3-6-q7-7.why.0: (a) るしゅ: Incorrect because 「守」in this word is read 「す」in Go-on, not 「しゅ」in Kan-on.
default.q.n3-6-q7-7.why.1: (b) るす: Correct. 「留守」(being away from home) has an irregular reading: 「留」is read as「る」and「守」as「す」.
default.q.n3-6-q7-7.why.2: (c) りゅうす: Incorrect because it confuses the usual reading of「留」(りゅう, as in 留学 / りゅうがく).
default.q.n3-6-q7-7.why.3: (d) りゅうしゅ: Both readings are incorrect; the standard reading is formed with る + す, not the usual on-readings りゅう + しゅ.
default.q.n3-6-q8-8.verdict: The correct answer is 1. こうか.
default.q.n3-6-q8-8.explanation:
Sentence meaning: I hear this is a very expensive flower vase.
- Kanji components: 高 (high) + 価 (price/value) → high-priced, expensive.
- Synonyms: 値段が高い (ねだんがたかい), 高級 (こうきゅう).
- Antonym: 安価 (あんか – inexpensive, reasonably priced).
- Distinction: 高価 (こうか – expensive in terms of price) differs from 豪華 (ごうか – luxurious or magnificent in appearance or scale).
- Example: 高価な貴金属を身につける。(to wear expensive precious-metal jewelry).
default.q.n3-6-q8-8.why.0: (a) こうか: Correct. 「高価」 (“expensive”) is formed from 「高」(こう) and 「価」(か); neither reading undergoes rendaku.
default.q.n3-6-q8-8.why.1: (b) ごうか is incorrect because it is the reading of「豪華」(ごうか — luxurious, extravagant).
default.q.n3-6-q8-8.why.2: (c) こうが: Incorrect because the sound of 「価」 has been incorrectly voiced, changing 「か」 to 「が」.
default.q.n3-6-q8-8.why.3: (d) ごうが: Both sounds are incorrect because they have been voiced as ごう and が.
default.q.n3-6-q9-9.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 短気.
default.q.n3-6-q9-9.explanation:
Translation: He has a very short temper.
• Kanji meaning: 短気 means hot-tempered or quick to anger.
• Example: 彼は短気ですぐ怒る。(He has a short temper and gets angry easily.)
default.q.n3-6-q9-9.why.0: (a) 「男気」 is usually read as 「おとこぎ」 or 「おとこけ」 and means gallantry or chivalrous spirit; it is not read as 「たんき」.
default.q.n3-6-q9-9.why.1: (b) 「単気」uses the wrong kanji;「単」does not combine with「気」to form a word describing a personality.
default.q.n3-6-q9-9.why.2: (c) 「短気」is read「たんき」and means short-tempered or impatient, which fits the context perfectly.
default.q.n3-6-q9-9.why.3: (d) 「断気」 uses the wrong kanji; 「断」 (DAN) has the on-reading 「だん」, not 「たん」, and this word does not exist.
default.q.n3-6-q10-10.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 心配.
default.q.n3-6-q10-10.explanation:
Translation: Mr. Ueda seems a little worried.
• Kanji reading: 心配 (worry, concern).
• Example: 心配しないでください。(Please don't worry.)
default.q.n3-6-q10-10.why.0: (a) 「心酔」 is read as 「しんすい」 and means being devoted to or idolizing someone or something; it is not read as 「しんぱい」.
default.q.n3-6-q10-10.why.1: (b) 「心配」is read「しんぱい」and means worry or concern, which fits the context perfectly.
default.q.n3-6-q10-10.why.2: (c) 「信配」 uses the wrong kanji 「信」; the correct word uses 「心」.
default.q.n3-6-q10-10.why.3: (d) 「信酔」 uses two incorrect kanji and has no meaning; this word does not exist in Japanese.
default.q.n3-6-q11-11.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 焼いて.
default.q.n3-6-q11-11.explanation:
Translation: Next, let's grill/fry this dish.
• Kanji reading: 焼 (to grill, fry, burn).
• Example: 肉と野菜を焼いて食べる。(Grill meat and vegetables and eat them.)
default.q.n3-6-q11-11.why.0: (a) 「焼いて」 is the te-form of the verb 「焼く」 (やく — to grill, fry, or burn), read as 「やいて」, and fits the context.
