default.q.n3-6-q31-31.why.0: Incorrect because a company’s growth and expansion in business scale should be expressed with 「成長した」or「発展した」, not 「進歩」.
default.q.n3-6-q31-31.why.1: Correct because 「技術が進歩する」 is a natural and standard collocation meaning that technology advances or develops.
default.q.n3-6-q31-31.why.2: Wrong because a returning appetite or gradually improving physical condition after an illness should be expressed with 「回復してきた」or「戻ってきた」.
default.q.n3-6-q31-31.why.3: Incorrect because an increase in rent or prices is expressed with 「値上がりして」, 「上がって」, or 「高くなって」, not 「進歩」.
default.q.n3-6-q32-32.explanation:
「話しかける」（はなしかける） means “to start a conversation” or “to take the initiative and speak to someone.”
- Common patterns: ～に話しかける (to speak to someone), ～に話しかけられる (to be spoken to by someone).
- Example: 隣の席の人に思い切って話しかけてみた。(I worked up the courage to speak to the person sitting next to me.)
default.q.n3-6-q32-32.why.0: Correct because 「（人に）話しかける」 means to actively speak to or start a conversation with someone. The passive form 「話しかけられた」 (“was spoken to by a tourist”) is completely accurate here.
default.q.n3-6-q32-32.why.1: Incorrect. Discussing and consulting with one’s family to make a decision requires「話し合って」or「相談して」.
default.q.n3-6-q32-32.why.2: Incorrect because calling people by name or taking attendance requires 「名前を呼ぶ（呼びます）」, not 「話しかける」.
default.q.n3-6-q32-32.why.3: Incorrect because when thanking someone, the correct expression is 「お礼を言われました」, not 「お礼を話しかける」.
default.q.n3-6-q33-33.explanation:
「交流」(こうりゅう) means “interaction” or “交流,” referring to contact, exchange, interaction, and the strengthening of relationships among people, groups, or cultures.
- Common expressions: 文化交流 (cultural exchange), 国際交流 (international exchange), 交流会 (交流 event), 交流を深める (deepen交流).
- Example: 地域のイベントに参加して、近所の人たちと交流を深めた。(I took part in a local event and deepened my交流 with my neighbors.)
default.q.n3-6-q33-33.why.0: Incorrect because when two colors blend together to create a new color, 「混ざって」 or 「混ざり合って」 is used, not 「交流」.
default.q.n3-6-q33-33.why.1: Incorrect because when mixing sauce with vegetables in cooking, 「混ぜる」 or 「和える」 must be used.
default.q.n3-6-q33-33.why.2: Correct because 「交流する」 is appropriately used for interaction and cultural exchange between people or groups, especially international exchange: 海外の人たちと交流する.
default.q.n3-6-q33-33.why.3: Incorrect because when several people's belongings are mixed together in a drawer, 「混ざっている」or「一緒に入っている」is used, not「交流」.
default.q.n3-6-q34-34.explanation:
「渋滞」（じゅうたい）means “traffic jam” or “congestion,” referring to a situation in which traffic is blocked and vehicles move with difficulty or cannot move.
- Common expressions: 交通渋滞 (traffic congestion), 道が渋滞する (the road is congested), 渋滞に巻き込まれる (get caught in a traffic jam), 渋滞を避ける (avoid traffic jams).
- Example: 連休中は高速道路がどこも激しく渋滞する。(During a long holiday, expressways are severely congested everywhere.)
default.q.n3-6-q34-34.why.0: Incorrect because delayed construction progress is expressed with 「遅れていて」 or 「滞っていて」, not 「渋滞」.
default.q.n3-6-q34-34.why.1: Correct because 「道が渋滞する」is the most accurate standard expression for roads being congested or blocked by a traffic accident.
default.q.n3-6-q34-34.why.2: Incorrect because for pressure or mental stress building up, use 「ストレスがたまっている」 or 「蓄積している」.
default.q.n3-6-q34-34.why.3: Incorrect because when unsold goods accumulate and remain in storage, expressions such as 「たまっている」, 「残っている」, or 「在庫になっている」 are used.
default.q.n3-6-q35-35.explanation:
「にこにこ」 is an onomatopoeic expression describing a bright smile, a cheerful smile, or a radiant, gentle expression showing happiness or satisfaction.
- Common expressions: にこにこ笑う (smile brightly), にこにこしている (have a cheerful smile), にこにこ顔 (a radiant, smiling face).
- Example: 彼女はいつもにこにこしていて、周囲を明るい雰囲気にする。(She is always smiling brightly and creates a cheerful atmosphere around her.)
default.q.n3-6-q35-35.why.0: Incorrect because the feeling of panic and anxiety when the car is about to run out of gas and stop in the middle of the road should be expressed with 「ハラハラした」 or 「ひやひやした」.
default.q.n3-6-q35-35.why.1: Incorrect. For the nervous, tense feeling that makes your heart pound when singing in front of a crowd, 「胸がドキドキした」 must be used.
default.q.n3-6-q35-35.why.2: Incorrect because a throbbing headache should be expressed as 「頭がズキズキしている」or 「ガンガンしている」.
default.q.n3-6-q35-35.why.3: Correct because 「にこにこ（する）」describes the grandmother's bright, gentle smile and cheerful eyes as she watches her grandchildren play.
default.q.n3-7-q36-36.explanation:
Sentence meaning: (In class) An: “Teacher, I’ve filled out the application form for the speech contest. I’m not quite sure how to fill in one part. Would it be all right if I write it like this?”
Common expressions: これで大丈夫でしょうか／これでいいですか (Is this all right?/Is this acceptable?). The particle で indicates a limit, condition, or means/manner.
default.q.n3-7-q36-36.why.0: (a) に: The particle に indicates direction, a target, an object, or a point in time. It is not used to express the method, scope, or manner of saying “this way is fine.”
default.q.n3-7-q36-36.why.1: (b) で: The particle で follows これ to form 「これで大丈夫」, meaning “Is this okay?” or “Will this way work?”
default.q.n3-7-q36-36.why.2: (c) と: The particle と indicates being together with someone or quotes content; it does not accompany 大丈夫 in this context.
default.q.n3-7-q36-36.why.3: (d) が: The particle が marks the subject or the object associated with an adjective, but here これ is not the subject of 大丈夫; it is the proposed option or method.
default.q.n3-7-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 1. において.
default.q.n3-7-q37-37.explanation:
(On the website of Kitayama City) The summer festival was held at Kitayama Park on July 25 and 26.
Pattern: N (place / time / context) + において: at, in (a formal written expression used in announcements and similar contexts, equivalent to で).
Example: 入学式は講堂において行われます。(The entrance ceremony will be held in the auditorium.)
default.q.n3-7-q37-37.why.0: (a) において: The grammar pattern N + において means “in/at” and indicates the place or context where an event occurs in formal language, such as official announcements.
default.q.n3-7-q37-37.why.1: (b) にとって: Means “for” or “from the standpoint of N”; it is not used to indicate the location where an event is held.
default.q.n3-7-q37-37.why.2: (c) に対して: Means “toward/with regard to N” (directing an attitude or action toward N) or “in contrast to N”; it is not used to indicate a place.
default.q.n3-7-q37-37.why.3: (d) について means “about” a topic or content, and is not used to indicate the location where an event takes place.
default.q.n3-7-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 3. にでも.
default.q.n3-7-q38-38.explanation:
Meaning: I have great respect for my older brother, who is kind and gentle to everyone.
Grammar: Interrogative + でも = anyone / anything / anywhere. 誰にでも = to anyone, to everyone.
Related vocabulary: 親切 (SHIN-SETSU - kind, helpful), 尊敬 (SON-KEI - respect, reverence).
default.q.n3-7-q38-38.why.0: (a) にだけ: Means “only toward...,” and does not naturally combine with the question word 誰 in the positive sense of praising someone's kindness toward everyone.
default.q.n3-7-q38-38.why.1: (b) からだけ: Means “only from...”; it uses the wrong particle for the target of the adjective 親切 (which requires に) and is also incorrect in meaning.
default.q.n3-7-q38-38.why.2: (c) にでも: The expression 誰にでも means “to anyone” or “to everyone,” referring to the recipients of the person’s friendliness and kindness (親切で優しい).
default.q.n3-7-q38-38.why.3: (d) からでも: Means “from anyone,” which is inappropriate because the recipient of kindness must be marked by the particle に.
default.q.n3-7-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 必ず.
default.q.n3-7-q39-39.explanation:
Meaning: (In class) Teacher: "You will need this handout for next week's class, so be sure to bring it with you."
Adverb: 必ず (TẤT - certainly, without fail).
Example: 明日の会議には必ず出席してください。(Please be sure to attend tomorrow's meeting.)
default.q.n3-7-q39-39.why.0: (a) 全く: An adverb meaning “completely,” usually used with negative sentences (全く～ない: not at all...) or exclamatory sentences.
default.q.n3-7-q39-39.why.1: (b) 非常に is an adverb of degree meaning “very” or “extremely.” It modifies adjectives or adverbs, not requests or commands in ～てください.
default.q.n3-7-q39-39.why.2: (c) 決して: An adverb meaning “absolutely not,” always used with a negative sentence (決して～ない).
default.q.n3-7-q39-39.why.3: (d) 必ず: An adverb meaning “certainly” or “without fail,” often used with requests, reminders, and instructions (必ず～てください).
default.q.n3-7-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 1. どうしても.
default.q.n3-7-q40-40.explanation:
Meaning: I was invited to my friend's wedding, but because I have a business trip, I absolutely cannot go.
Structure: どうしても～ない = no matter what, cannot... (expressing an unavoidable situation despite strongly wanting to do it).
Related vocabulary: 招待 (しょうたい) = invitation; 出張 (しゅっちょう) = business trip.
default.q.n3-7-q40-40.why.0: (a) どうしても: An adverb meaning “no matter what, cannot,” used with a negative potential form (行けない) to express unavoidable inability and regret.
default.q.n3-7-q40-40.why.1: (b) それほど: An adverb meaning “to that extent,” used with the negative form to indicate that something is not as much as that (それほど～ない).
default.q.n3-7-q40-40.why.2: (c) せっかく: Means “having taken the trouble to do something” and is often used with ～のに or ～から (e.g., せっかく誘ってくれたのに...); it does not directly modify 行けない.
default.q.n3-7-q40-40.why.3: (d) つい: an adverb meaning “inadvertently, without meaning to, or unable to resist,” often used with ～てしまう.
default.q.n3-7-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ために.
default.q.n3-7-q41-41.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: The baseball player I support is temporarily unable to play because of a shoulder injury. I am very worried.
Pattern: N + のために: because of / due to N (indicating the cause or reason for the result in the following clause, in an objective, formal style).
Related vocabulary: 応援 (supporting or cheering), 肩 (shoulder), 試合 (match or game).
default.q.n3-7-q41-41.why.0: (a) 途中で: Means “in the middle of...” or “while...”. It commonly follows a noun referring to an ongoing activity (会議の途中で...), so it is illogical with a noun referring to a state such as an injury.
default.q.n3-7-q41-41.why.1: (b) 一方で: means “on the other hand / at the same time,” and expresses two contrasting or parallel aspects of an issue; it is not used to state a cause.
default.q.n3-7-q41-41.why.2: (c) ように: Means “so that” (purpose) or “like/as,” and N + のように is not used to indicate a cause leading to the negative consequence that follows.
default.q.n3-7-q41-41.why.3: (d) ために: The pattern N + のために indicates a cause or reason (肩のけがのために = because of a shoulder injury).
default.q.n3-7-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 磨かずに.
default.q.n3-7-q42-42.explanation:
Meaning: Dentist: “If you go to sleep without brushing your teeth, you’ll be very likely to get cavities. Be sure to brush your teeth carefully before going to bed.”
Structure: V-ずに = V-ないで: without doing V; a formal expression. For する, use せずに.
Related kanji: 磨く (MA - to polish, brush one’s teeth), 虫歯 (MUSHIBA - cavity, tooth decay).
default.q.n3-7-q42-42.why.0: (a) 磨いて: It means “brush one’s teeth and then go to sleep” (磨いて寝る); if the teeth have been brushed, this contradicts the following logic that they are likely to develop cavities.
default.q.n3-7-q42-42.why.1: (b) 磨かずに: The V-ずに form means “without doing V”; 歯を磨かずに寝てしまう means “go to bed without brushing one’s teeth,” which is grammatically and semantically correct.
default.q.n3-7-q42-42.why.2: (c) 磨くたび means “every time [someone] brushes their teeth,” which is completely illogical in this sentence.
default.q.n3-7-q42-42.why.3: (d) 磨かなくて: The V-なくて form is generally used to indicate a cause or reason (“because one did not brush one’s teeth…”). It is not used to express doing one action without doing another, for which ずに/ないで is appropriate.
default.q.n3-7-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 出かけるところだから.
default.q.n3-7-q43-43.explanation:
Sentence meaning: (On the phone) Nakagawa: “Hello. Hayashi, is now a good time to talk?” — Hayashi: “Oh, I’m sorry. I’m about to go out now, so I’ll call you back later.”
Structure: V-るところ: be about to do something (often used with 今から, これから, ちょうど). The following clause explains the reason, so だから is used.
default.q.n3-7-q43-43.why.0: (a) 出かけるところなのに: Although V-るところ means “be about to do something” and is used with これから, なのに expresses dissatisfaction or an unexpected contrast (“even though”), so it is not used here to give a reason for refusing a call.
default.q.n3-7-q43-43.why.1: (b) 出かけているところなのに is incorrect both because V-ているところ (“in the middle of going out”) cannot be used with これから and because the conjunction なのに does not fit.
default.q.n3-7-q43-43.why.2: (c) 出かけるところだから: The structure これから + V-るところ means “be about to go out.” Combined with だから, it gives a valid reason: “because I am about to go out now...”.
default.q.n3-7-q43-43.why.3: (d) 出かけているところだから: The V-ているところ form describes an action in progress, so it does not combine with a time adverb indicating that something is about to happen, such as これから.
default.q.n3-7-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 1. のぼっていくと.
default.q.n3-7-q44-44.explanation:
Meaning: (On the street) A: "Excuse me, I'm looking for the East Library..." - B: "Oh, the East Library. Go up this hill and you'll see the post office; then turn right at that corner. The library is right after you turn right."
Directional structure: V-ると (When you go/do this, you will see...).
Movement direction: V-ていく describes movement away from the speaker's location.
default.q.n3-7-q44-44.why.0: (a) のぼっていくと: Because the route moves farther upward from the speaker’s position, のぼっていく (go up the slope) is used. The V-ると conditional indicates directions: “When you go up this slope, you will see the post office.”
default.q.n3-7-q44-44.why.1: (b) のぼっていきながら: The ながら form indicates that one subject performs two actions simultaneously; it is not used in a structure that gives directions for identifying a location ahead.
default.q.n3-7-q44-44.why.2: (c) のぼってくるには: くる indicates movement toward the speaker, which is the wrong direction for the person asking the question. には (in order to) is also not used to indicate a natural route leading to an objective result such as 郵便局があります.
default.q.n3-7-q44-44.why.3: (d) のぼってくるとき: The direction of movement indicated by くる is incorrect, and とき is less natural here than the route-guidance pattern ～と.
default.q.n3-7-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 知ってる.
default.q.n3-7-q45-45.explanation:
Meaning: A: "Do you know about the new ramen shop that opened near Sakura Station?" - B: "No, I don't." - A: "I went there for the first time yesterday, and it was really good."
Colloquial speech: In casual conversation, 知っている, a verb expressing a state of knowing, is often shortened to 知ってる by dropping 「い」.
default.q.n3-7-q45-45.why.0: (a) 知っとく: A contracted form of 知っておく (to know in advance, to make preparations); it is not used to ask whether someone knows information or a location.
default.q.n3-7-q45-45.why.1: (b) 知っちゃう is a shortened form of 知ってしまう (“end up finding out”), carrying a sense of regret or accidental discovery.
default.q.n3-7-q45-45.why.2: (c) 知ってく: An abbreviated form of 知っていく, meaning to gradually come to know something; it is not used to ask about current knowledge.
default.q.n3-7-q45-45.why.3: (d) 知ってる: A casual shortened form of 知っている (Do you know?), which fits perfectly with the negative reply 「ううん、知らない」(No, I don’t know).
default.q.n3-7-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 2. おります.
default.q.n3-7-q46-46.explanation:
- Translation: (On the phone) Yamashita: "Yes, Yamashita speaking from the sales department of X Construction Company." — Ishida: "This is Ishida from ABC Bank. May I ask whether Mr. Nakagawa or Mr. Hayashi is there?" — Yamashita: "Yes, Mr. Nakagawa is here. I will put you through right away."
Business honorific language: The verb いる (be present, be) becomes the humble form おる / おります when referring to someone inside one's own company while speaking to an outside business partner.
default.q.n3-7-q46-46.why.0: (a) いたします is the humble form of する (to do) and is not used to express a person's existence or presence.
default.q.n3-7-q46-46.why.1: (b) おります: The humble form of いる (“to be present,” “to be”). In business communication with a customer, the speaker lowers the status of the coworker Nakagawa (中川) by using the humble form おります.
default.q.n3-7-q46-46.why.2: (c) いただきます: The humble form of もらう or 食べる／飲む; it is not used to indicate presence.
default.q.n3-7-q46-46.why.3: (d) ございます: The polite form of ある or です, used for things or phenomena, not for the presence of people.
default.q.n3-7-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 行ったことはない.
default.q.n3-7-q47-47.explanation:
Sentence meaning: I love art museums, so I have visited many different museums over the years. Most of them have been museums in Japan, while I have never visited an art museum abroad.
Structure: V-たことがない means “have never experienced doing V.” The conjunction が creates a contrast between the two clauses: there are many museums in Japan (国内の美術館が多い), but I have never visited one overseas (海外の美術館に行ったことはない).
Related kanji vocabulary: 美術館 (art museum), 海外 (overseas, abroad).
default.q.n3-7-q47-47.why.0: (a) 行ったこともある means “have also been to.” However, the preceding clause, 国内の美術館が多いが (“there are many museums in Japan, but…”), expresses contrast with the following clause, so “have never been to” fits the logic better.
default.q.n3-7-q47-47.why.1: (b) 行ったことはない: The pattern V-たことはない means "have never done V." After the contrasting conjunction が, it contrasts 国内の美術館が多い (there are many museums domestically) with 海外の美術館には行ったことはない (I have never been to museums overseas).
default.q.n3-7-q47-47.why.2: (c) 行くこともできる: Means “can also go,” expressing present or future ability. It does not fit the context of describing experiences up to now (今まで).
default.q.n3-7-q47-47.why.3: (d) 行くこともできない: means “cannot go either,” expressing inability and not fitting the context of an experience.
default.q.n3-7-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 履いてみてもいいですか.
default.q.n3-7-q48-48.explanation:
- Meaning: (At a shoe store) Customer: "Excuse me, may I try on these shoes?" — Staff: "Of course. Are these the right size for you?" — Customer: "Yes."
Permission pattern: V-てみてもいいですか: May I try doing V? (V-てみる: try doing + ～てもいいですか: may I...? ).
Related vocabulary: 靴 (shoes), 履く (put on/wear shoes, socks, or trousers).
default.q.n3-7-q48-48.why.0: (a) 履いてもらえませんか means “could you try on the shoes for me?” It has the wrong subject because the customer wants to try them on personally.
default.q.n3-7-q48-48.why.1: (b) 履かないんですか: It means “Aren’t you going to try them on?” (a question to a store employee), so it does not fit a customer asking permission to try on an item.
default.q.n3-7-q48-48.why.2: (c) 履いてみてもいいですか: The pattern V-てみる (try doing something) + ～てもいいですか (may I...?) is used. The customer is asking permission to try on the shoes: “May I try these on?”
default.q.n3-7-q48-48.why.3: (d) 履くことになりますか: Means “Will it become a rule/decision that I wear them?”, which does not fit the meaning or context of asking permission to try on clothing.
default.q.n3-7-q49-49.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 1 → 3 (the ★ position is 1 - メール).
default.q.n3-7-q49-49.explanation:
Complete sentence: 留学している息子からのメールに毎日楽しく過ごしていると書かれていて安心した。
Meaning: I was relieved to read in an email from my son, who is studying abroad, that he was enjoying every day.
default.q.n3-7-q49-49.why.0: (a) Part 1 (メール): It follows the modifying phrase 「息子からの」 and comes before the particle 「に」 to form 「息子からのメールに」 (in the email from my son), functioning as an adverbial phrase indicating the source of the information in 「書かれていて」.
default.q.n3-7-q49-49.why.1: (b) Segment 2 (から): It comes directly after the noun「息子」to indicate the source or origin:「息子から」(from one’s son).
default.q.n3-7-q49-49.why.2: (c) Part 3 (に): It follows the noun 「メール」to form 「メールに」(in the email), indicating where the content 「～と書かれていて」is found.
default.q.n3-7-q49-49.why.3: (d) Fragment 4 (の): It follows 「息子から」 and modifies the noun 「メール」 that comes after it (息子からのメール - an email from my son).
default.q.n3-7-q50-50.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 1 → 4 → 2 (the ★ position is 4 - 東京に).
default.q.n3-7-q50-50.explanation:
Complete sentence: 来週から 1 か月間、出張で東京に行く。東京には友達がいるので、東京にいる間に一緒に食事でもしたいと思う。
Meaning: “Starting next week, I’ll be going to Tokyo on a business trip for one month. Since I have friends in Tokyo, I’d like to have a meal with them while I’m there.”
default.q.n3-7-q50-50.why.0: (a) Part 1 (いるので): It follows 「友達が」 to form the reason clause 「友達がいるので」 (because there are friends).
default.q.n3-7-q50-50.why.1: (b) Fragment 2 (いる間に): Following 「東京に」, it forms the structure 「～間に」 (“while / during the time that [someone] is in Tokyo”), providing the time frame for 「一緒に食事でもしたい」.
default.q.n3-7-q50-50.why.2: (c) Fragment 3 (友達が) comes immediately after 「東京には」 and serves as the subject of 「いる」 (“there is a friend in Tokyo”).
default.q.n3-7-q50-50.why.3: (d) Fragment 4 (東京に): It comes before 「いる間に」 to indicate the place of stay, 「東京にいる」 (being in Tokyo), throughout the period 「～間に」.
default.q.n3-7-q51-51.verdict: The correct order is: 4 → 1 → 3 → 2 (the ★ position is 3 - 弾けば).
default.q.n3-7-q51-51.explanation:
The complete sentence: バイオリンが弾けるようになりたくて1年前に習い始めたのだが、弾けば弾くほどこんなに面白い楽器はないと感じる。
Meaning: I started taking lessons a year ago because I wanted to learn to play the violin, but the more I play it, the more I feel that there is no instrument as interesting as this.
default.q.n3-7-q51-51.why.0: (a) Fragment 1 (1年前に習い始めたのだが): It follows 「弾けるようになりたくて」 and states the action of beginning to learn based on that desire. The conjunction 「のだが」 connects it to the feeling expressed in the following clause.
default.q.n3-7-q51-51.why.1: (b) Segment 2 (弾くほど): placed after 「弾けば」 to form the incremental comparison pattern 「～ば～ほど」 (“the more …, the more …”).
default.q.n3-7-q51-51.why.2: (c) Part 3 (弾けば): It follows the clause 「～のだが」 and begins the pattern 「～ば～ほど」 (the more one plays...).
default.q.n3-7-q51-51.why.3: (d) Fragment 4 (弾けるようになりたくて): It comes directly after 「バイオリンが」 to form the phrase expressing the desired goal 「バイオリンが弾けるようになりたくて」 (“because I wanted to be able to play the violin”).
default.q.n3-7-q52-52.verdict: The correct order is: 1 → 4 → 2 → 3 (the ★ position is 2 - 欲しい).
default.q.n3-7-q52-52.explanation:
Complete sentence: A「お誕生日おめでとう。これ、プレゼントだよ。」 B「わあ、かばんだ。ちょうどこういう色のかばんが欲しいと思っていたんだ。ありがとう。」
Translation: A: "Happy birthday! This is a present for you." B: "Wow, a bag! I was just thinking that I wanted a bag in this kind of color. Thank you."
default.q.n3-7-q52-52.why.0: (a) Part 1 (こういう色の): Comes after「ちょうど」and modifies the noun「かばん」that follows (a bag with this kind of color).
default.q.n3-7-q52-52.why.1: (b) Fragment 2 (欲しい): Follows「かばんが」to form the expression of desire「かばんが欲しい」(want a handbag) and comes before the quotative particle「と」in「と思っていた」.
default.q.n3-7-q52-52.why.2: (c) Fragment 3 (と思っていた): Following 「欲しいと」, it forms the pattern 「～と思っていた」(was thinking that...) and ends the sentence before 「んだ」.
default.q.n3-7-q52-52.why.3: (d) Fragment 4 (かばんが): It follows the modifying phrase 「こういう色の」 and serves as the subject of the adjective expressing desire, 「欲しい」.
default.q.n3-7-q53-53.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 1 → 2 → 4 (the ★ position is 2 - 違いは).
default.q.n3-7-q53-53.explanation:
Complete sentence: 都会と田舎には違うところも多いが、どちらも、人が働き、生活しているという点で違いはない。
Meaning: “There are many differences between cities and the countryside, but there is no difference in the fact that people work and live in both places.”
default.q.n3-7-q53-53.why.0: (a) Fragment 1 (という点で): It follows 「生活している」to form the grammar 「～という点で」(in that respect, in terms of...), used to state an aspect of comparison.
default.q.n3-7-q53-53.why.1: (b) Fragment 2 (違いは): It follows 「という点で」and serves as the emphasized subject, marked by 「は」, which goes with the negative predicate 「ない」at the end of the sentence.
default.q.n3-7-q53-53.why.2: (c) Fragment 3 (生活している): It follows the continuative form of the verb 「働き、」(work and...) to form the sequence of actions 「人が働き、生活している」(people work and live).
default.q.n3-7-q53-53.why.3: (d) Fragment 4 (ない) comes at the end of the sentence and combines with 「違いは」to form the predicate 「違いはない」(there is no difference).
default.q.n3-7-q54-54.explanation: In the previous sentence, the author says that during a trip to Kyoto, they stayed at a ryokan with a hot spring: 『京都では温泉のある旅館に泊まりました。』. The author then lists experiences they had for the first time during the trip: 『畳の部屋に入るのは初めてでした。温泉にも初めて入りました。』(It was my first time entering a tatami room. It was also my first time bathing in a hot spring.) Since the author is talking generally about a new experience (bathing in an onsen), using the plain noun 「温泉」is the most natural and accurate choice.
default.q.n3-7-q54-54.why.0: (a) 温泉: Correct. The author is describing a first-time experience—taking a bath in an onsen for the first time—so the general noun 「温泉」is the most natural and accurate choice.
default.q.n3-7-q54-54.why.1: (b) あの温泉: Incorrect. 「あの」 refers to a specific object that both the speaker and listener already clearly know, so it is unsuitable when talking about entering an onsen for the first time.
default.q.n3-7-q54-54.why.2: (c) そんな温泉: Incorrect. 「そんな」 (that kind of/such a) refers to a characteristic or type and may carry an evaluative nuance, so it does not fit a narrative describing an actual experience.
default.q.n3-7-q54-54.why.3: (d) これらの温泉: Incorrect. 「これらの」 means “these hot springs” in the plural, whereas the author is staying at one ryokan and referring to bathing in the hot spring.
default.q.n3-7-q55-55.explanation: In the sentence 『腕時計【20】ないことに気がつきました』, the clause 『腕時計……ない』 is a subordinate clause within the nominalized expression 『〜ことに気がつきました』(to realize that...). In a subordinate clause describing an objective state or phenomenon that has been discovered (the wristwatch is not there / is missing), the subject of the subordinate clause is always marked with the particle 「が」.
default.q.n3-7-q55-55.why.0: (a) まで: Incorrect. The particle 「まで」 (“up to” or “until”) does not make semantic sense with 「ない」 in the context of discovering that an object is missing.
default.q.n3-7-q55-55.why.1: (b) しか: Incorrect. The structure 「しか～ない」 means “only...”. If inserted here, it would produce the illogical meaning “there is only no watch,” which does not fit the situation of realizing that an item is missing.
default.q.n3-7-q55-55.why.2: (c) は: Incorrect. In a subordinate clause describing an event directly perceived or recognized (realizing that the clock was not there), the subject of the subordinate clause must take the particle 「が」, not 「は」.
default.q.n3-7-q55-55.why.3: (d) が: Correct. The structure 「[noun] が ないことに気がつく」 indicates discovering that the noun—in this case, the watch—is missing or absent in a subordinate clause.
default.q.n3-7-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (落ちていたそうです).
default.q.n3-7-q56-56.explanation: Earlier, the hotel staff found the author's watch and brought it back to the room: 『フロントの人が私の時計を見つけて、部屋に持ってきてくれました。』. The next sentence explains where the watch was found, according to the staff: 『温泉の入り口のところに落ちていたそうです。』 (Apparently, it had been dropped right by the entrance to the hot spring). The hearsay expression 「〜そうです」combined with the past progressive 「落ちていた」fits the flow of the story perfectly.
default.q.n3-7-q56-56.why.0: (a) 落ちたままです: Incorrect. 「〜まま」 describes a state that remains unchanged. However, the watch was picked up by a staff member and returned to the room, so it cannot be said to be “still lying there after falling.”
default.q.n3-7-q56-56.why.1: (b) 落ちたばかりです: Incorrect. 「〜ばかり」 describes an action that has just occurred, which does not fit because this refers to hearing about the location where it was found.
default.q.n3-7-q56-56.why.2: (c) 落ちていたそうです: Correct. The pattern 「plain form + そうです」reports information heard from someone else. Here, the receptionist reports that the watch had apparently been dropped at the hot spring entrance.
default.q.n3-7-q56-56.why.3: (d) 落ちていたことです: Incorrect. 「〜ことです」at the end of a sentence is used to give advice or state a definition/explain a rule, not to report an event.
default.q.n3-7-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (なるのだと感じました).
default.q.n3-7-q57-57.explanation: This is the concluding sentence of the passage, summarizing the author's deepest reflection after the trip: 『旅行では観光地や食べ物だけではなく、人の優しさもいい思い出になるのだと感じました。』 (I realized that when traveling, not only the sights and food but also people's kindness can become wonderful memories.) The pattern 「〜のだと感じました」 expresses sincere reflection and understanding of a lesson or truth gained from the author's own experience.
default.q.n3-7-q57-57.why.0: (a) なっただろうと思います: Incorrect. 「〜だろうと思います」expresses vague speculation about the past and lacks the author’s deep emotion and reflection on what was learned from the experience.
default.q.n3-7-q57-57.why.1: (b) なるのだと感じました: Correct. 「〜のだと感じました」 is used to summarize the realization, lesson, and profound feelings the author gained from the trip.
default.q.n3-7-q57-57.why.2: (c) なったのではないでしょうか: Incorrect. 「〜のではないでしょうか」 softly presents a supposition or seeks the reader’s opinion; it is not used to conclude a personal narrative by summarizing one’s own feelings.
default.q.n3-7-q57-57.why.3: (d) なるでしょうか: Incorrect. 「〜でしょうか」 is an interrogative or self-questioning form, so it is unsuitable for a sentence ending that expresses an affirmative impression.
default.q.n3-7-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 会計課でコピーをする。中島さんに言う必要はない。
default.q.n3-7-q58-58.explanation:
**Main point:** A notice sent to the sales department says that the department's photocopier is broken and will not be repaired until tomorrow afternoon. Anyone who urgently needs copies today should use the accounting department's photocopier. Only people who need 50 or more copies must notify Nakajima in advance so that he can contact the accounting department; fewer than 50 copies do not require notification.

**Question translation:** Mr. Hong from the sales department wants to make 5 copies of a document today for tomorrow morning's meeting. What should he do?

**Answer choices:**
1. Make the copies in the sales department. He does not need to tell Nakajima.
2. Make the copies in the accounting department. He does not need to tell Nakajima.
3. Tell Nakajima, then make the copies in the sales department.
4. Tell Nakajima, then make the copies in the accounting department.
default.q.n3-7-q58-58.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the copy machine in the sales department is currently broken and cannot be used (「営業課のコピー機は今、故障していて使えません」), so copying there is impossible.
default.q.n3-7-q58-58.why.1: (b) Correct. The notice states that documents needed urgently by the end of the day should be copied using the accounting department’s machine («今日中にコピーしなければならない書類がある場合は、会計課のコピー機を使用してください»), and that Nakajima must be notified only when making 50 or more copies («50枚以上コピーをする場合は...コピーをする前に中島に知らせてください»). Since Hong made only 5 copies, he did not need to notify him.
default.q.n3-7-q58-58.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the sales department’s photocopier is broken and cannot be used. Also, making 5 copies—fewer than 50—does not require notifying Nakajima in advance.
default.q.n3-7-q58-58.why.3: (d) Incorrect because prior notice to Nakajima is required only when making 50 or more photocopies («50枚以上コピーをする場合は...コピーをする前に中島に知らせてください»). Mr. Hong made only 5 copies, so he did not need to report it.
default.q.n3-7-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 4: ちょうどいい力の入れ方を体で覚える練習をさせていなかったから。
default.q.n3-7-q59-59.explanation:
Main point:
The writer taught his six-year-old daughter how to throw a ball by explaining what she was doing wrong and having her throw it many times, but she never improved. After watching a television program in which children threw balls of different sizes and weights or flew paper airplanes, allowing their bodies to learn naturally how much force to use, the writer realized that this might be exactly what his daughter needed.

Question translation:
After watching the television program, why did “I” think his daughter had never become good at throwing a ball?

Answer choices:
1. Because “my” explanations of how to throw well were inadequate.
2. Because he had not let her practice throwing repeatedly using the same throwing technique.
3. Because he had not shown her in person how well “I” could throw.
4. Because he had not let her practice until her body naturally learned how much force to use.
default.q.n3-7-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage only mentions the writer explaining the daughter’s shortcomings; it does not say that the writer’s explanation was poor or clumsy (下手).
default.q.n3-7-q59-59.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the writer repeatedly had the child throw the ball (何回もボールを投げさせている). The passage does not say that a lack of repetition is why the child has not improved.
default.q.n3-7-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage does not mention whether the writer actually demonstrated skillful ball throwing for their daughter.
default.q.n3-7-q59-59.why.3: (d) Correct. The quotation states: 「番組では、子供に大きさや重さの違うさまざまなボールを投げさせたり、紙飛行機を飛ばさせたりして、ちょうどいい力の入れ方を体で覚えさせていた。娘に必要なのは、これかもしれない。」 The writer realizes that the child’s lack of skill may be because she has not practiced enough to physically sense and remember how much force to use.
default.q.n3-7-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 3. The store announces that the product is out of stock and cannot be delivered until the beginning of March, and asks the customer whether they would like to wait for delivery, cancel the order, or change to another color.
default.q.n3-7-q60-60.explanation:
**Email summary:**
Takiguchi Wallet Shop emailed its customer Terasaka to say that the brown leather wallet ordered through the website was out of stock because someone had placed a telephone order just beforehand. Delivery would not be possible until early March, but the customer could cancel the order or switch to another color for immediate shipment. The shop is asking how the customer would like to proceed.

**Question translation:**
Which of the following correctly reflects what this email is saying?

**Answer choices:**
1. Because the product is out of stock, it will be shipped in early March.
2. Because the product is out of stock, the customer is being asked to place the order again in early March.
3. Because the product is out of stock and delivery will take some time, the customer is being asked to say how they would like to proceed.
4. Because a product in the wrong color was mistakenly shipped, the product in the correct color will be sent immediately.
default.q.n3-7-q60-60.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the store is not deciding on its own to ship the item at the beginning of March; it is asking the customer whether they wish to continue waiting, as shown by 「いかがいたしましょうか」.
default.q.n3-7-q60-60.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage contains no information requiring customers to reorder the product at the beginning of March.
default.q.n3-7-q60-60.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: 「お届けできるのは3月上旬になってしまいますが、いかがいたしましょうか。キャンセルもお受けいたしますので、ご希望をお聞かせください。」 The customer can wait until early March, cancel the order, or change to a different color, so the store wants to know what the customer would like to do.
default.q.n3-7-q60-60.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the store had not shipped the item and had not sent the wrong color. The color ordered by the customer was out of stock, so the store suggested that it could ship immediately if the customer changed to another color.
default.q.n3-7-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The author wants to exchange old shoes for a discount coupon to use when buying new shoes at a lower price.
default.q.n3-7-q61-61.explanation:
Main point of the passage:
The author has several pairs of old shoes that are no longer worn and was planning to throw them away. However, after reading a flyer from a shoe store, the author learned about a program that exchanges old shoes for discount coupons to use at the store. The heat produced by burning the collected shoes is also used to generate electricity and protect the environment. The author initially thinks that bringing in just one person's shoes would not help the environment very much, but decides to take the old shoes to the store instead of throwing them away because this would make it possible to buy new shoes at a lower price.

Question translation:
Among the reasons why “I” want to take the old shoes to the store, what is the main reason?

Answer choice translations:
1. Because I want to exchange the old shoes for discount coupons to use when buying new shoes.
2. Because I want to sell the old shoes for money and use that money to buy new shoes.
3. Because I want to have the old shoes repaired and made presentable so I can wear them one more time.
4. Because I want the old shoes to be reused in a way that improves the environment.
default.q.n3-7-q61-61.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage says: 「私一人が持っていっても、環境にそんなに大きい影響はないと思うが、新しい靴が安く買えるなら、古い靴は捨てないで店に持っていこうと思った。」 Together with the flyer: 「いらない靴を店に持っていけば、その店で使える割引券と交換してくれるそうだ。」, this shows that the author's main motivation for bringing in the shoes was to receive a discount coupon and buy new shoes more cheaply.
default.q.n3-7-q61-61.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The store exchanges the shoes for a discount coupon (割引券), rather than buying the shoes back and paying cash (売ってお金をもらい).
default.q.n3-7-q61-61.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The author took the old shoes to exchange them for a discount coupon, not to have the store repair them so they could be worn again (きれいに直してもらって、もう一度履きたい).
default.q.n3-7-q61-61.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author states: 「私一人が持っていっても、環境にそんなに大きい影響はないと思うが」 (I do not think that one person's actions would have such a major impact on the environment), so environmental protection is not the main reason.
default.q.n3-7-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The voice of the announcer whom “I” used to listen to when I was in high school.
default.q.n3-7-q62-62.explanation:
- Main point and evidence: The author finds their father's old radio and, when they turn it on, hears a familiar voice from the past. Immediately afterward, the author clearly explains that it is the voice of the radio announcer who hosted a music program that the author greatly enjoyed while in high school.
- Translation of the question: Whose voice is the "nostalgic/familiar voice"?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. The father's voice when "I" was in high school.
  2. "My" own voice from when "I" was in high school.
  3. The voice of a singer whom "I" liked very much when "I" was in high school.
  4. The voice of the announcer whom "I" listened to when "I" was in high school.
default.q.n3-7-q62-62.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the old radio found in the cabinet belonged to the father («父の古いラジオ»); the voice coming from the radio program was not the father's voice.
default.q.n3-7-q62-62.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the voice coming from the radio belongs to the radio announcer, not the author's own voice recorded when the author was in high school.
default.q.n3-7-q62-62.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the writer only says that they loved the music program («大好きだったラジオの音楽番組»); the person speaking was the announcer («アナウンサー»), not a singer.
default.q.n3-7-q62-62.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because the passage clearly says: «スイッチを入れてみたら、①懐かしい声が流れてきた。高校生のころ、大好きだったラジオの音楽番組のアナウンサーだった。» (When I tried turning on the switch, a familiar voice came on. It was the announcer of a radio music program I had loved when I was in high school).
default.q.n3-7-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Radio allows listeners to receive a great deal of information even while doing other things.
default.q.n3-7-q63-63.explanation:
- Main point & evidence: Although the number of radio listeners is declining because of the Internet, people who drive or farm still listen to the radio regularly. The author recognizes radio's unique convenience: listeners can take in a great deal of information while doing something else. The author therefore decides to listen to the radio again while doing housework, such as cleaning and cooking.
- Question translation: Why does the author think, "I will listen to the radio again"?
- Answer choices:
  1. Because a radio is smaller than a television and can be placed nearby.
  2. Because the radio tells us more than the Internet does.
  3. Because the radio conveys not only new things but also things from the past.
  4. Because even while doing something else, we can learn a great deal of information through the radio.
default.q.n3-7-q63-63.why.0: (a) Answer choice 1 is incorrect because paragraph 2 only compares radio with television, saying that radio was more familiar and convenient during the author's school years («私にとってラジオはテレビよりも身近で便利なものだった»). It does not mention the radio's smaller size as a reason for listening to it again.
default.q.n3-7-q63-63.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is incorrect because paragraph 3 clearly states that fewer people listen to the radio because the Internet allows them to watch or listen to all kinds of news. The passage does not claim that the radio provides more information than the Internet.
default.q.n3-7-q63-63.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the passage does not mention the radio conveying both old and new information.
default.q.n3-7-q63-63.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because the author explains in the preceding sentence: «ほかのことをしながらでも、さまざまな情報が手に入るというラジオにしかない良さ、便利さがあるのだ。私も掃除や料理をするようなときには、②また、ラジオを聞こうと思った。» (Radio has its own unique advantage and convenience: you can obtain various information while doing other things. So I thought I would listen to the radio again while cleaning or cooking).
default.q.n3-7-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The good point or advantage of radio (ラジオの良さ).
default.q.n3-7-q64-64.explanation:
- Main point and evidence: From a memory of listening to the news on the radio while studying in high school to the present reality of drivers, farmers, and people doing housework still listening to the radio, the passage focuses on clarifying and affirming the unique advantages of radio («ラジオにしかない良さ、便利さ»).
- Question translation: What is the topic of this passage?
- Answer choices:
  1. The appeal of radio programs.
  2. The good points / advantages of radio.
  3. The length of radio's history.
  4. Skillful ways of using radio.
default.q.n3-7-q64-64.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the appeal of the music program is only one detail recalled from school days; it cannot encompass the entire content and message of the essay.
default.q.n3-7-q64-64.why.1: (b) Correct because throughout the passage, the author analyzes and emphasizes the distinctive appeal and convenience found only in radio («ほかのことをしながらでも、さまざまな情報が手に入るというラジオにしかない良さ、便利さがあるのだ»), highlighting the main theme: radio's strengths and advantages.
default.q.n3-7-q64-64.why.2: (c) Answer choice 3 is incorrect because the article only mentions the author’s father’s old radio, 「父の古いラジオ」, and the author’s memories from high school. It does not discuss the long-term history of radio’s development.
default.q.n3-7-q64-64.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage does not provide or share any tips or creative techniques for using the radio.
default.q.n3-7-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 1. The town organized the information session in order to recruit residents to move to and live in the town.
default.q.n3-7-q65-65.explanation:
- Main idea: The town's population was declining, so it held an information session in Tokyo to attract and recruit people who would move there and live there.
- Question translation: What was the purpose of the town's information session ①?
- Answer choices:
  1. To recruit people to move to and live in the town.
  2. To recruit town residents to help people who move there.
  3. To recruit specialists to advise on the town's agriculture.
  4. To recruit people to think together about how to increase the town's population.
default.q.n3-7-q65-65.why.0: (a) Correct. Paragraph 2 clearly states the purpose: 「その町では人口が減ったので、町民を募集するために説明会を聞いています（開いています）。」 (Because the town's population had declined, it held an information session to recruit people to move there and become residents).
default.q.n3-7-q65-65.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage does not mention recruiting current residents to help newcomers (「町民を募集する」means recruiting people to become residents, not recruiting helpers).
default.q.n3-7-q65-65.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage does not mention recruiting an agricultural consultant or expert who could offer advice (「アドバイスをしてくれる専門家」).
default.q.n3-7-q65-65.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The town wants to recruit people to move there and increase its population, not people to think of ways to increase the population (「どうしたらいいか、考えてくれる人」).
default.q.n3-7-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 4. What the failed cases have in common is that real life differed from their initial expectations, leaving them dissatisfied and disillusioned.
default.q.n3-7-q66-66.explanation:
- Main point: All the failed examples share one feature: the initial expectations about rural life were exciting, but the actual experience was boring, farm work was too difficult, or village duties such as monthly cleanup were too bothersome. This led to dissatisfaction, dislike, or a return to the city.
- Question translation: The phrase ② “a common point” appears in the passage. What kind of point can it be considered?
- Answer choices:
  1. They cannot live the life they expected, but they continue enduring it.
  2. They have been able to live the life they expected and are living happily.
  3. Their actual life differs from their expectations, but they are still satisfied.
  4. Their actual life differs from their expectations, and they feel dissatisfied.
default.q.n3-7-q66-66.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage describes people becoming bored and giving up or moving back to the city (「すぐに退屈な毎日が嫌になった」「都会に戻ってしまった」), not enduring the situation and continuing to live there (「我慢して生活している」).
default.q.n3-7-q66-66.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The examples listed are cases that did not go smoothly or ended in failure (「うまくいかなかった例」), which is the complete opposite of achieving the expected life and living happily (「楽しく生活ができている」).
default.q.n3-7-q66-66.why.2: (c) Incorrect. These people felt fed up (「嫌になった」), found it far too difficult (「あまりにも大変で」), and considered it troublesome (「めんどうくさい」), not “satisfied” (「満足している」).
default.q.n3-7-q66-66.why.3: (d) Correct. Paragraph 3 lists several cases: someone admires rural life but becomes fed up soon after moving there (「田舎の生活にあこがれて引っ越して来ましたが、すぐに退屈な毎日が嫌になった」), someone wants to farm but returns to the city because it is too demanding (「農業がしたくて来たのにあまりにも大変で、都会に戻ってしまった」), and someone finds monthly cleaning troublesome (「めんどうくさい」). The common point is that reality differs greatly from expectations, resulting in disappointment and dissatisfaction.
default.q.n3-7-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 3. The narrator thinks it is necessary to take possible failures into account, investigate thoroughly, and make a solid plan to achieve the dream.
default.q.n3-7-q67-67.explanation:
- Main point: After hearing about cases of failure, the author realized that they had previously thought too simply because they had focused only on success. However, the author does not give up on the dream and wants to prepare carefully, learn more, and make a thorough plan that takes possible difficulties and failures into account.
- Question translation: After attending the information session, what did “I” think about my dream?
- Answer choices:
  1. Because there were so many examples of failure, it would probably be better to give up on pursuing the dream.
  2. Because “I” had learned about examples of failure, “I” wanted to reconsider whether to pursue it.
  3. Taking possible failures into account, “I” wanted to make a very thorough plan to pursue it.
  4. Because there were more examples of success than failure, “I” wanted to pursue it immediately without worrying about the examples of failure.
default.q.n3-7-q67-67.why.0: (a) Incorrect. At the end, the author clearly says 「でも、夢はあきらめたくないので」(But because I do not want to give up on my dream), which contradicts “it would probably be better to give up” (「あきらめたほうがよさそうだ」).
default.q.n3-7-q67-67.why.1: (b) Incorrect. This choice says “want to consider whether to carry it out” (「実行するかしないかを検討したい」), whereas the author has already decided to do it and wants to try to make it possible (「実行できるように頑張りたい」).
default.q.n3-7-q67-67.why.2: (c) Correct. The final paragraph states: 「成功例ばかり見ていた私たちは、考えが甘かったようです。でも、夢はあきらめたくないので、よく調べて、計画を立てて、実行できるように頑張りたいと思います。」 (We seem to have been naïve to look only at examples of success. But we do not want to give up on our dream, so we want to research carefully, make a plan, and work hard to carry it out.) This means that failures must also be considered in order to create a solid plan.
default.q.n3-7-q67-67.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author realizes that they had been naive in looking only at successful cases (「成功例ばかり見ていた私たちは、考えが甘かった」) and therefore need to investigate carefully, not "ignore failure cases and put it into practice immediately" (「失敗例は気にせずにすぐ実行したい」).
default.q.n3-7-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The condition of being unable to fall asleep for a long time even after getting into bed remains unchanged.
default.q.n3-7-q68-68.explanation:
- Main point: The author had a problem with being unable to fall asleep for a long time after getting into bed, which shortened their sleep and made them sleepy during the day. Thinking that exercise would make them tired enough to fall asleep immediately, the author jogged for one hour before bed. However, after doing this for two weeks, the difficulty sleeping had not changed at all.
- Question translation: The passage says that it "had not changed at all." What had not changed?
- Answer choices:
  1. The fact that the author still could not fall asleep for a long time after getting into bed.
  2. The fact that the author could not sleep without exercising.
  3. The fact that the author could not wake up on time in the morning.
  4. The fact that the author could not keep running for a certain amount of time.
default.q.n3-7-q68-68.why.0: (a) Correct because paragraph 1 clearly states: 「最近、私は布団に入ってもしばらく眠れなくて、悩んでいる。...体が疲れるまで運動をすれば、布団に入ってすぐに眠くなるだろうと考えて、寝る1時間前に走ることにした。だが、2週間続けてみても、①全然変わらない。」 Even after running one hour before bed for two weeks, the author's inability to fall asleep promptly after getting into bed had not changed.
default.q.n3-7-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author had already had trouble sleeping and deliberately tried exercising to sleep more easily, rather than meaning “if I do not exercise, I cannot sleep.”
default.q.n3-7-q68-68.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage says that the author still has to get up at a set time in the morning (「朝は決まった時間に起きなければならない」), not that they are unable to get up.
default.q.n3-7-q68-68.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not mention that the author was unable to continue running within the allotted time.
default.q.n3-7-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 2: First, it raises the body’s core temperature, thereby creating a state in which the core temperature falls.
default.q.n3-7-q69-69.explanation:
- Main point: To fall asleep easily, changes in core body temperature are very important. When the body is warmed all the way to its core (for example, by taking a warm bath or going for a light run 2–3 hours before bedtime), it begins releasing heat through the surface, causing the core temperature to drop. This drop in core temperature helps people fall asleep.
- Question translation: The passage states, "Changes in core body temperature are important." What should one do to bring about this change?
- Answer choices:
  1. First lower the core body temperature, thereby creating a state in which the core temperature rises.
  2. First raise the core body temperature, thereby creating a state in which the core temperature falls.
  3. Raise the core body temperature, thereby creating a state in which the core temperature does not fall from a fixed level.
  4. Raise and lower the core body temperature, thereby creating a state in which the core temperature changes continuously.
default.q.n3-7-q69-69.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the correct process is to warm the central part first, causing its temperature to rise first, rather than lowering the central temperature first (「まず下げる」).
default.q.n3-7-q69-69.why.1: (b) Correct because Paragraph 2 states: 「こうすることで、体が中心まで温まる。すると、体は表面から熱を出そうとする。表面から熱が出ていくと、中心の温度が下がっていく。このようにして、中心の温度が下がる状態を作ると、人は眠りやすくなるのだそうだ。」 (First warming the body to its core causes heat to escape from the surface, which lowers the core temperature.)
default.q.n3-7-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the goal is to lower the temperature at the center (「中心の温度が下がっていく」), not to keep the temperature from falling (「下がらない状態を作る」).
default.q.n3-7-q69-69.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the mechanism is to raise the body's core temperature and then let it gradually fall to induce sleepiness, not to keep raising and lowering it so that the temperature changes continuously (「変化し続ける」).
default.q.n3-7-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Exercise until your body feels tired, one hour before going to bed.
default.q.n3-7-q70-70.explanation:
- Main point: The author thought that exercising until the body was tired would make it easy to fall asleep, so they went jogging for an hour before bedtime. However, the book explained that strenuous exercise immediately before bed makes the mind alert and has the opposite effect. Therefore, the author's mistake was exercising to exhaustion one hour before going to bed.
- Question translation: What did "I" do wrong?
- Answer choices:
  1. Exercising until the body was tired one hour before going to bed.
  2. Doing light exercise one hour before going to bed.
  3. Exercising until the body was tired two or three hours before going to bed.
  4. Doing light exercise two or three hours before going to bed.
default.q.n3-7-q70-70.why.0: (a) Correct because paragraphs 1 and 3 clearly state:「体が疲れるまで運動をすれば...寝る1時間前に走ることにした。...寝る直前に運動しすぎたり...逆効果らしい。つまり、私のやっていたことは間違いだったのだ。」(The author ran until tired one hour before going to bed—both too close to bedtime and too strenuous.)
default.q.n3-7-q70-70.why.1: (b) Wrong because the author ran until becoming exhausted (「体が疲れるまで」), rather than doing light exercise (「軽い運動」).
default.q.n3-7-q70-70.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the author did it one hour before going to bed (「寝る1時間前に」), not two or three hours before bedtime.
default.q.n3-7-q70-70.why.3: (d) Incorrect because doing light exercise 2–3 hours before bedtime is the recommended method (「寝る2、3時間前に軽く走ったり...いいそうだ」), not something the author did wrong.
default.q.n3-7-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Take a leisurely soak in a warm bath, then go to bed.
default.q.n3-7-q71-71.explanation:
- Main idea: The author is afraid of running alone at night and does not like exercising either. After learning that, besides exercising, there is another effective way to fall asleep more easily—taking a leisurely warm bath 2–3 hours before going to bed—the author is delighted and decides to start taking warm baths from now on.
- Question translation: Which choice is most appropriate for filling in the blank ( )?
- Choice translations:
  1. Wake up later.
  2. Just get into bed and wait until you naturally feel sleepy.
  3. Take a leisurely warm bath and then go to bed.
  4. Go for a light jog and then go to bed.
default.q.n3-7-q71-71.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the first paragraph states that the author must get up at a fixed time in the morning (「朝は決まった時間に起きなければならない」); the author does not intend to postpone the wake-up time.
default.q.n3-7-q71-71.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author is actively looking for a solution to make it easier to sleep, rather than simply waiting to become sleepy naturally.
default.q.n3-7-q71-71.why.2: (c) Correct, as shown by quotations from paragraphs 2 and 4: 「ぬるめの風呂にゆっくり入ったりするといいそうだ。」and「実は運動も好きではない。運動以外にいい方法があると知ってうれしくなった。これからは、( )と思う。」 (The author does not like exercise and is pleased to learn that leisurely soaking in a warm bath is an effective alternative.)
default.q.n3-7-q71-71.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the author was afraid of running alone at night and did not like exercise (「夜に一人で走るのは少レ怖いと思っていたし、実は運動も好きではない」), so they would not choose jogging.
default.q.n3-7-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The grandmother kindly taught the author the rules of the neighborhood and the convenience store.
default.q.n3-7-q72-72.explanation:
Main point: When the author brought sweets as a return gift, the elderly neighbor was very happy and kindly explained the neighborhood's garbage-disposal rules as well as the nearby convenience store.

Question translation:
What did the elderly woman do when "I" brought sweets to thank her?

Answer choices:
1. She helped clean the apartment.
2. She kindly explained the rules of the neighborhood and the convenience store. (Correct)
3. She invited me to go shopping at a nearby supermarket.
4. She gave me another type of vegetable grown in her garden.
default.q.n3-7-q72-72.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage does not mention the grandmother helping clean the apartment.
default.q.n3-7-q72-72.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because paragraph 2 clearly states: 「すると、おばあさんはとても喜んでくれ、街のゴミ出しのルールや近くの便利なスーパーについて親切に教えてくれた。」 (Then the elderly woman was very pleased and kindly explained the neighborhood's garbage-disposal rules and the nearby convenient supermarket.)
default.q.n3-7-q72-72.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the grandmother only gave directions to a nearby supermarket; she did not invite the author to go shopping together.
default.q.n3-7-q72-72.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the grandmother did not give the author any additional type of vegetable when the author came to thank her.
default.q.n3-7-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Having a mutually supportive relationship with one's neighbors provides a strong sense of security when living alone.
default.q.n3-7-q73-73.explanation:
Main point: The author used to think that not interacting with the neighbors would provide more freedom and comfort. However, after receiving vegetables and help from an elderly neighbor, the author realized that having a mutually supportive relationship to rely on in difficult times brings great peace of mind when living alone.

Question translation:
What does “I” most want to convey in this passage?

Answer choices:
1. When living alone, it is best to live close to your workplace.
2. When receiving something from a neighbor, you must return the favor with an expensive gift that same day.
3. Not getting involved with your neighbors allows you to enjoy more free time for yourself.
4. Having a mutually supportive relationship with your neighbors brings peace of mind when living alone. (Correct)
default.q.n3-7-q73-73.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because moving to an apartment near the company is only the opening context, not the message the author intends to convey.
default.q.n3-7-q73-73.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the passage never says that an expensive gift must be reciprocated on the same day.
default.q.n3-7-q73-73.why.2: (c) Answer choice 3 is incorrect because this was the author's former way of thinking (「以前の私は、近所の人と関わらないほうが自由で楽だと思い込んでいた」), not something the author realized and wants to convey now.
default.q.n3-7-q73-73.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because the final paragraph clearly expresses the author’s realization and message: 「しかし、今回のことで、困ったときに助け合える関係があることは、一人暮らしの大きな安心感につながると気がついた。」 (However, through this experience, I realized that having relationships in which people help one another in difficult times leads to a great sense of security when living alone).
default.q.n3-7-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 2. ようき.
default.q.n3-7-q1-1.explanation:
- Meaning: This store sells many different kinds of containers.
- Sino-Japanese roots: 容器 (container, receptacle).
- Example: プラスチックの容器に食べ物を入れる。(Put the food in a plastic container.)
default.q.n3-7-q1-1.why.0: (a) 「ようぎ」is incorrect because the kanji 「器」has the on-reading 「き」, which does not undergo voicing to become 「ぎ」(the word 「容疑」, meaning suspicion or suspect, is read ようぎ).
default.q.n3-7-q1-1.why.1: (b) 「ようき」is correct. 「容」is read as よう and「器」as き, forming「容器」(ようき: container, receptacle).
default.q.n3-7-q1-1.why.2: (c) 「どうぐ」 is incorrect; this is the reading of 「道具」, meaning tools or equipment.
default.q.n3-7-q1-1.why.3: (d) 「どうく」is incorrect because both kanji are given the wrong on-reading, and the resulting expression has no meaning.
default.q.n3-7-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 1. くらべた.
default.q.n3-7-q2-2.explanation:
- Translation: "What did Mr./Ms. Yamamoto compare with what?"
- 比べる means to compare or contrast.
- Example: 兄と弟の背を比べる。(Compare the heights of the older and younger brothers.)
default.q.n3-7-q2-2.why.0: (a) 「くらべた」is correct. The verb「比べる」(くらべる, to compare) changes to「くらべた」in the past form.
default.q.n3-7-q2-2.why.1: (b) 「ならべた」 is incorrect. It is the past form of the verb 「並べる」 (to arrange, lay out).
default.q.n3-7-q2-2.why.2: (c) 「しらべた」is incorrect. It is the past form of the verb 「調べる」(look up; investigate).
default.q.n3-7-q2-2.why.3: (d) 「えらべた」 is incorrect. It is the past potential form of 「選ぶ」, meaning “was able to choose.”
default.q.n3-7-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 3. ふくすう.
default.q.n3-7-q3-3.explanation:
- Translation: There are many documents, so please be careful not to mix them up.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 複数 (FUKUSŪ — plural, multiple).
- Example: この問題には複数の答えがある。(This question has multiple answers.)
default.q.n3-7-q3-3.why.0: (a) 「ふくす」is incorrect because the on-reading of 「数」is すう (with a long vowel), not す.
default.q.n3-7-q3-3.why.1: (b) 「ふうすう」 is incorrect because 複 (fuku) is read with a short vowel, not the long vowel ふう.
default.q.n3-7-q3-3.why.2: (c) 「ふくすう」 is correct. 「複」 is read as ふく and 「数」 as すう → 「複数」 (ふくすう: plural, multiple).
default.q.n3-7-q3-3.why.3: (d) 「ふうす」 has incorrect readings for both 「複」 and 「数」.
default.q.n3-7-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 1. けつあつ.
default.q.n3-7-q4-4.explanation:
- Translation: Yesterday, I had my blood pressure measured at the hospital.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 血圧 (KETSUATSU — blood pressure).
- Example: 毎朝血圧を測る習慣がある。(I have a habit of checking my blood pressure every morning.)
default.q.n3-7-q4-4.why.0: (a) 「けつあつ」is correct. 血 has the on-reading けつ, and 圧 has the on-reading あつ, forming 「血圧」(けつあつ: blood pressure).
default.q.n3-7-q4-4.why.1: (b) 「けつやつ」 is incorrect because 「圧」 is read あつ, not やつ.
default.q.n3-7-q4-4.why.2: (c) ちあつ is incorrect because「血」is being misread with the kun-reading ち instead of the on-reading けつ used in Sino-Japanese compounds.
default.q.n3-7-q4-4.why.3: (d) 「ちやつ」is incorrect because the sounds of both kanji are misread.
default.q.n3-7-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ゆうひ.
default.q.n3-7-q5-5.explanation:
- Meaning: The sunset seen from here is beautiful.
- 夕日: setting sun, evening sunlight, sunset.
- Example: 夕日が海に沈んでいく。(The setting sun is gradually sinking into the sea.)
default.q.n3-7-q5-5.why.0: (a) 「ゆび」 is incorrect because 「夕」 lacks the long vowel (it should be ゆう), and 「日」 does not undergo the sound change to び here; the word 「指」 is read ゆび, meaning “finger.”
default.q.n3-7-q5-5.why.1: (b) 「ゆひ」is incorrect because 「夕」requires the long vowel ゆう.
default.q.n3-7-q5-5.why.2: (c) 「ゆうび」 is incorrect because the 「日」 in 「夕日」 retains the reading ひ and does not change to び (「優美」 is read ゆうび and means graceful or elegant).
default.q.n3-7-q5-5.why.3: (d) 「ゆうひ」is correct. 「夕」is read ゆう and「日」is read ひ, giving「夕日」(ゆうひ: evening sun, setting sun).
default.q.n3-7-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 4. むずかしい.
default.q.n3-7-q6-6.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: I think it would be very difficult to go there alone.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 難しい (difficult).
- Example: 日本語の漢字を覚えるのは難しい。(Memorizing Japanese kanji is difficult.)
default.q.n3-7-q6-6.why.0: (a) 「きびしい」is incorrect; this is the reading of the adjective 「厳しい」, meaning strict or harsh.
default.q.n3-7-q6-6.why.1: (b) 「めずらしい」 is incorrect; this is the reading of the adjective 「珍しい」 (rare, unusual, novel).
default.q.n3-7-q6-6.why.2: (c) 「さびしい」is incorrect; it is the reading of the adjective 「寂しい」(lonely, sad).
default.q.n3-7-q6-6.why.3: (d) 「むずかしい」 is correct. The kanji 「難」 (nan) in the i-adjective 「難しい」 has the native Japanese reading むずかしい (difficult, complicated).
default.q.n3-7-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 3. けん.
default.q.n3-7-q7-7.explanation:
- Meaning: There was a phone call from Mr./Ms. Nakamura regarding a business trip.
- Kanji note: 件 means a matter, issue, or case.
- Example: 先週の会議の件について確認したいです。(I would like to confirm something regarding last week’s meeting.)
default.q.n3-7-q7-7.why.0: (a) 「けい」 is incorrect because the nasal ん in 「件」 is missing; its on-reading is けん.
default.q.n3-7-q7-7.why.1: (b) 「よう」is incorrect; this is the reading of 「用」(business, an errand), not 「件」.
default.q.n3-7-q7-7.why.2: (c) 「けん」 is correct. The kanji 「件」 has the on-reading けん (ken: a matter, case, or issue).
default.q.n3-7-q7-7.why.3: (d) 「よん」 is the reading of the number 4 (四), so it is unrelated to 「件」.
default.q.n3-7-q8-8.verdict: The correct answer is 2. おうだん.
default.q.n3-7-q8-8.explanation:
- Meaning: Please be careful when crossing here.
- 横断: crossing, traversing.
- Example: 横断歩道を渡りましょう。(Let's cross at the pedestrian crossing.)
default.q.n3-7-q8-8.why.0: (a) 「おうざん」 is incorrect because 「断」 is read だん (dan), not ざん (zan).
default.q.n3-7-q8-8.why.1: (b) 「おうだん」 is correct. 「横」 is read おう in on-reading, and 「断」 is read だん in on-reading, giving 「横断」 (おうだん: cross, traverse).
default.q.n3-7-q8-8.why.2: (c) きだん is incorrect because the reading of「横」was misread (it should be おう).
default.q.n3-7-q9-9.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 吸った because the verb 吸う (すう - to inhale, smoke) forms its past tense as 吸った (すった).
default.q.n3-7-q9-9.explanation:
Meaning: “I got out of the car and breathed in the outside air.”
- Kanji: 吸 (きゅう; 吸う: to inhale or suck in, 呼吸: respiration, 吸収: absorption).
- Example: 深呼吸をして、新鮮な空気をたくさん吸った。(I took a deep breath and inhaled plenty of fresh air.)
default.q.n3-7-q9-9.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 吹 is used in the verb 吹く (ふく: to blow), whose past form is 吹いた (ふいた), not 吹った.

• Example: 試験の結果が出るまで不安でたまらない。(I’m extremely anxious until the exam results come out.)
default.q.n3-7-q29-29.why.0: (a) 賛成 (さんせい): Agreement or approval, not a word describing anxiety.
default.q.n3-7-q29-29.why.1: (b) 大変 (たいへん): difficult, hard, or serious; it does not mean feeling uneasy or worried.

default.q.n3-7-q29-29.why.3: (d) 反対 (はんたい): opposition, contrary; it does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-7-q30-30.explanation:
Meaning: As for the schedule, please ask Mr./Ms. Kawai.
• スケジュール (schedule): schedule, timetable, plan.
• 予定 (よてい): plan, schedule, intention.
• Example: 今週のスケジュールを確認する。(I check this week's schedule or plans.)
default.q.n3-7-q30-30.why.0: (a) 行き方 (いきかた) means “how to get somewhere” or “the way to a place,” not “schedule.”
default.q.n3-7-q30-30.why.1: (b) 理由 (りゆう – reason): cause or reason; it does not mean a plan or schedule.
