default.q.n3-8-q29-29.why.2: (c) 「簡単に」(かんたんに) means “simply” or “briefly,” which contrasts with explaining something in detail.
default.q.n3-8-q29-29.why.3: (d) 「熱心に」(ねっしんに) means enthusiastically or earnestly, describing the attitude toward performing an action, not the level of detail in the content.
default.q.n3-8-q30-30.explanation:
- Meaning: 「諦める」（あきらめる）is a transitive verb meaning "to give up" or "to abandon," that is, to stop pursuing a plan, goal, or hope because circumstances make it impossible or impractical.
- Usage: It commonly takes a noun referring to a dream, goal, plan, or activity, or a dictionary-form verb + の／こと: 夢／希望／進学／計画／登山を諦める.
- Example: どんなに困難でも、自分の夢を諦めてはいけません。(No matter how difficult it is, you must not give up on your dreams.)
default.q.n3-8-q30-30.why.0: Incorrect because for an item such as an umbrella that one is carrying, when there is no need to take it along, 「持っていかなくて」 or 「やめて」 should be used; 「諦める」 means giving up a goal or hope.
default.q.n3-8-q30-30.why.1: Correct because 「登山を諦める」 accurately expresses giving up or canceling a plan to climb a mountain because of a storm.
default.q.n3-8-q30-30.why.2: Incorrect because the context means “forgot to put on glasses” when leaving home, so 「忘れた」 must be used, not 「諦めた」.
default.q.n3-8-q30-30.why.3: Incorrect because, in the context of being unable to hold back tears while reading a sad story, 「泣くのを我慢できなかった / 止められなかった」 must be used, not 「諦められなかった」.
default.q.n3-8-q31-31.explanation:
- Meaning: 「参加」（さんか）is a noun and a する-verb meaning “to participate in” or “to take part in” an event, group activity, organization, seminar, party, and so on.
- Usage: The common pattern is 「〜に参加する」 (パーティー／試合／会議／ボランティア／ツアーに参加する).
- Example: 来週の日本語スピーチコンテストに参加する予定です。(I plan to participate in next week's Japanese speech contest.)
default.q.n3-8-q31-31.why.0: Incorrect because when a newborn family member joins the family, use 「家族に加わった / 家族が増えて」, not 「参加した」.
default.q.n3-8-q31-31.why.1: Incorrect. For encountering an accident or incident, use「事故に遭って（あって）」; never use「事故に参加して」.
default.q.n3-8-q31-31.why.2: Correct because 「パーティーに参加する」 is a completely standard and natural collocation meaning “participate in a party.”
default.q.n3-8-q31-31.why.3: Incorrect. For working at a company, use「貿易会社に勤めている / 勤務している」, not「参加している」.
default.q.n3-8-q32-32.explanation:
- Meaning: 「盛ん」（さかん）is a na-adjective meaning “popular,” “thriving,” or “active.” It describes activities, movements, exchanges, industries, or discussions taking place vigorously or extensively.
- Usage: It commonly appears with nouns such as 交流、貿易、スポーツ、議論 (交流が盛んだ, 盛んな活動).
- Example: この地域は昔から農業や伝統工芸が盛んです。(Agriculture and traditional crafts have flourished in this area since long ago.)
default.q.n3-8-q32-32.why.0: Incorrect because to express that the practice time is long or plentiful, use 「練習時間が長い / たっぷりある」, not 「盛んだ」.
default.q.n3-8-q32-32.why.1: Incorrect because when there is a large amount of luggage or belongings, use 「荷物が多い」, not 「盛んだ」.
default.q.n3-8-q32-32.why.2: Incorrect because fresh or abundant food/ingredients are described with 「新鮮で / 豊富で」, not 「盛んで」.
default.q.n3-8-q32-32.why.3: Correct because 「交流が盛んだ」 (“interaction is active and thriving”) is a highly standard and common collocation.
default.q.n3-8-q33-33.explanation:
- Meaning: 「整理」（せいり）is a noun and a Group 3 verb meaning to arrange, organize, tidy up, or put things in order, as well as to remove unnecessary items, such as belongings, documents, information, thoughts, or feelings.
- Usage: Commonly used with 引き出し／部屋／書類／情報を整理する and 気持ちの整理をつける.
- Example: 引っ越しをする前に、本棚の本や書類を整理した。(Before moving, I organized the books and documents on the bookshelf.)
default.q.n3-8-q33-33.why.0: Correct because 「机の引き出しを整理する」 (tidying and reorganizing a desk drawer and throwing away unnecessary items) is a perfect usage context for 「整理」.
default.q.n3-8-q33-33.why.1: Incorrect because when a hallway is dirty and is cleaned with a cloth, the appropriate expressions are 「掃除しました」 or 「拭きました」, not 「整理しました」.
default.q.n3-8-q33-33.why.2: Incorrect because opening a window to let fresh air into a room means 「空気を入れ換えた / 換気した」, not「整理した」.
default.q.n3-8-q33-33.why.3: Incorrect because brushing one’s teeth or cleaning the mouth after a meal is expressed with 「歯を磨いている」, not 「整理している」.
default.q.n3-8-q34-34.explanation:
- Meaning: 「通り過ぎる」（とおりすぎる）is an intransitive verb meaning “to pass by,” “to go past,” or “to pass through” a specific place without stopping.
- Usage: It commonly combines with a specific location: 〜の前／駅／交差点を通り過ぎる. Distinguish it from 「過ぎる」: 「通り過ぎる」is used mainly for physical movement through space, while 「過ぎる」is used for the passage of time, exceeding a degree, or being past a deadline.
- Example: 電車の中で居眠りをしてしまい、目的の駅を通り過ぎてしまった。(I fell asleep on the train and passed the station where I was supposed to get off.)
default.q.n3-8-q34-34.why.0: Correct because 「店の前を通り過ぎる」 (to pass by or drive past in front of the store) correctly uses the spatial-motion meaning of 「通り過ぎる」.
default.q.n3-8-q34-34.why.1: Incorrect: When the appointment time has passed, use 「（時間を）過ぎてしまった」, not 「通り過ぎる」.
default.q.n3-8-q34-34.why.2: Incorrect. Eating too much rice and becoming uncomfortably full is expressed with 「ご飯を食べ過ぎて」or 「ご飯の量が多すぎて」, not 「通り過ぎて」.
default.q.n3-8-q34-34.why.3: Incorrect. For not missing a document-submission deadline, use「締め切りを過ぎないように」, not「通り過ぎる」.
default.q.n3-9-q36-36.verdict: The correct answer is 3. を (the expression 〜顔をする describes a person’s facial expression or look).
default.q.n3-9-q36-36.explanation:
Meaning: After a long time, my mother finally spoke on the phone with my older brother, who is studying abroad, and she had a very happy-looking expression.
The kanji 母 means mother, 留学 means studying abroad, 兄 means older brother, 電話 means telephone, 話 means talk, and 顔 means face.
Example: 彼女は悲しそうな顔をして部屋を出て行った。(She left the room with a sad expression on her face.)
default.q.n3-9-q36-36.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the particle 「へ」 indicates the direction of movement and does not go with 「顔（ ）する」.
default.q.n3-9-q36-36.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「が」 commonly accompanies i-adjectives describing fixed characteristics. It does not go with 「していた」 to express a subject's temporary facial expression or emotion.
default.q.n3-9-q36-36.why.2: (c) Correct because the expression 「〜顔（かお）をする」describes someone showing a particular facial expression or look (うれしそうな顔をしていた: had a happy-looking expression).
default.q.n3-9-q36-36.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the particle 「の」 connects two nouns and does not come before the verb 「していた」.
default.q.n3-9-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ついに (an adverb meaning “finally,” describing a result achieved after a long period of time).
default.q.n3-9-q37-37.explanation:
Meaning: ABC Building had been under construction for a long time, and yesterday it was finally completed.
Kanji readings: 長 (long), 間 (period of time), 建設中 (under construction), 昨日 (yesterday), 完成 (completion).
Example: 何年も研究を重ねて、ついに新薬の開発に成功した。(After years of research, we finally succeeded in developing a new drug.)
default.q.n3-9-q37-37.why.0: (a) Incorrect because「ずっと」means “continuously” or “by far,” expressing a prolonged state or comparison; it does not naturally combine with a completed result such as「完成した」.
default.q.n3-9-q37-37.why.1: (b) Incorrect because「今にも」means “be about to” or “seem ready to,” and is usually used with the sentence ending「〜そうだ」to describe something about to happen.
default.q.n3-9-q37-37.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「次第に」 means “gradually; little by little,” indicating a step-by-step change. It does not fit a definite completion at a specific point in time (昨日).
default.q.n3-9-q37-37.why.3: (d) Correct because「ついに」means “finally” and describes an expected result that occurs after a long period of waiting or effort (長い間...ついに完成した).
default.q.n3-9-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 2. からなら, combining the starting point 「から」 with the conditional 「なら」: “if it is from... then...”.
default.q.n3-9-q38-38.explanation:
Meaning:
Shop manager: "Ooshita, I'm sorry for asking you at such short notice, but can you work tomorrow?"
Ooshita: "I can work from the afternoon. Would that be okay?"
Shop manager: "Thank you. I appreciate your help."
Vocabulary: 店長 (shop manager), 出勤 (going to work, reporting for work), 午後 (afternoon), 大丈夫 (all right, okay).
Example: 明日は忙しいですが、夕方からなら時間が取れます。(I am busy tomorrow, but I can make time from the evening onward.)
default.q.n3-9-q38-38.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the particle 「で」 is not used to indicate the starting time of a work shift; 「から」 is used instead.
default.q.n3-9-q38-38.why.1: (b) Correct because 「〜からなら」 combines the starting point 「から」 (from the afternoon) with 「なら」 (if it is...), creating a logical conditional sentence: if it is from the afternoon, I can go to work.
default.q.n3-9-q38-38.why.2: (c) Incorrect because「へ」indicates direction and「でも」means “even” or introduces an example; together they do not create a logical meaning in this sentence.
default.q.n3-9-q38-38.why.3: (d) Wrong because 「まで」indicates an endpoint (“up to” or “until”), which does not fit the context of wanting to accept work from the afternoon onward.
default.q.n3-9-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 4. において is a formal grammar pattern indicating the place where an event takes place.
default.q.n3-9-q39-39.explanation:
Meaning: The concert will be held at Sakura Plaza from 11:00 tomorrow.
Sino-Japanese terms: 音楽会 (concert), 広場 (plaza, square), 開 (to open; to hold an event).
Example: 入学式は体育館において行われます。(The entrance ceremony will be held in the gymnasium.)
default.q.n3-9-q39-39.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜に対して」 means “toward,” “regarding,” or “in contrast to,” and is not used to indicate the location where an event is held.
default.q.n3-9-q39-39.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「〜によって」means “by whom,” “due to what cause,” or “depending on,” and is not used to indicate the location where something is held.
default.q.n3-9-q39-39.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜について」 means “about” a topic or content and does not combine with a place noun such as 「さくら広場」.
default.q.n3-9-q39-39.why.3: (d) Correct because 「〜において」is a formal equivalent of 「で」in written language or announcements, used to indicate the location where an event takes place.
default.q.n3-9-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 1. たびに (the structure V-る + たびに means “whenever ...; every time ...”).
default.q.n3-9-q40-40.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: My older sister had a baby last year. I visit about once every two or three months, but each time I see the baby, it has grown more, which amazes me.
Kanji readings and meanings: 去年 (きょねん; last year), 姉 (あね; older sister), 子供 (こども; child), 生 (せい; be born), 回 (かい; time, occurrence), 会 (かい; meet).
Example: この写真を見るたびに、楽しかった学生時代を思い出す。(Every time I look at this picture, I remember my enjoyable school days.)
default.q.n3-9-q40-40.why.0: (a) Correct because the pattern 「V-る + たびに」means “whenever...,” expressing that each time the speaker meets the child, they notice the child has grown or changed.
default.q.n3-9-q40-40.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「〜うちに」 means “while / before the state changes,” which does not fit a context involving an action repeated many times.
default.q.n3-9-q40-40.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜間に」 means that another event occurs during the period when an action is taking place. It does not combine with a verb denoting a repeated point-in-time event, such as 「会う」.
default.q.n3-9-q40-40.why.3: (d) Incorrect because「〜前に」means “before,” so it does not express something gradually becoming greater with each encounter.
default.q.n3-9-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 使い (V-masu stem) + 続ける expresses an action that continues without interruption.
default.q.n3-9-q41-41.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: I have continued using this handbag from ten years ago up to the present.
Kanji components: 私 (I), 年前 (years ago), 同 (same), 使 (use), 続 (continue).
Example: 雨が降っても、彼は走り続けた。(Even though it started raining, he continued running.)
default.q.n3-9-q41-41.why.0: (a) Incorrect because verbs combined with 「〜続ける」must be in the continuative form (V-masu without masu), not the dictionary form 「使う」.
default.q.n3-9-q41-41.why.1: (b) Correct because 「使い」is the ます-stem of 「使う」, forming 「使い続けている」, meaning “to continue using” or “to use continuously.”
default.q.n3-9-q41-41.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「使おう」is the volitional form (V-よう), which cannot be combined with 「〜続ける」.
default.q.n3-9-q41-41.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「使った」 is the ta-form (past), which cannot be combined with 「〜続ける」.
default.q.n3-9-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 走ってくるのが (This combines the movement direction toward the speaker 「てくる」with the nominalizer 「の」before the sensory verb 「見えました」).
default.q.n3-9-q42-42.explanation:
Meaning: I saw Tanaka running toward me.
On’yomi: 方 (direction, side), 走 (to run), 見 (to see).
Grammar rule: When a sensory verb (見えます, 聞こえます, etc.) describes an action directly observed or heard by the speaker, 「の」is used to nominalize the clause instead of 「こと」.
Example: 星が空に光っているのが見えます。(I can see the stars shining in the sky.)
default.q.n3-9-q42-42.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜ていく」describes movement away from the speaker, whereas the prompt says 「わたしの方に」(toward me). Also, before the sensory verb 「見えました」, 「の」must nominalize the action, not 「こと」.
default.q.n3-9-q42-42.why.1: (b) Incorrect because with verbs describing direct sensory perception through sight, such as 「見えました」, 「の」 must be used rather than 「こと」 to nominalize the phrase.
default.q.n3-9-q42-42.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「走っていく」indicates running away from the speaker, which is the opposite of the context, where the person is moving toward the speaker (「わたしの方に」).
default.q.n3-9-q42-42.why.3: (d) Correct because 「走ってくる」 expresses running toward the speaker, and 「の」 nominalizes the action directly observed with the eyes before the sensory verb 「見えました」.
default.q.n3-9-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 出られるように (The structure potential form + ようになる expresses a change in ability: becoming able to do something.)
default.q.n3-9-q43-43.explanation:
Sentence meaning:
Yamada: “John, do you practice basketball every day?”
John: “Yes. I want to be able to play in a game soon.”
Sino-Japanese reading notes: 毎日 (every day), 練習, 早 (early/soon), 試合 (game/match), 出 (to go out/participate).
Example: 日本語で上手に会話ができるようになりたいです。(I want to be able to converse fluently in Japanese.)
default.q.n3-9-q43-43.why.0: (a) Correct because 「出られる」is the potential form of 「出る」. Combined with 「〜ようになる」, 「出られるようになりたい」means “I want to become able to compete on the field.”
default.q.n3-9-q43-43.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「〜ために」expresses purpose and does not combine with 「〜なりたい」to indicate a change in one’s ability.
default.q.n3-9-q43-43.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「出させる」is the causative form (“make or let someone else go out”), which does not fit John's own wish.
default.q.n3-9-q43-43.why.3: (d) Incorrect because it uses both the wrong verb form (the causative 「出させる」) and an incorrect grammar pattern before 「なりたい」.
default.q.n3-9-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 降っていない, which combines with 「もう」 to express that it is no longer raining now.
default.q.n3-9-q44-44.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: It rained very heavily this morning, but it has stopped raining now.
Kanji: 今朝: this morning, 雨: rain, 今: now, 降: to fall; to rain.
Example: さっきまで泣いていた赤ちゃんが、もう泣いていない。(The baby who was crying until a moment ago is no longer crying.)
default.q.n3-9-q44-44.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the contrastive conjunction 「が」 requires the following clause to contrast with the preceding one (“It rained heavily this morning, but now...” ).
default.q.n3-9-q44-44.why.1: (b) Correct because 「もう〜ていない」describes a state that is no longer continuing (it has stopped raining and is no longer raining now).
default.q.n3-9-q44-44.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the dictionary form「降る」describes a future action or a habitual occurrence, not the current weather condition at the moment of speaking, 「今」.
default.q.n3-9-q44-44.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「降らない」 states a general fact or future possibility. To express that it is not raining at the present moment, the negative progressive form 「降っていない」 must be used.
default.q.n3-9-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 落ちそうです, which uses the intransitive verb 落ちる with the V-masu stem + そうだ to describe signs that something is about to happen.
default.q.n3-9-q45-45.explanation:
Meaning:
Nishikawa: "Mr. Mori, your mobile phone is about to fall out of your pocket."
Mori: "You're right. Thank you."
On'yomi: 携帯電話 (mobile phone), 本当 (really, true), 落ちる (to fall).
Distinction: 落ちる (intransitive verb: something falls by itself) vs. 落とす (transitive verb: someone drops something).
Example: 木からりんごが落ちそうになっている。(The apple on the tree looks as if it is about to fall.)
default.q.n3-9-q45-45.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「dictionary-form verb + そうです」is the hearsay pattern (“I hear it will fall”), not the expression used when something appears about to happen before one’s eyes.
default.q.n3-9-q45-45.why.1: (b) Correct because 「落ちる」 is an intransitive verb used with the particle 「が」, combined with 「V-masu stem + そう」 to warn that something is about to happen (the phone is about to fall out).
default.q.n3-9-q45-45.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「落とす」 is a transitive verb (“drop something”) used with 「を」, and the hearsay structure is unsuitable for a direct reminder.
default.q.n3-9-q45-45.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「落とす」 is a transitive verb requiring a person as the subject and 「を」 for the object, whereas the sentence uses 「が」 to indicate something falling on its own, so the intransitive verb 「落ちる」 is required.
default.q.n3-9-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 4. みたいだ, a pattern used to make an inference based on information one has heard: “it seems” or “apparently.”
default.q.n3-9-q46-46.explanation:
Meaning:
A: “I hear a new cake shop is going to open in front of the station soon.”
B: “Really? I'm so excited!”
Kanji note: 今度 (this time, next time), 駅前 (in front of the station), 新 (new), 楽 (enjoyment, excitement).
Example: 田中さんは来月結婚するみたいですよ。(It seems that Mr. Tanaka is getting married next month.)
default.q.n3-9-q46-46.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜でしょう」is used for a confident guess or to seek agreement, so it is unnatural as B's surprised response to newly received information, 「本当ですか」.
default.q.n3-9-q46-46.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「〜といい」 expresses a wish or hope (“I wish I could open a bakery”), so it does not fit when Speaker B is asking whether the statement is true: 「本当ですか」 (“Is that true?”).
default.q.n3-9-q46-46.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜ほうがいい」 is used to give advice (saying what would be better to do), so it does not fit the context at all.
default.q.n3-9-q46-46.why.3: (d) Correct because 「〜みたいだ」 expresses a judgment based on information heard from someone else (it seems that a new bakery is about to open), which fits Speaker B’s response asking for confirmation.
default.q.n3-9-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 1. やりすぎるのもよくない (the grammar pattern V-masu + すぎる means “to do something excessively”).
default.q.n3-9-q47-47.explanation:
Meaning: This flower needs to be watered when the top layer of soil dries out, but watering it too much is also bad. If there is too much water, the roots will become waterlogged and rot.
Kanji-based meanings: 花 (flower), 乾 (dry), 水 (water), 根 (root), 腐 (rot).
Example: いくら体にいい食べ物でも、食べすぎるのはよくない。(No matter how healthy a food is, eating too much of it is not good.)
default.q.n3-9-q47-47.why.0: (a) Correct because 「やりすぎる」 (overwatering) combines with 「〜のもよくない」 (is also not good), perfectly matching the explanation that too much water causes the roots to rot.
default.q.n3-9-q47-47.why.1: (b) Incorrect because it means “it would be good not to need watering,” directly contradicting the previous clause, “when the surface is dry, it needs to be watered.”
default.q.n3-9-q47-47.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「やってやる」has a condescending nuance of doing something for someone, not the meaning of watering too much and causing root rot.
default.q.n3-9-q47-47.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「やらないでおく」means “leave it without watering it,” which contradicts the need to water it when the soil is dry.
default.q.n3-9-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 変えていただけないでしようか (a polite request using honorific language: “Would you be able to change it for me?”).
default.q.n3-9-q48-48.explanation:
Meaning:
Receptionist: “Yes, Yamada Hospital speaking.”
Patient: “Excuse me, I’m Tanaka, and I have an appointment at 10:00. Would it be possible to change it to 11:00?”
Sino-Japanese vocabulary: 患者 (patient), 受付 (reception desk; receptionist), 病院 (hospital), 予約 (appointment; reservation), 申 (to say; to state), 変 (change).
Example: 申し訳ありませんが、こちらの書類を確認していただけないでしょうか。(I am very sorry, but would you kindly check these documents?)
default.q.n3-9-q48-48.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜ましょうか」 offers to help the other person (“Shall I change it for you?”). It is not used when the speaker is the one asking for a favor.
default.q.n3-9-q48-48.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「〜たほうがいいですか」 asks for advice about whether one should do something; it does not express a request for the other person to reschedule the appointment.
default.q.n3-9-q48-48.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜ていただきましょう」 means “let us receive someone’s action” and has a suggestive or self-directed nuance; it is not used to make a request to the other person.
default.q.n3-9-q48-48.why.3: (d) Correct because 「〜ていただけないでしょうか」 is a very polite honorific request form, meaning “Could you please change the appointment time for me?”
default.q.n3-9-q49-49.verdict: The correct order is: 1 → 4 → 3 → 2. The choice in the ★ position is 3 (解けない).
default.q.n3-9-q49-49.explanation:
Complete sentence: この小学生は大人でも解けないような問題を簡単に解いてしまう。
Meaning: This elementary school student easily solves problems that even adults cannot solve.
default.q.n3-9-q49-49.why.0: (a) 1. 大人: It is in position 1 and combines with the particle 「でも」 (4) to form 「大人でも」 (even adults).
default.q.n3-9-q49-49.why.1: (b) 2. ような: It appears in the fourth position, following the verb 「解けない」 (3), in the structure 「〜ような＋noun」 to modify the noun 「問題」 that follows.
default.q.n3-9-q49-49.why.2: (c) 3. 解けない: It occupies the third position (★), expressing inability in the negative and following 「大人でも」. It modifies 「ような」 (2) to form 「大人でも解けないような」.
default.q.n3-9-q49-49.why.3: (d) 4. でも: It comes second, immediately after the noun 「大人」(1), to emphasize “even adults.”
default.q.n3-9-q50-50.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 4 → 1 → 2. The star ★ marks answer choice 1 (楽しいこと).
default.q.n3-9-q50-50.explanation:
Complete passage: 去年、初めて一人で海外を旅行した。行く前は心配なこともあったが、旅行していた週間は楽しいことばかりだった。
Meaning: Last year, I traveled abroad alone for the first time. I had some worries before I left, but the time I spent traveling was filled with nothing but enjoyable experiences.
default.q.n3-9-q50-50.why.0: (a) 1. 楽しいこと: It occupies the third position (★) and is a noun phrase preceding the particle 「ばかり」(2), forming the predicate phrase 「楽しいことばかり」.
default.q.n3-9-q50-50.why.1: (b) 2. ばかり: It occupies the fourth position, immediately before 「だった」, and combines with 「楽しいこと」 (1) according to the grammar pattern 「noun ＋ ばかりだ」 (consisting entirely of / nothing but...).
default.q.n3-9-q50-50.why.2: (c) 3. 旅行していた: It occupies position 1 as a past-tense modifying clause placed before and modifying the time noun 「週間は」 (4).
default.q.n3-9-q50-50.why.3: (d) 4. 週間は: It occupies the second position, follows 「旅行していた」(3), and uses 「は」to mark the topic or time period for the following clause.
default.q.n3-9-q51-51.verdict: The correct order is: 4 → 1 → 3 → 2. The starred position (★) is answer choice 3 (ほど).
default.q.n3-9-q51-51.explanation:
Complete dialogue: A「昨日は日曜日だったから、遊園地は人が多かったでしよう?」
B「いや、思っていたほど込んでいませんでしたよ。」
Meaning: A: “Yesterday was Sunday, so the amusement park must have been crowded, right?”
B: “No, it wasn’t as crowded as I had expected.”
default.q.n3-9-q51-51.why.0: (a) 1. いた: It appears in the second position and combines with the te-form 「思って」(4) to create the past progressive form 「思っていた」.
default.q.n3-9-q51-51.why.1: (b) 2. 込んで: It is in the fourth position, immediately before the final negative predicate 「いませんでしたよ」, forming 「込んでいませんでした」(was not crowded).
default.q.n3-9-q51-51.why.2: (c) 3. ほど: Appears in the third position (the ★ slot), following「思っていた」(4-1), in the negative comparison pattern「〜ほど…ない」(not ... to the extent expected).
default.q.n3-9-q51-51.why.3: (d) 4. 思って: It is in the first position, immediately after 「いや、」, and is the te-form linking to the auxiliary verb 「いた」 (1).
default.q.n3-9-q52-52.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 3 → 4 → 1. The ★ position is answer choice 4 (してくれていたことが).
default.q.n3-9-q52-52.explanation:
Complete sentence: 一人暮らしを始めて、両親が毎日仕事をしながら食事の準備や洗濯をしてくれていたことがどれだけ大変なことだったか、よくわかった。
Meaning: After I started living on my own, I truly realized how hard it must have been for my parents to work every day while also preparing meals and doing the laundry for me.
default.q.n3-9-q52-52.why.0: (a) 1. どれだけ: It comes in the fourth position, directly before 「大変なことだったか」, to emphasize the degree (“how difficult it was” / “just how hard it was”).
default.q.n3-9-q52-52.why.1: (b) 2. しながら: It comes first, immediately after 「仕事を」in the question, following the pattern 「V-masu stem ＋ ながら」(while doing...).
default.q.n3-9-q52-52.why.2: (c) 3. 食事の準備や洗濯を: This is in the second position and is the object, marked by 「を」, of the following action 「してくれていた」 (4).
default.q.n3-9-q52-52.why.3: (d) 4. してくれていたことが: It occupies the third position (the ★ slot), combining the benefactive pattern 「〜てくれる」 with nominalization by 「こと」 to serve as the subject, marked by 「が」, of the subordinate clause 「どれだけ大変なことだったか」.
default.q.n3-9-q53-53.verdict: Correct order: 4 → 1 → 3 → 2. The position marked ★ is choice 3 (熱が下がって).
default.q.n3-9-q53-53.explanation:
Complete dialogue: 患者「先生、おふろには人ってもいいんでしようか。」
医者「あしたになって熱が下がっていたらいいでよ」
Meaning: Patient: “Doctor, is it all right for me to take a bath?”
Doctor: “If your fever has gone down by tomorrow, it will be fine.”
default.q.n3-9-q53-53.why.0: (a) 1. なって: it occupies the second position after 「あしたに」(4), forming 「あしたになって」(when tomorrow comes).
default.q.n3-9-q53-53.why.1: (b) 2. いたら: In the fourth position, it follows the te-form 「熱が下がって」 (3) to form the conditional pattern 「〜ていたら＋いい」 (“it would be good if...” ).
default.q.n3-9-q53-53.why.2: (c) 3. 熱が下がって: It occupies the third position (★) and expresses the state of a fever going down in the te-form, linking to the auxiliary verb 「いたら」(2).
default.q.n3-9-q53-53.why.3: (d) 4. あしたに: It should be placed in position 1 and combined with the verb 「なって」 (1) to establish the point when it changes to the following day.
default.q.n3-9-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 3. でも.
default.q.n3-9-q54-54.explanation: The preceding sentence describes how the author enjoyed April, shortly after arriving in Japan, taking part in activities such as viewing cherry blossoms, shopping, and playing tennis (「楽しく過ごしていました」). The next sentence shifts to June and the rainy season, when frequent rain prevented the author from playing tennis and became bothersome (「6 月になると、梅雨で雨の日が多くなりました」). The relationship between the two sentences is contrastive, shifting from enjoyment to annoyance, so the conjunction 「でも」(but, however) is needed.
default.q.n3-9-q54-54.why.0: (a) 「だから」 (therefore) expresses a cause-and-effect relationship, so it is inappropriate because the latter clause is not an inevitable result of the former.
default.q.n3-9-q54-54.why.1: (b) 「つまり」 (“in other words / in short”) is used to summarize or restate the preceding content, so it does not fit a transition involving a change in time and state.
default.q.n3-9-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「でも」 (but/however) is a conjunction showing a contrast between April, filled with joy, and gloomy, troublesome June, the rainy season -> the best fit.
default.q.n3-9-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「そのうえ」(moreover / in addition) adds information in the same direction, so it is unsuitable for a contrastive context.
default.q.n3-9-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 友達.
default.q.n3-9-q55-55.explanation: Before this point in the passage, the writer has described only personal feelings and daily life after first arriving in Japan, without mentioning any friend. When a person or object is introduced for the first time in a Japanese text, the ordinary noun 「友達」(a friend) is used rather than the demonstrative 「その」. After the friend has been introduced, the text can refer back to that person, as in 「友達がくれた傘」(the umbrella the friend gave me). Therefore, 「友達」is the most appropriate choice.
default.q.n3-9-q55-55.why.0: (a) 「その友達」(that friend) contains the demonstrative 「その」, which is used when the referent has already been mentioned in the context. However, the friend had not appeared earlier in the passage.
default.q.n3-9-q55-55.why.1: (b) 「こういう友達」 (“a friend like this”) describes a type or characteristic of friend; it is not used to introduce a specific character into a story.
default.q.n3-9-q55-55.why.2: (c) 「どちらかの友達」 (“one of the two friends”) is used when two specific friends have already been mentioned, so it does not fit this context.
default.q.n3-9-q55-55.why.3: (d) 「友達」(friend / my friend) is a bare noun used to introduce a person appearing in the narrative for the first time, so it is the most appropriate choice.
default.q.n3-9-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 2. かいてあったのです.
default.q.n3-9-q56-56.explanation: The preceding sentence describes how, when the umbrella was opened, its inside was completely different from its ordinary black exterior (「ところが、傘を開くと内側は全く違っていました」). The next sentence explains the specific reason for this unexpected difference: a beautiful cherry-blossom picture had been painted inside the umbrella. The structure 「〜のです / 〜んです」 at the end of the sentence provides an explanation or background for what was just mentioned. Therefore, 「かいてあったのです」 is the correct answer.
default.q.n3-9-q56-56.why.0: (a) 「かいてあったそうです」 (I hear that it had been drawn) reports information heard from someone else, whereas this was something the author personally saw after opening the umbrella.
default.q.n3-9-q56-56.why.1: (b) 「かいてあったのです」 (“it turned out that it had been drawn” / “the reason was that it had been drawn”) uses 「〜のです」 to explain the surprising detail in the previous sentence—that the inside looked completely different when the box was opened. It is the best fit.
default.q.n3-9-q56-56.why.2: (c) 「かいてあったはずです」(It should have been drawn) expresses an evidence-based supposition and is not used when directly observing the actual situation.
default.q.n3-9-q56-56.why.3: (d) 「かいてあったおかげです」 (thanks to having been drawn) indicates a cause that produces a positive result, so it does not fit the grammar or the narrative description of the state here.
default.q.n3-9-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 思うこともあります.
default.q.n3-9-q57-57.explanation: The final part of the passage describes a clear change in the author's feelings because of the cherry-blossom umbrella: at first, the author disliked rainy days very much (「雨の日は嫌だと思っていました」), but now no longer dislikes them (「今は、この傘があるので雨の日が嫌ではありません」). In fact, when sunny weather continues for several days, the author sometimes hopes for rain in order to use the umbrella (「雨が降ってほしいなあと 思うこともあります」). The grammar structure 「V-る + こともある」(sometimes, there are also times when...) describes something that occurs occasionally and fits the author's astonished conclusion perfectly: "Just because of one umbrella, a person's mood can change this much."
default.q.n3-9-q57-57.why.0: (a) 「思うこともあります」 (“there are also times when I think...”), using the structure「V-る + こともある」(sometimes/there are times when...), expresses a change in feelings: from disliking rain to sometimes wishing for rain so that the speaker can open the beautiful umbrella. It is the best fit.
default.q.n3-9-q57-57.why.1: (b) 「思ったらいいです」 (“you should think that ... / I wish you would think that ...”) gives advice or expresses a wish directed at someone else, and is not used for narrating one’s own mental state.
default.q.n3-9-q57-57.why.2: (c) 「思うことができません」(cannot think...) expresses an inability to think that way, which is contrary to the author's fondness for the umbrella.
default.q.n3-9-q57-57.why.3: (d) 「思わなくなりました」 (“I no longer thought…”) combined with 「雨が降ってほしいなあと」 (“I wish it would rain”) would mean “I no longer wanted it to rain,” contradicting the passage’s positive feelings about rainy days.
default.q.n3-9-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 3: People who cannot attend the information session on the morning of the convention are not allowed to apply.
default.q.n3-9-q58-58.explanation:

The notice recruits approximately 100 volunteers to support the 3rd Yamakawa City Marathon:
- Event time: Saturday, April 17 (7:00 a.m. to approximately 3:00 p.m.).

  1. Applicants must apply through the Sports Department's website before January 8.

  3. People who cannot attend the morning briefing on the day of the event cannot apply.
  4. Only people with prior experience helping at a marathon event can apply.

default.q.n3-9-q58-58.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the specific details of the work will be sent by mail in late March (お願いする具体的な内容は、３月下旬に郵送でお知らせいたします), not revealed only on the day of the convention.
default.q.n3-9-q58-58.why.2: (c) Correct because the rules state the participation requirement: 「応募できる方：・・・大会当日の午前７時からの説明会に参加できる方」(Eligible applicants: ... those who can attend the briefing session beginning at 7:00 a.m. on the day of the competition). Therefore, anyone unable to attend this session is not eligible to apply.
default.q.n3-9-q58-58.why.3: (d) Incorrect, because the passage says 「特に、マラソン大会を手伝った経験がある方は歓迎します」 (“those with experience helping at a marathon event are especially welcome”), meaning that such experience is preferred, not that only experienced applicants may apply.
default.q.n3-9-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 道を歩きながら、たばこを吸ってはいけない (You must not smoke while walking).
default.q.n3-9-q59-59.explanation:
Main idea:
The city of Asahi enacted new regulations banning three behaviors in order to keep the city clean and pleasant to live in: (1) throwing trash anywhere other than designated places such as trash bins; (2) smoking while walking; and (3) parking bicycles outside designated areas. In some cases, violators may be fined.

Question translation:
Which of the following statements about these regulations is correct?

Answer choices:
1. Trash may not be thrown away anywhere except at one's own home.
2. Smoking while walking on the street is prohibited.
3. Bicycles may not be ridden anywhere outside designated areas.
4. Everyone who fails to follow the regulations must pay a fine.
default.q.n3-9-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the rule prohibits disposing of trash anywhere other than designated places such as trash cans (quoted:「ごみ箱などの決められた場所以外にごみを捨てること」); it does not prohibit throwing trash outside one's own home, as disposal is still allowed at designated public locations.
default.q.n3-9-q59-59.why.1: (b) Correct because the letter clearly states that the second prohibited action is ②「歩きながらたばこを吸うこと」among the prohibited behaviors (禁止している), exactly matching the meaning of not smoking while walking.
default.q.n3-9-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the notice prohibits parking or leaving bicycles outside the designated area (quote: 「指定の場所以外に自転車をとめること」— とめる means to stop or park a vehicle), not riding bicycles (走ってはいけない).
default.q.n3-9-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the notice only says that “there are also cases in which people are made to pay” (quote: 「お金を払わされることもある」), not that everyone who violates the rule must pay (全員).
default.q.n3-9-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (鈴木電気の新製品以外のパンフレットと説明書、価格表を送った。).
default.q.n3-9-q60-60.explanation:
- Main point of the passage: This is a business letter from Yamamoto Kazuo of Suzuki Electric Industries, Inc. (鈴木電気工業) to Aoyama Ichiro of Tanaka Electric Co., Ltd. Yamamoto thanks Aoyama for attending Suzuki's recent new-product presentation. In response to Aoyama's request for information about products other than the new product, Yamamoto enclosed pamphlets, manuals, and price lists for those products.

  1. Sent pamphlets, manuals, and price lists for Tanaka Electric's new products.
  2. Sent pamphlets, manuals, and price lists for Suzuki Electric's new products.
  3. Sent pamphlets, manuals, and price lists for Tanaka Electric's products other than the new product.
  4. Sent pamphlets, manuals, and price lists for Suzuki Electric's products other than the new product.
default.q.n3-9-q60-60.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the sender is Yamamoto from Suzuki Electric (鈴木電気工業), not Tanaka Electric (田中電気—the recipient), and the document concerns "other products" (その他の製品), not new products (新製品).
default.q.n3-9-q60-60.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the briefing on the new product (新製品説明会) had already taken place, while the materials enclosed this time were for products other than the new product (「その他の製品についての説明を、 ということでしたので、 バンフレットと説明書、 価格表をお送りいたします」).

default.q.n3-9-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 近所の店に断られたとき.
default.q.n3-9-q61-61.explanation:
- Main point: The author got ink on some clothing and took it to a nearby dry cleaner, but the shop refused because it could not remove the stain. The author then found a shop online that accepted stain-removal work, even though it was far away and the clothing had to be mailed. Although the clothing came back clean, the service was rather expensive, so the author decided to use that shop only when absolutely necessary, as in this case when the nearby shop had refused the job.

- Question:
  What kind of situation does “times when there is no other choice, like this time” refer to?

- Answer choices:
  1. When there is no time to go to a nearby shop.
  2. When the nearby shop refuses the job.
  3. When white clothing gets dirty.
  4. When one does not have much money.
default.q.n3-9-q61-61.why.0: (a) Incorrect because in the passage the author took the clothes to a nearby dry cleaner (「近所のクリーニング店に持っていったら」), not because they did not have time to go.
default.q.n3-9-q61-61.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage provides evidence: 「近所のクリーニング店に持っていったら、この汚れは落とせないと断られてしまった。」 (When I took it to a nearby dry cleaner, they refused because they could not remove the stain). Because the nearby shop refused, the author had to resort to the expensive option of sending the item to a distant cleaner.
default.q.n3-9-q61-61.why.2: (c) Incorrect because making something dirty is a specific event that has just occurred, not a reason explaining a situation in which one is "forced to" or has "no choice but to" use an expensive shop.
default.q.n3-9-q61-61.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the shop is expensive (「値段が高い」), so someone with little money could not ask the shop to do it; the passage also never mentions that the author lacks money.
default.q.n3-9-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (腕を骨折したから - because I broke my arm).
default.q.n3-9-q62-62.explanation:
The passage clearly states that the reason the mother lost her spirit and vitality was that she had fallen and broken her arm (腕を骨折し) six months earlier. She subsequently lost her appetite and lost weight. The fracture had actually healed after three weeks.

* Question translation: What caused the mother to lose her spirit and vitality?
* Answer choices:
1. Because she lost her appetite.
2. Because she lost weight.
3. Because she broke her arm.
4. Because the injury did not heal for a long time.
default.q.n3-9-q62-62.why.0: (a) Incorrect because losing one’s appetite (食欲が落ちた) occurred after the mother had completely lost her energy and spirit (それ以来すっかり元気をなくしてしまっていた); it was not the initial cause.
default.q.n3-9-q62-62.why.1: (b) Incorrect because weight loss (体重も減った) is also a result or consequence of feeling depressed and losing one’s appetite, not the cause of feeling depressed.
default.q.n3-9-q62-62.why.2: (c) Correct because the passage clearly states: 「実は、母は半年前に転んで腕を骨折し、それ以来すっかり元気をなくしてしまっていた。」 (Actually, half a year earlier, my mother fell and broke her arm, and since then she had completely lost her spirits.)
default.q.n3-9-q62-62.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage says: 「骨折は 3 週間で治った」 (the broken bone healed in 3 weeks), so saying that the injury did not heal contradicts the passage.
default.q.n3-9-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (若い人たちがいるところで運動したり、仲間と頑張ったりできたから - Because they could exercise where young people were and work hard together with peers).
default.q.n3-9-q63-63.explanation:
The author points out that both the hospital and the sports club offer exercises tailored to each individual without overexertion. However, only at the sports club can the mother exercise in the same space as energetic young people and make an effort alongside people her own age, which rekindled her will to live.

* Question translation: Why was the mother able to regain her health and spirits at the sports club rather than at the hospital?
* Answer choices:
1. Because an individualized exercise program was designed so it would not be too strenuous.
2. Because she could exercise in a place with young people and make an effort alongside people her own age.
3. Because an effective exercise program was designed that produced results after only one month.
4. Because she made friends with healthy people and did the same exercises as the young people.
default.q.n3-9-q63-63.why.0: (a) Incorrect because designing manageable exercises suited to each individual (無理をせずにできるトレーニングを一人一人に考えてくれる) takes place both at the hospital and at the sports club (病院でもスポーツクラブでも). Therefore, it is not a distinctive reason why the mother recovered at the sports club rather than at the hospital.
default.q.n3-9-q63-63.why.1: (b) Correct because the passage clearly states: 「しかし、元気な若い人たちと同じ場所で運動したり、同じくらいの年の仲間と一緒に頑張ったりすることは、スポーツクラブだからできたのである。そして、 それが母の生きる力を引き出してくれたのだろう。」
default.q.n3-9-q63-63.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the reading only states that the mother became energetic like a completely different person after just one month (たった 1 か月で全く違う人のように元気になった); it does not say that the club devised an exercise that was effective in exactly one month.

default.q.n3-9-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 安い値段がうれしくて買いたくなるから (Because the low price makes people happy and makes them want to buy it).
default.q.n3-9-q65-65.explanation:
**Main point:** The author explains that many people cannot tidy their rooms because of their shopping habits: whenever they see a sale sign, they happily enter the store, and whenever they see something cheap, they immediately open their wallets without considering whether they really need it, causing their rooms to become filled with belongings.

**Question:** The passage says “① open their wallets.” Why is that?
**Answer choices:**
1. Because there is still room for more things in the room.
2. Because they feel it would be wrong or awkward to leave the store without buying anything.
3. Because they are delighted to see a low price and want to buy the item.
4. Because they think the item must certainly be necessary for them.
default.q.n3-9-q65-65.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage says that buying things without thinking resulted in the room becoming filled with possessions (その結果、部屋に物があふれる). They did not buy things because there was still storage space.
default.q.n3-9-q65-65.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is incorrect because the passage never mentions that the customer felt guilty or embarrassed when leaving the store without buying anything.
default.q.n3-9-q65-65.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because the passage clearly states: 「「セール」や「割引」の看板を見つけると、喜んで、つい店に入ってしまう。そして、安くなっているのを見ると、それが必要かどうか深く考えず、①財布を開く。」 (When people see a sale sign, they happily enter the store, and when they see that something is cheap, they open their wallets without carefully considering whether they need it.)
default.q.n3-9-q65-65.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage clearly says that they bought things "without thinking deeply about whether they were necessary" (それが必要かどうか深く考えず), contrary to "being certain that the item was necessary."
default.q.n3-9-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 必要かどうか、同じような物がないか、しまう場所があるかを、よく考える (Think carefully about whether it is necessary, whether you already have something similar, and whether you have a place to store it).
default.q.n3-9-q66-66.explanation:
**Summary:** The author offers three steps to consider when shopping: (1) Ask whether the item is necessary; (2) if it is necessary, check whether you already have something similar; (3) if not, check whether you have somewhere to store it. If there is no storage space, give up on buying it. Only buy it if, after thinking it through that carefully, you still feel that it is necessary.

**Translation of the question:** Which statement matches the advice about shopping in ②?
**Translation of the choices:**
1. If you have storage space, you should buy it even if you already have something similar.
2. If you think it is necessary, you should buy it immediately without considering anything else.
3. Think carefully about whether it is necessary, whether you already have something similar, and whether you have somewhere to store it.
4. Think carefully about whether you already have something similar, whether you have storage space, and whether it is truly inexpensive.
default.q.n3-9-q66-66.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the author advises not buying another item if one already has something similar, rather than saying that it is acceptable to buy one as long as there is somewhere to store it.
default.q.n3-9-q66-66.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the author advises that even when something seems necessary, one should next consider whether one already owns something similar and whether there is space to store it; the advice is not to buy it immediately without thinking.
default.q.n3-9-q66-66.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because it exactly matches the three-step process recommended by the author: 「買う前に、まず、必要かどうかを考える。必要だと思ったら、次に、同じような物を持っていないかどうかを考える。持っていなければ、最後に、それをしまう場所があるかどうかを考える。」 (Before buying something, first consider whether it is necessary. If it seems necessary, then consider whether you already have something similar. If you do not, finally consider whether you have a place to store it).
default.q.n3-9-q66-66.why.3: (d) Answer choice 4 is incorrect because the author does not advise considering whether an item is “really cheap” (本当に安いか); the first step is to consider whether it is “necessary” (必要かどうか).
default.q.n3-9-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 部屋の整理に悩んでいる人は、気をつけよう (People who are struggling to organize their rooms should be careful).
default.q.n3-9-q67-67.explanation:
**Summary:** The conclusion directly connects to the introduction: the passage discusses people who suffer from cluttered rooms because of impulsive bargain shopping. As major sales at department stores approach, the author reminds these people to be careful and restrain themselves by following the advice given above.

**Question translation:** Which choice is most appropriate for filling in the blank （ ）?
**Answer choices:**
1. Even people who are good at cleaning their rooms should enjoy shopping.
2. People who like shopping should check the price carefully before buying.
3. People who want to buy things cheaply should hurry to the store.
4. People who are troubled by cleaning their rooms should be careful.
default.q.n3-9-q67-67.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the article is aimed at people who are struggling to tidy their rooms (「部屋が片付けられない」と悩む人), not at people who are good at cleaning and are advised to go shopping.
default.q.n3-9-q67-67.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the author recommends controlling unnecessary purchases, not “looking carefully at the price before buying.”
default.q.n3-9-q67-67.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the article warns against impulsively rushing to buy things whenever they see a discount. It does not encourage people to “quickly go to the store and buy cheap items.”
default.q.n3-9-q67-67.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because the author begins by discussing people who cannot tidy their rooms (「部屋が片付けられない」と悩む人) and concludes with a warning: if you keep buying unnecessary items just because they are cheap, it is only natural for the room to become cluttered. Therefore, people troubled by tidying their rooms should be careful (気をつけよう) when the sale season at shopping centers is about to begin, so that they do not shop impulsively again.

default.q.n3-9-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect because during his business trip to Kyoto, Ogawa met only Kawakami and Kinoshita, not Mr. Oyama (これからは時々先生にもお目にかかって... と話し合いました).

1. [14] years ago (shown in the question: 年前)

default.q.n3-9-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 1. しぜん.
default.q.n3-9-q1-1.explanation:
Translation: "The people of this country greatly value nature."
自然 means nature.
Example: 自然豊かな環境で暮らしたい。(I want to live in an environment rich in nature.)
default.q.n3-9-q1-1.why.0: (a) Correct. 「自然」 is read as 「しぜん」 and means nature or natural.
default.q.n3-9-q1-1.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「じぜん」 is the reading of 「事前」(beforehand) or 「慈善」(charity); the 自 in 自然 is read with the unvoiced sound し.
default.q.n3-9-q1-1.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「しせん」 is the reading of 「視線」 (gaze, line of sight) or 「四川」 (Sichuan); the 然 in 自然 is read as ぜん, not せん.
default.q.n3-9-q1-1.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「じせん」 is an incorrect voiced reading of 自然 in this context (or may refer to 自選, “self-selection,” which is not relevant here).
default.q.n3-9-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 3. びょう.
default.q.n3-9-q2-2.explanation:
Sentence meaning: It will be finished in about 30 seconds.
Kanji-based meaning: 秒 means “second” (びょう).
Example: 1分は60秒です。(One minute is 60 seconds.)
default.q.n3-9-q2-2.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「じょう」 is the reading of kanji such as 「条」, 「場」, and 「畳」; it is not the reading of 「秒」.
default.q.n3-9-q2-2.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「しょう」is the reading of「少」,「小」,「賞」, and others (easily confused because of the 少 component on the right), but 秒 is read as びょう.
default.q.n3-9-q2-2.why.2: (c) Correct. 「秒」 has the on-reading 「びょう」 (MIỄU) and means “second,” a unit of time.
default.q.n3-9-q2-2.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「ひょう」 is the reading of 「表」, 「票」, 「評」, and others; the voiced sound in 秒 is びょう.
default.q.n3-9-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 3. のこり.
default.q.n3-9-q3-3.explanation:
Sentence meaning: There are only three days left of summer vacation.
Sino-Japanese reading: 残 (remain — のこ・る / のこ・り).
Example: 残りの時間でテストの見直しをする。(Use the remaining time to review the test.)
default.q.n3-9-q3-3.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「もとり」 is not a valid Japanese word or reading in this context.
default.q.n3-9-q3-3.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「おわり」is the reading of 「終わり」(the end, the final part), which uses completely different kanji.
default.q.n3-9-q3-3.why.2: (c) Correct. 「残り」 has the kun-reading 「のこり」, comes from the verb 「残る」 (のこる), and means “the remainder” or “the amount left.”
default.q.n3-9-q3-3.why.3: (d) Incorrect.「あまり」is the reading of「余り」(excess, remainder), not「残」.
default.q.n3-9-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 2. ぞうげん.
default.q.n3-9-q4-4.explanation:
Sentence meaning: This chart shows the increase and decrease in population.
Sino-Japanese reading: 増減 (ZOUGEN).
Example: 売上の増減をグラフにまとめる。(Summarize fluctuations in sales in a graph.)
default.q.n3-9-q4-4.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「ぞうけん」 has the wrong voicing for 「減」; 減 is read げん, not けん.
default.q.n3-9-q4-4.why.1: (b) Correct. 「増減」 is formed from 「増」 (ぞう - INCREASE) and 「減」 (げん - DECREASE), read as 「ぞうげん」, meaning increase and decrease.
default.q.n3-9-q4-4.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「じょうけん」is the reading of「条件」(condition); both kanji readings are wrong.
default.q.n3-9-q4-4.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「じょうげん」 is the reading of 「上限」 (“upper limit”); 増 is read as ぞう, not じょう.
default.q.n3-9-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 1. つうち.
default.q.n3-9-q5-5.explanation:
Translation: The interview results will be announced within one week.
Kanji reading and meaning: 通知 (つうち) means notification.

Meaning: "After hearing your explanation, I fully understood why my answer was wrong."
- Vocabulary: 「納得」（なっとく）means to understand thoroughly, accept, and be completely convinced. The verb 「納得する」is synonymous with 「とてもよく分かる / 十分に理解する」.
- Example: 彼の説明にみんなが納得した。(Everyone fully understood and was convinced by his explanation.)
default.q.n3-9-q30-30.why.0: (a) 少し分かった means “understood a little,” which does not express the complete understanding and acceptance conveyed by 納得.
default.q.n3-9-q30-30.why.1: (b) とてもよく分かった means “understood very clearly / understood completely,” accurately conveying the meaning of 納得した (fully understanding and accepting something).
default.q.n3-9-q30-30.why.2: (c) もう一度考えた means “thought about it one more time”; it does not express the result of realizing or understanding the issue.
default.q.n3-9-q30-30.why.3: (d) 何度も考えた means “thought about it many times”; it is not synonymous with 納得した.
default.q.n3-9-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 1: あしたは駅前に 7 時に集合してください。
default.q.n3-9-q31-31.explanation: 「集合」（しゅうごう）means to gather or assemble (people gathering at a designated place at a designated time, or a set in mathematics). Example:「明日の朝8時にロビーに集合してください。」(Please gather in the lobby at 8 tomorrow morning.)
default.q.n3-9-q31-31.why.0: 「集合する」is used when people gather at a specific place at a scheduled time; 「駅前に 7 時に集合してください」is a natural and correct combination.
default.q.n3-9-q31-31.why.1: For heavy rain pouring down intensely over a short period, use 「集中（して）」 or 「まとまって」; 「集合」 is not used for weather phenomena.
default.q.n3-9-q31-31.why.2: For a shop carrying a wide variety of fine wines, use 「集まる」 or 「そろう」; 「集合」 is mainly used for people gathering together.
default.q.n3-9-q31-31.why.3: The verb「集める」or noun「収集（する）」is used for collecting stamps;「集合」is not used for collecting objects.
default.q.n3-9-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 3: あの店に行けば、中古のカメラが安く買えますよ。
default.q.n3-9-q32-32.explanation: 「中古」（ちゅうこ）means used or second-hand goods. It is commonly used for machinery, equipment, vehicles, books, and so on (e.g., 中古車, 中古品, 中古カメラ). Example:「中古の車を買うことにした。」(I decided to buy a used car.)
default.q.n3-9-q32-32.why.0: For eggs that have been stored for a long time or are nearing their expiration date, use「古い」or「賞味期限が近い」.「中古」is used for secondhand goods or products, not food.
default.q.n3-9-q32-32.why.1: A close friend from childhood is called「幼なじみ」or「昔からの友達」/「古い友達」;「中古」is not used for people or friendships.
default.q.n3-9-q32-32.why.2: 「中古」is used for used goods or secondhand items. The phrase 「中古のカメラ」, meaning a used camera, is completely correct.
default.q.n3-9-q32-32.why.3: An experienced or long-serving employee is described with 「ベテラン」(veteran), 「古株」, or 「先輩」; 「中古」is not used for employees or people.
default.q.n3-9-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 1: マラソンで前の人を追い抜くときに、腕がぶつかってしまった。
default.q.n3-9-q33-33.explanation: 「追い抜く」（おいぬく）means to catch up with and move ahead of someone or something (an object in motion, or an opponent in rank or achievement). Example:「前の車を追い抜いた。」(I overtook the car in front of me.)
default.q.n3-9-q33-33.why.0: 「追い抜く」 describes passing an object or person moving ahead; in a marathon, “passing the runner in front” is a completely appropriate usage.
default.q.n3-9-q33-33.why.1: To cross over a mountain, a stationary geographical feature, use 「越える」(この山を越えたら), not 「追い抜く」, because a mountain does not move.
default.q.n3-9-q33-33.why.2: To pass an age milestone, such as age 20, use 「超える」 or 「過ぎる」 (二十歳を過ぎると/超えると); 「追い抜く」 is not used for age.
default.q.n3-9-q33-33.why.3: When time passes a specific point, such as 2 o'clock, use 「過ぎる」 (2時を過ぎたので), not 「追い抜く」 for time.
default.q.n3-9-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 3: ここに申込書の書き方の見本があるので、参考にしてください。
default.q.n3-9-q34-34.explanation: 「見本」（みほん）means a sample, specimen, or model used for reference or preview. Example:「商品の見本をお送りします。」(We will send you a product sample.)
default.q.n3-9-q34-34.why.0: The person representing the school at the competition is called a「代表」(学校の代表), not a「見本」(sample, model).
default.q.n3-9-q34-34.why.1: For the average height of Japanese people, use 「平均」 (平均の身長); 「見本」 means a sample and is not used for average statistical data.
default.q.n3-9-q34-34.why.2: 「見本」is a model for others to look at and follow;「書き方の見本」(a model showing how to fill it in) is a very standard usage.
default.q.n3-9-q34-34.why.3: Learning basic, introductory material is expressed with「基本」or「基礎」, not「見本」.

default.q.n3-9-q35-35.explanation: 「だるい」means sluggish, listless, or extremely tired. It describes physical fatigue in the body, legs, arms, and so on: 体・足・腕がだるい. Example:「風邪をひいて、体全体がだるい。」(I have a cold, so my whole body feels sluggish and weak.)
default.q.n3-9-q35-35.why.0: To describe food that tastes bland, use「薄い」(味が薄い);「だるい」is not used to describe flavor.
default.q.n3-9-q35-35.why.1: Loose or baggy clothing after losing weight is expressed with 「緩い」 (ゆるくなった); 「だるい」 is not used for clothing size.
default.q.n3-9-q35-35.why.2: To rest and relax after submitting a report, use 「のんびりしたい」 / 「ゆっくりしたい」 / 「リラックスしたい」. 「だるい」 means feeling sluggish or exhausted, not relaxing.
default.q.n3-9-q35-35.why.3: 「体がだるい」is the precise standard expression for feeling physically heavy, sluggish, and lacking energy.
default.q.n3-20-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 出してしまったのです.
default.q.n3-20-q54-54.explanation: The preceding sentence says: ‘日本で初めてごみを出すとき、私はそのルールのことがまだあまりよくわかっていませんでした。’ (When I took out the garbage in Japan for the first time, I still did not really understand the rules.) The next sentence begins with the conjunction「それで」(therefore / because of that), connecting the cause— not understanding the rules—with the result: accidentally throwing out the garbage without sorting it. The structure「V-てしまう」(to accidentally do something, expressing regret or a mistake), combined with the explanatory ending「〜のです」, becomes「出してしまったのです」, which is the most natural and grammatically accurate choice in context.
default.q.n3-20-q54-54.why.0: (a) CORRECT. The verb 「出す」 combined with 「〜てしまう」 expresses a mistake or regret over doing something one should not have done. The ending 「〜のです」 presents or explains the actual circumstances leading to the following story.
default.q.n3-20-q54-54.why.1: (b) INCORRECT. The ending 「〜からです」 explains the reason for the preceding clause. Here, the sentence begins with 「それで」, a conjunction indicating a result (“therefore”), so it cannot end with 「〜からです」.
default.q.n3-20-q54-54.why.2: (c) INCORRECT. The ending「〜かもしれません」(might, may) expresses conjecture, whereas this was an actual past event carried out by the author and known with certainty.
default.q.n3-20-q54-54.why.3: (d) INCORRECT. It is wrong both because 「〜かもしれません」 is used to speculate about one's own action and because the reason-ending 「〜から」 is used after the conjunction 「それで」.
default.q.n3-20-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ところが.
default.q.n3-20-q55-55.explanation: The previous sentence describes the action: '朝、出かけるとき、アパートの前の決められた場所にごみを出しました。' (In the morning, when I went out, I put the garbage in the designated place in front of the apartment.) The following clause presents an unexpected result contrary to expectations: '夕方帰宅すると、私のごみは回収されずに残っていました。' (When I returned home in the evening, my garbage was still there because it had not been collected.) The conjunction「ところが」(however; even so) signals a change in direction when an unexpected event occurs after an action.
default.q.n3-20-q55-55.why.0: (a) INCORRECT. 「また」 (“also, furthermore”) adds information in the same direction, so it does not fit between an action and an unexpected opposite result.
default.q.n3-20-q55-55.why.1: (b) INCORRECT. 「たとえば」(for example) is used when introducing an example or illustration and is completely inappropriate in this context.
default.q.n3-20-q55-55.why.2: (c) INCORRECT. 「それに」 (“in addition,” “moreover”) adds another point to intensify the meaning; it is not used to express a development contrary to expectations.
default.q.n3-20-q55-55.why.3: (d) CORRECT. 「ところが」 (however / but) is a conjunction marking a contrast and indicating that something happened unexpectedly or contrary to what the speaker had thought after an action (the trash was taken out in the morning, but it was still there when the speaker returned in the afternoon).
default.q.n3-20-q56-56.explanation: The passage explains why garbage must be sorted: 「その日の夜、大家さんが来て、...分けなければいけない理由を説明してくれました。」(That evening, the landlord came and explained why we had to sort the garbage.) The next sentence makes this clear: 「ごみの中には、もう一度資源として使える物もたくさんあります。」(There are also many things in the garbage that can be reused as resources.) The particle 「も」emphasizes the abundance of recyclable resources and is used with 「たくさんあります」.
default.q.n3-20-q56-56.why.0: (a) CORRECT. The particle 「も」replaces 「が」and combines with 「たくさんあります」to emphasize a large quantity: garbage also contains many things that can be recycled into resources.
default.q.n3-20-q56-56.why.1: (b) INCORRECT. The particle 「と」 (“and” / “together with”) connects nouns or quotations; it is not appropriate before the predicate phrase 「たくさんあります」 in this structure.
default.q.n3-20-q56-56.why.2: (c) INCORRECT. 「だけ」(only) expresses limitation, which directly conflicts in meaning with「たくさん」(many, a lot).
default.q.n3-20-q56-56.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「より」means “more than” in comparisons or “from” when indicating a starting point; neither meaning fits this context.
default.q.n3-20-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 分けるようにしています.
default.q.n3-20-q57-57.explanation: After hearing the explanation and understanding that sorting waste helps protect the Earth's resources ('それをきちんと分ければ、大切な地球の資源が守れるということがわかりました'), the author changed their daily habits. The phrase 'それ以降は' (from then on) is followed by a good habit maintained consistently, so the pattern 「V-る + ようにしています」 (to make an effort to keep doing something / to make a habit of doing something) is exactly correct: 'それ以降は、きちんとごみを分けるようにしています。' (Since then, I have made a habit of sorting my garbage carefully.)
default.q.n3-20-q57-57.why.0: (a) INCORRECT. The structure 「〜ことになる」 expresses an objective rule or arrangement beyond the speaker’s control; it does not express a conscious effort to maintain a habit.
default.q.n3-20-q57-57.why.1: (b) Correct. The pattern 「V-る + ようにしている」 expresses a conscious effort to maintain a habit or behavior, which fits well with the time marker indicating a change in habit, 「それ以降は」.
default.q.n3-20-q57-57.why.2: (c) INCORRECT. The ending 「〜と思っていました」indicates a past intention (“I had intended to...”) and often implies that it was not actually done; it is not used for an ongoing habit.
default.q.n3-20-q57-57.why.3: (d) INCORRECT. The expression 「〜だろうと思います」 conveys vague speculation (“I think it may…”), so it does not express the author's actual actions or habits.
default.q.n3-20-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 気がします.
default.q.n3-20-q58-58.explanation: In the concluding sentence, the author summarizes their feelings and realization: 'ごみを分けるのは少し大変です。でも、今まで深く考えたことのなかった環境問題が少し身近になったような気がします。' (Sorting garbage is a little difficult. But I feel that environmental issues—something I had never thought deeply about before—have become a little more familiar to me.) The expression 「〜ような気がします」 (“I feel that …” / “It seems to me that …”) conveys subjective feelings or thoughts in a modest, gentle manner and is highly appropriate for concluding an essay.
default.q.n3-20-q58-58.why.0: (a) INCORRECT. The hearsay ending 「〜そうです」 (“I hear that...”) is used to report someone else's words, not the writer's direct personal impression.
default.q.n3-20-q58-58.why.1: (b) INCORRECT. The interrogative ending「〜でしょうか」is used to express uncertainty or ask the listener a question, so it is unsuitable as a concluding statement expressing the author's thoughts.
default.q.n3-20-q58-58.why.2: (c) CORRECT. The phrase 「〜ような気がします」 (“I feel that it seems…”) subtly and naturally expresses the writer's subjective impression or perception at the present moment in the concluding sentence.
default.q.n3-20-q58-58.why.3: (d) INCORRECT. The past tense 「気がした」 combined with 「〜ようです」 (it seems) expresses an indirect conjecture about a past state. It is not suitable for expressing the writer's present realization.
